name: Roof
description: The uppermost enclosing structure of a building that protects the interior from weather and environmental elements.

name: Wall
description: A vertical structural or non-structural element that encloses, divides, or supports loads within a building.

name: Foundation
description: The substructure element that transfers all building loads safely to the underlying ground or rock.

name: Beam
description: A horizontal structural member that spans between supports and carries transverse loads to columns or walls.

name: Column
description: A vertical structural member that carries compressive axial loads from beams and slabs down to the foundation.

name: Slab
description: A flat horizontal plate of reinforced concrete or other material that forms the floor or ceiling of a building level.

name: Window
description: A glazed opening in a wall or roof that admits natural light and ventilation while maintaining the building envelope.

name: Door
description: A movable barrier set in a wall opening that controls access between spaces and contributes to fire and security separation.

name: Curtain Wall
description: A non-load-bearing external facade system of glass and metal framing that provides weather enclosure and aesthetics.

name: Cladding
description: An external skin or layer applied to the structural frame to provide weather protection and visual finish.

name: Parapet
description: A low protective wall or barrier at the edge of a roof, balcony, or terrace that provides safety and aesthetic definition.

name: Staircase
description: A series of steps and associated structure connecting different floor levels within or outside a building.

name: Ramp
description: An inclined planar surface connecting two different levels to allow pedestrian or vehicular movement without steps.

name: Lift Shaft
description: A vertical enclosed structural enclosure that houses the lift car, guide rails, and associated lift machinery.

name: Retaining Wall
description: A structural wall designed to resist lateral earth or hydrostatic pressure and retain soil at different elevations.

name: Pile
description: A deep foundation element driven or cast into the ground to transfer structural loads to competent bearing strata.

name: Pile Cap
description: A reinforced concrete block cast over a group of piles to distribute column or wall loads evenly across the pile group.

name: Ground Beam
description: A reinforced concrete beam at or below ground level that connects pile caps or strip footings to form a stable substructure grid.

name: Transfer Slab
description: A thick reinforced concrete slab designed to redistribute loads from upper columns or walls to a different structural grid below.

name: Shear Wall
description: A stiff vertical structural panel designed to resist lateral forces such as wind and seismic loads in a building frame.

name: Core Wall
description: A reinforced concrete or structural steel enclosure at the centre of a building that provides primary lateral stability and houses vertical circulation and services.

name: Soffit
description: The exposed underside surface of a slab, beam, staircase, or arch visible from below.

name: Balcony
description: A projecting platform cantilevered or supported from the facade, providing external usable floor area.

name: Facade Panel
description: A prefabricated exterior cladding unit installed onto the structural frame to form the building skin.

name: Roof Drainage System
description: An assembly of gutters, downpipes, and outlets designed to collect and discharge rainwater from the roof safely.

name: Expansion Joint
description: A deliberate gap formed between adjacent structural elements to accommodate thermal movement, settlement, or seismic displacement.

name: HVAC System
description: An integrated system of equipment and ductwork that provides heating, ventilation, and air conditioning to maintain comfortable and healthy indoor environments.

name: Plumbing System
description: A network of pipes, fittings, and fixtures that supply potable water and remove wastewater and sewage from a building.

name: Electrical System
description: The complete installation of switchboards, cabling, and outlets that distributes electrical power and lighting throughout a building.

name: Fire Suppression System
description: An automatic or manual system of sprinklers, pipework, and pumps designed to detect and suppress fires within a building.

name: Lift System
description: A mechanised vertical transportation system consisting of a car, counterweight, guide rails, drive machinery, and control equipment.

name: Fire Detection and Alarm System
description: A network of detectors, sounders, and a central panel that identifies fire or smoke conditions and alerts occupants and emergency services.

name: Building Management System
description: A centralised computer-based control platform that monitors and manages all building services including HVAC, lighting, and security in real time.

name: Stormwater Drainage System
description: A system of drains, pipes, and retention structures that collects and conveys surface and roof runoff away from the building and site.

name: Sanitary Drainage System
description: A gravity-fed pipe network that conveys wastewater and sewage from fixtures to the sewer or treatment system.

name: Hot Water System
description: An assembly of heaters, storage vessels, and distribution pipework that provides hot water to sanitary fixtures throughout the building.

name: Gas Supply System
description: A network of pipes, meters, and regulators that distributes natural gas or LPG to appliances within the building.

name: Compressed Air System
description: A system of compressors, receivers, and pipework delivering pressurised air to pneumatic tools or process equipment.

name: Security and Access Control System
description: An integrated system of card readers, cameras, and control software that manages and monitors authorised entry and movement within the building.

name: Data and Communications Network
description: Structured cabling and active equipment infrastructure providing voice, data, and telecommunications connectivity throughout the building.

name: Lightning Protection System
description: A system of air terminals, conductors, and earth electrodes designed to safely intercept and discharge lightning strikes to ground.

name: Earthing and Bonding System
description: A network of conductors connecting metallic building components and electrical equipment to earth to ensure safety and fault protection.

name: Emergency Lighting System
description: A battery-backed or generator-supplied lighting installation that activates automatically on power failure to illuminate escape routes.

name: Pressurisation System
description: A mechanical system that maintains positive air pressure in stairwells and lift shafts to prevent smoke ingress during a fire event.

name: Chilled Water System
description: A closed-loop pipework and chiller plant system that distributes chilled water to air handling units and fan coil units for cooling.

name: Hydraulic System
description: High-pressure fluid pipework and actuator assemblies used to operate heavy doors, platforms, or lift mechanisms within the building.

name: Photovoltaic System
description: An array of solar panels with inverter and cabling infrastructure installed on the roof or facade to generate on-site renewable electricity.

name: Corridor
description: A long internal passageway connecting rooms or zones on the same floor level and providing a means of escape route.

name: Stairwell
description: An enclosed vertical shaft containing a staircase that provides protected fire egress and access between floor levels.

name: Plant Room
description: A dedicated room housing mechanical, electrical, or hydraulic plant and equipment that serves the building's services systems.

name: Car Park
description: A structured area or separate deck designed and marked for the parking of private and commercial vehicles.

name: Office
description: A workspace configured with desks, partitions, and services infrastructure for administrative and professional occupational activities.

name: Toilet
description: A sanitary space fitted with WC pans, basins, and drainage connections for personal hygiene use by building occupants.

name: Lobby
description: An entrance reception area at ground level or at lift landings that acts as a transition space between public and private zones.

name: Atrium
description: A large multi-storey void space within a building, typically covered by a glazed roof, providing natural light and a visual centrepiece.

name: Loading Dock
description: A recessed or at-grade area at the rear or side of a building designed for the loading and unloading of goods vehicles.

name: Basement
description: A below-ground floor level used for parking, storage, plant, or ancillary functions, enclosed by retaining and basement walls.

name: Roof Terrace
description: An accessible outdoor space on the roof of a building used for recreation, planting, or services access.

name: Server Room
description: A climate-controlled room housing IT servers, network switches, and UPS equipment critical to the building's digital operations.

name: Electrical Switchroom
description: A dedicated room containing main switchboards, distribution boards, and metering equipment serving the building's electrical supply.

name: Lift Machine Room
description: A room above or adjacent to the lift shaft housing the traction motor, gearbox, and control panels for the lift system.

name: Fire Control Room
description: A dedicated room housing the fire indicator panel, intercoms, and controls for fire safety systems, accessible to emergency services.

name: Amenity Space
description: A communal area provided for occupant wellbeing, such as a gym, breakout lounge, or rooftop garden.

name: Riser Shaft
description: A vertical enclosed space or duct that runs through multiple floors to contain and route mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic services.

name: Cleanroom
description: A highly controlled environment with strict limits on airborne particulates, temperature, and humidity for specialised processes or research.

name: Concrete
description: A composite construction material made of cement, aggregate, and water that hardens to form a strong and durable structural mass.

name: Timber
description: A natural wood product used as structural framing, flooring, formwork, or architectural finish in building construction.

name: Steel
description: A high-strength iron-carbon alloy used for structural beams, columns, reinforcement bars, and profiled decking in buildings.

name: Glass
description: A transparent or translucent silica-based material used in windows, curtain walls, skylights, and internal partitions.

name: Insulation
description: A low-conductivity material installed within walls, roofs, and floors to reduce heat transfer and improve energy efficiency.

name: Waterproof Membrane
description: A continuous impermeable sheet or liquid-applied coating applied to roofs, basements, and wet areas to prevent water ingress.

name: Brick
description: A fired clay or calcium silicate masonry unit laid in mortar to form walls, facades, or internal partitions.

name: Mortar
description: A workable paste of cement, sand, and water used to bind masonry units together and provide joint fill.

name: Reinforcement Bar
description: Deformed steel bars embedded within concrete to provide tensile strength and ductility to reinforced concrete members.

name: Structural Steel Section
description: Hot-rolled or cold-formed steel profiles including I-beams, columns, and hollow sections used as primary structural members.

name: Plasterboard
description: A prefabricated panel of gypsum plaster encased in paper facing used for internal wall and ceiling linings.

name: Screed
description: A thin cementitious or anhydrite layer applied over a structural slab to provide a smooth, level surface for floor finishes.

name: Sealant
description: A flexible polymeric compound applied to joints and interfaces to prevent air, water, or gas penetration between building elements.

name: Adhesive
description: A bonding compound used to fix floor tiles, cladding, insulation, and other building elements to substrates.

name: Paint
description: A liquid coating applied to surfaces for protection against corrosion, moisture, fire, or for aesthetic decoration.

name: Acoustic Insulation
description: A dense or fibrous material installed within partitions, floors, and ceilings to attenuate the transmission of airborne and impact sound.

name: Fire-Resistant Board
description: A specially formulated panel providing passive fire protection to structural elements, service penetrations, and partitions.

name: Grout
description: A fluid cementitious or resin-based material used to fill voids, anchor bolts, or seal joints between tiles and masonry.

name: Bitumen
description: A viscous black hydrocarbon material used as a waterproofing agent in felt membranes, damp-proof courses, and road surfaces.

name: Polystyrene
description: A lightweight expanded or extruded foam material used as thermal insulation and void former in concrete slabs and facades.

name: Aluminium
description: A lightweight, corrosion-resistant metal used for window frames, curtain wall mullions, cladding panels, and roofing systems.

name: Waterproofing
description: The application of membranes or coatings to below-ground, roof, and wet-area surfaces to prevent water penetration into the structure.

name: Formwork Installation
description: The erection of temporary mould systems of timber, steel, or proprietary panels that define the shape of a concrete pour.

name: Formwork Removal
description: The systematic stripping of temporary formwork from hardened concrete elements once the required strength has been achieved.

name: Concrete Pouring
description: The placement and compaction of fresh concrete into prepared formwork or excavations to form structural elements.

name: Curing
description: The process of maintaining adequate moisture and temperature in freshly placed concrete to ensure full hydration and strength development.

name: Finishing
description: Surface treatment operations applied to concrete, plaster, or floors to achieve the specified texture, level, and appearance.

name: Glazing
description: The installation of glass units into window frames, curtain wall systems, or skylights to complete the building envelope.

name: Painting
description: The application of primer, undercoat, and topcoat paint systems to internal and external surfaces for protection and decoration.

name: Testing and Commissioning
description: The systematic verification, adjustment, and performance testing of all building systems to confirm they operate to design intent.

name: Excavation
description: The removal of soil, rock, or fill material to reach the required founding level or to create basement and service trenches.

name: Piling
description: The installation of deep foundation elements by driving, boring, or casting into the ground to reach load-bearing strata.

name: Reinforcement Fixing
description: The cutting, bending, and tying of steel reinforcement bars into the specified arrangement prior to concrete placement.

name: Structural Steel Erection
description: The lifting, aligning, and bolting or welding of prefabricated steel sections to form the primary structural frame.

name: Masonry Construction
description: The laying of brick, block, or stone units in mortar courses to form walls, partitions, or decorative elements.

name: Roofing
description: The installation of roof structure, insulation, membrane, and weathering layers to complete the uppermost enclosure of the building.

name: Cladding Installation
description: The fixing of external facade panels, tiles, or sheets to the building structure to form the weather-resistant exterior skin.

name: Mechanical Services Installation
description: The installation of ductwork, pipework, equipment, and fittings for HVAC, plumbing, and fire systems throughout the building.

name: Electrical Services Installation
description: The routing of conduits, pulling of cables, and fixing of switchgear and accessories for the building's electrical and data systems.

name: Plastering
description: The application of wet plaster or render coats to masonry or plasterboard surfaces to produce a smooth finished wall or ceiling.

name: Tiling
description: The fixing of ceramic, porcelain, or stone tiles to floor and wall surfaces using adhesive and grout to provide a durable finish.

name: Screeding
description: The laying and levelling of a cementitious or anhydrite screed layer over a structural slab to prepare for floor finishes.

name: Insulation Installation
description: The placement or fixing of thermal or acoustic insulation materials into wall cavities, roof build-ups, and floor assemblies.

name: Damp-Proof Course Installation
description: The insertion of a horizontal impermeable barrier within masonry walls at or near ground level to prevent rising damp.

name: Dewatering
description: The pumping or drainage of groundwater from an excavation to maintain dry working conditions during substructure construction.

name: Surveying and Setting Out
description: The establishment of reference lines, levels, and grid points on site to accurately position all structural and architectural elements.

name: Backfilling
description: The replacement and compaction of fill material around completed substructure elements to restore ground levels and lateral support.

name: Jointing and Sealing
description: The application of flexible sealants or gaskets to movement joints, facade interfaces, and service penetrations to achieve weathertightness.

name: Fire Stopping Installation
description: The installation of passive fire protection materials around service penetrations and construction joints to maintain compartment integrity.

name: Lift Installation
description: The sequential installation of guide rails, car frame, drive machinery, controls, and finishing elements within the lift shaft.

name: Light On Two Sides Of Every Room
Paving With Cracks Between The Stones
Roof Deck
description: The structural base layer of the roof that spans between supports and provides the surface onto which roofing materials are applied.

name: Roof Truss
description: A prefabricated structural framework of triangulated members designed to support the roof deck and transfer loads to the walls.

name: Roof Rafter
description: An inclined structural member running from the ridge to the eave that supports the roof deck in traditional timber-framed roofs.

name: Ridge Beam
description: The horizontal structural member running along the apex of a pitched roof to which the upper ends of rafters are connected.

name: Eave
description: The lower edge of the roof that overhangs the exterior wall, directing rainwater away from the building facade.

name: Fascia Board
description: A horizontal board fixed to the ends of rafters at the eave that provides a finish surface and supports the guttering system.

name: Roof Insulation
description: Thermal and acoustic insulating material installed within or above the roof structure to reduce heat transfer and meet energy-efficiency standards.

name: Roofing Membrane
description: A continuous waterproofing layer—such as EPDM, TPO, or modified bitumen—applied to flat or low-slope roofs to prevent water ingress.

name: Roof Tiles
description: Individual interlocking or overlapping units made from clay, concrete, or slate that form the weatherproof outer skin of a pitched roof.

name: Roof Shingles
description: Overlapping rectangular cladding elements, typically asphalt, wood, or composite, laid in courses to shed water on sloped roofs.

name: Metal Roof Cladding
description: Standing-seam or corrugated metal panels—commonly steel or aluminium—used as a durable, lightweight weatherproof roof surface.

name: Roof Underlayment
description: A secondary water-resistant or vapour-control layer installed between the roof deck and the outer cladding as a redundant moisture barrier.

name: Flashing
description: Thin metal or composite strips installed at roof junctions, penetrations, and edges to prevent water infiltration at vulnerable transition points.

name: Parapet Wall
description: A low wall extending above the roof perimeter that provides edge protection, wind resistance, and an aesthetic finish on flat or low-slope roofs.

name: Skylight
description: A glazed opening integrated into the roof plane to admit natural daylight and, in operable versions, natural ventilation to the spaces below.

name: Roof Window
description: An openable window unit flush-mounted within a pitched roof slope, providing both daylighting and ventilation to loft or attic spaces.

name: Roof Hatch
description: An access panel installed in the roof that allows personnel to move between interior spaces and the roof surface for maintenance purposes.

name: Dormer
description: A structural projection from a pitched roof slope containing a vertical window, used to add headroom and light to upper-floor spaces.

name: Valley
description: The internal angle formed at the junction of two intersecting roof slopes, requiring special waterproofing treatment to manage concentrated water flow.

name: Hip
description: The external sloping ridge formed at the intersection of two adjacent roof planes meeting at an outward angle on a hipped roof.

name: Gutter
description: A channel fixed along the eave to collect rainwater runoff from the roof surface and direct it to downpipes for controlled disposal.

name: Downpipe
description: A vertical pipe connected to the gutter that conveys collected rainwater from the roof level to ground drainage systems.

name: Roof Ventilation System
description: A system of vents, ridges, and air pathways that manages airflow within the roof construction to control moisture, condensation, and thermal build-up.

name: Green Roof System
description: A layered assembly of waterproofing, drainage, growing medium, and vegetation installed on a flat or low-pitch roof to provide ecological and thermal benefits.

name: Solar Photovoltaic Roof System
description: An array of photovoltaic panels or integrated solar tiles mounted on or within the roof to generate on-site electrical energy.

name: Attic Space
description: The enclosed, often unconditioned volume between the topmost ceiling and the underside of the roof structure, used for storage or housing building services.

name: Plant Room on Roof
description: A dedicated enclosure on the roof level housing mechanical, electrical, or communications equipment serving the building.

name: Roof Construction
description: The on-site erection and assembly of the structural roof frame, decking, and primary weatherproofing layers according to design specifications.

name: Roof Waterproofing
description: The application of membranes, coatings, or specialist materials to the roof assembly to achieve a watertight envelope.

name: Roof Tiling and Cladding Installation
description: The process of fixing individual roof tiles, shingles, or metal cladding panels to the prepared roof substrate in the correct overlapping pattern.

name: Roof Insulation Installation
description: The fitting of insulating batts, boards, or spray-applied materials within or above the roof structure to achieve the required thermal performance.

name: Roof Inspection
description: A systematic examination of the roof assembly to assess condition, identify defects, and determine maintenance or repair requirements.

name: Roof Maintenance and Repair
description: Ongoing remedial and preventive works carried out on the roof surface, flashings, drainage, and structure to preserve performance and extend service life.

name: Flat Roof
description: A roof type with a near-horizontal pitch (typically 1–10°) requiring specialist waterproofing systems and internal or scupper drainage solutions.

name: Pitched Roof
description: A roof type with one or more slopes greater than 10°, shedding water by gravity to the eaves and suited to tile or shingle cladding.

name: Mansard Roof
description: A four-sided roof with a double slope on each face—a steeper lower slope and a shallower upper slope—maximising usable attic floor area.

name: Barrel Vault Roof
description: A curved roof structure forming a continuous semicircular or segmental arch profile, used for both structural expression and spatial character.

name: Load-Bearing Wall
description: A structural wall designed to carry and transfer loads from floors, roofs, or other walls down to the foundation.

name: Non-Load-Bearing Wall
description: A partition wall that supports only its own weight and is used purely for space division without structural responsibility.

name: Cavity Wall
description: A wall constructed with two separate masonry leaves separated by an air gap or insulation cavity to improve thermal and moisture performance.

name: Party Wall
description: A shared wall on a property boundary that provides structural separation and acoustic/fire division between two adjoining buildings or units.

name: Fire Wall
description: A wall with a specific fire-resistance rating built to prevent the spread of fire between building sections or occupancies.

name: Partition Wall
description: An interior non-structural wall used to subdivide floor space into rooms or functional zones.

name: Demountable Partition
description: A relocatable interior wall system assembled from prefabricated panels that can be dismantled and reconfigured without major works.

name: Masonry Wall
description: A wall constructed from individual masonry units such as bricks, blocks, or stone, bonded together with mortar.

name: Concrete Wall
description: A wall cast in-situ or as precast panels using reinforced or plain concrete for structural or enclosure purposes.

name: Timber Frame Wall
description: A wall system built from a structural timber stud framework, typically infilled or clad with sheathing and insulation.

name: Steel Frame Wall
description: A wall framed with cold-formed or hot-rolled steel studs, commonly used in commercial and industrial construction.

name: Straw Bale Wall
description: A sustainable wall construction method using compacted straw bales as the primary insulating and structural infill material.

name: Rammed Earth Wall
description: A wall formed by compacting layers of moist earth within formwork to create a dense, durable monolithic structure.

name: Insulated Concrete Form (ICF) Wall
description: A wall system where concrete is poured into stay-in-place foam insulation formwork, providing combined structural and thermal performance.

name: Structural Insulated Panel (SIP) Wall
description: A high-performance wall panel made from a rigid foam core bonded between two structural facing boards.

name: Wall Footing
description: A continuous strip foundation beneath a wall that distributes its load to the bearing soil or substructure.

name: Wall Plate
description: A horizontal timber or steel member fixed to the top of a wall to distribute roof or floor loads and anchor structural elements.

name: Wall Tie
description: A metal connector used to structurally link the two leaves of a cavity wall or bond a veneer to a backup structure.

name: Wall Insulation
description: Thermal or acoustic insulating material installed within, on, or between wall layers to improve energy performance and comfort.

name: Vapour Barrier
description: A membrane layer incorporated into a wall assembly to restrict moisture vapour diffusion and prevent interstitial condensation.

name: Wall Cladding
description: An external or internal surface layer applied to a wall for protection, weatherproofing, aesthetics, or fire resistance.

name: Wall Render / Plaster
description: A cementitious or gypsum-based coating applied to wall surfaces to provide a smooth, protective, or decorative finish.

name: Damp-Proof Course (DPC)
description: A horizontal barrier layer built into a wall at low level to prevent ground moisture from rising through the wall fabric.

name: Reinforcement Bar (Rebar)
description: Steel bars or mesh embedded in concrete or masonry walls to provide tensile strength and crack control.

name: Wall Framing
description: The construction activity of erecting the structural frame of a wall using timber or metal studs, plates, and noggins.

name: Masonry Laying
description: The trade activity of laying and bonding bricks, blocks, or stone units in courses to form a wall.

name: Wall Formwork & Concrete Pouring
description: The activity of assembling temporary molds and placing concrete to form cast-in-place concrete walls.

name: Wall Insulation Installation
description: The process of fitting insulation boards, batts, or injected fill into wall cavities or onto wall surfaces.

name: Wall Plastering / Rendering
description: The finishing activity of applying plaster or render coats to internal or external wall surfaces.

name: Wall Waterproofing
description: The application of membranes, coatings, or treatments to walls to prevent water ingress from rain or ground moisture.

name: Wall Opening Formation
description: The activity of cutting or forming openings in existing or new walls to accommodate doors, windows, or service penetrations.

name: Wall Demolition
description: The controlled breaking down or removal of an existing wall structure during renovation or deconstruction works.

name: Wall Surveying & Setting Out
description: The pre-construction activity of marking wall positions, checking plumb and alignment, and establishing reference lines on site.

name: Wall Finishing
description: All final surface treatment activities applied to a wall including painting, tiling, panelling, or wallpapering.

name: IfcWall
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcWallStandardCase
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcWall.

name: IfcCurtainWall
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: Wall Chase / Duct Space
description: A narrow void or recess within or behind a wall used to route electrical conduits, plumbing pipes, or mechanical services.

name: Shallow Foundation
description: A foundation type that transfers structural loads to near-surface soils, typically used when bearing capacity is adequate close to ground level.

name: Deep Foundation
description: A foundation type that transfers loads to deeper, more stable soil or rock layers, used when surface soils are inadequate.

name: Strip Foundation
description: A continuous linear footing that supports load-bearing walls along their entire length.

name: Pad Footing
description: An isolated, discrete footing that supports a single column or concentrated point load.

name: Raft / Mat Foundation
description: A large, continuous slab spanning the entire building footprint, distributing loads evenly across weak or variable soils.

name: Grade Beam
description: A reinforced concrete beam at ground level that connects pile caps or piers and supports the structure above.

name: Caisson / Drilled Shaft
description: A large-diameter bored and cast-in-place concrete element used to carry heavy loads to bearing stratum.

name: Spread Footing
description: A widened base beneath a column or wall that spreads the load over a larger soil area to reduce bearing pressure.

name: Combined Footing
description: A single footing that supports two or more columns, used when footings would otherwise overlap or one column is near a property boundary.

name: Cantilever / Strap Footing
description: Two isolated footings connected by a strap beam to balance eccentric loading, often used at property lines.

name: Foundation Wall
description: A below-grade wall that transfers loads from the superstructure to the footing and retains surrounding soil.

name: Basement Slab
description: A concrete slab forming the floor of a basement that also helps resist hydrostatic uplift pressure.

name: Underpinning
description: Additional support installed beneath an existing foundation to increase its depth or capacity.

name: Micropile
description: A small-diameter, high-capacity drilled and grouted pile used for underpinning, restricted access, or poor-soil conditions.

name: Helical Pier
description: A steel screw-anchor pile with helical plates that is rotated into the ground to support or lift foundations.

name: Frost Protection / Insulated Foundation
description: An insulated foundation design or element that prevents frost penetration and associated heave in cold climates.

name: Waterproofing Membrane
description: A sheet or liquid-applied membrane applied to below-grade foundation surfaces to prevent water ingress.

name: Reinforcing Steel (Rebar)
description: Steel bars embedded in concrete footings, piles, and foundation walls to resist tensile and bending forces.

name: Foundation Concrete
description: Structural concrete mixed to specification for use in footings, slabs, and below-grade walls.

name: Blinding Layer
description: A thin layer of lean concrete or compacted aggregate placed over prepared soil to provide a clean, level working surface for foundation construction.

name: Lean Concrete
description: Low-strength concrete used as a sub-base or blinding layer beneath structural foundations.

name: Drainage Layer / Granular Fill
description: Free-draining gravel or crushed stone placed around or beneath foundations to manage groundwater and reduce hydrostatic pressure.

name: Geotextile Fabric
description: A permeable fabric placed around drainage layers or retaining structures to filter soil while allowing water passage.

name: Soil Investigation / Site Survey
description: The geotechnical and topographic survey activity conducted before design to characterise soil bearing capacity and groundwater conditions.

name: Pile Driving / Installation
description: The construction activity of installing piles into the ground by driving, boring, or screwing to the required depth.

name: Concrete Pouring / Casting
description: The activity of placing and consolidating wet concrete into formwork to form footings, slabs, or foundation walls.

name: Rebar Fixing
description: The activity of cutting, bending, and tying reinforcing steel bars into position within the foundation formwork.

name: Waterproofing Application
description: The activity of applying waterproofing membranes, coatings, or drainage boards to below-grade foundation surfaces.

name: Backfilling and Compaction
description: The activity of returning excavated or imported fill material around completed foundation elements and compacting it to required density.

name: Load Testing
description: A quality-assurance activity in which piles or footings are tested under controlled loads to verify design bearing capacity.

name: Foundation Inspection
description: A formal inspection activity carried out by engineers or authorities to verify that foundation elements meet design and regulatory requirements.

name: Substructure
description: The complete below-grade structural system—comprising all foundation and below-ground elements—that supports the superstructure above.

name: Ground Drainage System
description: The network of perforated pipes, sumps, and drainage layers that manage groundwater around and beneath a building's foundations.

name: Foundation Zone / Subgrade Space
description: The below-grade volume of soil and rock directly influenced by and interacting with the building's foundation elements.

name: Crawl Space
description: A shallow, accessible void beneath a ground floor that allows inspection and maintenance of below-floor services and structure.

name: IfcFooting
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcPile
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcWall (Foundation Wall)
description: The IFC wall class as applied to below-grade foundation or basement retaining walls.

name: IfcSlab (Basement / Raft)
description: The IFC slab class as applied to raft foundations or basement floor slabs.

name: Steel Beam
description: A structural beam fabricated from steel sections, commonly used in frames and long-span structures.

name: Concrete Beam
description: A beam cast from concrete, either in-situ or precast, used to carry transverse loads in building frames.

name: Timber Beam
description: A beam made from solid or engineered wood, typical in residential and light-commercial construction.

name: Composite Beam
description: A beam combining steel and concrete acting together via shear connectors to improve structural efficiency.

name: Reinforced Concrete Beam
description: A concrete beam incorporating steel reinforcement bars to resist tensile and shear forces.

name: Pre-stressed Concrete Beam
description: A concrete beam in which internal stresses are introduced by pre- or post-tensioned tendons to counteract service loads.

name: Glulam Beam
description: An engineered timber beam made from glued laminated layers, offering high strength-to-weight ratio for large spans.

name: I-Beam
description: A steel or aluminum beam with an I-shaped cross-section optimized for bending resistance.

name: T-Beam
description: A reinforced concrete beam with a T-shaped cross-section formed integrally with a floor slab.

name: Box Beam
description: A hollow rectangular or square cross-section beam providing high torsional and bending stiffness.

name: Cantilever Beam
description: A beam fixed at one end and free at the other, used for overhangs, balconies, and canopies.

name: Transfer Beam
description: A large beam that redistributes loads from columns or walls above to supports below at a different grid.

name: Spandrel Beam
description: A perimeter beam spanning between columns at floor level, often supporting the building facade.

name: Coupling Beam
description: A short, deep beam linking adjacent shear walls to improve lateral load resistance in a structural system.

name: Tie Beam
description: A horizontal beam connecting column bases or wall footings to prevent differential settlement.

name: Lintel
description: A small beam spanning over a door or window opening to carry the load of the structure above.

name: Rafter
description: A sloped roof beam running from the ridge to the eave, supporting roof cladding and loads.

name: Purlin
description: A horizontal beam spanning between roof trusses or rafters to support roof decking or cladding.

name: Header Beam
description: A structural member placed over an opening in a load-bearing wall to transfer loads to adjacent framing.

name: Flange
description: The horizontal top or bottom plate of an I-beam or similar section that primarily resists bending stresses.

name: Web
description: The vertical plate connecting the flanges of a beam section, primarily resisting shear forces.

name: Shear Connector
description: A mechanical device (e.g., stud or channel) welded to a steel beam to ensure composite action with a concrete slab.

name: Beam Bearing Plate
description: A steel plate placed at the beam support to distribute concentrated reaction forces and prevent local crushing.

name: End Plate
description: A plate welded to the end of a beam to facilitate bolted moment or shear connections to columns or other beams.

name: Stiffener
description: A plate or angle welded to the beam web to prevent buckling under concentrated loads or at supports.

name: Beam Splice
description: A connection joining two beam segments end-to-end to achieve required lengths or facilitate transportation.

name: Beam Column Connection
description: A structural joint transferring forces and moments between a beam and a column.

name: Structural Steel
description: High-strength steel alloy used to fabricate steel beam sections and their connecting elements.

name: Prestressing Tendon
description: High-tensile steel strand or wire used to introduce pre-stress into concrete beams.

name: Ready-Mix Concrete
description: Factory-batched concrete delivered to site and used for casting in-situ beams.

name: Structural Timber
description: Graded solid wood used in the fabrication of timber beams in light-frame and heavy-timber construction.

name: Epoxy Adhesive
description: High-strength adhesive used for bonding laminated timber layers or repairing concrete beam cracks.

name: Fire Protection Coating
description: Intumescent paint or spray-applied material applied to beam surfaces to meet fire-resistance requirements.

name: Anti-corrosion Coating
description: Protective paint or galvanizing applied to steel beams to prevent corrosion in aggressive environments.

name: Beam Formwork
description: Temporary mould system used to shape and support wet concrete during the casting and curing of beams.

name: Structural Frame System
description: The overall skeletal system of columns, beams, and slabs that transfers building loads to foundations.

name: Floor System
description: An integrated assembly of beams, joists, and deck or slab elements that forms each building floor level.

name: Lateral Load Resisting System
description: The structural system including beams, walls, and braces designed to resist wind and seismic forces.

name: Beam Erection
description: The field activity of lifting and positioning steel or precast concrete beams into their final locations using cranes.

name: Beam Formwork Installation
description: The activity of assembling and fixing formwork in preparation for casting in-situ concrete beams.

name: Reinforcement Placement
description: The activity of cutting, bending, and positioning steel rebar cages within beam formwork prior to concrete pouring.

name: Concrete Curing
description: The controlled process of maintaining moisture and temperature in a cast beam to achieve design concrete strength.

name: Post-tensioning
description: The activity of stressing high-tensile tendons after concrete has hardened to introduce compressive pre-stress into the beam.

name: Beam Welding
description: The activity of joining steel beam components or connections using fusion welding processes.

name: Beam Bolting
description: The activity of fastening beam connections using high-strength structural bolts in shear or tension.

name: Beam Painting and Coating
description: The activity of applying protective or fire-resistant coatings to beam surfaces after fabrication or erection.

name: Beam Load Testing
description: A structural testing activity applying controlled loads to a beam to verify its capacity and deflection behaviour.

name: Beam Inspection
description: A quality-assurance activity involving visual and instrument-based checks of beams for defects, alignment, and code compliance.

name: Non-Destructive Testing of Beams
description: The use of ultrasonic, radiographic, or magnetic particle methods to detect internal flaws in beams without causing damage.

name: Beam Repair and Strengthening
description: Remedial works such as carbon-fibre wrapping, plate bonding, or re-casting to restore or enhance beam capacity.

name: IfcBeam
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: Column Base Plate
description: A steel plate fixed at the bottom of a column to distribute loads to the foundation below.

name: Column Capital
description: The widened top section of a column that provides a larger bearing area for beams or slabs above.

name: Column Footing
description: An isolated foundation element that transfers column loads safely into the ground.

name: Column Splice
description: A mechanical or welded connection joining two column sections end-to-end along the building height.

name: Column Tie / Lateral Tie
description: Transverse reinforcement loops that confine the concrete core and prevent buckling of longitudinal bars in RC columns.

name: Column Longitudinal Reinforcement Bar
description: Vertical steel bars embedded in a reinforced concrete column to carry axial and bending forces.

name: Column Casing / Encasement
description: A protective or decorative outer shell (concrete, steel, or architectural finish) wrapped around a structural column.

name: Column Corbel
description: A short cantilever bracket projecting from a column face to support beams or precast members.

name: Column Haunch
description: A tapered thickening at the column–beam junction that increases moment capacity and stiffness at the connection.

name: Column Anchor Bolts
description: Bolts cast into the foundation to secure a column base plate and transfer shear and uplift forces.

name: Steel Column (Wide-Flange / H-Section)
description: A hot-rolled structural steel column profile with wide flanges commonly used in steel-frame construction.

name: Hollow Structural Section (HSS) Column
description: A column made from square, rectangular, or circular hollow steel tubes offering high strength-to-weight ratio.

name: Reinforced Concrete Column
description: A cast-in-place or precast concrete column internally reinforced with steel bars to resist combined axial and lateral loads.

name: Composite Column
description: A column combining a steel section and concrete to exploit both materials' structural properties simultaneously.

name: Precast Concrete Column
description: A factory-manufactured concrete column unit transported to site and erected as a complete structural element.

name: Timber Column / Post
description: A vertical load-bearing member made from solid, glulam, or engineered timber used in wood-frame structures.

name: Slender Column
description: A column with a high slenderness ratio that requires second-order (P-delta) analysis for stability verification.

name: Short Column
description: A stocky column whose failure is governed by material strength rather than buckling behaviour.

name: Corner Column
description: A column located at the corner of a structural grid, subject to biaxial bending from two orthogonal beams.

name: Edge Column
description: A perimeter column along the building facade, often subject to eccentric loading from one-sided beam connections.

name: Interior Column
description: A column positioned within the interior structural grid, typically carrying the highest tributary loads.

name: Column Formwork
description: Temporary mould or shuttering used to shape wet concrete into the required column cross-section during casting.

name: Column Fire Protection (Intumescent / Board)
description: Passive fire-resistance material applied to a column surface to maintain structural integrity during a fire event.

name: Column Grout / Non-Shrink Grout
description: Cementitious or epoxy grout used to fill voids beneath base plates or between precast column connections.

name: Column Concrete Mix
description: The specified concrete grade and mix design used for casting reinforced or composite columns.

name: Column Rebar Cage
description: The prefabricated assembly of longitudinal bars and stirrups placed inside column formwork before concrete is poured.

name: Column Setting Out / Layout
description: The survey and marking activity that establishes precise column centreline positions on the structural grid.

name: Column Rebar Fixing
description: The on-site activity of assembling, positioning, and tying reinforcement cages within column formwork.

name: Column Concreting / Casting
description: The process of placing, compacting, and curing concrete within column formwork to form the finished element.

name: Column Formwork Erection & Striking
description: The activities of assembling column moulds before casting and removing them after concrete has gained sufficient strength.

name: Column Steel Erection
description: The crane-assisted lifting and bolting or welding of steel column sections into their final position in the frame.

name: Column Welding
description: Fusion welding operations performed on steel column splices, base plates, or beam-to-column moment connections.

name: Column Load Testing
description: Structural testing conducted on column specimens or in-situ elements to verify load-carrying capacity.

name: Column Plumbing & Alignment
description: Quality-control activity using plumb bobs or total stations to verify vertical alignment of erected columns.

name: Column Repair & Strengthening
description: Remedial works such as concrete jacketing, FRP wrapping, or steel plating to restore or upgrade column capacity.

name: Lateral Load-Resisting System
description: The structural system (moment frames, braced frames, shear walls) in which columns act as key elements to resist wind and seismic forces.

name: Gravity Frame System
description: The structural sub-system consisting of columns and beams designed primarily to carry vertical gravity loads.

name: Column Grid / Structural Grid
description: The coordinated layout of column positions that defines the modular planning and load-path organisation of the building.

name: IfcColumn
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcColumnType
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElementType.

name: Flat Slab
description: A slab without beams that transfers loads directly to columns, offering a flat soffit for simpler formwork and services routing.

name: Waffle Slab
description: A two-way ribbed slab system with a grid of beams on its underside, reducing self-weight while maintaining structural depth.

name: Hollow-Core Slab
description: A precast prestressed slab containing longitudinal voids to reduce weight and improve spanning capability.

name: Post-Tensioned Slab
description: A slab in which high-strength tendons are tensioned after concrete has cured, enabling longer spans and thinner sections.

name: Composite Slab
description: A slab formed by combining a profiled steel deck with in-situ concrete, utilising composite action for structural efficiency.

name: Ribbed Slab
description: A one-way slab with closely spaced ribs on its underside that reduce material use while maintaining flexural strength.

name: Raised Access Floor Slab
description: A structural slab designed to support a raised floor system that accommodates underfloor services and cabling.

name: Ground-Bearing Slab
description: A concrete slab cast directly on prepared subgrade, transferring loads to the ground without structural support from the building frame.

name: Suspended Slab
description: A slab supported on beams, walls, or columns above ground level, spanning across open spaces below.

name: Topping Slab
description: A thin layer of concrete cast on top of a structural slab to improve surface finish, level the floor, or add screed for services.

name: Precast Slab Panel
description: A factory-manufactured concrete slab unit delivered to site and installed as a structural floor or roof element.

name: Slab Reinforcement
description: Steel rebar or mesh embedded within a slab to resist tensile forces and control cracking under load.

name: Slab Edge Beam
description: A beam running along the perimeter of a slab to stiffen the edge, support cladding, or distribute loads to columns.

name: Slab Drop Panel
description: A localised thickening of a flat slab around a column head to increase punching shear resistance.

name: Slab Soffit
description: The exposed underside surface of a slab, which may require fire protection, acoustic treatment, or architectural finish.

name: Slab Opening / Penetration
description: An intentional void through a slab to allow passage of services, stairs, or lift shafts, requiring trimmer reinforcement.

name: Screed Layer
description: A cementitious or anhydrite layer applied to the structural slab surface to provide a smooth, level substrate for floor finishes.

name: Thermal Insulation Board
description: Rigid insulation placed above or below a slab to limit heat transfer and meet energy-performance requirements.

name: Reinforced Concrete
description: The primary structural material of most slabs, comprising Portland cement concrete with embedded steel reinforcement.

name: Profiled Metal Decking
description: Corrugated steel sheeting used as permanent formwork and tensile reinforcement in composite slab construction.

name: Post-Tensioning Tendon
description: High-strength steel strand or bar threaded through ducts in a slab and stressed after concrete has gained sufficient strength.

name: Formwork / Falsework
description: Temporary shuttering and propping system used to support wet concrete during slab casting until it achieves structural strength.

name: Underfloor Heating System
description: Pipework or electric elements embedded in or beneath a slab to deliver radiant heat to the floor surface.

name: Slab Drainage System
description: Channels, falls, and drain outlets integrated into a slab to manage surface water, particularly in car parks and plant rooms.

name: Shear Stud Connector
description: A welded steel stud on the top flange of a steel beam that mechanically connects the beam to the concrete slab for composite action.

name: Slab Formwork Striking
description: The removal of temporary formwork and propping after concrete has achieved sufficient strength to be self-supporting.

name: Post-Tensioning Stressing
description: The operation of hydraulically jacking and locking tendons in a post-tensioned slab after concrete reaches the required strength.

name: Slab Curing
description: The process of maintaining adequate moisture and temperature in freshly cast concrete to ensure complete hydration and strength gain.

name: Slab Grinding / Levelling
description: A finishing activity to remove high spots and achieve the required surface regularity (SR) or flatness (FF/FL) specification.

name: Non-Destructive Testing of Slab
description: Inspection techniques such as impulse-echo or cover-meter surveys used to verify slab thickness, rebar cover, and integrity without causing damage.

name: Precast Slab Installation
description: The crane-assisted placement and alignment of factory-made slab units onto structural supports on site.

name: Floor Zone / Structural Zone
description: The vertical depth allocated within a building storey to accommodate the structural slab, its services integration, and any suspended ceiling below.

name: IfcSlab
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: Window Frame
description: The structural border that holds the glazing and anchors the window unit within the wall opening.

name: Window Sash
description: The movable or fixed inner frame that holds the glass pane(s) and can open or tilt within the window frame.

name: Window Glazing
description: The glass or transparent panel installed within the sash, available as single, double, or triple pane for varying insulation levels.

name: Window Sill
description: The horizontal ledge at the bottom of a window opening, both interior and exterior, that provides support and weather protection.

name: Window Head
description: The horizontal structural member at the top of a window opening that carries loads from above and seals the upper edge.

name: Window Jamb
description: The vertical side members of the window frame that form the left and right edges of the window opening.

name: Window Mullion
description: A vertical dividing bar between multiple window panes or adjacent window units within a shared frame.

name: Window Transom
description: A horizontal dividing bar that separates a window into upper and lower sections, often above a door or larger glazed area.

name: Window Glazing Seal
description: The weatherproof gasket or sealant material applied around the glass perimeter to prevent air and water infiltration.

name: Window Hardware
description: Operational fittings such as hinges, handles, locks, and stays that enable opening, closing, and securing of the window.

name: Window Locking Mechanism
description: The security device integrated into or attached to the sash and frame to lock the window in a closed position.

name: Window Hinge
description: The pivot fitting that attaches the opening sash to the frame, allowing controlled rotation or swing of the window leaf.

name: Window Flashing
description: Thin waterproof material installed around the window perimeter at the wall interface to direct water away and prevent moisture ingress.

name: Window Trim / Casing
description: Decorative and functional moulding applied around the interior or exterior window opening to cover the joint between frame and wall finish.

name: Window Screen
description: A mesh panel fitted over the window opening to allow ventilation while preventing insects and debris from entering.

name: Window Blind / Shade
description: An internal or between-glass shading device that controls light, privacy, and solar heat gain for the window.

name: Window Shutter
description: Solid or louvred panels mounted beside or over a window to provide security, weather protection, and light control.

name: Bay Window
description: A multi-panel window assembly that projects outward from the main wall plane, creating a recessed interior space.

name: Curtain Wall Window Unit
description: A glazed panel integrated into a non-load-bearing curtain wall facade system, combining structural, thermal, and aesthetic functions.

name: Double-Hung Window
description: A window type with two vertically sliding sashes that can both move up and down independently within the frame.

name: Casement Window
description: A window with a sash hinged on one vertical side that swings outward or inward like a door for ventilation.

name: Awning Window
description: A top-hinged window sash that opens outward from the bottom, allowing ventilation even during light rain.

name: Fixed / Picture Window
description: A non-operable window with a sealed glazed panel providing unobstructed views and maximised daylight without ventilation capability.

name: Sliding Window
description: A window with one or more sashes that glide horizontally along tracks within the frame to open and close.

name: Louvre Window
description: A window composed of angled horizontal glass or aluminium slats that tilt to control ventilation and light.

name: Window Insulation / Draught Sealing
description: Weather-stripping or foam tape applied to moving sash joints to minimise air leakage and improve thermal performance.

name: Window Condensation Drainage System
description: Channels, weep holes, and drainage paths built into the frame to manage and expel condensation water.

name: Window Installation
description: The construction activity of fitting, aligning, securing, and sealing a window unit into a prepared wall or roof opening.

name: Window Glazing Replacement
description: The maintenance activity of removing broken or inefficient glass panes and installing new glazing within an existing sash or frame.

name: Window Frame Painting / Finishing
description: The finishing activity of applying paint, stain, or protective coating to timber, steel, or aluminium window frames.

name: Window Waterproofing / Flashing Installation
description: The construction activity of applying flashing tape or sheet metal around the window rough opening to ensure weather-tight integration with the wall.

name: Window Removal / Demolition
description: The activity of safely extracting an existing window unit from its opening during renovation or building alteration works.

name: Window U-Value / Thermal Rating
description: The measured thermal transmittance performance classification of a window assembly used for energy compliance and specification.

name: IfcWindow
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcWindowType
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElementType.

name: IfcWindowStandardCase
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcWindow.

name: Door Frame
description: The structural border surrounding a door opening that supports the door and anchors it to the wall.

name: Door Leaf
description: The movable panel that swings, slides, or folds to open or close a door opening.

name: Door Sill
description: The horizontal bottom member of a door frame that sits at floor level and provides weather sealing.

name: Door Threshold
description: A transitional strip fixed at the base of a doorway to bridge flooring levels and seal the gap under the door leaf.

name: Door Jamb
description: The vertical side members of a door frame against which the door leaf closes.

name: Door Head
description: The horizontal top member of a door frame spanning across the full width of the opening.

name: Door Stop
description: A narrow strip fixed to the door frame against which the door leaf rests when closed.

name: Door Hinge
description: A pivoting hardware fitting that attaches the door leaf to the frame and allows rotational movement.

name: Door Handle
description: A hand-operated fitting mounted on the door leaf used to operate the latch or lock mechanism.

name: Door Knob
description: A round rotating handle variant used to retract a latch bolt and open the door.

name: Door Lever
description: A horizontal bar-style handle that is pushed down to retract the latch bolt and open the door.

name: Door Lock
description: A security device integrated into or mounted on a door to restrict unauthorized access.

name: Door Latch
description: A spring-loaded bolt mechanism that holds a door closed without requiring a key.

name: Deadbolt
description: A key-operated or thumb-turn lock bolt that slides directly into the strike plate without a spring mechanism.

name: Door Strike Plate
description: A metal plate mortised into the door jamb that receives and retains the latch or deadbolt when the door is closed.

name: Door Closer
description: A mechanical or hydraulic device that automatically returns a door to its closed position after opening.

name: Door Viewer (Peephole)
description: A small wide-angle lens fitted through a door leaf allowing occupants to see outside without opening the door.

name: Door Chain / Security Chain
description: A sliding chain restraint that allows a door to be opened slightly while preventing full entry.

name: Door Weatherstripping
description: Flexible sealing material applied around door edges to prevent air, water, dust, and noise infiltration.

name: Door Sweep
description: A strip attached to the bottom of the door leaf that seals the gap between the leaf and the floor or threshold.

name: Door Glazing / Vision Panel
description: A glass or translucent insert within a door leaf that provides visibility and borrowed light.

name: Door Panel
description: A recessed or raised infill section within a framed door leaf that adds rigidity and aesthetic detail.

name: Door Transom
description: A horizontal bar or fixed glazed panel situated directly above a door opening within the same frame assembly.

name: Door Sidelight
description: A narrow fixed or operable glazed panel positioned beside a door within the surrounding wall opening.

name: Sliding Door
description: A door variant in which the leaf slides horizontally along a track rather than swinging on hinges.

name: Folding / Bi-fold Door
description: A door variant consisting of panels that fold against each other along a track to open a wide aperture.

name: Revolving Door
description: A door type with multiple leaves arranged around a central pivot that rotate to allow continuous pedestrian flow.

name: Automatic Door
description: A powered door system that opens and closes automatically via motion sensors, push buttons, or access control triggers.

name: Fire Door
description: A fire-rated door assembly designed to compartmentalize fire and smoke spread for a specified duration.

name: Flush Door
description: A door leaf with a smooth, flat surface formed by thin facing sheets over an internal core.

name: Panelled Door
description: A traditional door leaf constructed with a timber frame and recessed or raised infill panels.

name: Louvred Door
description: A door leaf incorporating angled slats that allow ventilation while maintaining visual privacy.

name: Dutch Door
description: A door divided horizontally so that the upper and lower halves can be opened independently.

name: Garage Door
description: A large door variant that provides vehicle access to a garage, typically sectional, roller, or up-and-over in operation.

name: Access Control System
description: An electronic system (card reader, keypad, biometric) integrated with a door to manage and log entry permissions.

name: Door Intercom / Video Doorbell
description: A communication device at the door entry point enabling two-way audio or video between visitor and occupant.

name: Door Installation
description: The construction activity of fitting and securing a complete door assembly into a prepared opening.

name: Door Frame Installation
description: The activity of fixing and aligning the door frame within the structural opening before hanging the door leaf.

name: Door Hardware Fitting
description: The activity of mounting handles, locks, hinges, closers, and other ironmongery to a door assembly.

name: Door Painting / Finishing
description: The surface treatment activity of applying paint, stain, varnish, or other finishes to a door leaf and frame.

name: Door Replacement
description: The maintenance activity of removing an existing door assembly and installing a new one in its place.

name: Door Fire Rating Inspection
description: A compliance activity to verify that a fire door assembly meets required integrity and insulation performance standards.

name: Timber (Door Grade)
description: Solid or engineered wood used as the primary structural and aesthetic material for door leaves and frames.

name: Steel (Door Grade)
description: Cold-rolled or galvanised steel used for security, fire-rated, and industrial door leaves and frames.

name: Aluminium (Door Grade)
description: Extruded aluminium profiles used for lightweight, corrosion-resistant door frames and glazed door systems.

name: uPVC (Door Grade)
description: Unplasticised polyvinyl chloride used for thermally efficient, low-maintenance external door frames and leaves.

name: Glass (Door Grade)
description: Toughened, laminated, or insulated glass units used for fully or partially glazed door leaves and panels.

name: IfcDoor
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcDoorType
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElementType.

name: IfcDoorLiningProperties
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet.

name: IfcDoorPanelProperties
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet.

name: Mullion
description: Vertical structural member that divides and supports the curtain wall panels between floors or across bays.

name: Transom
description: Horizontal structural member that spans between mullions to provide lateral support and divide the curtain wall into panel rows.

name: Spandrel Panel
description: Opaque panel used to conceal floor slabs, columns, and mechanical systems between vision glass zones.

name: Vision Glass Panel
description: Transparent or translucent glazing unit installed at eye level to allow daylight and views to the exterior.

name: Pressure Plate
description: Metal clamping plate that mechanically secures the glass or infill panel to the mullion frame.

name: Capping Strip
description: Decorative and weatherproofing cover strip snapped over the pressure plate to finish the exposed face of the mullion.

name: Anchor Bracket
description: Structural steel or aluminium bracket that attaches the curtain wall frame to the building's primary structure, accommodating tolerance and movement.

name: Dead Load Bracket
description: Primary support bracket that carries the full gravity (dead) load of the curtain wall back to the building structure.

name: Wind Load Bracket
description: Restraint bracket designed to transfer lateral wind pressure and suction forces from the curtain wall to the primary structure.

name: Stick Curtain Wall System
description: Assembly method where individual mullions and transoms are erected piece-by-piece on site and glazing is inserted in place.

name: Unitised Curtain Wall System
description: Factory-assembled panel units, typically one-storey tall, that are hoisted and interlocked on site for rapid installation.

name: Semi-Unitised Curtain Wall System
description: Hybrid system combining pre-assembled mullion ladders or sub-frames installed on site with field-glazed infill panels.

name: Structural Silicone Glazing (SSG) System
description: Frameless-appearance curtain wall system where glass panels are bonded to the frame with structural silicone adhesive rather than mechanical pressure plates.

name: Double-Skin Façade System
description: Two parallel glazed layers with a ventilated cavity between them, improving thermal and acoustic performance compared to a single-skin curtain wall.

name: Point-Fixed Glazing System
description: Glazing system where panels are supported at discrete patch fittings or spider connectors rather than a continuous perimeter frame.

name: Rainscreen Cavity
description: Vented air gap behind the outer skin of the curtain wall that manages water infiltration and allows pressure equalisation.

name: Inter-Skin Cavity
description: Enclosed or ventilated void between the two skins of a double-skin façade used for solar shading, maintenance access, or acoustic buffering.

name: Aluminium Extrusion (Curtain Wall)
description: Custom-profiled aluminium alloy sections that form the mullion, transom, and capping components of the curtain wall frame.

name: Structural Silicone Sealant
description: High-performance silicone adhesive used to bond glass panels to frames and provide a watertight, flexible joint in SSG systems.

name: EPDM Gasket
description: Extruded ethylene propylene diene monomer rubber gasket that provides a continuous weathertight and airtight seal between the glass and the frame.

name: Insulated Glass Unit (IGU)
description: Factory-sealed double or triple glazing assembly with hermetically sealed air or gas-filled cavities for thermal and acoustic performance.

name: Backer Rod
description: Compressible foam rod inserted into joints before sealant application to control joint depth and improve sealant performance.

name: Thermal Break
description: Low-conductivity polyamide or polyurethane insert within the aluminium frame profile that interrupts the thermal bridge between inner and outer metal faces.

name: Fire Safing Insulation
description: Mineral wool or intumescent material installed at slab-edge perimeter to prevent flame and smoke passage through the gap between the curtain wall and floor structure.

name: Curtain Wall Installation
description: On-site erection, alignment, and fixing of curtain wall frames and infill panels to the building structure.

name: Anchor Bracket Installation
description: Surveying, drilling, and fixing of structural anchor brackets to the slab or column prior to curtain wall frame installation.

name: Glazing Installation
description: Lifting, positioning, and securing of glass or opaque infill panels into the curtain wall frame openings.

name: Sealant Application
description: Application of structural or weatherseal silicone sealants to joints to achieve air, water, and fire performance requirements.

name: Curtain Wall Mock-Up Testing
description: Full-scale laboratory or on-site testing of an assembled curtain wall prototype for air, water, structural, and thermal performance prior to mass installation.

name: Curtain Wall Commissioning & Inspection
description: Post-installation checking, water-hose testing, and sign-off of the completed curtain wall to verify watertightness, alignment, and compliance.

name: Facade Cleaning & Maintenance
description: Periodic cleaning, sealant inspection, gasket replacement, and remediation works to maintain the curtain wall throughout its service life.

name: Rainscreen Cladding Panel
description: An outer panel system that creates a drained and ventilated cavity between the panel and the wall substrate to manage moisture.

name: Curtain Wall System
description: A non-load-bearing exterior wall system typically made of lightweight aluminium framing and glass panels hung from the building structure.

name: Ventilated Facade
description: A multi-layer facade system incorporating an air gap that allows moisture to escape and improves thermal performance.

name: Cladding Substrate / Sheathing Board
description: The structural backing layer fixed to the building frame onto which cladding panels or tiles are mounted.

name: Cladding Bracket / Fixing Anchor
description: Metal mechanical connectors that attach cladding panels or rails securely to the primary building structure.

name: Cladding Rail / Carrier System
description: Horizontal or vertical aluminium or steel rails that provide an intermediate fixing point between anchors and cladding panels.

name: Insulation Layer (Cladding)
description: A layer of thermal or acoustic insulation material installed behind the cladding panel to improve the building envelope's energy performance.

name: Weatherproof Membrane / Breather Membrane
description: A water-resistant but vapour-permeable sheet applied behind the cladding to prevent moisture ingress while allowing water vapour to escape.

name: Metal Cladding Panel
description: Factory-formed panels of aluminium, steel, zinc, or copper used as the outer face of a building's exterior envelope.

name: Composite Cladding Panel (ACM)
description: Aluminium composite material panels consisting of two thin aluminium sheets bonded to a polyethylene or mineral core, used as a lightweight facade finish.

name: Fibre Cement Cladding Board
description: Durable flat or profiled boards made from cement reinforced with cellulose fibres, suitable for exterior wall cladding.

name: Timber Cladding Board
description: Natural or engineered wood boards fixed horizontally, vertically, or diagonally to create an exterior timber-faced wall finish.

name: Stone / Natural Stone Cladding Panel
description: Thin-cut panels of granite, limestone, sandstone, or marble mechanically fixed or adhesively bonded to form a premium exterior facade finish.

name: Terracotta Cladding Panel
description: Extruded or pressed fired-clay panels used as a durable, colourful, and low-maintenance rainscreen facade element.

name: High-Pressure Laminate (HPL) Cladding Panel
description: Resin-impregnated multi-layer paper panels compressed under high pressure to produce a hard-wearing, decorative exterior cladding board.

name: Glass Reinforced Concrete (GRC) Panel
description: Lightweight precast concrete panels reinforced with alkali-resistant glass fibres, used for architectural facade cladding.

name: Brick Slip / Thin Brick Cladding
description: Thin slices of fired clay brick bonded or mechanically fixed to a substrate to replicate the appearance of traditional brickwork on a lightweight facade.

name: Profiled Metal Sheet Cladding
description: Corrugated or trapezoidal steel or aluminium sheets primarily used on industrial and commercial buildings as a cost-effective wall covering.

name: Photovoltaic (BIPV) Cladding Panel
description: Building-integrated photovoltaic panels that function simultaneously as exterior cladding and electricity-generating elements.

name: Joint Sealant / Cladding Gasket
description: Flexible sealant or pre-formed EPDM/silicone gasket used to seal the joints between adjacent cladding panels against wind and water penetration.

name: Cavity Closer / Fire Barrier (Cladding Cavity)
description: Non-combustible mineral-wool or intumescent barriers installed within the cladding cavity at floor lines and openings to restrict fire and smoke spread.

name: Parapet Coping / Cladding Termination Detail
description: A capping unit at the top of a clad wall that protects the cladding edge, substrate, and insulation from water ingress.

name: Reveal / Return Cladding Panel
description: Cladding panels wrapped around window or door openings to provide a finished reveal and maintain continuity of the facade system.

name: Cladding Inspection & Testing
description: Quality assurance checks—including pull-out tests, water penetration tests, and fire classification verification—performed on the installed cladding system.

name: Cladding Maintenance & Cleaning
description: Periodic inspection, re-sealing, panel replacement, and cleaning activities required to sustain cladding performance and appearance throughout its service life.

name: Cladding Removal / Recladding
description: The planned or remedial dismantling and replacement of an existing cladding system, often driven by fire-safety, weather-tightness, or energy-upgrade requirements.

name: Facade Engineering / Cladding Design
description: The specialist engineering design process that determines structural fixings, thermal performance, wind loading, fire strategy, and movement joints for a cladding system.

name: Exterior Wall Facade Zone
description: The external building zone encompassing all layers from the structural wall face outward to the finished cladding surface, used for coordination and clash detection.

name: IfcCovering
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcBuildingElementProxy
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: Coping Stone
description: A protective cap unit placed on top of the parapet to shed water and prevent moisture ingress into the wall below.

name: Coping Mortar Bed
description: A mortar layer used to bed and fix coping stones or coping units onto the top of the parapet.

name: Parapet Wall Core
description: The primary structural masonry, concrete, or framed body forming the main thickness and height of the parapet.

name: Parapet Flashing
description: A waterproof metal or membrane strip installed at the junction between the parapet and the roof to prevent water penetration.

name: Through-Wall Flashing
description: A continuous waterproofing layer embedded within the parapet wall to redirect moisture that has penetrated toward the exterior face.

name: Parapet Waterproofing Membrane
description: A flexible or rigid membrane applied to parapet surfaces to provide a continuous water-resistant barrier.

name: Parapet Cavity
description: An air gap within a cavity-wall parapet designed to interrupt moisture transfer between the outer and inner leaves.

name: Parapet Cavity Closer
description: An insulated or solid unit installed at the top of a cavity parapet to close and weatherproof the cavity opening.

name: Parapet Insulation
description: Thermal insulation incorporated into or onto the parapet to reduce cold bridging at the roof-wall junction.

name: Sealant Joint
description: A flexible sealant compound used to fill and weatherproof movement or construction joints within the parapet assembly.

name: Parapet Tie Bar / Wall Anchor
description: A metal tie or anchor rod connecting the parapet to the main building structure to resist lateral wind loads.

name: Parapet Reinforcement
description: Steel reinforcing bars embedded in a concrete or masonry parapet to provide tensile strength and resist overturning forces.

name: Parapet Capping (Metal)
description: A continuous metal capping profile (e.g., aluminium or GRP) fixed to the parapet top as an alternative to stone or concrete coping.
