name: Rendered Parapet Finish
description: A sand-cement or proprietary render coat applied to external parapet faces for weather protection and aesthetics.

name: Brick Parapet
description: A parapet variant constructed entirely of brickwork, requiring specific bonding, damp-proof courses, and coping detailing.

name: Precast Concrete Parapet
description: A factory-manufactured concrete parapet unit lifted and fixed in place, often used in bridge or multi-storey construction.

name: Balustrade Parapet
description: A parapet variant incorporating a series of balusters and a handrail, providing fall protection on accessible roofs or terraces.

name: Parapet Gutter
description: A concealed or open gutter formed between the parapet and the roof slope to collect and channel rainwater to outlets.

name: Parapet Rainwater Outlet / Scupper
description: A drainage opening or scupper built through the base of the parapet to discharge accumulated roof water.

name: Roof-to-Parapet Junction Detail
description: The critical built assembly where the roof membrane or covering meets and turns up against the parapet, requiring specific waterproofing upstand detailing.

name: Damp-Proof Course (DPC) at Parapet
description: A horizontal moisture barrier installed at the base of the parapet to prevent rising damp from migrating into the building fabric below.

name: Parapet Construction
description: The on-site activity of building the parapet structure, including setting out, masonry or forming work, and integration with adjacent construction.

name: Parapet Waterproofing Application
description: The trade activity of applying flashings, membranes, and sealants to make the parapet assembly weathertight.

name: Coping Installation
description: The activity of bedding, fixing, and jointing coping units on top of a completed parapet wall.

name: Parapet Inspection & Maintenance
description: Periodic examination and repair of parapet components to identify cracking, failed flashings, or water ingress issues.

name: Parapet Repair / Repointing
description: The remedial activity of raking out and replacing deteriorated mortar joints in a masonry parapet.

name: IfcWall (Parapet)
description: The IFC schema class used to model a parapet as a vertical building element with the predefined type PARAPET in OpenBIM environments.

name: IfcCovering (Coping)
description: The IFC class used to represent coping or capping elements placed on top of a parapet wall in a BIM model.

name: IfcRailing (Parapet Balustrade)
description: The IFC class applied when a parapet incorporates a handrail or balustrade system providing fall protection.

name: Stair Tread
description: The horizontal surface of each step that users walk on when ascending or descending the staircase.

name: Stair Riser
description: The vertical face between two consecutive treads that defines the step height.

name: Stringer
description: The structural side beam that supports the treads and risers along the length of the staircase.

name: Handrail
description: The graspable rail running alongside the staircase that provides support and safety for users.

name: Baluster
description: Vertical spindle or post that supports the handrail and forms the infill of the balustrade.

name: Newel Post
description: The main structural post at the top, bottom, or landing of a staircase that anchors the handrail and balustrade.

name: Landing
description: A flat platform between flights of stairs that provides a rest point and directional change area.

name: Balustrade
description: The complete railing assembly comprising balusters, handrail, and newel posts that guards open sides of the staircase.

name: Nosing
description: The projecting edge of a stair tread that overhangs the riser and is often reinforced or highlighted for safety.

name: Winder Step
description: A tapered step used in curved or space-saving staircases to change direction without a full landing.

name: Spiral Staircase
description: A staircase variant where steps wind around a central column in a helical form, minimising floor area.

name: Straight-Flight Staircase
description: A staircase variant consisting of a single uninterrupted flight with no directional changes.

name: Quarter-Turn Staircase
description: A staircase variant that changes direction by 90 degrees, typically via a landing or winders.

name: Half-Turn (Dog-Leg) Staircase
description: A staircase variant with two parallel flights connected by a 180-degree landing or winders.

name: Cantilevered Staircase
description: A staircase variant where treads are fixed to a wall or spine beam with no visible supporting stringer on one or both sides.

name: Staircase Enclosure / Stairwell
description: The shaft or enclosed vertical space within a building that contains and surrounds the staircase.

name: Stair Reinforced Concrete Structure
description: The cast or precast concrete structural system that forms the loadbearing body of a concrete staircase.

name: Steel Stair Structure
description: A fabricated structural steel framework used as the primary load-bearing system for metal staircases.

name: Stone / Marble
description: Natural stone or marble used for treads and landings, valued for durability and aesthetic quality.

name: Non-Slip Tread Insert
description: A rubber, metal, or abrasive insert embedded in or applied to the nosing/tread to reduce slip hazard.

name: Staircase Installation
description: The construction activity of assembling and fixing all staircase components in their final position on site.

name: Formwork for Stairs
description: The temporary mould construction activity required to cast in-situ concrete stair flights and landings.

name: Steel Stair Fabrication
description: Off-site workshop activity of cutting, welding, and assembling steel stair components before site delivery.

name: Balustrade Installation
description: The activity of fixing balusters, newel posts, and handrails to form the complete guard railing system.

name: Stair Finishing & Treading
description: The activity of applying final surface finishes, nosings, or cladding to treads, risers, and stringers.

name: Fire-Rating & Compartmentation Works
description: The activity of applying fire-resistant materials and sealing to the stairwell enclosure to meet fire escape regulations.

name: Staircase Inspection & Compliance Check
description: A formal review activity verifying that the staircase meets building regulations for rise, going, headroom, and balustrade height.

name: IfcStair
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcStairFlight
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcRailing
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcSlab (Landing)
description: The IFC schema class used to model a stair landing as a horizontal slab element within the building model.

name: Ramp Slab
description: The inclined structural slab forming the walking or driving surface of the ramp.

name: Ramp Handrail
description: A graspable rail mounted along the side of the ramp to provide support and safety for users.

name: Ramp Guardrail
description: A protective barrier along the open edges of a ramp to prevent falls.

name: Ramp Landing
description: A level platform at the top, bottom, or intermediate point of a ramp run that provides a rest area and transition zone.

name: Ramp Curb
description: A raised edge element along the sides of a ramp that prevents wheels or feet from slipping off the edge.

name: Ramp Nosing
description: A non-slip edge treatment applied at the top and bottom transitions of a ramp to improve traction and visibility.

name: Ramp Surface Finish
description: The anti-slip surface material or coating applied to the ramp deck to enhance grip and safety.

name: Ramp Structural Support
description: The underlying beams, columns, or walls that bear and transfer the loads of the ramp slab to the foundation.

name: Ramp Foundation
description: The below-grade footing or base structure that anchors and supports the ramp construction.

name: Ramp Drainage System
description: The gutters, drains, and channels integrated into or beside the ramp to remove rainwater and prevent surface pooling.

name: Ramp Lighting System
description: Dedicated lighting fixtures and controls installed along the ramp to ensure safe visibility at all times.

name: Tactile Warning Strip
description: A textured ground surface indicator placed at the top and bottom of a ramp to alert visually impaired users of the level change.

name: Wheelchair Ramp
description: An accessibility-compliant inclined surface specifically designed to accommodate wheelchairs and mobility devices.

name: Vehicle Ramp
description: A heavy-duty inclined surface engineered to support vehicular traffic, such as in parking structures or loading docks.

name: Helical Ramp
description: A spiral or curved ramp variant that continuously winds around a central axis, commonly found in multi-storey car parks.

name: Switchback Ramp
description: A ramp configuration that reverses direction at landings to achieve height gain within a compact footprint.

name: Ramp Waterproofing Membrane
description: A waterproof layer applied beneath the ramp surface to protect the structural slab from moisture penetration.

name: Ramp Concrete
description: The structural concrete mix used to cast the ramp slab and supporting elements.

name: Ramp Steel Reinforcement
description: Rebar or mesh embedded within the ramp slab to provide tensile strength and crack resistance.

name: Ramp Formwork
description: Temporary moulding framework used to shape and support fresh concrete during the casting of the ramp slab.

name: Ramp Construction
description: The overall process of building a ramp, including excavation, formwork, concrete pouring, and finishing.

name: Ramp Formwork Installation
description: The activity of setting up and securing temporary formwork to define the shape of the ramp before concrete is cast.

name: Ramp Concrete Pouring
description: The activity of placing and consolidating concrete into the prepared ramp formwork to form the structural slab.

name: Ramp Surface Treatment
description: The application of anti-slip coatings, textures, or finishes to the ramp surface after curing.

name: Ramp Handrail Installation
description: The activity of fixing handrail posts and rails to the ramp structure in compliance with safety regulations.

name: Ramp Inspection
description: A formal assessment of the completed ramp to verify compliance with structural, accessibility, and safety standards.

name: Ramp Maintenance
description: Ongoing upkeep activities such as resurfacing, cleaning, and checking structural integrity to keep the ramp safe and functional.

name: IfcRamp
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcRampFlight
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcRampFlightType
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElementType.

name: Shaft Enclosure Wall
description: The structural walls forming the vertical enclosure of the lift shaft, typically constructed from reinforced concrete or masonry.

name: Shaft Pit
description: The below-ground-level recess at the base of the shaft that accommodates the buffer, tension equipment, and overtravel clearance.

name: Shaft Headroom
description: The overhead clearance space above the highest landing that allows safe travel and maintenance of the lift car and machinery.

name: Lift Car
description: The enclosed passenger or goods cabin that travels vertically within the shaft along guide rails.

name: Counterweight
description: A weighted assembly connected to the lift car via ropes or belt to balance the car load and reduce motor effort.

name: Guide Rails
description: Vertical steel T-section or hollow-section tracks fixed to the shaft walls that guide the car and counterweight travel.

name: Guide Rail Brackets
description: Structural steel brackets anchored to the shaft walls at regular intervals to support and align the guide rails.

name: Buffer Assembly
description: Energy-absorbing spring or hydraulic devices installed in the pit to cushion the car or counterweight in the event of overtravel.

name: Traction Drive System
description: The electric motor, gearbox (or gearless unit), and sheave assembly that drives the hoisting ropes to move the car.

name: Hydraulic Drive System
description: A pump, cylinder, and fluid-power circuit that raises and lowers the lift car using pressurised hydraulic fluid.

name: Hoisting Ropes / Belts
description: Steel wire ropes or flat coated-steel belts connecting the car to the counterweight over the drive sheave.

name: Shaft Door (Landing Door)
description: Fire-rated sliding or swing doors at each floor landing that seal the shaft opening and interlock with the car door.

name: Landing Door Frame
description: The structural surround fixed to the shaft wall opening that supports and aligns each landing door leaf and sill.

name: Safety Gear (Car Safety Device)
description: Mechanical clamps mounted on the car frame that grip the guide rails to arrest the car if overspeed or rope failure is detected.

name: Speed Governor
description: A centrifugal overspeed sensing device connected by a governor rope to trigger the car safety gear when rated speed is exceeded.

name: Control Panel / Controller
description: The electronic or relay-logic panel that manages call registration, dispatch logic, door operation, and safety monitoring.

name: Shaft Lighting System
description: Permanent electric lighting installed within the shaft enclosure to meet code-required illuminance for maintenance access.

name: Shaft Ventilation System
description: Natural or mechanical ventilation provision within the shaft to manage heat, fumes, and smoke in normal and emergency conditions.

name: Shaft Ladder / Access Ladder
description: A fixed vertical ladder inside the shaft providing maintenance personnel with safe access from the pit to other shaft levels.

name: Compensation Ropes / Chains
description: Ropes or link chains hanging beneath the car and counterweight to compensate for the changing weight of hoisting ropes in tall installations.

name: Travelling Cable (Trailing Cable)
description: A flexible multi-core electrical cable that moves with the lift car to supply power, lighting, communications, and control signals.

name: Car Frame (Sling)
description: The structural steel framework that encases or supports the lift car body and carries the guide shoes, safety gear, and suspension elements.

name: Car Suspension (Sheave Arrangement)
description: The arrangement of sheaves and rope terminations that defines the roping ratio (1:1, 2:1, etc.) and load distribution on the drive system.

name: Shaft Waterproofing Membrane
description: Waterproof barrier applied to below-grade shaft walls and pit floor to prevent groundwater ingress.

name: Reinforced Concrete Shaft Construction
description: The formwork, reinforcement placing, and concrete pouring operations used to construct the structural shaft enclosure walls and pit.

name: Guide Rail Installation
description: The surveying, bracket fixing, and alignment activity of erecting and plumbing guide rails within the completed shaft.

name: Lift Equipment Installation
description: The mechanical and electrical installation of the drive machinery, car, counterweight, doors, and associated lift equipment.

name: Shaft Fire Rating / Compartmentation
description: Fire-resistance-rated construction and intumescent sealing of penetrations that maintains the shaft as a protected fire compartment.

name: Lift Commissioning and Testing
description: Statutory and manufacturer testing, load trials, speed checks, and safety device verification carried out before the lift is handed over for use.

name: Pit Drainage System
description: A sump, pump, or drain channel installed in the shaft pit to remove water ingress or condensation and keep the pit dry.

name: Machine-Room-Less (MRL) Lift Variant
description: A lift configuration where the drive machinery and controller are integrated within the shaft or at the top landing, eliminating a separate machine room.

name: Panoramic / Glass Lift Variant
description: A lift variant with glazed shaft walls and car enclosure designed for aesthetic visibility, typically in atriums or retail environments.

name: Goods Lift Variant
description: A heavier-duty lift variant with reinforced car structure, larger capacity, and robust door systems designed for freight and goods transport.

name: Accessibility (Disabled) Lift Variant
description: A low-rise platform or step-lift variant complying with accessibility standards for users with mobility impairments where a full shaft is impractical.

name: Footing / Base Slab
description: The structural foundation element at the base of the retaining wall that distributes loads to the underlying soil.

name: Stem Wall
description: The vertical wall element that resists lateral earth pressure and connects the footing to the top of the structure.

name: Heel
description: The rear extension of the footing slab that extends under the retained soil to provide overturning resistance.

name: Toe
description: The front extension of the footing slab projecting toward the open face to improve sliding and overturning stability.

name: Shear Key
description: A downward projection cast into the base footing to increase resistance against sliding failure.

name: Weep Holes
description: Small drainage openings through the wall face that relieve hydrostatic pressure behind the wall.

name: Drainage Pipe / Perforated Pipe
description: A perforated pipe placed at the base of the backfill to collect and redirect groundwater away from the wall.

name: Granular Drainage Layer / Filter Blanket
description: A layer of coarse granular material placed directly behind the wall to facilitate drainage of retained soil.

name: Geotextile Filter Fabric
description: A permeable fabric placed between the drainage layer and native soil to prevent fine particles from clogging drainage media.

name: Tie-Back Anchor / Ground Anchor
description: A tensioned rod or cable grouted into stable soil or rock behind the wall to resist lateral earth forces.

name: Deadman Anchor
description: A buried anchor plate or block connected to the wall by tie rods to provide lateral stability in anchored wall systems.

name: Reinforcement Bars (Rebar)
description: Steel bars embedded in concrete elements to provide tensile strength to the wall stem and footing.

name: Geogrid Reinforcement
description: Polymer grid layers interspersed within compacted backfill in mechanically stabilized earth walls to reinforce the retained soil mass.

name: Concrete (Cast-in-Place)
description: Portland cement concrete poured in formwork on-site to form gravity or cantilever retaining wall structures.

name: Precast Concrete Panels
description: Factory-manufactured concrete panels used as facing elements or full wall units in segmental and MSE wall systems.

name: Masonry Units / Concrete Blocks
description: Interlocking or mortared block units used to construct segmental retaining walls.

name: Shotcrete / Gunite Facing
description: Pneumatically applied concrete used as a facing layer for soil nail or rock-cut retaining systems.

name: Cantilever Retaining Wall
description: A reinforced concrete wall variant that uses the weight of backfill on its footing heel to resist overturning.

name: Gravity Retaining Wall
description: A wall variant that relies solely on its own mass to resist lateral earth pressure without significant reinforcement.

name: Sheet Pile Wall
description: A wall formed by driving interlocking steel, timber, or vinyl sheets into the ground to retain soil or water.

name: Soldier Pile and Lagging Wall
description: A wall system using vertical steel piles with horizontal timber or concrete lagging boards to retain soil in excavations.

name: Mechanically Stabilized Earth (MSE) Wall
description: A composite wall system combining compacted granular backfill reinforced with geogrids or metal strips and a segmental or panel face.

name: Soil Nail Wall
description: An in-situ wall system where closely spaced grouted steel bars (nails) reinforce existing soil, typically with a shotcrete face.

name: Gabion Wall
description: A gravity wall variant built from wire mesh baskets filled with rock or rubble to retain earth.

name: Crib Wall
description: A gravity wall constructed from interlocking precast concrete or timber cells filled with granular material.

name: Counterfort / Buttress
description: A transverse reinforced concrete rib connecting the stem to the footing at intervals to reduce bending moments in tall walls.

name: Cope / Coping
description: A protective cap placed on top of the wall to shed water and provide a finished edge.

name: Expansion / Control Joint
description: A planned gap in the wall structure that accommodates thermal movement and prevents uncontrolled cracking.

name: Backfill Material
description: Compacted soil or granular material placed behind the wall that generates the lateral earth pressure the wall must resist.

name: Surcharge Load Zone
description: The area above and behind the wall where additional loads (traffic, structures) increase lateral pressure on the wall.

name: Retained Soil Zone
description: The volume of soil held back by the wall whose weight and pressure govern wall design.

name: Excavation for Footing
description: The earthworks activity of digging the trench or pit required to install the wall footing at design depth.

name: Concrete Pouring and Curing
description: The activity of placing, vibrating, and curing concrete in wall forms to achieve design strength.

name: Waterproofing / Damp-proofing Application
description: The application of membranes or coatings to the retained face of the wall to prevent moisture ingress.

name: Sheet Pile Driving
description: The activity of installing sheet piles into the ground using impact, vibratory, or hydraulic pressing equipment.

name: Ground Anchor Installation
description: The drilling, grouting, and stressing of tie-back anchors into competent ground behind the wall.

name: Soil Nailing
description: The drilling and grouting of closely spaced steel nails into existing soil as part of a soil nail wall construction sequence.

name: Geotechnical Investigation
description: Site investigation including borings, lab testing, and bearing-capacity analysis required to design the wall safely.

name: Drainage Board / Composite Drain
description: A prefabricated geocomposite panel attached to the back face of the wall to channel water down to the perimeter drain.

name: IFCReinforcingBar
description: The IFC schema class representing individual rebar elements embedded within concrete wall and footing components.

name: Driven Pile
description: A pile installed by hammering or vibrating it into the ground using a pile driver.

name: Bored Pile
description: A pile formed by drilling a hole into the ground and filling it with reinforced concrete.

name: Screw Pile
description: A steel shaft with helical flights that is screwed into the soil to provide foundation support.

name: Sheet Pile
description: A thin interlocking pile section driven into the ground to retain soil or water rather than carry vertical loads.

name: Steel H-Pile
description: A structural steel H-section pile driven into the ground to transfer loads to deep bearing strata.

name: Precast Concrete Pile
description: A reinforced or prestressed concrete pile manufactured off-site and driven or pressed into the ground.

name: Timber Pile
description: A treated wooden pile driven into soft or waterlogged ground, one of the oldest foundation methods.

name: Pipe Pile
description: A hollow steel cylindrical pile that can be driven open- or closed-ended and optionally filled with concrete.

name: Pile Shoe
description: A hardened steel tip attached to the bottom of a pile to aid penetration through hard strata.

name: Pile Casing
description: A temporary or permanent steel tube used to stabilise the borehole walls during pile construction.

name: Pile Reinforcement Cage
description: A prefabricated assembly of longitudinal bars and links placed inside a bored pile before concrete is poured.

name: Pile Helmet
description: A protective steel cap placed on top of a pile during driving to distribute hammer blows and prevent splitting.

name: Pile Splice
description: A mechanical or welded connection joining two pile sections to achieve the required overall pile length.

name: Reinforcing Steel
description: Steel bar or cage embedded in concrete piles to resist tensile and bending forces.

name: Pile Driving
description: The construction activity of installing displacement piles into the ground using impact, vibratory, or hydraulic hammers.

name: Pile Boring / Drilling
description: The activity of drilling a borehole to the required depth prior to placing reinforcement and casting a bored pile.

name: Pile Load Testing
description: A testing activity applying static or dynamic loads to a pile to verify its design capacity and behaviour.

name: Pile Integrity Testing
description: Non-destructive testing of a completed pile to detect defects such as cracks, necking, or inclusions.

name: Pile Trimming / Cropping
description: The activity of cutting down pile heads to the correct level after driving or casting to allow pile cap construction.

name: Pile Installation
description: The overall site activity encompassing all operations required to place a pile at its specified location and depth.

name: Concreting of Pile
description: The activity of placing and compacting concrete into a drilled or formed pile shaft using tremie pipe or pump.

name: Pile Grouting
description: Injecting grout around or beneath a pile shaft or tip to enhance load capacity or fill voids post-installation.

name: Deep Foundation System
description: The overall engineered system of piles, pile caps, and connecting beams that transfers building loads to deep soil or rock strata.

name: Pile Group
description: An arrangement of multiple piles acting together beneath a single pile cap to carry combined structural loads.

name: Retaining Wall System
description: A system incorporating sheet piles or contiguous bored piles to retain earth or groundwater around an excavation.

name: IfcPileType
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElementType.

name: Reinforcement Cage
description: A prefabricated assembly of steel rebars and stirrups placed within the pile cap formwork to provide tensile strength and structural integrity.

name: Pile Head
description: The top portion of each pile that is trimmed and embedded into the pile cap to transfer loads from the cap to the piles below.

name: Formwork
description: Temporary shuttering structure used to contain and shape the fresh concrete of the pile cap during casting and curing.

name: Structural Concrete
description: High-strength concrete mix used to form the body of the pile cap, providing compressive resistance and load distribution.

name: Starter Bars
description: Vertical rebar dowels cast into the pile cap that project upward to lap with the reinforcement of the column or wall above.

name: Spacers and Cover Blocks
description: Plastic or concrete devices used to maintain the specified concrete cover distance between the rebar cage and the formwork faces.

name: Pile Cap Excavation
description: The earthworks activity of digging out the soil around pile heads to the required depth and extent to accommodate the pile cap.

name: Pile Head Cropping
description: The process of breaking or cutting pile heads down to the correct level and exposing sufficient rebar for bonding into the pile cap.

name: Strip Pile Cap
description: A linear variant of a pile cap used to support load-bearing walls by spanning across a row of closely spaced piles.

name: Isolated Pile Cap
description: A discrete pile cap variant supporting a single column, typically resting on one or a small cluster of piles.

name: Raft-Combined Pile Cap
description: A hybrid foundation variant where pile caps are integrated into a continuous raft slab to combine piled and mat foundation behaviour.

name: Anti-Heave Membrane
description: A compressible void-forming material placed around piles and beneath slabs to accommodate ground heave and prevent upward pressure on the pile cap.

name: IFC Footing
description: The IFC schema class (IfcFooting) used to model pile caps and other isolated foundation elements in BIM authoring tools.

name: Longitudinal Reinforcement Bar
description: Main steel bars running along the length of the beam to resist bending moments and tensile forces.

name: Stirrup / Link Bar
description: Transverse steel loops spaced along the beam to resist shear forces and hold longitudinal bars in position.

name: Concrete Cover
description: The specified thickness of concrete protecting the steel reinforcement from corrosion and fire exposure.

name: Blinding Concrete
description: A thin plain-concrete layer cast on the excavated ground to provide a clean, level surface before the beam is formed.

name: Formwork / Shuttering
description: Temporary molds (timber, steel, or plastic) that shape and contain the wet concrete until it gains sufficient strength.

name: Holding-Down Bolts
description: Anchor bolts cast into the beam to secure steel column base plates or structural frames to the foundation system.

name: Compressible Void Former
description: A sacrificial material placed beneath the beam to create a void that accommodates ground heave in expansive soils.

name: Granular Fill / Hardcore
description: Compacted aggregate or crushed stone placed around and beneath the beam to provide stable bearing and drainage.

name: Structural Concrete (RC)
description: The specified reinforced concrete mix used to cast the ground beam, designed to meet strength and durability requirements.

name: Pad Foundation / Pile Cap
description: Discrete foundation elements that the ground beam spans between, transferring loads to the subsoil or piles.

name: Ground Slab / Raft Interface
description: The junction detail between the ground beam and an adjoining suspended or ground-bearing slab that must be separately modeled and tracked.

name: Movement Joint
description: A designed gap or joint within or between beams to accommodate thermal movement, settlement, or seismic drift.

name: Trench Excavation
description: The earthworks operation of digging the trench to the required depth and width to accommodate the ground beam.

name: Blinding Concrete Placement
description: The activity of placing and leveling the lean-mix blinding layer at the base of the excavated trench.

name: Formwork Erection & Striking
description: The sequential activities of assembling the beam formwork before concreting and removing it after the concrete has cured.

name: Concrete Pouring & Compaction
description: The activity of placing, vibrating, and finishing the concrete mix within the formwork to achieve a dense, void-free beam.

name: Backfilling & Compaction
description: The earthworks activity of returning and compacting excavated or imported material around the completed beam.

name: Structural Inspection & Testing
description: Quality-assurance checks including rebar surveys, concrete cube tests, and cover measurements conducted during and after construction.

name: Tie Beam Variant
description: A ground beam variant designed primarily to connect pile caps or column bases and resist horizontal forces rather than carry vertical loads.

name: Capping Beam Variant
description: A beam cast on top of a contiguous or secant pile wall to distribute loads and tie the pile heads together.

name: Grade Beam Variant
description: A ground-level beam bearing directly on the soil or a compacted fill layer, common in light-frame and industrial construction.

name: Ring Beam Variant
description: A continuous closed-loop ground beam that encircles the building perimeter to resist lateral soil or water pressure.

name: Pre-cast Ground Beam Variant
description: A factory-manufactured beam unit delivered to site and placed into prepared trenches, reducing in-situ concrete operations.

name: Foundation System
description: The overall structural system—including ground beams, pads, piles, and rafts—that transfers building loads safely to the ground.

name: Substructure Zone
description: The below-ground spatial zone in which ground beams, foundations, and services are located and must be coordinated.

name: Post-Tensioned Transfer Slab
description: A transfer slab variant that uses post-tensioning tendons to efficiently carry heavy column or wall loads over large spans.

name: Reinforced Concrete Transfer Slab
description: A conventionally reinforced concrete slab variant designed to redirect structural loads from upper columns or walls to lower support points.

name: Flat Plate Transfer Slab
description: A flat, uniform-thickness transfer slab without beams or drop panels, used where ceiling clearance is critical.

name: Ribbed Transfer Slab
description: A transfer slab incorporating a series of ribs or waffle pattern to reduce self-weight while maintaining structural depth.

name: Transfer Plate
description: An extremely thick and stiff slab plate variant used to redistribute heavy loads from closely spaced upper columns to widely spaced lower columns.

name: Drop Panel
description: A localized thickening of the slab around column heads in a transfer slab to resist punching shear forces.

name: Punching Shear Reinforcement
description: Specialised shear studs, stirrups, or headed bars installed in the transfer slab around column connections to prevent punching shear failure.

name: Tendon Anchorage
description: The end-anchor hardware that locks prestressing tendons in place at the edges of a post-tensioned transfer slab.

name: Shear Wall Corbel
description: A structural corbel or ledge cast into a shear wall or core wall to provide bearing support for the transfer slab edge.

name: Construction Joint
description: A planned joint in the transfer slab concrete allowing phased pours to manage the large volume of concrete required.

name: High-Strength Concrete
description: Concrete mix with elevated compressive strength (e.g., C50–C80) commonly specified for transfer slabs to reduce required thickness and self-weight.

name: High-Yield Reinforcement Bar
description: High-tensile deformed steel bars used as primary flexural and shear reinforcement within the transfer slab.

name: Formwork and Shoring System
description: Temporary falsework, props, and formwork that support the wet concrete of a transfer slab during casting, often spanning multiple floors.

name: Re-shoring System
description: Additional temporary propping installed on floors below the transfer slab to redistribute construction loads back to the permanent structure.

name: Structural Health Monitoring System
description: Embedded sensors and data-acquisition systems used to monitor long-term deflection, strain, and crack development in the transfer slab.

name: Podium Level
description: The floor level at which the transfer slab is typically located, separating a podium structure from the tower above.

name: Plant Room / Mechanical Floor
description: A dedicated floor zone often located at the transfer slab level to accommodate MEP services and allow structural depth for transfer elements.

name: Transfer Slab Soffit Space
description: The ceiling void directly below the transfer slab, often requiring coordination for service penetrations and fire protection access.

name: Concrete Pouring – Transfer Slab
description: The controlled placement and compaction of large-volume concrete pours for the transfer slab, requiring careful thermal and sequence management.

name: Reinforcement Fixing – Transfer Slab
description: The installation and tying of dense, multi-layer rebar cages within the transfer slab formwork prior to concrete placement.

name: Structural Load Analysis – Transfer Slab
description: Engineering analysis to determine the load redistribution paths, bending moments, shear forces, and deflections acting on the transfer slab.

name: Deflection Monitoring and Propping Removal
description: Staged monitoring of slab deflections and controlled removal of temporary props as the transfer slab gains load-bearing capacity.

name: Fire Protection Application
description: Application of intumescent coatings, fire-rated boards, or spray-on materials to the soffit and exposed elements of the transfer slab to achieve required fire resistance.

name: Non-Destructive Testing – Slab Integrity
description: Use of ultrasonic, GPR, or other NDT methods to verify concrete quality, tendon grouting, and rebar positioning in the completed transfer slab.

name: Thermal Mass Management – Concrete Pour
description: Planning and execution of cooling measures, insulation blankets, or mix design adjustments to control heat of hydration in a mass concrete transfer slab pour.

name: Reinforced Concrete Shear Wall
description: A cast-in-place or precast concrete wall panel heavily reinforced with steel rebar to resist lateral seismic and wind forces.

name: Steel Plate Shear Wall
description: A lateral load-resisting system using thin steel infill plates welded or bolted between boundary columns and beams.

name: Composite Shear Wall
description: A hybrid wall system combining structural steel sections with concrete encasement or infill for enhanced lateral resistance.

name: Masonry Shear Wall
description: A shear-resisting wall constructed from grouted and reinforced concrete masonry units (CMU) or brick.

name: Timber Shear Wall
description: A wood-framed wall panel sheathed with structural panels (OSB or plywood) to transfer lateral loads to the foundation.

name: Coupled Shear Wall
description: Two or more individual shear wall piers connected by reinforced coupling beams that redistribute lateral forces and improve ductility.

name: Core Shear Wall
description: A central tubular or C-shaped wall cluster surrounding elevator and stair shafts that acts as the primary lateral spine of a building.

name: Boundary Element
description: Specially detailed, heavily confined columns or flanges at the ends of a shear wall that carry high compressive and tensile demands.

name: Wall Pier
description: A discrete vertical segment of a shear wall between openings that acts as an individual column-like element under lateral loading.

name: Horizontal Reinforcement (Shear Wall)
description: Horizontal rebar layers distributed across the web of a concrete shear wall to resist diagonal tension from shear forces.

name: Vertical Reinforcement (Shear Wall)
description: Vertical rebar within the wall web and boundary elements that resist flexural tension and compression under overturning moments.

name: Confinement Ties / Hoops
description: Closely spaced transverse reinforcement enclosing boundary element bars to provide ductile confinement under seismic loading.

name: Shear Wall Foundation / Mat
description: The spread footing, pile cap, or mat slab specifically designed to anchor the shear wall and transfer overturning forces to the ground.

name: Hold-Down Anchor
description: A mechanical connector bolted through the wall's boundary element into the foundation or lower floor to resist net uplift forces.

name: Structural Sheathing Panel
description: OSB or plywood panel nailed to wood-frame studs to form the shear-resisting skin of a timber shear wall.

name: High-Strength Concrete (Shear Wall Mix)
description: Specially proportioned concrete mix, often 5,000–10,000 psi, used in high-rise shear walls to reduce wall thickness while maintaining capacity.

name: Seismic-Grade Reinforcing Steel (Grade 60/80)
description: Rebar certified to ASTM A706 or equivalent standards with controlled yield strength and elongation for ductile seismic performance.

name: Steel Infill Plate
description: Thin-gauge structural steel plate used as the shear-resisting web in a steel plate shear wall system.

name: Shear Wall Formwork
description: Temporary or re-usable gang form panels used to shape and support wet concrete during casting of a reinforced concrete shear wall.

name: Shear Wall Layout & Structural Design
description: Engineering activity of determining wall placement, thickness, reinforcement ratios, and boundary element sizes to meet code drift and strength requirements.

name: Shear Wall Rebar Fabrication & Placement
description: Site or off-site cutting, bending, and tying of all horizontal, vertical, and confinement reinforcement within the shear wall.

name: Shear Wall Concrete Pouring & Curing
description: Placement of fresh concrete into the shear wall formwork followed by controlled curing to achieve design strength and prevent cracking.

name: Shear Wall Formwork Erection & Stripping
description: Installation and later removal of form panels and bracing at each floor lift during phased concrete shear wall construction.

name: Shear Wall Inspection & Testing
description: Special inspection of rebar placement, concrete sampling, and non-destructive testing to verify code-compliant shear wall construction.

name: Lateral Load-Resisting System (LLRS)
description: The overall building system—comprising shear walls, moment frames, and diaphragms—that collectively resists wind and seismic lateral forces.

name: Diaphragm
description: A horizontal floor or roof plate that collects and distributes lateral forces to vertical shear walls and frames acting as a rigid or flexible in-plane element.

name: Collector / Drag Strut
description: A beam or slab element that gathers diaphragm forces and 'drags' them into the shear wall along its length.

name: Shear Wall Opening / Penetration
description: A door, window, or MEP penetration within a shear wall that requires reinforced trimmer bars and lintels to redirect load around the void.

name: Seismic Joint at Shear Wall
description: A deliberately detailed gap between adjacent structures or building wings at the shear wall that allows independent lateral movement during an earthquake.

name: Shear Wall Repair & Retrofit
description: Post-construction or post-seismic activity of assessing and strengthening existing shear walls via jacketing, fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) wrap, or added steel.

name: Reinforced Concrete Core
description: The primary structural material composition of a core wall, combining concrete and steel reinforcement bars to resist lateral and gravity loads.

name: Shear Wall Panel
description: A discrete vertical planar element within the core wall system that resists in-plane lateral (shear) forces from wind or seismic activity.

name: Core Wall Boundary Element
description: Heavily reinforced zones at the edges or ends of a shear wall panel that provide ductility and confinement under extreme loading conditions.

name: Wall Lift / Pour Section
description: A discrete vertical concrete casting segment of the core wall, defined by construction joint locations and formwork cycle heights.

name: Vertical Rebar Cage
description: The assembled longitudinal steel reinforcement bars that run vertically through the core wall to carry axial and flexural forces.

name: Horizontal Rebar (Wall Ties)
description: Transverse steel reinforcement bars or ties spaced at regular intervals to resist shear forces and confine the vertical rebar cage.

name: Embedded Steel Plate / Embed
description: Steel plates cast into the core wall face to serve as connection points for floor plates, brackets, or MEP supports.

name: Slip-Form Formwork System
description: A continuously moving formwork system that enables uninterrupted, rapid vertical concrete casting of the core wall.

name: Jump-Form / Climbing Formwork System
description: A self-climbing or crane-lifted formwork system that advances floor-by-floor to form successive core wall lifts.

name: Core Wall Foundation / Raft Pedestal
description: The thickened raft slab, pile cap, or pedestal base element that transfers core wall loads into the ground or foundation system.

name: Core Wall Opening / Door Opening
description: A formed void within the core wall for lift-lobby doors, fire doors, or MEP penetrations, requiring special trimmer reinforcement.

name: Lift / Elevator Shaft
description: The vertical void enclosed by the core wall that houses elevator cars, guide rails, and associated mechanical equipment.

name: Stairwell Shaft
description: A fire-rated vertical circulation space formed within or adjacent to the core wall, containing stairs and evacuation routes.

name: Services / MEP Riser Shaft
description: A dedicated vertical shaft within the core wall zone that routes mechanical, electrical, and plumbing risers between floors.

name: Fire-Rated Lobby / Refuge Area
description: A protected space at each floor level within the core envelope that acts as a safe staging area during fire evacuation.

name: Rebar Installation Activity
description: The site activity of placing, tying, and inspecting all vertical and horizontal reinforcement steel within the core wall formwork prior to pouring.

name: Concrete Pouring & Vibration Activity
description: The controlled placement and compaction of concrete into the core wall formwork using internal vibrators to eliminate voids.

name: Formwork Striking & Advancing Activity
description: The activity of stripping, repositioning, or climbing the formwork system to the next lift level after the concrete has achieved sufficient strength.

name: Core Wall Surveying & Plumb Check
description: Precision surveying tasks performed each lift cycle to verify the core wall remains plumb, correctly positioned, and within dimensional tolerances.

name: Concrete Curing Activity
description: Post-pour activities including application of curing compounds, wet burlap, or temperature control measures to ensure proper concrete strength gain.

name: Post-Installed Anchor / Rebar Coupler
description: Mechanical anchors or threaded rebar couplers drilled or cast into the core wall surface to facilitate connections to future structural or non-structural elements.

name: Waterproofing & Sealant System
description: Membranes, coatings, or crystalline treatments applied to core wall surfaces to prevent moisture ingress, particularly in below-grade sections.

name: Exposed Soffit
description: A soffit left visible without cladding, often used in industrial or modern architectural styles to reveal structural elements.

name: Closed Soffit
description: A soffit that is fully enclosed with a flat or finished surface, concealing the underside of structural or framing members.

name: Vented Soffit
description: A soffit panel incorporating perforations or vents to allow airflow into the roof cavity, preventing moisture buildup.

name: Non-Vented Soffit Panel
description: A solid soffit panel without perforations, used where ventilation is provided by other means or not required.

name: Eave Soffit
description: The horizontal underside panel located at the roof eave, bridging the gap between the exterior wall and the fascia board.

name: Stair Soffit
description: The sloped or angled underside surface beneath a staircase, often finished or enclosed for aesthetics and safety.

name: Beam Soffit
description: The flat bottom face of a structural or decorative beam, visible from below and sometimes specially finished.

name: Arch Soffit (Intrados)
description: The inner curved surface of an arch, defining the underside of the arched opening.

name: Drop Soffit / Bulkhead
description: A lowered ceiling section that drops below the main ceiling plane to conceal ductwork, pipes, or structural elements.

name: Soffit Panel
description: An individual panel unit used to construct the soffit surface, available in various materials and perforation patterns.

name: Soffit Vent
description: A discrete ventilation insert or strip fitted into the soffit to provide controlled airflow into the roof or eave space.

name: J-Channel / F-Channel Trim
description: Extruded trim channel used to receive and secure the edges of soffit panels against the wall or fascia.

name: Lookout Rafter / Soffit Nailer
description: A short horizontal framing member that provides structural support for the soffit panel at the eave.

name: Vinyl Soffit
description: PVC-based soffit material widely used for its low maintenance, moisture resistance, and ease of installation.

name: Aluminum Soffit
description: Metal soffit cladding made from aluminum, valued for its durability, lightweight properties, and corrosion resistance.

name: Fiber Cement Soffit Board
description: A composite soffit material made of cement and cellulose fibers, offering high fire resistance and dimensional stability.

name: Wood Soffit Board
description: Traditional timber-based soffit cladding, typically painted or stained, requiring periodic maintenance to prevent rot.

name: Plywood Soffit Sheathing
description: Engineered wood panel used as a soffit substrate, often finished with paint or a cladding overlay.

name: EIFS / Stucco Soffit Finish
description: A plaster or synthetic stucco coating applied over a substrate to create a seamless, textured soffit surface.

name: Eave Space / Eave Cavity
description: The enclosed cavity above the soffit and below the roof deck at the eave, through which ventilation air travels from the soffit vents to the ridge.

name: Soffit Concealment Cavity
description: The hidden void created by a drop soffit or bulkhead used to route mechanical, electrical, and plumbing services.

name: Eave Drainage & Gutter System
description: The assembly of gutters, downspouts, and drip edges at the eave that collects and diverts roof runoff away from the soffit and building envelope.

name: Soffit Lighting System
description: Recessed or surface-mounted luminaires integrated into the soffit for exterior or interior accent and task lighting.

name: Soffit Installation
description: The construction activity of fitting and securing soffit panels, channels, and trim to complete the underside cladding of an eave or overhead structure.

name: Soffit Ventilation Installation
description: The activity of cutting openings and fitting vent inserts or continuous vent strips into soffit panels to achieve required ventilation ratios.

name: Soffit Painting & Finishing
description: Surface preparation, priming, and application of paint or sealant coatings to protect and aesthetically finish soffit materials.

name: Soffit Repair & Replacement
description: Maintenance activity involving removal of damaged soffit panels or boards and installation of new material to restore integrity and appearance.

name: Soffit Inspection
description: Periodic assessment of soffit condition to identify rot, pest intrusion, water damage, paint failure, or blocked vents.

name: Eave Baffle / Rafter Vent Installation
description: The activity of inserting cardboard or foam baffles between rafters above the soffit vent to maintain a clear airflow path into the roof cavity.

name: IfcCovering (Soffit)
description: The IFC schema class used to model soffit elements as a covering object applied to the underside of slabs, beams, or eave structures.

name: IfcPlate (Soffit Panel)
description: An IFC class representing flat panel elements, applicable to individual soffit panel components in a BIM model.

name: Balcony Slab
description: The structural horizontal platform forming the floor of a balcony, typically made of reinforced concrete or steel.

name: Balcony Railing
description: A protective barrier system installed along the open edges of a balcony to prevent falls.

name: Balcony Guardrail Post
description: Vertical structural members anchored to the slab that support the balcony railing system.

name: Balcony Handrail
description: The graspable horizontal or sloped rail fixed atop the guardrail posts for user grip and safety.

name: Balcony Balustrade
description: The infill panel or series of balusters between guardrail posts that forms a decorative and protective barrier.

name: Balcony Beam
description: Structural beam that supports or cantilevers the balcony slab from the main building frame.

name: Balcony Bracket
description: A steel or concrete corbel bracket used to support a cantilevered balcony slab or beam.

name: Balcony Waterproofing Membrane
description: A waterproof layer applied beneath balcony finishes to prevent water ingress into the structural slab.

name: Balcony Deck Finish
description: The surface finish material applied on the balcony floor, such as tiles, pavers, timber decking, or resin coating.

name: Balcony Drainage System
description: The integrated slope, drain outlets, and downpipes that collect and channel rainwater away from the balcony surface.

name: Balcony Door
description: An exterior door unit providing access from the interior space to the balcony, often glazed.

name: Balcony Threshold
description: The transition element at the base of the balcony door that seals the junction between interior flooring and the balcony slab.

name: Balcony Glazing Screen
description: A glass or polycarbonate wind/privacy screen installed on one or more sides of an open balcony.

name: Balcony Soffit
description: The underside exposed surface of the balcony slab, typically rendered or clad for weather protection and aesthetics.

name: Balcony Thermal Break
description: An insulating element installed at the slab-to-structure connection to prevent cold bridging through the balcony.

name: Balcony Lighting Fixture
description: Exterior-rated light fittings mounted on the balcony wall, ceiling, or railing for illumination and ambiance.

name: Balcony Waterproofing
description: The construction activity of applying waterproofing membranes and sealants to the balcony slab and upstands.

name: Balcony Formwork and Casting
description: The activity of erecting formwork and pouring concrete to form the balcony slab in-situ.

name: Balcony Railing Installation
description: The activity of fabricating and fixing the railing, posts, and balustrade system to the balcony slab or facade.

name: Balcony Tiling and Paving
description: The activity of laying tiles, stone, or paving units on the balcony deck over the waterproofing layer.

name: Balcony Inspection and Testing
description: Structural and waterproofing inspection activities including load testing and flood testing of the balcony assembly.

name: Balcony Maintenance and Repair
description: Ongoing activity covering inspection, crack repair, resealing, and refinishing of balcony elements over the building lifecycle.

name: Juliette Balcony
description: A false balcony variant consisting only of a railing or balustrade in front of a full-height opening door with no usable external floor.

name: Cantilevered Balcony
description: A balcony variant that projects from the building structure with no external supporting columns, relying on cantilever structural action.

name: Loggia
description: A recessed balcony-type space set within the building envelope, open on one side, offering a sheltered outdoor area.

name: Terrace
description: A large accessible outdoor platform on a roof or at ground level, closely related to the balcony but at a different scale and position.

name: Fixing Bracket
description: A structural anchor or clip that mechanically fastens the facade panel to the building's primary structure or substrate.

name: Thermal Insulation Layer
description: An insulating layer (e.g., mineral wool, PIR board) installed behind or within the facade panel to reduce heat transfer through the envelope.

name: Weather Sealing Joint
description: A flexible seal, gasket, or backer rod filling the gap between adjacent facade panels to prevent water and air infiltration.

name: Subframe / Support Rail
description: A secondary metal framework (aluminium or steel rail system) that transfers panel loads back to the primary structure and maintains panel alignment.

name: Rainscreen Cladding System
description: A drained and ventilated facade assembly that uses an air cavity behind the panel to manage moisture and equalise pressure.

name: Ventilated Cavity
description: The air gap between the facade panel and the backing wall that allows moisture to drain and air to circulate, preventing condensation build-up.

name: Vapour Control Layer
description: A membrane installed on the warm side of insulation to limit moisture vapour diffusion into the facade build-up.

name: Fibre Cement Panel
description: A specific facade panel variant manufactured from fibre-reinforced cement, offering durability and fire resistance.

name: High-Pressure Laminate (HPL) Panel
description: A facade panel variant made from compressed resin-impregnated paper layers, providing a lightweight, colourfast exterior finish.

name: Aluminium Composite Panel (ACP)
description: A sandwich panel variant with aluminium face sheets and a polyethylene or fire-retardant mineral core, widely used for curtain wall cladding.

name: Terracotta Rainscreen Panel
description: A fired-clay ceramic panel variant offering natural aesthetics and excellent long-term weathering performance.

name: Glass Fibre Reinforced Concrete (GRC) Panel
description: A thin, lightweight cladding panel made from concrete reinforced with alkali-resistant glass fibres, used for complex architectural forms.

name: Surface Coating / Finish
description: The outermost decorative and protective layer applied to the panel face, such as PVDF paint, anodising, or texture coat.

name: Fire-Resistant Barrier
description: A non-combustible cavity barrier or intumescent strip installed at floor levels within the facade build-up to prevent fire and smoke spread.

name: Facade Panel Installation
description: The site activity of lifting, positioning, aligning, and fixing facade panels to the subframe in accordance with the installation sequence and tolerances.

name: Facade Panel Fabrication
description: The off-site or on-site manufacturing process of cutting, forming, coating, and quality-checking panels to project specifications.

name: Facade Inspection & Testing
description: Commissioning and quality-assurance activity involving water-tightness tests, pull-out tests, and visual checks of the installed facade system.

name: Facade Panel Replacement / Maintenance
description: Planned or reactive maintenance activity involving the removal and substitution of damaged or end-of-life panels without disturbing adjacent units.

name: Subframe Installation
description: The site activity of setting out, drilling, and fixing the supporting rail or bracket system to the structural substrate prior to panel hanging.

name: IfcPlate
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: External Wall Build-Up
description: The complete layered assembly from structural wall to outer panel face, encompassing all thermal, acoustic, and weather-protection components.

name: Thermal Bridge
description: A localised area of increased heat flow through the facade, typically at fixing brackets or frame connections, requiring thermal break detailing.

name: Acoustic Backing Layer
description: A sound-absorbing or sound-damping material placed behind the facade panel to improve the acoustic performance of the external envelope.

name: Rainwater Head
description: A box-shaped collector fitting at the top of a downpipe that receives water from gutters or parapet outlets.

name: Roof Drain
description: A drain unit installed at low points of flat or low-slope roofs to collect and discharge accumulated rainwater.

name: Siphonic Roof Drainage System
description: A high-velocity drainage system that uses siphonic action to efficiently evacuate large volumes of water through smaller pipework.

name: Parapet Outlet
description: An opening or spout through a parapet wall that allows water to drain off a flat roof to the exterior.

name: Overflow Outlet
description: A secondary drainage point designed to prevent water build-up on a roof in the event the primary drain becomes blocked.

name: Leaf Guard / Gutter Filter
description: A mesh or perforated cover placed over gutters to prevent debris from blocking the drainage flow.

name: Downpipe Shoe
description: A curved fitting at the base of a downpipe that redirects water flow into a gully or drain at ground level.

name: Gully
description: A ground-level drainage inlet that receives water discharged from downpipes and conveys it to the underground drainage network.

name: Rainwater Harvesting Tank
description: A storage system that collects and retains rainwater from roof surfaces for later non-potable reuse.

name: Underground Stormwater Drainage Network
description: A subsurface pipe network that conveys collected roof runoff away from the building to a soakaway, watercourse, or sewer.

name: Soakaway / Infiltration System
description: A below-ground structure that allows collected roof rainwater to percolate slowly into the surrounding soil.

name: Green Roof Drainage Layer
description: A specially engineered drainage mat or aggregate layer within a green roof build-up that manages water retention and runoff.

name: Roof Waterproofing Membrane
description: An impermeable membrane applied to the roof substrate to prevent water ingress and direct runoff towards drainage points.

name: EPDM / PVC Gutter Liner
description: A flexible waterproof lining material used inside gutters to prevent corrosion and prolong service life.

name: Cast Iron
description: A traditional ferrous metal used for gutters, downpipes, and rainwater heads prized for its durability and aesthetic character.

name: uPVC
description: A lightweight, low-maintenance plastic widely used for modern gutters and downpipes due to its corrosion resistance.

name: Zinc
description: A self-protecting metal used for bespoke rainwater goods, valued for its longevity and distinctive weathered patina.

name: Roof Drainage Design & Sizing
description: The engineering calculation and design process that determines the required drainage capacity, pipe sizing, and outlet positions for a roof.

name: Gutter Installation
description: The trade activity of fixing and jointing gutter sections at the correct fall along roof eaves or internal valleys.

name: Downpipe Installation
description: The trade activity of securing vertical downpipe runs, offsets, and brackets from gutter outlets to ground drainage.

name: Roof Drain Installation
description: The activity of setting, sealing, and connecting flat-roof drain units into the roof build-up and internal pipework.

name: Gutter Cleaning & Maintenance
description: Periodic removal of debris, moss, and sediment from gutters and downpipes to maintain unobstructed water flow.

name: Drainage CCTV Inspection
description: A diagnostic activity using camera equipment to inspect the condition and integrity of underground drainage pipework.

name: Roof Fall / Slope Assessment
description: A survey activity to verify that roof surfaces have adequate gradient to direct rainwater efficiently towards drainage outlets.

name: Valley Gutter
description: A channel formed at the intersection of two roof slopes to collect and discharge rainwater to a downpipe.

name: Box Gutter
description: A wide, flat-bottomed concealed gutter built into the roof structure, typically used on large-span or parapet roofs.

name: IFC Roof Drainage Element (IfcPipeSegment)
description: The IFC schema class used to model pipe segments within a building's roof drainage and stormwater system in BIM environments.

name: Cover Plate
description: A metal plate that bridges the expansion joint gap to protect it from debris and provide a smooth surface transition.

name: Nosing Profile
description: A shaped edge element installed at the joint opening to protect the slab or deck edge from chipping and wear.

name: Compression Seal
description: A preformed elastomeric seal inserted under compression to fill the joint gap and prevent water and dirt ingress.

name: Anchor Rail
description: A recessed steel rail cast or fixed into the concrete substrate to secure the expansion joint assembly in place.

name: Sliding Plate Joint
description: An expansion joint variant using overlapping metal plates that slide relative to each other to accommodate structural movement.

name: Modular Expansion Joint
description: A multi-cell joint system with multiple seals and support bars designed to handle large movement ranges in bridges and structures.

name: Finger Joint
description: An expansion joint variant featuring interlocking metal fingers that allow longitudinal movement while maintaining a continuous surface.

name: Rubber Strip Seal
description: A profiled elastomeric strip bonded or mechanically fastened within a joint assembly to seal against water and accommodate cyclic movement.

name: Foam Filler
description: A compressible closed-cell foam material placed in the joint gap to accommodate movement and act as a thermal break.

name: Isolation Joint
description: A closely related joint type that completely separates two structural elements to prevent stress transfer, often confused with expansion joints.

name: Control Joint
description: A planned weakened plane in concrete or masonry designed to control cracking location, distinct from but related to expansion joints.

name: Seismic Joint
description: A wide structural gap specifically sized and detailed to permit differential movement between building sections during an earthquake.

name: Thermal Expansion Gap
description: The deliberate void between structural elements that accommodates thermally induced dimensional changes in materials.

name: Joint Installation
description: The construction activity of positioning, anchoring, and sealing an expansion joint assembly within the structure.

name: Joint Sealing
description: The activity of applying or replacing sealant and compression seals within a joint to restore weathertightness.

name: Joint Inspection
description: A periodic maintenance activity to assess the condition, movement capacity, and seal integrity of expansion joints.

name: Joint Replacement
description: The remedial activity of removing a deteriorated expansion joint assembly and installing a new one in its place.

name: Structural Movement Monitoring
description: The ongoing measurement of relative displacement across joint gaps to verify design assumptions and detect anomalies.

name: Expansion Joint System
description: The integrated assembly of all joint components, seals, and fixings that collectively manage structural movement across a building or infrastructure element.

name: Stainless Steel Armour
description: Corrosion-resistant steel edge protection fixed along joint faces to prevent concrete or masonry spalling under traffic or load.

name: Fire-Rated Joint Filler
description: An intumescent or mineral-wool-based filler installed within the joint to maintain fire compartmentation across the gap.

name: Fire-Stopping Activity
description: The construction activity of installing fire-rated fillers and collars within expansion joints to meet compartmentation requirements.

name: Air Handling Unit (AHU)
description: A large unit that conditions and circulates air as part of the HVAC system, typically containing a blower, heating/cooling elements, and filters.

name: Chiller
description: A machine that removes heat from a liquid via a vapor-compression or absorption refrigeration cycle to provide chilled water for cooling.

name: Boiler
description: A closed vessel that heats water or generates steam for distribution throughout the building's heating circuit.

name: Cooling Tower
description: An external heat-rejection device that expels waste heat from the chiller to the atmosphere via water evaporation.

name: Ductwork
description: A network of metal or flexible channels that distribute conditioned air from the AHU to occupied spaces.

name: Supply Air Diffuser
description: A ceiling or wall outlet that delivers conditioned air into a room in a controlled, dispersed pattern.

name: Return Air Grille
description: An opening that collects room air and channels it back to the AHU for reconditioning.

name: Exhaust Fan
description: A fan unit that expels stale or contaminated air from a space directly to the outside.

name: Fan Coil Unit (FCU)
description: A small terminal device containing a coil and fan that heats or cools a local zone using hot/chilled water from central plant.

name: Variable Air Volume (VAV) Box
description: A terminal unit that modulates the volume of conditioned air delivered to a zone to match its heating or cooling load.

name: Heat Recovery Ventilator (HRV)
description: A device that transfers heat between outgoing exhaust air and incoming fresh air to improve energy efficiency.

name: Energy Recovery Ventilator (ERV)
description: Similar to an HRV but also transfers moisture between airstreams, maintaining humidity balance while recovering energy.

name: Chilled Water Piping
description: Insulated pipework that circulates cold water from the chiller to cooling coils throughout the building.

name: Hot Water Piping
description: Insulated pipework that distributes heated water from the boiler to heating coils and terminal units.

name: Refrigerant Piping
description: Copper or steel pipework that carries refrigerant between condensing and evaporating units in a direct-expansion system.

name: Pump (Hydronic)
description: A circulating pump that moves chilled or hot water through the hydronic piping loops of the HVAC system.

name: Expansion Tank
description: A pressurised vessel that absorbs excess water volume caused by thermal expansion in a closed hydronic system.

name: Air Filter / Media Filter
description: A filtration device installed in the air stream to remove particulates, dust, and allergens before air is distributed.

name: HEPA Filter
description: A high-efficiency particulate air filter capable of capturing at least 99.97 % of airborne particles ≥ 0.3 µm.

name: Humidifier
description: A device that adds moisture to the air stream to maintain target relative humidity levels within conditioned spaces.

name: Dehumidifier
description: A device that removes excess moisture from the air to prevent condensation and maintain comfort conditions.

name: Thermostat / Room Temperature Sensor
description: A wall-mounted sensor and controller that monitors room temperature and sends signals to modulate heating or cooling output.

name: Building Automation System (BAS) / BMS Controller
description: A centralised control platform that monitors, schedules, and optimises all HVAC (and other building) equipment automatically.

name: Variable Frequency Drive (VFD)
description: An electronic drive that controls the rotational speed of fans and pumps to match actual demand, saving energy.

name: Damper (Fire / Smoke / Volume)
description: A mechanical valve within ductwork used to control airflow, isolate zones, or close automatically in a fire event.

name: Split-System Air Conditioner
description: A self-contained two-part cooling/heating system with an outdoor condensing unit and an indoor evaporator unit serving individual zones.

name: Packaged Rooftop Unit (RTU)
description: An all-in-one HVAC unit installed on the roof that supplies heating, cooling, and ventilation to the building below.

name: Ground Source Heat Pump (GSHP)
description: A heat pump that exchanges heat with the ground via buried loops to provide highly efficient heating and cooling.

name: Air Source Heat Pump (ASHP)
description: A heat pump that extracts heat from outdoor air to provide space heating and, in reverse cycle, space cooling.

name: Radiant Floor Heating System
description: A hydronic or electric in-floor system that delivers heat through radiation from the floor surface upward into the occupied zone.

name: Chilled Beam System
description: A ceiling-mounted terminal system that uses chilled water flowing through a beam to cool (and sometimes heat) a space via convection.

name: Displacement Ventilation System
description: A low-velocity ventilation strategy that introduces fresh air at floor level, displacing warmer contaminated air upward to exhaust points.

name: Dedicated Outdoor Air System (DOAS)
description: A system that handles only ventilation (outdoor) air separately from space conditioning, improving IAQ and energy control.

name: Mechanical Plant Room
description: A dedicated room housing central HVAC plant such as chillers, boilers, AHUs, and associated pipework and controls.

name: Roof Plant Area
description: A designated rooftop zone accommodating packaged units, cooling towers, and other HVAC equipment requiring outdoor placement.

name: Riser Shaft (HVAC)
description: A vertical shaft running through multiple floors that routes ductwork and pipework between the central plant and served floors.

name: Thermal Insulation (Duct & Pipe)
description: Mineral wool, foam, or flexible elastomeric insulation applied to ducts and pipes to minimise heat gain/loss and prevent condensation.

name: Sheet Metal (Ductwork)
description: Galvanised or stainless steel sheet used to fabricate rigid supply, return, and exhaust duct sections.

name: Refrigerant (e.g. R-410A, R-32, R-134a)
description: The working fluid in a refrigeration cycle that absorbs and releases heat as it changes phase between liquid and vapour.

name: HVAC System Installation
description: The construction activity of fitting, connecting, and commissioning all HVAC plant, equipment, ductwork, and controls on site.

name: Ductwork Fabrication & Erection
description: Off-site manufacture and on-site installation of all duct sections, fittings, hangers, and supports.

name: Pipe Pressure Testing
description: A commissioning activity that verifies the integrity of hydronic or refrigerant pipework by pressurising it to a test level.

name: Air Balancing & TAB (Testing, Adjusting & Balancing)
description: A commissioning process that measures and adjusts airflow rates at each outlet to meet design specifications.

name: HVAC Commissioning
description: The systematic process of verifying that all HVAC components and systems are installed, tested, and operating as designed.

name: HVAC Preventive Maintenance
description: Scheduled inspection, cleaning, lubrication, and part-replacement activities performed to sustain HVAC system performance and longevity.

name: IfcDistributionSystem
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcSystem.

name: IfcAirTerminal
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowTerminal.

name: IfcUnitaryEquipment
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcEnergyConversionDevice.

name: IfcCoil
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcEnergyConversionDevice.

name: IfcFan
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowMovingDevice.

name: IfcPump
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowMovingDevice.

name: IfcChiller
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcEnergyConversionDevice.

name: IfcBoiler
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcEnergyConversionDevice.

name: IfcFilter
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowTreatmentDevice.

name: IfcDuctSegment
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowSegment.

name: Water Supply Pipes
description: Network of pressurized pipes that distribute potable cold and hot water throughout the building to fixtures and appliances.

name: Drain-Waste-Vent (DWV) Pipes
description: Pipes that carry wastewater and sewage away from fixtures while venting sewer gases safely to the atmosphere.

name: Hot Water Heater
description: Appliance that heats and stores or instantaneously delivers hot water for domestic use throughout the building.

name: Water Meter
description: Device installed at the building's main supply entry to measure and record total water consumption.

name: Shut-Off Valves
description: Manual or automatic valves positioned at key points in the supply network to isolate sections for maintenance or emergency.

name: Pressure Reducing Valve (PRV)
description: Valve that reduces incoming mains water pressure to a safe, consistent level suitable for building fixtures.

name: Backflow Preventer
description: Device that stops contaminated or non-potable water from flowing backwards into the clean water supply.

name: Sump Pump
description: Submersible or pedestal pump installed in a sump pit to remove accumulated groundwater or drainage from below-grade areas.

name: Sump Pit
description: Below-floor cavity or basin that collects groundwater or sub-surface drainage before it is pumped away.

name: Floor Drain
description: Drain fitting flush-mounted in the floor to collect and direct incidental water to the waste system.

name: Pipe Insulation
description: Thermal or acoustic wrapping applied to supply and drain pipes to prevent heat loss, condensation, and noise transmission.

name: Copper Pipe
description: Traditional metallic piping material used for potable water supply lines, valued for durability and corrosion resistance.

name: PEX Tubing
description: Flexible cross-linked polyethylene tubing widely used in modern supply plumbing for ease of installation and freeze resistance.

name: PVC / CPVC Pipe
description: Rigid plastic piping used for drain-waste-vent runs and, in CPVC form, for hot and cold water supply lines.

name: Cast Iron Pipe
description: Heavy-duty iron pipe used for large-diameter drain and sewer runs, prized for sound attenuation and longevity.

name: Pipe Fittings & Couplings
description: Elbows, tees, reducers, and couplings that connect, redirect, and terminate pipe runs throughout the system.

name: Water Softener
description: Treatment sub-system that removes calcium and magnesium ions to reduce scale build-up in pipes and appliances.

name: Water Filtration System
description: Sub-system of filters and media that removes sediment, chlorine, or contaminants from the incoming water supply.

name: Greywater Recycling System
description: Sub-system that captures, treats, and reuses lightly soiled wastewater from sinks and showers for toilet flushing or irrigation.

name: Rainwater Harvesting System
description: Collection and storage sub-system that captures roof runoff for non-potable uses such as irrigation or toilet flushing.

name: Sanitary Sewer Connection
description: The building's outgoing drain line that ties into the municipal or private sewer network to convey wastewater off-site.

name: Septic System
description: On-site wastewater treatment and disposal system used where municipal sewer connection is unavailable.

name: Vent Stack
description: Vertical pipe extending through the roof that vents sewer gases and maintains atmospheric pressure in the drain system.

name: Trap (P-Trap / S-Trap)
description: Curved pipe section beneath fixtures that holds a water seal to block sewer gases from entering the occupied space.

name: Cleanout Access Point
description: Capped fitting installed in drain lines that provides access for drain-cleaning equipment during maintenance or blockage clearing.

name: Hose Bibb / Outdoor Spigot
description: Exterior-mounted faucet valve that provides outdoor water access for hoses, irrigation, or construction use.

name: Plumbing Rough-In
