description: Construction phase where supply and drain pipes are installed within walls, floors, and ceilings before surfaces are closed.

name: Plumbing Fixture Trim-Out
description: Final installation stage where visible fixtures, faucets, and valves are connected and finished after surfaces are complete.

name: Pressure Testing
description: Quality-assurance procedure in which pressurized air or water is used to verify pipe integrity and detect leaks before walls are closed.

name: Drain Cleaning & Descaling
description: Maintenance activity that removes blockages, scale, and build-up from drain and waste pipes to restore flow capacity.

name: Pipe Insulation Installation
description: Trade activity of wrapping or fitting insulating jackets around pipes to comply with energy codes and prevent freezing or condensation.

name: Water Heater Installation
description: Trade activity covering the positioning, connection, and commissioning of hot water heating equipment.

name: Leak Detection & Repair
description: Diagnostic and remediation activity using acoustic, thermal, or tracer-gas methods to locate and seal pipe leaks.

name: IfcDistributionFlowElement
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcDistributionElement.

name: IfcPipeSegment
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowSegment.

name: IfcPipeFitting
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowFitting.

name: IfcValve
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowController.

name: IfcFlowTerminal
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcDistributionFlowElement.

name: IfcSanitaryTerminal
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowTerminal.

name: IfcInterceptor
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowTreatmentDevice.

name: Main Distribution Board
description: The primary panel that receives incoming electrical supply and distributes it to sub-circuits throughout the building.

name: Sub Distribution Board
description: A secondary panel fed from the main board that further distributes power to a specific zone or floor.

name: Automatic Transfer Switch
description: A switching device that automatically transfers the load between the utility supply and a backup generator.

name: Busbar Trunking System
description: A prefabricated metal enclosure containing copper or aluminium busbars used for high-capacity power distribution along risers or plant rooms.

name: Circuit Breaker
description: A protective switching device that automatically interrupts a circuit under fault or overload conditions.

name: Residual Current Device
description: A safety device that disconnects a circuit when it detects leakage current to earth, protecting against electrocution and fire.

name: Surge Protection Device
description: A device installed to protect electrical equipment from voltage spikes and transient surges.

name: Power Cable
description: Insulated conductors used to transmit electrical power between distribution points, equipment, and outlets.

name: Cable Tray
description: A rigid structural support system used to route and manage power and data cables through a building.

name: Cable Conduit
description: A protective tube or duct, made of metal or PVC, through which electrical cables are threaded for mechanical and environmental protection.

name: Socket Outlet
description: A fixed point of connection providing accessible electrical power to portable equipment and appliances.

name: Switched Fused Connection Unit
description: A wall-mounted unit providing a switched, fused connection for permanently wired appliances such as fans and heaters.

name: Lighting Circuit
description: The dedicated branch circuit and associated wiring designed to supply power exclusively to lighting fixtures.

name: Power Circuit
description: A branch circuit that supplies electrical power to socket outlets and fixed equipment loads within a building.

name: Uninterruptible Power Supply
description: A battery-backed power conditioning system that provides continuous electrical power during mains supply interruptions.

name: Standby Generator
description: A diesel or gas engine-driven generator that provides backup electrical power when the utility supply fails.

name: Building Energy Management System
description: A supervisory control and monitoring platform that tracks and optimises electrical consumption across the building.

name: Smart Metering System
description: Digital meters and communication infrastructure that record and transmit real-time electricity consumption data.

name: Power Factor Correction Unit
description: Capacitor bank equipment installed to improve the power factor of the electrical supply and reduce reactive power losses.

name: Electric Vehicle Charging System
description: Dedicated circuits, charge points, and management equipment for charging electric vehicles in car parks or bays.

name: Motor Control Centre
description: An assembly of starters, drives, and protective devices that centrally control and protect electric motors serving building services plant.

name: Variable Speed Drive
description: An electronic controller that adjusts the speed and torque of an electric motor to match varying load demands, saving energy.

name: Transformer
description: A static electromagnetic device that steps utility high voltage down (or up) to the distribution voltage required within the building.

name: Electrical Riser
description: A dedicated vertical shaft or cupboard routed through floors to accommodate rising power cables and metering equipment.

name: Main Switchroom
description: A dedicated room housing the main distribution board, metering, and associated high-voltage or LV switchgear.

name: Electrical Substation
description: An enclosed space or building containing transformer and HV switchgear to receive and step down utility supply voltage.

name: Generator Room
description: A purpose-built room providing ventilation, fuel containment, and acoustic treatment for standby generator sets.

name: UPS Room
description: A dedicated, climate-controlled room housing uninterruptible power supply batteries and inverter equipment.

name: Electrical Containment Installation
description: The site activity of fixing cable trays, ladders, conduits, and trunking to support and route all electrical wiring.

name: Cable Pulling and Termination
description: The trade activity of drawing cables through containment and making secure, tested electrical connections at each end.

name: Distribution Board Installation
description: The activity of mounting, wiring, and labelling main and sub distribution boards in accordance with the design schedules.

name: Electrical Testing and Commissioning
description: The systematic inspection, testing, and verification of the completed installation against regulatory and design standards before handover.

name: Thermographic Survey
description: An infrared scanning inspection activity used to identify hot spots and potential faults in live electrical panels and connections.

name: Electrical Load Scheduling
description: The design and documentation activity of calculating and scheduling connected loads to ensure balanced and adequate circuit capacity.

name: IFC Electrical Element
description: The IFC schema class (IfcElectricDistributionBoard, IfcCableSegment, etc.) used to represent electrical components in BIM models.

name: Sprinkler Head
description: A heat-activated nozzle that disperses water over a fire area when triggered by elevated temperatures.

name: Fire Suppression Control Panel
description: The central unit that monitors, controls, and reports the status of all fire suppression zones and devices.

name: Wet Pipe Sprinkler System
description: A sprinkler variant where pipes are permanently charged with pressurized water, ready for immediate discharge.

name: Dry Pipe Sprinkler System
description: A sprinkler variant where pipes contain pressurized air or nitrogen, releasing water only when a head activates.

name: Pre-Action Sprinkler System
description: A two-signal system requiring both fire detection and sprinkler activation before water is discharged, protecting sensitive areas.

name: Deluge Sprinkler System
description: A system with open sprinkler heads that simultaneously flood an entire zone when triggered by a detection device.

name: Gaseous Suppression System
description: A clean-agent or CO₂ system that suppresses fire by displacing oxygen or chemically interrupting combustion without water damage.

name: Foam Suppression System
description: A system that discharges foam concentrate mixed with water to smother flammable liquid fires, common in hangars and fuel storage areas.

name: Kitchen Hood Suppression System
description: A wet chemical suppression system installed above commercial cooking equipment to extinguish grease fires.

name: Fire Pump
description: A dedicated pump that boosts water pressure in the suppression piping network to meet required flow rates.

name: Jockey Pump
description: A small pressure-maintenance pump that compensates for minor leaks and keeps the system pressurized without starting the main fire pump.

name: Fire Suppression Piping
description: The network of steel, CPVC, or copper pipes that distributes suppression agent from the supply source to all discharge points.

name: Suppression Agent Storage Cylinder
description: A pressurized vessel that stores clean agent, CO₂, or foam concentrate ready for system discharge.

name: Alarm Check Valve
description: A one-way valve that allows water flow to sprinkler heads and simultaneously triggers a water-motor alarm when a head activates.

name: Dry Pipe Valve
description: A differential clapper valve that holds back water in a dry-pipe system until air pressure drops upon sprinkler head activation.

name: Flow Switch
description: A sensor installed in piping that detects water movement and sends an alarm signal to the fire control panel.

name: Tamper Switch
description: A supervisory device mounted on isolation valves that alerts the control panel if a valve is moved from its normal open position.

name: Suppression System Riser Room
description: A dedicated room housing the main riser valve assembly, control valves, and fire pump for the suppression system.

name: Fire Suppression Piping Installation
description: The trade activity of cutting, threading, grooving, and hanging suppression system piping throughout the building structure.

name: Hydraulic Calculation and Design
description: The engineering activity of calculating pipe sizes, pressures, and flow rates to ensure adequate suppression coverage per NFPA standards.

name: Suppression System Commissioning and Testing
description: The inspection and acceptance-testing activity that verifies alarm functions, flow rates, and valve operation before building occupancy.

name: Suppression System Maintenance and Inspection
description: Periodic inspection, testing, and component replacement activities required to keep the system code-compliant over its service life.

name: Black Steel Pipe
description: Uncoated carbon steel pipe, the most common material used for wet-pipe and dry-pipe sprinkler distribution networks.

name: CPVC Pipe
description: Chlorinated polyvinyl chloride piping approved for use in residential and light-commercial wet-pipe sprinkler systems.

name: Clean Agent (FM-200 / Novec 1230)
description: Environmentally acceptable gaseous suppression agents that extinguish fire without leaving residue, used in data centers and archives.

name: Wet Chemical Suppression Agent
description: A potassium-based liquid agent used in kitchen hood systems that saponifies cooking grease to suppress flames.

name: Sprinkler Head Escutcheon Plate
description: A decorative trim ring that conceals the gap between the sprinkler head fitting and the finished ceiling surface.

name: IfcFireSuppressionTerminal
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowTerminal.

name: Machine Room
description: A dedicated room housing the lift drive machinery, control panels, and associated equipment, located at the top or base of the shaft.

name: Traction Drive Unit
description: The motor and gearbox assembly responsible for driving the hoist ropes or belt to move the lift car vertically.

name: Hydraulic Drive Unit
description: A pump and cylinder assembly used in hydraulic lifts to push the car upward using pressurised fluid.

name: Hoist Ropes / Belts
description: Steel wire ropes or flat steel belts that suspend and move the lift car and counterweight within the shaft.

name: Lift Control Panel
description: The electronic control system that manages call signals, car positioning, door operation, and safety interlocks.

name: Landing Doors
description: Fire-rated doors at each floor opening that provide safe access to the lift car and prevent shaft falls when the car is absent.

name: Car Doors
description: Automatic sliding or folding doors attached to the lift car that open and close in synchronisation with the landing doors.

name: Door Operator
description: The motorised mechanism mounted on the car that drives the opening and closing of the car and landing doors.

name: Safety Gear / Governor
description: A centrifugal speed governor and mechanical safety clamps that arrest the car on the guide rails if overspeed is detected.

name: Buffers
description: Energy-absorbing devices installed in the pit beneath the car and counterweight to cushion impact in the event of over-travel.

name: Lift Pit
description: The recessed area at the base of the shaft below the lowest landing that accommodates buffers, pit ladder, and maintenance access.

name: Passenger Lift
description: A standard lift variant designed and rated specifically for the vertical transport of people within a building.

name: Goods / Freight Lift
description: A heavy-duty lift variant engineered to transport large or heavy goods loads, often with reinforced car interiors and higher capacity ratings.

name: Service Lift (Dumbwaiter)
description: A small lift variant used to move food, laundry, or other items between floors without carrying passengers.

name: Bed / Stretcher Lift
description: An oversized lift variant with extended car dimensions designed to accommodate hospital beds or stretchers in healthcare buildings.

name: Home Lift (Residential Lift)
description: A compact low-speed lift variant intended for private residential use, often with reduced shaft and pit requirements.

name: Machine-Room-Less (MRL) Lift
description: A traction lift variant where the drive machinery is located within the shaft or at the landing, eliminating the need for a separate machine room.

name: Panoramic / Glass Lift
description: A lift variant featuring glass car and/or shaft walls to provide scenic views, typically installed in atria or feature lobbies.

name: Lift Pit Construction
description: The civil works activity of forming and waterproofing the reinforced concrete pit at the base of the lift shaft.

name: Shaft Construction
description: The structural activity of forming the lift shaft walls, openings, and lintel structure through each floor level.

name: Lift Commissioning
description: The testing, adjustment, and regulatory inspection activity carried out before a lift is handed over for operational use.

name: Lift Maintenance & Servicing
description: Periodic inspection, lubrication, adjustment, and parts-replacement activity required to keep the lift safe and operational throughout its service life.

name: Lift Modernisation / Refurbishment
description: The activity of upgrading or replacing ageing lift components, controls, or finishes to extend service life or improve performance.

name: Lift Lobby
description: The waiting area at each floor immediately in front of the landing doors where users call and board the lift.

name: Lift Core
description: The structural building core that groups one or more lift shafts together, often combined with stairs and service risers.

name: Escalator
description: A closely related motorised staircase system for continuous vertical passenger movement, often specified alongside lifts in multi-storey buildings.

name: Moving Walkway (Travelator)
description: A related horizontal or inclined conveyor system for passenger movement, commonly specified in tandem with lift systems in airports and large transit hubs.

name: IfcTransportElement
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcElement.

name: IfcSpace (Lift Shaft)
description: The IFC schema class used to define and bound the spatial volume of a lift shaft within a building model.

name: Smoke Detector
description: A sensing device that detects the presence of smoke particles in the air and triggers an alarm signal.

name: Heat Detector
description: A device that activates when ambient temperature rises above a set threshold or at an abnormal rate, indicating a fire condition.

name: Carbon Monoxide Detector
description: A sensor that monitors CO gas levels and alerts occupants to potentially life-threatening concentrations produced by combustion.

name: Manual Call Point
description: A wall-mounted break-glass or push-button device that allows occupants to manually trigger the fire alarm system.

name: Fire Alarm Control Panel
description: The central processing unit of the system that receives detector signals, manages zones, and initiates alarm and suppression outputs.

name: Annunciator Panel
description: A remote display panel that mirrors the fire alarm control panel status, showing alarm zones and fault conditions at a secondary location.

name: Notification Appliance
description: An output device such as a sounder, bell, or strobe light that alerts occupants and emergency responders to a fire event.

name: Sounder / Horn
description: An audible alarm device that emits a loud tone or pattern to warn building occupants of a detected fire condition.

name: Visual Alarm Device (Strobe)
description: A flashing light unit that provides visual fire warning for hearing-impaired occupants in compliance with accessibility codes.

name: Voice Evacuation System
description: A mass-notification sub-system that broadcasts pre-recorded or live voice instructions to guide occupants during evacuation.

name: Beam Smoke Detector
description: A projected-beam device that uses an infrared light path across a large open area to detect smoke obscuration.

name: Duct Smoke Detector
description: A detector installed inside HVAC ductwork to sense smoke in circulated air and initiate system shutdown to prevent smoke spread.

name: Flame Detector
description: An optical sensor that identifies the specific UV or IR radiation signatures of an open flame for rapid fire detection.

name: Aspirating Smoke Detection (ASD) System
description: A very early warning detection system that actively draws air samples through a pipe network to a central high-sensitivity detector unit.

name: Addressable Loop Wiring
description: A signalling cable circuit that individually identifies each device on the loop, enabling precise location reporting on the control panel.

name: Conventional Zone Wiring
description: A traditional wiring method that groups multiple detectors on a shared circuit, indicating alarms by zone rather than individual device.

name: Fire Alarm Wiring and Conduit
description: Fire-rated cabling and protective conduit used to interconnect all system devices and ensure circuit integrity during a fire event.

name: Backup Battery / Standby Power Supply
description: A rechargeable battery or UPS unit that maintains system operation for a code-required duration during a mains power failure.

name: Relay Module / Interface Module
description: An ancillary device that allows the fire alarm system to control or monitor third-party building systems such as elevators and dampers.

name: Fire Alarm System Installation
description: The trade activity encompassing mounting, wiring, and connecting all fire detection and alarm devices throughout the building.

name: Fire Alarm System Commissioning and Testing
description: The process of verifying, calibrating, and certifying that all system components operate correctly in accordance with design specifications and codes.

name: Fire Alarm System Maintenance and Inspection
description: Scheduled periodic testing and servicing of detectors, panels, and notification appliances to ensure ongoing operational reliability.

name: Fire Alarm Zone Planning
description: The design activity of dividing the building into logical alarm zones that correspond to floor plates, compartments, or evacuation areas.

name: Fire Suppression System Integration
description: The interfacing of the fire alarm control panel with sprinkler, gaseous, or other suppression systems to enable automatic activation upon alarm.

name: Building Management System (BMS) Integration
description: The data link between the fire alarm control panel and the BMS to coordinate HVAC shutdown, elevator recall, and door release on alarm.

name: Fire Alarm Riser Room / Panel Room
description: A dedicated or shared room housing the main fire alarm control panel, repeater panels, and associated power supplies.

name: Fire Command Centre
description: A dedicated room, typically at the building entry level, where fire department personnel can monitor and control the entire fire alarm system.

name: IFC Fire Alarm Device (IfcFireSuppressionTerminal)
description: The IFC schema class used to model fire alarm and detection terminal devices within a Building Information Model.

name: IFC Alarm (IfcAlarm)
description: The IFC schema class representing notification appliances and alarm output devices within a BIM authoring environment.

name: Central BMS Controller
description: The core hardware/software unit that aggregates data and sends commands across all building subsystems.

name: BMS Operator Workstation
description: A dedicated computer terminal used by facility managers to monitor, configure, and control the BMS in real time.

name: Field Control Panel
description: A distributed panel housing local controllers and I/O modules that interface directly with building equipment on each floor or zone.

name: BMS Communication Network
description: The wired or wireless network infrastructure (e.g., BACnet, Modbus, LonWorks) that connects all BMS devices and subsystems.

name: Sensors and Transmitters
description: Devices such as temperature, humidity, CO₂, occupancy, and pressure sensors that feed real-time data into the BMS.

name: Actuators and Damper Drives
description: Electromechanical devices that execute BMS commands by physically adjusting valves, dampers, and switches in HVAC and other systems.

name: Human–Machine Interface (HMI)
description: Touchscreen panels or graphical displays mounted locally that allow on-site operators to view system status and make adjustments.

name: Data Historian Server
description: A server that stores time-series operational data from all connected subsystems for trend analysis, reporting, and auditing.

name: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) for BMS
description: A dedicated power backup unit ensuring continuous BMS operation during mains power outages.

name: BMS Gateway / Protocol Converter
description: A device that translates between different communication protocols, enabling interoperability among disparate building subsystems.

name: HVAC Control System
description: The subsystem of the BMS that monitors and controls heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning equipment for comfort and energy efficiency.

name: Lighting Control System
description: A BMS-integrated subsystem managing automated switching, dimming, and scheduling of lighting throughout the building.

name: Access Control and Security System
description: A subsystem integrated with the BMS that manages entry/exit permissions, CCTV, and intrusion detection.

name: Fire Alarm and Life Safety System
description: A safety-critical subsystem connected to the BMS that monitors fire detectors and triggers alarms, sprinklers, and evacuation protocols.

name: Energy Metering and Management System
description: A subsystem that collects electricity, gas, and water consumption data to enable energy benchmarking and demand management.

name: Elevator and Escalator Control System
description: A subsystem integrated with the BMS to monitor vertical transportation equipment status, faults, and usage patterns.

name: Plumbing and Water Management System
description: A subsystem tracking domestic hot/cold water, leak detection, and pump operation within the BMS framework.

name: Renewable Energy Integration System
description: A BMS subsystem that monitors and optimises the output of on-site solar, wind, or battery storage assets.

name: BMS Control Room
description: A dedicated room housing the central BMS controllers, servers, operator workstations, and associated network equipment.

name: Server / Data Room
description: A climate-controlled space accommodating BMS data historian servers, gateways, and communication racks.

name: Field Equipment Room / MER
description: Mechanical and electrical rooms on each floor where field control panels and local BMS equipment are housed.

name: Network Cabling (BMS)
description: Structured cabling—including twisted-pair, coaxial, or fibre-optic cables—used to interconnect BMS components throughout the building.

name: Conduit and Cable Tray (BMS)
description: Protective conduit and tray systems that route and safeguard BMS signal and power cabling within the building fabric.

name: BMS System Design and Engineering
description: The professional activity of specifying BMS architecture, point schedules, sequences of operation, and network topology during design.

name: BMS Installation and Commissioning
description: Site activities covering the physical installation of controllers, sensors, and cabling, followed by functional testing and commissioning.

name: BMS Integration and System Testing
description: The process of connecting all subsystems to the BMS and verifying end-to-end communication, control logic, and interoperability.

name: BMS Operator Training
description: Structured training sessions that prepare facility management staff to operate, troubleshoot, and configure the BMS effectively.

name: Preventive Maintenance of BMS
description: Scheduled inspection, calibration, and servicing of BMS hardware and software to ensure continued reliable performance.

name: BMS Upgrade and Retrofitting
description: The activity of replacing or updating ageing BMS hardware, software, or communication protocols in an existing building.

name: Energy Auditing via BMS
description: The analytical activity of reviewing BMS-logged data to identify energy waste, optimise set-points, and produce compliance reports.

name: IfcBuildingSystem
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcSystem.

name: IfcController
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcDistributionControlElement.

name: IfcSensor
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcDistributionControlElement.

name: IfcActuator
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcDistributionControlElement.

name: IfcCommunicationsAppliance
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowTerminal.

name: Catch Basin
description: A surface inlet structure that collects rainwater runoff from paved areas and directs it into the underground drainage network.

name: Storm Drain Pipe
description: Underground piping that conveys collected stormwater from inlets and catch basins to discharge points or detention facilities.

name: Drainage Inlet Grate
description: A metal or polymer grate covering a catch basin or trench drain opening to prevent debris entry while allowing water flow.

name: Trench Drain
description: A linear channel drain installed flush with a surface to intercept sheet flow across driveways, plazas, or building entries.

name: Detention Basin
description: An engineered surface or subsurface basin that temporarily holds peak stormwater volumes to reduce downstream flooding.

name: Retention Pond
description: A permanent water-holding basin designed to retain stormwater long-term for gradual infiltration, evaporation, or reuse.

name: Underground Detention Tank
description: A buried modular or pre-cast tank system that stores stormwater beneath a site for controlled release or reuse.

name: Stormwater Manhole
description: An access chamber within the drainage network that allows inspection, cleaning, and connection of storm drain pipes.

name: Outlet Control Structure
description: A hydraulic structure at the outlet of a detention or retention facility that regulates the rate of stormwater discharge.

name: Headwall
description: A concrete or masonry wall at the end of a culvert or pipe outlet that stabilizes the pipe, prevents erosion, and controls flow.

name: Culvert
description: A transverse pipe or box structure that allows stormwater to pass beneath a road, driveway, or embankment.

name: Riprap Apron
description: A layer of loose stone placed at pipe outlets or channel transitions to dissipate energy and protect against scour erosion.

name: Bioretention Cell
description: A shallow landscaped depression filled with engineered soil and plants that filters and infiltrates stormwater runoff.

name: Permeable Pavement
description: A porous paving material—such as pervious concrete or permeable interlocking pavers—that allows rainwater to infiltrate through its surface.

name: Filter Fabric / Geotextile
description: A permeable textile membrane installed around drainage aggregates or pipes to prevent fine soil migration while allowing water passage.

name: Drainage Aggregate
description: Clean crushed stone or gravel used as a free-draining bedding or filter medium around pipes and in infiltration systems.

name: HDPE Corrugated Pipe
description: High-density polyethylene corrugated pipe commonly used for flexible, lightweight storm sewer conveyance.

name: Precast Concrete Pipe
description: Factory-manufactured reinforced concrete pipe segments used for high-load storm drainage applications.

name: Downspout / Rainwater Leader
description: A vertical pipe that conveys roof rainwater from gutters or roof drains down to grade-level drainage connections.

name: French Drain
description: A subsurface trench filled with gravel and a perforated pipe that intercepts and redirects groundwater or surface infiltration.

name: Swale
description: A shallow, vegetated open channel graded to convey, slow, and partially infiltrate stormwater runoff across a site.

name: Rain Garden
description: A planted shallow depression designed to capture and absorb roof or surface runoff, reducing peak flow and improving water quality.

name: Infiltration Trench
description: A subsurface excavated trench filled with aggregate that temporarily stores runoff and promotes infiltration into native soil.

name: Stormwater Pump Station
description: A mechanical system comprising pumps, wet wells, and controls that lifts stormwater where gravity drainage is not achievable.

name: Water Quality Treatment System
description: A system such as hydrodynamic separators or media filters that removes sediment, oils, and pollutants from stormwater before discharge.

name: Site Grading & Earthworks
description: The civil earthmoving activity that establishes ground slopes and landforms to direct surface runoff toward drainage features.

name: Storm Drain Pipe Installation
description: The construction activity of excavating trenches, bedding, laying, jointing, and backfilling underground storm sewer pipes.

name: Catch Basin Construction
description: The activity of forming or placing precast catch basin structures, setting frames and grates, and connecting lateral pipes.

name: Detention/Retention Basin Construction
description: Earthwork and liner placement activity to excavate, shape, compact, and waterproof stormwater storage basins.

name: Erosion & Sediment Control
description: Temporary construction-phase measures—such as silt fencing and sediment basins—to prevent stormwater from transporting disturbed soil.

name: CCTV Drainage Inspection
description: The post-installation or maintenance activity of using camera equipment to inspect the interior condition of buried storm drain pipes.

name: Drainage System Commissioning
description: The testing and verification activity that confirms designed flow capacities, connections, and outlet controls perform to specification.

name: Hydraulic Flushing & Cleaning
description: Routine maintenance activity using high-pressure water jetting to remove sediment and debris from storm drain pipes and structures.

name: Soil Stack
description: A vertical pipe that carries waste from toilets and urinals down to the building drain.

name: Waste Stack
description: A vertical pipe that conveys grey water waste from sinks, baths, and showers to the building drain.

name: Branch Drain
description: A horizontal pipe connecting individual sanitary fixtures to the main soil or waste stack.

name: Building Drain
description: The lowest horizontal piping inside a building that collects all drainage and conveys it to the building sewer.

name: Building Sewer
description: The pipe extending from the building drain to the public sewer or private disposal system outside the structure.

name: P-Trap
description: A U-shaped fitting beneath a fixture that retains a water seal to prevent sewer gases from entering the building.

name: S-Trap
description: An S-shaped trap fitting used in specific configurations to maintain a water seal on fixture outlets.

name: Bottle Trap
description: A compact trap with a removable bottle-shaped body, commonly used under basins where space is limited.

name: Grease Trap / Interceptor
description: A device installed in kitchen drainage lines to capture fats, oils, and greases before they enter the sewer.

name: Sediment Interceptor
description: An interceptor that captures sand, grit, and heavy solids from drainage flows in workshops or garages.

name: Inspection Chamber
description: An accessible chamber built at changes of direction or gradient to allow inspection and rodding of drain runs.

name: Manhole
description: A larger below-ground chamber providing access to major drain junctions for maintenance and blockage clearance.

name: Rodding Eye
description: A small access fitting at the end of a drain run that permits rodding equipment to be inserted for clearance.

name: Cleanout Plug
description: A removable plug in a fitting or pipe that provides access for cleaning or inspection of the drain interior.

name: Air Admittance Valve (AAV)
description: A one-way mechanical valve that admits air into the drainage system to equalise pressure without an open vent pipe.

name: Sewage Ejector Pump
description: A submersible pump unit that lifts wastewater from below-grade fixtures up to the gravity drain level.

name: Macerator Unit
description: An electrically driven device that grinds waste solids to allow discharge through small-bore pipework.

name: Drainage Pump Station (Sump)
description: A below-ground wet well with pumps and controls that collects and pumps wastewater where gravity drainage is not possible.

name: Single-Stack System
description: A drainage configuration in which soil and waste flows share one common stack without separate vent pipework.

name: Two-Pipe System
description: A drainage configuration that uses separate stacks for soil waste and grey water, each with independent venting.

name: Stub Stack System
description: A simplified drainage layout using a short unventilated stack serving a limited number of closely grouped fixtures.

name: Pressure Drain System (HDPE Siphonic)
description: A siphonic-action drainage system that uses full-bore pipe flow to achieve high-capacity roof or floor drainage.

name: Cast Iron Drain Pipe
description: Traditional cast-iron pipe material offering high durability and sound attenuation for above-ground drainage.

name: uPVC Drain Pipe
description: Unplasticised polyvinyl chloride pipe widely used for above- and below-ground sanitary drainage due to its light weight and corrosion resistance.

name: HDPE Drain Pipe
description: High-density polyethylene pipe used for drainage applications requiring flexibility, chemical resistance, and leak-free jointing.

name: Vitrified Clay Pipe
description: Fired clay pipe used predominantly for below-ground drains, prized for its chemical inertness and long service life.

name: Concrete Drain Pipe
description: Reinforced or plain concrete pipe used for large-diameter below-ground sewer runs and culverts.

name: Sanitary Drainage Installation
description: The site activity of laying, jointing, and fixing all drain pipes, fittings, and stacks in accordance with design drawings.

name: Drain Trenching and Bedding
description: Excavation of trenches and placement of granular bedding material to support and protect buried drain pipes.

name: Drain Testing (Air/Water)
description: Pre-handover testing of completed drain runs using air or water pressure to verify watertightness and joint integrity.

name: CCTV Drain Survey
description: Post-installation or maintenance inspection using a camera pushed through drain pipes to identify defects or blockages.

name: Drain Rodding / Jetting
description: Maintenance activity using rods or high-pressure water jets to clear blockages and debris from drain runs.

name: Drain Backfilling and Compaction
description: Systematic filling and compacting of material over bedded drain pipes to restore ground levels and prevent pipe damage.

name: Pipe Sleeve and Fire Stopping Installation
description: Fitting of sleeves and intumescent collars where drain pipes penetrate fire-rated walls or floors to maintain compartmentation.

name: Wastewater Treatment Plant
description: An on-site or off-site facility that receives, treats, and discharges or recycles building wastewater.

name: Septic Tank
description: An underground chamber providing primary settlement and anaerobic treatment of wastewater where mains sewer connection is unavailable.

name: Pump Room / Drainage Plant Room
description: A dedicated plant space housing sewage ejectors, sump pumps, and associated controls for sub-ground drainage systems.

name: Drainage Easement Zone
description: A legally protected strip of land within which building drain or sewer infrastructure is laid and must remain accessible.

name: Wet Room / Shower Room
description: A waterproofed room with integrated floor drainage designed to receive direct water discharge from showering or washing.

name: Storage Water Heater
description: A tank-based unit that heats and stores a volume of water ready for on-demand use throughout the building.

name: Tankless (Instantaneous) Water Heater
description: A flow-through heating unit that heats water on demand without storing it, providing continuous supply at reduced standby energy loss.

name: Heat Pump Water Heater
description: An energy-efficient unit that extracts heat from ambient air to heat domestic water rather than generating heat directly.

name: Solar Water Heater
description: A system using roof-mounted solar collectors to capture solar energy and pre-heat or fully heat domestic water.

name: Boiler (Domestic Hot Water)
description: A fuel-fired or electric boiler dedicated to or combined with space heating that supplies hot water to the distribution network.

name: Pressure Relief Valve (PRV)
description: A safety valve that automatically releases water when system pressure exceeds a safe threshold, preventing rupture or explosion.

name: Tempering / Thermostatic Mixing Valve (TMV)
description: A valve that blends hot and cold water to deliver a safe, scalding-prevention outlet temperature to fixtures.

name: Circulation Pump
description: A pump that continuously or periodically recirculates hot water through the distribution loop to minimise wait time at fixtures.

name: Hot Water Recirculation Loop
description: A dedicated return pipe circuit that keeps hot water moving through the building so it is instantly available at all draw-off points.

name: Hot Water Distribution Pipework
description: The network of insulated supply pipes that carry heated water from the heater or boiler to individual fixtures and appliances.

name: Pipe Insulation (Hot Water)
description: Thermal wrap or tube insulation applied to hot water pipes to minimise heat loss and maintain delivery temperature.

name: Cross-Linked Polyethylene (PEX) Pipe
description: A flexible plastic pipe material commonly used in hot water systems for its corrosion resistance and ease of installation.

name: Water Softener / Conditioner
description: A pre-treatment device that removes hardness minerals to protect heater elements, tanks, and pipework from limescale build-up.

name: Anode Rod
description: A sacrificial magnesium or aluminium rod inside a storage tank that corrodes preferentially to protect the tank lining from rust.

name: Hot Water Storage Tank
description: An insulated vessel used to store large volumes of pre-heated water, often paired with solar or heat pump systems.

name: Indirect Water Heater (Coil-in-Tank)
description: A storage vessel that heats domestic water via an internal coil carrying hot water or steam from a primary heating boiler.

name: Point-of-Use Water Heater
description: A small, localised heater installed directly at a single fixture to eliminate long pipe runs and reduce energy waste.

name: Check Valve (Hot Water)
description: A one-way valve that prevents backflow of hot water into the cold supply or between zones of the distribution system.

name: Gate / Ball Isolation Valve
description: Shut-off valves installed at strategic points to allow sections of the hot water system to be isolated for maintenance or repair.

name: Flow Meter
description: A metering device that measures volumetric flow rate through the hot water system for monitoring, billing, or balancing purposes.

name: Hot Water Zone Controller
description: An electronic or electromechanical control unit that manages hot water delivery to separate building zones based on demand or schedule.

name: Thermostat / Temperature Controller
description: A sensing and control device that maintains the storage or delivery temperature within programmed set-points for comfort and safety.

name: Flue / Exhaust Vent (Water Heater)
description: A duct or flue pipe that safely conveys combustion gases from gas or oil water heaters to the outside atmosphere.

name: Gas Supply Line (Water Heater)
description: The dedicated gas pipe and fittings that deliver natural gas or LPG fuel to a gas-fired water heating appliance.

name: Electrical Supply & Wiring (Water Heater)
description: Dedicated electrical circuits, breakers, and wiring that power electric resistance or heat pump water heating units.

name: Drain Pan & Floor Drain
description: A containment pan placed beneath the water heater to collect leaks and direct water to a floor drain, limiting water damage.

name: Plant Room / Mechanical Room
description: A dedicated building space that houses water heaters, boilers, pumps, and associated equipment in a secure and accessible location.

name: Roof Space / Plant Deck (Solar Collectors)
description: The roof area or elevated deck allocated for mounting solar thermal collector panels that feed the hot water system.

name: Hot Water System Installation
description: The construction activity of positioning, connecting, and commissioning all heaters, tanks, pipework, and controls that make up the hot water system.

name: Pipework Pressure Testing
description: A quality-assurance activity in which completed pipe runs are pressurised with water or air to verify leak-free joints before covering.

name: Hot Water System Commissioning
description: The systematic testing, balancing, and verification of the complete hot water system to confirm it meets design performance and safety standards.

name: Legionella Risk Assessment & Control
description: A regulatory compliance activity involving temperature checks, flushing, and treatment to prevent Legionella bacteria growth in hot water systems.

name: Water Heater Servicing & Maintenance
description: Periodic inspection, anode rod replacement, descaling, and safety-valve testing to maintain heater performance and extend service life.

name: Hot Water System Decommissioning
description: The controlled activity of draining, disconnecting, and safely removing water heating equipment and pipework at end of life or during major refurbishment.

name: IfcTank
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowStorageDevice.

name: Gas Meter
description: Measures the volume of gas consumed by the building or individual units.

name: Gas Pressure Regulator
description: Reduces and stabilizes the incoming gas pressure to a safe operating level for building appliances.

name: Gas Shutoff Valve
description: Manual or automatic valve used to isolate gas flow to the entire building or specific zones.

name: Gas Distribution Piping
description: Network of pipes that routes gas from the meter to all appliances and end-use points within the building.

name: Gas Riser Pipe
description: Vertical pipe segment that carries gas between floors in multi-story buildings.

name: Gas Flex Connector
description: Short flexible hose connecting a rigid gas pipe to an appliance, allowing minor movement and vibration absorption.

name: Gas Leak Detection Sensor
description: Electronic sensor that detects the presence of combustible gas and triggers an alarm or automatic shutoff.

name: Automatic Gas Shutoff Device (Seismic)
description: Safety device that automatically closes the gas supply line when seismic activity above a threshold is detected.

name: Gas Pressure Relief Valve
description: Safety valve that releases excess gas pressure to prevent pipe or equipment damage.

name: Natural Gas Service Connection
description: The utility-provided lateral line connecting the street main to the building's gas meter.

name: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) System
description: Alternative gas supply system using stored propane or butane cylinders or tanks instead of a utility mains connection.

name: Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Storage System
description: On-site high-pressure CNG storage and delivery infrastructure used where pipeline gas is unavailable.

name: Gas Booster System
description: Mechanical system that increases low-inlet gas pressure to meet the demand requirements of high-load appliances.

name: Combined Gas & Electricity Metering Room
description: Dedicated room or enclosure housing gas and electrical meters with required ventilation and access provisions.

name: Gas Meter Cupboard / Enclosure
description: Ventilated cabinet or recess that safely houses the gas meter and associated valves, typically at the building entry.

name: LPG Bottle Store
description: Designated outdoor or semi-open area for the secure storage of LPG cylinders meeting fire and safety codes.

name: Gas Pipe Sleeve / Duct Seal
description: Fire-rated or gas-tight sleeving material used where gas pipes penetrate walls, floors, or fire compartment boundaries.

name: Steel Gas Pipe (Black Iron)
description: Traditional threaded black steel pipe used for interior gas distribution due to its strength and durability.

name: Copper Gas Pipe
description: Copper tubing approved for gas service in many jurisdictions, valued for corrosion resistance and ease of installation.

name: Polyethylene (PE) Gas Pipe
description: Flexible plastic pipe used for underground gas distribution, resistant to corrosion and approved for buried service.

name: CSST (Corrugated Stainless Steel Tubing)
description: Flexible stainless steel tubing system used for interior gas distribution, allowing faster installation than rigid pipe.

name: Gas Pipe Joint Sealant / Thread Tape
description: Gas-rated sealant or PTFE tape applied to threaded pipe joints to ensure a leak-free connection.

name: Gas Service Installation
description: The initial work of connecting the building to the utility gas main, including excavation, pipe laying, and meter installation.

name: Gas Pipework Rough-In
description: Installation of all interior gas distribution piping within walls, floors, and ceilings before finishes are applied.

name: Gas System Pressure Testing
description: Pressurizing the completed gas pipework with inert gas or air to verify there are no leaks before commissioning.

name: Gas System Commissioning & Purging
description: Controlled introduction of live gas into the system and purging of air to bring the system into safe operational service.

name: Gas Appliance Connection & Testing
description: Final connection of gas appliances (boilers, cookers, heaters) to the distribution system with functional safety checks.

name: Gas System Inspection & Certification
description: Formal inspection by a certified gas engineer to verify code compliance and issue a safety certificate before occupancy.

name: Gas Pipe Trenching & Backfilling
description: Excavation of trenches for underground gas pipe installation and subsequent reinstatement of the ground surface.

name: Periodic Gas Safety Check
description: Scheduled maintenance inspection of all gas installations, appliances, and detectors to ensure ongoing safe operation.

name: IfcDistributionSystem (Gas)
description: IFC classification representing the logical gas distribution system entity within a building information model.

name: IfcFlowSegment (Gas Pipe)
description: IFC class representing a straight segment of gas pipe as a flow distribution element in a BIM model.

name: IfcValve (Gas)
description: IFC class used to model gas shutoff, pressure relief, and control valves within the gas distribution network.

name: IfcFlowMeter (Gas)
description: IFC class representing the gas meter device that measures consumption within the building model.

name: IfcSensor (Gas Detector)
description: IFC class representing gas leak detection sensors modelled as sensing devices in the building system.

name: Air Compressor Unit
description: The primary mechanical unit that compresses atmospheric air to a higher pressure for distribution throughout the building system.

name: Receiver Tank / Air Reservoir
description: A pressure vessel that stores compressed air to buffer demand fluctuations and stabilise system pressure.

name: Pressure Relief Valve
description: A safety valve that automatically releases excess pressure to prevent over-pressurisation and potential vessel failure.

name: Air Dryer Unit
description: A refrigerant or desiccant-based device that removes moisture from compressed air to protect downstream equipment and processes.

name: Coalescing Filter / Oil-Water Separator
description: A filtration device that removes oil aerosols, water droplets, and particulates from the compressed air stream.

name: Pressure Regulator / Pressure Reducing Valve
description: A control valve that reduces and maintains compressed air at a set downstream pressure for specific end-use requirements.

name: Distribution Piping Network
description: The network of pipes (typically steel, copper, or aluminium) that conveys compressed air from the compressor room to point-of-use outlets.

name: Compressed Air Outlet / Service Point
description: A wall- or floor-mounted coupling point where tools and equipment connect to draw compressed air.

name: Isolation Valve
description: A manually or automatically operated valve used to isolate sections of the distribution network for maintenance or emergency shut-off.

name: Condensate Drain / Auto-Drain Valve
description: A device that automatically removes accumulated liquid condensate from the receiver tank, filters, and dryer units.

name: Pressure Gauge / Monitoring Instrument
description: An instrument that measures and displays the real-time pressure at key points within the compressed air system.

name: Check Valve / Non-Return Valve
description: A one-directional valve that prevents backflow of compressed air towards the compressor or between system zones.

name: Aftercooler
description: A heat exchanger positioned immediately after the compressor that cools the hot discharge air and causes initial moisture condensation.

name: Compressor Control Panel / BMS Interface
description: The electrical control panel that governs compressor start/stop, load/unload cycles, and interfaces with the Building Management System.

name: Compressor Room / Plant Room
description: A dedicated, ventilated mechanical room housing the compressor unit, receiver tank, dryer, and associated ancillary equipment.

name: Instrument Air Sub-System
description: A high-purity, oil-free compressed air sub-system dedicated to powering pneumatic instrumentation and control devices.

name: Breathing Air Sub-System
description: A specialised, medically-grade compressed air sub-system that supplies clean breathable air for respiratory protection or medical use.

name: Pneumatic Controls & Actuators Network
description: The integrated set of pneumatic actuators, positioners, and solenoid valves that use compressed air to operate HVAC dampers, valves, and other building controls.

name: Condensate Drainage System
description: The pipework and collection infrastructure that safely conveys oil-contaminated condensate from the compressed air system to an appropriate disposal point.

name: Pipe Insulation (Compressed Air Lines)
description: Thermal insulation material applied to compressed air distribution pipes to minimise energy losses and prevent surface condensation.

name: Pipe Fittings & Couplings (Compressed Air)
description: Specialised high-pressure-rated connectors, elbows, tees, and quick-release couplings used throughout the compressed air distribution network.

name: Gaskets & Seals (Compressed Air)
description: Pressure-rated sealing materials installed at flanged joints and connections to ensure leak-free compressed air containment.

name: Compressed Air System Installation
description: The trade activity encompassing the mechanical installation of all compressor, receiver, dryer, filter, and pipework components.

name: Pressure Testing & Commissioning
description: The process of hydrostatic or pneumatic pressure testing and functional commissioning of the completed compressed air system prior to handover.

name: Compressor Servicing & Overhaul
description: Routine and periodic maintenance of the compressor unit including oil changes, filter replacements, belt inspections, and valve servicing.

name: Condensate Disposal & Treatment
description: The environmental compliance activity of treating oil-contaminated condensate before it is discharged to the drainage system.

name: Energy Audit (Compressed Air)
description: A systematic assessment of compressed air system energy consumption, leak rates, and operational efficiency to identify improvement opportunities.

name: Pipe Support & Hanger Installation
description: The structural fixing activity of installing brackets, hangers, and supports to secure compressed air pipework at correct gradients and spacing.

name: Access Control Panel
description: The central hardware unit that manages and processes access permissions for entry points throughout the building.

name: Card Reader / Credential Reader
description: A device mounted at entry points that reads keycards, fobs, or smart credentials to authenticate users.

name: Biometric Scanner
description: A sensor-based device that verifies identity through fingerprint, retina, facial recognition, or other biological traits.

name: Electric Door Strike
description: An electrically operated locking mechanism installed in door frames that releases upon receiving an authorized signal.

name: Electromagnetic Lock (Magloc)
description: A locking device using electromagnetic force to secure doors, disengaging when power is cut or access is granted.

name: Electronic Deadbolt
description: A motorized deadbolt lock controlled by electronic signals from an access control system or keypad.

name: Door Position Sensor
description: A magnetic or mechanical sensor that monitors whether a door is open or closed and reports status to the control panel.

name: Request-to-Exit (REX) Sensor
description: A passive infrared or push-button device that signals the access control system to unlock a door for egress.

name: Keypad / PIN Entry Terminal
description: A numeric or alphanumeric input device allowing users to authenticate by entering a personal identification number.

name: Video Surveillance Camera (CCTV)
description: A fixed or PTZ camera that continuously records or streams video footage for security monitoring purposes.

name: IP Network Video Recorder (NVR)
description: A networked device that captures, stores, and manages digital video streams from IP cameras.

name: Digital Video Recorder (DVR)
description: A standalone recording unit that stores analog camera footage onto a local hard drive for later retrieval.

name: Video Management Software (VMS)
description: Software platform used to manage, view, record, and analyze video feeds from multiple surveillance cameras.

name: Intrusion Detection System (IDS)
description: A networked set of sensors and alarms designed to detect unauthorized entry or movement within secured areas.

name: Motion Detector / PIR Sensor
description: A passive infrared sensor that detects movement within a defined area and triggers an alarm or notification.

name: Glass Break Detector
description: An acoustic sensor that identifies the specific frequency of shattering glass to trigger an intrusion alert.

name: Vibration Sensor
description: A device attached to walls, windows, or safes that detects physical impact or tampering attempts.

name: Perimeter Beam Sensor
description: An active infrared or microwave sensor that creates an invisible detection beam across an entry or boundary.

name: Alarm Control Unit
description: The central hub that receives signals from intrusion detectors and coordinates alarm outputs and notifications.

name: Siren / Audible Alarm Device
description: An acoustic warning device that emits a loud alert sound when an intrusion or security event is detected.

name: Strobe / Visual Alarm Indicator
description: A flashing light device that provides a visible warning signal during a security or fire alarm event.

name: Intercom System
description: A two-way audio (and optionally video) communication system used to verify visitor identity before granting access.

name: Video Door Phone / Video Intercom Unit
description: A combined camera and speaker/microphone unit at an entry door enabling visual and audio visitor verification.

name: Turnstile / Speed Gate
description: A mechanical or optical barrier installed at controlled entry points to allow only one person through per authentication.

name: Mantrap / Airlock Vestibule
description: A secure double-door entry space that traps individuals between two locked doors until identity is fully verified.

name: Security Control Room
description: A dedicated room housing monitoring stations, recording equipment, and communication tools for security personnel.

name: Server Room / Access Control Head-End Room
description: A secured equipment room containing access control servers, network infrastructure, and power supplies for the system.

name: Guard Booth / Security Kiosk
description: A staffed or unstaffed physical enclosure at building entry points used to screen and control visitor access.

name: Credential Management Software
description: A software platform used to issue, revoke, and manage user credentials, access levels, and audit trails.

name: Identity Management / Directory Integration
description: Integration layer connecting the access control system with HR or IT directories (e.g., Active Directory) for user lifecycle management.

name: Visitor Management System
description: A digital system for registering, tracking, and issuing temporary credentials to building visitors.

name: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) for Security
description: A battery backup unit ensuring continuous operation of access control and alarm equipment during power outages.

name: Security Cabling and Conduit
description: Dedicated wiring infrastructure (data, power, and signal cables) routed through protective conduit for security devices.

name: Tamper-Resistant Enclosure / Back Box
description: A hardened housing protecting security device electronics and wiring connections from physical interference.

name: Security Glazing / Ballistic Glass
description: Reinforced or laminated glass used in high-security areas to resist forced entry, impact, or ballistic threats.

name: Installation of Access Control Devices
description: The physical mounting, wiring, and commissioning of readers, locks, panels, and associated hardware at designated entry points.

name: Security System Commissioning and Testing
description: The structured process of configuring, testing, and verifying all security system components against design specifications.

name: Cable Pulling and Termination for Security Systems
description: The trade activity of routing, pulling, and terminating signal and power cables for all security devices throughout the building.

name: Security System Integration with BMS
description: The process of linking the security system to the Building Management System for unified monitoring, reporting, and automation.

name: Penetration Testing and Security Audit
description: A formal assessment activity that evaluates vulnerabilities in the installed security system before or after building occupancy.

name: Licence Plate Recognition (LPR) System
description: An optical camera and software system that automatically reads vehicle registration plates to control car park or gate access.

name: Fence / Perimeter Intrusion Detection System (PIDS)
description: A sensor network attached to or buried near the site perimeter fence to detect climbing, cutting, or breaching attempts.

name: IfcSystem (Security)
description: The IFC class used to model and group security system components and their relationships within a BIM environment.

name: IfcDoor (Controlled Entry)
description: The IFC class representing a door element that is part of an access-controlled opening within the building model.

name: Structured Cabling System
description: The backbone physical wiring infrastructure that carries data and communications signals throughout the building, including horizontal and vertical cable runs.

name: Network Rack / Server Cabinet
description: Enclosed or open frame mounting structures housed in IT rooms that hold network switches, patch panels, servers, and associated equipment.

name: Patch Panel
description: A passive termination panel mounted in a rack that provides organised connection points between incoming cabling and active network equipment.

name: Network Switch
description: An active device that connects multiple devices on a LAN and directs data packets between them using MAC addresses.

name: Router
description: A device that forwards data packets between computer networks, typically managing the boundary between the internal network and the internet.

name: Firewall Appliance
description: A hardware or software security device that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predefined security rules.

name: Wireless Access Point (WAP)
description: A device that creates a wireless local area network (WLAN) by broadcasting Wi-Fi signals, typically ceiling- or wall-mounted throughout the building.

name: Cat6 / Cat6A UTP Cable
description: Unshielded twisted-pair copper cable conforming to Category 6 or 6A standards, used for high-speed Ethernet runs to workstations and devices.

name: Fibre Optic Cable
description: Glass or plastic fibre cable used for high-bandwidth, long-distance backbone links between telecommunications rooms and floors.

name: Conduit and Cable Tray
description: Protective metallic or PVC conduits and open trays used to route and support cabling through walls, ceilings, and risers.

name: Telecommunications Room (TR)
description: A dedicated room or enclosure on each floor housing network equipment, patch panels, and cable termination points serving that floor.

name: Main Distribution Frame (MDF) Room
description: The primary equipment room containing the building's core network gear, the main patch frame, and the demarcation point with external service providers.

name: Cable Penetration / Fire Stop
description: Sealed openings through fire-rated walls and floors through which cables pass, maintaining the building's fire compartmentation integrity.

name: Network Outlet / Data Socket
description: A wall- or floor-mounted RJ45 or fibre outlet at a workstation or device location, forming the user-facing end of the structured cabling system.

name: PoE (Power over Ethernet) Infrastructure
description: Network switches and cabling configured to deliver electrical power alongside data signals to devices such as IP phones, cameras, and access points.

name: IP Telephony System
description: A voice communications platform that transmits telephone calls over the data network using VoIP protocols, including handsets, PBX server, and call management software.

name: Building Management System (BMS) Network
description: A dedicated or segmented data network carrying control and monitoring signals for HVAC, lighting, access control, and other building services.

name: Distributed Antenna System (DAS)
description: A network of spatially separated antenna nodes connected to a common source that extends cellular and radio coverage throughout the building interior.

name: Network Cable Installation
description: The construction activity of pulling, terminating, and labelling copper and fibre cables between equipment rooms and outlet locations.

name: Conduit Installation
description: The activity of fixing conduit, trunking, and cable trays in position prior to cable pulling, including core drilling through structural elements.

name: Network Equipment Commissioning
description: The process of configuring, testing, and validating all active network devices — switches, routers, firewalls, and access points — to meet performance specifications.

name: Cable Testing and Certification
description: Systematic testing of every installed cable run with a certified tester to verify compliance with TIA/ISO cabling standards and to produce formal test records.

name: Fibre Splicing and Termination
description: The specialist activity of joining or terminating fibre optic cables using fusion splicing or mechanical connectors to achieve low-loss optical connections.

name: Network Infrastructure Design
description: The engineering activity of designing the logical and physical network topology, equipment schedules, cable routes, and IP address plans for the building.

name: IFC:IfcDistributionControlElement
description: The IFC class used to represent active distribution control and monitoring devices within building services networks, including data and communications equipment.

name: IFC:IfcCableCarrierSegment
description: The IFC class representing physical cable carrier elements such as conduit segments, cable trays, and trunking runs modelled in BIM.

name: IFC:IfcCableSegment
description: The IFC class used to model individual cable runs — copper or fibre — as geometric and semantic objects within a BIM model.

name: Internet Service Provider (ISP) Demarcation Point
description: The physical point of handover between the external service provider's network and the building's internal data infrastructure.

name: Network Monitoring System (NMS)
description: Software and hardware platform that continuously monitors the performance, availability, and health of all network devices and links within the building.

name: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) for Network
description: A dedicated battery-backed power unit protecting network equipment rooms from power outages or quality issues, ensuring continuous communications availability.

name: Air Terminal (Strike Rod)
description: A pointed or blunt metal rod mounted at the highest points of a structure to intercept lightning strikes and provide a preferred attachment point.

name: Roof Conductor Network
description: A grid or mesh of bare copper or aluminum conductors laid across the roof surface to collect and distribute lightning current from air terminals.

name: Down Conductor
description: A heavy-gauge conductor cable that routes the captured lightning current safely from the roof collection network down the exterior of the building to the grounding system.

name: Earth Termination System (Ground Electrode)
description: Buried copper rods, plates, or ring conductors that dissipate lightning energy safely into the earth and maintain a low-impedance ground path.

name: Equipotential Bonding Bar
description: A metallic bar at building entry points that bonds all incoming conductive services (pipes, cables, structural steel) to the lightning protection system to prevent dangerous potential differences.

name: Test Clamp / Inspection Joint
description: A detachable mechanical connector installed in the down conductor path to allow periodic resistance and continuity testing of the earth electrode without dismantling the full system.

name: Surge Protection Device (SPD)
description: A voltage-limiting device installed on electrical, data, and telecommunication lines to suppress transient overvoltages induced by nearby lightning strikes before they damage equipment.

name: Isolating Spark Gap
description: A controlled air-gap device that prevents low-level currents from flowing between bonded systems during normal operation but closes instantly during a high-voltage lightning event.

name: Lightning Protection Conductor (Bare Copper Tape)
description: Flat or round bare copper or aluminium tape used as the primary conductive medium for down conductors and roof bonding in accordance with IEC 62305 standards.

name: Earth Rod (Copper-Clad Steel)
description: A steel core rod with a copper cladding driven vertically into the ground to provide a durable, corrosion-resistant earth electrode contact with the soil.

name: Conductive Bonding Clamp
description: A purpose-made metal clamp used to make reliable, low-resistance mechanical and electrical connections between conductors, rods, and structural metalwork.

name: Lightning Protection Zone (LPZ) Planning
description: A zoning methodology that divides a building into protected volumes (LPZ 0–4) based on expected electromagnetic threat levels, guiding the placement of surge protection and shielding measures.

name: Rolling Sphere Method Zone
description: A design-defined protected volume around a structure determined by the rolling sphere methodology to confirm that air terminals fully intercept potential lightning attachment points.

name: Faraday Cage Mesh
description: A closed metallic grid cage formed by roof conductors, down conductors, and foundation electrodes that provides electromagnetic shielding and distributes lightning current evenly around a structure.

name: Early Streamer Emission (ESE) Terminal
description: An active air terminal that emits an upward leader streamer earlier than a passive rod, claimed to intercept lightning over a larger protection radius (subject to regional standard acceptance).

name: Catenary Wire System
description: A horizontal cable suspended between masts above a structure to protect large open areas such as fuel storage tanks or substations from direct lightning strikes.

name: Foundation Earth Electrode (Ring Earth)
description: A closed loop conductor embedded in or around a building's concrete foundation that acts as a primary earth electrode, exploiting the moisture retention of the concrete for low-resistance grounding.

name: Soil Treatment (Bentonite Backfill)
description: Hygroscopic bentonite clay or conductive concrete placed around earth electrodes in high-resistivity soils to lower ground resistance and ensure reliable current dissipation.

name: Lightning Risk Assessment
description: A systematic engineering evaluation per IEC 62305-2 that calculates the risk of lightning-related loss to a structure and determines whether a protection system is required and to what level.

name: Lightning Protection System Design
description: The engineering design process that selects protection level, positions air terminals, routes conductors, specifies earth electrodes, and integrates SPDs in accordance with applicable standards.

name: LPS Installation
description: The on-site construction and assembly of all lightning protection components including fixing conductors, driving earth rods, installing bonding bars, and fitting surge protection devices.

name: Earth Resistance Testing
description: Periodic field measurement of ground electrode impedance using fall-of-potential or clamp-on methods to confirm the earth termination system meets the required resistance threshold (typically ≤10 Ω).

name: LPS Inspection and Certification
description: A formal visual and electrical inspection carried out by a competent authority after installation and at scheduled intervals to verify compliance with IEC 62305 or local national standards and issue a certificate.

name: Bonding of Metallic Services
description: The site activity of electrically connecting all external metallic infrastructure—gas pipes, water mains, HVAC ductwork, structural steel—to the lightning protection equipotential network.

name: IfcLightningProtectionSystem
description: The IFC schema classification used to represent a lightning protection system as a building services element within an openBIM/IFC-compliant building information model.

name: IfcCableCarrierSegment (LPS Conductor)
description: An IFC class instance used to model individual down-conductor or roof-conductor segments as cable carrier elements within a federated BIM environment.

name: Earth Electrode
description: A conductive element buried in the ground that provides the primary electrical connection to earth potential.

name: Earthing Conductor
description: A protective conductor connecting exposed conductive parts or the main earthing terminal to the earth electrode.

name: Main Earthing Terminal (MET)
description: The central terminal or busbar where all earthing and bonding conductors are connected within an installation.

name: Main Protective Bonding Conductor
description: A conductor that bonds incoming metallic services (gas, water, oil pipes) to the main earthing terminal to equalise potential.

name: Supplementary Bonding Conductor
description: A local bonding conductor connecting simultaneously accessible conductive parts in special locations such as bathrooms to prevent dangerous potential differences.

name: Functional Earthing Conductor
description: A conductor provided specifically for the correct operation of electronic or IT equipment rather than purely for safety.

name: Lightning Protection Earth Electrode
description: A dedicated earth termination network that dissipates lightning strike current safely into the ground as part of a lightning protection system.

name: Earth Rod
description: A cylindrical metallic rod driven vertically into the ground to achieve a low-resistance earth connection.

name: Earth Plate
description: A flat metallic plate buried horizontally or vertically in the soil to provide a large surface area earth electrode.

name: Earth Mat / Grid Electrode
description: An interconnected network of buried conductors spread over an area to achieve very low earth resistance, typically used in substations.

name: Tape / Strip Earth Electrode
description: A flat copper or steel tape buried horizontally in the ground acting as a ring or radial earth electrode.

name: Chemical / Enhancing Earth Electrode
description: An earth electrode surrounded by conducting backfill or electrolytic compound to reduce soil resistivity and improve earthing performance.

name: Earth Continuity Conductor (ECC)
description: The protective conductor within a wiring system that provides a continuous low-impedance path for fault current back to the source.

name: TN-S Earthing System
description: An earthing arrangement where the neutral and protective conductors are separate throughout the entire installation from the supply source.

name: TN-C-S Earthing System (PME)
description: An earthing arrangement in which the neutral and protective functions are combined in a single PEN conductor up to the consumer's installation.

name: TT Earthing System
description: An earthing arrangement in which the installation earth is provided by a local independent earth electrode separate from the supply network earth.

name: IT Earthing System
description: An earthing arrangement where the supply is either isolated from earth or connected through a high impedance, used in hospitals and critical facilities.

name: Surge Protection Device (SPD) Earthing
description: The earthing arrangement dedicated to connecting surge protective devices to ground for effective transient overvoltage suppression.

name: Telecommunications / Signal Reference Earthing System
description: A low-impedance earthing network designed specifically for telecommunications and ICT equipment to minimise noise and interference.

name: Cathodic Protection System
description: An electrochemical system that uses impressed current or sacrificial anodes to prevent corrosion of buried or submerged metallic structures.

name: Earth Fault Loop Impedance Testing
description: A commissioning and maintenance activity that measures the impedance of the complete earth fault current path to verify protective device operation.

name: Earth Electrode Resistance Testing
description: A site testing activity using a fall-of-potential or clamp method to measure the resistance of an earth electrode to remote earth.

name: Continuity Testing of Protective Conductors
description: An electrical testing activity that verifies the continuous low-resistance connection of all protective and bonding conductors throughout the installation.

name: Soil Resistivity Survey
description: A geotechnical survey activity that measures the electrical resistivity of the soil to inform earth electrode design and placement.

name: Earthing System Installation
description: The construction activity of installing all earth electrodes, conductors, clamps, and terminals in accordance with design drawings and standards.

name: Bonding Conductor Installation
description: The activity of running, connecting, and securing main and supplementary bonding conductors to metallic services and structural elements.

name: Periodic Inspection and Testing of Earthing
description: A scheduled maintenance activity to inspect, test, and certify the integrity and effectiveness of the earthing and bonding installation.

name: Earthing Clamp / Connector
description: A mechanical fitting used to make a secure, low-resistance, and corrosion-resistant connection between conductors and electrodes or metallic services.

name: Exothermic Welding (Cadweld) Joint
description: A permanent molecular bond formed by an exothermic reaction, providing a highly reliable and maintenance-free connection between earthing conductors.

name: Inspection Pit / Access Chamber for Earth Electrode
description: A buried chamber that provides access to the earth electrode termination point for inspection, testing, and disconnection.

name: Earthing and Bonding Schedule / Drawing
