description: A technical document that records the layout, sizes, materials, and test results of all earthing and bonding conductors in an installation.

name: Copper Conductor (Earthing Grade)
description: High-conductivity annealed copper used as the standard material for earthing conductors due to its low resistivity and corrosion resistance.

name: Galvanised Steel Conductor / Rod
description: Steel earthing material with a zinc coating providing corrosion resistance, used for earth rods and tapes in less corrosive soil conditions.

name: Stainless Steel Earth Rod
description: An earth rod fabricated from stainless steel for superior corrosion resistance in aggressive or high-moisture soil environments.

name: Copper-Bonded Steel Earth Rod
description: A steel rod with a molecularly bonded copper outer layer combining the mechanical strength of steel with the corrosion resistance of copper.

name: Conducting Backfill / Bentonite
description: A low-resistivity material such as bentonite or carbon-based compound placed around earth electrodes to reduce contact resistance with the soil.

name: PVC / XLPE Green-Yellow Insulated Protective Conductor
description: An insulated cable identified by the green-and-yellow colour code used as a protective conductor within the installation wiring.

name: Switchroom / Electrical Plant Room
description: A dedicated room housing main switchgear and the main earthing terminal where primary earthing connections are made and managed.

name: Cable Basement / Undercroft
description: A below-ground space through which earthing conductors and cables are routed between the earth electrode and the electrical installation.

name: Emergency Luminaire
description: A self-contained or central-battery-fed light fitting that activates automatically upon mains power failure to illuminate escape routes.

name: Exit Sign Fitting
description: An illuminated or retro-reflective sign luminaire permanently indicating the direction of a designated fire exit.

name: Central Battery Unit
description: A centralised battery bank and charger assembly that supplies power to multiple emergency luminaires across a building zone.

name: Self-Contained Battery Pack
description: An individual rechargeable battery module housed within a single luminaire, providing autonomous backup power without a central source.

name: Maintained Emergency Luminaire
description: A luminaire that operates continuously under normal conditions and switches to battery backup during a power failure.

name: Non-Maintained Emergency Luminaire
description: A luminaire that remains off under normal conditions and illuminates only when the mains supply is interrupted.

name: Sustained Emergency Luminaire
description: A luminaire containing two lamp circuits — one for normal operation and one that activates exclusively during mains failure.

name: Addressable Emergency Lighting Controller
description: An intelligent control unit that monitors and manages individual luminaire status, test results, and fault reporting across the network.

name: Automatic Test Module
description: A device that periodically triggers self-testing of emergency luminaires and logs duration and functional test results automatically.

name: Emergency Lighting Distribution Board
description: A dedicated electrical panel that segregates and protects the final circuits feeding emergency luminaires from the general power supply.

name: Inhibit / Override Switch
description: A key-operated or electronic switch used to temporarily disable automatic activation of emergency lighting during maintenance or testing.

name: Wiring and Cable Management
description: Fire-resistant cables, conduits, and trunking used to route power and data to emergency luminaires while maintaining circuit integrity under fire conditions.

name: Photoluminescent Escape Route Marking
description: Glow-in-the-dark floor or wall strips that absorb ambient light and re-emit it to mark escape paths without electrical power.

name: Escape Route Space
description: A designated corridor, stairwell, or passageway that must achieve minimum maintained illuminance levels as defined by life-safety standards.

name: Open Area (Anti-Panic) Zone
description: A large interior space such as an atrium or assembly hall requiring anti-panic emergency lighting to allow safe movement toward exits.

name: High-Risk Task Area
description: A zone containing hazardous processes or equipment where a higher level of emergency illuminance is mandated to allow safe shutdown procedures.

name: Emergency Lighting Installation
description: The physical fixing, wiring, and commissioning of all emergency luminaires, signs, and associated equipment in accordance with design drawings and standards.

name: Emergency Lighting Commissioning and Testing
description: The structured verification process that confirms each luminaire achieves rated lux levels, rated battery duration, and correct automatic activation.

name: Emergency Lighting Periodic Inspection
description: Scheduled maintenance visits to perform functional tests, battery duration tests, and certificate updates as required by BS 5266 / NFPA 101 or equivalent.

name: Emergency Lighting Design and Lux Calculation
description: The engineering activity of producing photometric layouts and point-by-point calculations to confirm code-compliant illuminance on escape routes.

name: Central Battery System
description: A subsystem architecture in which a shared battery plant distributes low-voltage or extra-low-voltage power to all connected emergency luminaires.

name: Addressable Emergency Lighting System
description: A networked subsystem where each luminaire has a unique address, enabling remote monitoring, automated testing, and individual fault identification.

name: Fire Alarm Interface
description: The integration link between the fire detection and alarm system and the emergency lighting system, enabling coordinated activation or zone control.

name: Building Management System Integration
description: The connection of emergency lighting monitoring and reporting functions to the wider BMS for centralised building operations oversight.

name: IFC Emergency Lighting Fixture Class
description: The IfcLightFixture entity with PredefinedType EMERGENCYLIGHT, used to model and schedule emergency luminaires within an IFC-compliant BIM dataset.

name: Pressurisation Fan Unit
description: The dedicated fan that supplies pressurised air into a protected stairwell, lobby, or corridor to prevent smoke ingress.

name: Air Supply Ductwork
description: The network of ducts that distributes pressurised air from the fan unit to the protected zones within the building.

name: Supply Air Grilles & Diffusers
description: Terminal devices fitted within protected enclosures that discharge pressurised air in a controlled pattern.

name: Pressure Relief Damper
description: An automatic damper that opens to release excess air pressure and maintain the design differential pressure across a door or barrier.

name: Automatic Pressure Differential Sensor
description: A sensor that continuously monitors the pressure difference between the protected zone and adjacent areas and feeds data to the control panel.

name: Variable Speed Drive (VSD) Controller
description: An electronic drive that modulates fan speed in real time to maintain the required differential pressure under varying door-open/close conditions.

name: Pressurisation Control Panel
description: The dedicated panel that processes sensor inputs and commands the fan and relief dampers to achieve and hold the target pressure differential.

name: Activation Interface / Fire Alarm Interface
description: Hardwired or protocol-based link between the fire detection system and the pressurisation panel that triggers system activation on alarm.

name: Stairwell Pressurisation System
description: A sub-variant of pressurisation designed specifically to protect escape staircases from smoke contamination during a fire event.

name: Lobby / Corridor Pressurisation System
description: A sub-variant that pressurises fire-fighting or escape lobbies and corridors rather than staircases, maintaining tenable conditions for occupants and fire-fighters.

name: Firefighter Lift Shaft Pressurisation System
description: A dedicated system that pressurises the lift shaft and associated lobbies used by fire and rescue services to keep them smoke-free.

name: Single-Stage Pressurisation System
description: A simpler variant that operates at a single fixed fan output rather than modulating with differential-pressure feedback.

name: Multi-Stage / Modulating Pressurisation System
description: An advanced variant using staged or continuously variable fan output controlled by differential-pressure feedback to handle multiple simultaneous door openings.

name: Protected Stairwell (Smoke-Free)
description: The enclosed staircase enclosure that is the primary protected zone maintained at positive pressure for occupant evacuation.

name: Fire-Fighting Lobby
description: An anteroom adjacent to a stairwell or lift shaft that is maintained under positive pressure for fire-fighter access and smoke separation.

name: Plant Room / Fan Room
description: The dedicated mechanical room housing the pressurisation fan unit, associated ductwork connections, and control equipment.

name: Smoke Control Ductwork Penetration Sealing
description: Intumescent or fire-rated collars and sealants applied at all points where pressurisation ductwork penetrates fire-compartment walls or floors.

name: Fire-Rated Flexible Duct Connector
description: A short flexible section of fire-rated duct that isolates vibration between the rigid ductwork and the fan unit while maintaining integrity.

name: Thermal & Acoustic Duct Insulation
description: Fire-rated insulation wrap applied to supply ductwork to maintain air temperature, reduce condensation, and attenuate fan noise.

name: Commissioning & Pressure Testing
description: The formal site activity of measuring achieved pressure differentials and air-flow rates against the design specification and BS EN 12101-6 / local code requirements.

name: Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)
description: Pre-installation testing of the fan unit, controls, and sensors at the manufacturer's facility to verify performance before delivery.

name: Installation of Fan Unit & Ductwork
description: The mechanical installation trade activity covering positioning, fixing, and connecting all fan, duct, and terminal components.

name: Fire Alarm Integration & Cause-and-Effect Testing
description: The site activity of verifying that the correct fire alarm signals trigger pressurisation activation in accordance with the agreed cause-and-effect matrix.

name: Routine Maintenance & Inspection
description: Periodic operational activity involving inspection, sensor calibration, fan belt/bearing checks, and test activation to ensure continued compliance.

name: Smoke Control System
description: A closely related active fire safety system that manages smoke movement through extraction or ventilation and often interfaces with pressurisation to form a coordinated strategy.

name: Mechanical Ventilation & Air Conditioning (MVAC) System
description: The building's general ventilation system, which must be coordinated with pressurisation to avoid opposing pressure differentials during a fire mode.

name: Fire Suppression / Sprinkler System
description: An active fire protection system tracked separately but requiring coordinated activation sequencing with the pressurisation system.

name: Building Management System (BMS) Integration Point
description: The BMS interface node through which pressurisation system status, alarms, and data are monitored and logged centrally across the building.

name: Chiller Unit
description: The primary refrigeration machine that removes heat from water to produce chilled water for distribution.

name: Chilled Water Pump
description: Circulates chilled water from the chiller to air handling units and fan coil units throughout the building.

name: Condenser Water Pump
description: Circulates condenser water between the chiller and the cooling tower to reject heat.

name: Air Handling Unit
description: Conditions and distributes air using chilled water coils to cool and dehumidify building spaces.

name: Fan Coil Unit
description: A terminal device that uses chilled water coils and a fan to cool individual zones or rooms.

name: Condenser Water Piping
description: Pipework connecting the chiller condenser to the cooling tower for heat rejection.

name: Air Separator
description: Removes entrained air and gases from the chilled water loop to prevent cavitation and corrosion.

name: Chilled Water Buffer Tank
description: Provides thermal storage and hydraulic buffering to stabilize chiller operation and meet peak demand.

name: Variable Frequency Drive
description: Controls pump and chiller motor speeds to optimize energy efficiency under varying load conditions.

name: Chilled Water Control Valve
description: Modulates chilled water flow to terminal units to maintain desired space temperature setpoints.

name: Differential Pressure Sensor
description: Monitors pressure differential across the chilled water distribution loop for pump speed control.

name: Temperature Sensor
description: Measures supply and return water temperatures to monitor system performance and control sequences.

name: Chemical Treatment System
description: Doses corrosion inhibitors, biocides, and scale inhibitors into the chilled water loop to protect equipment.

name: Strainer / Y-Strainer
description: Filters debris and particulates from chilled water to protect pumps, valves, and heat exchangers.

name: Heat Exchanger (Plate & Frame)
description: Isolates primary and secondary chilled water loops to allow independent pressure and temperature control.

name: Chiller Plant Room
description: A dedicated mechanical room housing chillers, pumps, headers, and associated plant equipment.

name: Cooling Tower Roof Plant Area
description: Rooftop or external area designated for cooling tower installation with adequate airflow and drainage.

name: Refrigerant
description: The working fluid within the chiller's refrigeration cycle used to transfer heat from water to condenser.

name: Glycol / Antifreeze Mixture
description: Added to chilled water loops in cold climates to prevent freezing and protect system components.

name: Condenser Water Treatment Chemical
description: Specialised chemicals dosed into the open condenser water loop to control scale, corrosion, and microbial growth.

name: Air-Cooled Chilled Water System
description: A variant that uses air-cooled condensers instead of a cooling tower, eliminating the condenser water loop.

name: District Cooling Connection
description: An interface allowing a building to receive chilled water from an external district cooling network instead of on-site chillers.

name: Free Cooling System
description: Uses ambient outdoor temperatures or a dry cooler to provide cooling without mechanical refrigeration during favourable conditions.

name: Chiller Plant Installation
description: Procurement, rigging, and commissioning of chiller units within the mechanical plant room.

name: Chilled Water Pipework Installation
description: Fabrication, installation, pressure testing, and insulation of all chilled water distribution pipework.

name: Hydronic Balancing
description: Adjusting flow rates at each terminal and branch to achieve design water distribution throughout the system.

name: System Flushing and Cleaning
description: Pre-commissioning cleaning of pipework loops to remove flux, debris, and construction contaminants.

name: Refrigerant Charging and Leak Testing
description: Filling the chiller with the specified refrigerant charge and verifying system integrity under pressure.

name: Commissioning and Performance Testing
description: Verifying that the complete chilled water system meets design capacity, energy efficiency, and control sequence requirements.

name: Preventive Maintenance Programme
description: Scheduled inspections, filter replacements, chemical dosing checks, and equipment servicing to sustain system reliability.

name: IfcCoolingTower
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcEnergyConversionDevice.

name: IfcHeatExchanger
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcEnergyConversionDevice.

name: Hydraulic Pump
description: Converts mechanical energy into hydraulic pressure to drive fluid through the system.

name: Hydraulic Cylinder
description: Converts hydraulic pressure into linear mechanical force and motion.

name: Hydraulic Motor
description: Converts hydraulic fluid energy into rotary mechanical motion.

name: Hydraulic Reservoir / Tank
description: Stores hydraulic fluid and allows for fluid conditioning and heat dissipation.

name: Hydraulic Accumulator
description: Stores pressurised hydraulic fluid to provide supplemental flow and absorb pressure shocks.

name: Hydraulic Control Valve
description: Regulates the direction, pressure, and flow rate of hydraulic fluid within the circuit.

name: Directional Control Valve
description: Routes hydraulic fluid to different actuators or return lines as commanded.

name: Flow Control Valve
description: Regulates the rate of hydraulic fluid flow to control actuator speed.

name: Check Valve
description: Allows hydraulic fluid to flow in one direction only, preventing backflow.

name: Hydraulic Filter / Strainer
description: Removes contaminants and particulates from hydraulic fluid to protect system components.

name: Hydraulic Heat Exchanger / Cooler
description: Dissipates excess heat from hydraulic fluid to maintain optimal operating temperature.

name: Hydraulic Manifold
description: Distributes hydraulic fluid to multiple circuit branches from a single supply point.

name: Hydraulic Hose and Tubing
description: Flexible or rigid conduits that convey pressurised hydraulic fluid between components.

name: Hydraulic Fitting and Connector
description: Coupling hardware that joins hoses, tubes, and components in a leak-free manner.

name: Hydraulic Fluid / Oil
description: The pressurised working medium that transmits power and lubricates hydraulic components.

name: Hydraulic Seal and Gasket
description: Elastomeric or PTFE sealing elements that prevent fluid leakage at joints and actuators.

name: Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU)
description: Self-contained assembly combining pump, motor, reservoir, and controls as the central power source.

name: Hydraulic Piping Network
description: The complete network of pipes and hoses routing fluid throughout the building infrastructure.

name: Electro-Hydraulic System
description: A hybrid system combining electronic control with hydraulic actuation for precision operation.

name: Pneumatic System
description: A compressed-air-based power transmission system closely related to but distinct from hydraulic systems.

name: Hydraulic Elevator System
description: A building vertical-transport system that uses hydraulic cylinders to raise and lower elevator cars.

name: Hydraulic Plant Room
description: A dedicated room housing hydraulic power units, reservoirs, and associated control equipment.

name: Hydraulic Equipment Maintenance Zone
description: Designated clearance space around hydraulic machinery required for safe inspection and servicing.

name: Hydraulic System Installation
description: The construction activity of mounting, connecting, and commissioning hydraulic components on site.

name: Hydraulic Pipe Pressure Testing
description: Testing completed hydraulic pipework under elevated pressure to verify integrity and detect leaks.

name: Hydraulic Fluid Flushing
description: Circulating clean fluid through the system to remove debris and contamination before commissioning.

name: Hydraulic System Commissioning
description: Systematic start-up and verification of hydraulic system performance against design specifications.

name: Hydraulic System Maintenance
description: Scheduled inspection, fluid replacement, filter change, and component servicing to sustain system reliability.

name: IfcFlowController
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcDistributionFlowElement.

name: IfcFlowMovingDevice
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcDistributionFlowElement.

name: IfcFlowStorageDevice
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcDistributionFlowElement.

name: PV Panel / Solar Module
description: The core photovoltaic unit made up of solar cells that converts sunlight directly into DC electricity.

name: Monocrystalline Silicon Cell
description: High-efficiency single-crystal silicon wafer used as the light-absorbing semiconductor in premium PV modules.

name: Polycrystalline Silicon Cell
description: Multi-crystal silicon wafer offering a cost-effective alternative semiconductor material for PV modules.

name: Thin-Film PV Module
description: Lightweight, flexible PV module variant deposited in thin semiconductor layers (CdTe, CIGS, or amorphous silicon) onto a substrate.

name: Building-Integrated PV (BIPV) Panel
description: PV module designed to replace conventional building envelope elements such as roof tiles, façade cladding, or glazing.

name: Solar Inverter
description: Electrical device that converts DC power generated by PV panels into grid-compatible AC power.

name: String Inverter
description: Single centralised inverter that processes the DC output of a series-connected string of PV modules.

name: Microinverter
description: Module-level inverter attached to each individual PV panel to maximise energy harvest and enable panel-level monitoring.

name: Power Optimizer
description: DC-DC converter mounted per module to perform maximum power point tracking before feeding a string inverter.

name: Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)
description: Rechargeable battery bank and associated electronics that store surplus PV-generated electricity for later use.

name: Charge Controller
description: Regulates the voltage and current flowing from PV panels to the battery bank to prevent overcharging or deep discharge.

name: PV Mounting Structure / Racking System
description: Structural framework—roof-mounted, ground-mounted, or façade-attached—that securely positions PV modules at the correct tilt angle.

name: Ballasted Flat-Roof Mounting System
description: Non-penetrating racking system that uses ballast weights to anchor PV arrays on flat roofs without roof penetrations.

name: Ground-Mount PV Structure
description: Steel or aluminium frame system driven into the ground or set on concrete piers to support utility or commercial PV arrays at grade level.

name: Solar Tracking System
description: Motorised single- or dual-axis mechanism that rotates PV panels to follow the sun's path and maximise daily energy yield.

name: DC Combiner Box
description: Electrical enclosure that aggregates multiple PV string DC cables into a single output feed with overcurrent protection per string.

name: AC Distribution Board / PV Sub-Panel
description: Dedicated electrical panel that manages circuit protection and distribution of AC power from the inverter to the building grid connection.

name: Bi-Directional Utility Meter
description: Revenue-grade meter that records both energy imported from and exported to the utility grid, enabling net metering or feed-in tariff billing.

name: PV DC Cabling & Conduit
description: UV- and weather-resistant cables and conduit runs carrying high-voltage DC from panels to the inverter.

name: Rapid Shutdown Device (RSD)
description: Safety device required by electrical codes that de-energises PV conductors on the roof within seconds for first-responder safety.

name: Energy Monitoring System
description: Hardware and software platform that collects, displays, and logs real-time and historical PV generation and consumption data.

name: Grid Connection & Interconnection Equipment
description: Utility-side switchgear, isolation transformers, and protection relays required for safe parallel operation with the electricity grid.

name: PV Rooftop Space / Solar Zone
description: Designated roof or ground area allocated exclusively for the installation and maintenance access of the PV array.

name: Electrical Plant Room / Inverter Room
description: Indoor mechanical/electrical room housing inverters, battery systems, switchboards, and associated PV electrical equipment.

name: PV System Design & Engineering
description: Engineering activity covering solar resource assessment, shading analysis, system sizing, electrical design, and structural load calculations.

name: PV Panel Installation
description: Site activity of fixing mounting structures, positioning, and fastening PV modules to the roof or ground support framework.

name: Electrical Wiring & DC/AC Connection
description: Licensed electrical work connecting PV strings, combiner boxes, inverters, and AC distribution boards with correct polarity and grounding.

name: Inverter & Battery Commissioning
description: Start-up and testing activity that verifies inverter settings, battery state-of-charge parameters, and protection relay coordination.

name: Grid Connection & Utility Inspection
description: Formal utility approval process and physical grid tie-in activity required before a PV system can export power to the network.

name: PV System O&M (Cleaning & Inspection)
description: Scheduled maintenance activity including panel cleaning, thermographic inspection, soiling loss assessment, and inverter log review.

name: PV Module Decommissioning & Recycling
description: End-of-life activity covering safe removal, transport, and recycling or disposal of PV modules in compliance with e-waste regulations.

name: Encapsulant (EVA Film)
description: Ethylene-vinyl acetate lamination film that encapsulates and protects PV cells from moisture and mechanical stress within a module.

name: PV Module Backsheet
description: Polymer or glass rear layer of a PV module providing electrical insulation, moisture barrier, and UV resistance.

name: Tempered Solar Glass
description: Low-iron, anti-reflective toughened glass front cover that protects PV cells while maximising light transmittance.

name: Aluminium Module Frame
description: Anodised aluminium extrusion that borders and stiffens the PV module laminate and facilitates mounting to racking hardware.

name: Corridor Floor Finish

name: Corridor Wall Finish

name: Corridor Ceiling
description: The overhead surface of the corridor, which may incorporate acoustic tiles, lighting fixtures, or fire-rated assemblies.

name: Corridor Door
description: Doors positioned along the corridor providing access to adjoining rooms or compartmentalizing sections for fire or security control.

name: Corridor Lighting
description: The electrical lighting system installed in the corridor, including emergency and general illumination fixtures.

name: Emergency Exit Lighting
description: Dedicated lighting and signage that activate during power failures to guide occupants safely to exits along the corridor.

name: HVAC Distribution in Corridor
description: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning ducts, grilles, and diffusers routed through or serving the corridor space.

name: Smoke Detector / Fire Alarm
description: Detection devices and alarm components mounted in the corridor to sense smoke or heat and trigger evacuation alerts.

name: Sprinkler System
description: Automatic fire suppression sprinkler heads and pipework installed within the corridor ceiling for life safety.

name: Skirting / Base Board
description: A protective trim strip at the junction of the corridor wall and floor, guarding against impact and providing a neat finish.

name: Corridor Signage
description: Wayfinding, room identification, and safety signs affixed to corridor walls or ceilings to guide building occupants.

name: CCTV / Security Camera
description: Surveillance cameras positioned along the corridor to monitor occupant movement and enhance building security.

name: Data / Telecommunications Cabling
description: Network and communication cable runs routed through the corridor's conduit or trunking to serve adjacent spaces.

name: Corridor Partition Wall
description: Non-structural or structural walls that define and enclose the corridor space and separate it from adjacent rooms.

name: Acoustic Treatment
description: Sound-absorbing panels, baffles, or wall linings installed in the corridor to reduce noise transmission and reverberation.

name: Accessible (Wheelchair) Corridor
description: A corridor variant designed with minimum width, turning radii, and tactile guidance to comply with accessibility standards.

name: Double-Loaded Corridor
description: A corridor layout with rooms on both sides, commonly used in residential, hotel, and healthcare buildings for efficient space use.

name: Single-Loaded Corridor
description: A corridor with rooms on one side only, often featuring an external glazed wall for natural light and ventilation.

name: Fire Escape Corridor
description: A dedicated, fire-rated corridor variant serving as a protected means of escape route to emergency exits.

name: Service Corridor
description: A back-of-house corridor used for maintenance, logistics, and building services access, separate from public-facing circulation.

name: Corridor Construction
description: The construction activity encompassing framing, partitioning, and enclosing works to physically form the corridor space.

name: Floor Finishes Installation
description: The site activity of laying and finishing floor coverings within the corridor to the specified material and quality standards.

name: Ceiling Installation
description: The activity of erecting suspended or fixed ceiling systems within the corridor, including grid, tile, and board work.

name: MEP Rough-In (Corridor)
description: The installation of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing services within corridor walls, floors, and ceilings before finishes are applied.

name: Fire Stopping Works
description: The activity of sealing penetrations and joints in corridor fire-rated assemblies to maintain compartmentation integrity.

name: Painting and Decoration
description: Application of paint, wallcovering, or decorative finishes to corridor walls and ceilings as a final interior finishing activity.

name: IFC Corridor Space
description: The IfcSpace IFC class instance representing the corridor volume within a building information model for data exchange.

name: Stair Flight
description: A continuous series of steps between two landings that forms the primary walking surface within a stairwell.

name: Stair Landing
description: A flat platform between flights of stairs that provides a resting point and directional change within the stairwell.

name: Stairwell Enclosure Wall
description: The fire-rated walls that enclose the stairwell shaft, separating it from adjacent building spaces.

name: Stairwell Lighting System
description: Electrical lighting fixtures and controls installed within the stairwell to ensure safe illumination at all times.

name: Emergency Egress Lighting
description: Battery-backed or dedicated-circuit lighting that activates during power failure to illuminate the escape route.

name: Pressurisation / Smoke Control System
description: Mechanical system that maintains positive air pressure in the stairwell to prevent smoke ingress during a fire event.

name: Handrail Fixing & Bracket System
description: Structural brackets and fixings that securely anchor the handrail to the wall or balustrade posts.

name: Non-Slip Stair Tread Insert
description: Anti-slip strips or inserts applied to the tread surface to reduce the risk of slipping on the stair.

name: Float Glass / Structural Glass
description: Toughened or laminated glass panels used for balustrade infill or stairwell enclosure in contemporary designs.

name: Fire-Rated Plasterboard
description: Gypsum board with fire-resistance properties used to line stairwell enclosure walls and soffits to achieve required fire ratings.

name: Stairwell Construction & Formwork
description: The activity of erecting formwork and casting or assembling the primary stair structure and enclosure walls.

name: Balustrade & Handrail Installation
description: Trade activity involving the fixing and finishing of balustrade systems and handrails to the completed stair structure.

name: Fire Door Installation
description: Specialist activity of hanging, aligning, and certifying fire doors at each stairwell entry opening.

name: Stairwell Finishing & Decoration
description: Application of final surface finishes, paint, tiles, or cladding to stair treads, risers, walls, and soffits.

name: Fire Rating & Compliance Inspection
description: Formal inspection and certification activity to verify that the stairwell assembly meets required fire-resistance and egress codes.

name: Mechanical & Electrical Rough-In (Stairwell)
description: Installation of conduit, cabling, pipework, and ductwork within the stairwell before wall finishes are applied.

name: Stairwell Waterproofing
description: Application of waterproof membranes or coatings to landings, wet areas, or external stairwells to prevent water ingress.

name: Evacuation Route / Means of Egress
description: The designated safe-travel path that the stairwell forms as part of the building's overall emergency evacuation strategy.

name: Lobby / Stair Lobby
description: A protected lobby space immediately adjacent to the stairwell entrance that provides an additional buffer against smoke and fire.

name: Building Core
description: The central structural and service zone of a multi-storey building within which the stairwell is typically located.

name: Heat Exchanger
description: A device that transfers heat between two fluid circuits without mixing them, used for district heating interfaces or system isolation.

name: Buffer Vessel
description: A thermal storage tank that balances supply and demand in heating or cooling circuits, preventing short-cycling of primary plant.

name: Pressurisation Unit
description: Equipment that maintains the correct hydraulic pressure within closed heating or cooling circuits to prevent cavitation and air ingress.

name: Expansion Vessel
description: A sealed tank that accommodates the volumetric expansion of water in a closed-loop system as temperature changes.

name: Circulating Pump
description: An electric pump that drives the flow of heated or chilled water through pipework distribution circuits within the building.

name: Domestic Hot Water Calorifier
description: An indirect storage heater that uses primary heating circuit energy to produce domestic hot water for building occupants.

name: Cold Water Storage Tank
description: A large cistern that stores incoming mains cold water to provide a gravity or boosted supply to the building's plumbing systems.

name: Water Softener / Treatment Unit
description: A water conditioning system that removes minerals and treats water to prevent scale, corrosion, and biological growth in pipework and equipment.

name: Main Electrical Distribution Board (MDB)
description: The primary electrical panel within the plant room that distributes power to all mechanical plant and building services equipment.

name: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
description: A battery-backed power conditioning unit that provides continuous power to critical controls and IT loads during mains outages.

name: Building Management System (BMS) Panel
description: The central control and monitoring panel that automates, sequences, and reports on all plant room and building services equipment.

name: Gas Meter and Regulation Assembly
description: Metering and pressure-regulation equipment at the gas supply entry point that measures consumption and steps down supply pressure for boilers and other gas appliances.

name: Fuel Oil Storage Tank
description: A tank storing heating oil or diesel fuel for boilers or generators, subject to secondary containment bunding requirements.

name: Hydraulic Header / Manifold
description: A large-bore pipe assembly that acts as a common interface between primary plant and multiple secondary distribution circuits.

name: Valve Assembly (Isolation & Control Valves)
description: A collection of shut-off, balancing, and motorised control valves that regulate and isolate flow throughout the pipework circuits.

name: Strainer / Dirt Separator
description: A filtration device installed in pipework circuits to remove particulates and debris that could damage pumps or heat exchangers.

name: Energy Meter Array
description: A set of sub-metering devices that measure gas, electricity, and heat consumption for energy management and billing purposes.

name: Flue and Exhaust System
description: The ductwork and chimney assemblies that safely discharge combustion products from boilers and generators to the external atmosphere.

name: Mechanical Ventilation (Plant Room)
description: A dedicated ventilation system supplying fresh air and extracting heat from the plant room enclosure to maintain safe operating temperatures for equipment.

name: Hydronic Heating Distribution System
description: The complete network of pipework, pumps, valves, and controls that circulates hot water from the boilers to terminal heating units throughout the building.

name: Chilled Water Distribution System
description: The closed-loop pipework network that distributes chilled water from chillers to fan coil units, AHUs, and other cooling terminals.

name: Domestic Water Services System
description: The combined cold and hot water supply pipework, storage, and boosting infrastructure serving all sanitary and catering outlets in the building.

name: Fire Suppression System (Plant Room)
description: A gaseous or water-mist suppression system protecting the plant room enclosure and high-value equipment from fire damage.

name: Electrical LV Distribution System
description: The low-voltage switchgear, cables, and distribution boards that supply and protect all electrical loads within and fed from the plant room.

name: Substation Room
description: An adjacent or integrated room housing high-voltage electrical switchgear and transformers, often directly connected to the main plant room.

name: Generator Room / Plantroom Annex
description: A fire-rated enclosure adjoining the plant room that houses standby generators and their associated fuel and exhaust systems.

name: Roof Plant Enclosure
description: A rooftop screened or walled area accommodating cooling towers, AHUs, and ancillary plant served by services risers from the main plant room.

name: Plant Room Access Corridor / Maintenance Zone
description: Designated circulation and working space within or around the plant room providing safe maintenance access clearances around all equipment.

name: Structural Steelwork / Plant Frame
description: Heavy steel framing and bespoke support structures fabricated to carry and align the weight of boilers, chillers, and other large plant items.

name: Insulated Pipework (HVAC)
description: Steel or copper pipework with factory- or site-applied thermal insulation and vapour barriers used to convey heating and cooling fluids with minimal energy loss.

name: Acoustic Lagging and Anti-Vibration Mounts
description: Specialist wrapping materials and spring or rubber isolators applied to plant and pipework to attenuate noise and vibration transmission to the building structure.

name: Chemical Dosing Agents
description: Inhibitors, biocides, and scale preventers dosed into closed and open water systems to maintain water quality and protect equipment longevity.

name: Fire-Rated Construction (Walls, Floors, Doors)
description: Minimum 60–120 min fire-rated structural and partition elements required to contain the plant room as a protected fire compartment.

name: Plant Room Commissioning
description: The systematic testing, balancing, and setting-to-work of all plant, pipework, and control systems to verify performance against design specifications.

name: Mechanical and Electrical (M&E) Installation
description: The trade activity of physically installing all mechanical plant, pipework, ductwork, electrical panels, and cabling within the plant room.

name: Pressure Testing of Pipework
description: A pre-commissioning activity where pipework circuits are subjected to hydraulic or pneumatic pressure tests to verify leak-free integrity.

name: Plant Room Fit-Out and Builder's Work
description: Structural penetrations, plinths, bunds, drainage channels, and finishes prepared by the main contractor to receive mechanical and electrical plant.

name: Water Treatment and Flushing
description: Pre-commission cleaning, chemical flushing, and ongoing dosing of water systems to remove debris and maintain biological and chemical water quality.

name: Energy Audit and Performance Verification
description: Post-occupancy measurement and analysis of plant room energy consumption against design benchmarks to identify inefficiencies and optimisation opportunities.

name: IFC Class: IfcBoiler

name: IFC Class: IfcChiller
description: IFC schema class for a chiller unit, enabling BIM-based coordination of chilled water plant with structural and architectural models.

name: IFC Class: IfcPump
description: IFC schema class for pumping equipment, used to model circulating pumps and their connections within hydronic distribution systems.

name: IFC Class: IfcHeatExchanger
description: IFC schema class representing heat exchanger components and their fluid port connections in an IFC-compliant BIM model.

name: IFC Class: IfcTank
description: IFC schema class for storage and buffer tanks, covering cold water tanks, calorifiers, expansion vessels, and fuel oil tanks.

name: IFC Class: IfcSpace (Plant Room)
description: IFC schema class used to define the plant room as a named, bounded space entity within the building's spatial structure hierarchy.

name: Parking Bay

name: Disabled Parking Bay

name: Electric Vehicle Charging Bay
description: A parking bay equipped with EV charging infrastructure for electric or hybrid vehicles.

name: Parent & Child Parking Bay
description: A wider bay positioned close to entrances, reserved for vehicles carrying young children.

name: Motorcycle Bay
description: A designated area sized and marked specifically for motorcycle or scooter parking.

name: Bicycle Parking Area
description: A secure zone within or adjacent to the car park providing stands or racks for bicycles.

name: Circulation Aisle
description: The driving lane between rows of parking bays allowing vehicles to manoeuvre in and out.

name: Entry / Exit Ramp
description: A sloped roadway connecting different floor levels within a multi-storey car park.

name: Pedestrian Walkway
description: A clearly delineated path segregating foot traffic from vehicle circulation within the car park.

name: Pay & Display / Ticketing Area
description: A zone housing payment machines or booths where drivers settle parking charges.

name: Security Booth / Kiosk
description: A manned or unmanned enclosure at the car park entrance used for access control and security.

name: Lift / Elevator Lobby
description: A waiting area adjacent to lifts, allowing pedestrians to move between floors safely.

name: Structural Column

name: Precast Concrete Plank / Slab

name: Post-Tensioned Concrete Slab

name: Vehicle Restraint Barrier

name: Anti-glare Screen / Mesh Façade

name: Speed Bump / Speed Ramp
description: A raised surface feature installed on internal roadways to enforce low vehicle speeds.

name: Wheel Stop / Parking Curb

name: Bay Marking & Line Painting

name: Wayfinding & Directional Signage

name: Height Restriction Bar / Gauge

name: Car Park Guidance System

name: CCTV & Security System

name: Lighting System

name: Mechanical Ventilation System
description: A fan-based system removing vehicle exhaust fumes and maintaining safe CO/NO₂ levels in enclosed car parks.

name: Fire Detection & Alarm System

name: Sprinkler / Suppression System
description: An automatic water or gas suppression system designed to control or extinguish fires within the structure.

name: EV Charging Infrastructure

name: Public Address / Intercom System
description: An audio communication system enabling announcements and two-way communication with car park users.

name: Structural Frame Construction

name: Precast Element Installation

name: Post-Tensioning Works

name: Floor Coating & Line Marking
description: The application of resin coatings and painted or thermoplastic bay markings to the finished floor surface.

name: Drainage Installation

name: Façade & Screening Installation

name: Signage & Wayfinding Installation
description: The fixing and commissioning of directional, informational, and regulatory signs throughout the facility.

name: Commissioning & Testing

name: Flooring Installation

name: Painting & Decorating

name: Furniture Installation & Commissioning

name: Snagging & Handover Inspection

name: Luxury Vinyl Tile (LVT)

description: The IFC class representing non-load-bearing internal partition walls that subdivide the office floor plate.

name: IFC Class: IfcZone
description: An IFC grouping construct used to aggregate multiple office spaces into functional or service zones for analysis.

name: WC Pan
description: The ceramic or porcelain bowl fixture used for waste disposal, forming the core sanitary unit of a toilet space.

name: Cistern
description: A water storage tank mounted above or behind the WC pan that supplies water for flushing.

name: Flush Mechanism
description: The valve and lever or button assembly inside the cistern that controls the release of water during flushing.

name: Toilet Seat and Lid
description: The hinged seat and cover fitted over the WC pan for comfort and hygiene.

name: Urinal
description: A wall-mounted or floor-standing fixture for male urination, typically installed in commercial or public toilet spaces.

name: Washbasin
description: A hand-washing sink installed within the toilet space, connected to hot and cold water supplies and a drain.

name: Basin Tap / Faucet
description: The tap or mixer fitting mounted on the washbasin that controls water flow for handwashing.

name: Soap Dispenser
description: A wall-mounted or counter-top unit that dispenses liquid or foam soap for hand hygiene.

name: Hand Dryer
description: An electric appliance fixed to the wall that dries hands using heated or high-velocity air.

name: Paper Towel Dispenser
description: A wall-mounted holder that stores and dispenses paper towels for hand drying.

name: Toilet Roll Holder
description: A wall-mounted bracket or spindle that holds and dispenses toilet paper rolls.

name: Grab Rail / Handrail
description: A structural support bar fixed to the wall to assist users with mobility impairments in sitting or standing.

name: Mirror
description: A reflective glass panel mounted above the washbasin for personal grooming.

name: Sanitary Bin
description: A hygienic disposal unit for sanitary products, typically pedal-operated and located in cubicles.

name: Cubicle Partition
description: Floor-to-ceiling or partial-height panels that divide the toilet space into individual private enclosures.

name: Cubicle Door and Lock
description: The door leaf and locking mechanism that secures each individual toilet cubicle for privacy.

name: Exhaust / Ventilation Fan
description: A mechanical fan unit that extracts odours and humid air from the toilet space to maintain air quality.

name: Soil and Waste Pipe
description: The drainage pipework that conveys waste water and sewage from fixtures to the building drainage system.

name: Water Supply Pipework
description: Hot and cold water pipes serving the WC cistern, washbasin, and any other fixtures within the toilet space.

name: Ceramic / Porcelain Wall Tile
description: Glazed tiles applied to wall surfaces in wet areas of the toilet for hygiene, durability, and aesthetics.

name: Non-slip Floor Tile
description: Textured or matt-finished floor tiles specified for toilet spaces to reduce slip hazards in wet conditions.

name: Grout and Sealant
description: Waterproof grout between tiles and silicone sealant at junctions to prevent moisture penetration.

name: Fixture Installation
description: The second-fix activity of fitting and connecting WC pans, cisterns, washbasins, and other sanitaryware to prepared pipework.

name: Wall and Floor Tiling
description: The application and grouting of ceramic or porcelain tiles to toilet wall and floor surfaces as a trade activity.

name: Electrical First and Second Fix
description: Installation of wiring, switch plates, and connections for lighting, exhaust fans, and hand dryers within the toilet space.

name: Commissioning and Testing
description: The activity of testing water flow, flush performance, drainage, ventilation, and electrical fittings to verify correct operation before handover.

name: Accessible (Disabled) Toilet
description: A larger, specially equipped toilet space designed to meet accessibility standards for wheelchair users and people with disabilities.

name: Ensuite Toilet
description: A private toilet space directly accessible from and dedicated to a single bedroom or suite.

name: Public Toilet Block
description: A building or zone containing multiple toilet facilities intended for use by the general public.

name: Unisex / Gender-Neutral Toilet
description: A toilet space designed for use by any gender, often specified to improve inclusivity in commercial buildings.

name: IFC Sanitary Terminal (IfcSanitaryTerminal)
description: The IFC class used to model individual sanitary fixtures such as WC pans, washbasins, and urinals in BIM authoring tools.

name: IFC Space (IfcSpace)
description: The IFC class that represents the toilet room as a defined spatial unit within the building model.

name: Reception Desk
description: A counter or workstation positioned at the lobby entrance where visitors are greeted, registered, and directed.

name: Entrance Vestibule
description: A transitional airlock space between the exterior and the main lobby that controls temperature, noise, and security.

name: Waiting Area
description: A designated seating zone within or adjacent to the lobby where visitors wait before being attended to.

name: Elevator Hall
description: The sub-space within or immediately off the lobby that houses elevator doors, call buttons, and associated signage.

name: Security Gate / Turnstile
description: Access-control barriers installed in the lobby to regulate the flow of authorised personnel and visitors.

name: Lobby Flooring
description: The finish floor material—commonly marble, granite, porcelain tile, or polished concrete—that defines the lobby's aesthetic and durability.

name: Suspended Ceiling / Ceiling Feature
description: A finished ceiling system—often featuring coffers, soffits, or atrium voids—that defines the vertical volume and houses services in the lobby.

name: Lobby Lighting System
description: An integrated arrangement of ambient, accent, and decorative luminaires designed to create the desired mood and meet illuminance requirements in the lobby.

name: CCTV / Surveillance System
description: Networked cameras and recording infrastructure positioned in the lobby for security monitoring and incident documentation.

name: Public Address / Wayfinding Signage
description: Directional signs, digital displays, and audio systems that guide visitors through the lobby and wider building.

name: Automatic Sliding Door
description: A sensor-operated door system providing hands-free, accessible entry into the lobby.

name: Glazed Curtain Wall / Facade
description: A non-structural exterior glazing system that forms the transparent or translucent lobby frontage, admitting daylight and providing visual connection to the street.

name: Feature/Statement Wall
description: A visually prominent wall within the lobby finished with artwork, branding elements, living greenery, or specialty materials as a focal point.

name: Lobby Furniture & Soft Furnishings
description: Seating, coffee tables, planters, and decorative objects that furnish the waiting and circulation areas of the lobby.

name: Concierge / Information Kiosk
description: A staffed or digital self-service station providing building information, parcel management, and visitor assistance.

name: Parcel / Mail Room Access Point
description: A dedicated counter or room reachable from the lobby for receiving and distributing deliveries and mail.

name: Atrium / Double-Height Volume
description: A tall, multi-storey void above the lobby that introduces natural light, grandeur, and vertical visual connectivity.

name: Accessible (Disabled) Entrance & Ramp
description: Ramped pathways, widened door openings, and tactile indicators that ensure barrier-free access through the lobby for people with disabilities.

name: Interior Landscaping / Planting
description: Live or preserved plants, green walls, and planter boxes integrated into the lobby to improve aesthetics and indoor air quality.

name: Artwork / Sculpture Installation
description: Commission or curated art pieces displayed prominently in the lobby as part of the building's identity and visitor experience.

name: Structural Column / Pillar
description: Load-bearing vertical elements within the lobby that transfer building loads to foundations and often become architectural features.

name: Floor Levelling & Screed
description: A cementitious or self-levelling compound layer laid beneath the finish flooring to create a flat, stable substrate throughout the lobby.

name: Waterproofing Membrane (Entrance Zone)
description: A moisture-resistant layer applied at the lobby threshold and below-grade areas to prevent water ingress from the exterior.

name: Lobby Fit-Out & Interior Finishes Installation
description: The construction activity encompassing installation of all finish materials, ceilings, joinery, and decorative elements within the lobby.

name: Structural Works (Lobby Slab & Columns)
description: Concrete or steel structural work forming the ground floor slab, columns, and beams that define the lobby volume.

name: MEP Rough-In (Lobby Services)
description: First-fix installation of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing conduits, pipes, and boxes concealed within lobby walls and ceilings before finishing.

name: Glazing & Curtain Wall Installation
description: Erection and sealing of the lobby's external glazed facade, revolving doors, and entrance frames.

name: Floor Finish Installation
description: Laying, grouting, and polishing of the specified floor material across the lobby, including setting-out for patterns and inlays.

name: Commissioning & Testing (Lobby Systems)
description: Functional testing and certification of all lobby mechanical, electrical, fire, and security systems prior to handover.

name: IfcSpace (Lobby)
description: The IFC schema entity used to represent the lobby as a named, bounded spatial unit within the building information model.

name: IfcFurnishingElement
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcElement.

name: IfcLightFixture
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowTerminal.

name: Skylight / Roof Glazing
description: Transparent or translucent overhead glazing system that admits natural daylight into the atrium void.

name: Atrium Floor
description: The ground-level or base-level finished floor surface within the atrium space, often featuring premium finishes.

name: Atrium Wall / Façade
description: The vertical bounding walls or curtain-wall glazing enclosing the sides of the atrium volume.

name: Structural Glazing System
description: Engineered system of glass panels, mullions, and transoms forming the transparent envelope of the atrium.

name: Steel Space Frame / Roof Structure
description: Primary load-bearing structural frame—often latticed steel—that spans the atrium opening and supports the glazed roof.

name: Smoke Exhaust / Natural Ventilation System
description: Mechanical or passive ventilation system that removes smoke and heat from the atrium in the event of a fire.

name: Atrium HVAC System
description: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning system specifically designed to manage the thermal stratification and comfort within a tall atrium void.

name: Smoke Curtain / Fire Curtain
description: Automatic descending barrier that compartmentalises the atrium to restrict smoke and fire spread between levels.

name: Fire Sprinkler System
description: Wet or dry pipe sprinkler network installed within the atrium to suppress fire at an early stage.

name: Balustrade / Guardrail
description: Protective railing or glass barrier installed along open gallery edges and mezzanines overlooking the atrium void.

name: Mezzanine / Gallery Level
description: Intermediate floor or open gallery tier that rings the atrium and provides circulation or usable space at upper levels.

name: Atrium Lobby / Reception Area
description: Ground-floor public zone within the atrium that acts as a main entrance, reception, or gathering area.

name: Planted / Green Wall or Landscaping
description: Interior planting, living walls, or landscape features integrated into the atrium to improve aesthetics and biophilic quality.

name: Decorative / Feature Lighting
description: Architectural and accent lighting scheme that enhances the visual character of the atrium beyond functional illumination.

name: Elevator / Lift Core
description: Vertical transportation shaft and cab serving the floors that open onto or adjoin the atrium.

name: Open Staircase
description: Architecturally prominent stair that traverses the atrium height, serving both circulation and visual focus.

name: Acoustic Treatment / Panels
description: Sound-absorbing materials or baffles applied within the atrium to control reverberation and noise amplification.

name: Thermal / Solar-Control Glazing
description: High-performance glass with coatings or interlayers that reduce solar heat gain and glare in the atrium roof or walls.

name: Waterproofing Membrane (Roof)
description: Membrane layer applied to roof abutments and flashings around the atrium glazing to prevent water ingress.

name: Steel Frame Erection
description: On-site assembly and erection of the structural steel space frame or portal structure that spans the atrium roof.

name: Scaffold / Temporary Works
description: Erection and dismantling of specialist internal scaffolding required to construct and finish the tall atrium void safely.

name: Atrium Fit-Out
description: Finishing works including flooring, feature lighting, planting, signage, and furnishings that complete the atrium to its design intent.

name: Fire Strategy / Smoke Modelling
description: Engineering analysis and computational fluid dynamics study used to design the atrium's passive and active fire safety measures.

name: Daylighting Analysis
description: Simulation and assessment of natural light penetration through the atrium glazing to optimise occupant comfort and energy performance.

name: Thermal Stratification Study
description: Engineering activity that models temperature layering within the atrium height to inform HVAC design and energy strategy.

name: Cleaning & Maintenance Gantry / BMU
description: Permanent cradle, track, or building maintenance unit enabling safe access for cleaning and maintaining the atrium glazing and structure.

name: IfcSpace (Atrium)
description: IFC schema entity used to represent the atrium as a named, bounded spatial zone within a building information model.

name: IfcRoof
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: Dock Leveler
description: A mechanical or hydraulic platform that bridges the height gap between the dock floor and a truck bed to enable smooth cargo transfer.

name: Dock Bumper
description: Rubber or steel buffers mounted at the dock face to absorb impact and protect the building structure when trucks back in.

name: Dock Seal / Dock Shelter
description: A foam-padded or fabric enclosure around the dock opening that creates a weather-tight seal between the building and the trailer.

name: Overhead Sectional Door
description: An insulated, motorized sectional door that closes the dock opening when not in use, providing security and thermal separation.

name: Dock Door Frame
description: The structural surround framing the overhead door opening, typically steel-reinforced to withstand repeated truck contact.

name: Truck Restraint / Wheel Chock System
description: A mechanical or automatic restraint device that secures a truck's rear-impact guard or wheels to prevent accidental departure during loading.

name: Dock Light / Work Light
description: An articulating or fixed luminaire mounted inside the trailer opening to illuminate the truck bed during loading and unloading operations.

name: Dock Safety Light / Traffic Signal
description: Red/green signal lights on both interior and exterior faces of the dock that communicate dock-occupancy status to drivers and forklift operators.

name: Pit / Dock Pit
description: The recessed concrete pit below the dock floor level that houses the dock leveler mechanism.

name: Apron / Truck Court
description: The exterior paved maneuvering area in front of the dock where trucks queue, turn, and position for backing into berths.

name: Staging Area
description: An interior floor zone immediately behind the dock doors reserved for temporary placement and sorting of inbound or outbound goods.

name: Dock Canopy / Canopy Structure
description: A projecting roof structure over the exterior dock face that protects trucks and workers from rain, snow, and direct sunlight.

name: Recessed Dock (Saw-Tooth / Inline Dock Layout)
description: A variant dock configuration—either inline or saw-tooth—that determines the angle and arrangement of multiple berths along a building wall.

name: Interior Dock Vestibule / Airlock
description: A temperature-controlled buffer space between the dock door and the main warehouse to minimize thermal infiltration during door operation.

name: Dock Concrete Apron Slab
description: A heavy-duty reinforced concrete slab at the exterior dock approach, designed to carry fully loaded truck axle loads without cracking.

name: Dock Floor Slab (Interior)
description: A high-strength, abrasion-resistant interior concrete slab at the dock level that supports repeated forklift and pallet-jack traffic.

name: Dock Leveler Installation
description: The construction activity of cutting the pit, forming and pouring the pit walls, and installing the leveler unit and its mechanical or hydraulic service system.

name: Dock Door and Frame Installation
description: The activity of setting the structural frame, hanging the overhead door, and commissioning the door operator and safety sensors.

name: Truck Court Paving
description: Site-work activity of subgrade preparation, base-course placement, and asphalt or concrete paving of the exterior maneuvering apron.

name: Dock Seal / Shelter Installation
description: The activity of fastening dock seals or shelters to the door surround and weather-testing them for proper truck-face compression.

name: Dock Safety System Commissioning
description: Testing and commissioning of interlock controls, traffic lights, and truck restraints to verify correct sequencing and fail-safe operation.

name: Truck Restraint Installation
description: The activity of embedding or surface-mounting wheel chocks or hook restraints and wiring them to the dock interlock control panel.

name: Dock Drainage System
description: A network of trench drains, sumps, and piping within the dock pit and apron area that collects water, oil, and runoff for proper disposal.

name: Dock Interlock Control System
description: An electrical/electronic control system that sequences dock leveler, truck restraint, and door operation to enforce safe use order.

name: Fire Suppression System (Dock)
description: Sprinkler heads or specialized suppression equipment installed at the dock opening and staging area per fire code requirements for high-hazard zones.

name: Dock HVAC / Air Curtain System
description: A high-velocity air curtain or dedicated HVAC unit that maintains interior temperature and reduces pest ingress when dock doors are open.

name: Grade-Level Dock (Drive-In Ramp)
description: A dock variant at ground level with an exterior ramp approach, allowing trucks to drive up to a raised platform rather than using a recessed pit leveler.

name: Refrigerated / Cold-Chain Dock
description: A specialized dock variant with insulated walls, doors, and an environmental seal system to maintain cold-chain integrity during transfer of temperature-sensitive goods.

name: Basement Floor Slab
description: Concrete slab forming the floor of the basement, typically cast on a gravel or sand base.

name: Footing
description: Reinforced concrete base beneath foundation walls that distributes structural loads to the soil.

name: Damp-Proof Course
description: Horizontal layer of impermeable material inserted in walls to prevent moisture rising from the ground.

name: Drainage Board
description: Dimpled or perforated panel placed against foundation walls to direct groundwater away from the structure.

name: Perimeter Drain (French Drain)
description: Subsurface drainage pipe system installed around the basement perimeter to collect and redirect groundwater.

name: Sump Pump System
description: Mechanical system comprising a pit and pump that removes accumulated water from below the basement slab.

name: Basement Waterproofing System
description: Integrated system of membranes, drainage, and pumps that collectively protect the basement from water infiltration.

name: Basement Window Well
description: Curved or rectangular enclosure installed around below-grade windows to allow light and egress while retaining soil.

name: Egress Window
description: Code-compliant window sized to serve as an emergency exit from a below-grade living space.

name: Basement Staircase
description: Stair assembly providing vertical circulation between the basement level and upper floors.

name: Bulkhead / Cellar Door
description: Exterior angled door structure that provides direct above-grade access into the basement.

name: Vapor Barrier
description: Polyethylene sheet or coating installed on floors and walls to control moisture vapor diffusion into interior spaces.

name: Insulation (Below-Grade)
description: Rigid foam or spray-applied insulation installed on basement walls or slab to reduce heat loss to the ground.

name: Bentonite Waterproofing
description: Clay-based waterproofing material applied as panels or slurry that swells on contact with water to seal the structure.

name: Basement HVAC System
description: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning equipment and ductwork serving the basement space for thermal comfort.

name: Mechanical Room
description: Dedicated below-grade room housing boilers, water heaters, pumps, and other building service equipment.

name: Utility Room
description: Basement space allocated for laundry appliances, electrical panels, and other domestic utility functions.

name: Walk-Out Basement
description: Basement variant built into a sloped site allowing at least one exterior wall to be at grade with a direct door exit.

name: Daylight Basement
description: Partially below-grade basement where one or more walls are exposed to allow natural light and window installation.

name: Cellar
description: Traditional below-grade storage space, typically unfinished and used for food, wine, or fuel storage.

name: Finished Basement (Living Space)
description: Basement that has been converted into habitable rooms with insulation, drywall, flooring, and code-compliant finishes.

name: Parking Garage (Underground)
description: Below-grade basement level designed and fitted for vehicle parking with ramps, markings, and ventilation.

name: Shoring & Temporary Support
description: Temporary bracing or sheet-pile installation to stabilize surrounding soil and adjacent structures during excavation.

name: Formwork & Concrete Pouring
description: Installation of molds and casting of concrete for foundation walls, footings, and basement slabs.

name: Basement Fit-Out
description: Construction activity of finishing an unfinished basement with partitions, insulation, MEP, flooring, and ceilings.

name: Underpinning Works
description: Structural operation to extend or reinforce existing foundations to permit basement creation beneath an existing structure.

name: Radon Mitigation System
description: Sub-slab depressurisation or ventilation system installed to remove radon gas accumulation from below-grade spaces.

name: IfcSpace (Basement)
description: IFC schema class representing the basement as a defined spatial zone within the building information model.

name: IfcSlab (Basement Slab)
description: IFC class representing the basement floor slab element within a building information model.

name: Structural Deck
description: The load-bearing concrete or metal base slab that supports all terrace finishes, furniture, and live loads.

name: Insulation Layer
description: Thermal insulation board or loose-fill installed above or below the waterproofing to regulate heat transfer through the roof assembly.

name: Drainage Layer
description: A dimple mat, gravel bed, or drainage board that channels rainwater away from the membrane towards outlets.

name: Overflow Drain / Scupper
description: A secondary emergency outlet positioned above the primary drain level to prevent ponding in case of blockage.

name: Paving / Decking Finish
description: The trafficable top surface — such as porcelain tiles, timber decking, or concrete pavers — laid over pedestals or bedding.

name: Pedestal Support System
description: Adjustable plastic or concrete risers that elevate paving slabs to create an accessible air gap above the waterproofing.

name: Parapet Coping
description: A capping element — typically metal, stone, or precast concrete — fixed to the top of the parapet to shed water and protect the wall.

name: Safety Balustrade / Railing
description: A structural guardrail system mounted at the terrace edge or on the parapet to prevent falls from height.

name: Green / Planted Roof Zone
description: A designated area of the terrace where a growing medium, filter fleece, and vegetation are installed over the waterproofing assembly.

name: Growing Medium / Substrate
description: Lightweight engineered soil or aggregate used to support planted vegetation on the terrace.

name: Root Barrier
description: A chemically resistant sheet layer that prevents plant roots from penetrating and damaging the waterproofing membrane.

name: Seating / Lounge Area
description: A defined zone on the terrace furnished for outdoor relaxation, typically shaded by a pergola or umbrella.

name: Pergola / Shade Structure
description: A freestanding or structurally attached overhead framework providing solar shading and aesthetic definition to the terrace.

name: Planter Box
description: A raised container for plants and shrubs, typically constructed from weatherproof materials and integrated with the terrace drainage.

name: Outdoor Kitchen / BBQ Area
description: A serviced zone equipped with cooking appliances, worktops, and utility connections for outdoor food preparation.

name: Mechanical Plant Zone
description: A reserved area of the roof terrace housing HVAC units, solar panels, or other building services equipment with maintenance access.

name: Solar Photovoltaic Array
description: A grid of PV panels mounted on the roof terrace structure to generate renewable electrical energy for the building.

name: Roof Terrace Lighting System
description: Low-voltage or LED luminaires, bollards, and controls providing safe and atmospheric illumination of the outdoor space.

name: Irrigation / Water Feature System
description: Pipework, drip lines, and controllers that supply water to planted areas and ornamental water features on the terrace.

name: Outdoor Power & Data Outlets
description: Weather-rated electrical sockets, USB, and data points distributed across the terrace for appliance and device connectivity.

name: Roof Access Stair / Hatch
description: A staircase or trapdoor assembly providing safe vertical access from the floor below to the terrace level.

name: Lift Overrun / Elevator Penthouse
description: The structural enclosure above the main roof housing lift machinery or overrun space, commonly located on or adjacent to the terrace.

name: Windbreak Screen
description: A vertical panel or glazed screen installed at the terrace perimeter or between zones to reduce wind speed and improve comfort.

name: Waterproofing Upstand
description: A continuous vertical turn-up of the waterproofing membrane at walls, parapets, and penetrations to prevent water tracking behind the system.

name: Pipe / Service Penetration Sleeve
description: A sealed collar or flashing detail where mechanical, electrical, or drainage services pass through the waterproofing assembly.

name: Waterproofing Installation
description: The site activity of preparing, priming, and applying the waterproofing membrane system across the structural deck.

name: Insulation & Drainage Board Installation
description: The laying and securing of insulation and drainage composite boards over the waterproofing prior to ballast or paving.

name: Paving & Decking Installation
description: The setting-out, cutting, and fixing of terrace surface finishes onto pedestals, adhesive beds, or timber joists.

name: Balustrade & Parapet Installation
description: The structural fixing, alignment, and finishing of edge-protection railings and coping elements to meet fall-prevention standards.

name: Landscaping & Planting Works
description: The installation of growing medium, root barrier, plants, and irrigation to complete planted zones on the terrace.

name: Roof Terrace Waterproofing Inspection
description: A flood or electronic leak-detection test carried out after membrane installation to verify integrity before overburden is placed.

name: Terrace Maintenance & Cleaning
description: Periodic inspection, drain clearing, sealant renewal, and surface cleaning required to keep the terrace watertight and safe.

name: Raised Access Floor
description: An elevated structural floor system installed above the concrete slab to route power, data, and cooling distribution beneath the server room.

name: Hot Aisle / Cold Aisle Containment
description: A physical airflow management arrangement that separates hot exhaust air from cold supply air to maximize cooling efficiency.

name: Computer Room Air Conditioning (CRAC) Unit
description: A dedicated precision cooling unit designed to maintain the exact temperature and humidity levels required by IT equipment.

name: Computer Room Air Handler (CRAH)
description: A chilled-water-based air handling unit that conditions and circulates air within the server room environment.

name: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System
description: A battery-backed power system that provides continuous, clean electrical power to IT equipment during utility outages or disturbances.

name: Power Distribution Unit (PDU)
description: A rack-mounted or floor-standing device that distributes electrical power from the UPS or utility feed to individual servers and equipment.

name: Server Rack / Cabinet
description: A standardized 19-inch or 21-inch enclosure used to house, organize, and secure servers, networking, and storage equipment.

name: Cable Management System
description: Trays, ladders, conduits, and patch panels that organize and route power and data cabling throughout the server room.

name: Structured Cabling Infrastructure
description: The complete network of copper and fiber-optic cabling, patch panels, and connectors that carry data signals between IT equipment.

name: Fire Suppression System (Clean Agent)
description: A gaseous suppression system (e.g., FM-200 or Novec 1230) designed to extinguish fires without damaging sensitive electronic equipment.

name: Early Warning Smoke Detection (VESDA)
description: A very early smoke detection apparatus that continuously samples air to detect pre-combustion particles before visible smoke or fire occurs.

name: CCTV / Security Surveillance
description: A closed-circuit camera network that continuously monitors and records activity inside and around the server room perimeter.

name: Environmental Monitoring System
description: Sensors and software that continuously track temperature, humidity, water leakage, and airflow conditions within the space.

name: Water Leak Detection System
description: Sensing cables or point sensors placed beneath raised floors and around cooling equipment to detect water intrusion immediately.

name: Generator / Standby Power System
description: A diesel or gas-powered generator that provides long-duration backup electricity to the server room during extended utility failures.

name: Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS)
description: An electrical switch that automatically transfers the power load from utility supply to the backup generator upon detecting a power failure.

name: Grounding and Bonding Network
description: A dedicated earthing infrastructure that protects equipment from static discharge and electrical faults by providing a low-impedance ground path.

name: Electromagnetic Shielding (Faraday Cage)
description: Conductive wall, floor, and ceiling treatments that prevent electromagnetic interference from entering or leaving the server room.

name: Anti-Static Flooring / Tiles
description: Electrostatic-dissipative floor tiles or coatings installed in the server room to prevent static charge buildup near sensitive electronics.

name: Acoustic Insulation Panels
description: Sound-absorbing materials applied to walls and ceilings to contain the high noise levels generated by servers and cooling equipment.

name: Data Hall / Colocation Space
description: A larger adjacent or sub-divided room within a data center where multiple tenants or departments house their individual server equipment.

name: Network Operations Center (NOC)
description: A dedicated room adjacent to the server room from which IT staff monitor, manage, and troubleshoot the infrastructure remotely.

name: Staging / Break-Out Area
description: A preparatory space outside the server room used for unpacking, imaging, and testing equipment before it is installed in racks.

name: Electrical Switch Room / MDF Room
description: An adjacent room housing main distribution frames, switchgear, and transformers that feed power into the server room.

name: IT Equipment Installation
description: The process of physically mounting, cabling, and configuring servers, switches, and storage units within the server room racks.

name: Cooling System Commissioning
description: Testing, balancing, and validating all CRAC/CRAH units and airflow containment to confirm design performance before go-live.

name: Power Infrastructure Testing (FAT/SAT)
description: Factory acceptance and site acceptance testing of UPS, PDUs, ATS, and generators to verify reliability and failover capability.

name: Cable Dressing and Labelling
description: The systematic routing, securing, and labelling of all power and data cables to ensure traceability and safe maintenance access.

name: Fire Suppression System Testing
