description: Commissioning and certification activity that verifies the clean-agent suppression system triggers correctly and achieves design concentration.

name: Thermal / CFD Survey
description: A computational fluid dynamics study or physical thermal scan performed to identify hotspots and optimize airflow within the server room.

name: Decommissioning and Data Sanitisation
description: The controlled process of powering down, wiping, and removing IT assets from the server room at end-of-life or relocation.

name: Main Switchboard (MSB)
description: The primary electrical distribution board that receives incoming supply and distributes power to downstream circuits and sub-boards throughout the building.

name: Distribution Board (DB)
description: A secondary panel that subdivides an electrical feed into branch circuits, each protected by a fuse or circuit breaker.

name: Busbar Chamber
description: An enclosure housing copper or aluminium busbars that carry and distribute high-current electrical supply within the switchroom.

name: Power Factor Correction (PFC) Unit
description: A bank of capacitors and associated controls installed to improve the power factor of the building's electrical load, reducing reactive power demand.

name: Metering Panel
description: An assembly containing electricity meters, current transformers, and instrumentation for measuring and recording energy consumption.

name: Residual Current Device (RCD)
description: A safety device that quickly disconnects a circuit when it detects current leakage to earth, protecting against electric shock and fire.

name: Fuse Disconnector
description: A combination device providing both overcurrent fuse protection and a means of isolating a circuit or piece of equipment.

name: Earthing & Bonding System
description: The network of conductors, earth bars, and bonding connections that provide a safe fault-current path and equalize potentials within the switchroom.

name: Lighting & Emergency Lighting System
description: General and battery-backed emergency luminaires providing safe working illumination inside the switchroom at all times.

name: Mechanical Ventilation & Cooling System
description: Fans, louvres, or air-conditioning units that maintain temperature and humidity within safe operating limits for electrical equipment.

name: SCADA / Building Management System (BMS) Interface
description: Communication gateways and protocols that relay switchroom status, alarms, and metering data to the central building management platform.

name: UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply)
description: A battery-backed power system providing seamless, conditioned power to critical loads during mains supply interruptions or quality events.

name: HV Switchgear Room
description: An adjacent or separate high-voltage switchroom housing MV/HV switchgear, transformers, and protection relays upstream of the LV switchroom.

name: Cable Basement / Cable Pit
description: An underground or sub-floor void through which incoming supply cables and inter-board cables are routed to the switchroom.

name: Transformer Enclosure / Kiosk
description: A fire-rated enclosure housing step-down transformers that convert the utility supply voltage to the building's LV distribution voltage.

name: Concrete Slab / Structural Floor
description: Reinforced concrete floor designed to carry the heavy static loads of switchboards and provide a stable, level installation surface.

name: Fire-Rated Wall & Door Construction
description: Masonry, fire-rated stud walls, and steel fire doors with appropriate FRL that contain any fire within the switchroom and prevent spread.

name: Anti-Static / Insulated Floor Finish
description: Specialised epoxy or rubber flooring that dissipates static electricity and provides an additional insulation layer for personnel safety.

name: Cable Insulation & Fireproof Seals
description: XLPE or LSF cable insulation materials and intumescent firestopping compounds used where cables penetrate fire-rated walls or floors.

name: Structural Steel Framing & Cable Supports
description: Hot-dip galvanised steel channels, brackets, and Unistrut supports that anchor switchboards and cable trays to the building structure.

name: Switchroom Installation & Fit-Out
description: The construction activity of preparing the room, installing cable containment, and positioning switchboards and ancillary equipment to the engineer's layout drawings.

name: HV/LV Cable Pulling & Termination
description: The trade activity of drawing high-voltage and low-voltage cables through containment and making safe, tested electrical terminations at both ends.

name: Switchboard Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)
description: Pre-delivery testing performed at the manufacturer's works to verify that switchboard assemblies meet specification before shipment to site.

name: Switchboard Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) & Commissioning
description: On-site testing, energisation, and functional verification of all switchroom equipment to confirm correct operation before handover.

name: Thermographic Inspection
description: Periodic infrared scanning of energised switchboards and connections to identify hot spots indicative of loose connections or overloaded components.

name: Preventive Maintenance (Scheduled)
description: Routine planned maintenance including cleaning, torque-checking connections, testing protection relays, and replacing consumables to sustain equipment reliability.

name: Arc Flash Hazard Assessment
description: An engineering study that calculates incident energy levels at each switchboard to define safe working distances and required PPE for maintenance personnel.

name: Protection Relay Coordination Study
description: An electrical engineering activity that sets and grades protection relay trip times to ensure selective, discriminative fault clearance across the distribution hierarchy.

name: Traction Machine (Motor Unit)
description: The electric motor and drive sheave assembly that powers the lift car movement up and down the hoistway.

name: Lift Controller Panel
description: The main electrical control cabinet housing logic boards and drives that govern lift operation, safety, and floor sequencing.

name: Governor Device
description: A centrifugal overspeed safety device that triggers the car safety gear if the lift exceeds rated speed.

name: Main Drive Sheave
description: The grooved wheel on the traction machine over which the hoist ropes run to move the lift car.

name: Hoist Ropes / Steel Wire Ropes
description: High-tensile steel wire ropes or belts that connect the lift car to the counterweight via the drive sheave.

name: Deflector Sheave
description: An auxiliary pulley used to redirect hoist ropes when the machine is not positioned directly above the hoistway.

name: Brake Assembly
description: Electromagnetic or spring-applied friction brake on the traction machine that holds the car stationary when not running.

name: Lift Power Supply & Isolator
description: Dedicated electrical supply board with isolating switch providing main power to all machine room equipment.

name: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) / ARD
description: Battery-backed automatic rescue device that moves the car to the nearest floor during a power failure.

name: Encoder / Pulse Generator
description: Rotary encoder mounted on the motor shaft that provides precise position and speed feedback to the controller.

name: Rope Tension Equaliser
description: Device or spring mechanism that maintains equal tension across all hoist ropes to prevent uneven wear.

name: Machine Bedplate / Support Frame
description: Structural steel frame that mounts and isolates the traction machine from the building structure to dampen vibration.

name: Anti-Vibration Mounts
description: Rubber or spring isolators placed beneath the bedplate to reduce transmission of motor vibration to the building.

name: Machine Room Flooring (Checkerplate / Reinforced)
description: Heavy-duty steel chequer plate or reinforced concrete floor finish designed to support machine loads and provide safe working surface.

name: Machine Room Access Door
description: Fire-rated, self-closing lockable steel door providing secure and compliant access to the machine room.

name: Ventilation & Cooling System
description: Mechanical or natural ventilation arrangement that maintains temperature and removes heat generated by machine room equipment.

name: Lighting & Emergency Lighting
description: Fixed general and maintained emergency lighting to illuminate the machine room for operation and maintenance safely.

name: Machine Room Earthing / Bonding System
description: Electrical earthing network connecting all metallic equipment in the machine room to the main building earth for safety.

name: Fire Detection & Suppression
description: Smoke detectors and, where required, clean-agent or gaseous suppression system protecting machine room equipment from fire.

name: CCTV / Remote Monitoring Terminal
description: Camera and remote monitoring interface that allows building management to observe and diagnose lift machine room status.

name: Lift Maintenance & Inspection Activity
description: Scheduled periodic inspection, lubrication, brake testing, and safety check carried out by a certified lift engineer.

name: Commissioning & Load Testing
description: Initial full-load and overload test runs performed to verify machine, brake, and safety gear performance before handover.

name: Rope Replacement Activity
description: Planned replacement of worn or broken hoist ropes or belts to maintain safe load-carrying capacity.

name: Controller Upgrade / Modernisation
description: Replacement or reprogramming of the lift controller to improve energy efficiency, safety compliance, or functionality.

name: Machine Room-Less (MRL) Lift Variant
description: A lift design variant where the drive machine is located in the hoistway, eliminating the need for a dedicated machine room.

name: Hydraulic Lift Plant Room
description: A separate room housing the hydraulic power unit and fluid reservoir for hydraulic-type lifts, analogous to the machine room.

name: Hoistway / Lift Shaft
description: The vertical shaft through which the lift car and counterweight travel, structurally connected to the machine room above.

name: IfcSpace – Lift Machine Room
description: IFC schema space entity used to model and tag the lift machine room volume in a BIM environment.

name: IfcElectricMotor
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcEnergyConversionDevice.

name: Sprinkler System Control Valves
description: Manual or automated valves located in the fire control room used to isolate or activate specific sprinkler zones.

name: Fire Suppression System Controls
description: Control interfaces for gaseous, foam, or other suppression systems that can be triggered or overridden from the fire control room.

name: Public Address & Voice Evacuation System
description: Audio system enabling emergency announcements and evacuation instructions to be broadcast across the building from the fire control room.

name: Fire Telephone (Firefighter's Intercom)
description: Dedicated hard-wired telephone or intercom network allowing direct communication between the fire control room and fire warden stations or stairwells.

name: CCTV Monitoring Station
description: Video surveillance monitors and recording equipment providing visual oversight of key building areas to support fire and emergency response.

name: Building Management System (BMS) Terminal
description: Interface terminal within the fire control room that integrates HVAC, lift, and other building systems for coordinated emergency response.

name: Emergency Power Supply Unit (EPSU)
description: Dedicated backup power supply ensuring all fire control room equipment remains operational during a mains power failure.

name: Smoke Control System Panel
description: Panel allowing manual override and monitoring of smoke exhaust fans, pressurisation systems, and dampers throughout the building.

name: Lift Control & Recall Panel
description: Control interface enabling emergency recall and manual operation of lifts to the ground floor during a fire event.

name: Emergency Lighting Control Panel
description: Panel used to monitor and test emergency and exit lighting systems across the building from the fire control room.

name: Firefighting Water Booster Pump Controls
description: Instrumentation and controls for the building's fire water booster pumps, allowing monitoring of pressure and manual activation.

name: Hazardous Materials Register Display
description: Printed or digital display of the building's dangerous goods and hazmat register, required to be accessible to attending fire services.

name: As-Built Building Plans Storage
description: Dedicated plan chest or digital terminal storing current as-built architectural and services drawings for use by emergency responders.

name: Key Safe / Master Key Cabinet
description: Secure cabinet holding master keys and access cards for all building areas, enabling rapid entry by emergency services.

name: Fire Control Room Door (Self-Closing, Fire-Rated)
description: Self-closing, fire-rated door assembly protecting the fire control room enclosure and maintaining its required fire-resistance level.

name: Fire-Rated Wall Construction
description: Walls enclosing the fire control room constructed to a specified fire-resistance level (FRL) using fire-rated framing, boards, or masonry.

name: Cable Penetration Fire Stopping
description: Intumescent or cementitious sealing systems applied to all service penetrations through fire-rated walls and floors of the fire control room.

name: Acoustic / Thermal Insulation
description: Insulation materials installed within walls and ceiling of the fire control room to meet acoustic and thermal performance requirements.

name: Dedicated HVAC / Pressurisation System
description: Separate heating, cooling, and air pressurisation system maintaining the fire control room at positive pressure and appropriate temperature for equipment and occupants.

name: Signage & Wayfinding (Fire Control Room)
description: Mandatory identification signage on or adjacent to the fire control room door to meet code requirements for emergency service access.

name: Fire Control Room Fitout Works
description: Construction activity encompassing the installation of all control panels, equipment, cabling, and furniture within the fire control room.

name: Fire-Rated Partition Installation
description: Construction activity involving the erection and certification of fire-rated wall and ceiling systems forming the fire control room enclosure.

name: Fire Services Commissioning & Testing
description: Systematic testing and commissioning of all fire detection, alarm, suppression, and communication systems connected to the fire control room.

name: Integrated Systems Testing (IST)
description: Coordinated testing activity verifying that all building systems—fire, BMS, lifts, smoke control—interact correctly when triggered from the fire control room.

name: Emergency Response Plan (ERP) Development
description: Preparation of the building's formal emergency response procedures that govern the use and operation of the fire control room.

name: Fire Control Room Inspection & Certification
description: Regulatory inspection activity by the authority having jurisdiction to certify the fire control room meets code and standard requirements prior to occupancy.

name: Warden Intercommunication Point (WIP)
description: Remote handset stations located throughout the building that communicate directly back to the fire control room telephone system.

name: Duress / Security Alarm Integration
description: Security alarm system integrated into the fire control room allowing monitoring of duress, intrusion, and access control events alongside fire events.

name: Firefighter Access Panel / Indicator Board
description: Graphical or mimic-board display showing the layout of the building and the status of all fire zones to assist attending firefighters.

name: Lobby / Reception Area
description: The primary entrance space within an amenity zone that greets occupants and visitors, often featuring seating and a staffed or unstaffed reception desk.

name: Fitness Center
description: A dedicated room or floor area equipped with exercise machines, free weights, and training zones for occupant wellness.

name: Swimming Pool
description: An indoor or outdoor aquatic facility used for recreation or lap swimming, requiring specialized waterproofing and mechanical systems.

name: Rooftop Terrace
description: An outdoor amenity deck situated on the building roof, designed for social gathering, relaxation, or events.

name: Lounge / Social Lounge
description: A comfortable communal sitting area furnished for informal socializing, co-working, or relaxation among occupants.

name: Conference / Meeting Room
description: A bookable enclosed room within the amenity floor equipped with AV technology and seating for business or community meetings.

name: Children's Play Area
description: A safe, supervised zone fitted with play equipment and soft flooring designed for young children's recreation.

name: Game Room / Entertainment Room
description: A recreation room containing entertainment features such as pool tables, arcade games, or home-theatre setups.

name: Spa / Wellness Suite
description: A dedicated zone housing sauna, steam room, or treatment rooms oriented toward occupant health and relaxation.

name: Café / Pantry
description: A small food-and-beverage service area providing coffee, snacks, or light meals to building occupants.

name: Pet Grooming Station
description: A purpose-built wash-and-groom area with drainage and fixtures designed for residents to clean and groom pets.

name: Package Room / Parcel Locker Area
description: A secure room or bank of automated lockers for the receipt and storage of delivered parcels.

name: Bicycle Storage & Repair Station
description: A secure storage room fitted with bike racks and a basic repair stand supporting sustainable commuting.

name: Outdoor Courtyard / Garden
description: A landscaped exterior or semi-exterior space at grade or podium level providing greenery and passive recreation.

name: Changing Room / Locker Room
description: A private-access room adjacent to the fitness center or pool containing lockers, showers, and changing facilities.

name: HVAC System (Amenity Zone)
description: The dedicated heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning system serving the amenity floor to maintain comfort and indoor air quality.

name: Pool Filtration & Chemical Dosing System
description: Mechanical and chemical treatment infrastructure maintaining water clarity, sanitation, and safety in the swimming pool.

name: Fire Sprinkler System (Amenity Zone)
description: Wet-pipe or alternate sprinkler network installed within amenity ceilings and spaces to suppress fire events.

name: IT / Wi-Fi Network Infrastructure
description: Structured cabling, access points, and network switches providing high-speed internet connectivity throughout amenity areas.

name: Gym Equipment Package
description: The curated set of cardio machines, strength-training apparatus, and accessories procured and installed in the fitness center.

name: Operable Partition / Movable Wall
description: A demountable wall system that allows amenity rooms to be combined or subdivided to suit variable event sizes.

name: Feature Lighting Fixture
description: Decorative or accent luminaires specified to reinforce the design character of lounges, lobbies, and social spaces.

name: Built-In Cabinetry & Millwork
description: Custom-fabricated joinery, bar counters, and shelving units that define the interior fit-out of amenity spaces.

name: Acoustic Ceiling Panel
description: Sound-absorbing ceiling tile or bespoke panel system installed to control noise levels in social and co-working spaces.

name: Outdoor Furniture & Shade Structure
description: Weather-resistant seating, tables, umbrellas, and pergolas furnishing rooftop terraces and courtyard amenity areas.

name: Sauna Enclosure & Heater
description: Pre-fabricated or site-built timber-lined sauna cabin complete with an electric or wood-burning heater unit.

name: Resilient Sports Flooring
description: Rubber, vinyl, or sprung hardwood flooring material selected for fitness and sports areas to absorb impact and reduce injury risk.

name: Pool Waterproofing Membrane
description: Specialist tanking or liner membrane applied to pool shell and surrounding wet areas to prevent water ingress.

name: Non-Slip Tile / Stone Finish
description: Slip-resistant ceramic, porcelain, or natural stone tile used on wet-area floors such as pool surrounds and shower rooms.

name: Acoustic Insulation Batt
description: Mineral wool or foam insulation installed within walls and floors to limit sound transmission between amenity spaces and residential units.

name: Exterior Decking Material
description: Composite timber, hardwood, or porcelain paver material forming the walking surface of rooftop terraces and outdoor amenity decks.

name: Amenity Fit-Out Construction
description: The trade work encompassing partition erection, ceiling installation, joinery fitting, and finishes within the amenity floor.

name: Pool Shell Construction & Waterproofing
description: Structural concrete or fiberglass pool formation followed by application of waterproof liners, tiling, and coping stones.

name: MEP Rough-In (Amenity Zone)
description: First-fix mechanical, electrical, and plumbing installation within amenity spaces prior to wall and ceiling closeout.

name: AV & IT Systems Installation
description: Pulling cables, mounting screens and speakers, configuring network hardware, and commissioning smart controls across amenity areas.

name: Landscaping & Planting
description: Supply and installation of trees, shrubs, planters, irrigation, and green-roof substrates within outdoor amenity zones.

name: Commissioning & Handover of Amenity Systems
description: Testing, balancing, and certifying all mechanical, electrical, pool, and AV systems before formal handover to building management.

name: Furniture, Fixtures & Equipment (FF&E) Installation
description: Delivery, placement, and anchoring of all loose and fixed furniture and equipment items throughout completed amenity spaces.

name: Fire Damper
description: A device installed within the shaft penetration to automatically close and prevent the spread of fire and smoke through the riser opening.

name: Smoke Damper
description: A controllable damper fitted at duct entries to the shaft to restrict smoke migration between floors during a fire event.

name: Access Panel
description: A removable or hinged panel set into the shaft wall or door to allow maintenance personnel to reach internal services without major disruption.

name: Shaft Door
description: A fire-rated door providing secure, code-compliant entry into the riser shaft for inspection and maintenance.

name: Cable Ladder
description: A heavier-duty open ladder-style support used inside the shaft for larger or heavier cable bundles running vertically.

name: Conduit
description: Protective tubing installed within the shaft to enclose and segregate individual electrical or data circuits.

name: Busbar Trunking
description: A prefabricated electrical distribution system run vertically through the shaft to supply power to each floor tap-off point.

name: Pipe Sleeve
description: A short cylindrical liner cast or built into the shaft wall where a pipe penetrates, protecting the pipe and maintaining fire compartmentation.

name: Fire Stop / Intumescent Seal
description: A passive fire protection material applied around penetrations in the shaft to seal gaps and prevent fire and smoke passage between floors.

name: Riser Pipe (Cold Water)
description: A vertical cold-water supply pipe rising through the shaft to distribute potable water to each floor level.

name: Riser Pipe (Hot Water)
description: A vertical hot-water distribution pipe within the shaft feeding domestic hot water to plumbing fixtures on every floor.

name: Riser Pipe (Heating)
description: A vertical flow and return pipe pair carrying heated water from plant to space-heating coils or radiators on each floor.

name: Riser Pipe (Chilled Water)
description: A vertical chilled-water supply and return pipe rising through the shaft to serve air-handling or fan-coil units on each floor.

name: Soil and Waste Stack
description: A vertical drainage pipe in the shaft that collects foul water and sewage from all floors and conveys it to the underground drain.

name: Compressed Air Riser
description: A vertical pipe distributing compressed air from a central plant to laboratory, medical, or industrial outlets at each floor.

name: Sprinkler Riser
description: A dedicated vertical pipe that feeds the pressurised water supply to the automatic sprinkler network on each floor.

name: Dry Riser
description: An unpressurised vertical pipe system installed in the shaft for fire-brigade use, charged with water only during a fire emergency.

name: Wet Riser
description: A permanently pressurised vertical pipe system within the shaft that provides an immediate water supply for firefighting on every floor.

name: HVAC Ductwork Riser
description: Vertical supply and return air ducts passing through the shaft to distribute conditioned air from central plant to each floor's distribution network.

name: Flue / Exhaust Riser
description: A vertical duct or liner within the shaft designed to safely discharge combustion gases or mechanical exhaust to the atmosphere.

name: Building Management System (BMS) Cabling
description: Low-voltage control and sensor wiring routed through the shaft to connect building automation devices across all floors to a central controller.

name: Data / Telecommunications Riser
description: A dedicated pathway within the shaft housing structured cabling, fibre optic, and telecom conduits serving every floor's IT infrastructure.

name: Shaft Wall / Enclosure
description: The fire-rated structural or non-structural wall assembly forming the four sides of the riser shaft and maintaining compartmentation.

name: Shaft Liner Board
description: Fire-rated gypsum or calcium-silicate board used to line the interior face of the shaft walls to achieve the required fire-resistance rating.

name: Structural Steel Shaft Frame
description: Steel framing members forming the structural skeleton of the riser shaft enclosure when it is a self-supporting non-load-bearing assembly.

name: Floor Penetration Slab Opening
description: A pre-formed or core-drilled opening through the concrete floor slab at each level through which riser services pass vertically.

name: Pipe Riser Clamp / Support
description: A mechanical fixing device anchored to the shaft wall or slab to restrain and support vertical pipes against gravity and thermal movement.

name: Cable Tray Support Bracket
description: A steel bracket anchored to the shaft structure at regular intervals to carry the weight of cable trays and their installed cables.

name: Thermal Insulation (Pipe)
description: Mineral wool, foam, or foil-faced insulation applied around pipes within the shaft to limit heat loss, prevent condensation, and meet energy regulations.

name: Acoustic Lagging
description: Sound-deadening wrap or cladding applied to pipes and ducts inside the shaft to reduce noise transmission to adjacent occupied spaces.

name: Shaft Construction and Enclosure Works
description: The construction activity of erecting the fire-rated walls, lintels, and structural frame that form the physical riser shaft enclosure.

name: Fire Stopping Application
description: The specialist activity of sealing all service penetrations in shaft walls and floors with certified intumescent or ablative materials.

name: Testing and Commissioning of Riser Services
description: The systematic pressure testing, flushing, and functional verification of all pipework and electrical systems installed in the shaft before handover.

name: Shaft Inspection and Survey
description: A periodic activity involving visual and instrument-based examination of shaft contents to verify integrity of supports, seals, and service conditions.

name: Clearance Zone / Maintenance Corridor
description: The clear working space within or immediately adjacent to the shaft required by regulations to allow safe maintenance of installed services.

name: Service Riser Room / Plantroom at Floor Level
description: A dedicated enclosed room at one or more floors adjacent to the shaft where riser services connect to horizontal distribution or local plant.

name: IfcShaft
description: The IFC schema class representing a vertical opening or enclosure through one or more building storeys used for the passage of building services.

name: IfcCableCarrierSegment
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowSegment.

name: IfcDamper
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowController.

name: HEPA Filtration Unit
description: High-Efficiency Particulate Air filtration system that removes airborne contaminants to maintain the required cleanliness class.

name: ULPA Filtration Unit
description: Ultra-Low Penetration Air filtration system offering even higher particle removal efficiency than HEPA, used in ISO Class 1–3 environments.

name: Fan Filter Unit (FFU)
description: Ceiling-mounted motorised fan and filter module that provides localised laminar airflow directly over the work area.

name: Laminar Airflow System
description: Unidirectional, low-turbulence airflow arrangement (horizontal or vertical) that continuously sweeps particles away from the critical zone.

name: Flush Ceiling Grid
description: Sealed, flush-mounted ceiling structure that supports fan filter units and light fittings while preventing particle accumulation.

name: Cleanroom Wall Panel
description: Smooth, non-shedding, chemical-resistant modular wall panel (often steel or composite) designed to minimise particle generation and allow easy decontamination.

name: Epoxy or Resin Floor Coating
description: Seamless, non-porous floor finish applied to eliminate joints and crevices that could harbour contaminants.

name: Antistatic Floor Material
description: Conductive or static-dissipative flooring material used to prevent electrostatic discharge in electronics and semiconductor cleanrooms.

name: Airlock / Entry Vestibule
description: Pressure-controlled transitional chamber at cleanroom entrances that prevents contaminated outside air from entering the controlled zone.

name: Gowning Room
description: Adjacent anteroom where personnel don cleanroom garments, gloves, and footwear before entering the controlled environment.

name: Pass-Through Chamber
description: Sealed double-door hatch that allows materials and equipment to be transferred into or out of the cleanroom without breaching the controlled environment.

name: Positive Pressure Cleanroom
description: Cleanroom variant maintained at higher-than-ambient air pressure to prevent ingress of external contaminants.

name: Negative Pressure Cleanroom
description: Cleanroom variant maintained at lower-than-ambient pressure to contain hazardous or biological contaminants within the space.

name: ISO Class 1–3 Cleanroom
description: Ultra-high-cleanliness room classification used in semiconductor fabrication, permitting fewer than 1,000 particles ≥0.1 µm per m³.

name: ISO Class 4–6 Cleanroom
description: Mid-range cleanliness classification typical for pharmaceutical manufacturing, medical device assembly, and precision optics.

name: ISO Class 7–9 Cleanroom
description: Lower cleanliness tier used in general pharmaceutical, biotech, or food-grade processing environments.

name: Temperature & Humidity Control System
description: Precision HVAC sub-system that maintains tightly specified temperature and relative humidity set-points critical to process quality.

name: Cleanroom Lighting Fixture
description: Sealed, flush-mounted luminaire with smooth surfaces and gaskets that prevents particle accumulation and leakage into the controlled space.

name: Differential Pressure Monitoring System
description: Network of pressure sensors and displays that continuously verifies and logs the pressure differential between zones to maintain containment integrity.

name: Particle Counter / Air Sampling System
description: Automated or portable instrumentation that continuously monitors and records airborne particle counts to verify ISO cleanliness classification compliance.

name: Cleanroom Garment (Gowning)
description: Specialised coveralls, hoods, gloves, and booties worn by personnel to minimise human-generated particle and microbial contamination.

name: Decontamination & Cleaning Activity
description: Scheduled cleaning, wiping, and disinfection procedures using approved agents to maintain surface cleanliness and microbial control.

name: Commissioning & Qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ)
description: Formal installation qualification, operational qualification, and performance qualification testing to certify that the cleanroom meets its design specification.

name: ISO Classification Testing
description: Periodic third-party particle-count and airflow testing performed to certify and re-certify the room's ISO cleanliness class per ISO 14644-1.

name: Cleanroom Construction & Fit-Out
description: Specialist construction activity involving the installation of modular panels, HVAC systems, and controlled-environment infrastructure to the required cleanliness standard.

name: Vibration Isolation System
description: Structural or mechanical damping measures that isolate sensitive equipment and the cleanroom slab from building or equipment-induced vibrations.

name: Chemical Distribution System
description: Dedicated piped network supplying ultra-pure process chemicals (acids, solvents, gases) to workstations within semiconductor or pharma cleanrooms.

name: Ultra-Pure Water (UPW) System
description: High-purity water treatment and distribution infrastructure delivering resistivity-controlled water for rinsing and process use in cleanroom environments.

name: IfcSpace (Cleanroom)
description: IFC schema entity used to represent the cleanroom as a defined, classified space within a building information model.

name: IfcZone (Controlled Environment Zone)
description: IFC grouping entity that aggregates cleanroom spaces and adjacent ancillary rooms into a single controlled-environment zone for facility management purposes.

name: Prestressed Concrete
description: Concrete in which internal stresses are introduced via tensioned steel tendons to counteract service loads.

name: Post-Tensioned Concrete
description: A form of prestressed concrete where tendons are tensioned after the concrete has cured, commonly used in slabs and bridges.

name: Precast Concrete
description: Concrete elements cast and cured off-site in a controlled factory environment before being transported and installed.

name: High-Performance Concrete (HPC)
description: Concrete engineered with a low water-to-cement ratio and supplementary cementitious materials to achieve superior strength and durability.

name: Ultra-High-Performance Concrete (UHPC)
description: An advanced cementitious composite with compressive strengths exceeding 150 MPa, typically incorporating steel fibers and silica fume.

name: Lightweight Concrete
description: Concrete produced with lightweight aggregates or aeration to reduce self-weight while maintaining adequate structural properties.

name: Heavyweight Concrete
description: Dense concrete made with heavyweight aggregates used for radiation shielding in nuclear and medical facilities.

name: Self-Compacting Concrete (SCC)
description: Highly flowable concrete that consolidates under its own weight without mechanical vibration, ideal for complex formwork.

name: Fiber-Reinforced Concrete (FRC)
description: Concrete mixed with discrete steel, glass, synthetic, or natural fibers to improve crack resistance and toughness.

name: Shotcrete
description: Concrete pneumatically projected at high velocity onto a surface, used for tunnel linings, slopes, and repair works.

name: Pervious Concrete
description: Open-graded concrete with high porosity that allows water to pass through, used in sustainable drainage applications.

name: Roller-Compacted Concrete (RCC)
description: Stiff, no-slump concrete placed in layers and compacted by vibratory rollers, commonly used in dams and pavements.

name: Geopolymer Concrete
description: Low-carbon concrete that replaces Portland cement with alkali-activated industrial by-products such as fly ash or slag.

name: Cement
description: The primary binding agent in concrete, most commonly Portland cement, responsible for hydration and strength development.

name: Supplementary Cementitious Materials (SCMs)
description: Pozzolanic or latent hydraulic materials—fly ash, slag, silica fume, metakaolin—blended with cement to modify concrete properties.

name: Coarse Aggregate
description: Crushed stone, gravel, or recycled material particles larger than 4.75 mm that form the bulk skeleton of a concrete mix.

name: Fine Aggregate
description: Sand or crushed fines passing a 4.75 mm sieve that fill voids between coarse aggregate in a concrete mix.

name: Concrete Admixtures
description: Chemical additives—plasticizers, retarders, accelerators, air-entraining agents—added in small doses to modify fresh or hardened concrete properties.

name: Concrete Mix Design
description: The engineering process of selecting and proportioning concrete constituents to meet specified strength, workability, and durability requirements.

name: Concrete Batching
description: The controlled weighing and measuring of all concrete ingredients prior to mixing at a batching plant or on site.

name: Concrete Mixing
description: The mechanical blending of cement, aggregates, water, and admixtures to produce a homogeneous concrete mix.

name: Concrete Placing
description: The controlled deposition of fresh concrete into formwork or onto a prepared surface at its final location.

name: Concrete Compaction / Vibration
description: The use of internal or external vibrators to eliminate air voids and ensure full consolidation of fresh concrete.

name: Concrete Formwork
description: Temporary or permanent molds—timber, steel, or plastic—that shape and support fresh concrete until it gains sufficient strength.

name: Concrete Pumping
description: The hydraulic conveyance of fresh concrete through pipelines or boom pumps to areas not accessible by direct discharge.

name: Concrete Testing & Quality Control
description: Site and laboratory procedures—slump tests, cube/cylinder crushing, non-destructive testing—to verify fresh and hardened concrete conformance.

name: Concrete Repair & Rehabilitation
description: Remediation works including patch repairs, carbonation treatment, and cathodic protection to restore deteriorated concrete structures.

name: Concrete Demolition
description: The controlled breaking, cutting, or crushing of existing concrete elements during deconstruction or renovation.

name: Concrete Column
description: A vertical structural concrete member primarily designed to carry compressive axial loads and transfer them to foundations.

name: Concrete Slab
description: A flat, horizontal concrete plate element forming floors, roofs, or bridge decks, spanning between beams or walls.

name: Concrete Foundation
description: Below-ground concrete elements—pads, strips, rafts, or piles—that transfer structural loads safely into the subsoil.

name: Concrete Core
description: A central reinforced concrete shaft in high-rise buildings housing lifts and stairs, providing primary lateral resistance to wind and seismic forces.

name: Concrete Frame
description: A structural system of interconnected concrete columns and beams forming the load-bearing skeleton of a building.

name: Concrete Staircase
description: A cast-in-situ or precast concrete flight of stairs providing vertical circulation within or between building levels.

name: Concrete Pavement
description: A rigid surface layer of concrete used for roads, aprons, hardstandings, and pedestrian areas.

name: IfcConcreteElement
description: The IFC schema entity representing a generic concrete building element for use in BIM model data exchange.

name: Softwood Timber
description: Timber sourced from coniferous trees such as pine, spruce, and fir, commonly used in structural framing and general construction.

name: Hardwood Timber
description: Timber sourced from deciduous trees such as oak, ash, and beech, valued for its density and durability in flooring, joinery, and furniture.

name: Engineered Wood
description: Manufactured wood products such as LVL, glulam, and I-joists created by binding wood fibres, veneers, or boards to enhance structural performance.

name: Cross-Laminated Timber (CLT)
description: A mass timber panel product made of layers of solid wood boards stacked crosswise and glued, used for walls, floors, and roofs in large-scale construction.

name: Glued Laminated Timber (Glulam)
description: Structural timber manufactured by bonding multiple layers of dimensioned lumber with durable adhesives to form beams, columns, and arches.

name: Laminated Veneer Lumber (LVL)
description: An engineered wood product made from thin wood veneers bonded together, offering high strength and consistency for beams and headers.

name: Oriented Strand Board (OSB)
description: An engineered wood panel formed from compressed wood strands and adhesive, widely used as structural sheathing and flooring substrate.

name: Plywood
description: A sheet material made from thin layers of wood veneer glued together in alternating grain directions, providing strength and dimensional stability.

name: Medium Density Fibreboard (MDF)
description: A composite wood panel produced from fine wood fibres and resin, commonly used in interior joinery, cabinetry, and furniture.

name: Timber Frame
description: A structural building system comprising a skeletal framework of timber posts, beams, and studs that carries loads to the foundations.

name: Mass Timber Structure
description: A structural system using large solid or composite wood panels and members (e.g., CLT, glulam) to create load-bearing walls, floors, and roofs.

name: Timber Roof Structure
description: The assembly of timber rafters, purlins, ridge boards, and trusses that form the load-bearing skeleton of a roof.

name: Timber Floor System
description: A floor construction system using timber joists, beams, or mass timber panels to span between supports and carry floor loads.

name: Timber Stud Wall
description: A wall assembly comprising vertical timber studs and horizontal plates used as the primary structural or partition wall element in light-frame construction.

name: Timber Truss
description: A prefabricated or site-built triangulated timber framework used to span large distances in roofs and floors with efficient load distribution.

name: Timber Column
description: A vertical timber member that transmits compressive loads from beams, floors, or roofs down to foundations or lower structural elements.

name: Timber Decking
description: Planks or boards of timber used to form walking surfaces on external decks, bridges, or roof terraces.

name: Timber Cladding
description: Timber boards, shingles, or panels fixed to the external face of a building to provide weatherproofing and aesthetic finish.

name: Timber Flooring
description: Finished floor surface material made from solid timber strips, planks, or engineered boards laid over a structural substrate.

name: Timber Joinery
description: Crafted timber elements including doors, windows, staircases, and built-in furniture that contribute to both function and interior finish.

name: Timber Preservation / Treatment
description: Chemical or physical processes applied to timber to protect it against decay, insects, moisture, and fire, extending its service life.

name: Fire-Retardant Timber Treatment
description: Application of fire-retardant chemicals or coatings to timber members to improve reaction-to-fire performance and meet regulatory requirements.

name: Timber Procurement
description: The sourcing, grading, and purchasing of raw or processed timber from certified or sustainable supply chains for a construction project.

name: Timber Frame Erection
description: The on-site construction activity of assembling and raising prefabricated or cut timber frame structural elements into their final position.

name: Timber Cutting and Machining
description: Workshop or site-based fabrication activity involving sawing, planing, routing, and shaping timber to specified dimensions and profiles.

name: Timber Jointing and Connections
description: The design and execution of mechanical or adhesive connections between timber members, including mortise-and-tenon, bolted, and metal-plate fastened joints.

name: Timber Installation (Flooring/Cladding)
description: The fixing and laying of timber finish products such as flooring boards or external cladding panels as part of the building envelope or interior fit-out.

name: Timber Maintenance and Refinishing
description: Periodic inspection, cleaning, sanding, oiling, or repainting of exposed timber surfaces to preserve appearance and structural integrity.

name: Sustainable Forestry Certification (FSC/PEFC)
description: The verification and documentation process ensuring that timber originates from responsibly managed forests in compliance with FSC or PEFC standards.

name: Timber Moisture Content Testing
description: Quality-control activity measuring the moisture content of timber to ensure it meets specification limits before installation to prevent warping or decay.

name: Timber Storage Area
description: A designated on-site or off-site area for the proper stacking and protection of timber materials prior to their use in construction.

name: Timber Workshop / Fabrication Shop
description: A facility where timber is measured, cut, shaped, and pre-assembled into components before delivery to the construction site.

name: Stainless Steel
description: Corrosion-resistant steel alloy used in cladding, fixtures, and exposed architectural elements.

name: Mild Steel
description: Low-carbon steel commonly used for general fabrication, connectors, and secondary structural elements.

name: High-Strength Low-Alloy (HSLA) Steel
description: Alloy steel offering improved mechanical properties and greater resistance to atmospheric corrosion than conventional mild steel.

name: Weathering Steel
description: A steel alloy that forms a stable rust-like patina, eliminating the need for painting in exposed outdoor applications.

name: Galvanized Steel
description: Steel coated with a zinc layer to protect against corrosion, widely used in roofing, framing, and connectors.

name: Cold-Formed Steel
description: Thin-gauge steel shaped at room temperature, commonly used for light-gauge framing, studs, and purlins.

name: Rebar (Reinforcing Steel Bar)
description: Deformed steel bars embedded in concrete to provide tensile strength in reinforced concrete structures.

name: Steel Wire Rope / Cable
description: Stranded steel wire assemblies used in suspension structures, cable-stayed systems, and tensile facades.

name: Steel Plate
description: Flat rolled steel product used for fabricating connection plates, base plates, and custom structural elements.

name: Steel Hollow Structural Section (HSS)
description: Tubular steel profiles (round, square, or rectangular) used as columns, braces, and architectural members.

name: Steel I-Beam / Wide Flange Section
description: Standard hot-rolled I-shaped steel section widely used as beams and columns in structural frames.

name: Steel Column
description: Vertical steel member that transmits compressive loads from beams and slabs down to the foundation.

name: Steel Truss
description: A triangulated framework of steel members used to span long distances in roofs, bridges, and floors.

name: Steel Deck / Metal Deck
description: Corrugated steel sheeting used as a permanent formwork and tensile reinforcement for composite concrete floor slabs.

name: Steel Connection / Joint
description: Bolted, welded, or pinned assemblies that transfer forces between steel members at structural nodes.

name: Steel Base Plate
description: A flat steel plate placed beneath a column to distribute load to the foundation or anchor bolts.

name: Steel Anchor Bolt
description: Bolts cast into concrete foundations to secure steel columns and equipment to the structure.

name: Steel Stud Framing
description: Light-gauge cold-formed steel stud system used for non-load-bearing interior partition walls and exterior wall framing.

name: Structural Steel Frame System
description: An integrated system of columns, beams, and bracing forming the primary skeleton of a steel-framed building.

name: Steel Moment Frame
description: A lateral-force-resisting system where rigidly connected steel beams and columns resist seismic and wind loads through bending.

name: Steel Braced Frame
description: A lateral-force-resisting system using diagonal steel braces to provide stiffness against horizontal forces.

name: Steel Roof System
description: An assembly of steel purlins, rafters, and decking that forms the structural and weather-resistant roof of a building.

name: Composite Steel-Concrete System
description: A structural system combining steel beams with concrete slabs acting compositely via shear connectors for enhanced efficiency.

name: Steel Fabrication
description: The workshop process of cutting, drilling, and welding steel members to produce fabricated structural components ready for site delivery.

name: Steel Erection
description: The on-site activity of lifting and assembling fabricated steel members into the final structural frame using cranes and bolting.

name: Steel Welding
description: The process of fusing steel components together using heat and filler material to form permanent structural connections.

name: Steel Bolting
description: The mechanical fastening of steel members using high-strength bolts, nuts, and washers at connection points.

name: Steel Surface Treatment / Painting
description: The application of primers, paints, or coatings to steel surfaces to protect against corrosion and achieve required fire ratings.

name: Steel Fire Protection (Intumescent Coating)
description: The application of intumescent or spray-applied fireproofing materials to steel members to achieve code-required fire resistance.

name: Steel Inspection & NDT Testing
description: Non-destructive testing activities such as ultrasonic and magnetic particle inspection to verify weld quality and material integrity.

name: Steel Recycling / Deconstruction
description: The end-of-life activity of disassembling or cutting structural steel for reuse or recycling, leveraging its high recyclability.

name: IfcMember
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcFastener
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcElementComponent.

name: Float Glass
description: Standard flat glass produced by floating molten glass on molten tin, used as the base for most architectural glazing products.

name: Tempered Glass
description: Heat-treated glass that is significantly stronger than standard glass and shatters into small, safer fragments upon breakage.

name: Laminated Glass
description: Two or more glass panes bonded together with a polyvinyl butyral (PVB) interlayer to hold fragments in place upon breakage.

name: Low-E Glass
description: Glass coated with a microscopically thin metallic layer that reflects infrared heat while allowing visible light to pass through.

name: Frosted Glass
description: Glass with a surface treated by sandblasting or acid etching to diffuse light and provide privacy.

name: Tinted Glass
description: Glass with colorants added during manufacturing to reduce solar heat gain and glare while maintaining transparency.

name: Wired Glass
description: Glass with an embedded wire mesh that holds fragments together in the event of breakage, traditionally used for fire-rated applications.

name: Patterned Glass
description: Rolled glass with a textured or decorative surface pattern on one or both faces, used for privacy and aesthetics.

name: Electrochromic Smart Glass
description: Glass that changes tint or opacity electronically in response to an electrical current, allowing dynamic control of light and solar gain.

name: Structural Glass
description: High-strength glass elements designed to bear loads as a primary structural component in facades, floors, or staircases.

name: Spandrel Glass
description: Opaque or semi-opaque glass panels used to conceal structural elements between floors in curtain wall and facade systems.

name: Glass Curtain Wall
description: A non-structural exterior building envelope system composed primarily of glass panels supported by a lightweight aluminum or steel framework.

name: Glazing Frame
description: The structural surround—typically aluminum, steel, timber, or uPVC—that holds glass panes in windows, doors, and curtain walls.

name: Glass Balustrade
description: A safety barrier or railing system constructed from structural glass panels used on stairs, balconies, and mezzanines.

name: Glass Roof / Skylight
description: A glazed overhead structure or opening designed to admit natural daylight into interior spaces below.

name: Glass Door
description: A door assembly where the primary infill panel is glass, used for both transparency and natural light transmission.

name: Glass Partition
description: An interior non-load-bearing dividing wall constructed with glass panels to separate spaces while maintaining visual openness.

name: Glazing Sealant / Silicone
description: A flexible, weatherproof sealant applied at glass-to-frame or glass-to-glass joints to ensure airtight and watertight performance.

name: Spacer Bar
description: The border element within an insulated glass unit that separates the panes and contains desiccant to prevent internal condensation.

name: Glass Installation
description: The construction activity of fitting, setting, and securing glass panes into frames, curtain walls, or structural assemblies.

name: Glass Cutting & Fabrication
description: The workshop or on-site process of cutting, shaping, edging, drilling, and finishing glass to specified dimensions and tolerances.

name: Glass Tempering
description: The heat-treatment manufacturing process that thermally toughens glass to increase its mechanical strength and safety performance.

name: Glass Replacement
description: The maintenance activity of removing broken or damaged glass units and installing new panes or assemblies in their place.

name: Glass Cleaning & Maintenance
description: Scheduled or reactive cleaning and inspection activities to preserve the clarity, coating integrity, and weather performance of glazed surfaces.

name: Glazing Bead
description: A thin strip of material fixed to a frame to retain the glass pane securely within its rebate.

name: Gas Fill (Argon / Krypton)
description: Inert gas injected between the panes of an insulated glass unit to reduce thermal conductivity and improve energy efficiency.

name: Solar Control Coating
description: A thin-film coating applied to glass surfaces to selectively control solar radiation transmission, reflection, and absorption.

name: Fire-Rated Glass
description: Specially manufactured glass that provides defined periods of integrity and/or insulation resistance to fire and heat transmission.

name: Acoustic Glass
description: Laminated or multi-pane glass systems engineered to attenuate sound transmission between exterior and interior environments.

name: Mineral Wool Insulation
description: A fibrous insulation material made from rock or slag, commonly used in walls, roofs, and floors for thermal and acoustic performance.

name: Fiberglass Batt Insulation
description: Pre-cut panels of spun glass fibers installed between studs and joists to resist heat transfer in building envelopes.

name: Spray Foam Insulation
description: A two-component liquid foam that expands on application to fill cavities, providing both thermal insulation and an air barrier.

name: Rigid Board Insulation
description: Solid panels of foam or fibrous material (e.g., XPS, EPS, PIR) used in continuous insulation applications on walls, roofs, and foundations.

name: Loose-Fill Insulation
description: Blown-in cellulose, fiberglass, or mineral wool particles used to insulate attics, wall cavities, and irregular spaces.

name: Reflective Foil Insulation
description: Thin metallic foil-faced material that reduces radiant heat transfer, often used in roofs and underfloor applications.

name: Aerogel Insulation
description: An ultra-low-density silica-based material offering extremely high thermal resistance in thin profiles for retrofit and space-constrained applications.

name: Cellulose Insulation
description: Recycled paper-based loose-fill or dense-pack insulation treated with fire retardants, valued for its sustainability credentials.

name: Phenolic Foam Insulation
description: A closed-cell rigid foam board with very low thermal conductivity and enhanced fire resistance, used in high-performance façades and roofs.

name: Vacuum Insulation Panel
description: A high-performance panel containing a evacuated core that delivers exceptional thermal resistance in very thin constructions.

name: Duct Insulation
description: Insulating wrap or board applied to HVAC ductwork to minimise thermal losses and prevent condensation on duct surfaces.

name: Cavity Wall Insulation
description: Material installed within the air gap of a double-leaf masonry wall to reduce heat loss through the wall assembly.

name: Under-Slab Insulation
description: Rigid insulation boards placed beneath a concrete ground-floor slab to limit heat loss to the ground.

name: Roof Insulation Layer
description: A dedicated insulation stratum within a flat or pitched roof build-up that meets the required U-value for the roof assembly.

name: Breather Membrane
description: A vapour-permeable, wind-resistive membrane installed on the cold side of insulation to allow drying while excluding air infiltration.

name: Insulation Fixings & Anchors
description: Mechanical fasteners, adhesives, or retaining clips used to secure insulation boards or batts to substrates.

name: Thermal Bridging Mitigation Element
description: Specially designed structural brackets, thermal breaks, or pads that interrupt conductive heat paths at junctions in the building envelope.

name: Fire-Rated Insulation
description: Insulation classified to meet specific fire reaction or fire resistance criteria, used in compartmentation and passive fire protection.

name: Floor Insulation
description: The combined assembly of insulating materials, fixings, and membranes designed to achieve the thermal performance target for a floor construction.

name: Wall Insulation System
description: An integrated system of boards, renders, fixings, and finishes (e.g., ETICS/EIFS) that delivers continuous thermal insulation to a wall.

name: Roof Insulation System
description: The full roof insulation assembly—including boards, vapour control, and waterproofing—designed and specified as a performance package.

name: Insulation Blowing / Spraying
description: A specialist activity using equipment to blow loose-fill or spray foam insulation into cavities and voids.

name: Insulation Removal & Disposal
description: The activity of stripping out existing insulation for replacement or refurbishment, including hazardous material handling where applicable.

name: Thermal Performance Testing
description: Site or laboratory testing—such as thermography, air-tightness tests, or heat-flux measurements—to verify in-situ insulation effectiveness.

name: U-Value Calculation
description: The engineering activity of calculating the overall thermal transmittance of a building element to confirm compliance with energy regulations.

name: Insulation Specification & Procurement
description: The design-stage activity of selecting, specifying, and procuring insulation products to meet performance, cost, and sustainability requirements.

name: Bituminous Sheet Membrane
description: A modified bitumen-based sheet material applied in layers to provide waterproofing on roofs and below-grade structures.

name: Liquid-Applied Membrane
description: A fluid coating applied by brush, roller, or spray that cures to form a seamless waterproof barrier over irregular surfaces.

name: EPDM Membrane
description: A synthetic rubber (ethylene propylene diene monomer) sheet widely used for flat and low-slope roof waterproofing.

name: TPO Membrane
description: A single-ply thermoplastic polyolefin sheet offering UV resistance and heat-weldable seams for roof waterproofing.

name: PVC Membrane
description: A flexible polyvinyl chloride single-ply sheet used for roofing and below-grade waterproofing with strong chemical resistance.

name: Bentonite Clay Membrane
description: A geosynthetic clay liner or panel that swells on contact with water to self-seal and waterproof below-grade foundations.

name: Cementitious Waterproofing Coating
description: A rigid or semi-flexible cement-based slurry applied to concrete surfaces to block water ingress in wet areas and foundations.

name: Polyurethane Waterproofing Membrane
description: A liquid-applied or sheet polyurethane system providing high elongation and flexibility for plaza decks, balconies, and roofs.

name: Self-Adhered Membrane
description: A pre-manufactured sheet with a factory-applied adhesive backing that bonds directly to substrates without additional adhesives.

name: Drainage Layer / Dimple Mat
description: A profiled plastic sheet placed over the waterproof membrane to channel water away and protect the membrane from soil pressure.

name: Protection Board
description: A rigid or semi-rigid board installed over a membrane to shield it from physical damage during backfill or traffic loading.

name: Primer Coat
description: A preparatory adhesion-promoting liquid applied to the substrate before membrane installation to ensure a secure bond.

name: Termination Bar
description: A metal or plastic bar used to mechanically secure and seal the top edge of a waterproof membrane to a vertical surface.

name: Waterstop
description: A strip or profile embedded in concrete construction joints to prevent water migration through the joint.

name: Drainage Composite System
description: An integrated assembly of filter fabric, drainage core, and membrane that manages hydrostatic pressure against waterproofed structures.

name: Waterproofing System Design
description: The holistic specification and layered assembly plan for a complete waterproofing solution including primary membrane, details, and drainage.

name: Surface Preparation
description: The process of cleaning, repairing, and priming substrates to achieve the required smoothness and adhesion for membrane application.

name: Membrane Installation
description: The trade activity of laying, bonding, welding, or torching the waterproof membrane onto the prepared substrate.

name: Seam Welding / Sealing
description: The hot-air or solvent welding process that joins membrane sheet overlaps to create a continuous, watertight bond.

name: Flood Testing / Water Testing
description: A quality-assurance activity where the installed membrane is ponded with water to detect leaks before covering.

name: Membrane Inspection & QA
description: Systematic on-site checks and electronic leak detection surveys to verify membrane integrity before and after installation.

name: Backfilling Over Membrane
description: The controlled placement of soil or aggregate over a below-grade waterproof membrane assembly to minimise puncture damage.

name: Repair & Patching of Membrane
description: Remediation work to locate and seal defects, blisters, or punctures in an existing waterproof membrane.

name: Below-Grade Waterproofed Space
description: A basement, underground car park, or substructure void that relies on a waterproof membrane to remain dry.

name: Podium / Plaza Deck
description: An occupied or landscaped roof slab over a structure where a waterproof membrane protects the structural deck below.

name: Wet Room / Tanked Bathroom
description: An interior space such as a bathroom or plant room where walls and floors are tanked with a waterproof membrane.

name: IfcCovering (Membrane Layer)
description: The IFC schema class used to model thin membrane or coating layers as part of a building element's layered construction.

name: IfcBuildingElementPart
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcElementComponent.

name: Clay Brick
description: A traditional fired-clay masonry unit available in various grades and finishes for structural and aesthetic applications.

name: Concrete Brick
description: A masonry unit manufactured from Portland cement and aggregate, used as a cost-effective alternative to clay brick.

name: Sand Lime Brick
description: A calcium-silicate masonry unit made from sand and lime, known for its smooth finish and dimensional accuracy.

name: Fire Brick
description: A refractory masonry unit designed to withstand high temperatures, used in fireplaces, kilns, and furnaces.

name: Fly Ash Brick
description: An eco-friendly masonry unit produced using fly ash, a coal combustion by-product, offering good compressive strength.

name: Engineering Brick
description: A high-density, low-absorption brick used in applications requiring superior strength and moisture resistance.

name: Facing Brick
description: A brick with a decorative exposed surface intended for visible external or internal wall finishes.

name: Common Brick
description: A general-purpose structural brick not intended for aesthetic exposure, used in backing courses and infill.

name: Hollow Brick
description: A masonry unit with internal voids that reduce weight and improve thermal and acoustic insulation performance.

name: Perforated Brick
description: A brick containing vertical perforations that reduce weight and improve mortar key for better wall bonding.

name: Reclaimed Brick
description: A salvaged brick recovered from demolished structures, valued for its aged appearance and sustainable reuse.

name: Brick Mortar
description: A cementitious or lime-based bonding compound used to join masonry units and transfer loads between them.

name: Brick Veneer
description: A single-wythe non-structural brick cladding layer applied to an external wall frame for aesthetic purposes.

name: Brick Wall
description: A structural or partition wall assembly constructed from brick units laid in a defined bond pattern with mortar joints.

name: Brick Arch
description: A curved masonry spanning element built from wedge-shaped or standard bricks to bridge openings.

name: Brick Column
description: A freestanding or engaged masonry pier constructed from brick units to carry vertical compressive loads.

name: Brick Lintel
description: A horizontal spanning element above an opening formed from soldier-course bricks, often steel-reinforced.

name: Brick Coping
description: A protective brick cap placed on top of a wall to shed water and prevent moisture ingress.

name: Brick Pavement
description: A hardscape surface layer constructed from brick units laid on a prepared sub-base for pedestrian or vehicular use.

name: Brick Bond Pattern
description: The defined arrangement of brick courses — such as Flemish, English, or Running bond — that determines structural and visual performance.

name: Bricklaying
description: The skilled trade activity of laying and bonding brick units with mortar to construct walls, piers, and other masonry elements.

name: Brick Cutting
description: The process of scoring and splitting or sawing bricks to fit non-standard dimensions at wall returns, openings, and closures.

name: Brick Pointing
description: The activity of finishing or repairing mortar joints between bricks for improved weather resistance and appearance.

name: Brick Cleaning
description: The post-construction or maintenance process of removing mortar stains, efflorescence, and soiling from brick surfaces.

name: Brick Demolition
description: The controlled dismantling or removal of brick masonry elements during renovation, repair, or building deconstruction.

name: Brick Repointing
description: A maintenance activity involving the removal of deteriorated mortar joints and their replacement with fresh mortar.

name: Masonry System
description: The overall structural and enclosure system comprising brick units, mortar, ties, lintels, and reinforcement working together.

name: Brick Insulation
description: Thermal insulation board or fill material installed within a cavity or behind a brick wall to meet energy performance requirements.

name: IfcBuildingElementProxy (Brick Unit)
description: An IFC representation class used to model individual or assembled brick masonry elements within a BIM environment.

name: Cement Mortar
description: A mortar mix made primarily from Portland cement, sand, and water, known for high strength and durability in structural applications.

name: Lime Mortar
description: A traditional mortar composed of lime putty or hydraulic lime and sand, valued for its flexibility and breathability in historic masonry.

name: Gypsum Mortar
description: A fast-setting mortar based on gypsum binder, commonly used for interior plastering and lightweight block laying.

name: Polymer-Modified Mortar
description: Mortar enhanced with polymer additives or latex to improve adhesion, flexibility, and resistance to cracking.

name: Refractory Mortar
description: A heat-resistant mortar formulated for laying firebricks and other refractory materials in furnaces, fireplaces, and chimneys.

name: Epoxy Mortar
description: A two-component mortar using epoxy resin as a binder, offering exceptional chemical resistance and bond strength for industrial floors and repairs.

name: Pre-Mixed Mortar
description: Factory-batched dry or wet mortar supplied ready to use, ensuring consistent mix proportions on site.

name: Rapid-Setting Mortar
description: A mortar formulated with accelerators to achieve fast early strength gain, used in repair and time-critical laying operations.

name: Coloured Mortar
description: Mortar incorporating pigments to match or contrast with masonry units for aesthetic jointing purposes.

name: Masonry Sand
description: Fine aggregate specifically graded for mortar production to control workability, strength, and joint appearance.

name: Hydrated Lime
description: Calcium hydroxide powder added to mortar mixes to improve workability, water retention, and long-term durability.

name: Mortar Admixture
description: Chemical additives such as plasticisers, retarders, or air-entraining agents used to modify the fresh or hardened properties of mortar.

name: Mortar Binder
description: The cementitious or hydraulic component (cement, lime, gypsum, or a blend) that provides cohesion and strength to the mortar matrix.

name: Mortar Joint
description: The filled gap between masonry units where mortar hardens to bond elements and distribute loads.

name: Bed Joint
description: The horizontal mortar layer placed beneath each course of masonry units to transfer compressive loads.

name: Perpend Joint
description: The vertical mortar joint between masonry units within the same course, also known as a cross joint or head joint.

name: Collar Joint
description: A vertical longitudinal mortar joint filling the space between two wythes of a masonry wall.

name: Mortar Mixing
description: The construction activity of combining binder, aggregate, water, and admixtures to produce a homogeneous mortar mix on site or in a batching plant.

name: Mortar Application
description: The process of spreading or placing mortar onto masonry surfaces or substrates during bricklaying, block laying, or plastering.

name: Repointing
description: The remedial activity of removing deteriorated mortar from existing masonry joints and replacing it with fresh mortar to restore weathertightness and aesthetics.

name: Mortar Curing
description: The process of maintaining adequate moisture and temperature conditions after mortar placement to ensure proper hydration and strength development.

name: Mortar Testing
description: Laboratory or site-based evaluation of fresh and hardened mortar properties such as compressive strength, workability, and water retention.

name: Grouting
description: The activity of filling voids, cores, or gaps in masonry or concrete structures with a fluid cementitious mix related to mortar compositions.

name: Pointing System
description: The overall specification and execution approach for mortar joint profiles and finishes on exposed masonry facades.

name: Render System
description: A layered external or internal coating system comprising scratch coat, base coat, and finish coat mortar applied to substrates for protection and appearance.

name: IFC Mortar Material
description: The IfcMaterial entity in IFC schema used to represent mortar as a construction material with associated properties and classification references.

name: Deformed Rebar
description: A ribbed or deformed steel bar providing enhanced mechanical bond with surrounding concrete through surface protrusions.

name: Plain Round Bar
description: A smooth, circular-section steel bar used in applications where bond strength is less critical, such as links or stirrups.

name: Epoxy-Coated Rebar
description: A steel bar coated with an epoxy layer to resist corrosion, commonly used in marine or chloride-exposed environments.

name: Galvanized Rebar
description: A steel bar with a zinc coating applied to inhibit corrosion in moderately aggressive exposure conditions.

name: Stainless Steel Rebar
description: A corrosion-resistant rebar manufactured from stainless steel alloy, used where long service life in aggressive environments is required.

name: Fibre-Reinforced Polymer (FRP) Rebar
description: A non-metallic rebar composed of glass, carbon, or basalt fibres in a polymer matrix, offering high strength and corrosion immunity.

name: High-Yield Steel Bar (Grade 500)
description: A high-tensile deformed rebar with a characteristic yield strength of 500 MPa, the most common structural grade in modern construction.

name: Mild Steel Bar (Grade 250)
description: A lower-strength plain or deformed bar with a yield strength of 250 MPa, used in light-duty or legacy structural applications.

name: Welded Wire Mesh / Fabric
description: A prefabricated grid of steel wires or bars welded at intersections, used to reinforce slabs and walls efficiently.

name: Helical / Spiral Reinforcement
description: Continuously wound steel bar forming a helix, used as confinement reinforcement around the core of columns and piles.

name: Stirrup / Link
description: A closed or open loop of bar bent to a specified shape, providing shear resistance and lateral confinement in beams and columns.

name: Transverse Reinforcement Bar
description: Bars placed perpendicular to the main reinforcement to resist shear, torsion, and lateral bursting forces.

name: Lap Splice
description: An overlap joint between two bar ends that transfers force by bond, used where continuous bar lengths are not practical.

name: Mechanical Coupler / Bar Coupler
description: A threaded or swaged device used to connect two rebar ends end-to-end, providing a full-strength mechanical joint.

name: Rebar Spacer / Cover Block
description: A plastic, concrete, or steel device used to maintain the specified concrete cover distance between reinforcement and formwork.

name: Bar Chair
description: A support device placed beneath reinforcement mats or cages to hold them at the correct elevation within formwork.

name: Rebar Cutting
description: The process of cutting steel bars to required lengths using shears, disc cutters, or hydraulic cutting machines on site or in a fabrication yard.

name: Rebar Bending
description: The mechanical shaping of bars into specified profiles—hooks, cranks, links, and spirals—using manual or powered bending equipment.

name: Rebar Fixing / Placement
description: The on-site activity of positioning, tying, and securing reinforcement bars in correct location and alignment before concrete is cast.

name: Bar Tying / Wire Tying
description: The process of securing bar intersections with annealed steel wire or automated tying tools to maintain the reinforcement assembly during concreting.

name: Welding of Reinforcement
description: Structural welding of bar connections where mechanical couplers or laps are not used, requiring certified procedures and qualified welders.

name: Rebar Prefabrication / Off-Site Fabrication
description: The factory or yard-based cutting, bending, and cage assembly of reinforcement prior to delivery to site.

name: Reinforcement Inspection & Testing
description: Quality assurance activities including dimensional checks, material certification review, bar identification, and pull-out or tensile testing.

name: Concrete Cover Checking
description: Verification using cover meters or direct measurement that the required protective concrete cover over reinforcement meets design specifications.

name: Reinforcement Scheduling (Bar Schedule)
description: The preparation of detailed bar bending schedules listing bar marks, shapes, dimensions, and quantities for procurement and fabrication.

name: Corrosion Protection System
description: An integrated set of measures—coatings, cathodic protection, inhibitors, or cover requirements—applied to protect embedded reinforcement from corrosion.

name: Prefabrication / Rebar Yard
description: A dedicated facility or site zone equipped for the cutting, bending, and assembly of reinforcement cages and bar assemblies.

name: Rebar Storage Area
description: A designated on-site or off-site area for the organised storage of steel bars, protecting them from contamination and corrosion prior to use.

name: Wide Flange (W-Section)
description: An I-shaped steel section with parallel flanges widely used in beams and columns due to its high strength-to-weight ratio.

name: HSS Rectangular Tube
description: Hollow structural section with a rectangular cross-section, commonly used for columns, braces, and architectural elements.

name: HSS Round Tube (Pipe Section)
description: Circular hollow structural section offering uniform strength in all directions, used for columns and truss members.

name: S-Section (American Standard Beam)
description: An I-shaped section with sloped inner flange surfaces, historically used in beams and crane rails.

name: C-Channel (MC/C-Section)
description: A C-shaped cross-section used for purlins, girts, bracing, and secondary framing members.

name: L-Section (Angle)
description: An L-shaped steel section available in equal or unequal legs, used for bracing, connections, and edge framing.

name: T-Section (WT Cut)
description: A T-shaped section typically cut from a wide flange, used for chord members in trusses and connection plates.

name: Z-Section (Z-Purlin)
description: A Z-shaped cold-formed section used as roof purlins and wall girts in metal building systems.

name: Plate Steel
