description: Flat rolled steel plate used to fabricate built-up sections, connection plates, base plates, and stiffeners.

name: Built-Up Girder
description: A custom fabricated beam assembled by welding or bolting plates and standard sections to meet specific load demands.

name: Steel Brace
description: A diagonal structural member resisting lateral forces such as wind and seismic loads within a steel frame.

name: Base Plate
description: A steel plate welded to the bottom of a column to distribute loads onto a concrete foundation or pedestal.

name: Connection Plate / Gusset Plate
description: A flat steel plate used at joints to connect beams, columns, and braces via bolts or welds.

name: Shear Tab
description: A simple shear connection plate shop-welded to a column or girder web to receive incoming beam ends.

name: Stiffener Plate
description: A plate welded to a web or flange to prevent local buckling and distribute concentrated loads.

name: Moment Frame System
description: A lateral force-resisting system where rigidly connected beams and columns resist lateral loads through bending.

name: Braced Frame System
description: A lateral force-resisting system that uses diagonal braces to transfer horizontal loads to the foundation.

name: Steel Deck (Composite)
description: Corrugated steel decking acting compositely with a concrete topping slab to form efficient floor or roof systems.

name: Bolted Connection Installation
description: The activity of installing, tightening, and inspecting high-strength bolts to specified pretension levels at structural joints.

name: Welding (Structural)
description: The process of fusing steel members using certified welding procedures to create permanent structural connections.

name: Steel Surface Preparation & Priming
description: Cleaning and applying primer or protective coatings to steel sections to prevent corrosion before and after erection.

name: Fireproofing Application (SFRM)
description: Applying spray-applied fire-resistive material to structural steel to achieve the required fire-resistance rating.

name: Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) of Welds
description: Inspection activities such as ultrasonic or magnetic particle testing used to verify weld quality without damaging the member.

name: Steel Plumb & Alignment Survey
description: Survey activity to verify that erected steel columns and frames are within tolerance for plumbness and alignment.

name: High-Strength Bolt
description: A structural fastener (e.g., ASTM A325/A490) used in slip-critical or bearing-type connections between steel members.

name: Shear Stud (Headed Anchor)
description: A welded steel stud that mechanically connects a steel beam to a concrete slab to enable composite action.

name: IfcStructuralMember
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcStructuralItem. Abstract type (not directly instantiable).

name: Standard Plasterboard Sheet
description: A regular gypsum-core plasterboard panel used for general wall and ceiling lining applications.

name: Moisture-Resistant Plasterboard
description: A specially treated plasterboard variant designed for use in high-humidity environments such as bathrooms and kitchens.

name: Fire-Resistant Plasterboard
description: Plasterboard with enhanced fire-retardant properties, typically containing glass fibres, used to achieve required fire ratings.

name: Thermal Plasterboard
description: Plasterboard bonded with an insulating layer (e.g. PIR or EPS foam) to provide improved thermal performance.

name: Impact-Resistant Plasterboard
description: A reinforced plasterboard variant offering greater resistance to surface damage in high-traffic or commercial areas.

name: Flexible Plasterboard
description: A thin, bendable plasterboard sheet used for curved or radius wall and ceiling applications.

name: Plasterboard Fixing Screw
description: A self-tapping drywall screw specifically designed to secure plasterboard sheets to timber or metal framing.

name: Plasterboard Adhesive
description: A bonding compound (dot-and-dab) used to fix plasterboard directly onto masonry or concrete substrates without mechanical fixings.

name: Joint Tape
description: Paper or fibreglass mesh tape embedded in jointing compound to reinforce and conceal the seams between adjacent plasterboard sheets.

name: Jointing Compound
description: A gypsum-based filler applied over joint tape and screw heads to create a smooth, seamless plasterboard surface.

name: Corner Bead
description: A metal or plastic extrusion fixed to external corners of plasterboard to protect edges and provide a straight, clean finish.

name: Metal Stud Framing
description: Light-gauge steel C-section studs and tracks that form the structural frame to which plasterboard is attached in partition walls and drywall systems.

name: Timber Stud Framing
description: Timber batten or stud framework used as the structural substrate for fixing plasterboard in walls and ceilings.

name: Resilient Bar
description: A spring-steel channel fixed between studs/joists and plasterboard to acoustically decouple the board from the structure and reduce sound transmission.

name: Plasterboard Ceiling System
description: An assembled system of suspension grid, hangers, and plasterboard panels forming a finished ceiling plane.

name: Drywall Partition System
description: A complete non-load-bearing internal wall system comprising metal or timber studs, plasterboard skins, and any insulation or services within the cavity.

name: Shaft Wall System
description: A specialised plasterboard assembly designed to line lift shafts and service risers, providing fire and acoustic separation.

name: Plasterboard Installation
description: The site activity of measuring, cutting, lifting, and fixing plasterboard sheets to frames or substrates.

name: Plasterboard Taping and Jointing
description: The finishing trade activity of applying tape and jointing compound to plasterboard seams and screw heads to prepare a smooth surface.

name: Plasterboard Sanding and Finishing
description: The process of sanding dried jointing compound to achieve a level, paint-ready surface on a plasterboard installation.

name: Plasterboard Cutting
description: The preparatory activity of scoring and snapping, or sawing, plasterboard sheets to required dimensions and shapes on site.

name: Dot-and-Dab Application
description: The technique of applying adhesive dabs to a masonry wall and pressing plasterboard directly onto them without stud framing.

name: Plasterboard Boarding (IFC)
description: The IFC classification entity representing plasterboard-lined wall or ceiling elements within a building information model.

name: Gypsum Core
description: The calcium sulphate dihydrate core material that gives plasterboard its rigidity, fire resistance, and surface stability.

name: Paper Facing
description: The kraft-paper liner bonded to both faces of a plasterboard sheet that provides tensile strength and a paintable surface.

name: Plasterboard Waste Management
description: The site activity of segregating, storing, and arranging recycling or disposal of plasterboard offcuts and waste in compliance with waste regulations.

name: Bonded Screed
description: A screed layer mechanically or adhesively bonded directly to the structural substrate to prevent delamination.

name: Unbonded Screed
description: A screed laid on a separating membrane over the substrate, allowing independent movement from the base.

name: Floating Screed
description: A screed cast over an insulation or acoustic layer without bonding to the structural base, used in thermal and acoustic floor systems.

name: Screed Mix Design
description: The specific ratio of cement, sand, and water (or alternative binders) formulated to achieve required strength and workability for a screed pour.

name: Sand-Cement Screed
description: Traditional screed composed of sharp sand and Portland cement mixed at a defined ratio, widely used as a floor levelling layer.

name: Calcium Sulphate (Anhydrite) Screed
description: A flow-applied screed using a calcium sulphate binder, offering self-levelling properties and compatibility with underfloor heating.

name: Self-Levelling Screed
description: A highly fluid screed compound that flows and settles to a flat surface under gravity with minimal manual intervention.

name: Rapid-Drying Screed
description: A screed formulation incorporating special binders or admixtures to significantly reduce drying and curing time before floor finishes are applied.

name: Polymer-Modified Screed
description: A screed enhanced with polymer additives to improve flexibility, adhesion, and resistance to cracking.

name: Fibre-Reinforced Screed
description: A screed containing synthetic or steel fibres dispersed through the mix to reduce shrinkage cracking and improve tensile performance.

name: Lightweight Screed
description: A screed using lightweight aggregates such as expanded clay or foamed concrete to reduce dead load on the structure.

name: Heated Screed (UFH Screed)
description: A screed layer specifically designed to encapsulate underfloor heating pipes or electric heating elements, optimising thermal mass and heat transfer.

name: Screed Thickness
description: The specified depth of the screed layer, determined by load requirements, substrate conditions, and the presence of embedded services.

name: Screed Joint
description: A deliberate gap or saw-cut introduced into a screed to control cracking caused by shrinkage, thermal movement, or structural deflection.

name: Screed Bay
description: A defined poured section of screed delimited by screeding rails or joints to manage workable areas and control cracking.

name: Screed Primer
description: A bonding or sealing agent applied to the substrate or screed surface to improve adhesion of subsequent floor finishes or the screed itself.

name: Screed Admixture
description: Chemical additives incorporated into the screed mix to modify properties such as workability, drying time, or frost resistance.

name: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
description: Steel or polypropylene mesh embedded within the screed to control cracking and improve structural integrity.

name: Screed Mixing
description: The site or factory process of combining screed constituents in the correct proportions to produce a homogeneous, workable mix.

name: Screed Laying
description: The construction activity of placing, spreading, and compacting the screed material across the floor area to the required level and falls.

name: Screed Levelling & Screeding Rails
description: The setting out and use of guide rails or pins to achieve an accurate, level surface during the screeding process.

name: Screed Curing
description: The controlled process of maintaining moisture and temperature conditions after screed placement to ensure adequate strength gain and minimise cracking.

name: Screed Drying & Moisture Testing
description: The monitoring and testing of residual moisture content in a cured screed to confirm it is safe to receive floor finishes.

name: Screed Grinding & Surface Preparation
description: Mechanical processing of the cured screed surface to remove high spots, laitance, or contamination prior to application of floor finishes.

name: Screed Repair & Patching
description: Remedial activity to fill cracks, voids, or delaminated areas in an existing screed using compatible repair mortars.

name: Screed Inspection & Testing
description: Quality-assurance checks including soundness testing, level surveys, and strength testing performed on completed screed installations.

name: Separation Layer / Slip Membrane
description: A polythene or similar sheet placed between the substrate and an unbonded or floating screed to prevent adhesion and allow differential movement.

name: Acoustic Underlay (below screed)
description: A resilient layer installed beneath a floating screed to attenuate impact and airborne sound transmission between floors.

name: Thermal Insulation (below screed)
description: Rigid insulation boards placed under a floating screed to provide thermal resistance as part of the floor build-up.

name: Floor Build-Up / Screed System
description: The complete assembly of substrate, separating layers, insulation, screed, and finish that together form the finished floor system.

name: IfcCovering (Floor)
description: The IFC schema class used to represent screed and other floor covering layers within a building information model.

name: Silicone Sealant
description: A flexible, waterproof sealant made from silicone polymers, widely used in wet areas, glazing, and exterior joints.

name: Polyurethane Sealant
description: A durable, paintable sealant offering high adhesion and flexibility, commonly used in construction joints and flooring.

name: Polysulfide Sealant
description: A chemical-resistant sealant ideal for fuel-resistant joints, glazing, and below-grade waterproofing applications.

name: Acrylic Sealant
description: A water-based, paintable sealant used for interior gaps, skirtings, and low-movement joints.

name: Butyl Sealant
description: A synthetic rubber-based sealant with excellent moisture resistance, often used in roofing and curtain wall applications.

name: Epoxy Sealant
description: A two-component, rigid high-strength sealant used for structural bonding and chemical-resistant joint sealing.

name: Intumescent Sealant
description: A fire-stopping sealant that expands when exposed to heat, used to seal penetrations in fire-rated walls and floors.

name: Acoustic Sealant
description: A permanently flexible sealant designed to fill gaps and reduce sound transmission between building elements.

name: Firestop Sealant
description: A passive fire protection material applied to joints and penetrations to prevent the spread of fire and smoke.

name: Weatherseal / Weatherstripping Sealant
description: A flexible sealant applied around doors, windows, and façade openings to prevent air and water infiltration.

name: Expansion Joint Sealant
description: A high-movement sealant specifically formulated to accommodate thermal expansion and contraction in structural joints.

name: Roof Sealant
description: A waterproof sealant applied to roof seams, penetrations, and flashings to prevent moisture ingress.

name: Concrete Joint Sealant
description: A durable sealant used to fill control, construction, and isolation joints in concrete slabs and pavements.

name: Glazing Sealant
description: A sealant specifically formulated for bonding and weatherproofing the interface between glass and framing systems.

name: Sanitary Sealant
description: A mould-resistant sealant used in bathrooms, kitchens, and wet rooms around fixtures and tile edges.

name: Structural Glazing Sealant
description: A high-strength silicone-based sealant used to structurally bond glass panels to building façades without mechanical fixings.

name: Backing Rod
description: A compressible foam rod inserted into joints before sealant application to control sealant depth and improve joint performance.

name: Bond Breaker Tape
description: A tape applied to the back of a joint to prevent the sealant from bonding to three surfaces, ensuring correct two-point adhesion.

name: Primer (Sealant)
description: A preparatory coating applied to joint substrates to improve adhesion between the sealant and the surrounding material.

name: Sealant Removal and Replacement
description: The maintenance activity of cutting out, cleaning, and reapplying failed or degraded sealant in existing joints.

name: Joint Preparation
description: Surface cleaning, widening, and priming activities carried out prior to sealant application to ensure adequate adhesion.

name: Sealant Inspection
description: A periodic assessment of sealant condition, checking for cracking, delamination, discolouration, or loss of adhesion.

name: Tooling (Sealant Finishing)
description: The process of pressing and shaping freshly applied sealant to ensure full contact with joint faces and a neat finish.

name: Caulking Gun
description: A handheld or pneumatic tool used to dispense sealant from cartridges into joints at a controlled rate.

name: Sealant Cartridge
description: A pre-filled, disposable or refillable container that holds sealant for use with a caulking gun.

name: Gasket
description: A pre-formed mechanical seal placed between mating surfaces as an alternative or complement to liquid-applied sealants.

name: Fire-Rated Joint System
description: An integrated assembly of firestop sealants, collars, and wraps designed to maintain the fire rating of a building element.

name: Façade Joint System
description: A coordinated system of sealants, backing rods, and primers used to weatherproof and accommodate movement in external cladding joints.

name: Polyurethane Adhesive
description: A flexible, moisture-curing adhesive suitable for bonding dissimilar materials such as wood, metal, and concrete.

name: Cyanoacrylate Adhesive
description: A fast-curing, single-component adhesive used for rapid bonding of small components and repairs on-site.

name: Silicone Adhesive
description: A highly flexible, waterproof adhesive ideal for sealing and bonding in wet or high-temperature environments.

name: Acrylic Adhesive
description: A durable, UV-resistant adhesive used for bonding glass, metals, and plastics in both interior and exterior applications.

name: Contact Cement
description: A solvent-based adhesive applied to both surfaces that bonds on contact, widely used for laminates and rubber.

name: Construction Adhesive
description: A general-purpose, heavy-duty adhesive used to bond structural elements such as subfloors, panels, and framing members.

name: Hot Melt Adhesive
description: A thermoplastic adhesive applied in molten form that solidifies quickly upon cooling, used for fast assembly and trim work.

name: Tile Adhesive
description: A cement- or polymer-based adhesive specifically formulated for fixing ceramic, porcelain, and stone tiles to surfaces.

name: Flooring Adhesive
description: A pressure-sensitive or hard-set adhesive designed for installing resilient, hardwood, or carpet flooring systems.

name: Structural Adhesive
description: A high-performance adhesive engineered to carry significant loads and replace or supplement mechanical fasteners in structural joints.

name: Pressure-Sensitive Adhesive (PSA)
description: An adhesive that forms a bond when light pressure is applied, used in tapes, labels, and membrane overlaps in building wraps.

name: Moisture-Cure Adhesive
description: An adhesive that uses ambient humidity to initiate and complete its curing process, suitable for damp substrates.

name: Elastomeric Adhesive
description: A rubber-based adhesive that retains flexibility after curing, accommodating thermal movement between bonded substrates.

name: Solvent-Based Adhesive
description: An adhesive dissolved in organic solvents that bonds by solvent evaporation, offering strong initial tack on porous materials.

name: Water-Based Adhesive
description: An environmentally friendlier adhesive using water as the carrier, commonly used for wallcoverings, paper, and light assembly.

name: Adhesive Primer
description: A preparatory coating applied to substrates to improve adhesion strength and compatibility before bonding operations.

name: Adhesive Bonding
description: The construction process of joining two or more building components by applying and curing an adhesive at their interface.

name: Surface Preparation for Bonding
description: The cleaning, abrading, or priming of substrate surfaces to ensure optimal adhesion performance prior to adhesive application.

name: Adhesive Application
description: The controlled dispensing or spreading of adhesive onto a substrate using tools such as trowels, guns, or rollers.

name: Cure Time Management
description: The scheduling and monitoring of adhesive curing periods to ensure full bond strength before loading or further construction.

name: Adhesive Joint
description: The discrete interface zone between two building elements where an adhesive has been applied and cured to create a bond.

name: Adhesive Dispenser / Caulking Gun
description: A hand-held or pneumatic device used to precisely apply cartridge- or tube-packaged adhesives on-site.

name: Adhesive Storage Area
description: A designated, climate-controlled space on a construction site for safe storage of adhesive products within manufacturer-specified temperature ranges.

name: Adhesive Tape
description: A strip of backing material coated with pressure-sensitive adhesive, used for sealing joints, securing membranes, and temporary fixings.

name: IfcAdhesiveFastener
description: An IFC classification entity representing adhesive-based fastening elements within a Building Information Model (BIM).

name: Interior Wall Paint
description: Paint formulated specifically for application on interior wall surfaces, available in various sheens such as matte, eggshell, and satin.

name: Exterior Paint
description: Weather-resistant paint designed for outdoor surfaces to withstand UV exposure, moisture, and temperature fluctuations.

name: Primer
description: Preparatory base coat applied before paint to improve adhesion, seal surfaces, and enhance final color uniformity.

name: Undercoat
description: Intermediate coating layer applied between primer and topcoat to build film thickness and improve opacity.

name: Topcoat
description: The final decorative and protective layer of a paint system that determines the surface's appearance and durability.

name: Ceiling Paint
description: Flat-finish paint specially formulated for ceiling surfaces to minimize light reflection and hide surface imperfections.

name: Floor Paint
description: Heavy-duty paint engineered to resist foot traffic, abrasion, and chemical exposure on floor substrates.

name: Masonry Paint
description: Breathable, water-resistant paint formulated for application on brick, concrete, and other masonry surfaces.

name: Metal Paint
description: Corrosion-inhibiting paint designed for steel, iron, and other metallic substrates in structural or decorative applications.

name: Wood Stain
description: Penetrating colorant applied to timber to enhance or alter grain appearance while preserving natural texture.

name: Varnish
description: Clear or tinted protective finish applied to wood and other surfaces to provide a hard, durable, and glossy coating.

name: Lacquer
description: Fast-drying solvent-based or water-based clear coating that forms a hard, high-gloss protective film on surfaces.

name: Epoxy Paint
description: Two-component chemical-resistant coating widely used on floors, walls, and industrial surfaces for maximum durability.

name: Fire-Retardant Paint
description: Intumescent or flame-resistant paint that swells under heat to slow the spread of fire across building surfaces.

name: Textured Paint
description: Paint containing aggregates or additives that create a three-dimensional relief texture on applied surfaces.

name: Waterproof Paint
description: Elastomeric or polymer-based coating that forms a watertight barrier on walls, roofs, and wet-area surfaces.

name: Anti-Mold Paint
description: Paint containing biocidal additives that inhibit mold, mildew, and fungal growth on interior surfaces.

name: Heat-Resistant Paint
description: High-temperature coating formulated to maintain adhesion and appearance on surfaces exposed to extreme heat, such as radiators and flues.

name: Road Marking Paint
description: Durable, retroreflective paint used on pavement and car park surfaces to delineate lanes, bays, and hazard zones.

name: Paint Solvent / Thinner
description: Chemical agent used to dilute paint to the correct application viscosity or to clean brushes and equipment after use.

name: Paint Additive
description: Substance mixed into paint to modify properties such as drying time, flow, leveling, or microbial resistance.

name: Painting (Application)
description: The physical process of applying paint coats to a building surface using brushes, rollers, or spray equipment.

name: Spray Painting
description: Mechanized paint application technique using pressurized spray equipment for uniform, high-speed coverage of large areas.

name: Paint Stripping / Removal
description: Process of removing existing paint layers from a surface using chemical strippers, heat guns, or abrasive methods prior to repainting.

name: Touch-Up Painting
description: Localized reapplication of paint to repair minor damage, scuffs, or coating failures on previously finished surfaces.

name: Paint Inspection & Quality Control
description: Assessment of applied paint for defects such as blistering, cracking, or inadequate coverage to ensure compliance with specifications.

name: Colour Scheduling
description: Design and documentation process that assigns specific paint colours and finishes to each surface or zone within a building project.

name: Paint Storage Area
description: Dedicated, ventilated, and fire-safe room or zone within a building or site facility used to store paint materials and equipment.

name: Paint Brush
description: Hand tool with bristles used to manually apply paint to surfaces, edges, and intricate architectural details.

name: Paint Roller
description: Cylindrical foam or fabric tool used to apply paint quickly and evenly across large flat surfaces.

name: Airless Spray Gun
description: High-pressure mechanical device that atomizes and projects paint onto surfaces for fast, uniform application.

name: Paint Tray
description: Shallow container used to hold and load paint onto a roller during manual painting operations.

name: Scaffolding / Access Equipment
description: Temporary elevated platform system erected to allow painters safe access to high or inaccessible building surfaces.

name: Paint Mixing System
description: Equipment or process used to blend base paints with colorants to achieve specified hues and consistent batch-to-batch colour accuracy.

name: Mineral Wool Acoustic Batt
description: A dense, fibrous batt made from rock or slag wool, used inside wall cavities and floor assemblies to absorb airborne sound.

name: Fiberglass Acoustic Batt
description: Glass-fiber batt insulation selected for its sound-damping properties in partition walls and ceiling assemblies.

name: Cellulose Acoustic Fill
description: Recycled paper-based loose-fill material blown into cavities to reduce sound transmission between spaces.

name: Mass Loaded Vinyl (MLV)
description: A thin, heavy flexible membrane added to walls, floors, or ceilings to block airborne sound through added mass.

name: Acoustic Foam Panel
description: Open-cell polyurethane or melamine foam panels applied to surfaces to absorb mid-to-high frequency sound waves.

name: Resilient Channel
description: A thin metal furring strip that decouples drywall from structural framing to interrupt structure-borne vibration paths.

name: Sound Isolation Clip
description: A rubber-and-metal clip that suspends hat channels away from framing, providing superior vibration decoupling over standard resilient channels.

name: Acoustic Underlayment
description: A thin layer of foam, cork, or rubber installed beneath floor finishes to reduce impact noise transmission to the floor below.

name: Cork Acoustic Board
description: Natural cork panels used as a wall or floor treatment to absorb sound and reduce impact noise due to cork's cellular structure.

name: Acoustic Sealant (Acoustical Caulk)
description: A permanently flexible, non-hardening sealant applied around penetrations and perimeters to close flanking paths for airborne sound.

name: Soundproof Drywall
description: Gypsum board engineered with constrained-layer damping compounds to achieve higher sound transmission class (STC) ratings than standard drywall.

name: Acoustic Ceiling Tile
description: Suspended ceiling tiles with high noise reduction coefficient (NRC) ratings, used in both commercial and residential settings.

name: Green Glue Damping Compound
description: A viscoelastic compound applied between two rigid panels (e.g., drywall layers) to convert sound energy into heat.

name: Rubber Acoustic Flooring
description: Dense rubber sheet or tile flooring that provides impact noise isolation in gyms, mechanical rooms, and multi-family buildings.

name: Acoustic Wall Assembly
description: An integrated wall system combining framing, insulation, decoupling hardware, and finish layers to meet a specified STC rating.

name: Floating Floor System
description: A floor construction method that isolates the finished floor surface from the structural slab using resilient isolators to control impact noise.

name: Acoustic Ceiling System
description: A suspended or applied ceiling system engineered with damping, decoupling, and absorptive layers to control both airborne and impact noise.

name: Sound-Rated Door Assembly
description: A door unit with an STC-rated core, gasketing, and threshold seal designed to maintain the acoustic integrity of an enclosing wall.

name: Acoustic Window Assembly
description: A laminated or multi-pane window unit with enhanced glazing and frame seals engineered to reduce external noise infiltration.

name: Installation of Acoustic Insulation
description: The trade activity of fitting, cutting, and placing acoustic batts, boards, or loose-fill material within building assemblies.

name: Acoustic Testing and Commissioning
description: Field measurement of STC and impact insulation class (IIC) values in completed assemblies to verify design performance targets.

name: Acoustic Design and Specification
description: The engineering or architectural activity of selecting materials, assemblies, and details to achieve required noise control criteria.

name: Flanking Path Inspection
description: A quality-control activity that identifies and seals gaps, penetrations, and structural connections that bypass the primary acoustic barrier.

name: Home Theatre / Media Room
description: A specialized room designed with acoustic insulation and treatment to achieve high sound containment and controlled internal acoustics.

name: Recording Studio
description: A professionally acoustic-isolated space that relies on multiple layers of acoustic insulation and decoupling to meet stringent noise criteria.

name: IfcAcousticInsulation (IFC Classification)
description: The IFC schema class used to represent acoustic insulation elements in BIM models for data exchange and facility management.

name: Calcium Silicate Board
description: A high-density fire-resistant board made from calcium silicate, offering excellent thermal insulation and fire protection up to very high temperatures.

name: Gypsum-Based Fire Board
description: A fire-resistant board composed primarily of gypsum core, widely used for partition walls and ceilings due to its passive fire protection properties.

name: Magnesium Oxide Board
description: A fire-resistant panel manufactured from magnesium oxide, known for its superior fire rating, moisture resistance, and structural strength.

name: Vermiculite Board
description: A lightweight fire-resistant board incorporating expanded vermiculite, commonly used for lining fire-rated enclosures and structural steelwork protection.

name: Intumescent Board
description: A reactive fire-resistant board that expands when exposed to heat, sealing gaps and preventing the spread of fire and smoke through penetrations.

name: Cement-Bonded Particle Board
description: A fire-resistant board formed by binding wood particles with Portland cement, offering fire resistance combined with structural rigidity.

name: Fire-Resistant Board Substrate
description: The structural backing layer onto which fire-resistant boards are fixed, providing load-bearing support and alignment within an assembly.

name: Fire-Resistant Board Fixing System
description: The screws, adhesives, clips, or brackets used to mechanically attach fire-resistant boards securely to substrates or framing systems.

name: Fire-Resistant Board Joint Tape
description: A specialised tape applied over board joints to maintain the fire integrity of the overall board assembly and prevent crack propagation.

name: Fire-Resistant Board Jointing Compound
description: A fire-rated filler compound used to finish and seal the joints between abutting fire-resistant boards in wall and ceiling assemblies.

name: Fire-Rated Wall Assembly
description: A complete wall system incorporating fire-resistant boards as a primary element to achieve a specified fire-resistance level (FRL) for separating spaces.

name: Fire-Rated Ceiling Assembly
description: A ceiling system that uses fire-resistant boards as the lining layer to protect the structure above and delay flame and heat passage between floors.

name: Structural Steel Fire Protection System
description: A system of boards or casing applied around structural steelwork to delay temperature rise and maintain load-bearing capacity during a fire event.

name: Passive Fire Protection System
description: The broader building system encompassing all static, non-active measures—including fire-resistant boards—to contain, limit, and retard the spread of fire.

name: Fire-Resistant Board Installation
description: The construction activity of cutting, fitting, and fixing fire-resistant boards to walls, ceilings, columns, or beams following manufacturer and regulatory specifications.

name: Fire-Resistant Board Jointing and Finishing
description: The process of taping, filling, and sanding board joints to achieve a smooth, fire-rated surface finish ready for decoration or further treatment.

name: Fire Rating Testing
description: A formal activity in which board assemblies are subjected to standardised fire exposure tests to verify and certify their fire-resistance performance.

name: Fire Stop Installation
description: The activity of sealing penetrations and service openings in fire-resistant board assemblies with rated materials to maintain the required fire barrier integrity.

name: Fire-Resistant Board Inspection
description: A quality-assurance activity in which installed fire-resistant board assemblies are checked against fire-rating specifications, fixing schedules, and regulatory requirements.

name: Fire-Resistant Board Removal and Replacement
description: The maintenance or remediation activity of safely removing damaged or non-compliant fire boards and reinstating new boards to restore fire-rating performance.

name: Fire-Rated Shaft
description: A vertically enclosed space lined with fire-resistant boards to contain mechanical, electrical, or plumbing services while preventing fire spread between floors.

name: Fire-Rated Compartment
description: A building zone bounded by fire-resistant board assemblies and other rated elements to contain a fire within a defined area for a specified duration.

name: Fire-Resistant Board Coating
description: A specialised surface coating applied to fire-resistant boards to enhance moisture resistance, improve finish quality, or add additional fire-protection performance.

name: Cementitious Grout
description: A grout type composed primarily of Portland cement, water, and sometimes sand, used for general filling and anchoring applications.

name: Epoxy Grout
description: A chemical-resistant, high-strength grout made from epoxy resins and a filler powder, ideal for industrial and wet environments.

name: Non-Shrink Grout
description: A pre-blended grout formulated with expansive agents to eliminate shrinkage during curing, commonly used for base plate installations.

name: Sanded Grout
description: A grout variant containing fine sand aggregate, suitable for filling wider tile joints (typically greater than 3 mm).

name: Unsanded Grout
description: A smooth, fine-textured grout without sand aggregate, used for narrow tile joints to avoid scratching delicate tile surfaces.

name: Furan Grout
description: A highly chemical- and heat-resistant grout based on furan resin, used in laboratories and industrial floors exposed to aggressive chemicals.

name: Latex-Modified Grout
description: A cementitious grout enhanced with polymer latex additives to improve flexibility, adhesion, and resistance to cracking.

name: Structural Grout
description: A high-strength, flowable grout used to fill voids in structural elements such as post-tensioning ducts and precast connections.

name: Masonry Grout
description: A fluid mixture of cement, aggregate, and water poured into the cores and cavities of concrete masonry unit (CMU) walls for structural reinforcement.

name: Coloured Grout
description: Grout formulated or pigmented to a specific colour for aesthetic coordination with tiles and surface finishes.

name: Tile Grouting
description: The construction activity of applying and finishing grout between tile joints on floors, walls, or ceilings after tile adhesive has cured.

name: Grouting of Post-Tensioning Ducts
description: The specialised process of injecting cementitious or epoxy grout into post-tensioning conduits to protect tendons from corrosion and bond them to the structure.

name: Base Plate Grouting
description: The activity of placing non-shrink grout beneath structural steel base plates to ensure full, even bearing on the foundation.

name: Anchor Bolt Grouting
description: The process of filling drilled holes with grout to fix anchor bolts or threaded rods into concrete or masonry substrates.

name: CMU Core Grouting
description: The construction activity of filling the hollow cores of concrete masonry units with masonry grout to create reinforced masonry walls.

name: Grout Injection / Pressure Grouting
description: A ground-improvement or repair technique where grout is injected under pressure to fill voids, cracks, or soil pores and improve structural integrity.

name: Grout Mixing
description: The preparatory activity of combining dry or liquid grout components in correct proportions, typically using mechanical mixers for consistency.

name: Grout Curing
description: The post-application process of maintaining moisture and temperature conditions to ensure proper strength development of placed grout.

name: Grout Admixture
description: Chemical additives such as plasticisers, accelerators, or retarders blended into grout mixes to modify workability, set time, or strength.

name: Grout Float
description: A rubber-faced hand tool used to spread and press grout into tile joints during the tile grouting activity.

name: Grout Pump
description: Mechanical equipment used to deliver and inject fluid grout under controlled pressure into ducts, voids, or cavities.

name: Grout Bag / Pointing Bag
description: A cloth or rubber bag with a nozzle used to manually squeeze grout into masonry joints and hard-to-reach areas.

name: Grout Spacer
description: A plastic cross or T-shaped insert placed between tiles during installation to maintain consistent joint width for grouting.

name: Grout Sealer
description: A penetrating or topical sealant applied over cured grout to protect it from staining, moisture ingress, and microbial growth.

name: Grout Joint
description: The intentional gap between adjacent tiles, masonry units, or precast panels that is filled with grout to complete the assembly.

name: Duct / Grout Duct
description: A metallic or plastic conduit embedded in post-tensioned concrete through which tendons run and which is subsequently filled with protective grout.

name: Grout Vent / Vent Port
description: An outlet port installed along a grout duct or void to allow air and bleed water to escape during grout injection, ensuring complete filling.

name: Oxidised Bitumen
description: Bitumen that has been air-blown to increase its softening point and hardness, commonly used in roofing and waterproofing applications.

name: Polymer-Modified Bitumen (PMB)
description: Bitumen enhanced with polymers such as SBS or APP to improve elasticity, durability, and temperature resistance.

name: Cutback Bitumen
description: Bitumen dissolved in a petroleum solvent to reduce viscosity for easier application in road and waterproofing works.

name: Bitumen Emulsion
description: A dispersion of bitumen in water used as a cold-applied binder for road surfacing, tack coats, and damp-proofing.

name: Mastic Asphalt
description: A dense, impermeable mixture of bitumen and fine aggregate used for flooring, roofing, and waterproofing layers.

name: Bituminous Waterproofing Membrane
description: A pre-fabricated sheet product made from bitumen (often polymer-modified) applied to roofs, basements, and foundations to prevent water ingress.

name: Bituminous Damp-Proof Course (DPC)
description: A horizontal layer of bitumen-based material installed in masonry walls to prevent rising damp.

name: Bituminous Paint / Coating
description: A liquid bitumen-based coating brushed or sprayed onto surfaces for corrosion protection and waterproofing.

name: Bituminous Felt (Sarking Felt)
description: A flexible sheet material made from bitumen-impregnated fibre used as an underlay beneath roof coverings.

name: Cold-Applied Bitumen Adhesive
description: A solvent- or water-based bitumen adhesive used to bond waterproofing membranes and insulation boards without heat.

name: Hot-Applied Bitumen Waterproofing
description: The process of melting and applying bitumen in liquid form using a boiler or torch to create a seamless waterproofing layer.

name: Torch-On Membrane Application
description: A waterproofing installation activity where a gas torch is used to heat and bond polymer-modified bitumen sheets to a substrate.

name: Cold Bitumen Application
description: Application of bitumen-based products (emulsions, cutbacks, or adhesives) at ambient temperature without the use of heat.

name: Bituminous Tanking
description: The construction activity of applying multiple layers of bitumen products to basement walls and floors to resist hydrostatic water pressure.

name: Bitumen Priming
description: The preparatory application of a dilute bitumen primer to a surface to improve adhesion of subsequent bitumen-based waterproofing layers.

name: Waterproofing System (Bituminous)
description: An integrated assembly of bitumen-based primers, membranes, and protective layers designed to provide complete water exclusion for a structure.

name: Roof Waterproofing Layer
description: The bituminous membrane or coating layer specifically installed on flat or low-pitched roofs to prevent water penetration.

name: Basement Tanking System
description: A complete below-ground waterproofing system using bituminous products to protect basement spaces from groundwater ingress.

name: Asphalt Road Surfacing
description: The laying and compaction of bitumen-bound aggregate mixtures to form durable road and pavement surfaces.

name: Bitumen Storage Tank
description: A heated tank used on construction sites or in refineries to store and maintain bitumen at the correct working temperature.

name: Bitumen Boiler / Melter
description: Site plant used to heat solid or semi-solid bitumen to a workable liquid state for hot-applied waterproofing operations.

name: IfcCovering (Waterproofing)
description: The IFC classification used to model bituminous waterproofing membranes and coatings as covering elements within a BIM environment.

name: IfcBuildingElementProxy (Bituminous DPC)
description: An IFC proxy element used to represent bituminous damp-proof course components that do not map to a dedicated IFC class.

name: Expanded Polystyrene (EPS)
description: A lightweight, rigid foam insulation board made from expanded polystyrene beads, widely used in wall, roof, and floor insulation applications.

name: Extruded Polystyrene (XPS)
description: A closed-cell rigid foam insulation board produced by extrusion, offering higher compressive strength and moisture resistance than EPS.

name: High-Impact Polystyrene (HIPS)
description: A toughened polystyrene variant blended with rubber for improved impact resistance, used in interior panels and fittings.

name: General Purpose Polystyrene (GPPS)
description: A rigid, transparent grade of polystyrene used for light diffusers, glazing panels, and decorative building elements.

name: Polystyrene Insulation Board
description: A pre-cut rigid board fabricated from EPS or XPS, installed as thermal insulation in walls, roofs, and floors.

name: Polystyrene Bead
description: Raw unexpanded or pre-expanded polystyrene bead used as feedstock for manufacturing EPS foam products and loose-fill insulation.

name: Polystyrene Loose-Fill Insulation
description: Small expanded polystyrene beads or shapes used as poured or blown-in insulation in cavity walls and attic spaces.

name: Polystyrene Foam Sheet
description: Thin sheets of polystyrene foam used as underlay, vapour control layers, or lightweight void-forming elements in construction.

name: Insulated Concrete Formwork (ICF) with Polystyrene
description: A permanent formwork system using interlocking EPS blocks that remain in place as insulation after concrete is poured.

name: Structural Insulated Panel (SIP) with Polystyrene Core
description: A composite building panel consisting of an EPS or XPS core bonded between two structural facing boards, providing combined structure and insulation.

name: External Wall Insulation System (EWIS) with Polystyrene
description: A complete external wall insulation and render system that uses polystyrene boards as the primary insulating layer fixed to the building facade.

name: Polystyrene Void Former
description: Shaped polystyrene blocks or pods used beneath concrete slabs to create hollow voids, reducing material use and dead load.

name: Polystyrene Ceiling Tile
description: Lightweight decorative or acoustic tiles made from polystyrene, applied to ceilings as a finishing or insulating element.

name: Polystyrene Coving and Moulding
description: Decorative architectural profiles such as cornices and skirting boards manufactured from polystyrene foam for interior finishing.

name: Polystyrene Packaging and Protection
description: EPS foam used on construction sites to protect and transport fragile building products, fixtures, and equipment.

name: Flame-Retardant Polystyrene
description: A polystyrene variant treated with flame-retardant additives to meet fire performance requirements in building applications.

name: Graphite Polystyrene (GPS)
description: An enhanced EPS insulation incorporating graphite particles to significantly reduce thermal conductivity and improve energy performance.

name: Polystyrene Thermal Insulation Installation
description: The on-site cutting, fitting, fixing, and sealing of polystyrene insulation boards or loose-fill in building elements.

name: Polystyrene Formwork Assembly
description: The construction activity of stacking and connecting polystyrene ICF blocks or void formers prior to concrete pouring.

name: Polystyrene Surface Rendering
description: The application of adhesive basecoat, mesh reinforcement, and render onto polystyrene insulation boards in EWIS applications.

name: Polystyrene Cutting and Shaping
description: The use of hot-wire, saw, or knife tools on site or in fabrication to cut polystyrene to required shapes and dimensions.

name: Polystyrene Waste Disposal and Recycling
description: Site management activities for collecting, compacting, and routing polystyrene offcuts and waste to recycling or disposal facilities.

name: Polystyrene Adhesive Fixing
description: The activity of bonding polystyrene insulation or decorative elements to substrates using compatible adhesive compounds.

name: IfcCovering (Polystyrene Ceiling/Wall Tile)
description: The IFC class used to model polystyrene ceiling tiles, cove mouldings, or decorative surface coverings in a BIM environment.

name: IfcBuildingElementProxy (Polystyrene Void Former)
description: The IFC class applied to model polystyrene void-forming pods or blocks embedded within concrete slab construction.

name: IfcMaterial (Polystyrene)
description: The base IFC material definition entity used to assign polystyrene material properties to building elements in a BIM model.

name: Aluminium Alloy
description: A blend of aluminium with other elements (e.g., magnesium, silicon) to enhance strength, corrosion resistance, or workability for specific building applications.

name: Aluminium Sheet
description: Flat-rolled aluminium product used for cladding, roofing, and facade systems in building construction.

name: Aluminium Plate
description: Thick flat aluminium product used in structural and heavy-duty construction applications requiring greater load-bearing capacity.

name: Aluminium Extrusion
description: Aluminium shaped into a continuous profile through an extrusion die, commonly used for window frames, curtain walls, and structural sections.

name: Aluminium Foil
description: Ultra-thin aluminium material used as a vapour barrier, thermal reflector, or insulation facing in building envelopes.

name: Aluminium Composite Panel
description: A sandwich panel consisting of two aluminium sheets bonded to a non-aluminium core, widely used in facade and cladding systems.

name: Aluminium Curtain Wall System
description: A non-structural aluminium framing system forming the outer skin of a building, providing weather resistance and aesthetic finish.

name: Aluminium Window Frame
description: An extruded or fabricated aluminium frame designed to hold glazing and provide thermal and acoustic performance in windows.

name: Aluminium Door Frame
description: A structural aluminium frame used to support and house door panels in both internal and external applications.

name: Aluminium Roof Panel
description: A profiled or flat aluminium panel used as a roofing element, offering lightweight, durable, and weather-resistant coverage.

name: Aluminium Cladding Panel
description: An aluminium panel applied to the exterior of a building as a protective and decorative facade layer.

name: Aluminium Structural Section
description: Rolled or extruded aluminium profiles (e.g., I-beams, channels, angles) used for lightweight structural framing in buildings.

name: Aluminium Handrail
description: An aluminium rail system installed along stairs, ramps, and balconies for safety and support.

name: Aluminium Balustrade
description: A protective aluminium railing system used on balconies, terraces, and staircases, combining safety with aesthetic design.

name: Aluminium Louvre
description: Angled aluminium slats assembled into a frame to control airflow, light, and privacy in building facades and ventilation systems.

name: Aluminium Soffit Panel
description: An aluminium panel installed on the underside of roof overhangs or eaves to provide a clean finish and protect the building structure.

name: Aluminium Gutter
description: A channel-shaped aluminium element installed at roof edges to collect and direct rainwater away from the building.

name: Aluminium Downpipe
description: A vertical aluminium pipe used to convey rainwater collected by gutters down to the drainage system.

name: Aluminium Flashing
description: Thin aluminium strips used to weatherproof joints and transitions in roofing, walls, and around openings.

name: Aluminium Space Frame
description: A three-dimensional aluminium truss system used to span large areas with minimal supporting columns in roofs and canopies.

name: Aluminium Decking
description: Profiled or plank-style aluminium panels used as flooring on terraces, balconies, and walkways.

name: Aluminium Ceiling System
description: A suspended or surface-mounted ceiling system using aluminium tiles, baffles, or panels for acoustic and aesthetic performance.

name: Anodised Aluminium
description: Aluminium that has undergone an electrochemical anodising process to increase surface hardness, corrosion resistance, and allow decorative colouring.

name: Powder-Coated Aluminium
description: Aluminium with a dry powder finish applied electrostatically and cured under heat, providing colour variety and enhanced surface protection.

name: Mill-Finish Aluminium
description: Aluminium in its natural uncoated state as it comes from the rolling mill, typically used where surface finish is not a primary concern.

name: Thermally Broken Aluminium Profile
description: An aluminium extrusion incorporating a low-conductivity material insert to reduce heat transfer, improving thermal performance in windows and facades.

name: Aluminium Fabrication
description: The process of cutting, bending, welding, and assembling aluminium components to specified dimensions and shapes on or off-site.

name: Aluminium Welding
description: The joining of aluminium parts using MIG or TIG welding techniques, requiring specialised processes due to aluminium's thermal properties.

name: Aluminium Installation
description: The on-site fixing and erection of aluminium building components such as frames, cladding, and structural sections.

name: Aluminium Surface Treatment
description: Processes such as anodising, powder coating, or painting applied to aluminium surfaces to improve durability, appearance, and corrosion resistance.

name: Aluminium Recycling
description: The collection, melting, and reprocessing of aluminium building waste or end-of-life components, valued for aluminium's near-total recyclability.

name: Aluminium Corrosion Protection
description: Application of coatings or isolation measures to prevent galvanic or chemical corrosion when aluminium contacts dissimilar metals or aggressive environments.

name: Aluminium Extrusion Manufacturing
description: The industrial process of forcing heated aluminium billets through a die to produce continuous profiles used in construction components.

name: IfcMaterial (Aluminium)
description: The IFC schema representation for aluminium as a named building material, used to assign material properties to building elements in BIM models.

name: IfcProfileDef (Aluminium)
description: The IFC class defining cross-sectional profile geometry for extruded aluminium sections used in structural and facade BIM elements.

name: Bituminous Membrane Application
description: The process of applying bitumen-based sheet or liquid membranes to surfaces to prevent water ingress.

name: Liquid Applied Membrane
description: A fluid-applied coating that cures into a seamless, flexible waterproof layer on surfaces.

name: Sheet Membrane
description: Pre-formed rolls of waterproof material, such as HDPE or TPO, that are adhered or mechanically fixed to substrates.

name: Cementitious Waterproofing
description: Application of rigid or semi-flexible cement-based compounds to concrete surfaces to block water passage.

name: Crystalline Waterproofing
description: A chemical admixture or coating that reacts with concrete to form insoluble crystals, permanently blocking capillary pores.

name: Polyurethane Coating
description: A flexible, durable liquid-applied polyurethane compound used as a seamless waterproof coating on roofs, decks, and wet areas.

name: Epoxy Injection
description: Pumping of epoxy resin into cracks or voids in concrete to restore structural integrity and prevent water infiltration.

name: Drainage Layer Installation
description: Placement of a permeable drainage layer (e.g., geocomposite or gravel) adjacent to the waterproof membrane to manage hydrostatic pressure.

name: Waterproof Admixture
description: Chemical additives blended into concrete or mortar mixes to reduce permeability and resist water penetration.

name: Tanking System
description: An integrated waterproofing system applied internally or externally to below-grade structures to resist hydrostatic water pressure.

name: Basement Waterproofing
description: Specialized waterproofing treatment of below-ground walls and floors to prevent groundwater and moisture intrusion into basement spaces.

name: Podium Deck Waterproofing
description: Waterproofing of elevated concrete slabs over occupied spaces, such as car parks or landscaped decks, to prevent leakage below.

name: Wet Area Waterproofing
description: Application of waterproofing systems in bathrooms, kitchens, and laundries before tile installation to contain water within designated zones.

name: Joint Sealant
description: A flexible filler compound applied at construction, expansion, or movement joints to prevent water ingress through gaps.

name: Waterproof Membrane Testing
description: Flood, vacuum, or electronic testing of installed membranes to verify continuity and absence of leaks before covering.

name: IFC Waterproofing Class
description: The IFC schema class (IfcCovering or IfcBuildingElementProxy) used to model waterproofing layers in BIM environments.

name: Hydrostatic Pressure Resistance
description: The designed capability of a waterproofing system to withstand positive or negative water pressure from groundwater or standing water.

name: Geocomposite Drainage Mat
description: A factory-assembled drainage product combining a geonet core with geotextile filter layers, used to manage water flow away from waterproofed surfaces.

name: Shoring System Setup
description: Erection of vertical support structures (shores and props) that carry the weight of formwork and fresh concrete during casting.

name: Falsework Assembly
description: Construction of temporary load-bearing scaffolding frameworks that support formwork until the concrete achieves sufficient strength.

name: Formwork Panel Placement
description: Positioning and fixing of individual form panels or boards to define the shape and surface finish of the concrete element.

name: Formwork Alignment & Levelling
description: Surveying and adjusting formwork assemblies to ensure correct geometry, plumb, and elevation before concrete is poured.

name: Tie Rod & Anchor Installation
description: Threading and tensioning of steel tie rods through opposing form faces to resist lateral pressure from wet concrete.

name: Formwork Stripping & Striking
description: Systematic removal of formwork components after concrete has cured to the required strength, without damaging the finished surface.

name: Formwork Cleaning & Oiling
description: Preparation of form surfaces with release agents and cleaning between pours to prevent concrete adhesion and extend panel service life.

name: Formwork Inspection & Sign-Off
description: Quality-assurance check of completed formwork assembly for dimensional accuracy, stability, and watertightness before concreting commences.

name: Slip Forming
description: Continuously moving formwork technique used for tall vertical structures such as cores and silos, allowing concrete to be placed without stopping.

name: Jump Forming
description: Crane-lifted, self-climbing form system used for repetitive vertical concrete pours in high-rise core walls and elevator shafts.

name: Tunnel Forming
description: Simultaneous casting of walls and slabs in a single pour using a wing-shaped steel form that creates a tunnel cross-section.

name: Proprietary Column Formwork
description: Pre-engineered circular or rectangular steel/fibreglass form system designed specifically for casting concrete columns.

name: Slab Soffit Formwork System
description: Integrated panel and prop system that supports the underside of flat slabs or beams during concrete placement and early curing.

name: Wall Formwork System
description: Engineered panel-and-waler assembly used to form vertical concrete walls, providing lateral containment for the concrete pour.

name: Formwork Panel
description: Flat or profiled facing board (timber, steel, aluminium, or plastic) that directly contacts the concrete to impart shape and surface texture.

name: Waler (Strongback)
description: Horizontal or vertical backing member that distributes concrete pressure from form panels into the shoring or tie system.

name: Adjustable Steel Prop (Acrow)
description: Telescopic steel post used as a vertical shore to support slab soffit formwork or falsework beams at variable heights.

name: Tie Rod & Wing Nut
description: Threaded steel rod and corresponding fastener that clamp opposing formwork panels together and resist hydrostatic concrete pressure.

name: Form Release Agent
description: Chemical oil or wax-based coating applied to form faces to prevent concrete adhesion and facilitate clean stripping.

name: Plywood Sheeting (Form-Grade)
description: Structural plywood manufactured to formwork tolerances, used as a facing material for timber-framed form panels.

name: Steel Formwork
description: Reusable steel plate panels used where high repetition, tight tolerances, or smooth concrete finishes are required.

name: Aluminium Formwork
description: Lightweight aluminium alloy panels and frames that offer fast assembly, high repetition cycles, and dimensional accuracy.

name: Foam/Polystyrene Void Former
description: Expanded polystyrene inserts cast into the concrete to create voids, reduce self-weight, or form complex shapes in slabs and beams.

name: Formwork Storage & Yard Area
description: Designated on-site zone for stacking, cleaning, repairing, and managing the formwork inventory between successive pours.

name: Concrete Pour Zone
description: Controlled area enclosed by installed formwork within which fresh concrete is placed, consolidated, and cured.

name: Embedded Insert & Cast-In Item Fixing
description: Securing of cast-in plates, anchor bolts, conduits, and sleeves to the formwork interior before concrete is poured.

name: IfcFormwork
description: IFC schema class representing a temporary formwork element in a building information model for quantity take-off and scheduling.

name: Stripping of Wall Formwork
description: The process of dismantling and removing formwork panels from concrete walls after sufficient curing time has been achieved.

name: Stripping of Slab Formwork
description: Removal of horizontal deck panels and supporting elements from beneath cast concrete floor or roof slabs.

name: Stripping of Column Formwork
description: Dismantling of formwork systems encasing concrete columns once the required early strength has been reached.

name: Stripping of Beam Formwork
description: Removal of soffit boards and side forms from concrete beams while ensuring structural integrity is maintained.

name: Stripping of Foundation Formwork
description: Removal of formwork from footings, pile caps, and foundation walls after concrete has gained adequate strength.

name: Stripping of Staircase Formwork
description: Careful dismantling of complex formwork assemblies used to cast concrete staircases, including risers and treads.

name: Prop and Shoring Removal
description: Sequential striking of temporary vertical props, reshores, and shoring towers that supported formwork during casting and curing.

name: Falsework Dismantling
description: Systematic deconstruction of temporary structural support frameworks that carried formwork loads during concrete placement.

name: Formwork Inspection Before Striking
description: Pre-removal assessment to verify concrete has achieved the minimum specified compressive strength before formwork is stripped.

name: Concrete Strength Testing (Strike-Off)
description: In-situ or lab testing of concrete cube/cylinder samples to confirm adequate curing strength prior to formwork removal.

name: Formwork Panel Cleaning
description: Removal of hardened concrete residue, release agent residue, and debris from stripped formwork panels to prepare them for reuse.

name: Formwork Oiling / Release Agent Application
description: Application of a chemical release agent to formwork faces before reuse to facilitate clean stripping in subsequent pours.

name: Formwork Storage and Stacking
description: Organised sorting and stacking of stripped formwork components on site for reuse or off-hire return.

name: Formwork Repair and Refurbishment
description: Rectification of damaged or warped formwork panels and hardware identified during or after the stripping operation.

name: Concrete Surface Inspection Post-Strip
description: Visual and physical examination of exposed concrete surfaces immediately after stripping to identify honeycombing, cold joints, or defects.

name: Concrete Remediation / Patching
description: Repair of surface defects, voids, or honeycombing revealed on concrete elements following formwork removal.

name: Tie Hole Sealing
description: Filling and finishing of holes left by formwork tie rods after wall or column formwork has been stripped.

name: Curing Continuation After Stripping
description: Application of curing compounds, wet hessian, or membranes to exposed concrete surfaces to maintain moisture and temperature after formwork is removed.

name: Debris and Waste Removal
description: Collection and disposal of timber offcuts, broken ties, nail plates, plastic cones, and other waste generated during stripping.

name: Waling / Soldier
description: Horizontal or vertical structural stiffener that backs up formwork panels and transfers loads to props or ties.

name: Formwork Prop (Acrow Prop)
description: Adjustable telescopic steel post used to vertically support slab and beam soffit formwork during and after casting.

name: Tie Rod and Wing Nut
description: Through-form tensioning rod with end hardware that holds opposing wall form panels apart at the correct spacing.

name: Plastic Cone / Tie Cone
description: Sacrificial plastic spacer element placed on tie rods to create a recessed hole in the concrete face for later sealing.

name: Release Agent (Form Oil)
description: Chemical compound applied to formwork contact surfaces to prevent concrete adhesion and allow clean stripping.

name: Patching Mortar
description: Cementitious or epoxy-based repair compound used to fill tie holes, honeycombing, and surface defects after stripping.

name: Curing Compound
description: Liquid membrane applied to stripped concrete surfaces to retain moisture and ensure continued hydration.

name: Freshly Stripped Concrete Surface
description: The exposed concrete face immediately after formwork removal, representing the working zone for inspection, remediation, and curing activities.

name: Temporary Works Area (Stripping Zone)
description: Designated site area where stripped formwork components are landed, inspected, cleaned, and sorted for reuse or removal.

name: Crane / Hoist for Formwork Handling
description: Lifting system used to safely lower and transport large or heavy stripped formwork assemblies to the landing area.

name: Reshoring System
description: Temporary support system installed beneath recently stripped slabs to redistribute loads while concrete gains full design strength.

name: Formwork Striking Schedule
description: Planned programme specifying the minimum time or strength criteria that must be met before each formwork element type may be stripped.

name: IFC Temporary Works Element (IfcBuildingElementProxy)
description: IFC class used to model temporary formwork and shoring elements within a building information model for construction sequencing.

name: Reinforcement Steel Placement
description: Positioning and securing rebar or mesh within the formwork before concrete is poured to provide tensile strength.

name: Concrete Transportation
description: Conveying ready-mixed or site-batched concrete from the mixing point to the pour location via trucks, pumps, or chutes.

name: Concrete Vibration / Compaction
description: Applying mechanical vibration to eliminate air voids and ensure full consolidation of fresh concrete around reinforcement.

name: Formwork Striking / Removal
description: Carefully dismantling and removing formwork components once the concrete has achieved sufficient strength to be self-supporting.

name: Surface Finishing
description: Leveling, screeding, and finishing the exposed concrete surface to achieve the specified texture and flatness tolerances.

name: Concrete Testing / Quality Control
description: Performing slump tests, cube/cylinder sampling, and other checks to verify the fresh and hardened concrete meets specification.

name: Portland Cement
description: The primary binding material in concrete that reacts with water through hydration to produce strength.

name: Fine Aggregate / Sand
description: Sand or crushed fines that fill voids between coarse aggregate particles and influence workability of the mix.

name: Concrete Pump
description: Mechanical equipment used to push concrete through pipelines to distant or elevated pour locations.

name: Concrete Vibrator
description: An immersion or external vibrating device used to compact fresh concrete and remove trapped air pockets.

name: Concrete Mixer
description: A drum-based machine that blends cement, aggregates, and water into a homogeneous concrete mix.

name: Formwork System
description: An engineered assembly of panels, props, and falsework designed to contain and shape poured concrete during placement and curing.

name: Reinforcement System
description: The complete network of rebar, ties, spacers, and couplers that provides structural reinforcement within a concrete element.

name: Concrete Batching Plant
description: An on-site or off-site installation that precisely weighs and mixes concrete ingredients at scale for construction use.

name: Post-Pour Inspection
description: Visual and structural assessment of hardened concrete surfaces to detect honeycombing, cracks, or other defects after formwork removal.

name: Cold Weather Concreting
description: Applying protective measures such as heating, insulating blankets, or mix adjustments to ensure proper hydration in low-temperature conditions.

name: Hot Weather Concreting
description: Implementing precautions like chilled water, ice addition, and shading to prevent premature stiffening of concrete in high-temperature environments.

name: Construction Joint Formation
description: Deliberately creating planned joints between sequential concrete pours to manage structural continuity and shrinkage cracking.

name: Waterstop Installation
description: Embedding flexible waterstop strips at construction joints to prevent water infiltration through concrete junctions.

name: Curing Compound Application
description: Spraying or rolling liquid membrane-forming compounds onto concrete surfaces to retain moisture during the curing period.

name: Wet Curing
description: Keeping concrete or masonry surfaces continuously moist using water, wet burlap, or soaker hoses to support hydration.

name: Steam Curing
description: Accelerated curing method using steam heat to increase the rate of strength gain in precast or cold-weather concrete elements.

name: Curing Blanket
description: An insulating blanket placed over freshly poured concrete to retain heat and moisture during the curing process.

name: Curing Duration Monitoring
description: Tracking and documenting the time elapsed since concrete placement to ensure minimum curing periods are met per specification.

name: Temperature Monitoring During Curing
description: Measuring and recording concrete or ambient temperatures during curing to detect freeze-thaw risks or excessive heat.

name: Cold-Weather Curing
description: Special curing procedures applied in sub-zero or near-freezing conditions to prevent concrete from freezing before adequate strength is gained.

name: Hot-Weather Curing
description: Measures taken in high-temperature or low-humidity conditions to slow moisture loss and prevent cracking in fresh concrete.

name: Masonry Curing
description: Controlled wetting and protection of newly laid masonry units and mortar joints to achieve proper bond strength and durability.

name: Epoxy Curing
description: The chemical cross-linking process of epoxy resin and hardener components used in adhesives, coatings, and flooring systems.

name: Sealant Curing
description: The time-dependent hardening or vulcanisation of joint sealants and caulking compounds after application.

name: Resin Curing
description: Hardening of synthetic resins used in composites, adhesives, and coatings through chemical or UV-initiated reactions.

name: Curing Time Schedule
description: A project management document or system that specifies required curing durations, hold points, and inspection milestones for various materials.

name: Moisture Retention System
description: An assembly of covers, sprinklers, or misting equipment designed to maintain adequate surface moisture throughout the curing period.

name: Curing Membrane
description: A thin film or sheet material laid over concrete or masonry to prevent surface moisture evaporation during curing.

name: Polythene Sheeting
description: Plastic film used to cover and seal concrete surfaces, trapping moisture and maintaining humidity during the curing process.

name: Burlap (Hessian) Fabric
description: A natural fibre fabric kept saturated with water and laid over concrete surfaces as a wet curing medium.

name: Formwork Retention for Curing
description: Deliberately delaying formwork removal to exploit its moisture-retaining properties and protect concrete during early strength gain.

name: Curing of Grout
description: Managing moisture and temperature conditions after grout placement to ensure complete hydration and bond development.

name: Post-Tensioning Curing Hold
description: A mandatory waiting period after concrete placement before post-tensioning stressing operations can commence, linked to curing strength targets.

name: Curing Inspection
description: Site inspection activity to verify that specified curing methods, materials, and durations are being correctly applied and maintained.

name: Accelerated Curing
description: Use of heat, pressure, or chemical admixtures to shorten the time required for materials to reach design strength.

name: Autogenous Curing
description: Internal curing technique using pre-wetted lightweight aggregates or superabsorbent polymers to supply moisture from within the concrete mix.

name: Curing Admixture
description: A chemical additive incorporated into a concrete mix to improve water retention, extend hydration, or enhance self-curing properties.

name: UV Curing
description: Hardening of coatings, adhesives, or polymer materials using ultraviolet light energy to initiate photochemical cross-linking.

name: Curing of Timber (Seasoning)
description: Controlled drying or conditioning of timber to reduce moisture content and stabilise dimensions before use in construction.

name: Kiln Drying
description: Accelerated drying of timber in a heated enclosure to achieve target moisture content faster than air seasoning allows.

name: Curing Record Documentation
description: Formal recording of curing start times, methods, material batch numbers, temperatures, and sign-off dates for quality assurance purposes.

name: Painting & Coating
description: Application of paint, primer, sealers, or specialist coatings to surfaces for protection and aesthetic finish.

name: Dry Lining / Plasterboard
description: Erection of gypsum plasterboard partitions, linings, and shaft walls as a dry alternative to wet plastering.

name: Joinery Installation
description: Fitting of timber or manufactured joinery elements such as skirting, architraves, cornices, and dado rails.

name: Door & Window Fitting
description: Hanging of internal doors, fitting of door frames, and installation of window reveals and trims as part of the finishing scope.

name: Cabinetry & Millwork
description: Installation of kitchen, bathroom, and built-in cabinets, shelving units, and bespoke millwork elements.

name: Skirting & Architrave
description: Profiled timber or MDF boards fixed at wall-floor junctions and around door openings to conceal gaps and provide decoration.

name: Cornice & Coving
description: Decorative mouldings fixed at the wall-ceiling junction to create a finished transition between planes.

name: Feature Wall Treatment
description: Application of decorative finishes such as wallpaper, textured render, stone, or timber panelling to a designated accent wall.

name: Wallpapering
description: Hanging of paper, vinyl, or fabric wall coverings as a decorative surface treatment.

name: Screed & Self-Levelling Compound
description: Pouring and finishing of cementitious or anhydrite screed layers to provide a flat substrate for final floor finishes.

name: Waterproofing & Tanking
description: Application of waterproof membranes or coatings in wet areas such as bathrooms and basements prior to tiling or other finishes.

name: Sealant & Caulking
description: Application of flexible sealants or caulk at joints, junctions, and perimeters to prevent moisture ingress and achieve a neat finish.

name: Render Coat
description: A cementitious or polymer-modified surface layer applied externally or internally to masonry to provide a weather-resistant or decorative finish.

name: Gypsum Plaster
description: A calcium sulphate-based material applied in coats to walls and ceilings to form a smooth internal finish surface.

name: Ceramic / Porcelain Tile
description: Fired clay-based tile units used as a durable and hygienic surface finish for floors and walls.

name: Hardwood Flooring
description: Solid or engineered timber boards installed as a premium finished floor surface.

name: Carpet
description: Textile floor covering laid over underlay to provide comfort, acoustic insulation, and decoration.

name: Vinyl / LVT Flooring
description: Resilient synthetic floor covering available in luxury vinyl tile or sheet form, offering durability and water resistance.

name: Polished Concrete Finishing
description: Mechanical grinding and polishing of a concrete slab surface to achieve a smooth, reflective decorative floor finish.

name: Epoxy Floor Coating
description: Application of a two-part epoxy resin system to concrete floors for a seamless, chemical-resistant, and decorative finish.

name: External Rendering
description: Application of sand-cement or acrylic render systems to external wall surfaces for weather protection and aesthetics.

name: Staircase Finishing
description: Cladding, nosing, balustrade finishing, and surface treatment of staircases as part of the interior fit-out.

name: IFC IfcCovering
description: IFC class representing building elements that cover floors, walls, or ceilings, including finishes such as flooring, skirting, and ceiling tiles.

name: IFC IfcCoatingType
description: IFC class used to define the type properties of coating layers applied to surfaces within a building model.

name: Finish Schedule
description: A documentation system that records and tracks all specified surface finishes by room, surface, and material across the entire project.

name: Color Scheme System
description: A coordinated palette management system used to specify, approve, and track paint and material colors across building zones.

name: Quality Inspection & Defect Tracking
description: Systematic inspection and recording of finishing defects, snagging items, and remediation work prior to handover.

name: Glass Pane
description: The primary transparent or translucent sheet material installed within a frame as part of a glazing assembly.

name: Glazing Gasket
description: A preformed rubber or silicone profile that cushions and seals the glass within the frame to prevent air and water infiltration.

name: Insulated Glazing Unit (IGU)
description: A factory-sealed assembly of two or more glass panes separated by spacer bars and an insulating gas fill to improve thermal performance.

name: Toughened / Tempered Glass
description: Heat-treated glass engineered to shatter into small blunt fragments, providing enhanced impact and thermal resistance.

name: Low-E Coated Glass
