description: Glass with a microscopically thin metallic coating that reflects infrared radiation to improve thermal insulation of the glazing unit.

name: Curtain Wall Glazing
description: A non-load-bearing external wall cladding system composed of glazed panels suspended from the building structure.

name: Skylight / Rooflight Glazing
description: A glazed assembly installed in a roof plane to admit natural daylight into interior spaces below.

name: Shopfront Glazing
description: Large-format glazed facades at ground-floor retail level, designed for visual display and pedestrian interaction.

name: Double Glazing Installation
description: The on-site activity of fitting double-pane insulated glazing units into prepared frame openings to meet thermal and acoustic performance requirements.

name: Triple Glazing Installation
description: The on-site activity of installing three-pane insulated glazing units, typically in high-performance or Passivhaus building envelopes.

name: Glass Cutting and Sizing
description: The trade activity of cutting glass sheets to precise dimensions required for a specific opening or unit.

name: Frame Preparation and Priming
description: The pre-installation activity of cleaning, priming, and applying setting blocks to frames to receive the glazing unit correctly.

name: Glazing Inspection and Testing
description: Post-installation quality assurance activities including air-leakage, water-penetration, and thermal performance testing of completed glazed assemblies.

name: Secondary Glazing
description: A supplementary inner glazed layer added to an existing window opening to improve thermal insulation and acoustic performance without replacing the primary frame.

name: Fire-Rated Glazing
description: Specially tested glass and frame assemblies that maintain integrity, insulation, or radiation control for a defined period during a fire event.

name: Acoustic Glazing
description: Glazing assemblies incorporating laminated interlayers or asymmetric pane thicknesses to achieve specified sound-reduction performance.

name: Bird-Friendly Glazing
description: Glass with UV-reflective fritting or surface patterns that are visible to birds, reducing fatal bird-strike incidents on buildings.

name: Electrochromic / Smart Glass
description: Electrically switchable glass that can alter its tint or opacity on demand to control solar gain and glare.

name: Solar Control Glass
description: Glass with tinted body or surface coatings designed to reduce solar heat gain while maintaining visible light transmission.

name: Setting Block
description: A small load-bearing pad, typically neoprene or plastic, placed at the base of a glass pane within the frame to distribute its self-weight.

name: Glazed Curtain Wall Panel
description: A prefabricated glazed unit incorporating both frame and glass, manufactured off-site for rapid installation into a curtain wall grid.

name: Window Replacement / Reglazing
description: The remedial activity of removing failed or broken glass units and installing new glazing into existing frames.

name: Desiccant Fill
description: A moisture-absorbing material packed within the spacer bar of an IGU to prevent internal condensation between the panes.

name: Primer Application
description: Applying a base coat primer layer to seal surfaces and improve paint adhesion and uniformity.

name: Topcoat Application
description: Applying the final decorative or protective paint layer over the primed surface.

name: Paintbrush
description: A hand-held tool with bristles used for detailed, edging, and trim painting work.

name: Spray Gun
description: A pneumatic or airless device that atomizes and sprays paint for fast, uniform coverage on large areas.

name: Drop Cloth
description: A protective sheet placed over floors and furnishings to prevent paint spills and splatters during painting activities.

name: Masking Tape
description: Adhesive tape applied to edges and borders to create clean paint lines and protect adjacent surfaces.

name: Paint Scraper
description: A tool used to remove old, peeling, or loose paint from surfaces prior to repainting.

name: Sandpaper
description: Abrasive material used to smooth surfaces and de-gloss existing paint layers before new paint application.

name: Interior Paint
description: Formulated paint designed for use on indoor walls, ceilings, and trim with appropriate sheen and VOC levels.

name: Anti-Corrosion Paint
description: Specialized protective paint applied to metal surfaces to prevent rust and corrosion over time.

name: Wall Painting
description: The specific activity of applying paint to interior or exterior wall surfaces of a building.

name: Ceiling Painting
description: The activity of painting overhead ceiling surfaces, often requiring specialized equipment and techniques.

name: Trim and Skirting Painting
description: Painting of architectural trim elements such as baseboards, door frames, and window casings.

name: Structural Steelwork Painting
description: Application of protective coatings to steel structural members to prevent corrosion and meet fire-rating requirements.

name: Floor Painting
description: Applying paint or epoxy coatings to concrete or timber floor surfaces for protection and aesthetics.

name: Line Marking
description: Painting demarcation lines, symbols, and markings on floors or pavements for safety and navigation purposes.

name: Paint Curing
description: The drying and hardening process of applied paint during which the coating develops its final properties and strength.

name: Paint Scaffold / Access Equipment
description: Temporary elevated platforms or access systems erected to enable safe painting of high or hard-to-reach surfaces.

name: Colour Scheme / Specification
description: The design activity of selecting, documenting, and specifying paint colours and finishes for building elements.

name: Paint Quality Inspection
description: Assessment and verification of applied paint for coverage, adhesion, thickness, and finish quality against specifications.

name: Site Acceptance Testing (SAT)
description: Verification testing carried out on-site after installation to confirm equipment performs correctly in its installed environment.

name: Pre-Commissioning Checks
description: Preliminary inspections and checks performed before full commissioning to ensure systems are ready for energisation and functional testing.

name: Performance Testing
description: Testing that verifies a system or component meets defined performance benchmarks such as capacity, efficiency, and output targets.

name: Functional Testing
description: Systematic verification that each system and component performs its intended function according to the design intent.

name: Leak Testing
description: Pressure or vacuum testing of pipework, ductwork, and containment systems to detect and quantify any unacceptable fluid or air leakage.

name: Electrical Continuity and Insulation Testing
description: Electrical tests verifying conductor continuity, insulation resistance, and earth loop impedance to ensure safety and compliance.

name: Fire and Life Safety System Testing
description: Comprehensive testing of fire detection, alarm, suppression, and evacuation systems to verify life-safety performance and code compliance.

name: HVAC Balancing and Commissioning
description: Adjustment and verification of air and water flow rates in HVAC systems to achieve design conditions throughout the building.

name: BMS/Controls Commissioning
description: Programming, calibration, and functional verification of the Building Management System and associated control sequences.

name: Plumbing and Drainage Testing
description: Testing of potable water, hot water, and drainage systems for correct flow, pressure, and watertightness.

name: Elevator and Escalator Testing
description: Statutory and functional testing of vertical transportation equipment for safety, speed, load capacity, and regulatory certification.

name: Structural Load and Deflection Testing
description: Physical testing of structural elements under applied loads to confirm deflection and capacity comply with design requirements.

name: Envelope Air-Tightness Testing
description: Pressurisation or depressurisation tests on the building envelope to measure air infiltration rates and energy performance.

name: Acoustic Testing
description: Measurement of sound insulation, background noise levels, and reverberation times to verify compliance with acoustic design criteria.

name: Lighting Control and Commissioning
description: Configuration and verification of lighting control systems, dimming scenes, occupancy sensors, and daylight harvesting functions.

name: Security and Access Control Testing
description: Testing and verification of CCTV, intruder detection, and access control systems to confirm correct operation and integration.

name: Water Quality Testing
description: Laboratory or on-site testing of domestic water systems for microbiological and chemical compliance, including Legionella risk assessment.

name: Thermal Imaging Inspection
description: Infrared thermographic survey of building fabric and electrical installations to identify thermal anomalies, moisture, and insulation defects.

name: Witness Testing
description: Formal observation and sign-off of critical tests by the client, certifying authority, or independent third party.

name: Defect Identification and Snagging
description: Systematic identification, recording, and scheduling of defects and incomplete works discovered during the commissioning process.

name: Retesting and Remediation
description: Re-execution of failed tests following corrective works to confirm that defects have been resolved to specification.

name: Commissioning Plan
description: A documented programme outlining the scope, sequence, responsibilities, and acceptance criteria for all commissioning activities.

name: Commissioning Schedule
description: Time-phased programme coordinating the sequencing of individual test activities relative to construction milestones and handover dates.

name: Test Records and Certificates
description: Formal documentation package capturing test results, calibration data, and signed certificates required for handover and regulatory sign-off.

name: O&M Manual Compilation
description: Assembly of operation and maintenance documentation, as-installed drawings, and test records into a structured handover package.

name: Training and Handover
description: Structured training of the client's facilities management team on system operation, maintenance procedures, and emergency protocols.

name: Post-Occupancy Seasonal Commissioning
description: Extended commissioning activities carried out across heating and cooling seasons after occupation to fine-tune system performance.

name: Independent Commissioning Agent (CxA)
description: A third-party specialist engaged to oversee, verify, and report on the entire commissioning process on behalf of the building owner.

name: Renewable Energy System Testing
description: Testing and verification of photovoltaic, solar thermal, wind, or other renewable energy installations for output, control, and grid interaction.

name: Data and IT Infrastructure Testing
description: Verification of structured cabling, data networks, and telecommunications infrastructure for connectivity, bandwidth, and resilience.

name: Gas Installation Testing
description: Pressure testing and purging of gas supply pipework and appliances to verify safety and compliance with gas regulations.

name: Bulk Excavation
description: Large-scale removal of soil or rock across a wide area to reach a required formation level for foundations or basements.

name: Pit Excavation
description: Localised digging of a defined hole or shaft to accommodate isolated footings, pile caps, or inspection chambers.

name: Rock Excavation
description: Specialist removal of hard rock strata using blasting, hydraulic breaking, or rock-sawing techniques.

name: Basement Excavation
description: Deep excavation carried out to create a subterranean floor level or multi-level underground structure within a building footprint.

name: Subsoil
description: The layer of soil beneath topsoil that is excavated and managed or disposed of during groundworks operations.

name: Topsoil Stripping
description: Removal and stockpiling of the uppermost fertile soil layer prior to bulk excavation to enable reuse in landscaping.

name: Spoil Disposal
description: Off-site haulage and licensed tipping or recycling of excavated material that cannot be reused on the project.

name: Earthwork Support
description: Temporary or permanent shoring, timbering, or sheet-piling system used to retain the sides of an excavation and prevent collapse.

name: Sheet Piling
description: Interlocking steel or timber sections driven into the ground to form a continuous retaining wall around or alongside an excavation.

name: Soldier Piles
description: Vertical steel H-piles installed at intervals with horizontal lagging boards to retain excavation faces.

name: Secant Pile Wall
description: Overlapping bored concrete piles forming a watertight retaining wall for deep excavations in urban or waterlogged conditions.

name: Diaphragm Wall
description: Reinforced concrete wall cast in situ within a slurry-supported trench to provide permanent earth and water retention.

name: Ground Anchor
description: Pre-stressed tendon or rod grouted into stable ground behind a retaining structure to resist lateral earth pressures.

name: Groundwater
description: Subsurface water encountered during excavation that must be monitored, controlled, or diverted to maintain stable working conditions.

name: Ground Bearing Capacity Assessment
description: Evaluation of the load-bearing strength of exposed formation level soils to confirm suitability for foundations.

name: Formation Level
description: The finished bottom surface of an excavation at which foundations, slabs, or sub-base layers are subsequently constructed.

name: Excavation Batter / Slope
description: Angled cutting of excavation sides to a safe gradient as an alternative to vertical shoring in open-cut operations.

name: Benching
description: Creation of stepped horizontal ledges in the excavation face to improve stability and provide safe working platforms.

name: Compaction
description: Mechanical densification of backfill material placed into an excavation to restore ground strength and prevent settlement.

name: Excavator (Plant)
description: Tracked or wheeled hydraulic machine used as the primary plant for digging, breaking, and loading excavated material.

name: Dumper / Tipper Truck
description: Haulage plant used to transport excavated spoil away from the dig face to stockpile areas or disposal sites.

name: Vibro-compactor / Plate Compactor
description: Mechanical plant used to compact backfill layers within excavated areas to specified density requirements.

name: Temporary Works Design
description: Engineering design of shoring, propping, and support schemes required to safely execute and maintain an open excavation.

name: Contaminated Land Remediation
description: Specialist excavation, treatment, or removal of chemically or biologically contaminated soils identified during groundworks.

name: Archaeology Watching Brief
description: Monitoring of excavation works by an archaeologist to identify, record, and preserve any heritage finds uncovered.

name: Driven Piling
description: Installation of piles by driving them into the ground using impact hammers or vibratory equipment.

name: Bored Piling
description: Formation of piles by drilling a hole into the ground and filling it with reinforced concrete.

name: CFA Piling (Continuous Flight Auger)
description: A displacement piling method using a continuous flight auger drilled to depth while concrete is pumped through the hollow stem.

name: Micro Piling
description: Installation of small-diameter, high-capacity piles used in restricted access or low-headroom conditions.

name: Screw Piling
description: Installation of helical steel piles screwed into the ground to provide load-bearing support.

name: Pile Cap Construction
description: Casting of reinforced concrete caps on top of pile groups to distribute structural loads from columns or walls.

name: Ground Investigation
description: Site investigation activity to assess soil and rock conditions prior to selecting and designing the piling solution.

name: Pile Cropping / Cutting
description: Removal of excess concrete or material from the top of a pile to expose reinforcement for connection to the pile cap.

name: Steel Tube Pile
description: A hollow steel tube driven or screwed into the ground, sometimes filled with concrete after installation.

name: Casing (Temporary/Permanent)
description: A steel liner tube used to stabilise the sides of a bored pile excavation during drilling and concreting.

name: Helical Screw Pile
description: A steel shaft with one or more helical plates that is rotated into the ground to achieve bearing capacity.

name: Pile Shoe / Driving Shoe
description: A hardened steel tip attached to the bottom of a driven pile to protect it and aid penetration into hard strata.

name: Bentonite Slurry
description: A drilling fluid used to stabilise the walls of a bored pile excavation and prevent collapse before concreting.

name: Structural Concrete (Pile Mix)
description: A specially designed concrete mix with high workability (often self-compacting) used to fill bored or CFA piles.

name: Pile Boring / Excavation
description: The drilling or augering operation that creates the void into which a bored or CFA pile is constructed.

name: Reinforced Concrete Pile
description: A cast-in-situ or precast concrete pile element reinforced with steel bars to carry both compressive and tensile forces.

name: Vibro-Compaction / Stone Column
description: Ground improvement technique closely related to piling that uses vibratory probes to compact or reinforce weak soils.

name: Retaining Wall (Contiguous / Secant Pile)
description: A wall system formed from closely spaced or interlocking bored piles used for earth retention around excavations.

name: Pile Rig / Drilling Rig
description: The specialist plant and machinery used to install piles by driving, drilling, or rotating methods.

name: Pile Layout / Set Out
description: The surveying activity of marking the precise locations of each pile position on site according to the structural drawings.

name: Rebar Scheduling
description: Preparing detailed bar-bending schedules that specify bar marks, sizes, shapes, and quantities for a pour.

name: Rebar Placement
description: Positioning cut and bent reinforcement bars accurately within formwork according to structural drawings.

name: Rebar Tying
description: Securing intersecting bars together with binding wire to maintain their position during concrete pouring.

name: Lap Splicing
description: Overlapping two rebar ends by a code-specified length to transfer tensile forces between bars.

name: Mechanical Splicing
description: Joining rebar ends using threaded couplers or swaged sleeves as an alternative to lapped joints.

name: Welded Splicing
description: Connecting rebar ends by butt or fillet welding where permitted by design and material grade.

name: Cover Block Installation
description: Placing plastic or concrete spacers beneath and around the cage to maintain the required concrete cover depth.

name: Reinforcement Cage Assembly
description: Pre-fabricating a complete three-dimensional steel cage off-site or on the ground before lifting into position.

name: Starter Bar Installation
description: Casting short projecting bars into a lower pour to provide continuity with the reinforcement of the next pour.

name: Shear Link / Stirrup Fixing
description: Installing closed or open links around main bars in beams and columns to resist shear and provide confinement.

name: Anchorage and Hook Formation
description: Bending bar ends into standard hooks or bends to develop the full anchorage length required by design.

name: Reinforcement Inspection and Sign-off
description: Checking completed steel placement against drawings for bar sizes, spacing, laps, and cover before concreting begins.

name: Steel Reinforcement Bar (Rebar)
description: Deformed or plain round steel bars that provide tensile strength within concrete structural elements.

name: Binding Wire
description: Annealed mild-steel wire used to tie rebar intersections and hold bars in position during construction.

name: Concrete Cover Spacer
description: Plastic, steel, or pre-cast concrete block used to maintain a precise gap between the bar and the formwork face.

name: Mechanical Bar Coupler
description: Threaded or swaged sleeve device that connects two rebar ends to create a continuous tension or compression joint.

name: Prefabricated Reinforcement Mesh
description: Factory-welded grid of steel bars supplied in sheets or rolls for use in slabs, walls, and pavements.

name: Bar Bending Machine
description: Mechanical or CNC-controlled equipment used on site or in a fabrication yard to bend rebar to precise angles.

name: Bar Cutting Machine
description: Powered shear or disc-cutter used to cut rebar cleanly to the lengths specified in bar schedules.

name: Rebar Tying Tool
description: Manual or battery-powered tool that twists binding wire quickly around bar intersections to speed up fixing.

name: Reinforcement Fabrication Yard
description: Designated site area or off-site facility where rebar is cut, bent, and assembled into cages or mats before delivery.

name: Concrete Cover Verification
description: Using cover meters or physical checks to confirm that the as-fixed cover to all bars meets specification requirements.

name: Anti-Crack Reinforcement Detailing
description: Positioning secondary bars at corners, openings, and re-entrant points specifically to control shrinkage and thermal cracking.

name: Pre-stressing Tendon Installation
description: Placing high-tensile steel tendons or strands within ducts or directly in concrete as an alternative or supplement to passive rebar.

name: Reinforcement Corrosion Protection
description: Applying epoxy coating, galvanising, or inhibitor treatments to rebar surfaces to extend service life in corrosive environments.

name: Structural Drawing Interpretation
description: Reading and translating engineer's reinforcement drawings into bar schedules and on-site fixing instructions.

name: Fixing Wire Mesh to Formwork
description: Attaching pre-welded mesh sheets securely to formwork panels to prevent displacement during concrete placement.

name: Steel Column Installation
description: The process of positioning, aligning, and securing vertical steel columns to foundation anchor bolts or base plates.

name: Steel Beam Installation
description: Lifting and connecting horizontal steel beams between columns to form the primary floor and roof framing.

name: Steel Decking Installation
description: Laying and fastening corrugated metal deck panels over steel framing to form floor or roof substrates.

name: Moment Frame Assembly
description: Erecting and bolting rigid moment-resisting frame connections designed to transfer lateral loads through bending.

name: Braced Frame Assembly
description: Installing diagonal steel bracing members within bays to provide lateral stability to the structural frame.

name: Truss Erection
description: Lifting and placing prefabricated or field-assembled steel trusses for long-span roof or floor systems.

name: High-Strength Bolting
description: Installing and tensioning ASTM A325 or A490 high-strength bolts at structural connections to achieve specified pretension loads.

name: Field Welding
description: Performing structural welds on-site to connect steel members where bolted connections are not used or to supplement bolted joints.

name: Plumbing and Alignment
description: Surveying and adjusting steel members to ensure columns are plumb and beams are level within specified tolerances before final connection.

name: Shear Stud Installation
description: Welding headed shear studs to steel beams to create composite action between the steel and a concrete deck or slab.

name: Steel Connection
description: A fabricated joint assembly—such as a shear tab, end plate, or clip angle—used to transfer loads between steel members.

name: Anchor Bolt
description: Embedded threaded rods cast into the concrete foundation that secure the steel column base plate.

name: Steel Girder
description: A primary horizontal framing member that supports secondary beams and transfers loads to columns.

name: Splice Plate
description: A connecting plate used at field splices to join two sections of a beam or column end-to-end.

name: Erection Bolt
description: A temporary bolt used to align and hold steel members in position during erection before final high-strength bolts are installed.

name: Weld Metal (Filler)
description: Electrode or wire-fed filler material deposited during welding to fuse structural steel members together.

name: High-Strength Bolt (A325/A490)
description: Alloy-steel fasteners with specified proof-load strengths used in slip-critical and bearing-type structural connections.

name: Primer / Shop Coat Paint
description: Protective coating applied in the fabrication shop to prevent corrosion of steel surfaces during transportation and erection.

name: Structural Steel Framing System
description: The complete three-dimensional skeletal framework of columns, beams, and girders that carries building loads to the foundations.

name: Lateral Force Resisting System
description: The subsystem—comprising moment frames, braced frames, or shear walls—that resists horizontal wind and seismic loads.

name: Composite Floor System
description: An integrated structural system combining steel beams, shear studs, metal deck, and concrete topping to act as a single structural element.

name: Shop Drawing Review
description: Engineering review and approval of fabricator-produced drawings detailing member sizes, connection geometry, and weld specifications.

name: Steel Delivery and Sequencing
description: Coordinating just-in-time delivery and lay-down of fabricated steel members to the site in the correct erection sequence.

name: Crane Rigging and Lifting
description: Attaching rigging hardware to steel members and operating mobile or tower cranes to hoist members to their installed position.

name: Bolt Tension Verification
description: Inspecting and confirming that high-strength bolts have been tightened to the specified pretension using turn-of-nut, DTI washers, or torque-wrench methods.

name: Steel Touch-Up Painting / Field Coating
description: Applying protective paint or coating to field welds, damaged shop coat areas, and connections after erection to restore corrosion protection.

name: Structural Steel Erection Safety Planning
description: Developing fall protection, decking sequencing, and multi-lift rigging plans to comply with OSHA 1926 Subpart R during steel erection.

name: Temporary Shoring and Bracing
description: Installing provisional supports and guys to stabilize partially erected steel frames until permanent connections are complete.

name: Erection Zone / Lay-Down Area
description: A designated site area used for receiving, sorting, and staging fabricated steel members before they are lifted into place.

name: Structural Bay
description: The rectangular grid module defined by four surrounding columns that forms the repetitive unit of the steel framing layout.

name: IFC Structural Member (IfcMember)
description: IFC entity used to model generic structural members such as braces, purlins, and secondary framing that do not fit column or beam classifications.

name: Brick Laying
description: The process of placing and bonding individual bricks in mortar to construct walls, piers, or other structural elements.

name: Stone Masonry
description: Construction using natural or cut stone units laid in mortar or dry-stacked to form walls and structural elements.

name: Concrete Block Laying
description: Installation of precast concrete masonry units (CMUs) to build load-bearing or partition walls.

name: Mortar Jointing & Pointing
description: Finishing of mortar joints between masonry units to improve aesthetics, weather resistance, and durability.

name: Reinforced Masonry
description: Masonry construction in which steel reinforcing bars or mesh are embedded to improve tensile and seismic resistance.

name: Cavity Wall Construction
description: Building of double-leaf masonry walls separated by an air gap or insulation to enhance thermal and moisture performance.

name: Masonry Veneer Installation
description: Application of a non-structural masonry facing layer to an existing or new structural backing for aesthetic or protective purposes.

name: Tuckpointing
description: Repair activity involving removal of deteriorated mortar from joints and replacement with fresh mortar to restore masonry integrity.

name: Masonry Waterproofing & Damp-Proofing
description: Application of barriers, coatings, or membranes to masonry surfaces to prevent moisture ingress and rising damp.

name: Lintel Installation
description: Placement of horizontal structural members above masonry openings such as doors and windows to transfer loads around the opening.

name: Masonry Arch Construction
description: Formation of curved masonry structures over openings using wedge-shaped units to transfer loads by compression.

name: Scaffold Erection for Masonry
description: Setup of temporary elevated working platforms required to safely carry out masonry work at height.

name: Concrete Masonry Unit (CMU)
description: A precast hollow or solid concrete block used as a structural masonry unit in wall and partition construction.

name: Natural Stone Unit
description: Quarried or field stone shaped for use in stone masonry walls, providing strength and aesthetic character.

name: Wall Ties & Masonry Anchors
description: Metal connectors embedded in mortar joints to mechanically link masonry leaves, veneers, or masonry to structural frames.

name: Masonry Lintel
description: A horizontal steel, precast, or reinforced masonry beam spanning an opening in a masonry wall to carry superimposed loads.

name: Masonry Cavity Insulation
description: Thermal insulating material placed within the cavity of a double-leaf masonry wall to improve energy performance.

name: Reinforcing Steel (Rebar / Mesh)
description: Steel bars or wire mesh embedded in masonry units or mortar beds to provide tensile and shear capacity.

name: Masonry Bond Pattern
description: The arrangement and overlap pattern (e.g., running, Flemish, English bond) of masonry units chosen for structural or decorative effect.

name: Grout Filling
description: Pouring of fluid cementitious grout into the cells or cavities of masonry units to increase mass, strength, and fire resistance.

name: Masonry Surface Treatment & Cleaning
description: Post-construction cleaning, sealing, or coating of masonry surfaces to remove efflorescence, staining, and to protect the finish.

name: IFC Masonry Element
description: The IFC schema class (IfcWall / IfcMember with masonry predefined type) used to digitally represent masonry construction elements in BIM models.

name: Roof Deck Installation
description: The process of laying and securing the structural deck surface that serves as the base layer for all roofing materials.

name: Waterproofing Membrane Application
description: Installation of impermeable membrane layers to prevent water ingress through the roof assembly.

name: Insulation Layer Installation
description: Placement of thermal insulation boards or batts within the roof assembly to regulate heat transfer.

name: Underlayment Installation
description: Laying of a secondary water-resistant barrier directly over the deck before the final roofing surface is applied.

name: Shingle Installation
description: Fastening of overlapping individual shingle units (asphalt, wood, or composite) to create the weathering surface of a sloped roof.

name: Metal Roofing Panel Installation
description: Fixing of standing-seam or corrugated metal panels to the roof structure to form a durable, weather-resistant skin.

name: Tile Roofing Installation
description: Setting and securing of clay, concrete, or slate tiles in an overlapping pattern on a pitched roof.

name: Flat Roof Membrane Installation
description: Application of single-ply or built-up membrane systems (TPO, EPDM, PVC) on low-slope or flat roofs.

name: Flashing Installation
description: Cutting and fixing of thin metal or flexible sheets at roof joints, edges, and penetrations to direct water away from vulnerable junctions.

name: Ridge Cap Installation
description: Fitting of cap shingles or prefabricated ridge units along the apex of a pitched roof to seal and protect the ridge line.

name: Roof Ventilation System Installation
description: Fitting of ridge vents, soffit vents, or mechanical units to maintain adequate airflow in the roof cavity and prevent moisture buildup.

name: Gutter and Downpipe Installation
description: Mounting of perimeter drainage channels and vertical pipes to collect and discharge rainwater away from the building.

name: Skylight and Roof Light Installation
description: Cutting roof openings and fitting glazed or polycarbonate units to introduce natural daylight into the building below.

name: Roof Truss / Structural Frame
description: The engineered structural assembly of rafters, trusses, or beams that supports the entire roof load and transfers it to the walls or columns.

name: Roofing Underlayment
description: Breathable or non-breathable felt or synthetic sheet fixed beneath the outer roof covering as a secondary weather barrier.

name: Asphalt Shingles
description: Fibreglass or organic-mat shingles coated with asphalt and mineral granules, widely used as the exposed surface on pitched roofs.

name: Metal Roofing Panels
description: Profiled steel, aluminium, copper, or zinc sheets forming the outermost weather-resistant layer of a metal roof system.

name: Clay or Concrete Roof Tiles
description: Fired clay or cast concrete units shaped for interlocking or lapping installation on pitched roofs for long-term durability.

name: Slate Tiles
description: Natural stone slabs split to uniform thickness and used as a premium, long-life pitched roofing surface material.

name: EPDM / TPO / PVC Membrane
description: Synthetic rubber or thermoplastic single-ply sheet membranes used as the primary weathering layer on flat or low-slope roofs.

name: Roof Flashing
description: Preformed or site-cut metal or flexible strips installed at abutments, valleys, and penetrations to redirect water and prevent leaks.

name: Ridge Vent
description: A continuous or segmented ventilation unit installed at the roof ridge to allow warm, moist air to escape the roof space.

name: Roof Hatch / Access Hatch
description: A framed, weatherproof opening unit built into the roof to provide safe maintenance access to the roof surface or void.

name: Solar PV Roofing Integration
description: The incorporation of photovoltaic panels or integrated solar tiles into the roof assembly for on-site renewable energy generation.

name: Roof Space / Attic
description: The enclosed void between the structural roof frame and the ceiling of the topmost floor, used for insulation, services, or storage.

name: Plant / Maintenance Zone
description: A dedicated area on or within the roof structure allocated for mechanical and electrical plant, providing safe access for maintenance activities.

name: Substrate Preparation
description: Cleaning, levelling, and priming the base surface to ensure proper adhesion and alignment of cladding panels.

name: Framing and Furring
description: Erecting metal or timber sub-frame and furring strips that provide the structural backing to which cladding is fixed.

name: Weather-Resistive Barrier Application
description: Installing a moisture- and air-resistant membrane over the substrate before cladding panels are attached.

name: Cladding Panel
description: Individual prefabricated or site-cut boards, sheets, or tiles that form the visible outer skin of the building envelope.

name: Cladding Sub-Frame
description: Secondary structural framework of rails, brackets, or channels that supports and spaces the cladding panels away from the primary wall.

name: Mechanical Fixing
description: Screws, rivets, clips, or anchors used to mechanically attach cladding panels to the sub-frame or substrate.

name: Concealed Fixing System
description: Hidden clip-and-groove or back-fix arrangement that secures panels without exposed fasteners on the finished face.

name: Sealant and Joint Filling
description: Applying weatherproof sealants, backer rods, or foam tape to panel joints to prevent water and air ingress.

name: Fibre Cement Cladding
description: Factory-manufactured panels composed of cement, cellulose fibres, and aggregate, offering durability and fire resistance.

name: Stone or Brick Slip Cladding
description: Thin slices of natural stone or brick adhered or mechanically fixed to a backing system to replicate traditional masonry.

name: Corner and Edge Trim
description: Purpose-made aluminium, PVC, or composite profiles that neatly terminate and protect cladding at building corners and openings.

name: Window and Door Surround Integration
description: Coordinating cladding panels and flashings around window and door frames to achieve weathertight and aesthetic transitions.

name: Fire Cavity Barrier Installation
description: Fitting intumescent or mineral-wool barriers within the cladding cavity at floor lines and compartment boundaries to restrict fire spread.

name: Cladding Fire Safety Compliance Check
description: Verifying that all materials and assemblies meet applicable fire performance classifications and building regulation requirements.

name: Facade Access and Scaffolding
description: Temporary scaffolding, mast climbers, or suspended access platforms erected to allow safe installation of cladding at height.

name: Cladding Fixing Schedule
description: Producing the engineering document that specifies fixing centres, load capacities, and anchoring details for the cladding system.

name: Panel Layout and Setting-Out
description: Surveying and marking the facade grid lines to ensure panels are plumb, level, and correctly positioned before fixing commences.

name: Quality Inspection and Sign-Off
description: Systematic inspection of installed cladding for correct fixing, joint tolerances, surface finish, and weathertightness before handover.

name: Plumbing System Installation
description: Installation of water supply, drainage, waste, and vent pipework throughout the building.

name: Fire Protection System Installation
description: Installation of sprinkler systems, fire suppression pipework, and associated detection and alarm equipment.

name: Building Automation System Installation
description: Installation of centralized control systems that monitor and manage mechanical, electrical, and environmental systems within the building.

name: Gas Supply System Installation
description: Installation of natural gas or LPG pipework, meters, and regulators serving building appliances and heating equipment.

name: Hydronic Heating System Installation
description: Installation of hot water heating circuits, boilers, radiators, underfloor pipework, and associated pumps and manifolds.

name: Chilled Water System Installation
description: Installation of chilled water pipework, chillers, cooling towers, and terminal cooling units for air conditioning.

name: Domestic Hot Water System Installation
description: Installation of hot water storage vessels, heat exchangers, circulation pumps, and associated pipework for potable hot water supply.

name: Ventilation Ductwork Installation
description: Fabrication and installation of sheet metal or flexible duct systems for supply, return, and exhaust air distribution.

name: Pump
description: A mechanical device that circulates water or other fluids through hydronic heating, chilled water, or domestic hot water systems.

name: Thermostatic Radiator Valve
description: A self-regulating valve fitted to radiators that controls flow based on room temperature to maintain thermal comfort.

name: Variable Air Volume Box
description: A terminal unit that modulates the volume of conditioned air delivered to a zone in response to thermostat demand.

name: Extract Fan
description: A mechanical fan unit installed to remove stale air, moisture, or contaminants from wet rooms or localised areas.

name: Grille and Diffuser
description: Architectural air terminal devices that distribute supply or return air evenly into occupied spaces.

name: Pipework System
description: The complete network of pipes, fittings, and valves that distributes fluids such as water, refrigerant, or gas around the building.

name: Refrigerant Pipework
description: Copper or stainless steel tubing that carries refrigerant between split or VRF system indoor and outdoor units.

name: Insulation of Pipework and Ductwork
description: Application of thermal and acoustic insulation to pipework and ductwork to minimise heat loss, condensation, and noise transmission.

name: Pipe Insulation Material
description: Mineral wool, foam rubber, or phenolic foam products applied to pipework to control heat transfer and prevent condensation.

name: Sheet Metal Duct Material
description: Galvanised or stainless steel flat sheet formed into rectangular or circular duct sections for air distribution systems.

name: Copper Pipework Material
description: Copper tubing used extensively for domestic hot and cold water, heating, and refrigerant piping due to its durability and corrosion resistance.

name: Commissioning of Mechanical Systems
description: The systematic process of testing, balancing, and verifying that all installed mechanical systems perform to design specifications.

name: Mechanical Services Coordination
description: The multi-discipline coordination process that resolves spatial clashes between mechanical, electrical, structural, and architectural elements before installation.

name: IFC Mechanical Equipment
description: The IFC classification IfcMechanicalElement covering mechanical plant and equipment objects modelled in a BIM environment.

name: IFC Flow Distribution System
description: The IFC IfcDistributionSystem class representing logical groupings of mechanical flow distribution components such as pipework and ductwork networks.

name: Cable Containment Systems
description: Trays, trunking, conduits, and ladders used to route and protect electrical cables throughout the building.

name: Power Distribution Boards
description: Panelboards and consumer units that distribute incoming electrical supply to individual circuits across the building.

name: Main Switchgear Installation
description: Installation of the primary high-current switching and protection equipment at the building's main electrical intake.

name: Sub-Distribution Board Installation
description: Fitting and connecting of secondary distribution boards that serve individual floors, zones, or tenancies.

name: Final Circuit Wiring
description: Running and terminating the last-leg wiring from distribution boards to individual outlets, luminaires, and equipment.

name: Containment Installation
description: Physical fixing and assembly of cable trays, trunking, conduits, and associated supports prior to cable pulling.

name: Cable Pulling and Laying
description: Drawing cables through containment or directly fixing them along their designated routes within the structure.

name: Termination and Connection Works
description: Making off, terminating, and connecting cables at all equipment, accessories, and distribution points.

name: Low Voltage (LV) Switchgear
description: Circuit breakers, isolators, fuses, and busbars operating at low voltage for protection and control of electrical circuits.

name: Standby Generator Connection
description: Electrical integration and changeover switching of a standby generator into the building's power distribution network.

name: Power Factor Correction Equipment
description: Capacitor banks or active correction units installed to improve the power factor and reduce reactive power demand.

name: Metering and Sub-Metering Installation
description: Fitting of utility meters and sub-meters to measure and monitor energy consumption at building or tenancy level.

name: Electrical Metering Equipment
description: Smart meters, energy meters, and associated current transformers used to record electrical consumption data.

name: Socket Outlet Installation
description: Fixing and wiring of general-purpose and specialist socket outlets at workstations, plant areas, and common spaces.

name: Lighting Circuit Installation
description: Wiring of dedicated lighting circuits from distribution boards to luminaire positions and switching points.

name: Containment Materials (Cable Tray/Conduit)
description: Steel, aluminium, or PVC trays, conduits, and trunking sections forming the physical pathway for electrical cables.

name: Electrical Cabling Materials
description: Copper or aluminium conductors in various insulation types (LSF, XLPE, SWA) used for power and control wiring.

name: Wiring Accessories
description: Switches, sockets, grid plates, and grid frames forming the visible and accessible interface of the electrical installation.

name: Motor Control Centre (MCC) Installation
description: Assembly and connection of motor starters, variable speed drives, and protective relays within a dedicated motor control enclosure.

name: Variable Speed Drive (VSD) Installation
description: Mounting and electrical commissioning of frequency inverters controlling motor speed for HVAC, pumps, and lift equipment.

name: Electrical Inspection and Certification
description: Formal verification and production of Electrical Installation Certificates (EIC) or Minor Works certificates by a qualified person.

name: Transformer Installation
description: Positioning, connecting, and commissioning of step-up or step-down transformers within the building's electrical infrastructure.

name: Dry-Type / Cast-Resin Transformer
description: Indoor transformer using solid insulation rather than oil, used to step voltage levels within the building safely.

name: High Voltage (HV) Switchroom
description: Dedicated room housing high-voltage switchgear, ring-main units, and protection equipment at the building's primary intake.

name: Main Electrical Intake Room / Substation
description: Designated plant space where the utility supply enters the building and connects to the main switchgear and metering.

name: Electrical Riser Shaft
description: Vertical duct or shaft through which electrical cables, busbar trunking, and containment rise between building floors.

name: Electrical Distribution Cupboard / Riser Cabinet
description: Enclosed floor-level or riser cupboard housing sub-distribution boards, metering, and inter-floor cable connections.

name: Surge Protection Device (SPD) Installation
description: Fitting of transient voltage surge suppressors at distribution boards and equipment to protect against overvoltage events.

name: Arc Flash Risk Assessment
description: Engineering study and labelling exercise quantifying arc flash incident energy levels to define safe working boundaries.

name: Containment Sealing and Fire Stopping
description: Application of approved fire-stopping materials at cable and containment penetrations through fire-rated walls and floors.

name: Cable Management Labelling and Schedules
description: Systematic tagging, labelling, and documentation of all cables and circuits to support operation and maintenance.

name: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Infrastructure
description: Dedicated circuits, charge points, and load-management controls installed to support electric vehicle charging in car parks or parking areas.

name: Scratch Coat Application
description: The first layer of plaster applied to a surface, scratched to improve adhesion for subsequent coats.

name: Brown Coat Application
description: The second intermediate plaster coat applied over the scratch coat to level and straighten the surface.

name: Finish Coat Application
description: The final thin plaster layer applied to achieve a smooth, decorative, or textured surface finish.

name: Cement Plaster
description: A durable plaster mix of cement, sand, and water used for exterior and wet-area wall surfaces.

name: Lime Plaster
description: A traditional plaster material composed of lime putty or hydraulic lime, valued for breathability and flexibility.

name: Acrylic Plaster
description: A polymer-based finish plaster offering enhanced durability, water resistance, and color retention.

name: Plaster Mix Preparation
description: The process of proportioning and mixing plaster ingredients to the correct consistency before application.

name: Surface Preparation for Plastering
description: Pre-plastering work including cleaning, wetting, and priming substrate surfaces to ensure good bond.

name: Lath Installation
description: Fixing of metal or wood lath to structural surfaces to provide a mechanical key for plaster adhesion.

name: Metal Lath
description: Expanded or woven metal mesh fixed to substrates as a reinforcing base for plaster coats.

name: Plaster Bead / Corner Bead
description: Metal or PVC edge trim installed at corners and openings to protect and define plaster edges.

name: Plaster Stop Bead
description: A profile fixed at the termination of a plastered area to provide a clean, controlled edge.

name: Bonding Agent Application
description: Application of a chemical bonding compound to low-suction or smooth substrates prior to plastering.

name: Plastering Trowel
description: A flat steel hand tool used to spread, smooth, and finish plaster onto wall and ceiling surfaces.

name: Hawk (Plastering Tool)
description: A flat square board with a handle used by plasterers to hold and carry plaster during application.

name: Floating Rule / Darby
description: A long straight-edged tool used to level and rule off plaster coats to a flat plane.

name: Rendering
description: External application of a cement or lime-based plaster coat to masonry facades for protection and aesthetics.

name: Skimming
description: Application of a very thin finishing plaster coat over existing surfaces or plasterboard to achieve a smooth finish.

name: Stucco Application
description: Application of a decorative exterior plaster finish, often textured, using cement or lime-based mixes.

name: Venetian Plaster Application
description: Application of polished lime-based plaster in thin layers to create a high-gloss marble-like decorative finish.

name: Plaster Curing
description: The controlled drying and hardening process of applied plaster, including misting or environmental control to prevent cracking.

name: Plaster Repair / Patching
description: Remedial plastering work to fill cracks, holes, or damaged areas in existing plaster surfaces.

name: Fibrous Plaster
description: A reinforced gypsum plaster incorporating hessian or glass fibre, used for decorative mouldings and ceiling features.

name: Plaster Cornice Installation
description: Fixing of prefabricated or in-situ plaster cornices at wall-ceiling junctions for decorative effect.

name: Plaster Moulding / Ornamental Plasterwork
description: Crafting and installation of decorative plaster profiles, medallions, and relief features on walls and ceilings.

name: Undercoat Plaster
description: A base-layer plaster product formulated for build-up coats, providing strength and background levelling.

name: Perlite / Vermiculite Plaster
description: Lightweight aggregate plaster used for thermal insulation, fire protection, or acoustic performance.

name: Waterproof / Tanking Plaster
description: A specialist plaster additive or product that provides water-resistant properties for wet or below-grade areas.

name: Plasterboard (Drywall) Lining
description: A dry-lining system using gypsum board panels fixed to framing as an alternative substrate to wet plastering.

name: Ceramic Tile
description: A fired clay-based tile commonly used for wall and floor finishes in wet and dry areas.

name: Porcelain Tile
description: A dense, low-porosity fired tile valued for high durability and water resistance in floors and walls.

name: Natural Stone Tile
description: Cut slabs of marble, granite, slate, or limestone used as premium tile finishes.

name: Glass Tile
description: Translucent or opaque glass units used decoratively on walls, backsplashes, and pool linings.

name: Mosaic Tile
description: Small-format tiles, often mesh-mounted, used to create decorative patterns or artwork on surfaces.

name: Encaustic / Cement Tile
description: Handcrafted pigmented cement tiles used for decorative patterned floor and wall applications.

name: Quarry Tile
description: Unglazed extruded clay tile known for slip resistance and durability in commercial and industrial areas.

name: Vinyl Composition Tile (VCT)
description: A synthetic resilient tile made from PVC and mineral fillers used in commercial floor applications.

name: Tile Adhesive / Thinset Mortar
description: Cementitious or epoxy bonding compound used to adhere tiles to substrate surfaces.

name: Tile Grout
description: Cement or epoxy-based filler material applied between tile joints to seal and finish the installation.

name: Tile Backer Board
description: Cement, fiber, or foam substrate board installed behind tiles to provide a stable, moisture-resistant surface.

name: Tile Spacers
description: Small plastic or rubber crosses placed between tiles during installation to maintain consistent joint widths.

name: Movement / Expansion Joint
description: Intentional gaps filled with flexible sealant within tile fields to accommodate thermal and structural movement.

name: Tile Trim and Edge Profile
description: Metal or plastic finishing strips used to terminate tile edges, transitions, and corners cleanly.

name: Tile Leveling System
description: A clip-and-wedge or spin-down system used during installation to keep large-format tiles flush and lippage-free.

name: Heated Floor System (Electric / Hydronic)
description: Under-tile radiant heating system integrated beneath the tile bed to provide floor warming.

name: Layout and Setting Out
description: Planning and marking tile grid lines and reference points to ensure balanced, symmetrical placement.

name: Tile Cutting
description: Cutting tiles to size using wet saws, angle grinders, or manual cutters to fit edges, corners, and penetrations.

name: Adhesive / Mortar Application
description: Spreading and combing thinset or adhesive onto the substrate or tile back prior to setting.

name: Tile Setting / Bedding
description: Pressing and aligning tiles into the adhesive bed to achieve full contact and correct plane.

name: Silicone / Sealant Application
description: Applying flexible silicone sealant to internal corners, change-of-plane joints, and expansion gaps.

name: Tile Sealing
description: Applying penetrating or surface sealers to porous tiles and grout lines to resist staining and moisture.

name: Tile Removal / Demolition
description: Breaking out and disposing of existing tile, adhesive, and screed in preparation for a new installation.

name: Screed / Self-Leveling Compound
description: Pouring and screeding a leveling layer over the substrate to achieve a flat, even surface for tiling.

name: Wall Tiling
description: Installation of tiles onto vertical wall surfaces in kitchens, bathrooms, and other interior or exterior areas.

name: Floor Tiling
description: Installation of tiles onto horizontal floor substrates for functional and decorative purposes.

name: External / Facade Tiling
description: Application of tiles to building exteriors, including cladding, plinths, and feature facades.

name: Pool and Wet-Area Tiling
description: Specialist tiling of swimming pools, spa shells, showers, and other fully immersed or saturated environments.

name: Roof Tiling
description: Installation of clay, concrete, or slate roof tiles onto battened roof structures for weather protection.

name: Tile Inspection and Quality Control
description: Checking tile lippage, joint consistency, bond strength, and surface finish against project specifications.

name: Tiled Floor (Finished)
description: IFC-classified finished floor element composed of a tile layer, adhesive, and substrate assembly.

name: Tiled Wall (Finished)
description: IFC-classified finished wall element incorporating tile cladding applied over a backing system.

name: Wet Room / Shower Enclosure
description: A dedicated waterproofed space designed to receive specialist tile systems for bathing and showering.

name: Tile Storage and Acclimatization Area
description: A designated on-site zone where tiles are stored flat and allowed to reach ambient temperature before installation.

name: Sand and Cement Screed
description: A traditional mix of sand, cement, and water applied as a levelling layer over structural floors.

name: Flowing/Liquid Screed
description: A self-compacting, pumpable screed (often anhydrite or calcium sulphate-based) that self-levels without manual compaction.

name: Screed Primer / Bonding Agent
description: A liquid adhesive or primer applied to the base slab to improve the bond between substrate and screed layer.

name: Polypropylene Fibres
description: Short synthetic fibres mixed into the screed to provide micro-reinforcement and control plastic shrinkage cracking.

name: Expansion / Movement Joint
description: A deliberate gap or proprietary strip installed within the screed to accommodate thermal movement and prevent uncontrolled cracking.

name: Screed Bay Former
description: A temporary or permanent metal or plastic strip used to divide large screed areas into manageable bays during laying.

name: Screed Depth Gauge / Pin
description: A calibrated pin or gauge tool inserted into fresh screed to verify the specified depth across the pour area.

name: Screed Level Datum / Screed Rails
description: Levelling screeds, laser-set rails, or dot-and-dab datum points that guide the finisher to achieve a flat, true surface.

name: Damp-Proof Membrane (DPM)
description: A polyethylene or liquid-applied barrier placed beneath or above the screed to prevent moisture migration from the substrate.

name: Insulation Layer (Below Screed)
description: Rigid or semi-rigid thermal or acoustic insulation boards installed beneath the screed to meet energy or sound performance requirements.

name: Underfloor Heating Pipe / Element
description: Warm-water pipes or electric heating elements embedded within the screed that form part of a radiant underfloor heating system.

name: Surface Preparation Activity
description: The cleaning, grinding, shot-blasting, or priming of the base slab to ensure adequate adhesion and remove contaminants before screed application.

name: Screed Pumping and Laying
description: The mechanical pumping and distribution of liquid or semi-dry screed across the floor area via a pump and hose system.

name: Screed Compaction and Tamping
description: The manual or mechanical compaction of sand-cement screed using a tamping beam or power float to consolidate the mix and remove voids.

name: Screed Floating and Finishing
description: The smoothing and levelling of the screed surface using a hand or power float to achieve the required surface regularity (SR) class.

name: Curing of Screed
description: The controlled moisture retention process (using polythene sheeting, curing compounds, or misting) applied after laying to prevent premature drying and cracking.

name: Screed Drying and Moisture Testing
description: The monitoring of screed moisture content using hygrometers or carbide bomb tests before floor finishes are applied.

name: Screed Crack Repair
description: The remediation of cracks in cured screeds using resin injection, routing, or flexible sealant to restore structural and surface integrity.

name: Wearing Screed
description: A screed designed to serve as the finished floor surface in industrial or utility spaces, typically with a power-floated or hardened top.

name: Floor Flatness / Surface Regularity Survey
description: A post-screed quality control survey using a straightedge, F-number measurement, or laser scanner to verify compliance with SR1/SR2/SR3 tolerances.

name: Screed Thickness Design
description: The engineering calculation or specification of screed depth based on load, bay size, screed type, and any embedded services.

name: Acoustic Screed System
description: A screed system installed over resilient acoustic layers to meet impact and airborne sound insulation requirements between floors.

name: Heated Screed Commissioning
description: The controlled heat-up and cool-down procedure applied to screed containing underfloor heating to condition it before floor finishes are installed.

name: Batt Insulation Installation
description: Installation of pre-cut fiberglass or mineral wool batts into wall cavities, floors, and ceilings between framing members.

name: Spray Foam Insulation Application
description: Application of two-component polyurethane foam that expands in place to seal and insulate cavities, gaps, and irregular surfaces.

name: Blown-In Loose Fill Insulation
description: Pneumatic installation of cellulose, fiberglass, or mineral wool loose-fill material into attic floors or enclosed wall cavities.

name: Rigid Board Insulation Installation
description: Cutting and fastening of rigid foam or mineral wool boards to exterior walls, roofs, or foundation surfaces for continuous insulation layers.

name: Reflective Radiant Barrier Installation
description: Stapling or draping of foil-faced radiant barriers in attics or wall assemblies to reduce radiant heat transfer.

name: Pipe and Duct Insulation Wrapping
description: Wrapping mechanical pipes and HVAC ducts with foam, fiberglass, or rubber insulation to prevent heat loss and condensation.

name: Vapor Barrier Installation
description: Installation of polyethylene sheeting or vapor-retarding membranes to control moisture diffusion through insulated building assemblies.

name: Air Sealing
description: Application of caulk, foam, weatherstripping, or tapes to close air leakage paths before or alongside insulation placement.

name: Thermal Bridging Mitigation
description: Strategic placement of continuous insulation layers or thermal breaks to interrupt conductive heat paths through structural framing.

name: Fiberglass Batt
description: Pre-formed glass fiber insulation blankets with kraft paper, foil, or unfaced options, rated by R-value for wall and ceiling cavities.

name: Mineral Wool (Rockwool) Batt
description: Dense, fire-resistant insulation batts made from spun volcanic rock or slag, offering superior acoustic and thermal performance.

name: Open-Cell Spray Foam
description: Low-density expanding polyurethane foam with an open cell structure providing moderate R-value and excellent sound dampening.

name: Closed-Cell Spray Foam
description: High-density rigid polyurethane foam with a closed cell structure delivering high R-value per inch and acting as a vapor retarder.

name: Cellulose Loose Fill
description: Recycled paper-based blown insulation treated with fire retardants, suitable for attic and dense-pack wall applications.

name: Extruded Polystyrene (XPS) Board
description: Rigid foam insulation board with high compressive strength and moisture resistance, commonly used below grade and in exterior wall assemblies.

name: Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) Board
description: Lightweight rigid foam insulation board used in continuous exterior insulation systems and under-slab applications.

name: Polyisocyanurate (Polyiso) Board
description: High R-value rigid foam board faced with foil or fiberglass, commonly installed on roofs and exterior wall continuous insulation layers.

name: Vapor Retarder Membrane
description: Polyethylene film or specialized variable-permeance membrane installed to control moisture movement through wall and floor assemblies.

name: Thermal Bridging Break Tape
description: High-performance adhesive tape applied at rigid insulation joints and penetrations to maintain air and thermal continuity.

name: Wall Cavity Insulation Zone
description: The enclosed framing cavity between interior and exterior wall sheathings where batt or blown insulation is placed.

name: Attic Insulation Zone
description: The attic floor or roof deck area designated for loose-fill, batt, or spray foam insulation to limit thermal exchange with conditioned spaces below.

name: Crawl Space Insulation Zone
description: The below-floor space where insulation is applied to the floor joists or foundation walls to condition or semi-condition the area.

name: Roof Assembly Insulation Layer
description: The above-deck or between-rafter zone where rigid board or spray foam insulation is integrated into the roof construction.

name: Below-Grade Foundation Insulation Zone
description: Exterior or interior surfaces of basement and foundation walls where rigid insulation boards are installed to reduce ground heat loss.

name: Insulation Contractor
description: Specialized trade subcontractor responsible for supplying, cutting, fitting, and verifying all types of insulation materials on a project.

name: R-Value Testing and Verification
description: Field inspection and documentation process confirming that installed insulation meets specified R-value and coverage thickness requirements.

name: Building Envelope System
description: The integrated assembly of walls, roof, floor, windows, and doors that collectively controls heat, air, and moisture transfer in a building.

name: HVAC System Integration
description: Coordination of insulation levels with mechanical heating and cooling system sizing to optimize energy performance and equipment efficiency.

name: Fire Blocking and Draft Stopping
description: Installation of non-combustible or intumescent materials within insulated assemblies at required intervals to prevent fire spread through cavities.

name: Insulation Safety and PPE Compliance
description: Enforcement of protective equipment protocols including respirators, gloves, and eye protection during handling and installation of insulation materials.

name: Horizontal DPC Layer
description: A continuous horizontal barrier membrane installed within masonry walls to prevent rising dampness from the ground.

name: Vertical DPC Membrane
description: A vertically applied damp-proof membrane used to isolate walls from adjacent earth or wet structures.

name: Cavity Tray DPC
description: A shaped tray inserted into the cavity of a wall to redirect water that enters the cavity back to the outside.

name: Stepped DPC
description: A DPC that follows a stepped profile at junctions such as abutments between a roof and a wall to ensure continuous moisture protection.

name: DPC Mortar Bed
description: A levelled mortar bed laid immediately below the DPC to provide a smooth, even surface for the membrane to sit on.

name: Bitumen-Based DPC Membrane
description: A flexible bituminous sheet material traditionally used as a damp-proof course due to its low permeability.

name: Polyethylene DPC Sheet
description: A modern low-density or high-density polyethylene sheet membrane used as a cost-effective and durable damp-proof course.

name: Slate DPC
description: Two courses of natural slate bedded in cement mortar, historically used as a damp-proof course in older masonry construction.

name: Lead Flashing DPC
description: Lead sheet used as a DPC at critical junctions such as wall-to-roof interfaces due to its malleability and impermeability.

name: Chemical Injection DPC
description: A remedial technique where water-repellent chemicals are injected into an existing wall to create a new damp-proof zone.

name: Masonry Wall Preparation
description: Raking out joints, cleaning, and levelling the masonry surface in preparation for DPC membrane placement.

name: DPC Lapping and Jointing
description: The process of overlapping and sealing adjacent sheets of DPC material at joints to maintain a continuous moisture barrier.

name: DPC to DPM Continuity Connection
description: Joining the wall-level DPC to the floor-level damp-proof membrane to form an unbroken moisture barrier envelope.

name: Masonry Cutting for DPC Slot
description: Mechanically cutting a continuous horizontal slot in an existing wall to receive a retrofitted damp-proof course membrane.

name: Damp-Proof Membrane (DPM) Installation
description: The laying of a horizontal membrane beneath a ground floor slab or screed to prevent ground moisture from rising into the floor.

name: Rising Damp Assessment
description: A diagnostic survey to measure moisture levels in walls and determine the necessity, position, and extent of DPC installation.

name: Masonry Wall System
description: The overall brick or blockwork wall assembly within which the DPC is installed as a key moisture-control element.

name: Below-Ground Waterproofing System
description: An integrated system of membranes, drainage layers, and DPCs applied to substructure elements to exclude groundwater.

name: Ground Floor Slab Zone
description: The construction zone at ground-floor level where the DPC in walls must align and connect with the floor DPM to prevent moisture ingress.

name: Wall-Floor Junction
description: The critical interface between a wall and a floor structure where DPC and DPM continuity must be achieved.

name: Threshold and Door Sill Zone
description: The external-to-internal transition zone at door openings requiring special DPC detailing to prevent moisture ingress at low-level gaps.

name: Wall Tie Installation
description: The fixing of cavity wall ties which must be correctly positioned relative to the DPC to avoid creating moisture bridges across the cavity.

name: Weep Hole Formation
description: The creation of open perpend joints or inserts in the outer masonry leaf directly above a cavity tray DPC to allow trapped water to drain out.

name: Mortar Joint Sealing
description: Filling and finishing mortar joints around the DPC location to prevent moisture paths bypassing the membrane.

name: Building Regulation Compliance Inspection
description: A statutory inspection by a building control officer to verify that the DPC installation meets required codes and standards.

name: Wellpoint System Installation
description: Installing a series of shallow wellpoints connected to a header pipe to lower the groundwater table around an excavation.

name: Deep Well Dewatering
description: Drilling and equipping deep wells with submersible pumps to extract groundwater from significant depths below the excavation level.

name: Sump Pumping
description: Collecting groundwater seeping into an excavation in a sump pit and pumping it out to maintain a dry working environment.

name: Eductor/Ejector Well System
description: Using high-pressure water jets to create a vacuum that draws groundwater from fine-grained soils where wellpoints are less effective.

name: Vacuum Dewatering
description: Applying a vacuum to the drainage system to enhance extraction of water from low-permeability soils.

name: Electro-osmosis Dewatering
description: Applying an electrical current through saturated fine-grained soil to drive pore water toward cathode wells for extraction.

name: Horizontal Drainage Installation
description: Installing horizontal perforated drain pipes or sand drains to intercept and redirect groundwater flow away from the construction area.

name: Groundwater Monitoring
description: Continuously measuring groundwater levels and piezometric pressures throughout the dewatering operation to ensure effectiveness and safety.

name: Settlement Monitoring
description: Tracking ground and structure settlement caused by drawdown of the water table due to dewatering activities.

name: Discharge Water Treatment
description: Filtering or chemically treating pumped groundwater to meet regulatory standards before discharging it off-site.

name: Recharge Well System
description: A system of injection wells used to reintroduce treated groundwater into the ground to prevent settlement in adjacent areas.

name: Dewatering Pump
description: A submersible or surface pump unit used to extract groundwater from wells, sumps, or header pipes during dewatering operations.

name: Header Pipe
description: A main collector pipe connecting multiple wellpoints or well casings to the dewatering pump in a wellpoint system.

name: Wellpoint Riser Pipe
description: A small-diameter pipe connecting an individual wellpoint screen to the header pipe, through which groundwater is drawn.

name: Well Casing
description: A rigid pipe installed in a drilled borehole to maintain the well bore and support the filter pack in a deep-well dewatering system.

name: Well Screen
description: A perforated or slotted section of pipe placed at the base of a dewatering well to allow groundwater entry while excluding soil particles.

name: Filter Pack / Gravel Pack
description: Graded gravel or sand placed around a well screen to stabilize the borehole and act as a hydraulic filter for incoming groundwater.

name: Piezometer
description: An instrument installed in the ground to measure pore water pressure or groundwater level at a specific depth during dewatering.

name: Discharge Pipe Network
description: The network of pipes and hoses routing pumped groundwater from the extraction points to the designated discharge or treatment location.

name: Dewatering Design & Hydrogeological Survey
description: Conducting site investigations and hydraulic analysis to design an effective and safe dewatering scheme prior to construction.

name: Perimeter Cut-off Wall
description: A subsurface barrier such as a sheet pile wall or slurry wall used to limit groundwater inflow into the excavation zone, complementing active dewatering.

name: Dewatering Regulatory Permitting
description: Obtaining required environmental and municipal permits for groundwater extraction and discharge associated with construction dewatering.

name: Decommissioning of Dewatering System
description: Safely removing pumps, pipes, and wells and grouting or capping boreholes after construction dewatering is no longer required.

name: Topographic Survey
description: Measurement and mapping of the natural and man-made features of a site, including contours, elevations, and existing structures.

name: Boundary Survey
description: Precise determination and marking of legal property boundaries and corner points prior to or during construction.

name: Control Network Establishment
description: Installation and coordination of primary survey control points (benchmarks and traverse stations) that serve as reference datums for all setting-out work.

name: Benchmark Installation
description: Physical placement of fixed reference markers with known elevation used as the vertical datum throughout the project.

name: Grid Line Setting Out
description: Transferring the structural or column grid from drawings onto the physical site using pegs, profiles, and string lines.

name: Building Offset Lines
description: Establishing offset reference lines parallel to building faces to allow undisturbed reference during excavation and foundation work.

name: Profile Boards
description: Horizontal timber or metal boards fixed to upright stakes at known heights around the building perimeter to define gridlines and finished floor levels.

name: Site Datum Peg
description: A robust fixed peg or bolt on site set to a known reduced level from which all vertical measurements are referenced.

name: Excavation Setting Out
description: Marking the extent, depth, and slope of excavations on the ground surface to guide earthworks plant and operatives.

name: Foundation Setting Out
description: Positioning and marking the exact plan location, level, and dimensions of all foundations ready for concrete or masonry placement.

name: Column and Pile Position Setting Out
description: Accurately locating and marking individual column bases or pile positions within the structural grid on the prepared formation level.

name: As-Built Survey
description: Post-construction measurement survey to record the actual positions and levels of completed elements for record drawings and compliance verification.

name: Total Station
description: Electronic theodolite combined with an electronic distance measurement device used for precise angle and distance measurement during setting out.

name: GNSS / GPS Survey Equipment
description: Satellite-based positioning equipment providing real-time coordinates for site control and setting-out in open areas.

name: Optical Level (Dumpy Level)
description: Precision optical instrument used to establish and transfer horizontal planes of known elevation across a site.

name: Laser Level
description: Self-levelling laser instrument that projects a horizontal or vertical reference plane for rapid level transfer and alignment checking.

name: Theodolite
description: Precision optical or electronic instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles during traverse and setting-out operations.

name: Digital Level (Digital Staff)
description: Electronic levelling instrument that reads a bar-coded staff automatically to provide precise height differences and distances.

name: Survey Staff (Levelling Rod)
description: Graduated rod held vertically on a point whose elevation is to be determined when used with a levelling instrument.

name: Measuring Tape / Steel Band
description: Calibrated flexible measuring tape used for short-distance linear measurements and checking dimensions on site.

name: Theodolite Traverse
description: A series of connected survey lines of measured length and direction used to extend control across a large site.

name: Levelling Run
description: A sequence of instrument set-ups and staff readings used to determine and transfer reduced levels between benchmarks.

name: Coordinate Geometry (COGO) Calculation
description: Mathematical computation of setting-out coordinates, bearings, and distances from design data prior to fieldwork.

name: Setting-Out Drawings / Survey Control Plan
description: Formal drawing set showing control point coordinates, grid lines, and all dimensions required to position the structure on site.

name: Building Information Model (BIM) Survey Integration
description: Process of linking BIM model coordinates to the site control network to enable model-guided setting out and as-built capture.

name: Robotic Total Station (RTS) Setting Out
description: Automated one-person setting-out method where a motorised total station tracks a prism and guides the operative to design points.

name: 3D Laser Scanning (Terrestrial LiDAR)
description: High-density point-cloud capture of existing conditions or completed works for dimensional verification and clash detection.

name: UAV / Drone Photogrammetry Survey
description: Aerial survey using unmanned aircraft with photogrammetric processing to produce orthomosaics and digital terrain models of the site.

name: Plumb Bob / Optical Plummet
description: Instrument used to transfer a point vertically between floor levels or to check the verticality of columns and formwork.

name: Structural Verticality Check
