description: Periodic survey measurement verifying that walls, columns, and cores are being constructed plumb within specified tolerances.

name: Floor Level Monitoring
description: Regular precise levelling of slab surface points to confirm finished floor levels comply with design tolerances.

name: Setting-Out Tolerance Management
description: Specification, tracking, and verification of permissible deviations from design positions for all set-out elements.

name: Survey Quality Assurance & Close-Out
description: Independent check surveys, closure computations, and documentation confirming that setting-out accuracy meets project requirements.

name: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) Survey
description: Non-invasive sub-surface survey technique used to locate buried utilities, voids, and obstructions before setting out and excavation.

name: Utility / Services Survey
description: Identification, location, and recording of all existing above and below ground services within and adjacent to the site.

name: Geotechnical / Ground Investigation Survey
description: Investigation of sub-surface soil and rock conditions through trial pits, boreholes, and testing to inform foundation design and setting out.

name: Monitoring Survey (Settlement & Movement)
description: Periodic precise measurement of survey targets installed on structures and ground to detect and record movement during and after construction.

name: Survey Prism / Target
description: Retro-reflective optical target attached to a detail pole or structure and used with a total station for distance and angle measurement.

name: Hand-Held Laser Distance Meter
description: Portable instrument that measures distances by emitting a laser pulse, used for quick dimensional checks on site.

name: Survey Peg / Ground Spike
description: Timber or steel peg driven into the ground to mark a setting-out point or control station on site.

name: Trench Backfilling
description: Filling excavated trenches (e.g., for utilities or foundations) with suitable material after installation work is complete.

name: Foundation Backfilling
description: Returning soil or fill material around a completed foundation structure to restore grade and provide lateral support.

name: Retaining Wall Backfilling
description: Placing and compacting fill material behind a retaining wall, requiring careful sequencing to avoid overstressing the structure.

name: Basement Backfilling
description: Filling the excavated area surrounding a basement or below-grade structure after waterproofing and drainage systems are in place.

name: Pipe Bedding
description: Placing a prepared layer of granular material beneath and around buried pipes before backfilling to provide uniform support.

name: Select Fill Placement
description: Placing engineered or specified fill material (e.g., clean gravel, crushed stone) in defined zones to meet structural or drainage requirements.

name: Lift Placement
description: Depositing backfill in controlled, incremental horizontal layers (lifts) to facilitate proper compaction throughout the fill mass.

name: Moisture Conditioning
description: Adjusting the water content of fill material to optimum moisture level before or during compaction to achieve maximum density.

name: Proctor Compaction Testing
description: Laboratory and field testing to determine and verify the optimum moisture-density relationship of backfill soils per project specifications.

name: Nuclear Density Testing
description: In-situ field testing using a nuclear gauge to measure the compacted density and moisture content of placed backfill layers.

name: Geotextile Placement
description: Installing geotextile fabric at the boundary between native soil and fill to prevent material migration and maintain drainage performance.

name: Granular Backfill
description: Coarse-grained material such as gravel or crushed stone used as backfill where free drainage or high bearing capacity is required.

name: Engineered Fill
description: Controlled, tested, and specified soil or aggregate mixture placed and compacted to predetermined engineering properties.

name: Controlled Low-Strength Material (CLSM)
description: A self-compacting, cementitious flowable fill used in lieu of compacted backfill in confined or inaccessible spaces.

name: Structural Fill
description: Select soil or aggregate placed and compacted beneath or around structures to provide load-bearing support.

name: On-Site Excavated Soil (Reuse)
description: Native soil excavated from the site and stockpiled for reuse as backfill material where it meets specification requirements.

name: Imported Fill
description: Backfill material sourced and transported from an off-site location when on-site material is unsuitable or insufficient.

name: Plate Compactor
description: A vibrating plate machine used to compact granular backfill in shallow lifts, especially in confined or trench conditions.

name: Vibratory Roller
description: Heavy compaction equipment that uses vibration and weight to densify large open areas of backfill to specified density.

name: Jumping Jack (Rammer) Compactor
description: A narrow-footprint percussive compaction machine suited for compacting cohesive soils in tight trenches or restricted zones.

name: Sheepsfoot Roller
description: A compaction roller with protruding feet used to compact cohesive (clay-type) backfill soils by kneading action.

name: Drainage Pipe (Sub-drain)
description: Perforated pipe installed within or at the base of the backfill zone to collect and redirect infiltrating groundwater.

name: Excavation Zone
description: The void or open area created by excavation that defines the volume to be filled during the backfilling operation.

name: Fill Zone
description: The designated spatial area within an excavation where specific fill materials and compaction requirements apply per engineering design.

name: Stockpile Area
description: A designated on-site area where excavated or imported fill material is temporarily stored prior to placement.

name: Grading and Finish Earthwork
description: Final shaping and levelling of the ground surface above the backfilled area to achieve design grades and drainage slopes.

name: Soil Stabilization
description: Treating weak or expansive on-site soils with lime, cement, or other agents to make them suitable for use as compacted backfill.

name: Caulking
description: A specific sealing activity using flexible caulking compounds to fill and seal gaps between building elements such as frames, walls, and fixtures.

name: Expansion Joint Installation
description: The placement and securing of expansion joints to accommodate thermal movement and structural loads between building components.

name: Control Joint Formation
description: The deliberate creation of control joints in concrete, masonry, or plaster to direct and manage cracking due to shrinkage or movement.

name: Weatherstripping
description: The installation of flexible sealing strips around doors and windows to prevent drafts, moisture, and air infiltration.

name: Fire-Stop Sealing
description: The application of fire-rated sealants or intumescent materials to penetrations and joints in fire-rated assemblies to maintain compartmentalization.

name: Acoustic Sealing
description: The sealing of gaps and joints using acoustically rated materials to reduce sound transmission between spaces.

name: Waterproofing Joint Treatment
description: Specialized treatment of joints in wet areas, basements, or roofs to prevent water ingress using membranes or waterproof sealants.

name: Backer Rod Installation
description: The insertion of a foam backer rod into a joint to control sealant depth and provide a backing surface for proper sealant adhesion and performance.

name: Joint Preparation and Cleaning
description: Surface preparation activities including cleaning, priming, and profiling joint faces to ensure proper adhesion of sealing materials.

name: Mastic Sealant
description: A flexible, adhesive sealing compound used to fill and seal joints in various building substrates, providing durable weathertight bonds.

name: Foam Backer Rod
description: A compressible polyethylene foam rod inserted into joints to provide backing support and control sealant depth.

name: Joint Primer
description: A preparatory chemical coating applied to joint faces to enhance adhesion of sealants or grouts to the substrate.

name: Expansion Joint Cover Plate
description: A metal or rubber cover assembly installed over expansion joints in floors, walls, and ceilings to allow movement while protecting the joint.

name: Preformed Joint Tape
description: A self-adhesive or mechanically fixed tape applied over joints in sheathing, air barriers, or roofing membranes to seal against air and water.

name: Sealant Gun / Applicator
description: A hand-held or pneumatic tool used to dispense sealant cartridges uniformly into joints during sealing activities.

name: Joint Design and Specification
description: The engineering and specification process for determining joint type, location, dimensions, and suitable sealing materials for a building assembly.

name: Sealant Inspection and Testing
description: Quality assurance activities including visual inspection, adhesion testing, and water testing of completed joint and sealant work.

name: Re-sealing and Maintenance
description: Periodic removal of degraded sealant and reapplication of fresh sealant to maintain joint performance over the building lifecycle.

name: Intumescent Collar Installation
description: Fitting intumescent collars around plastic pipes passing through fire-rated walls or floors to seal the opening upon exposure to heat.

name: Fire Rated Sealant Application
description: Applying specialist fire-rated sealants to gaps and joints in fire-compartment walls, floors, and ceilings to prevent fire and smoke passage.

name: Firestop Pillow Placement
description: Installing compressible intumescent or endothermic pillows within cable and pipe penetrations to block fire and smoke spread.

name: Intumescent Wrap Installation
description: Wrapping combustible pipes with intumescent strip material so the strip expands and seals the penetration under fire conditions.

name: Fire Rated Board Installation
description: Cutting and fixing calcium silicate or similar fire-rated boards to close large service penetrations in compartment elements.

name: Mineral Wool Packing
description: Packing rock wool or mineral fibre into void spaces around penetrations as a passive fire-stop substrate before over-sealing.

name: Fire Rated Duct Wrap Installation
description: Applying intumescent or ceramic-fibre blanket wrapping to HVAC ducts where they pass through fire-rated compartment boundaries.

name: Fire Damper Installation
description: Fitting mechanical fire dampers within ductwork at fire-compartment boundaries to automatically close and restrict fire spread.

name: Smoke Seal Installation
description: Installing intumescent and cold-smoke brush or blade seals around door frames and service penetrations to limit smoke migration.

name: Firestop Mortar Application
description: Pouring or trowelling cementitious or gypsum-based firestop mortar into sleeve openings around cable bundles and pipe penetrations.

name: Compartmentation Survey
description: Inspecting and documenting existing fire-compartment boundaries to identify breaches, missing stops, and remedial works required.

name: Third-Party Inspection & Certification
description: Engaging an independent inspector to witness, test, and certify completed firestop installations against approved system drawings.

name: Penetration Sleeve Installation
description: Casting or fixing pre-formed steel or plastic sleeves into walls and floors to provide a controlled conduit for services prior to fire-stopping.

name: Firestop Spray Application
description: Spraying intumescent or cementitious coatings onto structural steel and service penetrations to achieve a required fire-resistance rating.

name: Intumescent Collar
description: A ring-shaped device containing intumescent material that expands on heating to crush and seal a plastic pipe penetration.

name: Firestop Pillow
description: A flexible, re-enterable bag filled with intumescent or endothermic material used to pack cable and pipe transit openings.

name: Intumescent Strip / Wrap
description: A flexible tape or strip impregnated with intumescent compounds that expands significantly when exposed to elevated temperatures.

name: Fire-Rated Sealant
description: A tested and classified sealant compound providing air, smoke, and fire resistance when cured within joints and penetrations.

name: Firestop Mortar
description: A cementitious or gypsum-based castable compound used to reinstate fire-rated floors and walls around service entries.

name: Mineral Wool / Rock Fibre
description: High-temperature-resistant fibrous insulation used as a backing or infill material within firestop assemblies.

name: Intumescent Coating / Spray
description: A paint-like or spray-applied coating that forms an insulating char layer on substrate surfaces when exposed to fire.

name: Penetration Sleeve
description: A pre-formed tubular insert cast or fixed into a wall or floor opening to receive and register a service penetration for fire-stopping.

name: Smoke Seal
description: A brush, blade, or intumescent seal fitted to door frames and service openings to retard cold-smoke passage.

name: Fire-Rated Duct Wrap
description: A factory-produced blanket or board system wrapped around ventilation ducts to maintain the fire resistance of a compartment boundary.

name: Fire Compartment Boundary
description: A designated zone interface—wall, floor, or ceiling—required by regulation to limit the spread of fire and smoke between compartments.

name: Service Riser / Duct Space
description: A vertical or horizontal void used to route building services, representing a high-risk route for fire spread requiring rigorous stopping.

name: Fire Resistance Rating
description: The classified performance system (e.g. EI 60, EI 120) that defines the duration a firestop assembly must resist fire penetration and insulation failure.

name: Compartmentation Management System
description: A record-keeping and inspection regime that tracks the location, specification, and condition of all firestop installations throughout a building's lifecycle.

name: Door Operator System
description: The motorised mechanism that automatically opens and closes both the car and landing doors in a coordinated sequence.

name: Safety Gear
description: Mechanical devices mounted on the car frame that grip the guide rails and stop the car instantly in the event of overspeed.

name: Wire Ropes / Belts
description: High-strength steel wire ropes or flat polyurethane-coated steel belts that suspend and drive the lift car.

name: Lift Car Enclosure & Finishes
description: Internal wall panels, flooring, ceiling, and lighting materials that define the aesthetic and functional interior of the car.

name: Shaft Structural Works
description: Civil and structural construction work required to form the lift shaft, including concrete, blockwork, or steel framework.

name: Pit Waterproofing
description: Application of waterproof membranes or tanking systems to the lift pit to prevent water ingress.

name: Rail Bracket Installation
description: Fixing of steel brackets to the shaft walls at regular intervals to support and align the guide rails.

name: Electrical Supply & Wiring
description: Installation of dedicated power circuits, control cabling, earthing, and lighting within the shaft and machine room to serve the lift.

name: Lift Commissioning & Testing
description: Systematic testing, adjustment, and regulatory sign-off of the fully installed lift to verify safe and correct operation.

name: Lift Pit Ladder & Access
description: Fixed ladder and stop switch assembly providing safe maintenance access into the lift pit.

name: Intercom & Emergency Communication System
description: A two-way audio communication system inside the car that connects trapped passengers to a 24-hour response centre.

name: Overload & Safety Sensors
description: Load-weighing and presence-detection sensors that prevent the lift from operating when overloaded or when doors are obstructed.

name: Machine-Room-Less (MRL) System
description: A lift variant in which the drive machine is located within the shaft itself, eliminating the need for a separate machine room.

name: Goods Lift
description: A heavy-duty lift variant designed specifically for transporting goods, with reinforced car structure and higher load capacity.

name: Accessibility / Platform Lift
description: A low-rise lift or vertical platform lift variant designed to provide wheelchair and mobility-impaired user access between levels.

name: Firefighters Lift
description: A lift conforming to fire evacuation standards, with a protected shaft, power backup, and dedicated firefighter control mode.

name: Lift Removal & Hoisting Equipment
description: Temporary crane, gantry, or hoisting arrangements used during installation to lower components into the shaft.

name: Vibration Isolation & Acoustic Treatment
description: Anti-vibration mounts, acoustic lining, and isolation pads used to minimise noise and vibration transmission from the lift machinery to the structure.

name: Fire Compartment
description: A bounded zone within a building designed to contain fire and smoke spread for a defined period.

name: Acoustic Zone
description: A spatially isolated area engineered to limit sound transmission between adjacent building regions.

name: Thermal Zone
description: A separately conditioned or insulated area with distinct heating, cooling, or ventilation requirements.

name: Seismic Zone
description: A building region designed with specific lateral-force-resisting measures to perform independently during seismic events.

name: Tenant Demise
description: A legally and physically bounded occupancy area allocated to a single tenant within a multi-tenanted building.

name: Security Zone
description: An access-controlled region separated from adjacent areas by monitored barriers and entry points.

name: Cleanroom Zone
description: A tightly controlled environment isolated from surrounding spaces to maintain specified air-quality and particulate standards.

name: Explosion Relief Zone
description: A purpose-designed region with blast-rated separations to contain the effects of an accidental explosion.

name: Flood Containment Zone
description: A below-grade or ground-level region with waterproof bounding elements to prevent flood water migration.

name: Expansion Joint Cover
description: A proprietary cover plate or profile that bridges a movement joint while accommodating differential displacement.

name: Fire-Rated Separation Wall
description: A wall assembly with a certified fire-resistance rating that forms the boundary of a fire compartment.

name: Acoustic Partition
description: A partition system with high sound-transmission-class rating used to isolate acoustic zones.

name: Blast Wall
description: A reinforced or composite wall designed to withstand and contain overpressure from an explosion.

name: Seismic Separation Gap
description: A calculated void maintained between adjacent structural sections to prevent pounding during an earthquake.

name: Demising Wall
description: A partition wall that legally and physically divides one tenancy or occupancy from another.

name: Fire Door Assembly
description: A rated door, frame, and hardware set that maintains compartment integrity while allowing controlled passage.

name: Smoke Barrier
description: A continuous membrane or wall assembly rated to limit smoke migration between adjacent zones.

name: Soundproof Floor/Ceiling Assembly
description: A composite floor-ceiling sandwich designed to attenuate both airborne and impact sound between vertically stacked zones.

name: Blast-Resistant Glazing
description: Laminated or framed glass designed to remain intact and contain fragments under explosion overpressure.

name: Flexible Sealant / Gap Filler
description: An elastomeric compound used to seal movement joints while accommodating differential deflection between zones.

name: Zone Boundary Survey
description: The process of measuring, marking, and documenting the precise physical extents of each independent region prior to construction.

name: Fire Compartmentation Design
description: The engineering and code-compliance process of defining fire-rated boundaries, egress, and suppression for each compartment.

name: Acoustic Modelling
description: Computer or analytical simulation of sound paths to verify zone isolation targets are met before detailing partitions.

name: Thermal Zoning Analysis
description: Energy modelling to assign heating/cooling strategies and set points for each independently conditioned region.

name: Seismic Gap Calculation
description: Structural analysis to determine the minimum separation required between adjacent building sections to avoid seismic pounding.

name: Compartmentation Inspection
description: A post-construction survey that verifies fire and smoke barriers are continuous, correctly rated, and properly sealed.

name: Movement Joint Installation
description: The site process of forming, positioning, and finishing expansion or seismic joints between independently moving building sections.

name: Penetration Fire-Stopping
description: The installation and inspection of rated seals around all service penetrations through compartment boundaries.

name: Tenant Fit-Out Coordination
description: The managed process of aligning independent tenant construction works with base-building zone definitions and shared-service boundaries.

name: IFC Space
description: The IFC entity used to represent any bounded spatial unit, including independently defined building regions, in a BIM model.

name: IFC Zone
description: An IFC grouping construct that aggregates related spaces (e.g., a thermal or fire zone) into a named independent region.

name: IFC Building Storey
description: The IFC entity representing a horizontal slice of a building that may contain one or more independent spatial regions.

name: IFC Wall
description: The IFC entity for vertical planar elements, including fire-rated and demising walls that define region boundaries.

name: IFC Door
description: The IFC entity representing door openings in zone boundaries, including rated fire and security doors.

name: IFC Plate
description: The IFC entity used to model flat planar elements such as blast walls, barrier panels, or floor-ceiling separation assemblies.

name: Urban Core Zone
description: The central, highest-density area of a town that serves as its primary commercial and civic hub.

name: Residential District
description: A designated zone within a town primarily allocated for housing and domestic living.

name: Industrial Zone
description: A planned area within or on the periphery of a town reserved for manufacturing, logistics, and heavy industry.

name: Green Belt
description: A protected open-land buffer surrounding a town to restrict urban sprawl and preserve natural landscape.

name: Transportation Corridor
description: A networked route of roads, rail, or transit infrastructure that connects towns and enables movement of people and goods.

name: Mixed-Use Development
description: A planned urban area combining residential, commercial, and recreational uses within the same zone.

name: Satellite Town
description: A smaller, semi-autonomous settlement planned in proximity to a larger urban centre to relieve population pressure.

name: Town Centre Infrastructure
description: The integrated set of utilities, streets, and civic facilities that support the functioning of a town's central area.

name: Land Use Zoning Plan
description: A regulatory document that partitions town land into designated use categories to guide spatial development.

name: Urban Grid Layout
description: The geometric street and block pattern that defines the physical structure and navigability of a town.

name: Public Open Space Network
description: A system of parks, plazas, and green corridors distributed throughout a town for public recreation and ecological function.

name: Water Supply & Drainage System
description: The municipal infrastructure for delivering potable water and managing stormwater and wastewater across a town.

name: Energy Distribution Grid
description: The network of electrical and gas supply lines that distribute energy to buildings and facilities within a town.

name: Telecommunications Network
description: The physical and digital infrastructure providing broadband, mobile, and data connectivity across a town.

name: Civic & Institutional Buildings
description: Purpose-built structures such as town halls, schools, and hospitals that anchor civic life in a settlement.

name: Urban Master Planning
description: The professional process of designing the long-term spatial layout and functional organisation of a town.

name: Site Preparation & Earthworks
description: Ground-clearing, grading, and levelling operations undertaken before town-scale construction begins.

name: Road & Street Construction
description: The civil engineering activity of building the primary and secondary road network that structures a town.

name: Utility Infrastructure Installation
description: The laying of underground and above-ground pipes, cables, and ducts required to service a new town area.

name: Environmental Impact Assessment
description: A statutory evaluation of how proposed town development will affect the surrounding natural and social environment.

name: Urban Densification
description: The planned process of increasing the building density and population within an existing town footprint.

name: Brownfield Remediation
description: The decontamination and rehabilitation of previously industrial or developed land prior to new town construction.

name: Asphalt & Bituminous Surfacing
description: Road-surfacing material widely used to pave town streets, car parks, and pedestrian pathways.

name: Precast Concrete Units
description: Factory-manufactured structural elements deployed at scale in the rapid construction of town buildings and civil works.

name: IfcSite
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcSpatialStructureElement.

name: IfcBuilding
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcSpatialStructureElement.

name: IfcZone
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcSystem.

name: IfcRoad
description: The IFC class representing road infrastructure elements that form the street network of a town.

name: IfcSpatialZone
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcSpatialElement.

name: Urban Finger
description: A linear extension of urban development that penetrates into the surrounding rural or natural landscape, forming one 'finger' of the city-country pattern.

name: Green Wedge
description: A wedge-shaped corridor of open, rural, or natural land that intrudes between urban fingers, ensuring countryside remains accessible to city residents.

name: Rural Buffer Zone
description: A protected transitional area of agricultural or natural land separating urban fingers to prevent their lateral merging.

name: Urban Growth Corridor
description: A designated linear zone along which urban development is guided and concentrated to form a single finger of the pattern.

name: Transit Spine
description: A high-capacity public transport artery (rail, BRT, or metro) running along the axis of an urban finger to structure and anchor its development.

name: Radial Road Infrastructure
description: A network of radial roads or motorways that follow the alignment of urban fingers and connect them back to the city core.

name: Finger Node / District Centre
description: A compact, mixed-use activity hub located at intervals along an urban finger, concentrating services and reducing car dependence.

name: City Core / Central Hub
description: The central convergence point from which all urban fingers radiate, typically the historic city centre or main CBD.

name: Peri-Urban Fringe
description: The transitional edge zone at the tip of each urban finger where built development gives way to open countryside.

name: Ecological Corridor
description: A continuous natural or semi-natural strip within the green wedge that facilitates wildlife movement between rural hinterland and urban green spaces.

name: Urban-Rural Interface Infrastructure
description: Physical boundary elements such as greenbelts, hedgerows, ditches, or fencing that delineate the edge between urban fingers and green wedges.

name: Mixed-Use Development Block
description: A building block combining residential, commercial, and community uses, deployed densely along the transit spine of each urban finger.

name: Cycle and Pedestrian Network
description: An integrated active-travel infrastructure connecting finger nodes, transit stops, and green wedges within and between urban fingers.

name: Green Wedge Recreational Facility
description: Amenities such as sports fields, allotments, picnic areas, or visitor centres located within green wedges to encourage public use of open land.

name: Stormwater and Drainage Network
description: A drainage system, including sustainable urban drainage (SuDS) features, that manages runoff along urban fingers and within green wedges.

name: District Heating and Energy Grid
description: A shared energy infrastructure running along the urban finger corridor to supply heat and power to densely developed nodes.

name: Agricultural Land Use Zone
description: Farmland or market-garden areas preserved within or adjacent to green wedges as productive rural land between urban fingers.

name: Urban Densification Activity
description: The planning and construction process of increasing building density and land-use intensity along existing urban finger corridors rather than expanding laterally.

name: Green Wedge Conservation Activity
description: Ongoing land-management, ecological restoration, and legal protection actions to maintain the openness and biodiversity of the green wedge.

name: Transit-Oriented Development (TOD)
description: A planning and construction strategy that concentrates higher-density mixed uses within walkable catchments of transit stations along the urban finger spine.

name: Land-Use Zoning and Masterplanning
description: The regulatory and design activity of defining permitted uses, densities, and boundaries for urban fingers and green wedges across the metropolitan area.

name: Infrastructure Extension Activity
description: The engineering and construction work of extending roads, utilities, and transit lines incrementally along an urban finger as it grows.

name: Greenbelt Legislation and Enforcement
description: Legal and administrative activity establishing, monitoring, and enforcing protected open-land designations within green wedges to resist urban sprawl.

name: Finger Urban Sprawl Prevention
description: Urban planning interventions and controls specifically aimed at preventing the lateral merging of adjacent urban fingers.

name: Reinforced Concrete Frame
description: The primary structural material used in multi-storey mixed-use buildings erected at high-density nodes along urban fingers.

name: Permeable Paving Material
description: Surfaces such as permeable asphalt or concrete blocks used in streets and car parks within urban fingers to support stormwater infiltration.

name: Native Planting and Soil Media
description: Indigenous plant species and growing substrates used in ecological corridors and green wedge landscaping to restore biodiversity.

name: Polycentric Metropolitan Region
description: A broader urban form in which multiple city-country finger structures radiate from several interconnected centres, representing a scaled-up variant of the concept.

name: Linear City Model
description: A related spatial planning concept where urban development is organised along a single continuous linear corridor, conceptually similar to one urban finger in isolation.

name: Garden City
description: A closely related planned urban concept integrating green space into city structure, sharing the city-country integration principle with city-country fingers.

name: Radial-Concentric City Structure
description: An urban structural system combining radial growth fingers with concentric ring roads or green belts, directly related to and often co-existing with the finger plan.

name: IfcSpace
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcSpatialStructureElement.

name: Irrigation Canal
description: A network of channels and conduits designed to distribute water from a source across valley farmland for crop irrigation.

name: Drainage Ditch
description: A shallow trench or channel excavated along field boundaries to remove excess surface water and prevent waterlogging of agricultural soil.

name: Flood Control Levee
description: An earthen or reinforced embankment constructed along watercourses to protect valley farmland from seasonal flooding.

name: Terraced Field
description: A stepped platform carved into valley slopes to create level planting surfaces and reduce soil erosion on inclined terrain.

name: Grain Storage Silo
description: A tall cylindrical or rectangular structure used to store harvested grain and protect it from moisture, pests, and environmental degradation.

name: Farm Access Road
description: An unpaved or paved rural road network connecting fields, storage facilities, and processing areas within the valley.

name: Windbreak / Shelterbelt
description: A row of trees or shrubs planted along field edges to reduce wind erosion, protect crops, and moderate the microclimate.

name: Irrigation Pump Station
description: A mechanical installation housing pumps and controls that lift or pressurize water for distribution through irrigation networks.

name: Reservoir / Water Retention Pond
description: An artificial or semi-natural impoundment used to collect and store rainwater or diverted stream water for controlled release to farmland.

name: Greenhouse / Polytunnel
description: A light-transmitting enclosure structure that extends the growing season and protects sensitive crops from adverse valley weather.

name: Farmstead / Agricultural Compound
description: A cluster of farm buildings including dwelling, storage, and equipment facilities forming the operational hub of a valley farm.

name: Soil Preparation & Tilling
description: The mechanical cultivation and conditioning of valley floor soil prior to planting to optimize structure, aeration, and nutrient availability.

name: Irrigation System Installation
description: The civil works activity involving the laying, connecting, and commissioning of pipes, channels, and control structures for crop irrigation.

name: Levee & Embankment Construction
description: Earthmoving and compaction works to build flood-protection embankments and retaining berms along valley watercourses.

name: Terracing & Land Grading
description: The reshaping of sloped valley land through cut-and-fill operations to create stable, level cultivation surfaces.

name: Drainage Infrastructure Installation
description: The excavation and placement of sub-surface pipes, open ditches, and outlet structures to manage subsurface and surface water runoff.

name: Crop Rotation Zone
description: A defined field section managed under a planned sequence of different crops to maintain soil fertility and reduce pest cycles.

name: Agroforestry Plot
description: A mixed land-use area integrating trees with crops or livestock to improve biodiversity, carbon sequestration, and long-term soil health.

name: Topsoil / Agricultural Loam
description: The fertile upper layer of valley soil, rich in organic matter and minerals, that directly supports plant growth and water retention.

name: Geotextile Erosion Membrane
description: A permeable synthetic fabric laid on slopes and channel banks to stabilize soil and prevent erosion while allowing water infiltration.

name: Concrete Irrigation Liner
description: A cast or precast concrete lining applied to irrigation channels to reduce seepage losses and improve flow efficiency.

name: Riparian Buffer Strip
description: A vegetated zone maintained along stream banks within the valley to filter agricultural runoff and protect aquatic ecosystems.

name: Agri-Processing Facility
description: A building or complex where harvested valley produce is cleaned, sorted, packaged, or processed before distribution.

name: Weather Monitoring Station
description: An array of sensors and data-logging equipment installed in the valley to record microclimatic data for precision farming decisions.

name: Cobblestone Paving
description: Traditional stone paving material used to surface country streets, providing historic character and texture.

name: Asphalt Road Surface
description: Bituminous macadam surface applied to country streets for durable, low-maintenance vehicular travel.

name: Gravel Track
description: Loose aggregate surface layer commonly used on rural and country roads for cost-effective surfacing.

name: Street Kerb & Edging
description: Raised border elements that define the boundary between the carriageway and adjacent verges or footways.

name: Footpath / Pavement
description: Dedicated pedestrian walkway running alongside the country street, separated from vehicular traffic.

name: Grass Verge
description: Soft landscaped strip of grass bordering the street, providing ecological buffer and rural character.

name: Hedgerow Boundary
description: Dense shrub or bush planting forming a natural enclosure along the sides of country streets.

name: Dry Stone Wall
description: Traditional unmortared stone wall forming field and street boundaries in rural environments.

name: Timber Post-and-Rail Fence
description: Rustic fencing system using wooden posts and horizontal rails to delineate street edges on country roads.

name: Street Drainage Channel
description: Surface or subsurface drainage network that collects and conveys runoff water away from the street surface.

name: Rural Street Lighting
description: Low-intensity lighting infrastructure providing safe illumination along country streets at night.

name: Road Marking & Signage
description: Painted surface markings and erected signs that regulate and guide traffic along the street network.

name: Passing Place / Turning Bay
description: Widened section of narrow country street allowing vehicles travelling in opposite directions to pass safely.

name: Junction & Crossroads
description: Intersection node where two or more country streets meet, requiring traffic management and visibility splays.

name: Street Tree Planting
description: Amenity and shade trees planted within the street corridor to enhance biodiversity and rural aesthetic.

name: Underground Utility Duct
description: Buried conduit network accommodating electricity, telecommunications, water, and gas services beneath the street.

name: Sub-base & Road Foundation Layer
description: Compacted granular or bound structural layers below the surface course that bear vehicular loading.

name: Road Construction & Earthworks
description: Civil engineering activities involving excavation, grading, and compaction to establish the street formation level.

name: Surfacing & Resurfacing Works
description: Application or renewal of the wearing course material to restore or upgrade the street riding surface.

name: Kerbing & Edging Installation
description: Placing and bedding of kerb units and edge restraints to complete street boundary definition.

name: Street Furniture Installation
description: Fixing of benches, bollards, signposts, and other ancillary items within the street environment.

name: Street Furniture
description: Collection of benches, bollards, bins, and posts placed within the street space to serve users.

name: Rural Lane Network
description: Interconnected system of country streets and lanes forming the local circulation fabric of a rural area.

name: Bridge & Culvert Structure
description: Load-bearing structure carrying the street over a watercourse or depression in the rural landscape.

name: Traffic Calming Feature
description: Physical interventions such as pinch points or rumble strips that reduce vehicle speeds on country streets.

name: Field Gate & Access Point
description: Hinged or sliding gate providing controlled vehicular or pedestrian access from the street into adjacent land.

name: Public Right of Way
description: Legally designated route over which the public has a right to pass, often coinciding with or branching from country streets.

name: Main Street Corridor
description: The primary commercial and pedestrian spine of a country town, lined with shopfronts, services, and civic buildings.

name: Town Square / Village Green
description: A central open public space used for community gatherings, markets, and civic events in a country town.

name: Heritage Shopfront Precinct
description: A cluster of historically significant retail buildings with traditional façades that define the character of a country town centre.

name: Council Chambers / Civic Building
description: The local government administration building that serves as the civic hub of the town.

name: Country Pub / Hotel
description: A traditional public house and accommodation venue that is a cultural cornerstone of Australian and regional country towns.

name: Rural Residential Dwelling
description: Detached housing on larger allotments typical of country town residential zones, often with verandahs and outbuildings.

name: Agricultural Supply Store / Produce Store
description: A retail and warehouse facility supplying farming equipment, feed, seeds, and rural goods to the surrounding community.

name: Country Railway Station
description: A heritage or operational rail facility serving as a transport node and landmark in the country town.

name: Grain Silo / Bulk Storage Facility
description: Large cylindrical storage structures for agricultural produce such as grain, wheat, or canola, often defining the town's skyline.

name: Water Tower
description: An elevated water storage structure supplying reticulated water to the town's residents and businesses.

name: Timber Verandah Structure
description: A covered, colonnaded front porch extending over the footpath, characteristic of historic country town shopfronts and residences.

name: Corrugated Metal Roofing
description: Galvanised or Colorbond corrugated steel sheeting widely used for roofing on sheds, homes, and commercial buildings in country towns.

name: Local Stone / Brick Masonry
description: Locally quarried stone or handmade brick used in the construction of heritage buildings and retaining walls throughout the town.

name: Unsealed / Rural Road Network
description: The network of gravel or dirt roads connecting residential areas, farms, and outskirts to the town centre.

name: Reticulated Water Supply System
description: The town-wide potable water distribution infrastructure including pipes, pumps, and storage reservoirs.

name: Septic and On-Site Wastewater System
description: Decentralised wastewater treatment systems used in areas of country towns not connected to a centralised sewerage network.

name: Overhead Powerline Network
description: Aerial electrical distribution lines supplying power to buildings across the town, commonly above-ground in rural settings.

name: Heritage Precinct Conservation Works
description: Restoration and conservation activities undertaken to preserve the architectural character and fabric of historic country town buildings.

name: Shopfront Façade Restoration
description: Repair and reinstatement of traditional timber, masonry, or iron shopfront elements to their original or heritage-compatible appearance.

name: Rural Infrastructure Upgrade
description: Improvement works to roads, water, power, and communications networks to support the liveability and economic activity of country towns.

name: Flood Mitigation and Levee Construction
description: Civil engineering works to protect country towns from flooding via levee banks, retention basins, and drainage improvements.

name: Community Hall / Memorial Hall Construction
description: Design and construction of multipurpose community meeting and event buildings that serve as social anchors of a country town.

name: Subdivision and Land Release
description: Planning and civil works to create new residential or commercial allotments at the edge of an expanding country town.

name: Country School / Primary School
description: A small-scale educational facility serving the children of the town and surrounding rural properties.

name: Country Hospital / Health Centre
description: A small regional hospital or multipurpose health service facility providing essential medical care to the town and surrounds.

name: Sports Oval / Recreation Reserve
description: An open-air sporting ground used for football, cricket, and community events, typically located at the edge of the town.

name: War Memorial / Cenotaph
description: A commemorative monument honouring local residents who served in armed conflicts, typically located in a prominent public space.

name: Country Church / Chapel
description: A small religious building that serves as a place of worship and community congregation in the town.

name: Rural Shed / Farm Building
description: A utilitarian agricultural structure used for equipment storage, workshops, or animal sheltering on properties adjacent to the town.

name: Rural Residential Building
description: A dwelling unit located in a countryside setting, designed to accommodate rural living needs.

name: Farmhouse
description: A traditional agricultural residence that serves as the primary home on a farming property.

name: Barn
description: A large agricultural outbuilding used for storing crops, equipment, or housing livestock.

name: Stable
description: A dedicated structure for housing and caring for horses or other working animals.

name: Grain Silo
description: A tall cylindrical structure used for the bulk storage of harvested grain or other agricultural commodities.

name: Irrigation System
description: A network of pipes, channels, and sprinklers that distributes water across agricultural fields.

name: Rural Road
description: An unpaved or lightly paved road connecting countryside properties and fields to main infrastructure.

name: Farm Track
description: A narrow, often unpaved path providing vehicle access across farmland for machinery and livestock movement.

name: Hedgerow
description: A dense row of shrubs or trees planted as a boundary marker or windbreak between agricultural fields.

name: Agricultural Land
description: Open land designated and managed for crop cultivation or animal grazing in rural environments.

name: Pasture
description: A grassed area of land used for grazing livestock such as cattle, sheep, or horses.

name: Orchard
description: A planted area of fruit or nut trees managed for agricultural or domestic food production.

name: Pond or Rural Water Feature
description: A natural or man-made body of water on countryside land serving ecological, agricultural, or aesthetic purposes.

name: Woodland Coppice
description: A managed area of trees periodically cut back to ground level to encourage multi-stem regrowth for timber or fuel.

name: Field Drainage System
description: A subsurface network of perforated pipes or ditches installed to remove excess water from agricultural fields.

name: Rural Septic System
description: An off-grid wastewater treatment system used where mains sewage infrastructure is unavailable in rural areas.

name: Off-Grid Power System
description: A self-contained energy generation and storage system, such as solar or wind, serving buildings without grid connectivity.

name: Clay Roof Tile
description: A fired clay roofing element traditionally used on countryside buildings for durability and vernacular aesthetic.

name: Thatch Roofing
description: A traditional roofing material made from dried straw or reeds, characteristic of historical rural architecture.

name: Land Clearance and Grubbing
description: The site preparation activity of removing vegetation, roots, and debris from rural land before construction or cultivation.

name: Soil Survey and Ground Investigation
description: The assessment of rural ground conditions, soil composition, and load-bearing capacity prior to development.

name: Rural Infrastructure Installation
description: The construction of off-grid utilities including water supply boreholes, septic tanks, and private access roads in countryside locations.

name: Agricultural Building Construction
description: The erection of purpose-built structures such as barns, silos, and stables to support farming operations.

name: Boundary and Fencing Works
description: The installation or restoration of walls, hedgerows, and fences to demarcate property and field boundaries.

name: Landscape and Ecological Planting
description: The deliberate planting of native trees, shrubs, and grasses to restore or enhance the natural countryside environment.

name: Rural Planning Permission
description: The formal regulatory process of obtaining planning consent for development in countryside and green belt areas.

name: IfcBuildingStorey
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcSpatialStructureElement.

name: Cultural District Zone
description: A designated spatial zone within the building that represents and celebrates a specific subculture through its layout, aesthetics, and programming.

name: Communal Gathering Plaza
description: An open shared space at the intersection of subculture zones, facilitating cross-cultural interaction and community events.

name: Subcultural Exhibition Alcove
description: A semi-enclosed niche or recess dedicated to displaying artifacts, art, and narratives belonging to a particular subculture.

name: Performance & Expression Stage
description: A flexible performance area designed to host music, dance, spoken word, or ritual activities tied to diverse subcultural traditions.

name: Workshop & Making Studio
description: A hands-on creative studio space where community members can practice and teach subcultural crafts, arts, and skills.

name: Transitional Threshold Corridor
description: A deliberately designed passageway that marks the experiential transition between two distinct subcultural zones.

name: Cultural Archive Room
description: A secure, climate-controlled room for the storage and display of physical cultural records, textiles, and heritage objects.

name: Adaptive Partition System
description: A movable or reconfigurable partition infrastructure that allows subcultural spaces to expand, contract, or be reprogrammed over time.

name: Immersive Lighting System
description: A programmable, zone-specific lighting system that creates distinct atmospheric and chromatic identities for each subcultural area.

name: Acoustic Zoning System
description: Sound-isolation and acoustic-tuning infrastructure that ensures each subcultural zone can operate at appropriate sound levels without interference.

name: Digital Signage & Wayfinding System
description: An integrated digital display network providing culturally sensitive, multilingual navigation and storytelling across the facility.

name: Cultural HVAC Zoning System
description: A segmented HVAC layout that independently controls temperature and air quality in each subcultural zone to accommodate different activities.

name: Mural & Surface Art Panel
description: Pre-finished or substrate-prepared wall panels specifically designed to receive large-scale mural artwork representing subcultural identity.

name: Modular Display Fixture
description: Freestanding or wall-mounted display units that can be reconfigured to showcase subcultural artifacts, merchandise, or installations.

name: Cultural Threshold Gate
description: An architecturally expressive entry portal or gateway element that signals entry into a specific subcultural zone.

name: Flexible Seating Bleacher
description: Retractable or stackable tiered seating units used to accommodate audiences at performances and cultural demonstrations.

name: Acoustic Baffle Panel
description: Suspended or wall-mounted sound-absorbing panels tuned to the specific acoustic needs of individual subcultural activity zones.

name: Raised Access Floor Plinth
description: Elevated floor platform sections used to define subcultural zones and conceal zone-specific MEP services beneath them.

name: Reclaimed Timber Cladding
description: Salvaged wood material used for interior wall and ceiling finishes, evoking organic and vernacular subcultural aesthetics.

name: Pigmented Microcement Screed
description: A tinted, thin-coat cement finish applied to floors and walls to create distinct color identities for each subcultural zone.

name: Perforated Metal Screen
description: Decorative and functional metal sheeting with patterned perforations used as dividers, ceilings, or feature walls within subcultural zones.

name: Acoustic Mass-Loaded Vinyl
description: High-density flexible material installed within wall and floor assemblies to provide sound transmission loss between adjacent zones.

name: Recycled Glass Mosaic Tile
description: Decorative tiles made from recycled glass, used to create culturally symbolic patterns and motifs on floors and feature walls.

name: Cultural Space Programming & Design
description: The participatory process of engaging subcultural communities to define the functional and aesthetic requirements of their dedicated spaces.

name: Acoustic Treatment Installation
description: The construction activity of fitting sound-absorbing, diffusing, and isolating materials and panels throughout subcultural zones.

name: Mural & Artwork Commissioning
description: The process of procuring, coordinating, and installing large-scale cultural artwork from community artists onto prepared building surfaces.

name: Adaptive Partition Installation
description: The construction activity of erecting, tracking, and testing movable partition systems that define reconfigurable subcultural zones.

name: Cultural Lighting Commissioning
description: The process of programming, calibrating, and testing zone-specific lighting scenes to achieve the desired cultural atmospheres.

name: Heritage Material Salvage & Integration
description: The careful recovery, preparation, and incorporation of culturally significant salvaged materials into the building's fabric.

name: Community Co-Design Workshop
description: Facilitated design sessions with subcultural stakeholders to co-create spatial layouts, finishes, and programming for their zones.

name: IfcFurniture
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFurnishingElement.

name: Touchdown Space
description: A brief-stay work point designed for workers who need to connect, check messages, or make calls for short durations.

name: Collaborative Hub
description: A shared informal area that supports spontaneous team interaction and group work across a distributed floor plate.

name: Focus Booth
description: A small enclosed or semi-enclosed pod that provides acoustic privacy for concentrated individual work within a scattered layout.

name: Quiet Zone
description: A designated low-noise area within the scattered work environment where distraction-free solo work is enforced by protocol.

name: Phone Booth / Call Pod
description: A compact, acoustically treated enclosure that allows private voice or video calls without disturbing surrounding workers.

name: Breakout Lounge
description: An informal seating cluster that serves as an alternative work setting, encouraging relaxed posture and casual collaboration.

name: Agile Workstation
description: A reconfigurable desk unit—often height-adjustable—that can be rapidly relocated or repurposed to support shifting team sizes.

name: Movable Partition / Screen
description: A lightweight freestanding or track-mounted divider used to redefine sub-zones within the scattered work landscape on demand.

name: Flexible Power & Data Distribution System
description: An in-floor or overhead busway/grid system that delivers electrical and network connectivity to any point on the floor plate without fixed conduit runs.

name: Activity-Based Lighting System
description: A zoned, sensor-driven lighting installation that automatically adjusts colour temperature and intensity to suit the work mode of each scattered zone.

name: Occupancy Sensing & Desk-Booking System
description: An IoT platform combining occupancy sensors and a booking app that tracks desk utilisation and guides workers to available spaces in real time.

name: HVAC Zoning & Underfloor Air Distribution
description: A mechanical ventilation strategy that delivers conditioned air through floor diffusers, enabling re-zoning of thermal comfort as layouts change.

name: Acoustic Ceiling Treatment
description: High-NRC ceiling tiles or baffles installed overhead to reduce reverberation and speech intelligibility issues across large open work floors.

name: Biophilic Planting / Green Wall
description: Living plant installations used as natural spatial dividers and wellbeing enhancers within the scattered work environment.

name: Loose Furniture & Soft Seating
description: Lightweight, non-fixed chairs, sofas, and tables that can be rearranged by occupants to continuously reshape the work landscape.

name: Wayfinding & Zone Signage
description: Visual cues—digital or physical—that help occupants navigate between the different work modes and zones in a scattered layout.

name: Interior Fit-Out & Space Planning
description: The construction and design activity of partitioning, furnishing, and finishing an open floor plate to create a functional scattered work environment.

name: Mechanical & Electrical Re-zoning
description: Reconfiguration works to power, data, lighting, and HVAC circuits carried out whenever the scattered work layout is significantly changed.

name: Post-Occupancy Evaluation (POE)
description: A systematic assessment of how well the scattered work environment meets occupant needs, informing future layout iterations.

name: Activity-Based Working (ABW) Strategy
description: An organisational and spatial framework that aligns different task types with purpose-designed settings distributed across the floor plate.

name: Neighbourhood / Home-Base Zone
description: A loosely assigned cluster of workpoints where a team preferentially gathers, providing social cohesion within an otherwise unassigned floor.

name: IFC Furniture (IfcFurnishingElement)
description: The IFC entity that represents individual loose or agile furniture items placed within scattered work zones in the building model.

name: IFC Zone (IfcZone)
description: An IFC grouping entity that aggregates related IfcSpaces (e.g., all quiet zones on a floor) for facilities management and energy analysis.

name: Urban Plaza
description: An open public gathering area within the city that serves as a focal point for social interaction and civic life.

name: City Skyline View Corridor
description: A protected sightline or framed opening designed to maximize dramatic views of the urban skyline.

name: Rooftop Observation Deck
description: An elevated outdoor platform providing panoramic views over the cityscape for visitors and occupants.

name: Night Illumination System
description: An integrated lighting network that creates dramatic ambient and accent lighting to enhance the city's nocturnal atmosphere.

name: Landmark Facade

name: Tactile Paving Surface

name: Canopy / Roof Structure

name: Bicycle Parking Rack

name: Electric Vehicle Charging Point

name: Drainage System

name: Utilities and Power Supply Infrastructure

name: Construction of Platform / Hard Standing

name: Shelter Erection

name: Signage Installation

name: Utility Trenching and Ducting

name: Community Centre

name: Healthcare Centre / Clinic

name: Retail / Commercial High Street

name: Public Open Space & Parks

name: Sports & Leisure Facility

name: Place of Worship

name: Library / Knowledge Hub

name: Early Years / Nursery Facility

name: Emergency Services Station

name: Utilities & Energy Centre

name: Water Supply & Distribution System

name: Wastewater & Sewerage System
description: Foul and surface-water drainage network, pumping stations, and connections to treatment works serving all community parcels.

name: District Heating Network
description: A community-wide thermal energy distribution loop supplying heat and hot water to residential and commercial buildings.

name: Broadband & Telecommunications Infrastructure
description: Fibre, ducting, and wireless network infrastructure providing high-speed digital connectivity to every premise in the community.

name: Road & Street Network
description: The hierarchy of primary, secondary, and residential roads with kerbs, footways, and traffic-management features.

name: Cycling & Walking Path Network
description: Segregated cycle lanes and pedestrian routes connecting all land-uses within the community to promote active travel.

name: Public Transport Infrastructure
description: Bus stops, shelters, turning circles, and potential tram or rail stops linking the community to the wider urban network.

name: Stormwater Management & SuDS
description: Sustainable urban drainage features—swales, retention ponds, permeable paving—managing surface-water runoff across the site.

name: Street Lighting System
description: An energy-efficient public lighting network covering roads, paths, and public spaces throughout the community.

name: Waste Management & Recycling Infrastructure
description: Communal bin stores, underground waste systems, and recycling points facilitating refuse collection for 7,000 residents.

name: Structural Frame & Foundation System
description: The load-bearing skeletal structure—piles, ground beams, columns, and floors—common to the residential and civic buildings.

name: External Envelope / Façade System
description: Walls, cladding, windows, and roof assemblies forming the weathertight outer skin of community buildings.

name: Insulation & Thermal Performance Layer
description: High-performance insulation materials applied to walls, roofs, and floors to meet energy efficiency targets across the community.

name: Structural Steelwork
description: Steel sections and connections used in the frames of community buildings such as the leisure centre and school roofs.

name: Masonry & Brickwork
description: Clay brick, block, or stone masonry forming the external and internal walls of residential and civic buildings.

name: Timber & Engineered Wood Products
description: Structural and finish timber—CLT, glulam, joists—used in housing and community buildings to reduce embodied carbon.

name: Landscaping & Hard Landscaping Materials
description: Paving, gravel, topsoil, planting, and street furniture materials used to finish public realm and open-space areas.

name: Masterplanning & Urban Design
description: The professional planning activity of laying out land uses, densities, movement networks, and open spaces for the entire community.

name: Ground Investigation & Site Survey
description: Geotechnical and topographic surveys carried out prior to construction to characterise the site and inform foundation design.

name: Earthworks & Site Preparation
description: Bulk excavation, cut-and-fill, decontamination, and levelling operations that prepare the land for construction.

name: Infrastructure & Utilities Installation
description: The laying of underground pipes, ducts, cables, and road sub-bases forming the primary infrastructure backbone of the community.

name: Residential Building Construction
description: The phased design, procurement, and construction of all housing units across the community development.

name: Civic & Community Building Construction
description: Construction of schools, health centres, community centres, and other non-residential community buildings.

name: Public Realm & Landscaping Works
description: Installation of street furniture, planting, hard paving, and park features to complete the community's outdoor environment.

name: Phased Handover & Occupation
description: The staged process of completing, inspecting, and handing over parcels of the community to residents and operators.

name: Community Engagement & Consultation
description: Structured participation processes involving future residents and stakeholders in shaping the design of the community.

name: Transition Zone
description: A buffer space between two distinct cultural or functional areas that eases the shift in environment, acoustics, or use.

name: Acoustic Barrier Assembly
description: A layered wall, floor, or ceiling system engineered to attenuate sound transmission across subculture boundaries.

name: Threshold Marker
description: A physical element such as a change in flooring material, a step, or a low wall that signals the crossing from one zone to another.

name: Boundary Signage System
description: Wayfinding and identity signage installed at a boundary to communicate zone rules, identity, or cultural context.

name: Access Control Gate
description: A turnstile, sliding door, or barrier device that regulates who may cross a subculture boundary.

name: Security Glazing Panel
description: Laminated or tempered glass used at boundary points to allow visual continuity while maintaining physical separation.

name: Lighting Transition Layer
description: A lighting design zone that uses changing colour temperature or intensity to psychologically reinforce a spatial boundary.

name: Material Finish Change
description: A deliberate switch in surface material—such as carpet to polished concrete—used to mark the transition between subculture zones.

name: Boundary Corridor
description: A narrow circulation spine that runs along or between two subculture zones, serving as a neutral passage.

name: Airlock Vestibule
description: A small enclosed antechamber at a boundary that manages air pressure, odour, or noise bleed between adjacent zones.

name: Planter or Landscape Screen
description: A row of planters, hedges, or green walls used as a soft, informal separator between subculture areas.

name: Fire Separation Wall
description: A rated fire-resistive assembly that coincides with or reinforces a subculture boundary to meet code compartmentalisation requirements.

name: Zone Installation Activity
description: The construction process of erecting, finishing, and commissioning all boundary elements that define a subculture zone interface.

name: Access Control Integration
description: The installation and programming of electronic hardware and software to enforce passage rules at a subculture boundary.

name: Boundary Demolition and Reconfiguration
description: The planned removal or relocation of existing boundary elements to alter the extent or position of subculture zones.

name: Wayfinding Design and Implementation
description: The planning, fabrication, and installation of signs and floor graphics that guide occupants through or around a boundary.

name: Cultural Identity Zone
description: A defined area within a building intentionally designed to reflect and serve the norms, aesthetics, and activities of a specific subculture.

name: Mixed-Use Interface Node
description: A point or small area where two or more subculture zones meet, share amenities, or allow controlled interaction.

name: Operable Partition System
description: A moveable wall or folding panel system that allows the boundary between subculture spaces to be opened or closed as needed.

name: Smoke Curtain Assembly
description: A deployable or fixed smoke-containment screen positioned at a boundary to limit smoke migration between zones in an emergency.

name: Privacy Screen
description: A freestanding or fixed panel that provides visual separation without full enclosure at the edge of a subculture space.

name: IFC Space Boundary Element
description: The IfcRelSpaceBoundary IFC entity used to formally model the relationship between a space and its bounding construction elements in a BIM environment.

name: Distinct Street Pattern
description: A recognizable grid, organic, or radial road layout that gives the neighborhood its unique navigational character.

name: Landmark Building
description: A prominent, visually distinctive structure that serves as an orientation reference and symbolic anchor for the neighborhood.

name: Local Commercial Strip
description: A concentration of ground-floor retail, cafés, and services along a primary street that acts as the neighborhood's social and economic spine.

name: Public Open Space
description: Parks, plazas, squares, and pocket gardens that provide communal gathering and recreational areas within the neighborhood.

name: Residential Block Typology
description: The predominant building form—terrace, perimeter block, villa, slab block—that defines the neighborhood's architectural grain and density.

name: Pedestrian Network
description: An interconnected system of footpaths, crossings, and shared surfaces that enables safe walkability throughout the neighborhood.

name: Cycling Infrastructure
description: Dedicated lanes, shared paths, and bike-parking facilities that support cycling as a primary mode of local movement.

name: Neighborhood Center

name: Streetscape Furniture

name: Street Tree Canopy

name: Local Civic Building

name: Mixed-Use Zoning Area

name: Heritage Precinct

name: Public Art Installation

name: Surface Paving Material

name: Neighborhood Masterplanning

name: Infill Development

name: Heritage Conservation Works

name: Community Engagement Process

name: Edge Treatment

name: Stormwater Management System

name: Underground Utility Network
description: Coordinated below-ground infrastructure—water, sewer, gas, electricity, telecommunications—serving all premises in the neighborhood.

name: Neighborhood Branding & Identity Scheme

name: Perimeter Fence

name: Boundary Wall

name: Entry Gate

name: Stormwater Drainage Channel

name: Buffer Zone / Setback Strip

name: Pedestrian Pathway Along Boundary

name: Green Belt / Landscaped Border
description: A planted strip of vegetation, trees, or hedging that visually and physically softens the neighborhood boundary edge.

name: Service Corridor / Utility Easement

name: Masonry Block (CMU)

name: Precast Concrete Panel

name: Chain-Link Fencing Material

name: Wrought Iron / Steel Railing Material
description: Decorative and structural metal elements used for high-visibility, aesthetically appealing boundary fences and gates.

name: Hedge / Living Fence Planting
description: Dense shrub or hedge species planted as a natural, ecological alternative or complement to hard boundary structures.

name: Boundary Survey & Marking

name: Boundary Wall / Fence Construction
description: The construction activity involving excavation, foundation work, and erection of walls or fences along the defined boundary.

name: Gate & Access Point Installation

name: Perimeter Security System Installation
description: The activity of fitting cameras, sensors, lighting, and intercom systems along the boundary to establish a complete security envelope.

name: Landscaping & Planting Along Boundary
description: Horticultural activity involving the planting of trees, shrubs, and ground cover to establish the green boundary buffer.

name: Boundary Maintenance & Inspection
description: Periodic inspection, repair, and upkeep of all physical boundary elements to ensure structural integrity and functionality.

name: Legal Easement Registration
description: The administrative and legal process of recording boundary easements, rights-of-way, and encumbrances with the relevant land authority.

description: Electronic signage and announcement systems that provide real-time schedule, route, and service-disruption information.

name: Accessibility Ramp and Tactile Guidance

name: Acoustic Damping Material

name: Tunnel Boring and Excavation

name: Track Laying and Rail Installation

name: Station Fitout and Finishing Works
description: Interior construction activities including tiling, cladding, signage installation, and fixture fitting within transit stations.

name: Systems Integration and Commissioning
description: The process of testing and validating all mechanical, electrical, and digital systems prior to public transit operations commencing.

name: Depot and Maintenance Facility
description: An operational facility where transit vehicles are stored, inspected, serviced, and repaired overnight or between shifts.

name: Control and Operations Centre
description: A centralised facility housing staff and technology to monitor, manage, and coordinate the entire transit network in real time.

name: Central Island
description: The raised or landscaped circular area at the centre of a ring road junction that deflects and controls traffic flow.

name: Circulatory Carriageway
description: The one-way travel lane that loops around the central island and carries vehicles through the junction.

name: Entry Lane
description: The approach lane through which vehicles enter the circulatory carriageway from a connecting road.

name: Exit Lane
description: The dedicated lane through which vehicles leave the circulatory carriageway onto a connecting road.

name: Splitter Island
description: A triangular or elongated raised island placed on approach roads to separate entry and exit traffic and provide pedestrian refuge.

name: Kerb and Edging
description: Concrete or stone border elements that define the edge of the carriageway, islands, and footways around the junction.

name: Mountable Apron
description: A paved ring immediately surrounding the central island that allows large vehicles to overhang or mount it when negotiating tight roundabouts.

name: Pavement / Road Surface Layer

name: Sub-base and Base Course

name: Road Markings and Lane Lines

name: Traffic Signs and Gantries

name: Drainage and Stormwater System

name: Traffic Signal System

name: CCTV and Traffic Monitoring System

name: Pedestrian Crossing Infrastructure
description: Zebra crossings, dropped kerbs, tactile paving, and signal-controlled crossings that allow pedestrians to cross the arms safely.

name: Cycle Lane and Shared Path

name: Landscape and Planting Works
description: Establishment of grass, shrubs, trees, or hard landscaping on the central island and verges to enhance appearance and aid driver orientation.

name: Earthworks and Grading
description: Excavation, fill, and shaping of the ground to achieve the required levels and cross-fall for the junction and its approaches.

name: Pavement Construction Activity
description: Laying, compacting, and finishing of sub-base, base, binder, and wearing course layers across the carriageway.

name: Kerbing and Edging Installation
description: Setting out, bedding, and jointing of kerb units around the central island, splitter islands, and carriageway edges.

name: Road Marking Application
description: Spraying or thermoplastic application of lane lines, yield markings, and legends onto the finished road surface.

name: Traffic Management During Construction
description: Planning and implementation of temporary signs, barriers, and signal changes to maintain safe traffic flow while works are carried out.

name: Utility Diversion and Ducting
description: Relocation of existing underground services and installation of ducts to accommodate the new junction geometry.

name: Mini Roundabout

name: Double Roundabout
description: Two closely spaced roundabouts linked by a short section of road, used to handle complex multi-arm intersections.

name: Turbo Roundabout
description: A spiral-lane roundabout variant with raised lane dividers that pre-select exit lanes and reduce weaving conflicts.

name: Grade-Separated Interchange
description: A multi-level junction variant where the ring road passes over or under crossing roads via flyovers or underpasses, eliminating at-grade conflict points.

name: IFC Road Element (IfcRoad)
description: The IFC schema class representing a road spatial structure element, used to model the ring road geometry and data in BIM workflows.

name: IFC Kerb (IfcKerb)

name: Collaborative Classroom

name: Library & Resource Centre
description: A curated repository space providing access to physical and digital learning materials.

name: Maker Space / Innovation Lab
description: A hands-on workshop environment equipped for prototyping, STEM experiments, and creative production.

name: Seminar Room

name: Breakout Zone
description: An informal open or semi-open area adjacent to classrooms where small groups can work independently.

name: Lecture Theatre
description: A tiered, large-capacity auditorium-style space for formal didactic instruction to large cohorts.

name: Digital Learning Hub
description: A technology-rich space providing high-density computing, virtual reality, and e-learning stations.

name: Staff Collaboration Suite
description: A dedicated zone for educators to co-plan curricula, meet, and develop teaching resources.

name: Outdoor Learning Courtyard
description: A landscaped external area integrated into the learning campus for informal and nature-based education.

name: Quiet Study Room
description: A low-stimulus, acoustically controlled enclosure supporting individual focused study.

name: Presentation & Exhibition Gallery
description: An open gallery or display corridor where learner work and knowledge artefacts are exhibited.

name: IT & AV Infrastructure System
description: An integrated network of data cabling, wireless access points, interactive displays, and projection systems enabling digital pedagogy.

name: Acoustic Treatment System
description: A combination of sound-absorbing panels, baffles, and ceiling treatments that control reverberation in learning spaces.

name: Flexible Partition System
description: Operable or moveable wall panels that allow learning spaces to be subdivided or opened up to suit varying group sizes.

name: Mechanical Ventilation & Thermal Comfort System
description: A dedicated HVAC system engineered to maintain optimal CO₂ levels and temperature for learner concentration.

name: Specialist Learning Furniture
description: Modular, height-adjustable desks, writable surfaces, and mobile seating units designed to support agile pedagogy.

name: Interactive Display & Smartboard
description: A touch-enabled large-format digital screen used for collaborative annotation, multimedia delivery, and remote participation.

name: Glazed Internal Screen / Vision Panel
description: A transparent or translucent partition element providing visual connectivity between adjacent learning spaces while maintaining acoustic separation.

name: Writable Wall Surface
description: A whiteboard-finish or speciality-coated wall surface allowing spontaneous ideation and collaborative writing across entire wall planes.

name: Biophilic Finish Material
description: Natural or nature-inspired interior materials (timber, stone, living wall substrates) that improve wellbeing and cognitive performance in learning environments.

name: High-Performance Acoustic Ceiling Tile
description: A mineral-fibre or recycled-content ceiling tile with high noise-reduction coefficient (NRC) ratings specified for classroom environments.

name: Anti-Glare Glazing
