description: A treated or coated glass product used in windows and skylights to minimise screen glare and optimise daylighting in learning spaces.

name: Durable Resilient Flooring
description: Hard-wearing, low-maintenance flooring (LVT, rubber, or polished concrete) suited to the high foot-traffic conditions of learning corridors and studios.

name: Pedagogical Space Planning & Programming
description: The pre-design stakeholder engagement and briefing process that aligns spatial layouts with educational outcomes and teaching methodologies.

name: Acoustic Performance Testing
description: On-site measurement and verification of reverberation times and sound-transmission class values against educational building standards.

name: AV & IT Systems Integration & Commissioning
description: The installation, configuration, and testing of all audio-visual and network infrastructure to ensure seamless pedagogical operation.

name: Partition & Furniture Installation
description: The sequenced fit-out activity of installing moveable walls, specialist learning furniture, and writable surface elements.

name: Wayfinding & Signage Installation
description: The placement and commissioning of directional, informational, and identity signage that supports navigation across a multi-zone learning campus.

name: IFC Class: IfcSpace
description: The IFC entity used to model and classify all discrete room and zone volumes within the learning network for BIM data exchange.

name: IFC Class: IfcWallStandardCase (Operable)
description: The IFC entity used to represent moveable and operable partition walls within flexible learning space configurations.

name: Retail Unit
description: An individual leasable shop or store space within the shopping complex where goods or services are sold directly to consumers.

name: Anchor Store
description: A large, prominent retail tenant (e.g., department store or hypermarket) that draws foot traffic and anchors the overall shopping destination.

name: Food Court
description: A shared dining area with multiple food and beverage vendors arranged around communal seating for shoppers.

name: Central Atrium
description: A multi-storey, naturally lit open void at the heart of the complex that connects retail levels and serves as an orientation landmark.

name: Pop-Up Kiosk Zone
description: Flexible open floor areas within the concourse designed to host temporary retail kiosks, carts, and promotional stands.

name: Entertainment Zone
description: A dedicated area housing leisure attractions such as cinemas, arcades, or indoor play facilities to extend visitor dwell time.

name: Loading Bay & Service Yard
description: Back-of-house logistics area providing segregated access for delivery vehicles, waste collection, and tenant stock management.

name: Car Park Structure
description: A multi-level parking facility integrated with or adjacent to the shopping complex for customer and staff vehicles.

name: Rooftop Terrace / Sky Garden
description: An elevated outdoor amenity deck offering landscaped rest areas, dining, or event space above the retail floors.

name: Customer Toilet & Welfare Block
description: Public sanitary facilities distributed across the retail floors to serve shoppers and staff with accessible and family provisions.

name: Retail Mall Structural Frame
description: The primary load-bearing skeleton (steel or reinforced concrete) that spans large column-free retail floor plates and atrium voids.

name: Glazed Skylight / Atrium Roof
description: A large-span structural glazing system covering the atrium or concourse to provide natural daylight while maintaining weather protection.

name: Shopfront Glazing System
description: Standardised frameless or framed glass shopfront assemblies forming the demise boundary between retail units and the mall concourse.

name: Escalator & Travelator Array
description: Mechanised inclined conveyors connecting multiple retail levels and enabling high-volume vertical and horizontal shopper movement.

name: Passenger Lift Core
description: Vertical transportation shafts housing accessible lifts for mobility-impaired shoppers and goods movement between floors.

name: Retail Signage & Wayfinding System
description: An integrated hierarchy of directory totems, overhead blade signs, and digital displays guiding shoppers through the complex.

name: Security Shutter & Door System
description: Roller shutters or solid doors installed at each unit entrance for after-hours security and fire compartmentalisation.

name: Tenant Fit-Out Partition System
description: Demountable or semi-permanent internal partition systems used by tenants to configure their individual retail spaces.

name: Raised Access Floor (Tenancy Shell)
description: A modular raised flooring system within retail units enabling flexible routing of electrical and data services beneath the floor.

name: Suspended Ceiling & Bulkhead System
description: Ceiling grids, tiles, and feature bulkheads used in common areas and tenancies to conceal services and define retail ambience.

name: HVAC & Climate Control System
description: A centralised or distributed heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning installation maintaining thermal comfort across all retail and common areas.

name: Emergency Lighting & Exit Signage System
description: Battery-backed luminaires and illuminated exit signs ensuring safe egress for all occupants during a power failure.

name: Retail Lighting Design System
description: A layered lighting strategy combining ambient, accent, and feature luminaires to enhance merchandise visibility and shopping ambience.

name: Plumbing & Drainage Network
description: The cold water, hot water, and foul/surface drainage infrastructure serving toilets, food outlets, cleaning stations, and plant rooms.

name: Tenant Metering & Sub-Metering System
description: Individual utility meters for electricity, gas, and water installed at each tenancy boundary to enable accurate billing and consumption monitoring.

name: CCTV & Security Management System
description: A networked camera and monitoring platform covering retail floors, car parks, and service areas for loss prevention and public safety.

name: Public Address & Background Music System
description: An audio distribution system providing zoned background music, emergency evacuation announcements, and promotional messaging throughout the complex.

name: Retail Concrete Floor Topping
description: A hard-wearing polished or sealed concrete screed used in high-traffic concourse and common areas for durability and cleanability.

name: Porcelain / Stone Floor Tile
description: Large-format premium tiles applied to mall concourse and atrium floors to convey quality and facilitate easy maintenance.

name: Insulated Cladding Panel
description: Composite metal or GRC façade panels providing weatherproofing, thermal insulation, and architectural finish to the building envelope.

name: High-Performance Glazing Unit
description: Double or triple-glazed units with solar-control and low-emissivity coatings used in shopfronts, skylights, and external walls.

name: Retail Fit-Out Joinery Substrate (MDF/MFC)
description: Medium-density fibreboard and melamine-faced chipboard used as the primary substrate for tenant display fixtures and shopfitting joinery.

name: Demolition & Site Clearance
description: The controlled removal of existing structures and site preparation works prior to commencing the new shopping complex construction.

name: Piling & Ground Improvement Works
description: Installation of deep foundations or ground treatment to transfer structural loads safely to competent bearing strata beneath the site.

name: Structural Frame Erection
description: The fabrication, delivery, and crane-assisted assembly of the primary steel or concrete superstructure forming the retail floors and atrium.

name: Façade & Cladding Installation
description: Fixing of external cladding systems, curtain walling, and shopfront glazing to complete the weathertight building envelope.

name: MEP Rough-In & First Fix
description: The first-stage installation of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing conduits, pipework, and ductwork within the building fabric before linings.

name: Tenant Shell & Core Handover
description: The formal process of delivering unfinished but services-ready retail units to tenants at a defined specification for their own fit-out works.

name: Tenant Fit-Out Works
description: Retailer-led interior construction of shopfitting, branding, fixtures, and finishes within individual units prior to trading.

name: Landscaping & External Works
description: Hard and soft landscaping, entrance plaza paving, planting, and external lighting works forming the public realm around the shopping complex.

name: Retail Property Management
description: Ongoing operational activities including lease administration, planned maintenance, cleaning, and tenant coordination after the centre opens.

name: Wayfinding & Digital Experience Strategy
description: An integrated digital-physical navigation strategy using interactive kiosks, mobile apps, and mapping to help visitors locate stores and amenities.

name: Click-and-Collect Hub
description: A dedicated counter or locker zone within the complex where shoppers collect online orders placed with retail tenants or third-party retailers.

name: IFC IfcSpace (Retail Unit)
description: The IFC schema class used to model and exchange individual retail tenancy space boundaries within a BIM-compliant building model.

name: IFC IfcZone (Fire Compartment)
description: The IFC class grouping IfcSpaces into fire-compartmentation zones for life-safety analysis and regulatory compliance documentation.

name: Bus Bay / Boarding Lane
description: A designated lane or bay within the mini-bus terminal where vehicles stop to pick up and drop off passengers.

name: Passenger Waiting Area
description: A sheltered or open area where commuters queue and wait for their mini-bus service.

name: Ticket Booth / Fare Collection Point
description: A kiosk or counter structure where passengers purchase tickets or pay fares before boarding.

name: Canopy / Roof Shelter
description: An overhead roofing structure that protects passengers and vehicles from weather elements.

name: Driver Rest Room / Crew Facility
description: A dedicated space for mini-bus drivers and crew to rest, change, and store personal items between shifts.

name: Dispatcher / Operations Office
description: An administrative room used to coordinate schedules, communicate with drivers, and manage fleet operations.

name: Public Toilet / Sanitary Facility
description: Restroom facilities provided for passengers and staff within the mini-bus terminal.

name: Vehicle Turning / Manoeuvring Area
description: A paved zone designed to allow mini-buses to safely turn, reverse, and reposition within the terminal.

name: Parking / Staging Area
description: A holding area where mini-buses park while waiting for their departure time or during off-peak hours.

name: Fuel / Charging Station
description: Infrastructure for refuelling conventional mini-buses or recharging electric mini-bus fleets on-site.

name: Drainage & Stormwater System
description: Underground or surface drainage network that manages rainwater runoff from paved terminal areas.

name: Electrical & Lighting System
description: Power distribution and luminaire system providing adequate illumination for safety and operations around the clock.

name: PA / Passenger Information System
description: Public-address and digital display system that communicates real-time route and schedule information to passengers.

name: Signage & Wayfinding
description: Static and dynamic signs that direct passengers to the correct bays, routes, exits, and facilities.

name: Seating / Benches
description: Fixed or modular seating furniture installed in the waiting area for passenger comfort.

name: Paving / Hard-Standing Surface
description: Durable concrete, asphalt, or interlocking paver surface laid throughout the vehicle and pedestrian zones.

name: Structural Steel / Support Columns
description: Steel or reinforced-concrete columns that support canopy and roof shelter structures over bays and waiting areas.

name: Kerb & Channel
description: Raised kerb edging and channel drainage that delineate vehicle lanes from pedestrian walkways.

name: Accessible Ramp / Disability Access Feature
description: Ramps, tactile paving, and lowered kerbs ensuring the terminal is accessible to passengers with mobility impairments.

name: Landscaping / Green Buffer Zone
description: Planted areas, trees, and shrubs that provide shade, reduce heat-island effect, and improve the terminal environment.

name: Pavement Construction
description: Laying of sub-base, base course, and wearing-course materials to form the durable vehicle and pedestrian surfaces.

name: Structural Steelwork Erection
description: Fabrication and on-site erection of steel columns, beams, and trusses forming the canopy and building framework.

name: Roofing & Waterproofing Installation
description: Fixing of roofing sheets, membranes, and flashings to make shelter structures weather-tight.

name: Electrical & Mechanical Fit-Out
description: Installation of wiring, switchboards, lighting fixtures, PA systems, and CCTV equipment throughout the terminal.

name: Drainage & Civil Works
description: Excavation and laying of stormwater pipes, kerbs, channels, and gully pits across the terminal footprint.

name: Line-Marking & Signage Installation
description: Painting of road markings, bay numbers, and pedestrian lines, plus mounting of all directional and regulatory signs.

name: Commissioning & Handover
description: Testing of all installed systems and formal handover of the completed mini-bus terminal to the operator or authority.

name: Ground Floor
description: The first occupiable level of a building, sitting at or near grade, forming the base of a four-story structure.

name: Second Floor
description: The second occupiable level, elevated one story above the ground floor in a four-story building.

name: Third Floor
description: The third occupiable level, positioned mid-height within a four-story building envelope.

name: Fourth Floor (Top Floor)
description: The uppermost occupied level in a four-story building, immediately below the roof structure.

name: Roof Level
description: The topmost structural plane above the fourth floor, enclosing the building and potentially providing a terrace or mechanical zone.

name: Basement / Sub-Grade Level
description: An optional below-grade floor that may exist beneath the ground floor, not counted toward the four-story limit in many codes.

name: Inter-Story Height (Floor-to-Floor)
description: The measured vertical distance between finished floor levels, a critical dimensional parameter governing the total building height within the four-story envelope.

name: Building Height Datum
description: The reference elevation point (e.g., average grade or lowest adjacent grade) from which story count and overall height are legally measured.

name: Structural Floor Slab
description: The horizontal reinforced-concrete or composite deck separating each story, providing the structural platform for every occupied level.

name: Load-Bearing Wall System
description: Vertical structural walls that transfer gravity and lateral loads from each story down to the foundation, common in low-rise four-story construction.

name: Moment Frame / Structural Frame
description: A rigid or semi-rigid skeletal system of columns and beams designed to resist both vertical loads and lateral forces across all four stories.

name: Shear Wall System
description: Reinforced concrete or masonry walls specifically designed to resist lateral wind and seismic forces distributed across the full height of the four-story building.

name: Staircase Core
description: The enclosed vertical circulation element containing stairs that connect all four floors, serving as both a means of egress and a lateral-stability core.

name: Elevator Shaft
description: A vertical enclosure housing elevator equipment to provide accessible vertical transport across all floors of the four-story building.

name: Exterior Cladding / Facade System
description: The weather-resistant outer envelope applied to all four story faces, integrating insulation, waterproofing, and aesthetic finish.

name: Mezzanine Level
description: An intermediate partial floor inserted within one story's height that may affect code story-count calculations for the four-story limit.

name: Penthouse / Mechanical Penthouse
description: A rooftop enclosure housing HVAC and other mechanical equipment that may or may not be counted as an additional story under zoning regulations.

name: Fire Egress Stairway
description: A dedicated, fire-rated vertical escape route required by code to serve each of the four occupied floors during an emergency.

name: Zoning Height Restriction Compliance
description: The regulatory review and documentation process confirming that the proposed four-story building does not exceed the maximum height, story count, or FAR allowed by the local zoning ordinance.

name: Story Count Verification Survey
description: A professional measurement and inspection activity performed during design and construction to confirm that floor count and inter-story heights conform to the approved four-story limit.

name: Structural Erection (Floor-by-Floor)
description: The sequential construction activity of erecting each of the four structural levels, including formwork, reinforcement placement, and concrete pouring or steel erection.

name: Floor-to-Floor Facade Installation
description: The construction activity of installing cladding, windows, and waterproofing panel by panel across each story of the four-story facade.

name: Building Code Story-Count Classification
description: The formal administrative activity of categorizing the building's number of stories under applicable building codes to determine fire-rating, egress, and construction-type requirements.

name: Lightweight Wood-Frame Construction (Type V)
description: A combustible structural framing system of dimensional lumber commonly used up to four stories where permitted by building codes.

name: Cold-Formed Steel Framing
description: Light-gauge steel stud framing used as an alternative to wood in four-story residential and mixed-use construction for improved fire and acoustic performance.

name: Masonry (CMU / Brick)
description: Concrete masonry units or clay brick used for load-bearing or infill walls, offering fire resistance across the full height of a four-story structure.

name: Surface Parking Lot
description: An at-grade open-air paved area designated for vehicle parking, typically the most space-inefficient parking typology.

name: Structured Parking Garage
description: A multi-storey building or podium structure dedicated to vehicle parking, enabling higher density use of land.

name: Underground Parking
description: Below-grade parking facility constructed beneath a building or open space to preserve surface area for other uses.

name: Parking Bay / Stall
description: An individual demarcated space sized to accommodate a single parked vehicle.

name: Accessible (ADA/Disabled) Parking Stall
description: A wider, specially marked parking stall with adjacent access aisle reserved for users with disabilities.

name: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Stall
description: A parking stall equipped with EV charging infrastructure for plug-in electric vehicles.

name: Motorcycle / Bicycle Parking Area
description: Dedicated zones within a parking facility sized and equipped for two-wheeled vehicles.

name: Drive Aisle
description: The internal circulation lane within a parking facility that provides vehicular access to individual stalls.

name: Parking Ramp / Ramp Structure
description: An inclined concrete or structural-steel surface connecting different parking levels within a multi-storey facility.

name: Parking Barrier / Bollard System
description: Physical barriers, bollards, or wheel stops installed to delineate stalls and protect structural elements from vehicle impact.

name: Parking Guidance & Counting System
description: Electronic sensor and display system that monitors occupancy and guides drivers to available stalls in real time.

name: Access Control System (Parking Gates & Ticketing)
description: Barrier-gate, ticket-dispensing, or ANPR-based system controlling entry and exit of vehicles and managing revenue.

name: EV Charging Infrastructure System
description: Electrical distribution, conduit, and charging-point hardware system supplying power to EV stalls throughout the facility.

name: Parking Ventilation System
description: Mechanical exhaust and supply-air system designed to dilute vehicle exhaust fumes, especially in enclosed or underground parking.

name: Parking Drainage & Waterproofing System
description: Drainage channels, sumps, and waterproof membranes that manage surface run-off and protect the parking structure from water ingress.

name: Parking Lighting System
description: Luminaire and controls network providing adequate illumination levels for safety and security within the parking facility.

name: CCTV & Security System (Parking)
description: Surveillance camera network and monitoring infrastructure dedicated to parking facility security.

name: Fire Detection & Suppression System (Parking)
description: Sprinkler heads, heat detectors, and alarm systems specifically rated and configured for parking facility fire safety.

name: Precast Concrete Parking Structure
description: Factory-manufactured precast concrete planks, double-tees, and columns commonly used as the primary structural material in parking garages.

name: Asphalt / Bituminous Paving
description: Bituminous surfacing material used for surface parking lots and drive aisles, providing a durable and cost-effective finish.

name: Parking Structure Waterproof Membrane
description: Traffic-rated elastomeric or epoxy membrane applied to deck surfaces to prevent chloride and moisture penetration into the concrete structure.

name: Line Marking & Signage Paint
description: High-visibility thermoplastic or epoxy paint used to demarcate stall boundaries, arrows, and regulatory text on parking surfaces.

name: Parking Layout Design & Zoning Study
description: Planning activity to determine optimum stall dimensions, aisle widths, turning radii, and compliance with local parking ratios.

name: Parking Demand & Ratio Analysis
description: Quantitative study establishing the required number of parking spaces relative to gross floor area or occupancy—directly pertinent to the nine-percent standard.

name: Structural Engineering of Parking Deck
description: Engineering activity covering load calculations, slab thickness, and reinforcement design for parking-level floor plates.

name: Waterproofing & Sealant Application
description: Construction activity of applying traffic-rated membranes and sealants to parking decks to achieve long-term durability.

name: Line Marking & Bay Demarcation
description: On-site painting or thermoplastic application of stall lines, directional arrows, and regulatory markings on finished parking surfaces.

name: Pavement Construction & Resurfacing
description: Laying, compacting, and finishing asphalt or concrete pavement for parking surfaces, including periodic resurfacing maintenance.

name: EV Charging Infrastructure Installation
description: Electrical rough-in, conduit installation, and fitting of charging-point hardware within designated EV stalls.

name: Parking Guidance System Commissioning
description: Testing, calibration, and handover of sensor networks and display boards that form the parking guidance system.

name: Parking Ratio / Provision Standard
description: Regulatory or planning policy framework that specifies the minimum or maximum number of parking spaces per unit of building floor area—the direct parent concept of the nine-percent rule.

name: Shared / Public Parking Facility
description: A parking area shared among multiple land uses or tenants, often used as a strategy to reduce per-building parking provision.

name: Mechanical / Automated Parking System
description: Robotic or pallet-based automated parking system that maximises vehicle storage density within a minimal footprint.

name: Green / Landscaped Parking Area
description: A parking area incorporating trees, planting strips, or green infrastructure to mitigate heat-island effects and improve aesthetics.

name: Median Strip
description: A raised or flush divider running between parallel road carriageways to separate opposing or same-direction traffic flows.

name: Carriageway
description: Each individual roadway surface allocated to a direction of travel within a parallel road system.

name: Road Pavement Layer
description: The structural layering of asphalt, concrete, or composite materials forming the drivable surface of each carriageway.

name: Kerb and Gutter
description: Concrete or masonry edge restraints that define carriageway boundaries and channel stormwater runoff.

name: Road Marking System
description: Painted or thermoplastic lane lines, arrows, and symbols applied to carriageway surfaces to guide traffic movement.

name: Traffic Signage
description: Regulatory, warning, and informational signs installed along parallel roads to direct and inform road users.

name: Footpath / Sidewalk
description: Paved pedestrian walkways running parallel to and alongside each carriageway for safe non-motorised movement.

name: Bicycle Lane
description: A dedicated lane or separated path within or adjacent to the parallel road reserve for cyclist travel.

name: Service / Utility Corridor
description: Underground or above-ground zone within the road reserve accommodating water, sewer, gas, telecoms, and electrical utilities.

name: Intersection / At-Grade Junction
description: The point where parallel roads cross or merge with other roads, requiring specific geometry and traffic control design.

name: Road Sub-base and Base Course
description: Compacted granular or stabilised layers beneath the pavement surface providing load distribution and structural support.

name: Road Embankment / Earthworks
description: Bulk excavation, filling, and compaction works to establish the required road formation level and cross-section.

name: Line Marking and Signage Installation
description: Application of traffic line markings and erection of signage as part of road commissioning works.

name: Utility Trenching and Reinstatement
description: Excavation of trenches for underground services within the road reserve and subsequent pavement reinstatement.

name: Traffic Management Plan
description: Planning and implementation of temporary traffic control measures to safely maintain road access during construction.

name: Shared Zone / Shared Path
description: A designated area adjacent to parallel roads where pedestrians and cyclists share the same paved surface.

name: Bus Lane / Transit Corridor
description: A reserved lane within the parallel road system exclusively or preferentially allocated to public transport vehicles.

name: Road Reserve / Right-of-Way
description: The total land corridor set aside for road infrastructure, including carriageways, verges, footpaths, and services.

name: Noise Barrier / Sound Wall
description: Acoustic fencing or wall structures erected alongside parallel roads to reduce traffic noise impacts on adjacent land uses.

name: Guardrail and Safety Barrier
description: Longitudinal safety devices installed at roadsides or medians to redirect errant vehicles and reduce crash severity.

name: Verge / Road Shoulder
description: The unpaved or paved strip between the carriageway edge and the road reserve boundary used for emergency stopping and landscaping.

name: Landscaping and Street Trees
description: Planted vegetation, turf, and trees within the road reserve that provide amenity, shade, and environmental benefits.

name: Altar
description: A raised platform or table serving as the focal point for rituals, offerings, and worship within a sacred site.

name: Sanctuary
description: The innermost or most holy zone of a sacred site, often restricted to clergy or officiants.

name: Nave
description: The central hall or main body of a religious building where congregants gather during services.

name: Chapel
description: A smaller, subordinate place of worship within or adjacent to a larger sacred site.

name: Crypt
description: An underground chamber beneath a sacred site, typically used for burial or housing relics.

name: Bell Tower / Campanile
description: A vertical tower structure housing bells used to call worshippers to religious services.

name: Minaret
description: A slender tower attached to a mosque from which the call to prayer is traditionally announced.

name: Dome
description: A hemispherical roof structure symbolic in many religious traditions and defining the silhouette of sacred buildings.

name: Stained Glass Window
description: Decorative colored glass panels depicting religious narratives or symbols, admitting filtered light into the interior.

name: Pew / Seating System
description: Fixed or movable seating elements arranged within the worship space for congregants.

name: Pulpit
description: An elevated platform or stand from which religious leaders deliver sermons or sacred readings.

name: Font / Baptismal Pool
description: A basin or pool used for baptismal rites and the administration of holy water.

name: Confessional Booth
description: A small enclosed structure within a church providing privacy for the sacrament of confession.

name: Columbarium
description: A wall or structure with niches for storing funerary urns, commonly found within or adjacent to sacred sites.

name: Sacristy / Vestry
description: A utility room where vestments, sacred vessels, and liturgical items are stored and clergy prepare for services.

name: Narthex / Vestibule
description: An entrance hall or lobby at the front of a religious building acting as a transitional zone between secular and sacred space.

name: Choir / Chancel
description: The area of a church reserved for the choir and clergy, typically located between the nave and the altar.

name: Ambulatory
description: A processional walkway around the apse or altar of a religious building, allowing movement during services.

name: Transept
description: The transverse arms of a cross-shaped church plan, perpendicular to the nave, creating the cruciform layout.

name: Apse
description: A semicircular or polygonal recess at the end of a nave, typically housing the altar in Christian churches.

name: Pilgrimage Route / Processional Path
description: A designated path within or approaching a sacred site intended for ceremonial processions or pilgrimage movement.

name: Sacred Garden / Contemplation Garden
description: An outdoor landscaped area within the sacred precinct designed for meditation, reflection, and spiritual retreat.

name: Cemetery / Burial Ground
description: Land consecrated for the interment of the deceased, traditionally situated adjacent to a place of worship.

name: Mosaic / Fresco System
description: Decorative wall and ceiling finishes comprising colored tesserae or painted plaster depicting religious imagery.

name: Natural Stone Masonry
description: Load-bearing or cladding masonry constructed from cut stone such as limestone, marble, or granite, historically dominant in sacred architecture.

name: Sacred Timber Joinery
description: Structural and ornamental woodwork crafted for roof structures, screens, and furniture within religious buildings.

name: Acoustic System
description: The design of surfaces, materials, and geometries to achieve appropriate reverberation and sound distribution for liturgical music and speech.

name: Lighting System (Liturgical)
description: A combination of natural and artificial lighting designed to create atmosphere, highlight sacred objects, and support ceremonial functions.

name: HVAC / Environmental Control System
description: Mechanical systems managing temperature, humidity, and air quality to preserve the building fabric and ensure congregant comfort.

name: Fire Protection System
description: Sprinkler, detection, and suppression systems adapted to protect historic fabric and irreplaceable artifacts within sacred sites.

name: Security & Access Control System
description: Electronic and physical systems managing entry, surveillance, and protection of sacred artifacts and the site perimeter.

name: Organ & Pipe System
description: A large wind-driven musical instrument integrated into the architecture of a place of worship for liturgical music.

name: Construction of Sacred Site
description: The initial design, planning, and erection of the primary sacred building and its ancillary structures.

name: Heritage Conservation & Restoration
description: Specialist works to repair, stabilize, and restore historic fabric, finishes, and structure of a sacred site to its original or significant state.

name: Liturgical Fit-Out
description: The installation of altars, furnishings, artwork, and liturgical equipment tailored to the specific faith tradition of the site.

name: Archaeological Investigation
description: Systematic excavation and survey conducted on or around a sacred site to uncover historical layers and inform conservation decisions.

name: Stained Glass Installation & Restoration
description: The fabrication, installation, or conservation of decorative stained glass windows within a sacred building.

name: Acoustic Commissioning
description: The testing, measurement, and tuning of a sacred space's acoustic environment to meet liturgical and musical performance requirements.

name: Grounds & Landscape Maintenance
description: Ongoing horticultural and civil maintenance of cemeteries, gardens, pathways, and outdoor sacred precincts.

name: Relic & Artifact Conservation
description: Specialist conservation treatment and environmental management for irreplaceable religious objects, relics, and artworks housed at the site.

name: IFC Site (IfcSite)
description: The IFC class representing the land and geographic context within which a sacred site is situated.

name: IFC Building (IfcBuilding)
description: The IFC class used to model the overall sacred building as a discrete structure within a project.

name: Water Supply Pipe Network
description: The network of pipes that distributes potable and non-potable water throughout a building to various access points.

name: Tap / Faucet
description: A valve-controlled fixture that provides the physical point of water access for users.

name: Stopcock / Isolation Valve
description: A shut-off valve that allows water flow to be isolated at a specific branch or point of access.

name: Drinking Water Fountain
description: A fixed fixture providing a dedicated, hygienic point of access to potable drinking water.

name: Hose Bib / Outdoor Tap
description: An externally mounted tap fitting that provides water access for outdoor or utility use.

name: Utility / Janitorial Sink
description: A deep sink fixture installed in service or cleaning areas to provide water access for maintenance activities.

name: Emergency Eyewash Station
description: A safety fixture that delivers a controlled flow of water for emergency eye or body rinsing.

name: Water Pressure Regulator
description: A device that reduces and stabilises incoming mains water pressure to a safe working level at access points.

name: Backflow Prevention Device
description: A mechanical assembly that prevents contaminated water from flowing back into the potable supply.

name: Water Storage Tank / Header Tank
description: A vessel that stores a reserve supply of water to maintain consistent access when mains pressure is insufficient.

name: Booster Pump Set
description: A pumping system that increases water pressure to ensure adequate supply at elevated or remote access points.

name: Water Treatment / Filtration Unit
description: Equipment that filters or treats water at the point of entry or use to meet quality standards for access.

name: Greywater Reuse System
description: A system that collects, treats, and redistributes waste water from sinks and showers for secondary non-potable access.

name: Wet Room / Wash Area
description: A dedicated room or zone specifically designed and fitted out to facilitate water access for washing or cleaning.

name: Plant Room (Hydraulic)
description: A designated room housing water supply plant and distribution equipment serving the building's access points.

name: Water Main Connection / Service Entry
description: The point at which the public water main connects to the building's internal supply network.

name: Water Connection / Tie-In
description: The construction activity of physically connecting the building's internal network to the external water authority main.

name: Water Quality Testing & Commissioning
description: Post-installation testing to confirm that water quality and flow rates at access points meet regulatory standards.

name: CPVC / uPVC Pipe
description: Rigid chlorinated or unplasticised PVC pipe used for cold water supply and service distribution.

name: Stainless Steel Pipe
description: A hygienic, corrosion-resistant pipe material used in applications requiring high water purity, such as food service or hospitals.

name: IFC: IfcDistributionPort
description: The IFC schema class representing a connection point on a distribution system element where water flow enters or exits.

name: IFC: IfcPipeSegment
description: The IFC class used to model straight or curved pipe segments within a building's water supply network.

name: IFC: IfcValve
description: The IFC class representing valves (including stopcocks and isolation valves) within a piped distribution system.

name: IFC: IfcSanitaryTerminal
description: The IFC class that models sanitary fixtures such as drinking fountains, sinks, and wash stations providing water access.

name: IFC: IfcFlowController
description: The IFC class covering devices such as pressure regulators and backflow preventers that control water flow in a distribution system.

name: Construction Phase
description: The initial building phase encompassing all construction activities from groundbreaking to project handover.

name: Commissioning
description: Systematic process of verifying and documenting that building systems perform as intended before occupancy.

name: Occupancy Phase
description: The active use period of a building where occupants reside or work within the facility.

name: Planned Preventive Maintenance
description: Scheduled inspection and servicing of building components to prevent premature failure and extend service life.

name: Corrective Maintenance
description: Reactive repair activities performed after a component or system has failed or degraded below acceptable performance.

name: Refurbishment
description: Partial or full upgrade of building interiors, finishes, or systems without major structural alteration.

name: Renovation
description: Significant remodelling or reconfiguration of building spaces, structures, or systems to meet new requirements.

name: Adaptive Reuse
description: Repurposing an existing building for a fundamentally different use than originally designed.

name: Energy Retrofit
description: Upgrade of building envelope or MEP systems specifically aimed at improving energy performance and reducing carbon footprint.

name: Decommissioning
description: Formal process of safely shutting down and disconnecting building systems prior to demolition or repurposing.

name: Deconstruction
description: Selective and careful disassembly of building components to maximise material recovery and reuse.

name: Demolition
description: Controlled destruction and removal of a building structure at the end of its serviceable life.

name: Material Recovery & Recycling
description: Collection, sorting, and processing of salvaged building materials for reintegration into new construction or manufacturing cycles.

name: Waste Management Plan
description: Documented strategy for minimising, diverting, and disposing of construction and demolition waste responsibly.

name: Building Condition Assessment
description: Periodic technical survey of a building's physical state used to inform maintenance, repair, or replacement decisions.

name: Asset Register
description: Structured database recording all building components, their specifications, installation dates, and maintenance history.

name: Building Information Model (BIM)
description: Digital representation of the physical and functional characteristics of a building used across all life-cycle stages.

name: Embodied Carbon
description: Greenhouse gas emissions associated with the extraction, manufacture, transport, and disposal of building materials over the full life cycle.

name: Operational Carbon
description: Carbon emissions produced by the energy consumed during a building's operational phase for heating, cooling, lighting, and appliances.

name: Whole-Life Cost Analysis
description: Financial appraisal that accounts for all costs—capital, operational, maintenance, and disposal—over the entire building life span.

name: Service Life Planning
description: Engineering process of designing and specifying components to achieve target durability and replacement intervals.

name: Component Replacement Cycle
description: Defined schedule dictating when specific building components—such as roofing, glazing, or M&E plant—must be replaced.

name: Post-Occupancy Evaluation
description: Structured assessment of a building's performance against design intentions after a period of occupation.

name: Sustainability Certification
description: Third-party rating scheme (e.g., BREEAM, LEED, Green Star) measuring and benchmarking environmental performance across life-cycle stages.

name: End-of-Life Strategy
description: Pre-planned approach defining how a building and its components will be deconstructed, recycled, or repurposed at closure.

name: Men's Restroom
description: A dedicated sanitary space for male occupants containing urinals, toilets, and wash basins.

name: Women's Restroom
description: A dedicated sanitary space for female occupants containing toilets, vanity areas, and wash basins.

name: Accessible (ADA) Toilet Stall
description: An enlarged toilet compartment designed to accommodate wheelchair users and persons with disabilities.

name: Toilet Stall / Cubicle
description: A partitioned enclosure within a restroom providing privacy for a single toilet fixture.

name: Water Closet (Toilet)
description: A sanitary fixture for waste disposal connected to the building's drainage system.

name: Wash Basin / Hand Wash Sink
description: A plumbing fixture for hand washing, typically mounted on a countertop or wall in restrooms.

name: Vanity Counter
description: A horizontal surface housing wash basins and providing storage or grooming space, commonly found in women's restrooms.

name: Restroom Partition System
description: A system of floor-to-ceiling or suspended panels that divide a restroom into individual stalls or zones.

name: Plumbing Supply System
description: The network of pipes, valves, and fittings that delivers hot and cold water to restroom fixtures.

name: Exhaust Ventilation System
description: A mechanical ventilation system that removes odours and humid air from restroom spaces.

name: Restroom Accessory Package
description: A collection of fittings including soap dispensers, paper towel dispensers, toilet roll holders, mirrors, and waste bins.

name: Baby Changing Station
description: A fold-down or counter-mounted surface provided for infant nappy changing, installed in one or both restrooms.

name: Restroom Floor Finish
description: Water-resistant and slip-rated floor covering material, typically ceramic or porcelain tile, applied in restroom spaces.

name: Restroom Wall Finish
description: Moisture-resistant wall cladding or tile applied to restroom walls for hygiene and durability.

name: Grout and Tile Adhesive
description: Jointing and bonding compounds used to install and seal floor and wall tiles in wet restroom areas.

name: Restroom Door with Privacy Hardware
description: An entry or stall door equipped with locks, indicators, and self-closing hinges suited for restroom use.

name: Signage and Wayfinding
description: Gender-identifying and accessibility signage affixed to restroom entrances to direct occupants.

name: Sanitary Fixture Installation
description: The trade activity of setting and connecting toilets, urinals, and basins to supply and drain pipework.

name: Tiling and Waterproofing Works
description: Construction activity involving the application of waterproof membranes, adhesives, and tiles to restroom floors and walls.

name: Rough-in Plumbing
description: Early-stage construction activity of running supply and drain pipes to restroom fixture locations before finishes are applied.

name: Mechanical Ventilation Installation
description: The activity of installing ductwork, exhaust fans, and controls for restroom ventilation systems.

name: Accessibility Compliance Inspection
description: A review and verification activity ensuring restroom layouts, clearances, and fittings meet ADA or local accessibility codes.

name: Unisex / Gender-Neutral Restroom
description: A single-occupancy or multi-occupancy restroom designed to be used by any gender, often provided alongside gendered facilities.

name: Ante-room / Restroom Lobby
description: A transitional buffer space between the main corridor and the restroom providing visual privacy and noise separation.

name: Janitor's Utility Closet
description: A small service room adjacent to restrooms housing cleaning equipment and a mop sink for maintenance purposes.

name: Offset Core Shaft
description: A deliberately off-center structural and service shaft that shifts the nucleus away from the building's geometric center.

name: Cantilevered Floor Plates
description: Horizontally projecting floor slabs extending outward from the eccentric core to create usable floor area beyond the core's footprint.

name: Lateral Bracing System
description: A structural system (e.g., outriggers or diagonal bracing) that counteracts the asymmetric loads generated by the eccentric core position.

name: Outrigger Frame
description: Rigid horizontal structural arms connecting the offset core to perimeter columns to redistribute eccentric loads.

name: Vertical Circulation Hub
description: Consolidated zone within the nucleus housing elevators, stairs, and escalators offset from the building center.

name: MEP Riser Cluster
description: Grouped vertical mechanical, electrical, and plumbing risers integrated within the eccentric core shaft.

name: Fire Escape Stairwell
description: Enclosed emergency egress stair positioned within or adjacent to the eccentric nucleus meeting life-safety codes.

name: Structural Concrete Core Wall
description: High-strength reinforced concrete used to construct the shear walls of the eccentric nucleus for lateral and gravity load resistance.

name: High-Strength Reinforcement Steel
description: Steel rebar or post-tensioning elements embedded in the core walls to handle tensile forces from eccentric loading.

name: Damping System
description: Tuned mass or viscous dampers integrated near the eccentric core to mitigate dynamic sway caused by asymmetric mass distribution.

name: Foundation Pile Group
description: A cluster of deep foundation piles positioned to counteract the eccentric overturning moments transmitted from the offset core.

name: Curtain Wall Interface Zone
description: The perimeter space between the eccentric nucleus and the building envelope where structural and glazing systems interact.

name: Core Formwork Construction
description: The activity of erecting and striking specialized slip-form or jump-form formwork to cast the eccentric concrete core walls.

name: Structural Load Testing
description: Testing activity to verify that the eccentric core and connected structure perform within acceptable deflection and stress limits.

name: Outrigger Installation
description: The construction activity of fabricating and connecting outrigger trusses or beams between the eccentric core and perimeter columns.

name: MEP Rough-In
description: Early-stage installation activity for running mechanical, electrical, and plumbing conduits and pipes through the core's riser shafts.

name: Seismic Retrofit of Core
description: Remedial construction activity to upgrade the eccentric core's seismic resistance, often required when the offset increases torsional vulnerability.

name: Torsional Analysis Model
description: A computational structural model specifically developed to evaluate torsional effects arising from the eccentricity between the center of mass and center of rigidity.

name: Perimeter Column Grid
description: The array of outer columns whose spacing and sizing are directly influenced by the eccentric position of the central core.

name: Lobby Space
description: Entrance reception area positioned relative to the eccentric nucleus, often requiring careful planning due to the asymmetric core layout.

name: Core High-Density Zone
description: The innermost ring of maximum building density, typically housing the highest floor-area-ratio structures and most intensive land uses.

name: Transition Density Buffer Zone
description: An intermediate ring that mediates between high-density cores and lower-density peripheries, blending land-use intensities gradually.

name: Low-Density Peripheral Zone
description: The outermost ring characterised by reduced building coverage, open space, and lower plot ratios at the edge of the density gradient.

name: Density Gradient Boundary
description: A defined physical or regulatory demarcation line separating one density ring from the next.

name: Ring Road Infrastructure
description: Concentric or radial road network designed to serve and reinforce the boundaries and circulation between density rings.

name: Mixed-Use Podium Block
description: A low-rise podium structure at the base of high-density zones accommodating retail, civic, or commercial uses that activate the ring edge.

name: High-Rise Residential Tower
description: A tall residential building type typical of the inner density rings, maximising floor area on a compact footprint.

name: Mid-Rise Mixed-Use Block
description: A medium-height building typology deployed in transitional density rings to bridge between towers and low-rise fabric.

name: Low-Rise Courtyard Housing
description: A ground-hugging housing typology with enclosed courtyards suited to outer, low-density rings.

name: Open Space Network
description: An interconnected system of parks, plazas, and green corridors distributed across and between density rings to balance built-up ratios.

name: Public Transit Spine
description: A transit corridor (rail, BRT, or tram) that radially or circumferentially connects density rings to facilitate density-supported ridership.

name: Utility Infrastructure Ring
description: Looped or concentric utility networks (water, sewer, power, data) scaled and routed to match the service demands of each density tier.

name: Floor Area Ratio (FAR) Zoning Layer
description: A regulatory system layer that assigns and enforces permissible floor-area ratios for each density ring within the planning framework.

name: Density Ring Masterplan Layout
description: The design and planning activity of defining ring boundaries, target densities, and land-use allocations across the concentric zones.

name: Urban Density Modelling
description: Computational simulation activity used to test and optimise population, built form, and infrastructure capacity across ring configurations.

name: Infrastructure Capacity Assessment
description: An engineering activity evaluating whether existing or planned infrastructure systems can support the density loads assigned to each ring.

name: Phased Densification Construction
description: A staged construction activity that sequentially builds out each density ring in accordance with population growth and demand triggers.

name: Demolition and Land Clearance
description: Site preparation activity involving removal of existing structures to enable redevelopment at higher densities within inner rings.

name: Landscaping and Green Infrastructure Installation
description: Construction activity for planting, grading, and installing green infrastructure elements that soften density transitions between rings.

name: Prefabricated Facade Panel
description: Factory-manufactured cladding units used to rapidly enclose high-density buildings while maintaining quality and reducing on-site time.

name: Permeable Paving Surface
description: A surface material used in public realm and transition zones to manage stormwater runoff generated by high-density impervious coverage.

name: IFC Site
description: The IFC class defining the overall site boundary within which density rings are spatially organised and referenced.

name: IFC Building
description: The IFC class representing individual buildings within a density ring, aggregated to calculate ring-level density metrics.

name: Parking Structure
description: A structured car-parking facility integrated into or adjacent to density rings to manage vehicle accommodation in high-density areas.

name: Pedestrian Priority Street
description: A street type within high-density rings designed to prioritise walking and cycling over vehicular traffic to support urban vitality.

name: Community Amenity Hub
description: A designated community facility space within a density ring providing health, education, and social services scaled to ring population.

name: Reception / Lobby Node
description: A dedicated entry-level space that serves as the primary transition point and wayfinding hub for occupants and visitors.

name: Elevator Lobby
description: A circulation buffer space directly in front of elevator banks that manages passenger flow between floors.

name: Stairwell Landing
description: A flat platform within a stair enclosure that acts as a rest and directional transition node between flights.

name: Corridor Junction / Intersection Node
description: A widened or marked point where two or more corridors meet, enabling multi-directional pedestrian routing.

name: Atrium Node
description: A multi-storey void space that acts as a vertical activity and social hub connecting multiple floor levels visually and physically.

name: Break-out / Informal Collaboration Zone
description: An open or semi-open seating area adjacent to primary circulation paths that supports spontaneous interaction and short-duration work.

name: Waiting Area Node
description: A designated seating and holding zone positioned at key decision or service points within the building circulation network.

name: Transition Airlock / Vestibule
description: A small enclosed buffer space at building or zone entries that controls climate, security, and pedestrian flow between environments.

name: Access Control Barrier
description: A turnstile, gate, or door assembly placed at activity nodes to regulate authorised pedestrian entry and exit.

name: Security Checkpoint Counter
description: A staffed or automated desk unit at entry nodes used for visitor registration, baggage screening, and identity verification.

name: Information / Concierge Desk
description: A built-in or freestanding counter component positioned at primary nodes to provide occupant assistance and building information services.

name: Seating & Soft Furnishing Cluster
description: A grouped arrangement of chairs, benches, or soft seating elements that defines usable dwell zones within activity nodes.

name: Node Flooring Finish
description: Hard-wearing or tactile floor material — such as terrazzo, polished concrete, or patterned tile — selected specifically to demarcate and reinforce activity node boundaries.

name: Acoustic Absorption Panel
description: Sound-absorbing wall or ceiling material installed at high-traffic nodes to reduce reverberation and improve speech intelligibility.

name: Feature / Landmark Element
description: A sculptural, artistic, or architectural feature element placed at a node to create a memorable landmark that aids spatial orientation.

name: Node Lighting Fixture Array
description: A coordinated set of pendant, recessed, or feature luminaires designed to distinguish the activity node visually from adjoining circulation paths.

name: Digital Information Kiosk
description: A freestanding or wall-mounted interactive screen unit deployed at nodes to provide real-time directories, booking, and building information.

name: HVAC Distribution Node
description: A local branch point in the mechanical ventilation and air-conditioning network serving the activity node's thermal comfort and air quality requirements.

name: Fire Evacuation Assembly Point
description: A designated safe-gathering node — internal or external — where occupants congregate during emergency egress procedures.

name: Construction Layout & Setting-Out Activity
description: Site activity of surveying and marking the precise floor positions, boundaries, and alignment of activity nodes before structural or fit-out works begin.

name: Raised Floor / Podium Construction
description: Construction activity involving the installation of a raised platform or podium within a node space to create level changes and define zones.

name: Feature Ceiling Installation
description: Specialist fit-out activity for erecting feature or coffered ceiling assemblies that visually frame and elevate the character of activity nodes.

name: Stone / Tile Flooring Installation
description: Finishing trade activity covering the laying and grouting of hard floor finishes within activity nodes to required patterns and tolerances.

name: Low-Voltage & AV Systems Fit-Out
description: Specialist trade activity for installing data, CCTV, public-address, and interactive display systems that serve activity node functions.

name: Soft Landscaping / Planting Installation
description: Landscape activity covering the placement and establishment of indoor planting, green walls, or water features within atrium or lobby nodes.

name: Node Commissioning & Occupancy Trial
description: Post-construction activity that tests pedestrian flow, environmental systems, and technology performance across all activity nodes before practical completion.

name: IfcSpace (Activity Node)
description: The IFC schema class used to model and exchange the bounded spatial unit representing a discrete activity node within a building information model.

name: IfcSignal / IfcSign
description: IFC class used to represent signage and wayfinding elements positioned at activity nodes within the building information model.

name: Paving Surface
description: The ground-level surfacing material (e.g., stone, concrete, brick pavers) that forms the walkable floor of a promenade.

name: Planted Median Strip
description: A landscaped central or side strip with trees, shrubs, or flowers that provides greenery and visual separation along the promenade.

name: Street Tree
description: Individual trees planted at regular intervals along the promenade to provide shade, aesthetic value, and ecological benefit.

name: Tree Pit / Tree Grate
description: The structural surround or grate at the base of street trees that protects roots while maintaining a flush, walkable surface.

name: Bench / Seating Element
description: Fixed or movable seating units placed along the promenade to allow rest and social interaction.

name: Lighting Column / Lamp Post
description: Vertical posts with luminaires providing ambient and safety lighting along the promenade at night.

name: Balustrade / Railing
description: A continuous guardrail system used at edges, level changes, or waterfront promenades for safety and delineation.

name: Kiosk / Retail Pod
description: Small freestanding commercial structures sited along the promenade offering food, retail, or information services.

name: Cycle Lane
description: A designated lane within or adjacent to the promenade reserved for bicycle traffic, separated from pedestrian flow.

name: Drainage / Stormwater Channel
description: The underground or surface drainage infrastructure managing rainwater runoff from the promenade surface.

name: Kerb / Edging
description: Border elements that define the boundary between the promenade surface and adjacent roadway, planting, or lower ground levels.

name: Bollard
description: Short vertical posts used to restrict vehicle access, delineate zones, or provide collision protection along the promenade.

name: Wayfinding Signage
description: Informational and directional signs installed along the promenade to guide pedestrians to key destinations.

name: Drinking Fountain
description: Fixed water-supply fixtures provided for public use along the promenade for hydration and amenity.

name: Waste / Recycling Bin
description: Strategically placed receptacles for the collection of litter and recyclable materials from promenade users.

name: Sub-base / Foundation Layer
description: The structural compacted aggregate or concrete bed beneath the paving surface that bears and distributes pedestrian loads.

name: Outdoor Dining Terrace
description: A semi-enclosed or open seating area affiliated with adjacent cafés or restaurants that spills onto the promenade edge.

name: Ramp / Accessible Path
description: Gently sloped surfaces ensuring the promenade is fully accessible to wheelchair users and people with mobility impairments.

name: Step / Staircase
description: Stepped connections between different levels or platforms along the promenade where grade changes require vertical access.

name: Underground Utility Corridor
description: Conduits and ducts beneath the promenade carrying electricity, telecommunications, water, and other services to street furniture and kiosks.

name: Smart / Sensor Lighting System
description: An automated or IoT-enabled control network managing lighting levels, schedules, and energy use across the promenade.

name: CCTV / Security System
description: Surveillance cameras and monitoring infrastructure installed along the promenade for public safety and crime deterrence.

name: Paving Laying & Bedding Works
description: The construction activity of setting paving units on a prepared bed, ensuring correct falls, joints, and alignment.

name: Excavation & Earthworks
description: Site preparation including bulk excavation, grading, and compaction of subgrade prior to promenade construction.

name: Landscape Planting Works
description: The activity of installing trees, shrubs, ground cover, and turf within the promenade's planted areas.

name: Utility Ducting & Services Installation
description: The activity of laying underground conduits and making connections for electrical, data, and water services prior to paving.

name: Waterfront / Seawall Interface
description: The structural edge treatment where a waterfront promenade meets the sea, river, or lake, including wave protection and mooring features.

name: IfcPavement
description: The IFC schema class used to model the paved surface and its layer composition within a BIM environment.

name: Retail Unit / Shop Front
description: Individual leasable commercial spaces lining the street, each with its own facade and entrance.

name: Display Window
description: Large glazed shopfront window used to showcase merchandise and attract passing customers.

name: Shopfront Canopy / Awning
description: A projecting roof structure or retractable fabric cover over shop entrances providing weather protection.

name: Signage & Fascia Board
description: Branded signage panels and illuminated fascias mounted above shop fronts identifying retailers.

name: Paving & Hard Landscaping
description: Surface materials such as natural stone, concrete flags, or brick pavers forming the street floor.

name: Kiosk / Market Stall Structure
description: Temporary or permanent small-format retail structures positioned within the street zone.

name: Covered Arcade / Glazed Roof
description: A structural glazed or polycarbonate overhead enclosure spanning the street to create an all-weather environment.

name: Drainage & Surface Water System
description: Channel drains, gullies, and underground pipework managing rainwater runoff from the pedestrianised surface.

name: Underground Utility Duct Network
description: Buried conduit routes carrying electricity, data, gas, and water services to each retail unit.

name: Loading Bay / Service Yard
description: A rear or side area providing controlled vehicle access for deliveries and waste collection away from shoppers.

name: Pedestrian Crossing & Traffic Management
description: Raised tables, zebra crossings, signal-controlled crossings, and retractable bollards managing vehicle–pedestrian conflict points.

name: Public Address / Wayfinding System
description: Speakers, digital totems, and directional signage helping visitors navigate the retail environment.

name: Landscaping & Planting Zones
description: Tree pits, raised planters, and green corridors integrated into the street for biodiversity and visual amenity.

name: Outdoor Seating / Dining Terrace
description: Licensed al-fresco areas adjacent to cafés and restaurants within the street for customer use.

name: Public Toilet / Welfare Facility
description: Publicly accessible sanitary facilities located within or immediately adjacent to the shopping street.

name: Shopfront Installation & Fit-Out Works
description: Construction activities covering the fitting of glazed shopfronts, internal partitions, and retail interior elements.

name: Paving & Surface Laying Works
description: Civil works involving sub-base preparation, bedding, and laying of the chosen street paving material.

name: Utility Diversion & Ducting Works
description: Excavation, rerouting, and reinstatement activities required to install or relocate underground service runs.

name: Lighting Installation Works
description: Erection of lighting columns, cable pulls, luminaire mounting, and commissioning of the street lighting system.

name: Canopy / Arcade Steelwork Erection
description: Structural assembly and weatherproofing of any overhead canopy or glazed arcade spanning the street.

name: Natural Stone Paving
description: Granite, sandstone, or limestone slabs used as a premium durable surface finish for the pedestrian zone.

name: Concrete Block Paving
description: Interlocking precast concrete units providing a cost-effective and maintainable street surface.

name: Structural Steel (Canopy Frame)
description: Hot-rolled or hollow-section steel members forming the primary skeleton of any overhead arcade or canopy.

name: Toughened / Laminated Glazing
description: Safety glass used in shopfronts, canopy roofs, and display windows to meet safety and thermal standards.

name: IfcPedestrian Thoroughfare Zone
description: IFC spatial element classifying the open pedestrian circulation area of the shopping street within a BIM model.

name: IfcRetailUnit (IfcSpace)
description: IFC space entity representing each individual shop or retail bay within the building knowledge model.

name: IfcFurniture (Street Furniture)
description: IFC furniture class used to model benches, bins, bollards, and other installed street furniture elements.

name: IfcDistributionSystem (Drainage)
description: IFC system object grouping all drainage channels, gullies, and pipework servicing the street surface.

name: Bar / Cocktail Lounge
description: A dedicated area serving alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, typically featuring counter seating and mood lighting.

name: Nightclub Dance Floor
description: A large open floor area designed for dancing, with specialized acoustic and lighting provisions.

name: DJ Booth
description: An elevated or enclosed station housing audio equipment and controls for the resident disc jockey.

name: VIP Lounge
description: A semi-private or private area offering premium seating and services to exclusive guests.

name: Smoking Terrace / Outdoor Area
description: An outdoor or semi-covered zone designated for smoking and fresh-air breaks compliant with local regulations.

name: Cloakroom / Coat Check
description: A staffed room or counter where patrons securely store coats, bags, and personal belongings.

name: Backstage / Artist Green Room
description: A private rest and preparation area for performing artists and entertainment staff.

name: Security / Entry Checkpoint
description: A controlled entry zone equipped for ID checking, bag search, and crowd management.

name: Stage / Performance Platform
description: A raised structural platform designed to support live performances, including load requirements for performers and equipment.

name: Professional Sound System
description: A high-power, multi-zone audio system including subwoofers, line arrays, monitors, and amplifiers engineered for large crowds.

name: Architectural Lighting System
description: A programmable LED and moving-head lighting rig that creates dynamic visual atmospheres throughout the venue.

name: Acoustic Treatment & Soundproofing
description: Sound-absorbing panels, mass-loaded vinyl, and resilient isolators applied to walls, ceilings, and floors to contain noise within the venue.

name: HVAC / Mechanical Ventilation System
description: A high-capacity heating, cooling, and fresh-air system sized for the elevated occupancy and body-heat loads typical of nightlife venues.

name: Fire Suppression & Safety System
description: Sprinkler networks, smoke detectors, emergency lighting, and clearly marked egress paths required by life-safety codes for high-occupancy entertainment spaces.

name: Bar Millwork & Counter
description: Custom-built bar counters, back-bar shelving, and cabinetry fabricated to house glassware, bottles, and point-of-sale equipment.

name: Cellar / Bottle Storage Room
description: A climate-controlled storage space for beverages, kegs, and bar supplies inventory.

name: Commercial Kitchen / Prep Area
description: A food-safe preparation and cooking area supporting any food menu offered to patrons.

name: Patron Restrooms
description: Gender-specific or all-gender toilet facilities scaled to high-occupancy nightlife loads with durable, easy-clean finishes.

name: Staff / Service Corridors
description: Back-of-house circulation paths allowing staff to move equipment and supplies without crossing public areas.

name: Crowd-Control Barrier & Queue Management
description: Retractable belt stanchions, permanent railings, and exterior queue enclosures used to manage patron entry lines safely.

name: Themed Interior Fit-Out
description: The construction and installation of decorative finishes, bespoke furniture, and branded aesthetic elements that define the venue's identity.

name: Acoustic & Vibration Testing
description: Post-construction testing of sound containment and structural vibration levels to ensure compliance with noise ordinances.

name: AV System Installation & Commissioning
description: The mounting, cabling, and programming of all audio-visual equipment including speakers, amplifiers, and lighting consoles.

name: Liquor License & Regulatory Fit-Out
description: Construction modifications—such as secure storage, age-verification stations, and signage—required to satisfy licensing authority inspections.

name: Structural Reinforcement for Dynamic Loads
description: Engineering and construction work to strengthen floors and roof structures against rhythmic crowd movement and heavy speaker/stage loads.

name: Late-Night Venue (Entertainment License Class)
description: The IFC/zoning classification designating a building or tenancy as a licensed late-night entertainment premises subject to specific operating conditions.

name: IfcSpace – Assembly Occupancy
description: The IFC schema space classification for assembly and entertainment occupancies used in BIM models of nightlife venues.

name: Polished Concrete / Resin Floor Finish
description: Hard-wearing, easy-to-clean floor finishes suited to high foot-traffic, spill exposure, and the aesthetic requirements of nightlife environments.

name: Specialist Lighting Fixtures (LED Par, Moving Head)
description: Individual programmable lighting units—including LED PAR cans and moving-head spots—that are installed on rigging above the dance floor and stage.

name: Rigging & Truss System
description: Overhead structural steel trusswork used to hang speaker arrays, lighting rigs, and decorative elements safely above the venue floor.

name: Platform
description: A raised surface area where passengers board or alight from vehicles such as trains, buses, or trams.

name: Concourse
description: A large open circulation space connecting various parts of the interchange where passengers navigate between services.

name: Ticket Hall
description: A dedicated area housing ticketing machines, counters, and fare gates for passenger entry and exit processing.

name: Bus Bay
description: A designated stopping and loading zone for buses within a multi-modal interchange.

name: Taxi Drop-off Zone
description: A marked forecourt area reserved for taxi and private hire vehicle pick-up and drop-off.

name: Cycle Storage Facility
description: A secure, covered area providing bicycle parking and sometimes repair facilities for commuters.

name: Pedestrian Underpass
description: A below-grade tunnel allowing safe pedestrian movement beneath roadways or rail lines within the interchange.

name: Overhead Walkway
description: An elevated enclosed or open bridge structure linking separate terminal buildings or platforms.

name: Control Room
description: A staffed operational room housing monitoring, communication, and management systems for the interchange.

name: Staff Amenity Room
description: Back-of-house accommodation providing rest, welfare, and storage facilities for interchange staff.

name: Fare Gate Array
description: A set of automated turnstiles or barriers controlling paid access between the unpaid and paid zones of the interchange.

name: Canopy Structure
description: A roof or shelter covering platforms, bus bays, or pedestrian areas to provide weather protection.

name: Tactile Paving
description: Textured ground surface indicators installed at platform edges and circulation routes to assist visually impaired passengers.

name: Anti-slip Flooring
description: High-traction surface material applied to concourses, platforms, and stairs to reduce slip hazards in wet conditions.

name: Glazed Facade System
description: A curtain wall or window system providing natural daylighting and weather enclosure to concourse and terminal spaces.

name: Fire Detection and Suppression System
description: Integrated smoke detectors, sprinklers, and alarm panels providing life safety coverage throughout the interchange.

name: Emergency Evacuation Route
description: Clearly marked and maintained corridors and exits designed to safely evacuate occupants in an emergency.

name: Drainage and Surface Water Management System
description: Channels, gullies, and pipes managing rainwater runoff from platforms, forecourts, and roof structures.

name: Site Enabling Works
description: Preliminary groundworks including demolition, decontamination, and temporary diversions required before main interchange construction.

name: Substructure and Foundation Construction
description: The process of installing piled, pad, or raft foundations to support interchange structures above and below ground.

name: Canopy and Roof Installation
description: The fabrication, delivery, and fixing of platform and concourse canopy steelwork, cladding, and waterproofing layers.

name: Platform Surface Laying
description: Installation of platform finishes including tactile paving, edge treatments, and waterproof membranes to operational standards.

name: M&E Fit-Out
description: Installation of all mechanical, electrical, and plumbing services including lighting, HVAC, and public information systems.

name: Wayfinding and Signage Installation
description: Fixing and commissioning of all static and dynamic passenger signage in accordance with the interchange design standard.

name: Systems Integration Testing and Commissioning
description: End-to-end testing of all building and transport systems to confirm interoperability and compliance before handover.

name: Landscaping and External Works
description: Construction of external paving, planting, lighting, and street furniture forming the interchange's public realm.

name: Multi-modal Hub
description: A broader interchange variant integrating three or more transport modes — rail, bus, tram, cycle, and car — in a single facility.

name: Park and Ride Facility
description: A peripheral car park connected to the interchange allowing drivers to transfer to public transport for onward travel.

name: Kiss and Ride Zone
description: A short-stay drop-off and collection area for private vehicles adjacent to the main interchange entrance.

name: Master Bedroom
description: The primary sleeping space in a household, typically the largest bedroom with an en-suite or walk-in wardrobe.

name: Secondary Bedroom
description: Additional bedrooms beyond the master, used by other occupants or as guest rooms.

name: Living Room
description: The main communal space for relaxation and social interaction within a household unit.

name: Dining Room
description: A dedicated space for meals, either separate or open-plan with the kitchen or living area.

name: Kitchen
description: The primary food preparation and cooking space, typically fitted with cabinetry, appliances, and worktops.

name: Bathroom
description: A sanitary space containing a bathtub and/or shower, basin, and toilet for personal hygiene.

name: En-Suite Bathroom
description: A private bathroom directly accessible from a bedroom, serving only that room's occupants.

name: Guest Toilet / WC
description: A small sanitary space containing only a toilet and basin, typically located on a ground floor for visitor use.

name: Home Office / Study
description: A dedicated workspace within the household for remote work, study, or administrative tasks.

name: Utility Room / Laundry Room
description: A service space housing washing machines, dryers, and storage for cleaning equipment and supplies.

name: Hallway / Entrance Foyer
description: The transitional entry space connecting the external entrance to the internal circulation of the household.

name: Staircase / Stair Hall
description: The vertical circulation space containing stairs that connect different floor levels within a multi-storey household.

name: Storage Room / Cupboard
description: Dedicated enclosed storage space for household items, linen, or seasonal goods.

name: Garage
description: An enclosed space for vehicle parking and storage, either attached to or integral within the household structure.

name: Garden / Outdoor Area
description: External private open space associated with the household, used for recreation, planting, or outdoor living.

name: Balcony / Terrace
description: An elevated or ground-level private outdoor platform attached to the household for outdoor amenity use.

name: Basement / Cellar
description: A below-ground-level space used for storage, plant rooms, or additional living accommodation.

name: Loft / Attic Space
