description: Fixed or retractable upright posts placed in front of the main gateway to prevent unauthorised vehicle access and protect pedestrians.

name: Gate / Ceremonial Gate Leaf
description: A large hinged or sliding gate panel—often decorative—used at campus, estate, or institutional main gateways to mark the formal entrance boundary.

name: Gatehouse / Security Booth
description: A small staffed enclosure positioned at the main gateway to house security personnel who control and monitor access to the site.

name: Interstitial Airlock Lobby
description: A double-door vestibule zone between two sets of entrance doors that maintains indoor climate and security by preventing direct outdoor-indoor air exchange.

name: IfcSpace (Entrance)
description: The IFC schema class representing the bounded spatial zone of the entrance lobby or gateway area within a BIM dataset.

name: Door & Frame Installation (Activity)
description: The on-site construction activity of fitting, aligning, and fixing door frames, leaves, and hardware within the prepared gateway opening.

name: Concrete & Masonry Opening Formation
description: The construction activity of forming, cutting, or casting the structural opening in walls or frames to receive the main gateway assembly.

name: Access Control Commissioning
description: The testing, programming, and handover activity that activates and verifies all electronic access-control and intercom systems at the gateway.

name: Canopy Steelwork Erection
description: The structural assembly activity of fabricating and installing the steel framework that supports the entrance canopy over the main gateway.

name: Ironmongery & Hardware Fitting
description: The installation activity covering hinges, closers, panic bars, locks, handles, and other door furniture on the gateway door assembly.

name: Crosswalk Markings
description: Painted or thermoplastic lines and patterns on the road surface that delineate the pedestrian crossing zone.

name: Tactile Paving / Detectable Warning Surface
description: Textured ground surface indicators installed at the edges of the crossing to alert visually impaired users.

name: Kerb Ramp / Dropped Kerb
description: A sloped transition between the footpath and the road surface to allow wheelchair and mobility aid access.

name: Traffic Signal Controller
description: The electronic unit that manages the sequencing and timing of traffic and pedestrian signals at the crossing.

name: Pedestrian Signal Head (Walk/Don't Walk)
description: A visual signal device mounted on a pole that indicates when pedestrians may safely cross.

name: Audible / Tactile Pedestrian Push Button
description: A push-button unit that allows pedestrians to request a crossing phase, often with audible and vibrating feedback.

name: Signal Pole / Mast Arm
description: Structural steel or aluminium pole that supports traffic signal heads, signs, and pedestrian devices at the crossing.

name: Vehicle Traffic Signal Head
description: Overhead or pole-mounted light unit displaying red, amber, and green phases to control approaching vehicle traffic.

name: Pedestrian Refuge Island
description: A raised or flush median island that provides a safe waiting area for pedestrians crossing in two stages.

name: Guard Rail / Pedestrian Barrier
description: Metal or concrete fencing installed to guide pedestrians to the designated crossing point and prevent jaywalking.

name: Countdown Timer Display
description: A digital display attached to the pedestrian signal that shows the remaining seconds of the walk phase.

name: CCTV / Crossing Surveillance Camera
description: Camera system installed to monitor crossing activity for safety compliance, incident recording, and traffic management.

name: Road Surface / Carriageway Pavement
description: The asphalt, concrete, or block-paving surface material that forms the drivable area within the crossing zone.

name: Street Lighting at Crossing
description: Dedicated lighting fixtures positioned to illuminate the crossing area for visibility during night-time and low-light conditions.

name: Signage (Crossing Warning Signs)
description: Regulatory and warning signs installed in advance of and at the crossing to alert drivers to the pedestrian zone.

name: Underground Conduit / Cable Duct
description: Sub-surface ducting infrastructure that routes electrical and data cables to signals, cameras, and controllers.

name: Junction Box / Pull Box
description: An in-ground enclosure providing access points for cable connections and maintenance within the crossing electrical network.

name: Drainage / Surface Water Channel
description: Gullies, channels, and drainage connections that manage rainwater run-off from the crossing surface.

name: Road Marking Installation
description: The construction activity of applying thermoplastic or paint road markings to define the crossing boundaries and stop lines.

name: Signal Installation & Commissioning
description: The activity of erecting signal poles, mounting signal heads, and testing and commissioning the full signal control system.

name: Kerb & Ramp Construction
description: Civil works activity involving the removal of existing kerbs and construction of dropped kerbs and ramps at crossing entry points.

name: Carriageway Resurfacing
description: The activity of removing and relaying road pavement within the crossing area to the required specification.

name: Tactile Paving Installation
description: The laying and fixing of tactile warning surface units at the top and base of kerb ramps and crossing approaches.

name: Electrical & Ducting Works
description: Excavation, ducting installation, cable pulling, and reinstatement activities to establish the power and data network for the crossing.

name: Pelican Crossing
description: A signal-controlled pedestrian crossing variant where pedestrians push a button to request a green walk phase.

name: Puffin Crossing
description: An intelligent signal-controlled crossing variant that uses kerbside detection to extend or cancel the pedestrian phase based on demand.

name: Toucan Crossing
description: A shared-use signal crossing designed to accommodate both pedestrians and cyclists crossing simultaneously.

name: Pegasus / Equestrian Crossing
description: A signal-controlled crossing variant that includes a higher push button and a separate phase for horse riders.

name: Zebra Crossing
description: An uncontrolled priority crossing marked with alternating black-and-white stripes giving pedestrians right of way.

name: Raised Crossing / Speed Table
description: A crossing where the road surface is raised to footway level to slow vehicles and improve pedestrian priority.

name: Pedestrian Detection System
description: Infrared or video-based sensors mounted at the crossing that detect the presence of pedestrians to adapt signal timings.

name: Vehicle Detection Loop / Sensor
description: In-ground inductive loops or above-ground radar sensors that detect approaching or waiting vehicles to inform signal phasing.

name: Elevated Deck Structure
description: The primary load-bearing platform assembly that sits above grade, forming the walkable surface of the raised walk.

name: Support Columns / Piers
description: Vertical structural members (timber, steel, or concrete) that transfer loads from the deck down to the foundations.

name: Foundation Footings
description: Below-grade concrete or masonry bases that anchor support columns and distribute structural loads into the soil.

name: Guardrail System
description: Protective barrier assembly comprising posts, top rails, and infill panels installed at open edges to prevent falls.

name: Decking / Walking Surface
description: The finish surface material (timber boards, composite planks, concrete, or grating) applied to the structural frame that pedestrians walk on.

name: Structural Framing (Joists & Beams)
description: Horizontal framing members—joists and beams—that span between columns and support the decking surface.

name: Bracing System
description: Diagonal or cross members installed between columns to resist lateral forces such as wind and seismic loads.

name: Staircase / Access Stair
description: A stepped structure providing safe vertical access between the raised walk level and the ground or other floor levels.

name: Waterproofing / Weather Barrier Membrane
description: A protective membrane applied beneath or over the deck surface to prevent moisture ingress into the structural assembly.

name: Anti-Slip Surface Treatment
description: Grit coatings, grooved profiles, or grip tape applied to the walking surface to reduce slip hazard in wet conditions.

name: Expansion Joints
description: Designed gaps with flexible fillers placed at intervals to accommodate thermal movement and prevent cracking or warping.

name: Fascia Board / Skirting
description: Trim boards fixed to the perimeter framing to conceal the structural edge, improve aesthetics, and deter pest ingress.

name: Utility / Service Conduit Run
description: Conduits or duct runs routed beneath the deck to carry electrical, data, or plumbing services along the raised walk corridor.

name: Boardwalk (Wetland / Coastal Variant)
description: A variant of raised walk constructed over water, wetland, or sensitive ecological areas where ground disturbance must be minimized.

name: Elevated Pedestrian Bridge
description: A long-span raised walk variant that crosses a gap, road, or waterway, often requiring dedicated structural engineering.

name: Skybridge / Skywalk
description: An enclosed or semi-enclosed raised walk connecting two buildings at upper floor levels, often climate-controlled.

name: Mezzanine Walkway
description: An interior raised walk at an intermediate floor level within a building, typically used for access to shelving, plant, or seating areas.

name: Substructure Excavation & Footing Works
description: Site preparation and excavation activities to install foundation footings that support the raised walk columns.

name: Column / Pier Installation
description: The construction activity of erecting and securing vertical support columns or piers on prepared footings.

name: Decking Installation
description: Laying and fixing of deck boards or surface panels onto the completed structural frame.

name: Guardrail & Handrail Installation
description: Fabrication and erection of edge protection systems to meet safety and building code requirements.

name: Surface Finishing & Anti-Slip Treatment
description: Final surface preparation, sanding, staining, painting, or grip-coating of the walk surface.

name: Structural Inspection & Load Testing
description: Engineering inspection and proof-load testing of the completed raised walk to verify structural adequacy and code compliance.

name: Timber (Hardwood / Softwood)
description: Traditional wood species used for decking boards, framing joists, and handrails, selected for strength and durability.

name: Composite Decking Material
description: Wood-plastic or fibre-reinforced composite boards used as a low-maintenance alternative to natural timber decking.

name: Galvanized / Stainless Steel Fixings & Connectors
description: Corrosion-resistant fasteners, joist hangers, and post bases critical for structural integrity of outdoor raised walk assemblies.

name: Bicycle Rack
description: A fixed or freestanding structure used to park and secure individual bicycles in an organized manner.

name: Wall-Mounted Bike Bracket
description: A bracket affixed to a wall that holds a bicycle vertically or horizontally to save floor space.

name: Two-Tier Bike Rack
description: A double-level rack system that maximizes bike storage density by stacking bikes on two levels.

name: Bike Locker
description: An enclosed, lockable individual storage unit providing secure and weather-protected parking for a single bicycle.

name: Bike Lane Pavement Markings
description: Painted symbols, arrows, and demarcation lines applied to the pavement surface to designate dedicated cycling lanes.

name: Bike Lane Signage
description: Regulatory and informational signs installed along cycling routes to guide cyclists and inform other users.

name: Bike Repair Station
description: A publicly accessible kiosk equipped with tools and a pump for cyclists to perform on-site bicycle maintenance.

name: Bike Pump Station
description: A dedicated air pump fixture mounted in a fixed location for cyclists to inflate tires without tools.

name: Cargo Bike Storage Area
description: An oversized designated zone designed to accommodate cargo bikes, tricycles, and non-standard cycling equipment.

name: Bike Shelter / Canopy
description: A weatherproof overhead structure covering bike racks or storage areas to protect bicycles from rain and sun.

name: Dedicated Bike Path
description: A physically separated or clearly demarcated route exclusively or primarily designed for bicycle travel within or around a building site.

name: Shared Cycling-Pedestrian Path
description: A shared surface route designed to accommodate both cyclists and pedestrians, typically with clear zoning markings.

name: Bike Parking Area
description: A designated zone within a site plan allocated specifically for bicycle parking and associated infrastructure.

name: Asphalt Paving
description: A bituminous surface material commonly used for constructing durable and smooth bike paths.

name: Thermoplastic Road Marking
description: A durable, heat-applied plastic material used for bike lane symbols and markings due to its high visibility and longevity.

name: Bike Path Layout and Marking Installation
description: The construction activity of setting out, painting, and applying thermoplastic markings to designate cycling routes on a surface.

name: Bike Rack Installation
description: The site activity of fixing, anchoring, or assembling bicycle parking racks in their designated location.

name: Bike Shelter Erection
description: The construction activity of assembling and erecting a canopy or enclosure structure over a bike parking area.

name: Subbase and Paving Works for Bike Paths
description: Ground preparation, subbase compaction, and surface paving activities specific to constructing bike path corridors.

name: Signage and Bollard Installation
description: The activity of positioning and securing directional signs and bollards along bike routes and at parking areas.

name: Bike Locker Installation
description: The activity of placing, anchoring, and commissioning enclosed individual bicycle lockers on site.

name: E-Bike Charging Station
description: An electrical charging system providing power outlets or dedicated connectors for recharging electric bicycles.

name: Bike Counting / Monitoring System
description: A sensor-based system that tracks and records bicycle usage volumes along paths or at parking facilities for occupancy and planning data.

name: Access Control System for Bike Storage
description: An electronic or mechanical system restricting entry to secured bike storage rooms or lockers to authorized users only.

name: Drainage System for Bike Paths
description: A stormwater management and drainage infrastructure integrated into or adjacent to bike paths to prevent waterlogging.

name: Lighting System for Bike Paths
description: Dedicated low-level or overhead lighting infrastructure ensuring safe visibility along cycling routes and parking areas at night.

name: Children's Playground
description: An outdoor or indoor area specifically designed with equipment and surfaces for children's play and physical activity.

name: Daycare / Nursery Facility
description: A dedicated space providing supervised care and early education for infants and young children within or near an urban building.

name: After-School Club Room
description: A room or suite used for structured after-school programs, homework support, and supervised recreational activities for school-age children.

name: Children's Library / Reading Nook
description: A quiet, child-scaled space furnished with age-appropriate books and seating to encourage literacy and independent reading.

name: Sensory Play Room
description: A specially equipped room offering tactile, visual, and auditory stimuli to support sensory development and inclusive play for children of all abilities.

name: Soft-Play Area
description: A padded, foam-lined zone with climbing structures and slides designed for safe active play by toddlers and young children.

name: Children's Art & Craft Studio
description: A bright, washable-surface workspace equipped with art supplies and craft tables for creative activities led by or for children.

name: Family Changing & Nursing Room
description: A private, hygienic room providing changing tables, seating for nursing, and baby-care amenities for parents and caregivers.

name: Child-Safe Fencing & Barriers
description: Perimeter and internal barriers with child-proof latches and appropriate heights to prevent unsupervised egress and ensure safe containment.

name: Low-Level Sanitary Fixtures
description: Child-height toilets, basins, and hand-dryers scaled and mounted to be safely and independently accessible by young children.

name: Impact-Absorbing Flooring
description: Rubber, foam-composite, or engineered wood surfacing that cushions falls and meets playground safety standards for children's activity zones.

name: Anti-Slip Safety Surfacing
description: Textured, slip-resistant surface material applied to floors, ramps, and steps to reduce fall risk in wet or high-traffic children's areas.

name: Child-Safe Glazing
description: Laminated or toughened safety glass used in low-level windows and partitions to prevent injury from breakage in children's environments.

name: Non-Toxic Paint & Finishes
description: Low-VOC, heavy-metal-free paints and surface coatings specified to meet child-safety standards for indoor air quality and contact safety.

name: Acoustic Insulation System
description: Sound-absorbing panels, ceiling baffles, and wall linings that control noise levels in active children's spaces to protect hearing and aid concentration.

name: Child-Safe Mechanical Ventilation System
description: HVAC and air-filtration system with child-proof grilles and enhanced filtration to maintain healthy indoor air quality in children's occupied spaces.

name: CCTV & Child Safety Monitoring System
description: Integrated camera and access-control network providing real-time supervision and security monitoring across all children's zones.

name: Emergency Evacuation & Alarm System
description: Visual and audible alarm system with child-height call points and evacuation routes specifically designed and practised for safe child egress.

name: Child-Scale Furniture & Fixed Casework
description: Built-in shelving, cubbies, lockers, and seating designed at child ergonomic heights to support independent use and safe storage.

name: Shade Structures & Canopies
description: UV-protective overhead structures over outdoor play areas to shield children from sun exposure and enable year-round outdoor activity.

name: Wayfinding & Signage for Children
description: Pictographic, colour-coded signs and floor markings at child eye-level to aid navigation and reinforce safety rules within the facility.

name: Fit-Out & Interior Installation Works
description: Construction activity covering the installation of child-scaled fixtures, fittings, furniture, and specialist play equipment within the completed shell.

name: Safety Surfacing Installation
description: Specialist laying and certification of impact-absorbing and anti-slip floor surfaces in play and activity zones to meet safety standards.

name: Playground Equipment Erection
description: Fabrication, delivery, and structural installation of climbing frames, slides, swings, and other play structures in accordance with BS EN 1176.

name: Child Safety Audit & Commissioning
description: Formal inspection and sign-off process verifying that all spaces, equipment, and systems meet statutory child safety and safeguarding requirements prior to occupation.

name: Urban Play Street / Traffic-Free Zone
description: A designated car-free urban street or public realm area temporarily or permanently reclaimed for children's outdoor play and social interaction.

name: Child-Friendly Public Realm
description: Outdoor urban spaces—squares, courtyards, and green corridors—designed with child-scale elements, safe surfacing, and stimulating landscaping.

name: Dedicated Drop-Off & Pick-Up Zone
description: A safe, sheltered vehicular or pedestrian area adjacent to the facility specifically planned for the supervised arrival and departure of children.

name: Inclusive Accessibility System
description: Ramps, wide doorways, tactile paving, and adaptive equipment ensuring children with disabilities can access and enjoy all spaces equally.

name: Water Play Feature
description: Splash pad, water jets, or interactive water feature designed for supervised sensory and physical play with safe, recycled water management.

name: Ticket Booth
description: A small enclosed structure at the entrance where visitors purchase admission tickets or ride tokens.

name: Entrance Gate
description: The main access control structure that manages visitor flow into and out of the carnival grounds.

name: Midway
description: The central pedestrian corridor flanked by game stalls, food vendors, and attractions where guests circulate.

name: Ferris Wheel
description: A large rotating wheel-shaped amusement ride with passenger gondolas offering elevated views of the grounds.

name: Carousel
description: A rotating circular platform fitted with decorative horses or seats for riders, typically accompanied by fairground music.

name: Roller Coaster Track
description: The elevated steel or timber rail structure along which coaster cars travel at high speed through hills and curves.

name: Fun House
description: An enclosed walk-through attraction featuring mirrors, optical illusions, moving floors, and novelty obstacles.

name: Haunted House
description: A themed walk-through or ride-through attraction designed to frighten guests with horror scenery and effects.

name: Game Stall
description: An open-fronted booth where guests pay to play skill or chance games to win prizes.

name: Food Concession Stand
description: A service kiosk or booth that sells carnival food items such as cotton candy, popcorn, and funnel cakes.

name: Temporary Tent Structure
description: A large tensile fabric canopy or marquee tent erected to shelter attractions, performances, or vendors.

name: Grandstand Seating
description: Tiered spectator seating platforms positioned to view central performance rings or stage shows.

name: Performance Ring
description: A circular or oval arena floor used for acrobatic acts, animal shows, or live entertainment performances.

name: Stage Platform
description: A raised floor structure providing a performance area for bands, magicians, or other entertainers.

name: Ride Foundation Pad
description: A reinforced concrete or compacted gravel base pad that supports and anchors temporary or permanent ride equipment.

name: Perimeter Fencing
description: Boundary fencing that defines the carnival site, controls access, and ensures guest safety.

name: Temporary Electrical Distribution System
description: The network of generators, cabling, distribution boards, and outlets that supplies power to all rides and vendors.

name: Lighting Rig
description: A system of decorative and functional light fixtures, strings, and towers that illuminate the grounds after dark.

name: PA and Sound System
description: The public address and background music infrastructure distributing audio announcements and entertainment sound across the site.

name: Water Supply and Sanitation System
description: Temporary plumbing connections and portable or permanent facilities providing fresh water, waste disposal, and handwashing stations.

name: Portable Restroom Facility
description: Self-contained or trailer-mounted toilet units deployed on-site to serve visitor and staff sanitary needs.

name: First Aid Station
description: A designated medical triage area equipped with basic emergency supplies to treat minor injuries on site.

name: Security Booth
description: A staffed monitoring post that coordinates crowd management, surveillance, and emergency response across the grounds.

name: Waste Management Station
description: Clustered bins, recycling points, and compactor units strategically placed for visitor refuse disposal.

name: Asphalt / Compacted Gravel Surfacing
description: The ground surface material used to create stable, all-weather pedestrian pathways and ride staging areas.

name: Structural Steel (Ride Framework)
description: High-strength steel sections and tubes forming the load-bearing skeleton of rides, stages, and overhead structures.

name: PVC Tensile Fabric
description: Coated woven fabric used for tent coverings, banners, and canopies throughout the carnival site.

name: Site Preparation and Grading
description: Earthworks activity to level, compact, and drain the ground surface before any structures or rides are installed.

name: Ride Assembly and Commissioning
description: The sequential mechanical erection, safety inspection, and test-running of all amusement rides prior to public opening.

name: Temporary Structure Erection
description: The installation of tents, scaffolding, staging, and modular booths that form the non-ride built environment.

name: Electrical Hook-up and Testing
description: The connection of generators and distribution equipment followed by load testing and compliance verification.

name: Signage and Theming Installation
description: Fixing decorative facades, branded signage, lighting garlands, and themed props to create the visual carnival atmosphere.

name: Ride Decommissioning and Dismantling
description: The systematic safe disassembly, inspection, and packing of ride equipment at the close of the event.

name: Site Restoration and Clean-up
description: Post-event removal of all temporary structures, waste clearance, and ground reinstatement to its original condition.

name: Rear Garden
description: Private outdoor space located at the back of a building, typically enclosed and used for recreation or planting.

name: Back Yard
description: Hard-landscaped or mixed-surface outdoor area to the rear of a building, distinct from a planted garden.

name: Rear Courtyard
description: Enclosed outdoor court at the back of a building, often shared or semi-private in nature.

name: Rear Fence
description: Fencing structure forming the boundary of the back space, providing privacy and security.

name: Garden Gate
description: Access gate set within the boundary wall or fence, controlling entry to the rear space.

name: Back Alley / Service Lane
description: Narrow lane running behind a row of buildings giving servicing, cycle, or pedestrian access to rear spaces.

name: Rear Access Path
description: Hard-surfaced footpath at the back of buildings connecting individual rear spaces to a lane or street.

name: Acoustic Barrier
description: Purpose-built wall, berm, or screen designed to attenuate noise reaching the rear quiet zone from roads or other sources.

name: Noise-Reducing Fence
description: Specialist close-boarded or composite fence panel with acoustic mass or absorption to reduce transmitted noise.

name: Green Buffer Planting
description: Dense planting of shrubs, hedges, or trees along boundaries to provide both visual screening and a degree of noise attenuation.

name: Rear Elevation
description: The back-facing external facade of a building looking onto the quiet rear space, often featuring windows and doors.

name: Rear Extension
description: Single- or multi-storey addition built out from the rear elevation into the back space, affecting its extent and character.

name: Outbuilding / Garden Structure
description: Detached ancillary structure such as a shed, garage, or studio located within the rear space.

name: Rear Drainage System

name: Glass / Glazing

name: Floor Finishes (Tiles, Hardwood, Carpet)

name: Paint & Render

name: Site Preparation & Excavation
description: Groundworks including clearing vegetation, levelling terrain, and excavating for foundations and services.

name: Structural Framing & Erection
description: Assembly of the primary structural skeleton — walls, columns, beams, and floor decks — to form the building shell.

name: Roof Construction & Weatherproofing

name: External Wall Construction & Cladding

name: Window & Door Installation

name: Internal Lining & Plastering

name: Kitchen & Bathroom Fitout

name: Building Commissioning & Handover

name: Detached House Variant
description: A free-standing house configuration with no shared walls, providing maximum privacy and outdoor space.

name: Semi-Detached House Variant

name: Terraced / Townhouse Variant

name: Single-Storey (Bungalow) Variant

name: Two-Storey House Variant

name: Passive House / Energy-Efficient Variant
description: A house built to stringent airtightness and insulation standards to minimise heating and cooling energy demand.

name: Modular / Prefabricated House Variant

name: Open-Plan Living Area

name: Guest Bedroom

name: Garage / Carport

name: Garden / Outdoor Living Area

name: Structural Frame

name: Roof Assembly

name: External Wall Assembly

name: Internal Partition Walls

name: Windows & Glazing

name: External Doors

name: Flooring System

name: Ceiling Assembly

name: Security & Alarm System

name: Timber Framing Lumber
description: Dimensioned softwood or engineered timber members forming the structural frame of walls, floors, and roofs.

name: Brick / Masonry Cladding
description: External facing material providing weather protection, aesthetics, and additional thermal mass.

name: Site Survey & Geotechnical Investigation

name: Planning Permission & Building Regulations Approval

name: Roof Construction & Waterproofing

name: Mechanical & Electrical First Fix
description: Installation of concealed pipework, ductwork, and wiring before internal surfaces are closed up.

name: Plastering & Drylining

name: Mechanical & Electrical Second Fix

name: Internal Fit-Out & Finishing

name: Compact Terraced House

name: Single-Storey Bungalow

name: Detached Villa

name: Passive House (Passivhaus) Design

name: Bedroom

name: Entryway / Foyer

name: Storage Room / Closet

name: Outdoor Terrace / Balcony

name: Exterior Wall Assembly

name: Interior Partition Wall

name: Exterior Door

name: Interior Doors

name: Interior Fit-Out & Finishes

name: Home Office

name: Windows

name: Internal Doors

name: Timber Framing
description: Structural wood members used to form the skeletal frame of walls, floors, and roofs.

name: Brickwork / Masonry

name: Plasterboard / Drywall

name: Smart Home / BMS

name: Garden

name: Data / AV Infrastructure
description: Structured cabling, wireless access points, and audio-visual equipment installed to support modern pedagogical technology in the shopfront learning environment.

name: Security / Access Control System

name: Change-of-Use Planning Approval
description: The statutory planning and building permit process required to reclassify a commercial retail tenancy to an educational facility use class.

name: Facade Branding / Signage Installation
description: Design and installation of school identity signage, graphics, and wayfinding elements on the shopfront facade and glazing.

name: Acoustic Treatment / Noise Mitigation

name: Polished Concrete / Resilient Flooring
description: Durable, easy-clean floor finish materials such as polished concrete or resilient vinyl appropriate for high-footfall school-in-retail environments.

name: High-Performance Glazing (Low-E / Acoustic)
description: Thermally and acoustically upgraded glass units specified for the shopfront facade to balance transparency, thermal comfort, and noise control.

name: Exposed Services / Industrial Ceiling Finish
description: Deliberately exposed structural and services ceiling retained from the existing shell, finished for an open, loft-style aesthetic common in shopfront school fitouts.

name: Adaptive Reuse / Temporary School
description: A broader category of non-purpose-built, adaptively reused or temporary school environments of which the shopfront school is a specific typology.

name: Pop-Up / Micro-School
description: A closely related typology characterised by a small, flexible, non-permanent educational space often deployed in commercial or community settings similar to shopfront schools.

name: Street-Level Learning Hub
description: A community-embedded educational space at grade level designed for open access and neighbourhood engagement, overlapping with the shopfront school concept.

name: Dormitory / Sleeping Room
description: Shared or individual sleeping quarters designed for the safe overnight accommodation of children residents.

name: Communal Dining Room
description: Shared meal area with child-scaled tables and chairs where residents eat together in a supervised setting.

name: Kitchen / Catering Area
description: Commercial-grade kitchen facility for preparing nutritious meals for all residents and staff.

name: Staff Office
description: Administrative workspace for care workers, social workers, and management to handle records and case files.

name: Counselling / Therapy Room
description: Private, calming room used for one-on-one therapeutic sessions and psychological support for children.

name: Outdoor Play Area / Garden
description: Secured external space with play equipment, soft landscaping, and seating to support physical activity and outdoor learning.

name: Homework / Study Room
description: Quiet room furnished with desks, shelving, and adequate lighting to support children's educational activities.

name: Bathroom / Wet Room
description: Age-appropriate and accessible bathing and hygiene facilities designed for children's safety and dignity.

name: Sensory Room
description: Specially designed room with lighting, sound, and tactile features to support children with sensory processing needs.

name: Medical / First Aid Room
description: Dedicated clinical space for routine health checks, medication storage, and first-aid treatment of residents.

name: Staff Break Room
description: Rest and welfare space exclusively for care staff away from resident areas.

name: Secure Perimeter Fencing
description: Child-safe boundary fencing and gates that prevent unauthorised entry and ensure residents cannot leave unsupervised.

name: CCTV & Access Control System
description: Integrated surveillance and electronic access system that monitors entry points and common areas for child safeguarding.

name: Mechanical Ventilation & Heating System
description: HVAC system maintaining safe indoor air quality and thermal comfort appropriate for children's health needs.

name: Nurse Call / Staff Alert System
description: Electronic call system enabling children or staff to raise alarms quickly in any room or corridor.

name: Anti-Ligature Fixtures & Fittings
description: Specially designed door handles, curtain rails, and fixings that minimise risk of self-harm in line with safeguarding standards.

name: Impact-Resistant Wall Cladding
description: Durable, washable wall lining in high-traffic areas that withstands physical activity and is easy to sanitise.

name: Soft Flooring / Carpet Tiles
description: Cushioned floor covering in playrooms and bedrooms that reduces injury risk and provides warmth and comfort.

name: Planning & Regulatory Approval
description: Obtaining change-of-use consent and care-home-specific planning permissions from local authorities before construction begins.

name: Safeguarding Risk Assessment
description: Formal evaluation of all design features against child safeguarding standards prior to and during the construction phase.

name: Specialist Interior Fit-Out
description: Installation of child-specific furniture, anti-ligature fittings, sensory equipment, and play infrastructure by specialist contractors.

name: Fire Safety Compliance Inspection
description: Statutory inspection and sign-off of fire detection, suppression, and escape route provisions by the fire authority.

name: Building Commissioning & Care Registration
description: Final testing of all building systems and submission of the completed facility for registration with the relevant care regulator (e.g., Ofsted/CQC).

name: Landscaping & Play Equipment Installation
description: Groundworks, planting, and certified installation of outdoor play structures within the secured perimeter.

name: IfcSystem
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcGroup.

name: Retail Shell Unit
description: The bare structural enclosure forming an individual shop unit before any tenant fit-out works are carried out.

name: Shop Front Assembly
description: The façade element of a shop unit comprising glazed panels, framing, signage zone, and entrance door facing the street or mall concourse.

name: Tenant Demise Boundary Wall
description: The partition or structural wall that legally and physically separates one individually owned shop unit from an adjacent unit or common area.

name: Internal Shopfitting Partition
description: Non-load-bearing internal walls erected by the tenant to sub-divide the retail floor area into sales, storage, and staff zones.

name: Shop Entrance Door
description: The primary access door set into the shop front, which may be automatic sliding, swing, or roller-shutter type depending on tenant requirements.

name: Display Window Glazing
description: Large-format glazed panels at the shop front designed to showcase merchandise and maximise visibility from the street or mall.

name: Tenant Electrical Distribution Board
description: A dedicated electrical panel within each shop unit that distributes power to lighting, equipment, and HVAC serving that tenancy.

name: Retail Lighting System
description: The complete lighting installation within a shop unit, including track spotlights, display lighting, and emergency luminaires tailored to retail ambience.

name: HVAC Fan Coil Unit

name: Tenant Mechanical Ventilation System

name: Fit-Out Works

name: Shell & Core Construction

name: Shop Front Installation

name: Shopfitting & Joinery Installation

name: Tenant Electrical First & Second Fix

name: Service Charge Metering Installation

name: Retail Floor Tile / Flooring

name: Shop Front Aluminium Framing

name: Acoustic Partition Board

name: Intumescent Fire Seal

name: Shopfront Toughened Laminated Glass

name: Common Circulation Mall / Arcade

name: Back-of-House Service Corridor

name: Loading Dock / Delivery Area

name: Tenancy Storage Room

name: Owners Corporation / Management Body

name: Fire Detection & Alarm System (Tenancy)

name: Acoustic Insulation Material

name: Mechanical & Electrical (M&E) Installation

name: Canopy & Awning Installation
description: Structural fixing and commissioning of retractable or fixed shade structures over the outdoor terrace.

name: Outdoor Terrace Construction

name: Signage & Branding Installation
description: Fabrication and mounting of all external fascia signs, illuminated panels, and interior menu board systems.

name: Health & Safety / Food Hygiene Compliance Inspection

name: Refrigeration Equipment Installation

name: Health Department Inspection & Permitting

name: Storefront Framing & Glazing Installation

name: Commercial Kitchen Installation

description: A dedicated sink with running water and soap dispenser required by health codes for food-handler hygiene.

name: Utility Connection Panel
description: An access panel housing electrical, water, and gas hookups that supply the food stand's operational systems.

name: Storage Shelving
description: Stainless-steel or NSF-rated shelving units inside the stand for storing dry goods, packaging, and supplies.

name: Canopy or Shade Structure
description: An overhead covering (fabric awning, tensile canopy, or rigid roof) that shelters customers and operators from weather.

name: Waste Bin Enclosure
description: A screened or enclosed housing for customer-facing waste, recycling, and compost receptacles adjacent to the stand.

name: Queuing Lane
description: A defined pedestrian pathway or stanchion-guided corridor that organises customer queues in front of the stand.

name: Outdoor Dining Area
description: An adjacent seating zone furnished with tables and chairs for customers consuming food purchased at the stand.

name: Preparation Zone
description: The back-of-house area within or directly behind the stand reserved for food assembly, cooking, and plating.

name: Staff Circulation Path
description: The narrow passage behind the service counter allowing operators to move between cooking, storage, and service areas.

name: Kiosk (Food Kiosk)
description: A compact, fully enclosed permanent variant of a food stand with a sealed structure and integrated utility connections.

name: Food Truck Bay
description: A designated paved parking and utility-hookup space where mobile food trucks operate in lieu of a fixed stand.

name: Market Stall
description: A temporary or semi-permanent open-sided vendor booth typically used in farmers' markets or street fairs.

name: Concession Stand
description: A fixed food-service booth embedded within a stadium, arena, or entertainment venue serving high-volume crowds.

name: Pop-Up Food Stand
description: A rapidly deployable, short-term food service structure assembled for events and disassembled afterwards.

name: Stainless Steel Countertop
description: A hygienic, corrosion-resistant metal surface material used for food preparation and service counter tops.

name: Food-Safe Non-Slip Flooring
description: Slip-resistant, easy-to-clean flooring material (e.g., quarry tile or epoxy coating) required in food-handling zones.

name: Grease-Resistant Wall Cladding
description: Smooth, washable wall panel material (FRP or stainless steel) used in cooking areas to resist grease penetration.

name: Electrical Supply System
description: The wiring, circuit breakers, and outlets providing power to cooking appliances, lighting, and POS equipment.

name: LED Task Lighting System
description: Energy-efficient lighting fixtures providing adequate illumination over preparation, cooking, and service surfaces.

name: Foundation and Slab Construction
description: Pouring of a concrete slab or footings to anchor a permanent food stand and support equipment loads.

name: Utility Rough-In
description: Installation of embedded electrical conduit, water supply lines, and gas piping before finishes are applied.

name: Canopy or Awning Installation
description: Erection and anchoring of the overhead shade or weather protection structure above the food stand.

name: Equipment Installation and Commissioning
description: Placement, connection, and testing of cooking appliances, refrigeration units, and POS systems within the stand.

name: Health and Safety Inspection
description: Regulatory inspection by health authorities to verify compliance with food-handling, hygiene, and fire-safety codes before operation.

name: Signage and Branding Installation
description: Mounting of menu boards, logo panels, and wayfinding signs as part of the final fit-out of the food stand.

name: Grease Trap Installation
description: Placement of an interceptor device in the drain line to capture fats, oils, and grease before they enter the sewer system.

name: Nap Pod
description: An enclosed or semi-enclosed individual sleeping unit designed for short-term rest in public or shared environments.

name: Rest Lounge
description: A dedicated room or zone within a public building fitted with recliners, cots, or soft seating to facilitate brief sleep or rest.

name: Sleep Cabin
description: A compact, bookable private cabin with a flat sleeping surface, typically found in airports or transit hubs.

name: Recliner Chair
description: An ergonomic chair that reclines to a near-horizontal position to support comfortable rest without requiring a full bed.

name: Acoustic Privacy Screen
description: A sound-absorbing partition installed around sleeping areas to reduce ambient noise and increase perceived privacy.

name: Blackout Curtain or Blind
description: A light-blocking textile or blind used in sleeping zones to enable restful conditions regardless of external daylight.

name: Adjustable Ambient Lighting System
description: A controllable lighting system that allows dimming and colour-temperature adjustment to support circadian-friendly sleeping conditions.

name: HVAC Zoned Climate Control
description: A zoned heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning system that maintains optimal temperature and air quality specifically within sleeping areas.

name: White Noise or Soundmasking System
description: An electronic system that emits consistent broadband sound to mask disruptive noise and improve sleep quality in open environments.

name: Hygienic Surface Material
description: Antimicrobial or easy-clean materials applied to mattresses, headrests, and contact surfaces to maintain sanitation in shared sleeping spaces.

name: Memory Foam Mattress or Topper
description: A pressure-relieving foam layer placed on sleeping surfaces to improve comfort during short-term rest.

name: Booking and Access Control Kiosk
description: A self-service terminal or digital interface that allows users to reserve, pay for, and unlock individual sleeping units.

name: Lockers and Personal Storage
description: Secure storage units adjacent to sleeping areas where users can stow belongings while they rest.

name: Charging and Connectivity Station
description: Integrated power outlets, USB ports, and wireless charging pads built into or near sleeping units to keep personal devices powered during rest.

name: Sleeping Pod Installation Activity
description: The construction and fit-out activity involving structural fixing, electrical connection, and commissioning of prefabricated sleeping pods.

name: Acoustic Treatment Works
description: The construction activity of installing sound-absorbing panels, baffles, and seals to achieve target noise levels in rest areas.

name: FF&E Procurement and Installation
description: The activity of sourcing, delivering, and installing furniture, fixtures, and equipment specific to sleeping and rest functions.

name: Hygiene and Cleaning Protocol Implementation
description: The operational activity of establishing and commissioning regular sanitisation routines for shared sleeping surfaces and enclosures.

name: Wellness or Wellbeing Room
description: A broader multi-use recovery space within a workplace or public facility that encompasses quiet rest, meditation, and stress relief alongside sleeping.

name: Airport Transit Hotel Room
description: A compact, private hotel room located within an airside or landside terminal zone, designed for layover sleep and short stays.

name: Overnight Shelter Sleeping Area
description: A designated sleeping zone within a social or emergency shelter providing beds or mats for vulnerable populations needing overnight accommodation.

name: IfcFurniture (Sleep Unit)
description: The IFC classification for furnishing elements such as pods, cots, and recliners that constitute the sleeping unit within a building model.

name: IfcSpace (Rest Zone)
description: The IFC spatial element used to formally define and bound a dedicated rest or sleeping zone within the building information model.

name: Individual Building Unit
description: A single, self-contained building within the complex that functions independently but shares infrastructure or grounds with other units.

name: Shared Podium / Basement
description: A common below-grade or podium-level structure that serves multiple towers or blocks within the complex.

name: Central Courtyard
description: An open or semi-open communal outdoor area enclosed by surrounding buildings within the complex.

name: Pedestrian Circulation Spine
description: Internal pathways, arcades, or covered walkways that connect buildings and amenities across the complex.

name: Service Yard
description: A designated back-of-house area for deliveries, waste management, and maintenance activities serving the complex.

name: Amenity Block
description: A standalone or integrated facility offering shared services such as a gym, clubhouse, or concierge for complex occupants.

name: Landscape / Grounds
description: Soft and hard landscaped areas, gardens, and public realm spaces that form the setting of the complex.

name: Boundary Wall / Perimeter Fence
description: Structural enclosure elements that define the outer edge and security perimeter of the building complex.

name: Security Gatehouse
description: A controlled-access entry point structure managing vehicle and pedestrian ingress and egress to the complex.

name: Shared Structural Frame
description: A common structural grid or transfer structure that supports multiple building blocks within a unified complex.

name: Expansion Joint Assembly
description: Engineered joints that accommodate differential movement between adjacent structures within the complex.

name: Master Utility Tunnel / Culvert
description: An underground passage housing shared mechanical, electrical, and plumbing services distributed across the complex.

name: Shared MEP Infrastructure
description: Centralised mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems such as district cooling, power substations, and water mains serving the entire complex.

name: District Heating / Cooling Plant
description: A central energy plant providing thermal conditioning distributed to multiple buildings across the complex.

name: Site-Wide Electrical Distribution
description: High-voltage switchgear, transformers, and cable networks supplying power to all buildings within the complex.

name: Integrated Fire Protection Network
description: Complex-wide fire alarm, suppression, and evacuation systems coordinated across all buildings and shared spaces.

name: Campus Security & Access Control System
description: Unified CCTV, intercom, and electronic access management covering all buildings and entry points in the complex.

name: Site-Wide ICT / Data Network
description: Shared telecommunications, fibre backbone, and data infrastructure interconnecting all buildings in the complex.

name: Reinforced Concrete (Structural)
description: Primary structural material used for shared foundations, podium slabs, and cores across the complex.

name: Precast Concrete Cladding Panel
description: Factory-produced concrete facade elements applied uniformly or variably across building exteriors to unify the complex aesthetic.

name: Asphalt / Paving Material
description: Hard-surfacing material used for roads, car parks, and pedestrian routes within the complex grounds.

name: Master Planning & Site Layout
description: The design activity of establishing the overall arrangement, zoning, massing, and connectivity of all buildings within the complex.

name: Phased Construction Sequencing
description: Planning and executing the construction of the complex in defined stages to allow partial occupation while other phases are built.

name: Site Enabling & Bulk Earthworks
description: Large-scale ground preparation, excavation, and levelling activities carried out across the full complex site before individual building construction.

name: Shared Infrastructure Installation
description: The coordinated installation of site-wide utilities, drainage, and service tunnels prior to or alongside individual building construction.

name: Facade Coordination Across Buildings
description: Design and construction management activity ensuring visual and technical consistency of external envelopes across all buildings in the complex.

name: Commissioning & Integrated Systems Testing
description: The process of testing and verifying that all shared and building-level systems operate correctly as a unified complex.

name: Estate Management & FM Setup
description: Establishing facilities management protocols, service charge structures, and operational procedures for the complex as a whole.

name: Ground Floor / Level 1
description: The lowest occupiable story of a building, typically at or near grade level, counted as the first story.

name: Above-Grade Story
description: Any full story whose floor level is at or above the surrounding finished grade, directly contributing to the official story count.

name: Below-Grade Story / Basement Level
description: A story where the floor is below the finished grade line, which may or may not be counted depending on local code definitions.

name: Penthouse Level
description: A rooftop story set back from the building perimeter, sometimes excluded from story counts depending on height and area thresholds.

name: Mechanical / Plant Room Floor
description: A dedicated story housing HVAC, electrical, or other building-service equipment, which may be counted or excluded based on occupancy classifications.

name: Transfer Floor
description: A structural story containing large transfer beams or trusses that redirect loads from upper columns to fewer lower columns.

name: Refuge / Sky Lobby Floor
description: A dedicated story in high-rise buildings used as an emergency evacuation refuge or elevator transfer lobby, counted as a full story.

name: Split-Level Story
description: A floor arrangement where sections of the same story are offset by a half-level, complicating straightforward story counting.

name: Floor-to-Floor Height
description: The vertical distance between finished floor surfaces of consecutive stories, a key variable that determines overall building height per story count.

name: Floor-to-Ceiling Height (Clear Height)
description: The usable vertical clearance within a story from finished floor to finished ceiling, distinct from structural floor-to-floor height.

name: Vertical Circulation Core
description: The system of stairs, elevators, and escalators that connects all stories and whose design is directly driven by the number of stories.

name: Elevator / Lift System
description: Mechanical vertical transport whose capacity, speed, and quantity are engineered specifically to serve the total number of stories in the building.

name: Staircase System
description: The egress and circulation stair assemblies scaled and designed to span the full number of stories for life-safety compliance.

name: Building Height (Total)
description: The cumulative vertical measurement from grade to the highest occupied floor or roof, directly derived from story count and floor-to-floor heights.

name: Story Height Zoning Classification
description: The regulatory framework that assigns permitted building heights in stories or feet/meters for a given land-use zone.

name: High-Rise Classification
description: A code-based designation (typically 7+ or 10+ stories depending on jurisdiction) that triggers additional fire protection, structural, and egress requirements.

name: Mid-Rise Classification
description: An intermediate story-count category (often 4–12 stories) subject to its own set of fire, structural, and accessibility code requirements.

name: Low-Rise Classification
description: A building classification for structures of one to three or four stories, governed by the least restrictive set of height-driven code requirements.

name: Structural System Selection
description: The choice of structural framing strategy (e.g., moment frame, shear wall, core-and-outrigger) that is heavily influenced by the total number of stories.

name: Pressurized Stair Enclosure
description: A mechanically pressurized stairwell system required above certain story thresholds to keep egress paths smoke-free during a fire event.

name: Multi-Story Construction Activity
description: The phased construction process of sequentially erecting structural floors, facades, and fit-outs story by story, often using jump-form or slip-form techniques.

name: Floor-by-Floor Concrete Pour / Topping
description: The activity of placing and curing concrete for each successive structural slab, directly repeated for every story in cast-in-place construction.

name: Façade Installation per Story
description: The sequential installation of cladding, curtain wall, or window systems at each floor level as construction progresses upward.

name: Vertical MEP Riser Installation
description: The activity of running mechanical, electrical, and plumbing risers vertically through all stories, coordinated floor by floor.

name: Crane / Hoist Setup and Climbing
description: The erection, jump-climbing, and eventual dismantling of tower cranes or construction hoists to serve each new story as the building rises.

name: Storey Numbering Convention
description: The adopted naming or numbering scheme for stories (e.g., Ground/First floor, European vs. American convention) recorded in the building knowledge system for coordination.

name: Gross Floor Area (GFA) per Story
description: The total enclosed floor area measured at each individual story, aggregated across all stories to yield the building's total GFA.

name: Occupancy Load per Story
description: The calculated number of occupants assigned to each floor level, used for egress sizing and structural live-load design.

name: IFC IfcBuildingStorey
description: The IFC schema class that digitally represents each individual story of a building in a BIM model, enabling software interoperability across all story levels.

name: Covered Parking Structure
description: An enclosed or semi-enclosed parking facility that provides overhead protection from weather and environmental elements.

name: Multi-Story Parking Deck
description: A stacked parking structure with multiple levels, where upper floors shield lower ones and a roof shields the top level.

name: Carport
description: A semi-open roofed structure providing partial shielding for parked vehicles without full enclosure.

name: Basement Parking Level
description: A dedicated parking floor located below ground level, inherently shielded by surrounding earth and the building slab.

name: Mechanical Parking System
description: An automated or semi-automated lift-and-stack system that moves vehicles within a shielded enclosure to maximize space utilization.

name: Ventilation System
description: A mechanical or natural system designed to remove vehicle exhaust fumes and maintain air quality within an enclosed parking space.

name: Drainage & Waterproofing System
description: A system of drains, membranes, and coatings preventing water ingress and managing runoff within the parking enclosure.

name: Parking Roof Slab
description: The overhead concrete or steel deck that forms the primary weather shield over the parking area.

name: Parking Bay Marking
description: Painted or physical delineators on the floor that define individual parking stalls within the shielded space.

name: Shutter / Roller Door
description: A motorized or manual door securing the entrance to an enclosed parking area while allowing controlled vehicle access.

name: Speed Bump / Traffic Calming Device
description: Raised floor features used to slow vehicle speeds within the shielded parking area for safety.

name: Structural Excavation
description: The earthworks activity of digging out soil and rock to create the below-grade void for an underground shielded parking space.

name: Mechanical & Electrical Rough-In
description: The first-fix installation of conduits, ductwork, pipework, and cabling for all building services within the parking space.

name: Line Marking & Bay Layout
description: The finishing activity of applying paint or thermoplastic markings to define parking bays, traffic lanes, and pedestrian paths.

name: Commissioning of Safety Systems
description: The testing and sign-off process for fire suppression, ventilation, lighting, and security systems before the parking space is occupied.

name: Hallway
description: An interior passage within a building providing access between rooms and spaces.

name: Foyer
description: A transitional entrance space connecting the exterior entry to the main interior circulation network.

name: Vestibule
description: A small anteroom or buffer space at an entrance that provides thermal and acoustic separation.

name: Escalator Bay
description: The structural opening and surrounding zone accommodating an escalator between floor levels.

name: Ramp Zone
description: A sloped circulation space providing accessible or vehicular grade-change movement.

name: Exit Passageway
description: A protected egress corridor leading occupants safely from a building exit to the public way.

name: Skybridge / Link Bridge
description: An elevated enclosed walkway connecting two separate building volumes at upper levels.

name: Elevator (Lift) Installation
description: The mechanical car, guide rails, drive system, and cab that move people vertically.

name: Escalator Unit
description: A motorised moving stairway assembly providing continuous vertical people-flow between levels.

name: Handrail & Balustrade System
description: The continuous graspable rail and infill panel assembly providing fall protection along stairs and ramps.

name: Circulation Door Assembly
description: Doors—including fire doors, automatic sliding doors, and swing doors—controlling access along circulation routes.

name: Emergency Exit Hardware
description: Panic bars, push-pads, and exit devices that allow rapid egress under emergency conditions.

name: Floor Finish – Circulation
description: Wear-resistant, slip-rated surface materials such as polished concrete, terrazzo, or hard-wearing carpet applied to circulation floors.

name: Wall Finish – Circulation
description: Durable wall cladding and paint systems selected for high-traffic corridor and lobby surfaces.

name: Tactile Ground Surface Indicator (TGSI)
description: Raised-profile tiles or strips embedded in floors to guide vision-impaired users through circulation routes.

name: Non-Slip Stair Nosing
description: A contrasting-colour, slip-resistant edge profile fixed to stair treads to improve safety and visibility.

name: Circulation Space Planning
description: The design process of determining widths, paths, and flow capacities for all circulation routes in the building.

name: Egress & Life-Safety Analysis
description: Engineering assessment of evacuation travel distances, exit widths, and compliance with fire-safety codes.

name: Accessibility & Compliance Audit
description: Review and documentation of circulation routes against universal design and disability-access standards.

name: Wayfinding Strategy Development
description: The planning and design of signage, landmarks, and cues to support intuitive occupant navigation.

name: Staircase Construction
description: Structural formwork, casting or prefabrication, and finishing works to build a code-compliant stair flight.

name: Elevator Installation & Commissioning
description: Mechanical, electrical, and safety testing works to install and bring an elevator system into service.

name: Corridor Partitioning & Finishing
description: Framing, boarding, plastering, and decorating works that form and finish enclosed corridor walls.

name: Flooring Installation – Circulation Areas
description: Laying and fixing floor finishes, nosings, and TGSIs throughout all circulation routes.

name: People-Flow / Crowd Simulation
description: Computational modelling of occupant movement to optimise circulation widths and identify bottlenecks.

name: Building Egress & Fire Escape System
description: The code-mandated network of protected routes, exit doors, and discharge points for emergency evacuation.

name: Access Control System – Circulation
description: Electronic readers, turnstiles, and barriers that regulate authorised movement through controlled circulation zones.

name: Circulation Lighting System
description: The luminaire layout and control strategy providing adequate illumination and emergency lighting along all circulation routes.

name: Mechanical Ventilation – Circulation Zones
description: HVAC supply and extract provisions maintaining air quality and smoke control within corridors and lobbies.

name: Exterior Facade
description: The outer skin of the building, including cladding, curtain walls, and exterior finishes.

name: Office Floor
description: A typical floor level within the main building designated for office or workspace use.

name: Basement Level
description: Below-grade floor space used for parking, storage, or mechanical plant rooms.

name: Electrical Room
description: Secured space containing switchgear, distribution panels, and electrical infrastructure.

name: Building Automation System
description: Centralized control system managing lighting, HVAC, security, and energy usage intelligently.

name: Suspended Ceiling
description: A secondary ceiling hung below the structural slab to conceal services and improve acoustics.

name: Site Preparation
description: Earthworks, grading, and clearing activities carried out before construction of the building begins.

name: Structural Erection
description: Assembly and installation of the primary structural frame, including columns, beams, and floor slabs.

name: Street Furniture Zone
description: Designated lateral strip along the street accommodating benches, bins, bollards, and other urban furniture.

name: Planting Strip
description: Linear landscaped area integrated into the street for trees, shrubs, or ground-cover planting.

name: Bench / Seating
description: Fixed or movable seating element placed along the street for rest and social interaction.

name: Outdoor Dining / Café Terrace
description: Licensed area of the street surface given over to al-fresco restaurant or café seating.

name: Kiosk / Market Stall Pitch
description: Defined ground-level location reserved for temporary or permanent retail kiosks and market stalls.

name: Public Lighting System
description: Network of street luminaires, columns, and controls that illuminate the pedestrian street at night.

name: Street Lighting Column
description: Individual pole or mast that supports one or more luminaires along the pedestrian street.

name: Linear Drain / Channel
description: Continuous slot or grated channel set flush with the paving to intercept and redirect surface runoff.

name: Sub-base / Road Bed
description: Compacted granular or bound layer below the paving surface that provides structural load distribution and drainage.

name: Kerb / Edge Restraint
description: Upstand or flush edge unit that defines boundaries between the street surface and adjacent zones or planters.

name: Accessibility Ramp
description: Graded transition element that provides step-free access between different surface levels along the street.

name: Signage & Wayfinding System
description: Network of directional signs, maps, and information panels helping users navigate the pedestrian street and surroundings.

name: Public Art / Sculpture
description: Artistic installations or sculptures integrated into the street to enhance cultural identity and visual interest.

name: Bicycle Parking Stand
description: Fixed rack or hoop structure providing secure short-stay parking for bicycles along the street.

name: Waste & Recycling Bin
description: Fixed or semi-fixed receptacle for collecting litter and recyclable materials in the public realm.

name: Emergency Vehicle Access Route
description: Designated path within the pedestrian street engineered to bear emergency vehicle loads while remaining unobtrusive in normal use.

name: Loading Bay / Service Access
description: Time-restricted zone at the street edge permitting goods deliveries to adjacent retail or commercial units.

name: Retail Frontage Zone
description: Transitional strip directly in front of shops where display, signage, and canopies interact with the public street.

name: Canopy / Arcade
description: Overhead weather-protection structure extending from building facades over the pedestrian street.

name: Earthworks & Excavation
description: Site preparation work involving bulk excavation and grading to establish the correct formation level for the street.

name: Sub-base Compaction & Formation
description: Construction activity of laying and mechanically compacting granular sub-base material to the required bearing capacity.

name: Utility Diversion & Installation
description: Relocation or new installation of underground services prior to and during street construction.

name: Paving Laying & Jointing
description: Precision placement, bedding, and grouting of surface paving units to achieve levels, falls, and pattern.

name: Surface Reinstatement & Snagging
description: Final inspection, repair of defects, and cleaning of paving surfaces before public opening.

name: Fire Exit Passage
description: A dedicated egress route designed and maintained exclusively for emergency evacuation.

name: Skybridge
description: An enclosed or open elevated pedestrian bridge linking two separate building structures.

name: Loading Bay Access Corridor
description: A service passage connecting loading docks to internal circulation routes for goods movement.

name: Ceiling Finish
description: The overhead surface treatment of a thoroughfare, such as suspended tiles, plaster, or exposed concrete.

name: Door Assembly
description: A door, frame, and hardware unit controlling access and separation between thoroughfare and adjacent spaces.

name: Lighting Fixture
description: Artificial light fittings mounted to ceilings or walls of thoroughfares to ensure safe visibility for occupants.

name: Emergency Lighting Unit
description: Battery-backed luminaires that activate automatically upon power failure to illuminate egress paths.

name: HVAC Diffuser
description: An air distribution outlet in thoroughfare ceilings or walls supplying conditioned air for occupant comfort.

name: CCTV Camera
description: A surveillance camera installed along thoroughfares to monitor occupant movement and enhance building security.

name: Intercom Station
description: A communication device fixed within thoroughfares enabling voice or video contact between occupants and security.

name: Circulation System
description: The integrated network of passages, vertical connectors, and nodes that enables occupant movement throughout the building.

name: Egress System
description: The complete assembly of escape routes, exits, and associated hardware ensuring safe evacuation of a building.

name: Wayfinding System
description: A coordinated system of visual, tactile, and digital cues guiding occupants through complex building layouts.

name: Building Automation System (BAS) Integration
description: Automated controls linking lighting, HVAC, and security in thoroughfares for centralised monitoring and optimisation.

name: PA / Emergency Communication System
description: Speakers and control infrastructure installed in thoroughfares for broadcast of announcements and emergency alerts.

name: Thoroughfare Layout Planning
description: Design activity that determines the configuration, widths, and flow logic of all circulation routes within the building.

name: Accessibility Compliance Assessment
description: Evaluation activity verifying that thoroughfare dimensions, gradients, and features meet disability access regulations.

name: Wall and Ceiling Finishing
description: Application of plaster, paint, cladding, or other finishes to thoroughfare wall and ceiling surfaces.

name: Lighting Installation and Commissioning
description: Electrical installation and testing of general and emergency lighting fixtures across all thoroughfare areas.

name: Egress Route Testing and Certification
description: Formal inspection and sign-off by authorities verifying that all evacuation paths comply with life-safety codes.

name: Secondary Entrance
description: An auxiliary entry point providing additional access to a building, often used by staff or for service purposes.

name: Emergency Exit Entrance
description: A designated entry/exit space required by safety codes for rapid evacuation during emergencies.

name: Accessible Entrance
description: An entry point designed to comply with accessibility standards, accommodating users with mobility impairments.

name: Service Entrance
description: A dedicated entry space used for deliveries, maintenance, and back-of-house operations.

name: Entrance Canopy
description: An overhead roof-like structure projecting over an entrance to provide weather protection for users.

name: Entrance Door
description: The primary door assembly at a building entrance, which may be single, double, sliding, or revolving.

name: Door Hardware
description: Operational and security fittings on entrance doors including handles, locks, hinges, closers, and panic bars.

name: Entrance Step
description: A raised tread element at the threshold of an entrance managing the level transition between exterior and interior.

name: Entrance Ramp
description: An inclined surface at the entrance threshold providing step-free access in compliance with accessibility requirements.

name: Threshold
description: The bottom seal/strip at the base of a door opening that manages weather, acoustic, and fire separation at the entrance.

name: Entrance Flooring
description: Durable, slip-resistant floor finish materials used in entrance zones to withstand high foot traffic and moisture ingress.

name: Entry Mat / Grating System
description: A recessed or surface-mounted dirt-scraping and moisture-absorbing mat system installed at building entrances.

name: Entrance Glazing
description: Glass panels or curtain wall elements forming transparent or translucent walls and sidelights around an entrance.

name: Intercom / Video Entry System
description: A communication system at the entrance enabling remote visual and audio verification of visitors before granting access.

name: Entrance Lighting System
description: Dedicated interior and exterior luminaires providing safe illumination levels at entrance areas for safety and security.

name: Fire and Smoke Door System
description: A rated door assembly and control system at entrances that compartmentalises fire and smoke spread in an emergency.

name: Entrance Waterproofing
description: Waterproof membranes and sealants applied at entrance thresholds and below-grade entrance areas to prevent water ingress.

name: Entrance Wall Cladding
description: Exterior and interior finish materials applied to the walls flanking an entrance for aesthetics, durability, and weatherproofing.

name: Entrance Construction / Installation
description: The site activity covering structural openings, door frame fixing, door installation, and associated finishing works for entrances.

name: Entrance Fit-Out Works
description: The finishing and furnishing activity within entrance spaces including flooring, signage, mats, and hardware installation.

name: Access Compliance Inspection
description: A statutory inspection activity verifying that entrances meet accessibility, fire egress, and building code requirements.

name: Entrance Maintenance and Servicing
description: Routine upkeep activities for entrance doors, hardware, automatic systems, and finishes to ensure safe continued operation.

name: Security Assessment of Entrances
description: An evaluation activity that analyses entrance vulnerabilities and recommends physical or electronic security improvements.

name: IFC Space (Entrance Zone)
description: The IfcSpace class used to define and bound entrance, lobby, and vestibule spatial units within a BIM model.

name: IFC Opening Element
description: The IfcOpeningElement class representing the physical void cut into a wall or slab to accommodate an entrance door or gate.

name: Parking Stall
description: An individually marked area designated for parking a single vehicle.

name: Parking Lot Entrance/Exit
description: The designated ingress and egress points connecting the parking lot to the adjacent roadway or site.

name: Pavement Surface
description: The hardscape surface layer (asphalt or concrete) that forms the drivable and walkable area of the parking lot.

name: Pavement Markings
description: Painted or thermoplastic lines, symbols, and arrows applied to the pavement to delineate stalls and traffic flow.

name: Wheel Stops
description: Low concrete or rubber barriers placed at the front of parking stalls to prevent vehicles from overrunning the stall boundary.

name: Curb and Gutter
description: Concrete edging installed along the perimeter and islands of the parking lot to define boundaries and channel stormwater.

name: Parking Island / Landscaped Median
description: A raised or planted divider strip within the parking lot that separates rows of stalls and provides greenery.

name: Parking Lot Lighting
description: Pole-mounted or bollard light fixtures that illuminate the parking area for safety and security during low-light conditions.

name: Accessible (ADA/Handicap) Parking Stall
description: A wider, specially marked parking space with adjacent access aisle compliant with accessibility standards for disabled users.

name: EV Charging Station
description: Electrical supply equipment installed within a parking lot to charge electric vehicles.

name: Pedestrian Walkway / Crosswalk
description: A designated, often marked path within or across the parking lot that provides safe pedestrian access to the building entrance.

name: Fence or Perimeter Barrier
description: A fence, bollard line, or barrier installed around the parking lot boundary to control access and define the site edge.

name: Subbase / Base Course
description: The compacted aggregate layer beneath the pavement surface that provides structural support and load distribution.

name: Subgrade Preparation
description: Earthwork activity involving excavation, grading, and compaction of native soil to establish a stable foundation for the parking lot.

name: Pavement Installation
description: The construction activity of placing and compacting asphalt or pouring concrete to form the finished parking lot surface.

name: Pavement Marking Application
description: The activity of applying paint, thermoplastic, or epoxy markings to the finished pavement surface for stalls and traffic guidance.

name: Lighting Installation
description: The activity of erecting light poles, running electrical conduit, and commissioning fixtures to provide parking lot illumination.

name: Landscaping and Planting
description: Site activity involving placement of trees, shrubs, and groundcover within parking islands and perimeter buffers to meet aesthetic and environmental requirements.

name: Surface Sealing and Maintenance
description: Periodic application of sealcoat or crack filler to the pavement surface to extend its service life and prevent deterioration.

name: Cart Corral / Storage Area
description: A fenced or marked enclosure within a parking lot for collecting and storing shopping carts.

name: IFC Parking Space
description: The IFC schema class (IfcSpace with occupancy type 'PARKING') used to model individual parking spaces in BIM authoring tools.

name: IFC Site Pavement
description: Represented via IfcCovering or IfcPavement in IFC4x3, used to model the hardscape pavement layer of a parking lot in a BIM model.

name: Grading and Earthworks
description: Reshaping and levelling the ground surface to correct elevations, slopes, and drainage patterns across the site.

name: Erosion Control Layer
description: Protective ground covering such as geotextile fabric, mulch, or riprap applied to prevent soil loss from wind or water.

name: Compacted Fill Zone
