description: A designated area where imported or re-used soil material is placed and mechanically compacted to engineered specifications.

name: Contaminated Soil Remediation Area
description: A demarcated site zone where polluted or hazardous soils are excavated, treated, or isolated to meet environmental standards.

name: Surface Drainage Channel
description: Open or lined channel designed to collect and convey surface runoff away from repaired site areas.

name: French Drain / Sub-surface Drain
description: Perforated pipe and gravel trench system installed below grade to redirect groundwater and relieve hydrostatic pressure.

name: Geotextile Membrane
description: Permeable synthetic fabric used for separation, filtration, reinforcement, or drainage within repaired ground layers.

name: Gabion Basket
description: Wire-mesh cage filled with stone used for slope stabilisation, embankment repair, and erosion control.

name: Topsoil Reinstatement
description: Stripping, stockpiling, and re-spreading of fertile topsoil to restore agricultural or landscape capability after ground works.

name: Pavement Reinstatement
description: Removal and reconstruction of hard-surfaced areas — roads, paths, or yards — disturbed during excavation or repair work.

name: Landscaping and Revegetation
description: Planting of grass, shrubs, or trees on repaired ground to stabilise soil, restore ecology, and improve visual amenity.

name: Site Hoarding / Temporary Fencing
description: Temporary boundary enclosure erected around the repair zone to ensure safety, security, and site demarcation.

name: Settlement Monitoring Point
description: Instrumented marker or datum installed to measure post-repair ground movement and long-term settlement behaviour.

name: Utility Reinstatement Zone
description: Area where buried services — pipes, cables, ducts — are relocated, repaired, or reinstated following site remediation.

name: Aggregate Base Course
description: Compacted layer of crushed stone or gravel placed over sub-grade to provide a stable load-bearing platform for surfaces.

name: Ground Improvement Piling
description: Array of stone columns, micro-piles, or driven piles used to reinforce weak sub-soils and transfer loads to competent strata.

name: Environmental Impact Assessment Zone
description: Defined boundary within which ecological surveys, contamination testing, and environmental compliance activities are conducted.

name: South-Facing Terrace
description: An elevated outdoor platform oriented to maximise southern solar exposure for warmth and light.

name: South-Facing Balcony
description: A projecting platform attached to an upper floor, oriented south to capture sunlight throughout the day.

name: South-Facing Courtyard
description: An open-air enclosed or semi-enclosed outdoor area positioned on the southern aspect of a building.

name: South-Facing Patio
description: A ground-level paved outdoor area on the southern side of a building, optimised for solar gain and outdoor living.

name: South-Facing Garden
description: A planted outdoor area oriented southward to maximise sunlight availability for planting and amenity.

name: South-Facing Roof Terrace
description: An accessible rooftop outdoor space designed and oriented to benefit from maximum southern solar exposure.

name: South-Facing Deck
description: A timber or composite decked outdoor platform on the southern elevation of a building.

name: South-Facing Pergola
description: An open overhead structure on the southern aspect providing partial shade while allowing low-angle winter sun penetration.

name: South-Facing Louvred Canopy
description: An adjustable louvred overhead screen on a southern outdoor space providing controllable solar shading.

name: Solar Shading Device
description: A fixed or adjustable element such as a brise-soleil or overhang that manages solar heat gain on south-facing outdoor and façade areas.

name: Balustrade / Railing System
description: A safety barrier system installed around elevated south-facing outdoor spaces such as balconies and roof terraces.

name: Paving / Hard Landscaping
description: Hard surface materials such as stone, concrete, or porcelain used to finish south-facing outdoor floor areas.

name: Decking Boards
description: Timber or composite board material forming the walking surface of south-facing deck areas.

name: Thermal Mass Flooring
description: Dense materials such as concrete or stone that absorb solar energy during the day and release heat in south-facing outdoor or transitional spaces.

name: Planting / Green Infrastructure
description: Vegetation, planting beds, and associated growing media used within south-facing outdoor spaces for amenity and microclimate benefits.

name: Photovoltaic (PV) Array
description: Solar panels installed on south-facing outdoor structures or roofs to harvest maximum solar radiation for electricity generation.

name: Solar Thermal Collector
description: A panel system on south-facing roofs or structures that captures solar energy to heat water or support building heating systems.

name: External Drainage System
description: The complete network of drains, gullies, and downpipes managing surface water from south-facing outdoor areas to the foul or surface water sewer.

name: Passive Solar Design Strategy
description: An integrated design approach exploiting the south-facing orientation to reduce heating loads through solar gain, thermal mass, and natural ventilation.

name: Landscape & Hard Landscaping Works
description: Construction activities involving the laying of paving, planting, and finishing of south-facing outdoor spaces.

name: Waterproofing & Tanking Works
description: Application of waterproof membranes and protective coatings to south-facing balconies, terraces, and roof decks during construction.

name: Solar Panel Installation
description: Mounting, wiring, and commissioning of PV or solar thermal panels on south-facing structures or rooftops.

name: Drainage & Gulley Installation
description: Excavation, laying, and connection of drainage channels and gullies serving south-facing outdoor areas.

name: Shading Structure Erection
description: The construction and installation of pergolas, canopies, or louvred screens on south-facing outdoor spaces.

name: Orientation Solar Analysis
description: A design-stage assessment using sun-path modelling to optimise the layout and elements of south-facing outdoor spaces.

name: IfcSpace (Outdoor Zone)
description: The IFC class used to model and represent defined south-facing outdoor spatial zones within a BIM environment.

name: IfcSlab (Terrace/Balcony)
description: The IFC class representing the structural slab element forming the floor of a south-facing balcony or terrace.

name: IfcShadingDevice
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcBuildingElement.

name: IfcCovering (Paving/Decking)
description: The IFC class used to model surface finish layers including paving and decking in south-facing outdoor floor areas.

name: Rooftop Garden
description: A planted outdoor space located on the roof of a building, providing greenery and recreational area.

name: Plaza
description: A large, open paved outdoor area designed for public gathering and social interaction.

name: Atrium (Outdoor)
description: An open-air central void or lightwell within a building footprint that functions as a positive outdoor space.

name: Colonnade
description: A row of evenly spaced columns supporting a roof or entablature that edges and defines outdoor space.

name: Arcade (Covered Walkway)
description: A covered passageway with arches or columns along the edge of a building that transitions between inside and outside.

name: Pergola
description: An overhead structure of posts and cross-beams providing partial shade and defining an outdoor room.

name: Trellis
description: A lattice framework supporting climbing plants, used to create enclosure and vertical definition in outdoor spaces.

name: Raised Planter
description: An elevated planting bed that defines edges, provides greenery, and adds spatial enclosure to outdoor areas.

name: Paving
description: Hard surface material such as stone, brick, or concrete used to define and finish the floor of outdoor spaces.

name: Soft Landscaping
description: Planting, turf, and ground-cover materials that provide greenery, biodiversity, and sensory quality to outdoor space.

name: Drainage System (Outdoor)
description: A system of channels, gullies, and soakaways that manages surface water runoff from outdoor paved and planted areas.

name: Boundary Enclosure
description: Walls, fences, hedges, or railings that define the edges of an outdoor space, contributing to its sense of enclosure and safety.

name: Shade Structure
description: A canopy, sail, or tensile structure providing solar shading and weather protection over outdoor activity areas.

name: Outdoor Furniture
description: Fixed or loose benches, tables, and chairs that support human activity and occupancy of outdoor spaces.

name: Landscape Design
description: The professional design activity that shapes the layout, planting, and material palette of an outdoor space.

name: Soft Landscaping Installation
description: The planting of trees, shrubs, turf, and ground cover as part of completing an outdoor space.

name: Boundary Construction
description: The building of walls, fences, or railings that enclose and define the perimeter of an outdoor space.

name: Water Feature Installation
description: The construction and commissioning of fountains, rills, or ponds as focal elements within an outdoor space.

name: Microclimate Analysis
description: An analytical activity assessing wind, sun, shade, and thermal comfort to optimise the design of outdoor spaces.

name: IfcSpace (Outdoor)
description: The IFC class used to model and represent defined outdoor spatial zones within a building information model.

name: Skylight Array
description: A series of overhead glazed openings designed to flood interior spaces with natural daylight from above.

name: Clerestory Window Band
description: A continuous row of high-level windows positioned near the roofline to admit diffused light deep into the space.

name: Light Shelf
description: A horizontal reflective surface mounted at mid-height on a façade to redirect sunlight onto the ceiling and further into the interior.

name: Structural Wing Canopy
description: The primary overhead canopy structure that forms the wing-like silhouette and supports the glazing and shading elements.

name: Translucent Roof Panel
description: Semi-transparent cladding panels used across the roof surface to diffuse sunlight while maintaining weather protection.

name: Solar Shading Louvre
description: Adjustable or fixed external fins that modulate direct solar gain entering the glazed wing surfaces.

name: Tensile Membrane Sail
description: Lightweight fabric or ETFE membrane stretched between structural masts to create the curved wing profile and filter light.

name: Daylighting Control System
description: An automated system of sensors, motorised blinds, and dimming controls that optimises interior daylight levels throughout the day.

name: Natural Ventilation System
description: A passive or hybrid ventilation strategy using operable glazed sections and thermal buoyancy to manage air quality beneath the wing.

name: Artificial Lighting Integration System
description: LED and accent lighting infrastructure integrated into the structural frame to supplement daylight after dark while complementing the wing aesthetic.

name: Photovoltaic Glazing System
description: Building-integrated PV cells embedded within the translucent roof or façade panels to generate renewable energy from the wing surface.

name: Transition Colonnade
description: A covered walkway along the perimeter of the wing where structural columns frame views and mediate between interior and exterior.

name: Glazed Courtyard
description: An enclosed outdoor or semi-outdoor area defined by the extending wing forms, softened by natural planting and diffused light.

name: Mezzanine Gallery Level
description: An intermediate floor level overlooking the central atrium that benefits directly from the overhead light admitted by the wing.

name: High-Performance Structural Glass
description: Toughened, laminated, or fritted glass specified for the wing glazing to balance transparency, solar control, and structural performance.

name: ETFE Foil Cushion
description: Lightweight ethylene tetrafluoroethylene inflated cushions used as a translucent, thermally efficient alternative to glass in the wing canopy.

name: High-Tensile Steel Cable
description: Slender tensioned cables used in conjunction with the wing canopy frame to resist wind uplift and maintain structural form.

name: Reflective Interior Finish
description: High-albedo paint, polished concrete, or metallic cladding applied to interior surfaces to maximise the distribution of admitted daylight.

name: Daylighting Design & Simulation
description: Computational modelling and physical mock-up testing to optimise the wing geometry and glazing specification for target daylight levels.

name: Structural Steelwork Fabrication & Erection
description: Off-site fabrication and on-site assembly of the primary steel or aluminium wing frame elements using crane and specialist rigging.

name: Membrane Tensioning & Commissioning
description: The controlled pre-stressing and adjustment of tensile membrane or cable elements to achieve the designed wing profile and load capacity.

name: Solar Shading Commissioning
description: Testing and calibration of motorised louvre or blind systems to ensure correct solar angle tracking and occupant comfort performance.

name: Post-Occupancy Daylighting Evaluation
description: On-site measurement of illuminance levels and occupant satisfaction surveys conducted after building handover to verify design intent.

name: Biophilic Design Integration
description: The deliberate incorporation of planting, water features, and natural materials within the light-filled wing space to enhance occupant wellbeing.

name: Solar Radiation Analysis
description: Climate-based modelling of annual solar exposure on the wing surfaces to inform orientation, shading strategy, and thermal performance.

name: Acoustic Treatment of Glazed Enclosure
description: Specialist absorptive linings, baffles, or resonators installed within the wing volume to control reverberation in the hard-surfaced glazed space.

name: Underground Tunnel Connector
description: A below-grade passageway that connects two or more buildings, allowing pedestrian or service movement without surface exposure.

name: Shared Structural Transfer Deck
description: A horizontal structural platform that bridges and distributes loads between two adjacent building cores or towers.

name: Shared Podium Base
description: A common low-rise platform structure at ground or lower levels upon which multiple towers or wings of connected buildings sit.

name: Inter-Building Atrium
description: A shared enclosed courtyard or glazed void space positioned between and connecting two or more buildings, acting as a common interior environment.

name: Connecting Lobby
description: A transitional lobby space located at the junction of two buildings that manages pedestrian flow and serves as a shared arrival point.

name: Shared Service Corridor
description: A utility and maintenance corridor running between connected buildings to route MEP services and allow staff movement without public access.

name: Integrated MEP Bridge Distribution System
description: A coordinated mechanical, electrical, and plumbing network that runs across connection elements to serve all linked buildings from shared or distributed plant rooms.

name: Unified Fire Compartmentation System
description: A fire safety strategy that defines and enforces compartment boundaries and smoke control zones across the junction points of connected buildings.

name: Shared BMS (Building Management System)
description: A centralised or federated building automation platform that monitors and controls HVAC, lighting, and security across all connected building assets.

name: Common Structural Grid Coordination
description: An engineered alignment of structural grids between adjacent buildings to enable seamless load transfer and connection detailing.

name: Inter-Building Data & Communications Network
description: A dedicated cabling, fibre-optic, or wireless infrastructure layer that links IT, telecom, and security systems across all buildings in the complex.

name: Structural Steel Connection
description: High-strength steel members, plates, and fixing assemblies used to physically join structural frames of separate building bodies.

name: Fire-Rated Glazing Panel
description: Glazed units with certified fire resistance used at connection interfaces and shared atria to maintain compartmentation while preserving transparency.

name: Flexible Expansion Joint Sealant
description: Elastic, weather-resistant sealant compounds applied at movement joints between buildings to prevent water ingress and maintain airtightness.

name: Acoustic Isolation Material
description: Resilient pads, barriers, and insulation used at connection interfaces to prevent sound and vibration transmission between linked buildings.

name: Interface Coordination & Design (IFC-BIM)
description: A design and coordination process using Building Information Modelling to resolve geometric, structural, and service clashes at the interface of connected buildings.

name: Differential Settlement Monitoring
description: Ongoing structural surveying and sensor-based monitoring to detect and manage uneven settlement between the foundations of adjacent connected buildings.

name: Connection Joint Inspection & Maintenance
description: Periodic physical inspection and remediation of expansion joints, seals, and bridging elements to ensure long-term structural and weathertight performance.

name: Multi-Building Phased Construction Sequencing
description: Planning and managing the construction order across multiple connected buildings to safely permit simultaneous or sequential building works without conflict.

name: Cross-Building Fire Evacuation Drill
description: A coordinated emergency preparedness exercise that tests evacuation routes, refuge areas, and communication systems spanning all connected buildings.

name: Shared Basement & Parking Structure
description: A common below-ground level providing parking, storage, and plant space that structurally and functionally underpins multiple connected buildings above.

name: Mixed-Use Complex
description: A broader urban development typology where connected buildings host multiple programmatic uses such as residential, commercial, and retail within a single integrated precinct.

name: IfcBuildingStorey (Shared Level)
description: An IFC entity representing a storey level that is common to or shared across multiple connected building instances within the same site model.

name: IfcRelConnectsElements
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcRelConnects.

name: Linear Corridor
description: A long, narrow passage running the full length of the house connecting all rooms along a single axis.

name: Narrow-Span Structural Frame
description: A structural framing system designed for minimal width spans typical of elongated building footprints.

name: End-Gable Wall
description: The short terminal wall at each end of the long axis, typically featuring windows or entrance doors.

name: Skylight / Roof Light
description: Overhead glazing introduced along the roof plane to bring natural light deep into the narrow interior.

name: Single-Loaded Corridor Layout
description: A spatial arrangement where rooms open off one side of a central spine corridor to maximise daylight on the other side.

name: Double-Loaded Corridor Layout
description: A spatial arrangement where rooms are arranged on both sides of a central spine, common in deeper long-thin plans.

name: Open-Plan Living Zone
description: A wide, unpartitioned living, dining, and kitchen area occupying one end of the linear plan.

name: Rear Garden / Courtyard
description: An outdoor amenity space accessed from the rear elevation of the elongated plan.

name: Terrace House
description: A row of attached long-thin dwellings sharing party walls along their length, the most common urban variant.

name: Shotgun House
description: A vernacular American single-storey variant where rooms are aligned sequentially front-to-back with no corridor.

name: Narrow Townhouse
description: A multi-storey urban dwelling with a very tight frontage, distributing the long-thin plan vertically across floors.

name: Villa Extension / Rear Addition
description: A linear extension appended to an existing dwelling that creates or extends a long-thin configuration.

name: Staircase Tower
description: A vertical circulation element typically located at mid-span or at one end to serve upper floors without breaking the linear flow.

name: Longitudinal Roof Structure
description: A pitched or flat roof spanning across the short dimension and running continuously along the long axis of the house.

name: Long-Span Floor Joist System
description: A floor structure engineered to span the narrow width efficiently while accommodating the extended length.

name: Natural Ventilation Strategy
description: A passive ventilation system exploiting through-flow between the two short end elevations and any courtyard openings.

name: Passive Solar Orientation
description: The deliberate alignment of the long elevation to face south (or north in southern hemisphere) to maximise solar gain.

name: Daylighting System
description: A coordinated set of roof lights, light wells, and glazed internal partitions to distribute daylight throughout the deep plan.

name: Light Well
description: A narrow vertical void cut through the building section to admit daylight and ventilation to interior rooms lacking external walls.

name: Masonry Brick
description: Clay or concrete brick commonly used for the long party walls and gable ends of traditional long-thin terrace construction.

name: Structural Insulated Panel (SIP)
description: A composite panel material used for walls and roof, providing structure and insulation in the thin-wall depths common in narrow houses.

name: Site Survey & Setting Out
description: The surveying activity that establishes the precise linear boundaries and orientation of the narrow plot before construction begins.

name: Party Wall Agreement Negotiation
description: The legal and consultative process of agreeing shared-wall construction terms with adjoining owners on either long side.

name: Demolition of Existing Rear Extension
description: The controlled removal of a previous addition to enable a new linear rear extension to be constructed.

name: Foundation Construction on Narrow Plot
description: The excavation and pouring of strip or pad foundations constrained by limited access width on either side of the long building.

name: Roof Light Installation
description: The fitting of factory-made or bespoke roof-light units into the longitudinal roof plane to admit top-light.

name: Internal Wall Removal (Spatial Rationalisation)
description: The structural alteration activity of removing cross-walls or partitions to open up the linear sequence of spaces.

name: Linear Services Run Installation
description: The routing of plumbing, electrical, and HVAC services along the long axis spine, typically concealed in ceiling or floor voids.

name: Narrow-Plot Urban Infill Development
description: The planning and construction process of building a new dwelling on a gap site between existing party walls.

name: IFC Wall (IfcWall)
description: The IFC class representing both the long party walls and short gable walls that define the long-thin house envelope.

name: IFC Roof (IfcRoof)
description: The IFC class capturing the longitudinal roof geometry spanning the narrow width of the house.

name: IFC Opening Element (IfcOpeningElement)
description: The IFC class representing apertures cut through walls and roof planes for windows, doors, and roof lights in the narrow elevations.

name: Security Intercom System
description: Audio/video communication system allowing remote verification of visitors before granting entry.

name: Automatic Door Operator
description: Electromechanical device enabling doors to open and close automatically for accessibility and convenience.

name: Entrance Steps
description: Stepped approach structure providing level changes between the exterior ground and the entrance threshold.

name: Accessible Ramp
description: Sloped pathway alongside or replacing steps to ensure wheelchair and mobility-aid access compliant with accessibility standards.

name: Entrance Mat / Matwell
description: Recessed or surface-mounted mat system at the threshold to trap dirt and moisture from footwear.

name: Flooring – Entrance
description: Durable, slip-resistant floor finish material selected specifically for the high-traffic entrance zone.

name: Glazing / Curtain Wall
description: Large-area glass elements or curtain-wall system forming the transparent façade of the entrance zone.

name: Interstitial Weatherstripping
description: Sealing strips applied to door edges and frames to prevent drafts, water, and noise infiltration.

name: Threshold Plate
description: Transition strip fixed at the base of the entrance door to seal the gap between door and floor finish.

name: Fire Exit / Egress Door
description: Secondary or combined door at the entrance zone specifically rated and designated for emergency evacuation.

name: Panic Hardware / Push Bar
description: Crash-bar device mounted on egress doors enabling rapid exit without a key in emergency situations.

name: Letterbox / Mail Slot
description: Aperture or slot in or adjacent to the entrance door for delivery of postal mail without requiring entry.

name: Building Directory Board
description: Display board listing tenants or departments and their locations, typically positioned near the main entrance.

name: Intercom / Video Door Phone
description: Wall-mounted unit combining doorbell, speaker, and camera functions for two-way visitor communication.

name: Façade Cladding – Entrance Zone
description: Exterior finish material applied to the wall surfaces immediately surrounding the entrance for aesthetic and weather protection.

name: Entrance Door Installation
description: Construction activity involving the fitting and commissioning of the entrance door assembly within its frame.

name: Entrance Landscaping
description: Horticultural and hardscaping works shaping the external approach and planting around the main entrance.

name: Waterproofing & Weatherproofing Works
description: Application of sealants, membranes, and coatings to prevent moisture ingress at the entrance threshold and canopy.

name: Security System Commissioning
description: Testing and activation activity ensuring access control, CCTV, and intercom systems are fully operational at handover.

name: Sunken Garden Area
description: A below-grade outdoor zone partially recessed into the ground, forming the defining characteristic of the half-hidden spatial experience.

name: Garden Terrace
description: A stepped or leveled outdoor platform adjacent to the sunken area, providing a transitional zone between ground level and the hidden garden.

name: Boundary Hedge or Planting Screen
description: Dense vegetation used along the garden perimeter to visually conceal or partially screen the garden from street or exterior views.

name: Garden Entry Staircase
description: A descending stair element connecting the upper grade to the sunken garden floor level.

name: Garden Entry Ramp
description: An accessible sloped pathway providing an alternative descent into the below-grade garden area.

name: Garden Perimeter Fence or Wall
description: A low-height enclosure element defining the garden edges while allowing partial visual connection to the surroundings.

name: Landscape Planting Bed
description: Designated soil zones within the garden for cultivated plantings, shrubs, or ground cover.

name: Garden Paving or Hardscape
description: Surface material such as stone, brick, or concrete pavers used to finish walkable areas within the sunken garden.

name: Subsurface Drainage System
description: A below-ground network of drains, channels, and sumps designed to manage stormwater in the recessed garden area.

name: Garden Irrigation System
description: A piped or drip-feed water supply system serving planted beds and lawn areas within the garden.

name: Water Feature or Reflecting Pool
description: A fountain, rill, or still pool element integrated into the garden design to enhance the secluded garden atmosphere.

name: Garden Seating Area
description: A dedicated sub-zone within the garden containing benches, furniture, or built-in seating for outdoor occupation.

name: Pergola or Garden Structure
description: An overhead lattice or canopy structure within the garden providing partial shade and contributing to the enclosed feel.

name: Privacy Screen or Trellis
description: A vertical element supporting climbing plants or providing direct visual screening to reinforce the garden's hidden character.

name: Garden Soil and Growing Medium
description: Engineered or natural substrate placed in planting beds to support healthy plant growth in the enclosed environment.

name: Earthwork and Excavation
description: Site excavation works required to create the below-grade depression that forms the sunken garden volume.

name: Retaining Wall Construction
description: The structural construction activity of forming, pouring, or assembling the walls that retain earth around the sunken garden.

name: Garden Paving Installation
description: The laying and finishing of hard surface materials across the garden floor and pathways.

name: Courtyard Garden
description: A closely related enclosed outdoor space type that shares the walled, intimate character of a half-hidden garden but sits at grade level.

name: Ha-Ha Wall
description: A recessed landscape design element using a vertical drop and ditch to create an invisible boundary, closely related to the sunken garden concept.

name: Secret Garden
description: A variant typology characterised by strong enclosure and restricted visibility, sharing the concealed and intimate qualities of the half-hidden garden.

name: Green Roof Garden
description: A related elevated planted space that, like the half-hidden garden, separates occupants from the surrounding public realm using level change.

name: IfcWall (Retaining)
description: The IFC schema class representing the retaining wall components enclosing the sunken garden in a BIM environment.

name: Airlock
description: A double-door sealed chamber that prevents air exchange between conditioned interior spaces and the outside environment.

name: Canopy / Porte-cochère
description: A covered overhead structure projecting from the building facade that shelters the immediate approach and drop-off zone.

name: Entry Plaza
description: An exterior paved open area directly fronting the entrance used for pedestrian assembly and wayfinding.

name: Ramp Approach
description: An accessible sloped pathway leading to the entrance door to accommodate mobility-impaired users.

name: Entry Door Assembly
description: The complete door unit at the building entry including frame, leaf, hardware, and seals that controls access and environmental separation.

name: Swing Door
description: A hinged door panel that pivots on a vertical axis and is the most common manual entry door type.

name: Bi-folding Entry Door
description: A door system whose panels fold back on themselves to create a wide, unobstructed opening at the entry.

name: Weather Stripping
description: Flexible sealing material fitted around door perimeters to prevent air, water, and dust infiltration.

name: Panic Bar / Crash Bar
description: A horizontal push-bar exit device that allows emergency egress without requiring grip or prior knowledge of the latch mechanism.

name: Access Control Reader
description: An electronic device (card, fob, or biometric) mounted at the entrance to authenticate and grant or deny entry.

name: Intercom / Video Doorbell
description: An audio-visual communication device enabling remote identification and admission of visitors before unlocking the entry.

name: Entryway Mat / Grating
description: A recessed or surface-mounted mat or grid system that removes dirt and moisture from footwear at the point of entry.

name: Sidelight / Transom Glazing
description: Fixed or operable glazed panels flanking or above the entry door that introduce natural light into the transition zone.

name: Curtain Wall Entry Section
description: A non-load-bearing glazed facade system integrated with the entrance opening that provides weather protection and visual transparency.

name: Overhead Sensor / Motion Detector
description: A ceiling- or lintel-mounted sensor that detects occupant presence to trigger automatic doors or lighting.

name: Signage and Wayfinding Panel
description: Visible directional or informational signs installed at the entry zone to guide occupants to interior destinations.

name: Letterbox / Parcel Locker
description: A secure receptacle integrated into the entry zone for the receipt and collection of mail and deliveries.

name: Security Glazing
description: Laminated or tempered glass specified for entry assemblies to resist impact, forced entry, or ballistic threats.

name: Structural Steel Header
description: A steel beam spanning the entry opening to carry superimposed loads above the door or glazed assembly.

name: Aluminium Extrusion Frame
description: Extruded aluminium profiles used to construct thermally broken door and curtain wall frames at the entry.

name: Concrete Entry Slab
description: A reinforced concrete platform forming the structural floor of the entrance approach and vestibule.

name: Fire Egress System
description: A coordinated set of fire-rated doors, alarms, and signage ensuring safe and rapid evacuation through the entry zone.

name: HVAC Infiltration Control
description: Mechanical heating, ventilation, and air-curtain equipment installed at the entry to maintain interior climate despite frequent door operation.

name: Intercom and Door-release System
description: An integrated wired or wireless system linking visitor calling stations to interior stations and electric door strikes for remote entry control.

name: Threshold and Weatherseal Installation
description: The trade activity of fitting threshold bars and perimeter seals to ensure airtight and watertight closure of the entry assembly.

name: Structural Opening Formation
description: The demolition or formwork activity of creating the correctly sized and lintel-supported opening in the building structure for the entry assembly.

name: Entry Paving and Landscaping
description: The external works activity of laying hard and soft landscaping elements to define and finish the pedestrian approach to the entrance.

name: Facade Waterproofing at Entry
description: The application of membranes and sealants around the entry frame perimeter to prevent water ingress at the facade-to-door junction.

name: IfcOpeningElement
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction.

name: Driveway
description: A paved or surfaced path connecting a public road to a building's parking or entry area.

name: Parking Deck
description: An above-grade multi-level structure dedicated to vehicle parking.

name: Parking Barrier / Boom Gate
description: A controlled horizontal bar mechanism regulating vehicle entry and exit at access points.

name: Turntable Platform
description: A motorised rotating platform allowing vehicles to reverse direction without manoeuvring in tight spaces.

name: Car Lift
description: A mechanical vertical-transport system raising or lowering vehicles between floor levels.

name: Parking Guidance System
description: A sensor-based electronic system directing drivers to available parking spaces within a facility.

name: Ventilation System (Parking)
description: A mechanical air-extraction and supply system controlling fume levels in enclosed vehicle areas.

name: Drainage System (Parking)
description: A network of channels, gullies, and sumps managing surface water and vehicle fluid runoff in parking areas.

name: Pavement / Surface Finish
description: The hard-wearing surface material—such as concrete, asphalt, or resin—applied to vehicle circulation and parking areas.

name: Wheel Stop
description: A low physical barrier fixed to the parking surface to prevent vehicles from overrunning the designated bay.

name: Security Camera (CCTV)
description: A video-surveillance system monitoring vehicle and pedestrian activity within parking and access areas.

name: Fire Suppression System (Parking)
description: A sprinkler or gaseous fire-suppression installation providing fire safety coverage in enclosed vehicle areas.

name: Structural Slab (Parking Deck)
description: A reinforced concrete slab forming the load-bearing floor and ceiling of each parking level.

name: Waterproofing Membrane (Underground Parking)
description: A continuous impermeable layer applied to below-grade structures to prevent water ingress into parking areas.

name: Pedestrian Walkway / Footpath
description: A dedicated safe-passage zone separating pedestrians from vehicle traffic within a parking facility.

name: Site Works & Excavation
description: Ground preparation and excavation works required to form the base or subterranean volume of a parking facility.

name: Garage Door Installation
description: The fixing, alignment, and commissioning of garage door assemblies including tracks, motors, and safety sensors.

name: Waterproofing Works
description: Application and testing of waterproofing membranes and sealants to below-grade or exposed parking structures.

name: Line Marking & Signage Installation
description: Painting, thermoplastic application, and erection of directional signs and parking-bay markings within the facility.

name: Public Plaza
description: A large, open, publicly accessible outdoor area at ground level serving as a civic gathering point within or adjacent to a building complex.

name: Semi-Public Courtyard
description: An enclosed or partially enclosed outdoor space shared by a defined group of residents or users, bridging fully public and private realms.

name: Communal Garden
description: A shared outdoor green space accessible to a community of building occupants for recreation and social interaction.

name: Private Terrace
description: An outdoor space directly attached to a single dwelling or unit, accessible only to its occupants.

name: Private Balcony
description: A small projecting platform off an individual unit providing personal outdoor space above ground level.

name: Podium Deck
description: An elevated open platform above a building's podium level that provides landscaped outdoor space for building residents.

name: Entrance Forecourt
description: A transitional open space at the building entrance that mediates between the public street and the private interior.

name: Arcade
description: A covered passage open to the street on at least one side, providing sheltered pedestrian movement while remaining semi-public.

name: Access Path Network
description: The interconnected system of pathways and routes that link open spaces of different privacy levels across a development.

name: Landscape Planting System
description: The designed arrangement of planting, trees, and soft landscaping that defines and enriches open spaces at every hierarchy level.

name: Boundary Enclosure Element
description: Walls, fences, hedges, or planters that physically define the transition between open spaces of different privacy levels.

name: Landscape Design and Layout
description: The planning and design activity that establishes the spatial hierarchy, zoning, and character of open spaces within a development.

name: Open Space Masterplanning
description: The strategic activity of allocating, sizing, and connecting open spaces across a site to achieve a coherent public-to-private hierarchy.

name: Soft Landscaping Works
description: Construction activities involving planting of vegetation, turf laying, and soil preparation within open spaces.

name: Hard Landscaping Works
description: Construction activities covering installation of paving, steps, retaining walls, and other hard surface elements in open spaces.

name: Boundary Treatment Installation
description: The construction activity of erecting fences, walls, gates, and railings that delineate the boundaries between open space tiers.

name: Outdoor Furniture and Fixtures Installation
description: The activity of placing benches, lighting, litter bins, and other street furniture to support usability of open spaces.

name: IfcSpace (Open Space)
description: The IFC class used to model and represent discrete open space zones within a building information model.

name: Open-Air Central Court
description: An unroofed central void within or adjacent to a building that serves as the primary gathering and light-distribution heart of the courtyard complex.

name: Semi-Enclosed Transitional Zone
description: A partially covered edge space between the courtyard floor and the surrounding building volume that mediates indoor and outdoor conditions.

name: Planted Courtyard Garden
description: A landscaped interior ground plane within the court featuring trees, shrubs, or ground cover that supports biodiversity and microclimate regulation.

name: Reflecting or Fountain Pool
description: A water feature integrated into the courtyard floor that contributes to evaporative cooling, acoustic character, and sensory vitality.

name: Arcade / Colonnade Walkway
description: A covered perimeter passage formed by columns or arches that provides shaded circulation around the courtyard perimeter.

name: Upper-Level Gallery / Balcony Tier
description: An elevated open corridor or balcony ring overlooking the courtyard that extends usable floor area and visual connection between floors.

name: Load-Bearing Perimeter Wall
description: The structural wall enclosing the courtyard that carries floor and roof loads while defining the spatial boundary of the court.

name: Colonnade Column
description: A vertical structural element supporting the arcade roof or upper gallery, typically expressed architecturally as a rhythm-setting element of the courtyard facade.

name: Courtyard Paving / Ground Surface
description: The finished floor surface of the courtyard—stone, tile, brick, or permeable paving—that manages drainage, heat absorption, and pedestrian comfort.

name: Permeable Drainage Layer
description: A sub-surface drainage assembly beneath courtyard paving that channels rainwater away and supports sustainable water management.

name: Courtyard Roof / Glazed Atrium Cover
description: An optional overhead enclosure—glass, ETFE, or tensile membrane—that allows daylight while protecting the court from weather.

name: Operable Skylight or Lantern
description: A ventilating roof element positioned above the court that can be opened to expel hot air and draw fresh air through the stack effect.

name: Planting Bed and Tree Pit
description: Contained soil volumes within the courtyard floor or raised planters that support mature tree and shrub growth.

name: Irrigation and Water-Feature Pipework
description: The network of supply, return, and drainage pipes serving courtyard fountains, pools, and planted areas.

name: Boundary Screen Wall / Mashrabiya
description: A decorative or privacy screen element—lattice, perforated panel, or carved screen—that filters views and sunlight at the courtyard edge.

name: Staircase Linking Court to Upper Galleries
description: A stair structure set within or adjacent to the courtyard that provides vertical circulation while remaining visually part of the court experience.

name: Natural Ventilation System (Stack/Cross)
description: A passive airflow system exploiting the courtyard's thermal chimney effect to ventilate surrounding rooms without mechanical energy.

name: Courtyard Daylighting System
description: A coordinated arrangement of reflective surfaces, light wells, and glazing designed to distribute natural light deep into adjacent spaces.

name: Stormwater Harvesting System
description: An integrated system of channels, cisterns, and filtration units that collects and reuses rainwater falling into the courtyard.

name: Landscape and Planting System
description: The totality of soil profiles, irrigation, drainage, and plant species selection that sustains living vegetation within the court.

name: Acoustic Comfort System
description: Surfaces, water sounds, and soft landscaping coordinated to manage reverberation and provide pleasant ambient sound within the court.

name: Microclimate Thermal Regulation System
description: A holistic assembly of shading devices, water features, vegetation, and material choices engineered to moderate the courtyard's internal temperature.

name: Terracotta / Ceramic Tile
description: Fired clay tile used as courtyard paving or wall cladding, offering rich colour, texture, and moderate thermal mass.

name: Structural Masonry (Brick / Stone)
description: Load-bearing masonry forming the perimeter walls of the courtyard, contributing thermal mass and the enclosure's architectural character.

name: Structural Timber (Columns / Screens)
description: Hardwood or engineered timber used for colonnade columns, screens, and gallery balustrades in courtyard construction.

name: Glazing / Structural Glass
description: High-performance glass used for atrium roofs, courtyard enclosures, or screen walls to admit light while providing weather protection.

name: ETFE or Tensile Membrane
description: Lightweight translucent roofing material stretched over a frame to cover a courtyard with minimal structural intrusion and high light transmission.

name: Planted Groundcover and Turf
description: Low-growing vegetation forming a living ground plane within the court that cools the microclimate and supports biodiversity.

name: Rammed Earth or Adobe Wall Panel
description: Earthen wall material used in vernacular and contemporary courtyard buildings for its high thermal mass and low embodied carbon.

name: Courtyard Design and Space Planning
description: The architectural design process of proportioning, orienting, and programming the courtyard void in relation to the surrounding building.

name: Excavation and Ground Preparation
description: Site earthworks to form the courtyard level, including bulk excavation, grading, and preparation of sub-base layers.

name: Structural Frame Erection (Perimeter)
description: Construction of the load-bearing walls, columns, and beams that define and enclose the courtyard volume.

name: Paving and Hard Landscaping Installation
description: Laying of courtyard floor finishes, including bedding mortar, stone or tile setting, and joint grouting.

name: Soft Landscaping and Planting Works
description: Soil preparation, tree planting, and establishment of ground-cover vegetation within the courtyard.

name: Glazed Roof / Atrium Cover Installation
description: Erection of the steel or aluminium frame and fixing of glazing or membrane panels to form a covered courtyard atrium.

name: Drainage and Stormwater Works
description: Installation of surface channels, gullies, underground pipes, and cisterns to manage courtyard rainwater.

name: Facade and Screen Wall Finishing
description: Application of render, tile, masonry detailing, or decorative screens to the internal courtyard-facing elevations.

name: Commissioning of Passive Ventilation
description: Testing and adjustment of openings, vents, and stack-effect pathways to verify the courtyard's natural ventilation performance.

name: IfcSpace (Courtyard)
description: The IFC space entity used to model and tag the courtyard void as a distinct bounded space within the building information model.

name: IfcWall (Courtyard Perimeter)
description: The IFC wall entity applied to the internal-facing enclosure walls that bound and define the courtyard space.

name: IfcColumn (Arcade)
description: The IFC column entity used to model colonnade or arcade columns that structure the courtyard perimeter walkway.

name: IfcRoof (Atrium Cover)
description: The IFC roof entity representing any overhead cover—glass, membrane, or solid—placed over the courtyard opening.

name: IfcOpeningElement (Courtyard Void)
description: The IFC opening entity that formally registers the courtyard void cut through the building volume in the BIM model.

name: Upper Roof Tier
description: The highest level of a cascading roof arrangement, forming the uppermost sheltered plane and defining the overall roof ridge height.

name: Intermediate Roof Tier
description: A mid-level roof plane that steps down from the upper tier, creating the characteristic cascading visual rhythm.

name: Lower Roof Tier
description: The lowest plane in the cascade sequence, typically covering the outermost or lowest-floor building volume.

name: Roof Step Junction
description: The structural and weatherproofing detail where one roof tier transitions vertically down to the next lower tier.

name: Stepped Parapet Wall
description: A low protective wall at the edge of each roof tier that follows the stepping profile of the cascade and prevents water ingress at tier changes.

name: Roof Drainage Downpipe
description: A vertical pipe that carries collected rainwater from each roof tier level down to the ground drainage system.

name: Roof Framing Structure
description: The load-bearing structural framework (rafters, purlins, trusses) that supports each individual roof tier in the cascade.

name: Roof Cladding
description: The outer surface material (tiles, metal sheets, shingles) applied to each roof tier providing weathering and aesthetic finish.

name: Eave Overhang
description: The projecting portion of each roof tier beyond the supporting wall, providing shade and weather protection to the facade below.

name: Structural Bearing Wall
description: A load-bearing wall that supports the roof structure of an individual tier and transfers gravity and lateral loads to the foundations.

name: Snow Guard
description: A device fixed to the surface of each roof tier to prevent sudden shedding of accumulated snow onto lower tiers or occupied areas below.

name: Roof Drainage Installation
description: The activity of fixing gutters, valley linings, and downpipes to manage rainwater collection and discharge across all tiers.

name: Roof Cladding Installation
description: The finishing activity of laying or fixing the external roof surface material on each tier according to the design specification.

name: Stepped Building Form
description: The overall massing concept of a building whose successive floor or volume setbacks directly give rise to the cascading roof profile.

name: Solar Photovoltaic Panel Array
description: Photovoltaic modules mounted on the angled or flat surfaces of roof tiers to generate on-site renewable electricity.

name: Roof Sheathing
description: Structural panels or boards fixed to rafters or trusses to form a continuous substrate for the finished roofing membrane or tiles.

name: Roof Tile
description: An individual unit of clay, concrete, or slate fixed in overlapping courses to form the weather-resistant outer skin of a pitched roof.

name: Green Roof
description: A roof system incorporating growing medium and vegetation layers over a waterproofing membrane to provide ecological and thermal benefits.

name: Snow Guard System
description: Devices or rails fixed to the roof surface to retain accumulated snow and prevent sudden dangerous shedding onto occupants below.

name: Photovoltaic Roof System
description: Solar panel arrays integrated into or mounted on the roof to generate electricity from solar irradiance.

name: Roof Framing
description: The construction activity of cutting, assembling, and erecting the structural timber or steel members that form the roof skeleton.

name: Roof Waterproofing Application
description: The trade activity of installing membranes, felts, or liquid-applied coatings to make the roof surface impervious to water.

name: Roof Tiling and Cladding
description: The activity of fixing tiles, slates, or metal sheets in the correct lapping pattern to form the finished external weathering layer.

name: Roof Inspection and Maintenance
description: Periodic examination and remedial works carried out to identify and repair defects, ensuring long-term weather-tightness and structural safety.

name: Skylight / Rooflight
description: A glazed opening set into the roof plane to admit daylight and ventilation into the spaces below.

name: IfcMember (Rafter/Purlin)
description: The IFC schema class used to represent linear structural members within the roof framing, such as rafters, purlins, and ridge beams.

name: Filter Fabric
description: A geotextile sheet placed between the growing medium and drainage layer to prevent fine particles from clogging the drainage system.

name: Growing Medium
description: A lightweight engineered substrate, distinct from standard soil, designed to support plant growth while minimising structural load.

name: Structural Reinforcement
description: Additional beams, columns, or slab enhancements added to the roof structure to bear the extra loads imposed by the garden assembly and occupants.

name: Safety Railing
description: A guardrail system installed at exposed edges to prevent falls by occupants and maintenance personnel.

name: Access Stairway
description: A dedicated stair structure providing safe pedestrian access from the building interior to the roof garden level.

name: Roof Hatch / Access Door
description: A weatherproof opening unit set into the roof or wall that allows controlled entry to the roof garden space.

name: Paving / Decking
description: Hard-surface tiles, pavers, or timber decking used to create walkways and seating areas within the garden.

name: Green Roof Assembly
description: The complete layered build-up—membrane, drainage, filter, substrate, and vegetation—considered as an engineered system distinct from an accessible garden.

name: Intensive Roof Garden
description: A deep-substrate variant supporting large shrubs, trees, and diverse planting, designed for regular human occupancy and recreation.

name: Extensive Green Roof
description: A shallow, low-maintenance variant with sedum or moss cover, typically not designed for regular human access.

name: Semi-Intensive Green Roof
description: A mid-depth variant that balances plant diversity with manageable structural load and occasional human access.

name: Rooftop Urban Farm
description: A productive variant of the roof garden dedicated to growing food crops, often incorporating raised beds and hydroponic systems.

name: Growing Medium Placement
description: The activity of transporting and spreading the engineered substrate to specified depths across the prepared roof area.

name: Structural Load Assessment
description: An engineering analysis activity that calculates and verifies the additional dead and live loads imposed by the full garden assembly on the roof structure.

name: Roof Garden Maintenance
description: Ongoing operational activities including weeding, pruning, fertilising, and system inspection to keep the garden healthy and functional.

name: Outdoor Furniture and Amenities
description: Fixed or movable benches, planters, tables, and similar elements that support human use and comfort in the garden space.

name: Arcade Arch
description: The curved or pointed arch spanning between columns or piers that defines the open bays of the arcade.

name: Pier
description: A solid masonry or concrete vertical support used in place of or alongside columns to carry arcade arches.

name: Arcade Vault
description: The ceiling structure—barrel, groin, or ribbed—spanning the covered walkway between columns and the backing wall.

name: String Course
description: A continuous horizontal projecting band running along the facade at impost level, tying together the tops of arches or columns.

name: Impost Block
description: The transitional block or capital element placed atop a column or pier from which an arch springs.

name: Keystone
description: The wedge-shaped voussoir at the crown of an arch that locks the arch structure together.

name: Arcade Soffit
description: The exposed underside surface of the arcade arches and vault visible to pedestrians walking beneath.

name: Backing Wall
description: The solid wall running along the inner side of the arcade that encloses the covered walkway and separates it from interior spaces.

name: Paving / Floor Finish
description: The ground-level surface material—stone, tile, or concrete—used to finish the arcade walkway floor.

name: Column Shaft
description: The vertical cylindrical or polygonal body of a column between its base and capital, carrying compressive arcade loads.

name: Column Base
description: The moulded foot of a column that distributes its load onto the plinth or stylobate.

name: Stylobate / Plinth
description: The continuous raised platform or step upon which the arcade columns or piers are set.

name: Fascia / Entablature
description: The horizontal band of mouldings above the columns or arches carrying the arcade's upper wall or roof structure.

name: Balustrade / Parapet
description: A low protective barrier placed at the open face of an upper-level arcade gallery to prevent falls.

name: Shopfront / Tenant Unit
description: A commercial unit opening directly onto the arcade walkway, the primary driver of retail arcade typologies.

name: Pedestrian Walkway / Gallery
description: The covered linear circulation space sheltered by the arcade, providing weather-protected passage for pedestrians.

name: Upper-Level Gallery
description: A secondary arcade tier stacked above the ground-level walkway, often providing additional retail or residential units.

name: Glazed Arcade Roof
description: A glass-and-steel or glass-and-timber roof system spanning the full width of an enclosed shopping arcade to admit daylight.

name: Drainage and Gutter System
description: The rainwater collection and discharge infrastructure integrated into the arcade roof and floor to manage stormwater.

name: Stone / Masonry
description: Dressed stone, brick, or concrete masonry used to construct columns, piers, arches, and backing walls of the arcade.

name: Structural Steel / Cast Iron
description: Ferrous metal used for slender columns, arch ribs, and glazed roof framing, characteristic of 19th-century commercial arcades.

name: Decorative Tilework
description: Ornamental ceramic or mosaic tiles applied to arcade floors, dados, and spandrels as a finishing material.

name: Arch Formwork and Centering
description: The temporary timber or steel falsework erected to support masonry or concrete arches during construction until they are self-supporting.

name: Column Installation
description: The erection and plumbing of prefabricated or cast-in-situ columns, including base-plate fixing and capital placement.

name: Vault Construction
description: The forming, casting, or laying of vaulted ceiling structures over the arcade walkway, including shuttering and curing.

name: Glazed Roof Installation
description: The assembly of structural glazing frames and glass panes to form the weather-tight overhead covering of an enclosed arcade.

name: Stone Carving / Ornamental Masonry
description: The craft cutting and dressing of decorative stone elements such as capitals, keystones, and moulded cornices.

name: Floor Laying
description: The installation of paving slabs, tiles, or other floor finishes on the arcade walkway surface.

name: Facade Restoration / Conservation
description: Specialist repair and cleaning of historic arcade facades, including re-pointing, stone replacement, and protective coating.

name: Shopping Arcade
description: A fully enclosed, glazed-roof retail passageway lined with shopfronts on both sides, a distinct commercial typology derived from the arcade form.

name: Portico
description: A colonnaded porch forming the entrance bay of a building, sharing arcade geometry but functioning as a threshold rather than a through-passage.

name: Cloister Walk
description: A covered arcaded walkway enclosing a courtyard in monastic or collegiate buildings, representing the ecclesiastical arcade typology.

name: Travelator / Moving Walkway
description: A horizontal or slightly inclined motorised belt walkway used to assist pedestrian movement across long distances.

name: Exit Route / Means of Escape
description: A designated protected circulation path that safely directs occupants to a place of safety during an emergency.

name: Fire Exit Door
description: A self-closing, fire-rated door positioned along an escape route to compartmentalise fire while allowing egress.

name: Pedestrian Pathway (External)
description: A paved or surfaced outdoor route that connects building entrances, parking areas, and external amenities.

name: Covered Walkway / Colonnade
description: A sheltered external or semi-external passage with overhead cover that protects occupants from weather while moving between destinations.

name: Bridge Link / Skybridge
description: An elevated enclosed or open walkway connecting two separate buildings or building sections above ground level.

name: Door (Circulation)
description: A movable barrier controlling passage between circulation spaces, including swing, sliding, and automatic variants.

name: Automatic Door Opener
description: A motorised or sensor-activated mechanism that opens and closes doors automatically to assist accessibility and flow.

name: Floor Finish (Circulation)
description: The surface material applied to floors in circulation zones, selected for durability, slip resistance, and wayfinding cues.

name: Slip-Resistant Flooring
description: Flooring material with enhanced surface texture or coating to reduce the risk of falls in high-traffic or wet circulation areas.

name: Circulation Zone Layout Planning
description: The design activity of organising and dimensioning paths, nodes, and destinations to achieve efficient and safe occupant movement.

name: Egress Modelling / Evacuation Simulation
description: A fire-safety design activity that simulates occupant movement along escape routes to verify adequate exit capacity and timing.

name: Handrail Installation
description: The construction activity of fixing handrail and balustrade assemblies to staircases, ramps, and elevated walkways.

name: Stair Construction
description: The building activity encompassing the fabrication and installation of stair flights, landings, and associated structural elements.

name: IfcCirculationElement
description: The IFC schema class representing physical elements that form part of the circulation system within a built environment model.

name: IfcSpace (Circulation)
description: An IFC Space instance typed or zoned as a circulation area, used to track net circulation area in building models.

name: Straight Path
description: A linear, uninterrupted walkway or corridor that runs in a single direction without bends or curves.

name: Curved Path
description: A walkway or circulation route that follows a gentle arc or sinuous curve rather than a straight line.

name: L-Shaped Path
description: A path that makes a single 90-degree turn, forming an L configuration between two zones.

name: T-Shaped Path
description: A three-way junction path where one main corridor meets another at a perpendicular intersection.

name: U-Shaped Path
description: A path that doubles back on itself in a U form, often used to connect parallel spaces or floors.

name: Z-Shaped Path
description: A path with two offset parallel segments connected by a diagonal or perpendicular link, forming a Z profile.

name: Radial Path
description: A circulation route that emanates outward from a central hub or node to peripheral spaces.

name: Spiral Path
description: A helical or continuously turning path that gains or loses elevation while revolving around a central axis.

name: Grid Path Network
description: An orthogonal system of intersecting paths forming a regular grid pattern for efficient multi-directional circulation.

name: Branching Path
description: A path that splits from a single spine into multiple sub-paths, resembling a tree branch structure.

name: Loop Path
description: A closed circular or oval circulation route that returns to its starting point without dead ends.

name: Diagonal Path
description: A walkway oriented at an oblique angle to the principal axes of a building or site layout.

name: Transition Node
description: A widened or articulated junction space where two or more path segments meet, change direction, or intersect.

name: Path Edge Treatment
description: The physical boundary element—such as a kerb, handrail, or planting strip—that defines and contains the edges of a path.

name: Path Surface Material
description: The finish or paving material applied to the walking surface of a path, such as concrete, asphalt, or tile.

name: Path Width Variation
description: Intentional changes in the clear width of a path segment to accommodate pinch points, gathering areas, or accessibility requirements.

name: Waypoint Marker
description: A signage or physical landmark element placed along a path to aid orientation and wayfinding.

name: Path Gradient / Slope
description: The longitudinal incline of a path segment, critical for accessibility compliance and drainage design.

name: Path Layout Planning
description: The design activity of determining the geometric form, alignment, and connectivity of paths within a building or site.

name: Path Construction / Paving
description: The construction activity of laying the base course and surface finish of a path according to the specified shape and alignment.

name: Path Accessibility Audit
description: An inspection activity that evaluates whether path shapes meet universal design and disability access standards.

name: Path Marking and Wayfinding Installation
description: The activity of installing floor markings, signage, and tactile indicators that reinforce path geometry and guide users.

name: Pedestrian Desire Line Analysis
description: A study activity that observes or predicts the natural routes people take to inform optimal path shape and placement.

name: Ramp Path
description: An inclined path segment designed to connect floor levels or overcome grade changes accessibly.

name: Dead-End Path
description: A path that terminates without a return loop, requiring users to retrace their steps—relevant for egress and safety analysis.

name: IFC Spatial Zone
description: The IFC class used to represent defined spatial zones or path extents within a building information model.

name: IfcSpace (Path Geometry)
description: The IFC element that models an individual path as a bounded space with geometric shape attributes in a BIM environment.

name: Facade Cladding
description: The outer skin or surface layer applied to the building front, including materials such as brick, stone, glass, metal panels, or composite systems.

name: Cornice
description: A horizontal decorative or functional molding projecting along the top of the facade to cap the building front and manage water runoff.

name: Signage Zone
description: The designated area on the building front allocated for commercial or identity signage, regulated by setback and illumination standards.

name: Window Openings
description: Fenestration elements embedded in the facade wall, providing daylight, ventilation, and visual connection between interior and exterior.

name: Weather Barrier System
description: Membranes, flashings, and sealants integrated into the front wall assembly to prevent water and air infiltration.

name: Columns & Pilasters
description: Vertical structural or decorative elements on the building front that articulate bays, support canopies, or express architectural rhythm.

name: Spandrel Panels
description: Opaque infill panels between vision glazing bands on multi-story facades, concealing floor slabs and mechanical elements.

name: Exterior Lighting Fixtures
description: Mounted luminaires on the building front that provide security, wayfinding, and aesthetic illumination at night.

name: Rainscreen System
description: A ventilated cladding system that creates a drainage cavity between the outer cladding and the wall substrate to manage moisture.

name: Facade Inspection & Cleaning
description: Scheduled maintenance activity involving visual inspection, pressure washing, or chemical cleaning of the building front surfaces.

name: Facade Repair & Restoration
description: Remediation activity addressing cracks, spalling, sealant failure, or damaged panels on the building front to restore performance and appearance.

name: Recessed Entry Alcove
description: A setback zone at the building front that shelters the entrance threshold and creates a transitional space between the public realm and interior.

name: Street-Level Plinth Zone
description: The base section of the building front at pedestrian level, often differentiated in material or expression from the upper facade.

name: Pedestrian Flow Zone
description: A defined area within a building or site where the movement and volume of foot traffic is monitored and analyzed.

name: Occupancy Zone
description: A spatial subdivision used to track the number of people present at any given time for safety and comfort planning.

name: Egress Path
description: A designated route providing safe exit for building occupants during normal use or emergency evacuation.

name: Congregation Area
description: An open space intended to accommodate temporary gatherings or high-density pedestrian activity such as lobbies or plazas.

name: Queuing Zone
description: A demarcated area where occupants are expected to wait in line, requiring dedicated space allocation per person.

name: People Counter Sensor
description: An electronic device installed at entrances or key nodes to automatically count and record pedestrian throughput.

name: Occupancy Sensor
description: A sensor that detects the presence of people within a defined space to enable real-time density monitoring.

name: Turnstile / Access Gate
description: A physical barrier component that controls and counts individual pedestrian entries and exits at controlled access points.

name: Crowd Management System
description: A building-wide platform that aggregates sensor data to model, predict, and actively manage pedestrian density levels.

name: Video Analytics / CCTV System
description: A camera-based system using computer vision to track, count, and analyze pedestrian movement patterns in real time.

name: Floor Marking & Pedestrian Lane Material
description: Durable floor surface treatments such as painted lines or tactile strips used to delineate pedestrian lanes and queue boundaries.

name: Acoustic Absorption Material
description: Sound-dampening materials applied in high-density pedestrian spaces to manage noise levels generated by large crowds.

name: Pedestrian Traffic Impact Study
description: A pre-design or planning-stage analysis that models expected pedestrian volumes and their effect on space layout and capacity.

name: Occupancy Load Calculation
description: An engineering activity that determines the maximum number of occupants a space can safely accommodate per code requirements.

name: Crowd Simulation Modelling
description: A computational activity using agent-based or fluid-dynamics models to simulate pedestrian movement and identify congestion risk.

name: Sensor Calibration & Commissioning
description: The on-site activity of configuring and verifying counting and occupancy sensors to ensure accurate density measurement.

name: Post-Occupancy Pedestrian Audit
description: A structured observation and data-collection exercise conducted after building occupation to evaluate real-world pedestrian flow against design intent.

name: Egress Compliance Inspection
description: A regulatory inspection activity confirming that egress paths and capacity comply with life-safety codes relative to occupant density.

name: IfcSpace (Pedestrian Zone)
description: The IFC schema entity used to represent and exchange pedestrian-designated spatial zones within a BIM model.

name: IfcSensor (OccupancySensor)
description: The IFC schema entity representing occupancy and people-counting sensor objects within a federated building model.

name: Nook Seating Alcove
description: A recessed, semi-enclosed seating area carved into a wall or building volume to encourage informal gathering or focused individual use.

name: Reading Corner
description: A compact, quiet sub-space within a larger room furnished and lit specifically to support sustained reading or study.

name: Play Nook
description: A child-scaled enclave embedded within a floor plan designed to stimulate imaginative or physical play.

name: Collaboration Pod
description: A small, semi-private enclosure accommodating two to six people for short-duration teamwork or discussion.

name: Maker Bench Station
description: A dedicated worktop-level pocket space equipped for hands-on making, crafting, or light fabrication tasks.

name: Display Ledge Recess
description: A shallow wall recess sized to exhibit objects, artwork, or signage as part of the spatial experience.

name: Contemplation Corner
description: An intimate, acoustically buffered pocket intended for quiet reflection, meditation, or sensory decompression.

name: Window Seat Bay
description: A projecting or recessed bay at window level providing a built-in seat that frames views and daylight.

name: Built-in Bench
description: A fixed seating element integrated into the structure or millwork of an activity pocket to define and activate the space.

name: Canopy or Overhead Definition Element
description: A lowered ceiling, soffit, or canopy structure that psychologically encloses the pocket and differentiates it from the surrounding space.

name: Partial-Height Partition Wall
description: A low or mid-height wall used to demarcate an activity pocket while maintaining visual connectivity to adjacent areas.

name: Recessed Shelving Unit
description: Built-in shelving set into a wall cavity within or beside a pocket to store materials, books, or display items.

name: Task Lighting Fixture
description: A focused luminaire — pendant, wall-mounted, or recessed — positioned to illuminate the specific activity occurring in the pocket.

name: Acoustic Lining Panel
description: Sound-absorbing surface treatment applied to walls, ceiling, or floor of the pocket to control noise and improve comfort.

name: Integrated Power and Data Outlet
description: Electrical and data connection points embedded in the pocket's surfaces to support technology-enabled activities.

name: Soft Flooring Insert
description: A distinct floor finish — rug, carpet tile, or raised platform — used within the pocket to signal its boundary and add comfort.

name: Sliding or Folding Enclosure Screen
description: A movable partition that allows the pocket to be fully opened to the wider space or enclosed for privacy on demand.

name: Raised Platform Base
description: A stepped or elevated floor structure that elevates the pocket zone, reinforcing territorial definition and spatial interest.

name: Upholstered Cushion System
description: Custom-fitted seat and back cushions integrated with built-in bench or window seat elements for occupant comfort.

name: Timber Millwork Lining
description: Warm-toned wood panelling or joinery applied to the interior surfaces of a pocket to create a cosy, tactile character.

name: Acoustic Foam or Felt
description: Porous, sound-absorbing material used as wall or ceiling cladding within a pocket to dampen reflected noise.

name: Fabric Wall Covering
description: Textile-based surface material that adds softness, colour, and acoustic absorption to the pocket's enclosing surfaces.

name: Glazing (Partial)
description: Glass panels used selectively in pocket enclosures to allow borrowed light and visual connection while maintaining spatial separation.

name: Durable Cushion Foam
description: High-resilience foam core used in built-in seating elements to provide lasting comfort under repeated occupant use.

name: Pocket Layout Design and Space Planning
description: The design process of identifying, sizing, and distributing activity pockets within a floor plan to support programmatic diversity.

name: Structural Niche or Recess Formation
description: Construction activity of forming wall recesses or bay projections in structure to create the physical shell of each pocket.

name: Millwork and Joinery Fabrication
description: Shop or site fabrication and installation of custom cabinetry, benches, shelving, and lining elements that constitute the pocket.

name: Specialist Lighting Installation
description: Electrical rough-in and fixture installation for task and ambient lighting circuits dedicated to each activity pocket.

name: Data and Power Rough-In
description: First-fix installation of conduit, cabling, and back-boxes within pocket walls and floors before finishes are applied.

name: Soft Furnishing and Cushion Fit-Out
description: Final-fix activity of installing custom cushions, upholstery, and soft goods that complete the pocket's functional character.

name: Post-Occupancy Pocket Performance Review
description: Evaluation activity assessing how effectively activity pockets are used after building occupation to inform future design iterations.

name: IfcSpace (Activity Pocket Instance)
description: The IFC schema class used to model each discrete activity pocket as a bounded, named space within a building information model.

name: IfcWall (Partial-Height)
description: IFC wall entity used to model the low or partial-height partition elements that bound activity pockets spatially.

name: IfcCovering (Acoustic)
description: IFC class capturing acoustic lining panels and fabric wall coverings applied to the surfaces of activity pocket enclosures.

name: Lighting System (Zoned Task Circuit)
description: An independently switched or dimmed lighting circuit serving a cluster of activity pockets to allow occupant control of ambiance.

name: Low-Voltage Data Distribution System
description: The structured cabling and wireless access-point network ensuring reliable connectivity at every technology-enabled activity pocket.

name: HVAC Micro-Zone Supply
description: A dedicated or branch supply-and-return ventilation arrangement providing thermal comfort within partially enclosed pocket volumes.

name: Seating Tread
description: The horizontal stepped surface that serves as both a stair tread and a seating platform for occupants.

name: Riser Panel
description: The vertical face between seating treads that provides structural enclosure and defines the step height.

name: Handrail / Guardrail
description: Safety rail running along the sides or aisles of stair seats to prevent falls and assist with circulation.

name: Aisle Stair
description: Dedicated stair access running perpendicular through the seating tiers to allow audience ingress and egress.

name: Seat Nosing
