name: Sliding / Pocket Door
description: Space-saving door type that slides along a track or retracts into the wall cavity, common in dressing rooms with limited swing clearance.

name: Soft Furnishing / Rug
description: Area rug or soft textile placed on the floor to add warmth, comfort, and decorative layering to the space.

name: Jewellery / Accessory Storage
description: Specialised inserts, trays, hooks, or display cases integrated into cabinetry for organising jewellery and accessories.

name: Safe / Secure Storage
description: In-built or recessed security safe for valuables such as watches, jewellery, and documents.

name: Laundry Hamper Recess
description: Built-in compartment or pull-out basket concealed within cabinetry for collecting worn garments.

name: Valet Stand / Hook Rail
description: Wall-mounted or freestanding hooks and rails for temporarily hanging next-day outfits or worn garments.

name: Integrated Lighting Control System
description: Smart or conventional system managing multiple lighting circuits, scenes, and dimming levels throughout the dressing room.

name: Home Automation / Smart System
description: IoT-enabled integration of lighting, climate, and access controls operable via a central interface or mobile device.

name: Walk-In Wardrobe (WIW)
description: Larger variant of a dressing room fully enclosed with dedicated circulation space and comprehensive storage zones.

name: En-Suite Dressing Area
description: Dressing zone directly connecting a bedroom to a bathroom, creating a private grooming suite.

name: Dressing Alcove
description: Recessed or open niche carved out of a bedroom providing dressing and storage functions without a fully enclosed room.

name: Stage / Performance Dressing Room
description: Backstage dressing room in theatres or venues equipped with costume storage, make-up stations, and performer amenities.

name: Retail Fitting Room
description: Commercial dressing room in a retail environment where customers try on merchandise before purchase.

name: Sports / Team Changing Room
description: Communal dressing room in sports facilities providing lockers, benches, and shower access for athletes.

name: Cabinetry Installation
description: Construction activity involving the fixing, alignment, and finishing of bespoke or modular wardrobe cabinetry within the space.

name: Electrical Rough-In & Fit-Out
description: First and second-fix electrical works for outlets, lighting circuits, and control systems serving the dressing room.

name: Plastering & Wall Finishing
description: Application of plaster, render, or skim coat to internal wall and ceiling surfaces prior to decoration.

name: Mirror Installation
description: Precise fixing and silicone-sealing of large mirrors to walls, including structural backing and edge treatment.

name: Door & Frame Installation
description: Supply and fitting of door frames, door leaves, ironmongery, and sliding or pocket door track systems.

name: HVAC Ducting & Diffuser Installation
description: Routing of ductwork and fixing of air supply/return diffusers to integrate climate control into the dressing room.

name: IfcOutlet
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowTerminal.

name: Standard Ceiling Height Zone
description: A room or area with a conventional, code-compliant ceiling height typically ranging from 8 to 10 feet.

name: High Ceiling Zone
description: A space deliberately designed with ceilings exceeding 10 feet to create a sense of openness or grandeur.

name: Low Ceiling Zone
description: An area with intentionally or structurally constrained ceiling heights below standard, often used for intimate or utilitarian spaces.

name: Double-Height Space
description: A volumetric space spanning two full floor levels without an intermediate floor, creating dramatic vertical volume.

name: Cathedral Ceiling
description: A steeply pitched, symmetrical ceiling that follows the roofline, adding significant vertical dimension to a space.

name: Vaulted Ceiling
description: An arched or curved ceiling form that provides additional height at the apex and architectural character to a room.

name: Coffered Ceiling
description: A ceiling featuring a grid of recessed panels that add visual depth and perceived height variation within a single plane.

name: Dropped Ceiling / Suspended Ceiling
description: A secondary ceiling hung below the structural soffit to conceal MEP services, reduce ceiling height, or define sub-zones acoustically.

name: Bulkhead / Soffit Drop
description: A localised lowered ceiling section used to house ducts, beams, or lighting and creating deliberate height transitions within a room.

name: Clerestory Window Zone
description: A band of windows positioned at the upper section of a tall wall enabled by a higher ceiling, admitting daylight deep into the plan.

name: Structural Beam / Exposed Joist
description: Visible load-bearing or decorative beams that punctuate the ceiling plane and influence the perceived and actual ceiling height.

name: Ceiling Height Transition Element
description: An architectural device such as a step, cove, or reveal that mediates the visual change between two adjacent zones of different ceiling heights.

name: Acoustic Ceiling Panel System
description: A system of sound-absorbing panels installed at varied heights to control reverberation while reinforcing the spatial height strategy.

name: Ceiling Finish Material
description: Surface materials applied to ceilings (e.g., gypsum board, timber, plaster, metal) that visually define and differentiate height zones.

name: HVAC Zoning by Ceiling Height
description: Mechanical conditioning strategy that accounts for thermal stratification and air distribution differences caused by varying ceiling heights across zones.

name: Sprinkler & Fire Suppression Layout
description: A fire-suppression system whose head spacing, flow rates, and coverage areas must be recalculated for each distinct ceiling-height zone.

name: Ceiling Height Survey / As-Built Measurement Activity
description: A field measurement process to record actual ceiling heights throughout a building for compliance, renovation, or BIM documentation purposes.

name: Ceiling Framing / Furring Activity
description: The construction task of installing metal or timber framing to set and support a ceiling at a specified height, particularly for dropped or varied ceilings.

name: Height Variance Compliance Review
description: A design and regulatory activity verifying that all ceiling heights meet applicable building codes, accessibility standards, and occupancy requirements.

name: Acoustic Modelling by Height Zone
description: An engineering activity that simulates sound behaviour within each ceiling-height variant to optimise room acoustics and noise control.

name: IfcSpace (Height-Attributed)
description: An IFC space entity carrying ceiling-height property sets that enable interoperable tracking of height parameters across BIM authoring tools.

name: IfcCovering (Ceiling Type)
description: The IFC class representing ceiling finish elements, linked to the bounding space to record material, height offset, and finish type.

name: Floor Plan Geometry
description: The two-dimensional layout and boundary shape of an indoor space as viewed from above.

name: Ceiling Height
description: The vertical distance from finished floor to finished ceiling, defining the volumetric feel of a space.

name: Room Volume
description: The total three-dimensional cubic capacity enclosed within the walls, floor, and ceiling of an indoor space.

name: Wall Geometry
description: The angles, curvature, thickness, and planarity of interior wall surfaces that define spatial boundaries.

name: Ceiling Geometry
description: The shape, slope, coffers, or curvature of the ceiling plane bounding a space from above.

name: Floor Geometry
description: The shape, level changes, ramps, or undulations of the floor surface within an indoor space.

name: Column Grid Layout
description: The regular or irregular arrangement of structural columns that subdivides and influences the perceived shape of an interior.

name: Alcove
description: A recessed area set back from the main volume of a room, creating a subsidiary spatial pocket.

name: Niche
description: A shallow, often arched recess in a wall used functionally or decoratively, locally altering the wall plane.

name: Vaulted Space
description: An interior whose ceiling or roof forms a continuous curved or arched surface rather than a flat plane.

name: Irregular Polygon Plan
description: A floor plan whose boundary is a non-orthogonal polygon, producing angled corners and complex spatial geometry.

name: Curved Plan Space
description: An indoor space whose plan boundary incorporates one or more curved walls, creating a non-rectilinear enclosure.

name: Open-Plan Space
description: A large, minimally partitioned interior where multiple functions coexist within a single continuous spatial volume.

name: Cellular Room Layout
description: A configuration of multiple small, fully enclosed rooms arranged adjacently, each with a distinct boundary.

name: Spatial Zoning
description: The design process of dividing an interior into functional sub-areas based on use, privacy, or circulation requirements.

name: Space Measurement Survey
description: The on-site activity of measuring and recording the precise dimensions and geometry of an indoor space.

name: As-Built 3D Scanning
description: The use of laser or photogrammetric scanning technology to capture the exact existing shape of an interior in three dimensions.

name: Demolition of Internal Walls
description: The removal of existing interior walls to merge spaces and alter the overall shape of an indoor area.

name: Ceiling Fit-Out
description: The installation of suspended, stretched, or shaped ceiling systems that define the upper boundary geometry of a space.

name: Floor Levelling
description: The activity of correcting or adjusting the floor surface to achieve the intended planar or graded geometry.

name: Acoustic Volume
description: The engineered spatial volume defined by room shape and finish materials that governs reverberation and sound behaviour.

name: Daylighting Geometry
description: The spatial configuration of windows, roof lights, and surfaces that determines how natural light penetrates and models the interior shape.

name: Structural Grid System
description: The coordinating framework of structural axes that constrains and informs the permissible shapes of indoor spaces.

name: Spatial Data Model (BIM)
description: The digital information system that stores, relates, and queries the geometric and semantic properties of all indoor spaces.

name: Thermal Envelope Geometry
description: The three-dimensional shape of the air volume enclosed within insulated building boundaries, relevant to energy modelling.

name: Masonry (Brick/Block)
description: Stacked unit construction material used to form load-bearing or non-load-bearing walls that enclose and shape interior spaces.

name: Acoustic Plaster
description: A spray-applied or trowelled finish material that can be sculpted into complex curved ceiling or wall geometries while absorbing sound.

name: Glazing Panel
description: The transparent or translucent glass or polycarbonate infill within a window frame that admits light and views.

name: Transom Bar
description: A horizontal dividing element separating panes or lights within a window assembly, often above a lower operable sash.

name: Operable Sash
description: The movable part of a window that holds the glazing and can be opened for ventilation, available in casement, sliding, or hung variants.

name: Window Hardware & Ironmongery
description: Handles, locks, hinges, stays, and restrictors that control the operation and security of an operable window sash.

name: Weatherstripping & Seals
description: Flexible gaskets and foam or brush seals installed around sash and frame perimeters to prevent air and water infiltration.

name: Double-Glazed Unit (IGU)
description: An insulating glass unit comprising two panes separated by a sealed, gas-filled spacer to improve thermal and acoustic performance.

name: Triple-Glazed Unit
description: A high-performance insulating glass unit with three panes and two sealed cavities for superior thermal insulation in cold climates.

name: Single-Glazed Window
description: A window containing a single pane of glass, typically found in heritage buildings or low-thermal-demand environments.

name: Bow Window
description: A curved projecting window formed by multiple window units set at gentle angles, creating a rounded bay projection.

name: Picture Window
description: A large, fixed, un-divided window designed to frame an exterior view without operable elements obstructing the sightline.

name: Window Seat / Nook
description: A built-in seating area integrated within a window recess or bay, creating an intimate vantage point overlooking the exterior.

name: Interior Glazing System
description: A system of glazed partitions or internal windows used to borrow light and views between interior rooms within a building.

name: Window Ventilation System
description: An integrated arrangement of trickle vents, actuators, and controls enabling natural or hybrid ventilation through window openings.

name: Solar Control Film / Coating
description: Low-emissivity or spectrally selective coatings applied to glazing surfaces to limit solar heat gain while maintaining visible light transmission.

name: Acoustic Glazing Material
description: Laminated or thickened glass assemblies specifically designed to attenuate external noise transmission through window units.

name: Damp-Proof Course at Window
description: A moisture-resistant membrane installed at the window sill and jamb interfaces to prevent rising or penetrating damp entering the structure.

name: Window Installation & Fixing
description: The construction activity of positioning, aligning, securing, and sealing window units within prepared wall openings to manufacturer and specification tolerances.

name: Glazing Replacement
description: The maintenance or upgrade activity of removing existing glass panes or IGUs and installing new glazing units within an existing frame.

name: Window Frame Painting & Finishing
description: The surface treatment activity of preparing, priming, and applying decorative or protective coatings to timber, steel, or aluminium window frames.

name: Air-Tightness Testing at Windows
description: A quality assurance procedure measuring air leakage at window frame-to-wall junctions to verify compliance with energy performance targets.

name: Thermal Bridging Assessment
description: An analytical activity evaluating heat loss pathways at window frames, reveals, and sills to inform detailing and insulation strategies.

name: View & Visual Connection Study
description: A design activity assessing sightlines, privacy, and quality of views from window positions to optimise occupant connection with the surrounding life and landscape.

name: External Window Shading Device
description: Fixed or adjustable fins, brise-soleil, overhangs, or shutters mounted externally to a window to control solar gain and glare.

name: Internal Blind & Curtain Track System
description: Tracks, rollers, and motorisation infrastructure installed within the window reveal to support blinds, curtains, or shading screens.

name: Knee Wall
description: A short vertical wall segment that partially encloses a space, typically used beneath stairs or at the eave line of a sloped roof.

name: Pony Wall
description: A short dividing wall that does not extend to the ceiling, used to partially separate areas while maintaining visual openness.

name: Screen Wall
description: A perforated or slatted wall structure that provides partial visual privacy and weather protection without full enclosure.

name: Louvered Panel
description: A panel fitted with angled slats that allows airflow and partial light transmission while limiting direct sightlines.

name: Brickwork
description: Fired clay bricks laid in mortar courses to form the body of a partial wall, offering durability and aesthetic finish.

name: Foundation Stem Wall
description: A partial-height structural wall rising from the footing to the floor level, forming the base enclosure of a building.

name: Retaining Wall (Partial)
description: A wall built to hold back soil or grade change that may be partially exposed above ground, acting as a half-open boundary.

name: Half-Height Partition
description: An interior dividing element reaching only partway to the ceiling, used in offices or open-plan layouts to define zones without full separation.

name: Open-Plan Zone
description: A floor area that is partially bounded by low walls or partitions, creating a defined zone within a larger undivided space.

name: Courtyard Boundary Wall
description: A partial enclosing wall that defines the perimeter of a courtyard while allowing views or access through openings.

name: Masonry Wall Construction
description: The trade activity of laying brick or block units in mortar to build up a partial or full wall to specified height.

name: Wall Reinforcement Installation
description: The activity of placing and tying steel rebar within wall sections prior to concrete placement to ensure structural integrity.

name: Wall Capping and Waterproofing
description: The finishing activity of applying coping, sealants, or membranes to the top and exposed faces of a partial wall to prevent water ingress.

name: Damp-Proof Course (DPC) Installation
description: The activity of inserting a moisture-resistant layer at the base of a wall to prevent rising damp from penetrating the structure.

name: Wall Rendering and Plastering
description: The finishing activity of applying cement, lime, or gypsum coatings to wall surfaces for protection and aesthetics.

name: Acoustic Barrier (Partial)
description: A system using partial-height wall construction to attenuate sound between zones while maintaining visual and spatial connectivity.

name: Structural Load-Bearing System
description: The engineered system of walls and supports that transfers vertical and lateral loads from a partial wall to the foundation.

name: Waterproofing and Drainage System
description: An integrated system of membranes, flashings, and drains protecting exposed partial wall assemblies from water infiltration and damage.

name: Interior Window Frame
description: The structural border surrounding an interior window opening, typically made of wood, metal, or vinyl, that holds the glazing in place.

name: Interior Window Sill
description: The horizontal ledge at the bottom of an interior window frame that provides a finished edge and may serve as a small shelf.

name: Interior Window Casing / Trim
description: Decorative moulding applied around the interior perimeter of a window frame to conceal the gap between the frame and the wall finish.

name: Interior Window Glazing
description: The glass or glazing unit fitted into an interior window frame, which may be clear, frosted, tempered, or laminated for privacy or safety.

name: Interior Window Sash
description: The movable or fixed panel within an interior window frame that holds the glazing and, where operable, can be opened for ventilation or access.

name: Interior Window Hardware
description: Handles, latches, locks, hinges, and stays used to operate, secure, and hold open interior window sashes.

name: Interior Window Head
description: The top horizontal member of the interior window frame assembly that spans the full width of the window opening.

name: Interior Window Jamb
description: The vertical side members of the interior window frame that run from the sill to the head and form the sides of the opening.

name: Interior Window Mullion
description: A vertical or horizontal dividing bar between individual window panes or sashes within a larger interior window unit.

name: Interior Window Transom
description: A fixed or operable glazed panel located above a door or window opening, used to borrow light between adjacent interior spaces.

name: Interior Window Sidelight
description: A narrow fixed or operable glazed panel positioned to the side of a door or main window to allow light transfer between rooms.

name: Interior Window Borrowed Light Panel
description: A full system of glazed openings built into an interior partition specifically to transfer natural or artificial light between enclosed spaces without direct visual access.

name: Interior Partition Wall with Window Opening
description: The non-structural or structural interior wall assembly that contains and supports one or more interior window units.

name: Fixed Interior Window
description: A non-operable interior window variant where the glazing is permanently sealed within the frame, used solely for light transfer or visual connection.

name: Operable Interior Window
description: An interior window variant fitted with a sash that can be opened—sliding, hinged, or pivoting—for ventilation or pass-through purposes.

name: Sliding Interior Window
description: An interior window variant in which one or more sashes slide horizontally or vertically along tracks rather than swinging open.

name: Casement Interior Window
description: An interior window variant with a sash hinged at the side that swings inward or outward to open.

name: Frosted / Obscure Glazing Interior Window
description: An interior window variant that uses textured, frosted, or sandblasted glass to allow light transmission while maintaining visual privacy.

name: Fire-Rated Interior Window
description: An interior window assembly tested and certified to resist the passage of fire and smoke for a specified period, required in fire-compartment walls.

name: Acoustic Interior Window
description: An interior window unit designed with laminated or double-glazed panels and sealed frames to reduce sound transmission between rooms.

name: Steel-Frame Interior Window
description: An interior window variant featuring slender steel profiles, commonly used in industrial-loft or contemporary interiors for a distinctive aesthetic.

name: Timber-Frame Interior Window
description: An interior window variant using solid or engineered timber for the frame, suited to traditional or warm-aesthetic interior designs.

name: Aluminium-Frame Interior Window
description: An interior window variant using lightweight aluminium profiles, offering durability and slim sightlines for modern interiors.

name: Interior Window Rough Opening Preparation
description: The construction activity of cutting, framing, and lintelling an opening in an interior wall in preparation for window installation.

name: Interior Window Installation
description: The on-site activity of fixing the window frame, sash, and glazing unit into a prepared interior wall opening, including levelling, securing, and sealing.

name: Interior Window Glazing Installation
description: The trade activity of fitting, bedding, and sealing glass panes or glazed units into prepared interior window frames.

name: Interior Window Trim & Casing Installation
description: The carpentry activity of cutting, fitting, and fixing decorative mouldings and sills around the perimeter of an installed interior window frame.

name: Interior Window Painting & Finishing
description: The finishing activity of sanding, priming, and applying paint or stain to interior window frames, sills, and casings to achieve the specified surface finish.

name: Interior Window Hardware Installation
description: The activity of fitting and adjusting handles, locks, hinges, and other ironmongery onto interior window sashes and frames.

name: Interior Window Acoustic Sealing
description: The specialist activity of applying acoustic sealant, gaskets, or brush seals around interior window perimeters to meet sound-insulation performance targets.

name: Interior Window Fire-Rating Inspection
description: The compliance activity of inspecting and certifying that fire-rated interior window assemblies are installed correctly per the relevant fire-resistance standards.

name: Window Glazing Sealant / Putty
description: A flexible compound applied between the glass edge and the frame rebate to create a weathertight and airtight seal around interior window glazing.

name: Window Draught Seal / Weatherstrip
description: A compressible foam, rubber, or brush seal fitted to sash edges or frame rebates to prevent air infiltration around operable interior windows.

name: Window Blind / Shade Integration
description: A system of roller blinds, venetian blinds, or privacy film integrated within or mounted directly to interior window frames for on-demand privacy control.

name: Baluster / Spindle
description: Vertical infill members spaced along the balustrade that prevent falls and contribute to the visual character of the stair.

name: Stair Nosing
description: A projecting or finished edge at the front of each tread that improves visibility, safety, and durability of the step.

name: Stringer / Stair Stringer
description: The inclined structural board or beam running along the side of a stair flight that supports the treads and risers.

name: Stairwell / Stairshaft
description: The vertical shaft or enclosure surrounding the stair flights and landings, defined by surrounding walls and floor openings.

name: Stair Enclosure Walls
description: The fire-rated or non-rated wall assemblies that bound and enclose the stairwell from adjacent building spaces.

name: Stair Door / Fire Door
description: A door assembly—often fire-rated—at each floor level that controls access to and egress from the stairwell.

name: Stair Lobby / Pressurised Lobby
description: An anteroom separating the stairwell from the main floor area, often pressurised for smoke control in tall buildings.

name: Emergency / Escape Lighting
description: A secondary lighting system with battery back-up that activates during power failure to guide safe evacuation via the staircase.

name: Mechanical Ventilation / Pressurisation System
description: A mechanical system that maintains positive air pressure in the stairwell to prevent smoke ingress during a fire event.

name: Sprinkler System (Stairwell)
description: Fire suppression sprinkler heads installed within the stairwell enclosure as required by fire safety regulations.

name: Stair Drainage / Floor Drain
description: Drainage provisions at stair landings or base to manage water ingress from cleaning, leaks, or external access points.

name: Tactile / Slip-Resistant Tread Surface
description: A slip-resistant or tactile-indicator surface material applied to stair treads to improve safety and accessibility compliance.

name: Tread Finish Material
description: The visible surface material of the stair tread—such as timber, stone, tile, carpet, or metal—selected for durability and aesthetics.

name: Stair Structural Frame / Carriage
description: The primary load-bearing structural element (e.g., central spine beam or paired stringers) that carries the dead and live loads of the entire stair flight.

name: Precast Concrete Stair
description: A stair flight manufactured off-site as a factory-cast concrete unit and craned into position, representing a common industrial stair variant.

name: Spiral / Helical Stair
description: A stair variant with a circular plan winding around a central column or open well, often used where floor area is limited.

name: Scissor Stair
description: A stair arrangement containing two interlocking stair flights within a single stairwell volume, providing two independent egress paths.

name: Alternating Tread Stair
description: A compact stair type with offset half-treads that allows steeper pitch while maintaining foot support, used in space-constrained situations.

name: Stair Construction & Installation
description: The on-site fabrication, placement, and fixing of stair flights, stringers, treads, and risers as part of the building construction sequence.

name: Formwork & Concrete Pouring (In-situ Stair)
description: The temporary formwork erection and concrete placement activity required to cast monolithic in-situ reinforced concrete stair flights.

name: Stair Balustrade Installation
description: The fixing and securing of handrails, balusters, and newel posts to the stair structure in accordance with safety standards.

name: Stair Tread & Finish Application
description: The laying, bonding, or fixing of finished tread materials and nosings as a final trade activity on the completed stair structure.

name: Stair Safety Inspection & Compliance Testing
description: Formal inspection and testing of geometry (rise, going, headroom), structural adequacy, balustrade loads, and slip resistance to verify regulatory compliance.

name: Accessibility / DDA Compliance Assessment
description: Evaluation of stair design against disability and accessibility standards, including handrail continuity, tread dimensions, and contrast markings.

name: Headroom / Clearance Zone
description: The minimum vertical clearance space above each stair tread and landing required by building codes to ensure safe passage.

name: Egress / Means of Escape Route
description: The designated evacuation path through the staircase that must meet minimum width, travel distance, and fire-safety requirements.

name: Pivot Hinge Corner Door
description: A corner door variant that uses a pivot hinge mechanism to allow the door leaf to swing from a corner-mounted pivot point rather than a traditional side rail.

name: Bi-Fold Corner Door Panel
description: A folding door panel system designed to fold flat against adjacent walls when opened at a corner junction.

name: Sliding Corner Door Track
description: A curved or angled track system that guides sliding door panels around a corner transition between two wall faces.

name: Corner Door Frame Assembly
description: A structural frame unit specifically engineered to sit at the junction of two intersecting walls and support the door leaf.

name: Corner Door Jamb
description: The vertical side member of a corner door frame that forms the finished edge at the wall corner and provides a surface for hinges or seals.

name: Corner Door Threshold
description: A floor-level transition strip positioned at the base of a corner door opening to seal the gap and manage level changes between spaces.

name: Corner Door Seal Strip
description: A compressible gasket or brush seal applied along the edges of a corner door leaf to prevent air, sound, and light infiltration.

name: Corner Door Glass Panel
description: A glazed panel integrated into a corner door leaf, often used in frameless glass corner door designs for transparency and aesthetics.

name: Frameless Glass Corner Door System
description: A fully integrated door system using tempered or laminated glass panels without visible framing, commonly installed at room corners for a minimalist look.

name: Corner Door Hardware Set
description: The collection of locks, handles, hinges, and closing mechanisms specifically rated and sized for use on corner-mounted door assemblies.

name: Corner Door Closer Mechanism
description: A hydraulic or spring-loaded device mounted on a corner door to control the speed and force of door closure.

name: Automated Corner Door Operator
description: An electromechanical system that automates the opening and closing of a corner door, used in accessible or high-traffic building environments.

name: Corner Wall Stud Framing
description: Structural timber or metal stud framing configured at the corner wall intersection to provide a solid rough opening for the corner door.

name: Corner Door Rough Opening
description: The framed opening within intersecting walls left during construction to accommodate the corner door frame and clearances.

name: Corner Door Alcove
description: A recessed or angled spatial zone created at a room corner specifically to house a sliding or folding corner door when in the open position.

name: Corner Door Installation
description: The on-site construction activity of fitting, aligning, and securing a corner door frame and leaf within the prepared corner wall opening.

name: Corner Door Frame Fabrication
description: The off-site or on-site manufacturing and assembly process for producing a bespoke corner door frame to match specific wall angle and size requirements.

name: Corner Wall Opening Formation
description: The demolition or new-build carpentry/masonry activity of creating the structural opening at a wall corner to receive a corner door assembly.

name: Corner Door Waterproofing
description: The application of waterproof membranes or sealants around a corner door frame, critical in wet rooms or exterior-facing corner door installations.

name: Corner Door Finishing & Painting
description: The surface preparation, priming, and painting or staining activity applied to the corner door frame, jambs, and leaf after installation.

name: Angled Wall Intersection
description: The spatial condition formed where two non-parallel walls meet at an acute or obtuse angle, creating the physical context for a corner door installation.

name: Corner Door Fire Rating Assembly
description: A fire-rated door system assembled with tested components — frame, leaf, seals, and hardware — to achieve a certified fire resistance at a corner location.

name: Acoustic Corner Door System
description: A door system with enhanced sound-dampening seals, mass-loaded leaves, and reinforced frames designed to reduce sound transmission at a corner opening.

name: Timber Corner Door Leaf
description: A solid or engineered timber door panel manufactured to fit a corner door frame, providing aesthetic warmth and structural integrity.

name: Steel Corner Door Leaf
description: A pressed or hollow-metal steel door panel used in corner door assemblies where enhanced security, fire resistance, or durability is required.

name: IfcDoor (Corner Configuration)
description: The IFC building data schema class used to model and exchange corner door objects with geometry, properties, and spatial relationships in a BIM environment.

name: IfcOpeningElement (Corner)
description: The IFC class representing the void or opening cut into intersecting walls to host a corner door element within a BIM model.

name: Adobe Wall
description: A thick wall constructed from sun-dried mud bricks, traditionally used in arid climates for its high thermal mass.

name: Stone Rubble Wall
description: A thick wall built from irregularly shaped natural stone units laid with or without mortar, common in historic and vernacular construction.

name: Composite Wall Assembly
description: A multi-layer wall system combining structural, insulating, and finishing materials to meet modern energy and structural codes.

name: Wall Core Insulation
description: Insulating material—such as mineral wool, foam board, or blown-in cellulose—placed within the wall thickness to reduce heat transfer.

name: Thermal Mass Layer
description: A high-density material layer within or forming the wall that stores and slowly releases heat to moderate internal temperature swings.

name: Masonry Mortar Joint
description: The cementitious or lime-based bonding layer between masonry units that transfers stress and seals the wall against air and water infiltration.

name: Reinforced Masonry Wall
description: A masonry wall with steel reinforcement bars grouted into cores or bed joints to enhance tensile strength and ductility.

name: Structural Concrete Wall
description: A monolithic cast-in-place or precast concrete wall providing significant structural depth and inherent thermal mass.

name: External Wall Render / Plaster
description: A protective and decorative coating applied to the outer face of a wall to seal the surface and improve weathering resistance.

name: Internal Wall Lining
description: A finish layer—such as plasterboard, timber boarding, or plaster—applied to the internal face of a thick wall for aesthetics and services integration.

name: Wall Foundation Interface
description: The critical zone where the base of a thick wall bears onto or is tied into the foundation element, requiring careful detailing for load transfer and waterproofing.

name: Window / Door Reveal Recess
description: The deep recess formed in a thick wall at window or door openings, which must be detailed to manage solar shading, thermal bridging, and weatherproofing.

name: Splayed Reveal
description: An angled or chamfered internal or external edge of a wall opening that optimises daylight distribution and reduces thermal bridging in thick-wall construction.

name: Formwork Erection for Concrete Walls
description: The temporary works activity of assembling and aligning formwork panels to contain wet concrete during casting of a thick wall.

name: Rammed Earth Compaction
description: The construction activity of pneumatically or manually tamping moistened earth in successive layers within formwork to form a dense, monolithic wall.

name: Waterproofing and Damp-Proofing Application
description: The activity of applying membranes, coatings, or DPC materials to protect a wall from moisture ingress and rising damp.

name: Wall Rendering / Plastering
description: The finishing activity of applying one or more coats of render or plaster to the face of a wall to provide a smooth, weatherproof, or decorative surface.

name: IfcMaterialLayerSet
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcMaterialDefinition.

name: Shared Wall Between Closets
description: The common partition wall separating two back-to-back closets that serves as the structural and acoustic boundary between adjacent rooms.

name: Closet Rod
description: A horizontal bar installed within the closet space for hanging garments, typically mounted between two side walls or on brackets.

name: Closet Shelf
description: Fixed or adjustable horizontal storage surface installed above or alongside hanging rods to provide folded-item or accessory storage.

name: Bi-Fold Closet Door
description: A folding door system that splits into two panels, commonly used for closet access where swing clearance is limited.

name: Sliding Closet Door
description: A door that travels along an overhead track and floor guide, allowing closet access without requiring swing space into the room.

name: Hinged Closet Door
description: A traditional swinging door on hinges providing full-width access to a closet opening.

name: Closet Door Frame
description: The structural surround and trim assembly that borders the closet opening and supports the door hardware.

name: Closet Lighting Fixture
description: An interior light source, such as an LED bar or recessed fixture, installed inside the closet to illuminate contents.

name: Closet Electrical Outlet
description: An electrical receptacle placed within the closet for powering organizer lighting, vacuums, or charging accessories.

name: Closet Ventilation Louver
description: A louvered panel or grille integrated into the closet door or wall to promote air circulation and prevent moisture buildup.

name: Modular Closet Organizer System
description: A configurable assembly of shelves, drawers, rods, and dividers designed to maximize storage efficiency within the closet volume.

name: Closet Electrical Circuit
description: The dedicated or shared electrical branch circuit supplying power to lighting and outlets within the closet space.

name: Sound Insulation System (Inter-Room Closet)
description: An acoustic insulation assembly—batts, resilient channels, or mass-loaded vinyl—installed within shared closet walls to reduce sound transmission between flanking rooms.

name: Reach-In Closet
description: A shallow closet accessed from the front without entering, typically 24–30 inches deep, positioned between two adjoining rooms.

name: Double-Entry Closet (Pass-Through)
description: A closet configuration accessible from two different rooms, functioning as a shared storage buffer zone between spaces.

name: Linen Closet Between Rooms
description: A narrow closet positioned on a shared wall used specifically for storing linens, towels, and bedding for adjacent rooms.

name: Sound Buffer Closet
description: A closet intentionally placed between rooms in a design strategy to act as an acoustic buffer reducing noise transfer.

name: Closet Interior Drywall
description: Gypsum board used to finish the interior walls and ceiling of the closet, providing a paintable and fire-resistant surface.

name: Closet Floor Finish Material
description: The flooring surface inside the closet, such as carpet, hardwood, or laminate, chosen for durability and continuity with adjacent rooms.

name: Acoustic Batt Insulation
description: Sound-dampening insulation material, typically mineral wool or dense-pack fiberglass, placed within shared closet wall cavities.

name: Closet Rod Bracket
description: A wall-mounted metal or plastic support that holds the closet rod at the correct height and prevents sagging under load.

name: Closet Framing (Stud Wall)
description: The wood or metal stud framing that defines the closet enclosure and supports the surrounding walls, shelving, and door opening.

name: Closet Rough-In and Framing
description: The construction activity of building the stud walls, headers, and rough openings that establish the closet's structural enclosure between rooms.

name: Closet Door Installation
description: The work of fitting, aligning, and securing closet doors—bi-fold, sliding, or hinged—including hardware and track mounting.

name: Closet Shelving and Rod Installation
description: The carpentry activity of mounting shelves, rods, brackets, and organizer systems to the closet interior walls and ceiling.

name: Closet Insulation Installation
description: The task of placing acoustic or thermal insulation batts within the wall cavities of shared closet partitions to improve performance.

name: Closet Electrical Rough-In
description: The electrical trade activity of running conduit or cables for closet lighting circuits and outlets before walls are closed.

name: Closet Drywall and Finishing
description: The process of hanging, taping, mudding, and painting interior drywall surfaces within the closet enclosure.

name: Closet Trim and Casing Work
description: The finish carpentry activity of installing door casings, baseboard, and any decorative molding around and within the closet.

name: Countertop Surface
description: The horizontal working surface of the sunny counter, typically made of stone, laminate, or solid surface material that receives direct sunlight.

name: Base Cabinet
description: The lower structural cabinet unit that supports the countertop and provides enclosed storage beneath the work surface.

name: Skylight Above Counter
description: An overhead glazed opening installed directly above the counter to flood the workspace with natural daylight from above.

name: Splashback / Backsplash
description: A vertical protective panel mounted on the wall behind the counter to guard against moisture, heat, and light reflection.

name: Under-Counter Storage Drawer
description: Pull-out drawer units integrated into the base cabinet for organised storage of tools, utensils, or supplies.

name: Countertop Lighting Fixture
description: Supplemental task-lighting units mounted above or under shelving to complement natural sunlight on the counter surface.

name: Solar-Gain Glazing System
description: An integrated window and glazing system engineered to optimise passive solar light transmission onto the counter workspace.

name: Electrical Service System
description: The in-counter or under-counter electrical outlets, switches, and wiring serving appliances and lighting at the counter position.

name: Solar Shading / Blind System
description: Roller blinds, louvres, or external shading devices that modulate sunlight intensity reaching the counter to prevent glare or overheating.

name: Counter Workspace Zone
description: The defined activity area immediately above and around the countertop where users perform tasks in a naturally lit environment.

name: Under-Counter Storage Space
description: The enclosed spatial volume beneath the countertop occupied by cabinets, drawers, or open shelving.

name: Window Sill Ledge Space
description: The shallow horizontal surface at the base of the adjacent window, often used as an extension of the sunny counter for plants or display.

name: Stone / Engineered Stone Countertop
description: Natural granite, marble, or engineered quartz used as a durable, heat-resistant, and aesthetically desirable counter surface material.

name: Laminate Surfacing
description: A cost-effective layered synthetic surface material applied to the countertop substrate, available in light-reflective finishes suited for sunny areas.

name: Solar-Control Glazing
description: Specialised low-emissivity or tinted glass used in adjacent windows to filter UV and infrared radiation while maintaining visible light.

name: Moisture-Resistant MDF Substrate
description: Engineered wood panel used as the structural base layer of the countertop, chosen for dimensional stability in variable sun and humidity conditions.

name: Heat-Reflective Paint / Coating
description: A specialised finish applied to surfaces near the counter to reduce thermal absorption from sustained solar exposure.

name: Counter Installation
description: The construction activity of fabricating, positioning, levelling, and fixing the countertop and its supporting cabinet structure in place.

name: Electrical Rough-In and Fit-Out
description: First- and second-fix electrical work to install outlets, under-cabinet lighting, and associated wiring serving the counter area.

name: Plumbing Installation
description: The activity of running and connecting supply and drainage pipework if a sink or water point is incorporated into the counter design.

name: Splashback Tiling or Panel Fixing
description: The trade activity of applying tiles, glass panels, or sheet materials to the wall surface directly behind the countertop.

name: Sealant and Waterproofing Application
description: Application of silicone sealants or waterproofing agents at joints between the countertop, wall, and sink to prevent moisture ingress.

name: Solar Orientation Assessment
description: A design-stage analysis activity to determine the optimal position and angle of the counter relative to sun path for maximum daylighting benefit.

name: Kitchen Counter
description: A closely related counter typology in a kitchen context that shares many components and construction methods with a sunny counter.

name: Window Seat / Bay Window Nook
description: An adjacent or alternative sun-bathed seating or work surface space that shares solar access characteristics with the sunny counter concept.

name: Shelf Board
description: A horizontal panel that forms the primary load-bearing surface for storing items on open shelves.

name: Shelf Bracket
description: A support element fixed to the wall or upright that carries the weight of the shelf board.

name: Upright / Side Panel
description: A vertical structural member that defines the ends of a shelving unit and supports multiple shelf levels.

name: Back Panel
description: An optional rear surface attached to the shelving frame to provide stability and a visual backdrop.

name: Shelf Edge / Lip
description: A raised front trim along the shelf board that prevents stored items from sliding off.

name: Adjustable Shelf Pin
description: A small peg or clip inserted into pre-drilled holes in uprights, allowing shelf height to be repositioned.

name: Wall Anchor / Fixing
description: A fastener assembly (bolt, anchor, or screw) used to secure shelving units or brackets to wall substrates.

name: Shelving Rail / Track
description: A wall-mounted metal channel that accepts brackets at multiple positions for flexible shelf placement.

name: Base / Plinth
description: A low platform or kick-board at the bottom of a freestanding shelving unit that provides stability and toe clearance.

name: Top Cap / Crown
description: A finishing panel placed on top of a shelving unit to give a neat, closed appearance to the uppermost section.

name: Solid Wood Shelving
description: Natural timber used as a shelf board material, valued for its aesthetic appeal and load-bearing capacity.

name: MDF / Particleboard Shelving
description: Engineered wood panels commonly used for budget-friendly shelf boards due to their smooth surface and ease of finishing.

name: Tempered Glass Shelf
description: A toughened glass panel used as a shelf surface to create a visually light, transparent storage element.

name: Metal / Steel Shelf
description: A shelf board or frame fabricated from steel or aluminium, commonly used in industrial or commercial shelving systems.

name: Melamine / Laminate Finish
description: A protective and decorative surface coating applied to shelf boards to resist wear, moisture, and staining.

name: Freestanding Shelving Unit
description: A self-supporting shelving assembly that stands independently without attachment to walls, offering flexibility in placement.

name: Wall-Mounted Shelving System
description: A shelving configuration that is anchored directly to walls, maximising floor space and providing a built-in appearance.

name: Modular Shelving System
description: An expandable, interchangeable shelving system made of standardised units that can be reconfigured to suit changing storage needs.

name: Cantilever Shelving
description: A shelving system in which shelf boards project outward from a single wall-fixed support without front legs or uprights.

name: Industrial / Wire Shelving
description: Open-grid wire or tubular steel shelving commonly used in storage, retail, and utility spaces for ventilation and visibility.

name: Floating Shelf
description: A shelf mounted with concealed fixings that appears to float on the wall without visible brackets or supports.

name: Display Alcove Shelving
description: Shelves fitted within a recessed wall niche to display objects while maintaining a flush wall surface around them.

name: Library / Bookcase Bay
description: A dedicated spatial zone containing multiple shelving units arranged for the organised storage and retrieval of books or files.

name: Retail Display Shelving Area
description: A designated floor area within a retail environment fitted with open shelves for product presentation and customer access.

name: Shelving Installation
description: The on-site process of assembling, positioning, levelling, and fixing shelving units or brackets into their final location.

name: Wall Preparation & Fixing
description: The activity of preparing wall surfaces, drilling, inserting anchors, and securing wall fixings prior to shelf mounting.

name: Shelf Board Cutting & Sizing
description: The workshop or on-site task of cutting shelf panels to the required dimensions and finishing the cut edges.

name: Surface Finishing & Painting
description: The application of paint, varnish, lacquer, or laminate to shelf components to achieve the desired aesthetic and durability.

name: Load Capacity Assessment
description: The structural evaluation of the maximum weight that a shelf or shelving system can safely support under intended use conditions.

name: Shelving Reconfiguration / Adjustment
description: The process of repositioning, adding, or removing shelf levels to adapt the shelving layout to new storage requirements.

name: Wall Mounting Plate
description: A metal or timber plate fixed to the wall substrate to provide a secure anchor point for shelf brackets.

name: Shelf Upright / Side Panel
description: Vertical panel or post at either end of the shelf unit that provides lateral support and defines the overall height.

name: Shelf Edging / Lip
description: A raised front edge or trim strip along the shelf board that stops items from sliding off the front.

name: Fixing Fastener (Screw / Bolt / Anchor)
description: Mechanical fasteners used to secure shelf components to walls, floors, or each other.

name: Solid Timber Shelving
description: Natural or engineered solid wood used as the primary material for the shelf board, offering strength and aesthetics.

name: MDF / Particleboard
description: Manufactured wood-based sheet material commonly used for shelf boards due to its flat surface and cost-effectiveness.

name: Powder-Coated Steel
description: Steel with a durable epoxy or polyester coat used for industrial-style shelf boards, brackets, and frames.

name: Laminate / Veneer Finish
description: Decorative surface layer applied to a shelf board to improve appearance, durability, and moisture resistance.

name: Timber Stud Wall System
description: Light-frame wall construction requiring stud-finding and appropriate fixings for secure shelf installation.

name: Modular Storage System
description: A coordinated kit-of-parts system incorporating waist-high shelves, uprights, and accessories for flexible configuration.

name: Display / Retail Shelving System
description: A purpose-built commercial shelving system designed to present products at ergonomic waist-height for easy customer access.

name: Counter-Height Shelf Space
description: The usable horizontal area at approximately 900–1000 mm AFF that defines the ergonomic working zone of a waist-high shelf.

name: Under-Shelf Storage Space
description: The volume beneath the shelf board, often utilised for cabinets, drawers, or open storage.

name: Wall Recess / Alcove Shelf Space
description: A recessed niche in a wall at waist height into which a shelf board is fitted, maximising floor space.

name: Shelf Installation
description: The on-site activity of fixing brackets, uprights, and shelf boards to walls or floors at the correct height and level.

name: Wall Surface Preparation
description: Preparatory work including marking, drilling, and patching the wall before shelf brackets or plates are mounted.

name: Substrate Anchor Testing
description: Load-testing of wall anchors and fixings post-installation to verify they meet the required pull-out strength for shelf loads.

name: Edge Banding / Finishing
description: Application of edge trim or veneer strip to exposed shelf board edges to seal and finish the material.

name: Shelf Load Calculation
description: Structural assessment of bracket spacing and fixing capacity to ensure the shelf safely supports its intended distributed load.

name: Countertop / Benchtop
description: A closely related waist-high horizontal surface that is typically thicker, deeper, and used as a work surface rather than pure storage.

name: IFC Shelf Element (IfcFurnishingElement)
description: The IFC schema class used to represent a shelf as a furnishing element within a Building Information Model.

name: Banquette Seating
description: A fixed upholstered bench seat typically built along a wall or into a corner, commonly used in dining areas.

name: Inglenook Bench
description: A built-in bench seat positioned within or flanking a fireplace inglenook recess.

name: Bleacher / Tiered Seating
description: Fixed tiered rows of seating built into a floor structure, used in auditoria, lecture halls, or stadiums.

name: Seat Substrate / Carcass
description: The structural box or frame that forms the load-bearing body of a built-in seat unit.

name: Seat Platform / Decking
description: The horizontal surface on which a person sits, typically a timber panel or concrete slab forming the top of the seat.

name: Seat Back Panel
description: A vertical panel attached to the wall or carcass providing back support and enclosing the rear of the seat unit.

name: Back Cushion / Bolster
description: A cushion or bolster placed against the back panel to provide lumbar and upper-back support.

name: Under-Seat Storage Compartment
description: An enclosed storage void built beneath the seat platform, accessible via a hinged lid or drawer.

name: Hinged Lid / Access Hatch
description: A hinged panel on top of the seat platform that provides access to the under-seat storage space.

name: Nosing / Seat Edge Detail
description: A finished edge profile applied to the front of the seat platform for durability and a clean appearance.

name: Structural Bracket / Corbel
description: A metal or timber bracket fixed to the wall to carry and support the seat platform cantilever.

name: Foam / Batting Padding
description: High-density foam or polyester batting used as the resilient core of seat and back cushions.

name: Timber / Plywood Sheet
description: Structural or decorative timber panels used to construct the carcass, platform, and back of built-in seats.

name: MDF (Medium-Density Fibreboard)
description: A smooth engineered wood panel commonly used for painted built-in seat components and panel faces.

name: Solid Timber Hardwood
description: Durable hardwood used for exposed seat platforms, nosings, and armrests requiring a high-quality finish.

name: Paint / Primer Finish
description: Protective and decorative paint system applied to MDF or timber surfaces of the built-in seat.

name: Piano Hinge / Butt Hinge
description: Metal hinges used to attach hinged seat lids or access panels to the seat carcass.

name: Lid Stay / Soft-Close Mechanism
description: A hardware stay or damper that controls and limits the opening angle of a hinged seat lid for safety.

name: Fixings & Fasteners
description: Screws, bolts, and wall plugs used to secure the seat carcass and components to the building fabric.

name: Carpentry & Joinery Works
description: The primary trade activity involving cutting, assembling, and installing the timber or sheet-material seat structure.

name: Upholstery Installation
description: The trade activity of cutting, padding, and fitting fabric or leather covers to seat and back cushions.

name: Painting & Finishing
description: Application of primer, undercoat, and topcoat finishes to exposed timber or MDF surfaces of the built-in seat.

name: Structural Assessment / Engineer Sign-Off
description: Verification by a structural engineer that the floor, wall, or platform supporting the built-in seat can carry the imposed loads.

name: Skirting Board Integration
description: Fitting or modifying existing skirting boards to align seamlessly with the base of the built-in seat unit.

name: Electrical / Lighting Fit-Out
description: Installation of integrated LED strip lights, reading lights, or USB charging points within the seat unit.

name: Integrated Lighting
description: LED or low-voltage light fittings recessed into or beneath the built-in seat for ambient or task illumination.

name: USB / Power Outlet
description: Electrical outlets or USB charging ports built into the seat unit for convenient device charging.

name: IfcFurnishedSpace
description: The IFC classification used to represent a space that contains or is defined by built-in furniture elements such as fixed seating.

name: Padded Floor Matting
description: Thick, cushioned floor covering installed within the cave space to protect children from injury during play.

name: Crawl Tunnel Entry
description: Low-profile tunnel opening that serves as the primary entrance/exit to the child cave, sized for small children.

name: Soft Interior Lining
description: Foam or fabric lining applied to interior walls and ceiling surfaces to eliminate hard edges and ensure child safety.

name: Low-Level Ambient Lighting
description: Dim, child-safe lighting system installed at low heights or recessed into surfaces to illuminate the cave without harsh glare.

name: Structural Cave Shell
description: The primary load-bearing or self-supporting enclosure that defines the cave's shape, typically formed from timber, GRP, or steel.

name: Child-Safe Latch & Door
description: Miniature door or hatch fitted at the cave entrance with a child-safe, non-locking latch to prevent entrapment.

name: Built-In Bench or Ledge
description: Low-height integrated seating surface inside the cave providing a place to sit, read, or store items.

name: Interactive Wall Panel
description: Tactile or sensory activity panel mounted to the interior wall to support imaginative and educational play.

name: Storage Nook
description: Small recessed alcove within the cave designed for storing toys, books, or personal items.

name: Skylight or Light Well
description: Small overhead glazed opening or light pipe that introduces natural daylight into the cave interior.

name: Non-Slip Surface Finish
description: Textured or rubberised finish applied to the floor of the cave to prevent slipping during active play.

name: Cave Construction & Installation
description: On-site fabrication and fixing of the cave shell, linings, and integrated components within the building.

name: Soft Play Fitout
description: The specialist installation of padded elements, mats, and soft furnishings inside the completed cave structure.

name: Fire Safety & Egress Assessment
description: Compliance activity evaluating escape routes, material fire ratings, and smoke detection requirements for the enclosed cave space.

name: Sensory Play Den
description: A variant of the child cave specifically fitted with multi-sensory stimuli such as fibre optics, textures, and scent elements.

name: Outdoor Play Cave
description: An exterior-grade variant of the child cave constructed with weather-resistant materials for use in outdoor or semi-covered environments.

name: Integrated Sprinkler Head
description: Concealed or low-profile fire suppression sprinkler fitted within the cave ceiling in compliance with fire safety regulations.

name: CCTV Monitoring Point
description: Discreet camera or monitoring system positioned at the cave entry to allow supervising adults to observe children safely.

name: Hidden Room
description: A concealed room within a building that is not visible or accessible through conventional means.

name: Concealed Door
description: A door disguised as a wall panel, bookcase, or other architectural element to hide the entrance to a secret space.

name: Panic Room
description: A fortified hidden room designed to provide safety and refuge during emergencies or security threats.

name: Safe Room
description: A secured, hidden space within a building intended to protect occupants or store valuables.

name: Hidden Passage
description: A concealed corridor or tunnel connecting two areas of a building covertly.

name: Secret Compartment
description: A small hidden cavity within a wall, floor, or furniture designed to store objects discreetly.

name: Priest Hole
description: A historical hiding space built into a structure to conceal a person, traditionally used for religious or political refuge.

name: False Wall
description: A wall constructed to appear as a standard partition while concealing a space or passageway behind it.

name: Trap Door
description: A hinged or sliding panel set flush with a floor or ceiling that provides covert access to a hidden space below or above.

name: Bookcase Door
description: A bookcase unit engineered to pivot or slide and act as a disguised entrance to a hidden area.

name: Hidden Staircase
description: A stairway concealed behind walls or furniture that leads to a secret level or room.

name: Acoustic Isolation System
description: Soundproofing materials and assemblies used to prevent sound from revealing the presence of a hidden space.

name: Biometric Access Control
description: An electronic security system using fingerprint, retinal, or facial recognition to restrict entry to a secret space.

name: Electromagnetic Lock
description: A locking mechanism using magnetic force to secure a concealed door without visible hardware.

name: RFID Keypad System
description: A radio-frequency identification system that grants covert access to a hidden space via a disguised reader.

name: Reinforced Concrete Shell
description: High-strength concrete used to construct the walls and structure of a secure hidden space for blast or intrusion resistance.

name: Ballistic-Resistant Wall Panel
description: Specialized panel material providing bullet and impact resistance within the walls of a secure hidden room.

name: Concealment Cladding
description: Surface finish materials applied to hidden doors and walls to perfectly match surrounding finishes and avoid detection.

name: Ventilation System (Covert)
description: A hidden HVAC or air supply system that maintains air quality in a sealed secret space without external visual cues.

name: Independent Power Supply
description: A dedicated backup power system (UPS/generator) ensuring the hidden space remains functional during power outages.

name: Concealed CCTV System
description: Surveillance cameras disguised within decorative elements to monitor the area surrounding a secret space.

name: Construction of Concealed Spaces
description: The building activity of framing, finishing, and fitting out hidden rooms or passages within a structure.

name: False Wall Installation
description: The construction activity of erecting and finishing partition walls designed to disguise the presence of a hidden area.

name: Concealed Door Fitting
description: The specialist trade activity of installing and aligning disguised door systems to ensure seamless concealment.

name: Soundproofing Installation
description: The construction activity of applying acoustic insulation and barriers to prevent sound transmission from a hidden space.

name: Security System Integration
description: The activity of installing and commissioning access control, surveillance, and alarm systems within a hidden space.

name: Underground Bunker
description: A below-grade fortified hidden space designed for long-term occupation during extreme security or disaster scenarios.

name: Vault Room
description: A highly secured hidden room with reinforced walls and a heavy-duty door for storing high-value assets.

name: IFC Hidden Space Object
description: The IfcSpace IFC class instance used to model and track a concealed or hidden space within a BIM environment.

name: IFC Door (Concealed)
description: The IfcDoor IFC class instance representing a disguised or concealed door element in a BIM model.

name: Community Atrium
description: A tall, multi-story interior void space that anchors social interaction and dictates the structural framing layout around it.

name: Flexible Open Floor Plate
description: A column-free or minimal-column interior space designed to adapt to evolving social and programmatic needs.

name: Transitional Threshold Zone
description: An intermediate spatial buffer—such as a lobby or vestibule—that mediates between public social spaces and private structural zones.

name: Long-Span Structural Frame
description: A structural framing system using trusses, arches, or moment frames to bridge large spans and liberate social floor areas from columns.

name: Transfer Truss
description: A deep truss element spanning over open social zones to carry loads from upper structure to perimeter or core supports.

name: Exoskeleton / External Structure
description: A structural system placed on the building exterior to eliminate interior columns and maximize unobstructed social space within.

name: Raised Pilotis
description: Slender columns that elevate the building off grade, creating a sheltered semi-public social space beneath the structure.

name: Moment-Resisting Connection
description: A rigid structural joint that transfers bending moments, enabling fewer and more strategically placed supports around social areas.

name: Post-Tensioned Flat Slab
description: A prestressed concrete floor system providing maximum clear-span flexibility to accommodate varied social space configurations.

name: High-Strength Structural Steel
description: Steel sections used in long-span beams, trusses, and frames that enable wide, column-free social spaces with minimal material depth.

name: Engineered Timber (Mass Timber)
description: Cross-laminated or glulam timber elements used structurally to create warm, human-scale social environments driven by the wood's spanning capability.

name: Structural Glazing Façade
description: A glass curtain wall system that carries lateral loads and visually connects interior social spaces to the exterior environment.

name: Social Space Programming
description: The design process of defining the size, adjacency, and hierarchy of social spaces that will subsequently dictate structural decisions.

name: Structural Feasibility Assessment
description: An engineering evaluation confirming that proposed social space layouts can be feasibly supported by available structural systems.

name: Integrated Design Workshops
description: Collaborative sessions bringing architects, structural engineers, and stakeholders together to align social space goals with structural strategies.

name: Load Path Analysis
description: The engineering process of tracing gravity and lateral forces through structure configured around socially driven spatial voids and openings.

name: Transfer Structure Installation
description: The on-site construction activity of erecting beams, trusses, or plates that redistribute structural loads around large open social areas.

name: Formwork for Complex Geometry
description: The fabrication and placement of temporary molds shaped to produce curved or irregular structural elements dictated by social space forms.

name: Post-Occupancy Space Evaluation
description: A systematic assessment of how well the structure has enabled or hindered the intended social behaviors and spatial quality after occupation.

name: Floor Plate
description: A horizontal structural diaphragm that spans between supports and distributes lateral and gravity loads.

name: Column Grid
description: The planned spatial layout of vertical structural columns that defines bays and optimises material use.

name: Steel Frame
description: A structural skeleton fabricated from steel sections offering high strength-to-weight ratio for efficient spanning.

name: Moment Frame
description: A rigid structural system where beam-to-column connections resist lateral forces without the need for diagonal bracing.

name: Braced Frame
description: A structural system that uses diagonal bracing members to efficiently resist lateral wind and seismic forces.

name: Flat Plate System
description: A two-way concrete slab system supported directly on columns, eliminating beams for maximum floor-to-floor efficiency.

name: Post-Tensioning System
description: A method of pre-stressing concrete with tensioned cables to achieve thinner slabs and longer spans.

name: Space Frame
description: A three-dimensional truss system that distributes loads in multiple directions for highly efficient long-span roofs.

name: Structural Analysis
description: The engineering process of calculating load paths and member sizes to optimise structural efficiency before construction.

name: Structural Engineering Design
description: The professional activity of designing structural members, connections, and systems to achieve safety and material efficiency.

name: Prefabrication and Modular Assembly
description: Off-site manufacturing of structural components to improve precision, reduce waste, and accelerate on-site construction.

name: Concrete Formwork and Pouring
description: The activity of constructing temporary moulds and placing concrete to form efficient structural elements in situ.

name: Load Path Optimisation
description: An engineering activity focused on directing forces through the shortest and most direct routes to minimise material usage.

name: Structural Health Monitoring
description: Ongoing instrumentation and inspection activities that track structural performance and detect inefficiencies or defects over time.

name: Sustainable Timber
description: Responsibly sourced or certified wood used for structural, cladding, or interior finish applications.

name: Recycled Steel
description: Steel produced from reclaimed scrap metal, reducing embodied carbon in structural and secondary elements.

name: Low-Carbon Concrete
description: Concrete mix incorporating supplementary cementitious materials (e.g., fly ash, GGBS) to reduce CO₂ emissions.

name: Natural Insulation
description: Insulation products derived from renewable or bio-based sources such as hemp, sheep wool, or cork.

name: Recycled Content Insulation
description: Thermal insulation manufactured partly or wholly from post-consumer or post-industrial recycled material.

name: Rammed Earth
description: Compacted natural subsoil used as a load-bearing or non-load-bearing wall material with high thermal mass.

name: Hempcrete
description: Bio-composite building material combining hemp hurds and lime binder, used for insulating walls.

name: Bamboo
description: Fast-growing grass used as a structural or finish material owing to its high strength-to-weight ratio.

name: Breathable Membrane
description: Vapour-permeable sheet material installed in wall or roof build-ups to manage moisture while preventing air infiltration.

name: Non-Toxic Paint & Coatings
description: Interior and exterior finishes formulated without harmful VOCs or heavy metals for healthier indoor environments.

name: Photovoltaic Glazing
description: Glass units with integrated solar cells that generate electricity while functioning as a building envelope element.

name: Aerogel Insulation Panel
description: Ultra-thin, high-performance insulation panel based on silica aerogel, used where space is at a premium.

name: Embodied Carbon Assessment
description: Whole-life carbon calculation process evaluating greenhouse gas emissions associated with material extraction, manufacture, and transport.

name: Material Lifecycle Analysis (LCA)
description: Systematic evaluation of environmental impacts of building materials across all life stages from cradle to grave.

name: Material Specification & Scheduling
description: Process of selecting, documenting, and scheduling approved materials in project specifications and NBS clauses.

name: Sustainable Procurement
description: Procurement strategy that prioritises certified, low-impact, or locally sourced materials and products.

name: Materials Testing & Certification
description: On-site or laboratory testing and third-party certification of materials to verify compliance with standards.

name: Deconstruction & Disassembly Planning
description: Design-stage activity that plans for end-of-life material recovery, reuse, and recyclability.

name: Material Passport Creation
description: Documentation activity that records material identity, location, quantity, and recovery potential for future reuse.

name: Waste Minimisation Planning
description: Pre-construction planning to reduce material offcuts and site waste through efficient ordering and cutting schedules.

name: Green Label / EPD Verification
description: Review and validation of Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) or ecolabels for specified materials.

name: Circular Economy Materials Strategy
description: Project-wide system for tracking material flows to maximise reuse, recycling, and minimal waste to landfill.

name: Material Information Management System
description: Digital platform or BIM-linked database for storing, querying, and auditing material data across a project.

name: Supply Chain Traceability System
description: System for verifying and documenting the origin and chain of custody of materials from source to site.

name: Healthy Materials Library
description: Dedicated physical or virtual repository of vetted, low-toxicity material samples and data sheets for design teams.

name: On-Site Materials Store
description: Secure, weather-protected storage area on a construction site for managing and protecting materials prior to installation.

name: IfcMaterial
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcMaterialDefinition.

name: IfcMaterialConstituentSet
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcMaterialDefinition.

name: Moment-Resisting Frame
description: A structural frame system where beam-column connections are rigid, allowing the frame to resist lateral loads through bending stiffness that can be tuned per floor level.

name: Outrigger System
description: A structural system connecting a central core to perimeter columns via stiff arms, strategically placed at multiple levels to step up overall building stiffness.

name: Tuned Mass Damper
description: A dynamic device installed in a structure to counteract vibrations, complementing the stiffness gradient by absorbing energy at critical frequencies.

name: Base Isolation System
description: A seismic isolation strategy placed at the base of a building that decouples the structure from ground motion, forming the softest point in a stiffness gradient.

name: Progressive Concrete Wall Thickening
description: A design strategy where reinforced concrete walls are specified with decreasing thickness from base to top, physically embodying the gradual stiffening principle.

name: Steel-Concrete Composite Section
description: A hybrid structural member combining steel and concrete to achieve a calibrated stiffness level at specific floors within a graded stiffness scheme.

name: Stiffness Gradient Zone
description: A defined vertical band or story range within a building where structural properties are intentionally varied to achieve a targeted stiffness transition.

name: Mechanical Plant Floor
description: A dedicated full floor reserved for mechanical equipment that often doubles as a stiffening belt-truss level within a tall building's stiffness strategy.

name: Belt Truss Level
description: A story height occupied by perimeter belt trusses that tie the facade columns together and stiffen the building at a discrete elevation.

name: Structural Analysis and Stiffness Tuning
description: The engineering design activity of modeling and iteratively adjusting member stiffnesses across building levels to meet drift and frequency targets.

name: Lateral Load Testing
description: A construction-phase or post-construction activity involving physical or analytical testing to verify the actual lateral stiffness of each structural zone.

name: Staged Concrete Pouring
description: The controlled sequencing of concrete placement in walls and cores by zone to match design stiffness values and manage differential shortening.

name: Seismic Performance-Based Design
description: A design methodology that explicitly targets stiffness and ductility at each level to achieve prescribed seismic performance objectives.

name: Inter-Story Drift Monitoring
description: An ongoing monitoring activity measuring relative horizontal displacement between floors to confirm the stiffness gradient is performing as designed under loading.

name: Soft Story
description: A floor level with significantly lower lateral stiffness than adjacent floors, representing the inverse extreme of gradual stiffening that must be identified and mitigated.

name: Setback Structure
description: A building form where floor plates reduce in plan area with height, naturally reducing mass and stiffness demand in a stepped manner aligned with gradual stiffening.

name: Diagrid System
description: A diagonal grid of interconnected steel members forming the building envelope that inherently provides a distributed, tunable stiffness profile along the building height.

name: Viscous Fluid Damper
description: A velocity-dependent energy dissipation device installed between structural members to supplement stiffness and reduce dynamic response in targeted zones.

name: Concrete Mix Specification by Zone
