description: The practice of specifying progressively higher compressive-strength concrete mixes at lower floors to contribute to the intended stiffness gradient of the structural system.

name: Ridge
description: The highest horizontal line of the roof where two opposing roof slopes meet at the apex.

name: Gable
description: The triangular section of an end wall between the edges of a pitched roof and the top of the wall beneath.

name: Roof Pitch
description: The slope or angle of a roof surface, typically expressed as a ratio of rise to horizontal run.

name: Roof Span
description: The horizontal distance measured between the supporting walls or beams across which the roof structure extends.

name: Roof Overhang
description: The horizontal projection of the roof beyond the exterior wall face, providing weather protection and shading.

name: Rooflight Kerb
description: A raised upstand frame around a roof opening that supports a skylight or rooflight above the deck level.

name: Roof Membrane
description: A continuous waterproof layer applied to flat or low-slope roofs to prevent water penetration into the structure below.

name: Roof Decking
description: The structural panel or board layer fixed to roof framing that provides the base surface for waterproofing or tiling.

name: Roof Battens
description: Horizontal timber or metal strips fixed to rafters to provide the fixing substrate for roof tiles or slates.

name: Pitched Roof Space
description: The enclosed triangular volume beneath a sloped roof, which may be used as an attic, loft, or habitable room.

name: Green Roof Area
description: A designated roof zone covered with vegetation and growing media to provide ecological, thermal, and stormwater benefits.

name: Plant Room Zone
description: A dedicated area on or within the roof layout reserved for mechanical and electrical plant and equipment.

name: Roof Framing System
description: The structural assembly of rafters, purlins, trusses, or beams that supports the roof covering and transfers loads to walls.

name: Solar PV Array
description: Photovoltaic panels mounted on the roof surface to convert solar radiation into electrical energy for the building.

name: Roof Waterproofing Works
description: The construction activity of applying membranes, coatings, or overlapping sheet materials to create a watertight roof surface.

name: Roof Tiling and Slating
description: The trade activity of fixing individual tile or slate units to battens to form the finished weatherproof covering of a pitched roof.

name: Roof Framing Erection
description: The on-site assembly and fixing of structural roof members including rafters, trusses, and purlins.

name: Roof Inspection and Survey
description: A periodic assessment activity to evaluate the condition, integrity, and performance of all roof components and coverings.

name: IfcCovering (Roofing)
description: An IFC class used to represent non-structural roof covering layers such as tiles, membranes, or insulation boards.

name: Floor Slab
description: The structural concrete or composite slab that forms the base layer of a floor system, providing load-bearing support.

name: Ceiling Plenum
description: The concealed space between the structural floor above and the suspended ceiling below, used for routing MEP services.

name: Floor Screed
description: A cementitious or anhydrite layer applied over the structural slab to provide a smooth, level surface for floor finishes.

name: Floor Finish
description: The top visible layer of flooring material such as tiles, hardwood, carpet, or vinyl that defines the walking surface.

name: Vapor Barrier Membrane
description: A moisture-resistant sheet membrane integrated into the floor build-up to prevent vapour migration and damp ingress.

name: Ceiling Tile
description: Individual panel units—mineral fibre, gypsum, or metal—that are laid into or fixed to a ceiling grid to form the finished ceiling face.

name: Ceiling Grid Runner
description: The T-bar metal framing members that interlock to create the structural lattice of a suspended ceiling grid.

name: Hanger Rod
description: A vertical threaded or wire rod that suspends the ceiling grid from the structural soffit above.

name: Floor Joist
description: Horizontal structural members spanning between beams or walls to support the floor deck in timber or light-gauge steel construction.

name: Beam and Block Floor
description: A ground-floor system composed of precast concrete T-beams infilled with dense aggregate or lightweight blocks.

name: Floor Levelling Compound
description: A self-levelling cementitious product poured over uneven subfloors to achieve a flat, defect-free substrate before finishing.

name: Ceiling Cornice
description: A decorative moulding fixed at the junction between wall and ceiling to conceal the joint and provide architectural detail.

name: Downlight Recess
description: A pre-formed or cut aperture in the ceiling layer designed to house recessed luminaires flush with the ceiling surface.

name: Floor Survey and Setting Out
description: The site activity of establishing reference levels, datum points, and grid lines to guide accurate floor and ceiling installation.

name: Ceiling Grid Installation
description: The trade activity of fixing hanger rods, running mains, and cross-tees to assemble and level the suspended ceiling framework.

name: Flatness and Level Survey
description: A precision survey activity using laser levels or optical instruments to verify that completed floors meet specified surface regularity standards.

name: Floor Void
description: The accessible or inaccessible cavity between two floor layers or beneath a raised floor used for service distribution.

name: Structural Soffit
description: The exposed underside surface of the structural floor slab or beam, which may be left exposed or receive a ceiling finish below.

name: Interior Wall Lining
description: An internal layer added to the inside face of an existing outer wall to increase overall wall thickness and improve thermal or acoustic performance.

name: Exterior Cladding Layer
description: An outer-facing panel or material system applied to the outside of the existing wall to add thickness, protection, and aesthetic finish.

name: Cavity Fill Insulation
description: Blown or injected insulation material used to fill the void created between existing and new wall layers.

name: Structural Masonry Leaf
description: An additional leaf of brick, block, or stone construction added as a primary load-bearing or stabilising element to thicken the wall.

name: Stud Frame Infill
description: A timber or metal stud framework built against the existing wall face to create a service cavity and support insulation and lining boards.

name: External Wall Insulation System (EWIS)
description: A proprietary composite system of insulation, adhesive, mechanical fixings, render, and finish applied to the external face of a wall.

name: Internal Wall Insulation System (IWIS)
description: A proprietary composite system of insulation and lining boards applied to the internal face of an outer wall to improve thermal performance without altering the exterior appearance.

name: Cavity Closer
description: A pre-formed section used at window and door reveals to seal the edge of the enlarged cavity, maintaining continuity of insulation and weather tightness.

name: Air Barrier System
description: A continuous layer of airtight materials and sealed junctions within the wall assembly that minimises uncontrolled air movement through the thickened construction.

name: Thermal Bridge Mitigation Detail
description: Engineered junctions, brackets, or breaks designed to interrupt conductive heat paths at interfaces such as floor edges, window frames, and wall corners.

name: Window Reveal Extension
description: A framed or formed enlargement of the window opening jamb, sill, and head to accommodate the increased wall depth after thickening.

name: Mechanical Fixing Anchor
description: A screw, bolt, or proprietary anchor used to secure insulation boards, cladding rails, or new wall layers back to the existing substrate.

name: Wall Thickening Design & Specification
description: The architectural and engineering design process that determines the composition, dimensions, and detailing of the thickened wall assembly.

name: Substrate Preparation & Repair
description: Site work to clean, stabilise, and repair defects in the existing wall surface before new layers are applied.

name: Cladding or Render Application
description: The process of applying the outermost protective and decorative finish layer to the external face of the thickened wall.

name: Airtightness Testing
description: A pressure-differential test (e.g., blower door) carried out after construction to verify that the wall assembly meets air-leakage performance targets.

name: Thermal Performance Modelling (U-value Calculation)
description: Computational analysis used to predict the steady-state heat loss through the proposed thickened wall build-up and confirm regulatory compliance.

name: Fire-Stopping & Cavity Barrier Installation
description: The installation of intumescent or mineral wool barriers within wall cavities and at junctions to contain fire spread within the thickened assembly.

name: Party Wall / Boundary Condition Assessment
description: A legal and spatial review to confirm that wall thickening does not encroach on adjacent properties or violate planning constraints.

name: Heritage / Conservation Constraint Assessment
description: An appraisal of planning and heritage restrictions that may limit the choice of external thickening methods on listed or conservation-area buildings.

name: Façade Zone (Increased Depth)
description: The additional spatial zone created between the original wall plane and the new outer or inner face as a result of thickening, affecting usable floor area and room dimensions.

name: Service Cavity Within Wall
description: A purposely created void within the thickened wall assembly used to route electrical conduits, plumbing pipes, or mechanical services without penetrating the insulation layer.

name: Interstitial Condensation Zone
description: The region within the wall cross-section where dew-point conditions may occur, requiring careful design to prevent moisture accumulation and degradation.

name: Corner Beam
description: A horizontal structural member spanning between corner columns to frame the perimeter of the space.

name: Corner Tie Beam
description: A tie or grade beam connecting corner column footings to resist lateral spreading and differential settlement.

name: Column Reinforcement Cage
description: The assembled rebar skeleton (longitudinal bars and stirrups) placed inside a concrete corner column before casting.

name: Corner Column Splice
description: A mechanical or welded connection joining two column segments at an intermediate storey at a building corner.

name: Column Cladding / Encasement
description: Protective or decorative finish material (stone, GRC, drywall) applied around the exposed corner column.

name: Corner Column Layout / Grid Intersection
description: The plan-grid node or zone at the building corner where column centrelines from two axes intersect.

name: Column Clear Height Zone
description: The unobstructed vertical space between the top of a column base and the underside of the beam or slab above.

name: Perimeter Structural Frame System
description: The integrated framework of corner and intermediate columns with connecting beams that defines the building's outer structural boundary.

name: Column Formwork System
description: The temporary mould system (proprietary or bespoke) erected around a corner column prior to concrete placement.

name: Column Setting-Out & Survey
description: On-site surveying activity to accurately locate and mark corner column centrelines from the structural grid.

name: Column Excavation & Pit Preparation
description: Earthworks activity to excavate the ground to the required depth for each corner column footing.

name: Column Footing Concrete Pouring
description: Placement and compaction of concrete into the prepared footing formwork at each corner column location.

name: Column Rebar Fabrication & Fixing
description: Cutting, bending, and tying of reinforcement steel into a cage ready for installation within the column formwork.

name: Column Concrete Pouring & Curing
description: Casting fresh concrete into the column formwork and applying curing procedures to achieve design strength.

name: Steel Column Erection & Bolting
description: Lifting, aligning, and permanently connecting steel corner columns to baseplates and connecting beams.

name: Column Inspection & Load Testing
description: Structural inspection and non-destructive or load testing to verify integrity and capacity of completed corner columns.

name: Column Fire Protection Application
description: Application of intumescent paint, boarding, or sprayed fire-resistant material to corner columns to achieve required fire ratings.

name: Bi-Axial Bending Design
description: Structural engineering analysis and design process addressing simultaneous bending about both axes in a corner column.

name: Column-to-Slab Connection Detail
description: The structural detailing (drop panel, column head, punching shear reinforcement) at the interface of a corner column and flat slab.

name: IFC Column (IfcColumn)
description: The IFC schema class used to model any vertical structural column element, including corner columns, in a BIM environment.

name: IFC Footing (IfcFooting)
description: The IFC schema class representing the isolated footing foundation element beneath each corner column.

name: IFC Beam (IfcBeam)
description: The IFC schema class used to model beams spanning between corner columns along the building perimeter.

name: Transfer Column
description: A column that terminates above grade and transfers its load to a transfer beam or plate, enabling column layout changes between floors.

name: Column Spacing
description: The centre-to-centre distance between adjacent columns, directly influencing beam spans, slab thickness, and overall structural efficiency.

name: Column Bay
description: The rectangular or polygonal floor area bounded by four or more columns, defining the primary structural module of a floor plate.

name: Column Drop Panel
description: A localised thickening of a flat slab directly above a column that improves shear and bending resistance at the column-slab interface.

name: Column Splice Connection
description: A structural joint that connects two column segments vertically, ensuring continuity of axial and moment transfer between floors.

name: Column Setout Survey
description: The site survey activity of precisely marking column positions on the slab or ground in accordance with the structural grid drawings.

name: Column Formwork Installation
description: The temporary shuttering erected around a column position to contain and shape freshly poured concrete until it achieves adequate strength.

name: Column Reinforcement Fixing
description: The activity of bending, placing, and tying steel rebar cages within column formwork prior to concrete placement.

name: Column Concrete Pouring
description: The controlled placement and compaction of concrete into prepared column formwork to form the structural column element.

name: Column Stripping
description: The removal of column formwork after concrete has cured to the required strength, exposing the finished column surface.

name: Column Load Path Analysis
description: The engineering process of tracing vertical and lateral forces through each column from the roof to the foundations to verify structural adequacy.

name: Column Schedule
description: A structured design document listing each column's mark, dimensions, reinforcement details, and concrete grade for construction reference.

name: Column Eccentricity
description: The offset distance between a column's geometric centroid and the applied load resultant, introducing bending moments that must be designed for.

name: Slenderness Ratio
description: The ratio of a column's effective length to its least radius of gyration, determining susceptibility to buckling failure.

name: Punching Shear Zone
description: The critical perimeter area around a column-slab interface where punching shear stresses are checked and reinforced against failure.

name: Column Fire Protection
description: Intumescent coatings, concrete encasement, or board systems applied to columns to achieve required fire resistance ratings.

name: Column Inspection and Testing
description: Quality assurance activities including plumb checks, cover meter surveys, and core sampling to verify column construction compliance.

name: Pad Foundation
description: An isolated square or rectangular footing used to support a single column or concentrated point load.

name: Pile Foundation
description: Deep slender structural elements driven or cast into the ground to transfer loads to competent bearing strata below.

name: Caisson Foundation
description: A watertight deep foundation element constructed by excavating and filling with concrete, used in waterlogged or deep soil conditions.

name: Micro-pile
description: A small-diameter drilled and grouted pile used where access is limited or where high-capacity support is needed in restricted spaces.

name: Reinforcement Steel (Rebar)
description: Steel bars or mesh embedded in concrete foundation elements to provide tensile strength and resist cracking.

name: Lean Concrete Fill
description: A low-strength concrete mix used to fill voids, stabilise ground, or provide a working platform beneath structural foundations.

name: Sub-grade
description: The in-situ soil or rock layer directly beneath the foundation that provides the primary bearing support for the structure.

name: Foundation Drainage System
description: An integrated network of perforated pipes, sumps, and aggregate designed to collect and redirect groundwater away from foundation elements.

name: Ground Improvement System
description: Engineered techniques such as compaction grouting, vibro-compaction, or soil stabilisation used to enhance bearing capacity before foundation construction.

name: Shoring System
description: Temporary or permanent structural supports including sheet piles, soldier piles, and struts installed to retain soil during excavation.

name: Dewatering System
description: Pumps, wellpoints, and drainage infrastructure used to lower the groundwater table during foundation excavation and construction.

name: Soil Investigation
description: Geotechnical surveys including borehole drilling, sampling, and testing to characterise soil properties and determine appropriate foundation design.

name: Foundation Excavation
description: The controlled removal of soil or rock to the specified depth and extent required for placing foundation elements.

name: Concrete Pouring (Foundations)
description: Placing and consolidating fresh concrete into formwork or excavated profiles to form structural foundation elements.

name: Foundation Waterproofing Application
description: The process of applying membranes, coatings, or tanking systems to below-grade surfaces to achieve water resistance.

name: Foundation Load Testing
description: Static or dynamic tests performed on trial piles or footings to verify bearing capacity and load-settlement behaviour.

name: Subgrade Soil
description: The compacted native or imported soil layer beneath the slab that provides the primary load-bearing foundation support.

name: Granular Sub-base Layer
description: A compacted layer of gravel or crushed stone placed over the subgrade to improve drainage and distribute loads evenly.

name: Blinding Concrete Layer
description: A thin lean-mix concrete layer poured over the sub-base to create a clean, level working surface before reinforcement placement.

name: Damp Proof Membrane
description: A polyethylene or similar sheet barrier installed beneath the slab to prevent ground moisture from migrating upward into the structure.

name: Perimeter Edge Formwork
description: Temporary or permanent boarding fixed around the slab perimeter to contain poured concrete and define the slab's boundary shape.

name: Reinforcement Bar Mesh
description: Steel rebar or welded wire fabric placed within the slab thickness to resist tensile and flexural stresses during loading.

name: Concrete Mix
description: The structural concrete, specified by grade and mix design, that forms the primary body of the ground floor slab.

name: Slip Membrane
description: A thin polythene sheet placed between the blinding and the slab to allow thermal and shrinkage movement without friction restraint.

name: Underfloor Heating Pipework
description: A network of embedded heating pipes cast into the slab to provide radiant floor heating to the occupied space above.

name: Slab Thickening / Downstand Beam
description: A localised increase in slab depth or an integral downstand rib used to carry additional point loads or span greater distances.

name: Construction Joints
description: Planned discontinuities formed between successive concrete pours to control cracking and accommodate differential movement.

name: Movement / Expansion Joints
description: Deliberate gaps with compressible filler allowing the slab to expand and contract thermally without inducing damaging stresses.

name: Crack-Control Saw-Cut Joints
description: Post-pour sawing of shallow lines into the hardened slab surface to predetermine where controlled shrinkage cracking will occur.

name: Steel Fibre Reinforcement
description: Discrete steel fibres blended into the concrete mix to enhance ductility and reduce shrinkage cracking as an alternative to mesh.

name: Surface Power Floating
description: Mechanical finishing of the fresh concrete surface using rotating float blades to achieve a smooth, dense, and level wearing surface.

name: Surface Hardener / Sealer Application
description: Application of chemical hardeners or sealers to the cured slab surface to improve abrasion resistance and reduce dusting.

name: Subgrade Compaction
description: Mechanical compaction of the soil or granular layers beneath the slab to achieve specified density and bearing-capacity values.

name: Concrete Pouring and Placing
description: The site operation of transporting, placing, and consolidating fresh concrete within the formwork to form the slab body.

name: Radon Barrier / Gas-Resistant Membrane
description: A sealed membrane system incorporated under or within the slab to prevent ingress of ground gases such as radon into the building.

name: Drainage Channel / Floor Drain
description: Cast-in drainage channels or point drains recessed into the slab to manage surface water or process liquid run-off.

name: Holding-Down Bolt Cast-In
description: Pre-positioned anchor bolts or sleeves cast into the slab to provide fixing points for structural columns, machinery, or partitions.

name: Conduit and Service Duct
description: Embedded electrical conduits, drainage pipes, or service ducts cast into the slab for concealed routing of building services.

name: IfcSlab (Ground Floor)
description: The IFC schema class used to digitally represent and exchange the ground floor slab element within BIM models.

name: IfcMember (Downstand Beam)
description: The IFC class representing integral downstand beams or ribs that are part of the slab structural assembly in BIM data.

name: IfcBuildingStorey (Ground Floor Level)
description: The IFC spatial structure element that defines the ground floor storey to which the slab is assigned in a BIM model.

name: Polished Concrete Floor Finish
description: A finished wearing surface achieved by mechanically grinding and polishing the top of the structural slab as a final floor treatment.

name: Screed Topping Layer
description: A sand-cement or flowing anhydrite layer applied on top of the structural slab to achieve precise levels and embed services.

name: Pile Cap / Ground Beam
description: A structural element sitting below or integrated with the slab edge to transfer loads to piles or pad foundations in poor ground conditions.

name: Steel Box Column
description: A hollow, rectangular or square structural column fabricated from steel plates welded together to form a closed box section.

name: Concrete-Filled Steel Tube Column (CFST)
description: A box column variant where the hollow steel section is filled with concrete to enhance load-bearing capacity and fire resistance.

name: Reinforced Concrete Box Column
description: A box-shaped column cast from reinforced concrete, providing high compressive strength for heavy structural loads.

name: Composite Box Column
description: A column combining steel and concrete elements within a box cross-section to optimize structural performance.

name: Column Cap Plate
description: A flat steel plate welded to the top of a box column to provide a bearing surface for connecting beams or trusses.

name: Diaphragm Plate
description: An internal stiffening plate inserted horizontally inside a box column at beam connection levels to distribute concentrated forces.

name: Web Stiffener
description: A vertical plate welded inside the box column walls to prevent local buckling under high axial or bending loads.

name: Shear Connector Stud
description: A headed stud welded to the interior or exterior of a box column to ensure composite action between steel and concrete.

name: Beam-to-Column Moment Connection
description: A rigid connection detail at the face of the box column that transfers both shear and bending moment from framing beams.

name: Fire Protection Casing
description: An intumescent coating, spray-applied fireproofing, or board encasement applied around the box column to achieve required fire ratings.

name: Corrosion Protection Coating
description: A primer and topcoat paint system or galvanizing layer applied to the steel box column surfaces to prevent oxidation.

name: Grout Bed
description: Non-shrink cementitious or epoxy grout placed beneath the column base plate to ensure full and even bearing on the foundation.

name: Anchor Bolt Group
description: A set of high-strength bolts cast into the foundation to secure the column base plate and resist uplift and shear forces.

name: Column Erection
description: The crane-assisted lifting and plumbing of box column sections into their final position within the structural frame.

name: Column Fabrication
description: Shop-based cutting, fitting, and welding of steel plates to produce the box column section to specified dimensions and tolerances.

name: Column Welding Inspection
description: Non-destructive testing (UT/MT) and visual examination of welds on box column sections to verify structural integrity.

name: Column Base Grouting
description: Placement and curing of non-shrink grout beneath the base plate after column alignment to achieve full bearing.

name: Fireproofing Application
description: Site or shop application of fire-resistant material to the exterior surfaces of the box column to comply with building codes.

name: Column Survey & Plumb Check
description: Theodolite or total-station survey activity confirming the erected box column is within vertical tolerance before final connection.

name: Column Painting & Coating
description: Field or shop application of corrosion-protective paint systems to the steel box column after fabrication or erection.

name: Column Chase / Enclosure Space
description: The architectural recess or enclosure built around a structural box column to conceal it within a wall or finish element.

name: IfcStructuralPointConnection
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcStructuralConnection.

name: Ring Beam
description: A continuous perimeter beam that ties together the tops of walls or columns to distribute lateral and vertical loads around the building envelope.

name: Upstand Beam
description: A perimeter beam that projects above the floor slab level, commonly used at roof edges to provide parapet support and restraint.

name: Downstand Beam
description: A perimeter beam that projects below the floor slab soffit, increasing structural depth while keeping the top face flush with the slab.

name: Steel Perimeter Beam
description: A hot-rolled or fabricated steel section used as the perimeter beam, offering high strength-to-weight ratio and flexibility in connection detailing.

name: Precast Concrete Perimeter Beam
description: A factory-cast reinforced or prestressed concrete beam delivered to site as a finished unit for rapid installation at the building perimeter.

name: In-Situ Reinforced Concrete Perimeter Beam
description: A perimeter beam cast on-site using formwork and reinforcing bars, allowing integration with monolithic slab and column construction.

name: Glulam Perimeter Beam
description: An engineered timber perimeter beam made from glued laminated lumber, used in timber-framed structures for its structural performance and aesthetic appeal.

name: Composite Perimeter Beam
description: A perimeter beam system in which a steel section acts compositely with a concrete slab via shear connectors, increasing load-carrying efficiency.

name: Perimeter Beam Formwork System
description: A temporary falsework and shuttering assembly used to form and support in-situ concrete perimeter beams during casting and curing.

name: Perimeter Beam Reinforcement Cage
description: A pre-assembled arrangement of longitudinal bars, stirrups, and links that provides tensile and shear reinforcement within a concrete perimeter beam.

name: Shear Connector (Perimeter Beam)
description: A headed stud or other mechanical device welded to the top flange of a steel perimeter beam to achieve composite action with the concrete deck.

name: Beam-to-Column Connection (Perimeter)
description: The structural joint detail — bolted, welded, or cast — that transfers moment and shear between a perimeter beam and its supporting column.

name: Perimeter Beam Bearing Pad
description: A neoprene, steel, or concrete pad placed beneath a precast or steel perimeter beam end to distribute bearing stresses and accommodate movement.

name: Facade Bracket on Perimeter Beam
description: A steel bracket welded or bolted to the perimeter beam to provide anchorage and support for external cladding or curtain-wall systems.

name: Fire Protection of Perimeter Beam
description: The passive fire protection system — intumescent coating, board encasement, or concrete cover — applied to perimeter beams to achieve required fire resistance ratings.

name: Perimeter Beam Installation
description: The on-site construction activity involving lifting, positioning, and securing perimeter beam elements using cranes and specialist rigging.

name: Perimeter Beam Reinforcement Fixing
description: The trade activity of cutting, bending, and tying reinforcing bars into the correct configuration within perimeter beam formwork prior to concrete placement.

name: Perimeter Beam Concrete Pouring
description: The construction activity of placing and compacting fresh concrete into perimeter beam formwork, including vibration and curing procedures.

name: Perimeter Beam Welding
description: The fabrication or site activity of making structural welds at steel perimeter beam connections and shear stud attachments.

name: Perimeter Beam Survey & Setting Out
description: The surveying activity that establishes precise horizontal and vertical alignment of perimeter beams relative to grid lines and level datums.

name: Perimeter Beam Load Testing
description: A structural quality-assurance activity that verifies the load-carrying capacity and deflection behaviour of installed perimeter beams.

name: Floor Slab (Perimeter Zone)
description: The structural deck area directly supported by or cast integrally with perimeter beams, defining the usable floor space at the building edge.

name: Perimeter Structural Bay
description: The repetitive structural zone between adjacent perimeter columns that is bounded and defined by the perimeter beam grid.

name: IfcBeam (Perimeter)
description: The IFC schema entity used to represent perimeter beam elements in a BIM model, capturing geometry, material, and connectivity data.

name: IfcMember (Perimeter Edge)
description: An IFC class used for linear structural members at the building perimeter that do not strictly fit the primary beam classification, such as edge channels or rim members.

name: Air Barrier Membrane
description: A continuous membrane system designed to minimise uncontrolled air movement through the wall assembly.

name: Self-Adhesive Membrane
description: A peel-and-stick bituminous or polymeric sheet membrane that bonds directly to the wall substrate without additional adhesive.

name: Bituminous Membrane
description: An asphalt or coal-tar based sheet or torch-applied membrane providing robust moisture and waterproofing protection to wall assemblies.

name: Polyethylene Sheeting
description: A low-cost plastic film used as a basic vapour barrier or temporary weather protection within wall construction.

name: Cavity Tray
description: A pre-formed or flexible tray membrane installed within a cavity wall to collect and redirect water to weep holes, preventing moisture ingress.

name: Flashing Membrane
description: A strip or sheet membrane installed at junctions, openings, and terminations to seal transitions and direct water away from the wall assembly.

name: Membrane Protection Board
description: A rigid or semi-rigid board installed over a waterproofing membrane to shield it from mechanical damage during backfilling or cladding installation.

name: Membrane Termination Bar
description: A metal or plastic bar used to mechanically secure and seal the top edge of a wall membrane to prevent water tracking behind it.

name: Membrane Primer
description: A preparatory coating applied to wall substrates to improve adhesion and compatibility before membrane installation.

name: Membrane Adhesive
description: A solvent-based, water-based, or contact adhesive used to bond sheet membranes fully or partially to the wall substrate.

name: Seam Welding and Lapping
description: The technique of overlapping and heat-welding or solvent-bonding membrane sheet edges to create a continuous, watertight joint.

name: Membrane Testing and Inspection
description: Quality-assurance procedures such as flood testing, spark testing, or visual inspection to verify membrane continuity and watertightness.

name: Membrane Repair and Remediation
description: The patching, re-bonding, or replacement of damaged or failed sections of an installed wall membrane during or after construction.

name: Below-Grade Wall Waterproofing System
description: An integrated assembly of membranes, drainage layers, and protection boards applied to subterranean wall surfaces to manage groundwater.

name: Wall Airtightness Zone
description: The defined spatial boundary within which air barrier membranes must be continuous and sealed to meet building airtightness performance targets.

name: IFCCoveringType
description: The IFC classification used to represent membrane layers and coverings applied to wall surfaces within a building information model.

name: Barrel Vault
description: A semicircular or pointed continuous arch forming the simplest type of vault, spanning between two parallel walls.

name: Groin Vault
description: A vault formed by the intersection of two barrel vaults at right angles, creating distinctive arched groins at the crossing edges.

name: Rib Vault
description: A vault reinforced by a framework of projecting stone or concrete ribs that define and support the surfaces between them.

name: Fan Vault
description: A decorative vault type featuring concave conical surfaces with ribs spreading out like a fan from a single springer point.

name: Pointed Vault
description: A vault variant where the arch profile is pointed rather than semicircular, common in Gothic architecture for structural efficiency.

name: Cloister Vault
description: A vault formed by four curved triangular surfaces rising from a square or rectangular base to a central point or ridge.

name: Domical Vault
description: A vault that rises to a central apex over a polygonal or square bay, resembling a dome in profile.

name: Vault Springer
description: The lowest voussoir or starting stone of a vault arch, positioned at the impost level where the vault meets its support.

name: Vault Keystone
description: The central wedge-shaped stone or element at the crown of a vault arch that locks all other voussoirs in place.

name: Vault Rib
description: A projecting band or molded arch element that runs along the surface of a rib vault to articulate and structurally define the vault geometry.

name: Voussoir
description: An individual wedge-shaped masonry unit used in the construction of a vault or arch that transfers compressive loads.

name: Vault Web (Severy)
description: The infill surface panel of a vault between the ribs, typically constructed of lighter masonry or thin-shell material.

name: Vault Haunch
description: The lower flanking portion of a vault between the springer and the crown, where lateral thrust is highest.

name: Vault Crown
description: The highest point or apex of a vault arch, typically where the keystone is located and compressive forces are at a minimum.

name: Vault Impost
description: The horizontal molding or block at the top of a pier or wall from which a vault arch springs.

name: Centering Formwork
description: Temporary timber or steel falsework framework that supports a vault during construction until the mortar or concrete has cured.

name: Vault Spandrel
description: The triangular or irregular space between the outer curve of a vault arch and the surrounding rectangular enclosure or adjacent arch.

name: Buttress
description: A projecting masonry or concrete support built against a wall to resist the lateral outward thrust generated by a vault.

name: Flying Buttress
description: An arched masonry prop that transmits vault thrust from an upper wall to an outer freestanding pier or abutment.

name: Vault Abutment
description: The solid masonry or concrete mass at each end of a vault that resists and absorbs the horizontal thrust forces.

name: Pendentive
description: A concave triangular surface that transitions between a square bay and a circular dome or vault above it.

name: Squinch
description: A small arch, corbelling, or bracket placed across the corner of a square space to support a vault or dome above.

name: Masonry (Stone)
description: Cut or rubble stone used as the primary structural and finish material in traditional vault construction.

name: Vault Layout & Setting Out
description: The surveying and marking activity used to establish the precise geometry, centerlines, and springer positions of a vault on site.

name: Centering Erection
description: The construction activity of assembling temporary formwork or falsework to support the vault during masonry or concrete placement.

name: Vault Masonry Construction
description: The activity of laying voussoirs, bricks, or stone courses in correct sequence to build up the vault shell.

name: Vault Concrete Casting
description: The activity of pouring and finishing concrete into vault formwork to produce a monolithic curved floor-ceiling structure.

name: Centering Striking (Decentering)
description: The controlled removal of temporary centering after the vault has gained sufficient strength to be self-supporting.

name: Vault Backfill & Haunching
description: The activity of placing fill material above the vault haunches to stabilize the structure and level the floor above.

name: Vault Waterproofing
description: The application of waterproof membranes or coatings to the extrados of a vault to prevent moisture ingress.

name: Structural Analysis of Vaults
description: The engineering activity of calculating thrust lines, load paths, and stability of vault geometry using graphic statics or computational methods.

name: Vault Repair & Repointing
description: The maintenance activity of replacing deteriorated mortar joints and repairing cracked voussoirs in existing masonry vaults.

name: Vault Intrados
description: The inner curved surface of a vault visible from below, often decorated with plasterwork, painting, or carved ornament.

name: Vault Extrados
description: The outer convex surface of a vault shell above which fill, waterproofing, or the floor of the story above is placed.

name: Catalan Vault
description: A thin-shell masonry vault built with multiple layers of flat tiles laid in staggered courses using fast-setting gypsum mortar.

name: Vault Pier
description: A freestanding or engaged vertical support column that carries the concentrated load and thrust from vault springers.

name: IFC Structural Surface Member
description: The IFC class used to represent curved shell or vault structural elements in a building information model.

name: IFC Slab (IfcSlab)
description: The IFC class commonly used to represent floor-ceiling vault elements as curved slab assemblies in BIM workflows.

name: Ribbed Vault
description: A vault reinforced by a framework of diagonal and transverse arched ribs that support the infill web panels.

name: Stilted Vault
description: A vault in which the springing line is raised above the level of the impost, giving greater height to the arch.

name: Spandrel Fill
description: Material packed into the triangular space between the extrados of a vault and the surrounding structure to stabilize and distribute loads.

name: Pier / Vault Support Column
description: A vertical structural element that receives and transfers the concentrated loads from vault ribs down to the foundations.

name: Centering (Falsework)
description: A temporary wooden or steel framework erected to support the vault masonry or formwork during construction until the arch becomes self-supporting.

name: Vault Intrados (Soffit)
description: The visible inner concave surface of the vault as seen from the interior space below.

name: Abutment
description: A solid mass of masonry or concrete that resists the lateral thrust exerted by a vault or arch at its ends.

name: Tie Rod / Tension Rod
description: A metal rod installed between opposing vault supports to counteract outward horizontal thrust without the need for external buttressing.

name: Cut Stone (Ashlar)
description: Precisely cut and dressed stone blocks used for the voussoirs, ribs, and web panels of high-quality masonry vaults.

name: Rubble Masonry
description: Irregularly shaped stones or brick used as infill within vault haunches or webs in utilitarian vault construction.

name: Hydraulic Lime / Pozzolanic Cement
description: A fast-setting binding agent used in vault construction where early strength or moisture resistance is required.

name: Thin-Shell Concrete Vault
description: A modern structural system using a thin reinforced concrete shell following a vaulted form to achieve long spans with minimal material.

name: Masonry Vault Structural System
description: The integrated load-path system of arches, piers, buttresses, and abutments that transfers vault forces safely to the ground.

name: Vault Drainage System
description: The arrangement of gutters, downpipes, and waterproofing layers on the vault extrados to manage rainwater runoff.

name: Vault Lighting System
description: Artificial lighting fixtures and tracks integrated into or mounted below vault surfaces to illuminate the interior space.

name: Vault Centering Erection
description: The construction activity of assembling temporary falsework frames that support vault masonry or formwork during the building process.

name: Vault Formwork Striking
description: The controlled removal of centering or formwork after vault masonry or concrete has achieved sufficient strength to be self-supporting.

name: Vault Waterproofing Application
description: The process of applying membranes, coatings, or lead sheeting to the extrados of a vault to protect it from water penetration.

name: Vault Inspection and Condition Survey
description: The systematic examination of vault ribs, webs, and supports to identify cracks, deformation, moisture damage, or structural movement.

name: Vault Repair and Repointing
description: Maintenance activity involving replacement of deteriorated mortar joints and patching of damaged voussoirs or web masonry.

name: Vault Underpinning
description: Structural intervention activity to stabilize or strengthen failing vault supports, piers, or abutments to arrest or prevent collapse.

name: Operable Casement Window
description: A side-hinged window sash that swings open to allow natural ventilation and light.

name: Fixed Picture Window
description: A non-operable glazed window unit designed purely for daylighting and views without ventilation.

name: Sliding Sash Window
description: A window with one or more panels that slide horizontally or vertically within the frame.

name: Roof Light
description: A flat or pitched transparent panel set into a roof to provide passive daylighting to interior spaces.

name: Pivot Window
description: A window that rotates on a central horizontal or vertical axis, offering flexible ventilation control.

name: Solid Timber Door
description: An interior or exterior door fabricated from solid wood, providing thermal mass and acoustic insulation.

name: Glazed Door
description: A door incorporating full or partial glass panels to borrow natural light between spaces or to the exterior.

name: French Door
description: A pair of full-height glazed doors hinged at opposing jambs that open outward or inward to connect interior and exterior.

name: Bi-fold Door
description: Multiple door panels hinged together that fold back against a wall to create a wide, unobstructed opening.

name: Sliding Patio Door
description: A large glazed door panel that slides along a track to connect an interior room with an outdoor space.

name: Pocket Door
description: A door that slides into a recess within the wall cavity, saving floor space in tight natural-light corridors.

name: Screen Door
description: A secondary mesh-clad door fitted over an opening to allow airflow while excluding insects.

name: Door Frame and Jamb
description: The structural border assembly that anchors a door within a wall opening and supports hinges and latches.

name: Head Flashing
description: A metal or membrane strip installed above a window or door opening to divert water away from the rough opening.

name: Timber Window/Door Frame Material
description: Sustainably sourced wood species used for window and door frames, valued for its natural insulating properties.

name: uPVC Frame Material
description: Unplasticised polyvinyl chloride used for low-maintenance, thermally efficient window and door frames.

name: Aluminium Frame Material
description: Lightweight extruded metal profile used for slim, durable window and door frames with thermal-break technology.

name: Solar Shading System
description: External or internal devices such as overhangs, blinds, and fins coordinated with glazed openings to control solar heat gain.

name: Window Hardware and Ironmongery
description: The collection of handles, hinges, stays, and locking mechanisms that operate and secure windows.

name: Door Hardware and Ironmongery
description: The assembly of hinges, knobs, levers, locks, closers, and thresholds that control door operation and security.

name: Rough Opening Preparation
description: The construction activity of framing and sizing wall apertures to receive door and window units accurately.

name: Flashing and Weatherproofing
description: The application of flashings, membranes, and sealants around openings to create a durable weather-resistant envelope.

name: Window and Door Finishing
description: The application of paint, stain, or cladding to window and door components as part of the decorative build-out.

name: Window Reveal / Jamb Recess
description: The depth of wall between the outer face and the window frame that influences light quality and solar shading.

name: Threshold Space
description: The transitional zone immediately at a doorway that mediates between two different interior or exterior environments.

name: Sill Board
description: The horizontal flat board forming the interior shelf of a low sill, typically at or near floor level.

name: Sill Plate
description: A structural plate element at the base of a low sill that distributes loads and anchors the assembly to the substrate.

name: Sill Nosing
description: The front-edge trim profile of the sill board that provides a finished appearance and protects against wear.

name: Sub-sill
description: A secondary supporting sill installed beneath the primary sill board to provide additional structural depth or level the surface.

name: Sill Flashing
description: A waterproof membrane or metal sheet fitted under and around the sill to prevent water ingress at the low sill junction.

name: Sill Weatherbar
description: A weather-seal strip fixed along the outer edge of the sill to block wind-driven rain and drafts.

name: Sill Drip Edge
description: A projecting metal or PVC edge on the outer face of the sill that directs rainwater away from the wall below.

name: Acoustic Sill Seal
description: A compressible gasket or foam seal integrated into the sill to attenuate sound transmission through the low sill aperture.

name: Low Sill Threshold
description: The transitional element at the base of an opening within a low sill configuration, managing the junction between floor finish and frame.

name: Sill Bracket / Cleat
description: A metal or timber fixing bracket that supports and secures the sill board to the structural wall or frame.

name: Perimeter Sill Trim
description: Decorative or functional trim pieces that cover the gap between the sill board and adjacent wall or floor finishes.

name: Low Sill Window Assembly
description: A complete glazing system designed with its sill positioned at or close to floor level, combining frame, glass, and sill in a coordinated unit.

name: Sill Drainage System
description: A network of channels, weep holes, and outlets built into the sill assembly to manage and evacuate condensation or rainwater.

name: Low Sill Balustrade System
description: A safety barrier system mounted at or above a low sill to provide fall protection where the sill is at or near floor level.

name: Sill Insulation System
description: A coordinated assembly of insulating boards, membranes, and seals designed to achieve target thermal performance at the low sill zone.

name: Low Sill Bay / Alcove
description: A recessed or projecting floor-level window bay formed by the low sill construction, creating usable space such as a window seat area.

name: Window Seat Recess
description: A purposefully designed recessed space immediately above and around the low sill, intended to accommodate built-in seating.

name: Floor-to-Sill Zone
description: The transitional spatial zone between the finished floor level and the low sill head, critical for detailing continuity of insulation and finishes.

name: Sill Substrate / Blockwork
description: The masonry, concrete, or timber substrate upon which the sill assembly is bedded and which provides its primary structural support.

name: Sill Mortar Bed
description: A layer of mortar applied beneath a masonry or stone sill to achieve level bearing and full contact with the substrate.

name: Sill Mastic / Sealant
description: A flexible sealant compound applied at joints between the sill and adjacent frame or wall to provide an airtight and watertight seal.

name: Natural Stone Sill
description: A sill formed from dressed natural stone such as limestone or granite, chosen for durability and aesthetic quality.

name: Precast Concrete Sill
description: A factory-cast concrete sill unit produced to precise dimensions for repetitive installation in a low sill assembly.

name: Timber Sill
description: A sill element fabricated from solid or engineered timber, commonly used in timber-frame or traditional construction.

name: uPVC / Aluminium Sill
description: An extruded plastic or aluminium sill profile offering corrosion resistance, low maintenance, and integration with window frame systems.

name: Sill Installation
description: The site activity of positioning, levelling, bedding, and fixing the sill assembly to the prepared structural opening.

name: Sill Flashing Installation
description: The process of applying and sealing waterproof flashing membranes or metal trays beneath and around the low sill during construction.

name: Sill Sealing & Pointing
description: The finishing activity of filling joints between the sill and surrounding structure with mortar, mastic, or sealant for weathertightness.

name: Sill Thermal Testing
description: An inspection and testing activity using thermography or air-permeability methods to verify thermal and airtightness performance of the sill assembly.

name: Balustrade / Guard Rail Installation
description: The activity of fixing fall-protection barriers to a low sill where the sill height creates a safety risk under building regulations.

name: Sill Replacement / Refurbishment
description: A maintenance or renovation activity involving the removal and renewal of a deteriorated or non-compliant sill assembly.

name: IFC Sill Property Set
description: The IFC property set (e.g., Pset_WindowCommon) that stores sill height, reference level, and related parametric data for a low sill.

name: Reveal Lining
description: The finished interior surface lining applied to the sides of a deep window or door reveal, typically of timber, plasterboard, or stone.

name: Reveal Jamb
description: The vertical side element of a deep reveal that forms the structural or finish boundary between the opening and the wall face.

name: Reveal Soffit
description: The horizontal overhead surface spanning the depth of a deep reveal between the outer wall face and the window or door frame.

name: Reveal Sill
description: The horizontal lower surface at the base of a deep reveal, often sloped for drainage and finished in stone, tile, or render.

name: Window Frame Setback
description: The deliberate positioning of a window frame recessed into the wall thickness to create or enhance the depth of a reveal.

name: Stepped Reveal
description: A reveal variant featuring one or more recessed ledges or offsets along its depth, used for decoration, seating, or shelving.

name: Arched Reveal
description: A deep reveal variant where the inner or outer opening is finished with an arch form, common in masonry construction.

name: Shadow Gap Detail
description: A deliberate recessed joint or gap at the junction of the reveal lining and adjacent surfaces to create a clean visual shadow line.

name: Insulation Infill
description: Thermal or acoustic insulation material packed within the reveal cavity to prevent cold bridging and condensation in deep reveals.

name: Reveal Render / Plaster Finish
description: A coat of render or plaster applied to masonry or blockwork reveal faces to provide a smooth, paintable finished surface.

name: Stone Reveal Facing
description: Natural or reconstituted stone cladding applied to reveal surfaces for durability and aesthetic expression in high-quality construction.

name: Timber Reveal Lining Board
description: Machined timber boards used to line reveal sides, soffits, and sills, typically in joinery-quality finishes for interior reveals.

name: Damp Proof Course at Reveal
description: A moisture barrier installed at the reveal junction to prevent water ingress tracking inward along the wall depth.

name: Reveal Reveal Formwork / Shuttering
description: Temporary formwork used to cast accurate reveal geometry in in-situ concrete construction.

name: Airtightness Membrane at Reveal
description: A continuous airtight membrane or tape applied around the reveal perimeter to seal the junction between frame and wall construction.

name: Window/Door Frame Installation in Deep Reveal
description: The construction activity of accurately positioning and fixing a window or door frame at the correct depth within a thick wall reveal.

name: Reveal Lining Fixing
description: The trade activity of cutting, fitting, and securing finish linings to the sides, soffit, and sill of a reveal opening.

name: Reveal Plastering / Rendering
description: The wet-trade activity of applying plaster or render coats to masonry reveal surfaces to achieve the specified finish.

name: Cavity Closer Installation
description: The activity of fitting insulated cavity closers around the perimeter of an opening before frame installation to seal and insulate the reveal.

name: Reveal Weatherproofing & Sealing
description: Application of sealants, flashings, and weatherstripping at reveal junctions to ensure weather-tightness around the opening.

name: Thermal Bridge Assessment at Reveal
description: An engineering or compliance activity analysing heat loss at reveal junctions to ensure the design meets thermal performance targets.

name: Wall Thickness
description: The overall depth of the wall construction that directly determines the potential depth and proportion of any window or door reveal.

name: Thermal Bridging / Cold Bridge Junction
description: A building physics system concern representing heat-loss pathways at reveal edges where insulation continuity may be compromised.

name: Natural Daylighting Strategy
description: The broader architectural system governing window placement, reveal depth, and splay angles to optimise interior daylight distribution.

name: Door Header
description: The horizontal beam or lintel spanning the top of the doorway opening, which in a low doorway sits at a reduced height.

name: Head Clearance Warning Indicator
description: A visual or tactile marker (e.g., painted stripe, foam pad, sign) attached near the low header to alert occupants of reduced height.

name: Cripple Wall Framing
description: Short stud framing members above the door header filling the space between the header and the ceiling or floor above in a low doorway condition.

name: Rough Opening
description: The framed structural void in a wall sized to receive the door frame, intentionally dimensioned smaller than standard for a low doorway.

name: Reduced-Height Door Opening
description: The clear opening space below the header of a low doorway, typically less than the standard 2000 mm clear height.

name: Transition Space
description: The immediate floor area on either side of the low doorway where occupant posture adjustment (ducking) typically occurs.

name: Masonry Surround
description: Brick, stone, or blockwork forming the walls immediately adjacent to and above a low doorway, common in historic or vernacular construction.

name: Timber Door Frame Material
description: Sawn or engineered timber used to fabricate the frame members of a low doorway, typical in traditional and residential buildings.

name: Steel Door Frame Material
description: Cold-rolled or hot-rolled steel sections formed into a door frame suitable for low doorway applications in commercial or industrial settings.

name: Door Hanging
description: The activity of fitting and adjusting the door leaf onto its hinges within the low doorway frame.

name: Opening Formation
description: Cutting, breaking out, or forming the wall void to the required reduced-height dimensions for a low doorway.

name: Head-Height Survey
description: A measurement and compliance-checking activity to record and verify the clear height of existing or proposed low doorways against applicable standards.

name: Accessibility Assessment
description: An evaluation activity to determine whether the reduced door height meets disability access regulations or requires compensatory design measures.

name: Substandard Doorway
description: A doorway whose clear height falls below the minimum code-required dimension, often flagged during building surveys as a deficiency.

name: Cellar Access Door
description: A traditionally low doorway providing access to a basement or cellar, often found in older residential and historic buildings.

name: Loft Hatch Door
description: A small, low-profile door or hatch opening giving access to a roof space or loft, inherently limited in height by the sloping ceiling.

name: Crawl Space Access Door
description: A very low doorway or hatch providing entry to an under-floor crawl space, sized only for maintenance access.

name: Structural Frame Member
description: An individual load-bearing bar, post, or beam that forms the skeleton of a thickened-edge frame and defines its depth and profile.

name: Thickened Edge Beam
description: A deep or widened beam running along the perimeter or interior of a space whose visible bulk is deliberately expressed as an architectural feature.

name: Thickened Edge Column
description: A column enlarged beyond its structural minimum so that it reads as a fat, wall-like vertical edge within or around a space.

name: Space Frame System
description: A three-dimensional trussed grid whose depth and lattice density give the appearance of a thick structural edge enclosing or defining a volume.

name: Vierendeel Frame System
description: A rectangular open-web frame without diagonals that transfers loads through rigid joints, producing a deep, grid-like thickened edge suitable for inhabited or service-bearing frames.

name: Interstitial Service Space
description: The occupiable or accessible cavity within the depth of a thickened frame that accommodates mechanical, electrical, or plumbing services.

name: Inhabited Frame Cavity
description: A usable room or circulation zone deliberately carved into the depth of an oversized structural frame, blurring the boundary between structure and enclosure.

name: Frame Connection Node
description: The joint or gusset assembly at the intersection of frame members, engineered and detailed to transfer moment, shear, and axial forces in a thickened-edge frame.

name: Gusset Plate
description: A steel plate welded or bolted at a frame node to distribute forces between converging members and contribute to the visual bulk of the connection zone.

name: Haunch
description: A tapered or curved enlargement at the beam-column junction that increases moment capacity and accentuates the perceived thickness of the frame edge.

name: Corbel
description: A projecting bracket cast or built into the face of a column or wall to carry beam loads and visually reinforce the thickened-edge condition.

name: Precast Concrete Frame
description: A factory-made reinforced concrete frame system whose large-section members are transported and erected on site, commonly used to create thick, expressive structural edges.

name: In-Situ Concrete Frame
description: A reinforced concrete frame cast in place using formwork, allowing plastic shaping of deep or complex cross-sections characteristic of thickened-edge design.

name: Glulam Timber Frame
description: A frame made from glued-laminated timber members whose large cross-sections and exposed grain express structural depth as an architectural thickened edge.

name: Cross-Laminated Timber (CLT) Frame
description: A mass-timber frame using thick CLT panels as load-bearing walls or slabs whose panel depth reads as a pronounced structural edge.

name: Glued-Laminated Timber
description: Engineered wood product made by adhesive-bonding lumber laminations into large structural sections that give timber frames their characteristic thick-edge appearance.

name: High-Performance Concrete
description: Concrete mix with enhanced strength and durability properties that allows thinner yet visually deep frame members without sacrificing structural performance.

name: Fire-Resistant Intumescent Coating
description: A protective paint or board system applied to exposed steel or timber frame members to meet fire-rating requirements while preserving the visual expression of the thickened edge.

name: Formwork Installation and Striking
description: The sequential setting up and removal of temporary molds that define the shape and surface of cast-in-place thickened concrete frame members.

name: Welding and Bolting of Steel Connections
description: Shop or site welding and high-strength bolting operations that rigidly join steel frame members at nodes to create moment-resisting thickened-edge connections.

name: Structural Frame Design
description: The engineering and architectural design process that determines member sizes, depths, and connection details to realise the thickened-edge frame concept.

name: Structural Analysis and Load Testing
description: Computational modelling and physical testing to verify that thickened-edge frame members and connections meet strength, stiffness, and serviceability requirements.

name: Surface Treatment and Finishing
description: Application of paint, cladding, or exposed-concrete finishing to the visible faces of thickened-frame members to achieve the intended architectural appearance.

name: Frame Inspection and Quality Control
description: Systematic checking of dimensions, weld quality, alignment, and material compliance during and after erection of the thickened-edge frame.

name: IfcStructuralFramedElement
description: IFC schema class grouping linear structural elements within a framed system, supporting the semantic representation of entire thickened-edge frame assemblies.

name: Column Pedestal
description: A short, stocky sub-element sitting between the foundation and the column shaft to elevate and isolate the column from ground level.

name: Column Casing / Enclosure
description: A protective or decorative enclosure wrapping around the structural column for fire protection, aesthetic finish, or impact resistance.

name: Column Splice Joint
description: A mechanical or welded connection used to join two column segments vertically when the full height cannot be erected in one piece.

name: Circular Column
description: A column variant with a round cross-section, often used for aesthetic appeal or uniform moment resistance in all directions.

name: Rectangular Column
description: A column variant with a square or oblong cross-section, common in reinforced concrete framed buildings for ease of formwork construction.

name: Steel I-Section Column
description: A structural steel column with an I- or H-shaped cross-section providing high strength-to-weight ratio for framed steel structures.

name: Timber Post / Column
description: A vertical load-bearing element made from solid timber, glulam, or engineered wood used in timber-framed or hybrid structures.

name: Column Zone (Slab-Column Interface)
description: The critical punching-shear zone of a flat slab or plate immediately surrounding the column head that governs structural design.

name: Column Corridor / Colonnade
description: A covered passageway or open gallery formed by a regular row of columns supporting a roof or upper floor.

name: Column Niche
description: A recessed pocket in a wall or structure designed to receive or partially conceal a column while maintaining spatial flow.

name: Concrete (Structural Grade)
description: High-strength Portland-cement-based mix used to cast or encase structural columns, selected by compressive strength class.

name: Grout / Non-Shrink Grout
description: A cementitious or epoxy material used to bed column base plates and fill voids to ensure full and uniform bearing contact.

name: Fire-Protective Coating / Intumescent Paint
description: A surface-applied material that expands under heat to insulate a steel or timber column and delay structural failure in a fire event.

name: Concrete Formwork Panels
description: Modular plywood, steel, or plastic panels assembled around a column outline to contain wet concrete during poured-in-place construction.

name: Column Layout & Grid Setting-Out
description: The surveying and marking activity that establishes precise column centre-line positions on a floor slab or ground according to structural drawings.

name: Column Excavation & Footing Construction
description: Earthworks and concrete pouring operations to form individual pad or pile-cap foundations at each column location.

name: Rebar Fabrication & Cage Assembly
description: Cutting, bending, and tying reinforcement bars into a cage ready for placement inside column formwork before concrete is poured.

name: Column Formwork Erection & Stripping
description: The temporary installation of shuttering panels around the column and their removal after the concrete has gained sufficient strength.

name: Concrete Pouring & Vibration (Column)
description: The placement of fresh concrete into column formwork and use of internal vibrators to consolidate the mix and eliminate voids.

name: Column Curing
description: Post-pour moisture and temperature management of a concrete column to ensure adequate hydration and attainment of design strength.

name: Steel Column Fabrication
description: Workshop cutting, drilling, and welding of steel sections and connection plates to produce a finished steel column ready for delivery.

name: Steel Column Erection & Plumbing
description: On-site lifting, positioning, and temporary bracing of steel columns followed by precise verticality checks before final bolting or welding.

name: Column Splicing
description: The bolted or welded joining of upper and lower column segments at a designated splice level during multi-storey erection.

name: Column Inspection & Plumb Survey
description: Quality-control checks using optical or laser instruments to verify that erected columns are within permitted verticality tolerances.

name: Column Structural System
description: The overall structural subsystem comprising all columns, beams, and connections that together form the gravity and lateral load-resisting frame of the building.

name: Column Monitoring System
description: An embedded sensor and data-logging infrastructure that tracks strain, settlement, or deformation of critical columns throughout the building's service life.

name: Cap Plate
description: A plate fixed to the top of a column to facilitate load transfer and connection to beams or upper columns.

name: Beam-to-Column Connection
description: The structural interface where a horizontal beam is attached to a vertical column, classified as shear, moment, or semi-rigid.

name: Moment Connection
description: A rigid connection system designed to transfer bending moments between connected structural members without rotation.

name: Shear Connection
description: A pinned or semi-rigid connection system that transfers only shear forces while allowing rotation between members.

name: Bolted Connection System
description: A connection system using high-strength bolts to join structural members, allowing for field assembly and adjustability.

name: Welded Connection System
description: A connection system using fusion welding to permanently join steel members with high strength and rigidity.

name: Mixed Bolted-Welded Connection System
description: A hybrid connection system combining shop welds and field bolts to optimize fabrication and erection efficiency.

name: High-Strength Structural Bolt
description: A hardened, high-tensile bolt (e.g., ASTM A325/A490) used in structural steel connections to resist shear and tension.

name: Structural Steel (Column Material)
description: Hot-rolled or fabricated steel sections forming the column body, graded for yield strength and weldability.

name: Weld Filler Metal
description: Consumable electrode or wire material deposited during welding to fuse structural steel components together.

name: Connection Fabrication
description: Shop-based cutting, drilling, welding, and fitting of column connection components prior to site delivery.

name: Bolt Tightening and Tensioning
description: The controlled tightening of structural bolts to specified pretension using torque, turn-of-nut, or direct tension methods.

name: Column Alignment and Plumbing
description: Surveying and adjusting columns to ensure they are perfectly vertical and correctly positioned before final connection.

name: IfcMechanicalFastener
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcElementComponent.

name: IfcConnectionGeometry
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Abstract type (not directly instantiable).

name: Vault Soffit
description: The curved or inclined underside surface of the stair vault structure, typically exposed to the space below.

name: Tread
description: The horizontal surface of each step on which a person places their foot when ascending or descending.

name: Riser
description: The vertical face of a step connecting successive treads that defines the step height.

name: Vault Arch Rib
description: A structural or decorative curved rib that defines and reinforces the vault geometry over the stair well.

name: Stair Well Opening
description: The void through successive floor slabs through which the stair rises, determining the spatial envelope of the vault.

name: Stair Core Enclosure
description: The fully enclosed vertical shaft surrounding the stair, which may serve as a fire compartment or service shaft.

name: Head Clearance Zone
description: The regulated clear height measured vertically from any tread nosing to the vault soffit directly above.

name: Masonry Vault Shell
description: Load-bearing curved masonry construction (brick, stone, or tile) that forms the vaulted ceiling over the stair.

name: Natural Stone Treads
description: Cut stone slabs used as stair treads, common in historic stair vaults for durability and aesthetics.

name: Lime Mortar Bedding
description: Traditional lime-based mortar used to bed masonry units in historic stair vault construction.

name: Plaster Intrados Finish
description: Decorative or protective plaster applied to the vault soffit to achieve a smooth, paintable interior finish.

name: Acoustic Lining System
description: Absorptive or damping materials applied to vault surfaces to control reverberation and impact sound within the stair.

name: Centering Formwork Erection
description: Construction activity of building temporary curved formwork (centering) to support masonry or concrete during vault casting.

name: Masonry Vaulting
description: The craft activity of laying brick or stone in a curved pattern to construct the load-bearing vault shell over the stair.

name: Concrete Shell Casting
description: Pouring and curing reinforced concrete over the centering formwork to form a monolithic stair vault shell.

name: Formwork Striking
description: The activity of removing temporary centering or formwork after the vault shell has achieved sufficient strength.

name: Stair Flight Installation
description: Placement and fixing of prefabricated or in-situ stair flights, including setting treads, risers, and stringers.

name: Soffit Plastering
description: Application of plaster coats to the vault intrados to achieve the specified interior finish and fire protection.

name: Heritage Conservation Survey
description: Condition assessment and documentation of historic stair vault fabric prior to repair or restoration works.

name: Supply Duct
description: Duct segment that delivers conditioned air from the AHU to occupied zones within the building.

name: Return Duct
description: Duct segment that carries used air back from occupied spaces to the AHU for reconditioning.

name: Exhaust Duct
description: Duct segment that expels stale or contaminated air from the building to the outside environment.

name: Fresh Air Intake Duct
description: Duct segment that draws outside air into the ventilation system to maintain indoor air quality.

name: Flexible Duct Connector
description: Short flexible section used to connect rigid ductwork to equipment, reducing vibration transmission.

name: Volume Control Damper (VCD)
description: Adjustable blade device installed inside a duct to regulate and balance airflow to individual zones.

name: Diffuser
description: Ceiling or wall-mounted outlet that distributes conditioned air evenly into an occupied space.

name: Grille / Return Air Grille
description: Louvred face plate covering a return-air opening that allows air to flow back into the duct system.

name: Air Filter / Filter Bank
description: Media or HEPA filter installed in the airstream to remove particulates and contaminants before air distribution.

name: Sheet Metal Ductwork
description: Galvanised steel or aluminium formed into rectangular or circular duct sections as the primary structural duct material.

name: Flexible Duct (Flex Duct)
description: Factory-made insulated flexible tubing used for short final connections between rigid ductwork and terminal devices.

name: Duct Sealant / Mastic
description: Paste or tape compound applied to duct joints and seams to prevent air leakage and maintain system efficiency.

name: HVAC Ductwork System
description: Integrated network of ducts, fittings, and components that distributes heating, cooling, and ventilation air throughout a building.

name: Riser / Vertical Duct Shaft
description: Vertical shaft running through multiple floors that houses the primary vertical duct runs connecting floor-level distribution.

name: Duct Coordination / BIM Clash Detection
description: Design-phase activity of modelling and coordinating duct routes against structure and other services to eliminate spatial conflicts.

name: Ductwork Fabrication
description: Off-site or on-site manufacturing of sheet metal duct sections, fittings, and transitions to project specifications.

name: Ductwork Installation
description: Site activity of hanging, joining, and securing duct sections and components within the allocated duct space.

name: Duct Pressure Testing / Air Leakage Testing
description: Post-installation testing activity that verifies ductwork airtightness against specified leakage classes.

name: Balancing and Commissioning (TAB)
description: Testing, adjusting, and balancing activity that sets airflow rates to design values across all terminals and zones.

name: Duct Cleaning
description: Maintenance activity that removes accumulated dust, debris, and microbial growth from internal duct surfaces.

name: Fire Stopping / Penetration Sealing
description: Activity of installing fire-rated seals where ducts penetrate fire-compartment walls or floors to maintain structural fire integrity.

name: IfcDuctFitting
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcFlowFitting.

name: IfcSpace (Duct Shaft)
description: IFC schema class used to model the bounded spatial volume of a vertical or horizontal duct shaft within the building.

name: Hydronic Radiant Floor System
description: A network of water-filled tubing embedded in or beneath the floor that circulates hot water to warm the floor surface and radiate heat upward into the space.

name: Electric Radiant Floor System
description: A system of electric resistance cables or mats installed beneath flooring materials to generate and radiate heat through the floor surface.

name: Radiant Ceiling Panel
description: A panel mounted at the ceiling level that circulates hot water or uses electric elements to emit infrared radiant heat downward into the occupied space.

name: Radiant Wall Panel
description: A wall-mounted heating panel that uses hydronic or electric means to radiate heat horizontally across the room.

name: Manifold (Radiant)
