description: A distribution hub that splits the hot water supply into multiple individual tubing loops and balances flow across a radiant heating system.

name: Boiler (Radiant Heat Source)
description: The heat-generating appliance—gas, oil, electric, or heat-pump-based—that produces the hot water supplied to a hydronic radiant system.

name: Thermal Mass Slab
description: A concrete or gypsum slab layer in which radiant tubing is embedded, storing and slowly releasing heat to moderate room temperature fluctuations.

name: Radiant Heat Insulation Board
description: Rigid insulation installed beneath radiant tubing to direct heat upward and prevent energy loss into the subfloor or ground.

name: Heat Transfer Plates (Aluminum)
description: Aluminum plates clipped around PEX tubing in thin-slab or staple-up installations to spread heat evenly across the floor surface.

name: Radiant Thermostat / Zone Controller
description: A programmable control device that regulates water temperature and flow to individual radiant zones based on room temperature setpoints.

name: Zone Valve
description: An electrically actuated valve on a radiant loop that opens or closes to control hot water flow to a specific heating zone.

name: Mixing Valve (Thermostatic)
description: A valve that blends hot boiler water with cooler return water to deliver the precise lower-temperature supply required by radiant floor loops.

name: Radiant-Ready Floor Assembly
description: A floor construction zone specifically designed and prepared with sleepers, channels, or conduit to accommodate future or current radiant heating installation.

name: Infloor Tubing Installation
description: The construction activity of laying, spacing, and securing PEX or other tubing within a floor assembly prior to concrete pour or overlay.

name: Pressure Testing (Radiant Loops)
description: A commissioning activity in which radiant tubing loops are pressurised with air or water to verify there are no leaks before the floor is covered.

name: Concrete Pour Over Radiant Tubing
description: The activity of placing and finishing a concrete topping slab over installed radiant tubing to embed it within the thermal mass.

name: Radiant System Balancing
description: The commissioning process of adjusting flow rates at the manifold to equalise heat output across all loops in a multi-zone radiant system.

name: Radiant System Design & Layout
description: The engineering and planning activity of determining tubing spacing, loop lengths, zone boundaries, and heat-loss calculations for a radiant installation.

name: Low-Temperature Heating Zone
description: A building zone served by radiant heat operating at supply-water temperatures typically between 85 °F and 120 °F, optimised for comfort and efficiency.

name: Infrared Radiant Heater
description: A gas-fired or electric overhead unit that emits infrared radiation to directly warm occupants and surfaces without heating the air as the primary medium.

name: Snow-Melt Radiant System
description: An outdoor extension of a radiant hydronic or electric system embedded in driveways, walkways, or ramps to melt snow and ice automatically.

name: IfcHydronicHeatingSystem
description: The IFC classification representing a complete hydronic-based heating system, applicable to radiant floor and panel configurations in building information models.

name: Dormer Cheek Wall
description: The vertical side wall of a dormer window that projects from the sloping roof and supports the dormer structure.

name: Dormer Roof
description: The small roof covering the dormer projection, which can be gabled, hipped, shed, or curved in form.

name: Dormer Fascia Board
description: A horizontal board fixed to the front face of the dormer, finishing the edge between the dormer roof and the window frame.

name: Dormer Soffit
description: The underside surface of the dormer overhang, typically finished with boards or cladding to seal and protect the structure.

name: Dormer Flashing
description: Weatherproof metal or membrane strips installed at the junction between the dormer and the main roof to prevent water ingress.

name: Dormer Window Frame
description: The structural surround holding the glazed pane within the dormer opening, typically timber, uPVC, or aluminium.

name: Dormer Lintel
description: A horizontal structural member spanning the top of the dormer window opening to carry loads from above.

name: Dormer Sill
description: The horizontal bottom member of the dormer window frame that sheds water and provides a bearing surface for the glazing unit.

name: Dormer Cladding
description: External surface material applied to the cheek walls and front face of the dormer, such as timber boards, zinc, lead, or render.

name: Dormer Insulation
description: Thermal and acoustic insulation installed within the dormer walls, roof, and floor to meet energy performance standards.

name: Dormer Vapour Control Layer
description: A membrane installed on the warm side of the dormer insulation to prevent moisture-laden air from migrating into the structure.

name: Dormer Structural Trimmer Rafters
description: Strengthened rafter members that frame the opening in the main roof slope to carry the load imposed by the dormer structure.

name: Dormer Header Beam
description: A horizontal structural beam spanning across the top of the dormer opening in the main roof, transferring loads to the trimmer rafters.

name: Shed Dormer
description: A dormer variant with a single, gently sloping shed roof that spans a wide portion of the main roof, maximising interior headroom.

name: Gable-Fronted Dormer
description: A dormer with a symmetrical pitched gable roof at the front, commonly found on traditional and period-style buildings.

name: Hipped Dormer
description: A dormer variant whose roof slopes on three sides, giving a compact pyramidal profile often used for aesthetic integration with the main roof.

name: Eyebrow Dormer
description: A low-profile dormer with a smoothly curved roof that sweeps up from the main roof surface, resembling an arched eyebrow.

name: Blind Dormer
description: A decorative dormer with no functional window opening, used purely as an architectural feature to add symmetry or visual interest.

name: Lucarne Dormer
description: A tall, narrow Gothic-style dormer with a steeply pitched gable, commonly seen on ecclesiastical and high-Victorian buildings.

name: Dormer Loft Space
description: The habitable or storage floor area created or enlarged within a roof by the addition of one or more dormer windows.

name: Dormer Construction
description: The overall building activity of erecting a new dormer structure, including structural alteration of the existing roof and installation of all components.

name: Dormer Roof Tiling / Slating
description: The activity of laying tiles, slates, or sheet metal on the dormer roof surface to provide a weathertight outer finish.

name: Dormer Flashing Installation
description: The trade activity of cutting, shaping, and fixing metal flashings at all junctions between the dormer and the surrounding main roof.

name: Dormer Glazing Installation
description: The activity of fitting and sealing the window unit—frame, glazing, and any ironmongery—within the prepared dormer opening.

name: Dormer Cladding Installation
description: The activity of applying external cladding boards, sheet metal, or render to the cheek walls and front face of the dormer.

name: Dormer Insulation Installation
description: The activity of fitting thermal insulation batts or boards within the dormer walls and roof to achieve the required U-values.

name: Dormer Structural Opening Formation
description: The activity of cutting and trimming the existing roof structure to form the opening required for the dormer, including installation of trimmers and headers.

name: Dormer Planning Approval
description: The regulatory process of obtaining planning permission or permitted development confirmation before constructing a dormer on an existing building.

name: Dormer Waterproofing Membrane
description: An underlayer or breather membrane installed beneath the dormer roof covering to provide a secondary line of defence against water penetration.

name: Lead Sheet Dormer Covering
description: Rolled lead used as a traditional and durable weathering material for flat or low-pitch dormer roofs and their associated flashings.

name: Zinc Sheet Dormer Covering
description: Pre-patinated or natural zinc sheet used as a modern lightweight cladding and weathering system for dormer roofs and cheek walls.

name: IfcRoof (Dormer)
description: The IFC schema class used to model the dormer's own roof element within a building information model.

name: IfcWindow (Dormer)
description: The IFC schema class used to represent the window unit inserted within the dormer opening in a BIM environment.

name: IfcWall (Dormer Cheek)
description: The IFC schema class applied to model the vertical cheek walls of a dormer as distinct wall elements in a building information model.

name: Ridge Cap
description: A finishing cap placed along the apex (ridge line) of a pitched roof to seal and protect the topmost joint between two roof slopes.

name: Hip Cap
description: A specially shaped cap unit applied along the hip edges of a roof where two sloping sides meet at an external angle.

name: Rake Cap
description: A cap or trim piece installed along the sloping edge (rake) of a gable roof to seal the edge against weather intrusion.

name: Eave Cap
description: A formed metal or rigid cap placed at the eave edge of a roof to protect the lower perimeter and direct water into the gutter.

name: Parapet Cap / Coping
description: A protective cap mounted on top of a parapet wall to shed water away from the wall face and prevent moisture infiltration.

name: Flat Roof Edge Cap
description: A metal or composite cap trim fastened along the perimeter of a flat or low-slope roof to terminate the roofing membrane and deflect water.

name: Ventilated Ridge Cap
description: A ridge cap incorporating continuous air vents that allow warm, moist attic air to escape while excluding rain and pests.

name: Snow Guard Cap Strip
description: A cap-integrated device or strip installed near the eave line to prevent sudden snow and ice slides from the roof surface.

name: Metal Roof Cap
description: A roof cap fabricated from galvanized steel, aluminum, copper, or zinc, providing high durability and weather resistance.

name: Concrete / Clay Tile Ridge Cap
description: A purpose-made concrete or clay tile unit shaped to cap ridge and hip lines on tile roof systems.

name: Asphalt Shingle Cap
description: A three-tab or laminate asphalt shingle cut or pre-formed to serve as a cap unit on shingle ridge and hip sections.

name: EPDM / TPO Cap Flashing
description: Flexible rubber or thermoplastic membrane used to cap and flash roof edges and penetrations on low-slope membrane roofing systems.

name: Foam Ridge Cap Vent
description: A compressible foam closure strip installed beneath metal ridge caps to filter airflow and block insects and debris.

name: Roof Cap Installation
description: The trade activity of measuring, cutting, and fastening cap units to ridge, hip, rake, and eave edges per manufacturer and code requirements.

name: Roof Cap Sealing & Caulking
description: Application of roofing sealant or butyl tape along lap joints and fastener penetrations of cap units to ensure watertight performance.

name: Roof Cap Inspection & Maintenance
description: Periodic inspection, re-fastening, and replacement of worn or displaced cap units to maintain roof integrity over its service life.

name: Flashing Integration
description: The process of coordinating and installing metal flashings at cap terminations, transitions, and penetrations to prevent water infiltration.

name: Roofing Membrane System
description: The waterproofing layer assembly on flat or low-slope roofs to which edge and parapet cap flashings are mechanically terminated.

name: Attic / Roof Space
description: The enclosed space directly beneath the roof cap and decking that is thermally and hygro-thermally influenced by cap ventilation performance.

name: Parapet Wall Zone
description: The vertical wall extension above the main roof deck whose top surface is protected by a parapet cap or coping unit.

name: Subfloor
description: The structural base layer installed beneath the finished floor surface that provides support and levelness.

name: Underlayment
description: A thin cushioning or moisture-barrier layer placed between the subfloor and the finish flooring material.

name: Laminate Flooring
description: A multi-layer synthetic flooring product that simulates wood or stone through a photographic applique layer.

name: Ceramic Tile Flooring
description: Fired clay tiles used as a hard-wearing, water-resistant floor finish, typically set in mortar or adhesive.

name: Vinyl Plank Flooring
description: Resilient, waterproof flooring planks made from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) designed to mimic natural materials.

name: Polished Concrete Floor
description: A concrete slab that has been mechanically ground and polished to achieve a smooth, durable, and decorative floor surface.

name: Natural Stone Flooring
description: Flooring cut from natural stone such as marble, granite, or slate, prized for durability and aesthetic character.

name: Moisture Barrier / Damp Proof Membrane
description: A waterproof membrane installed within the floor build-up to prevent ground moisture from migrating upward into the floor structure.

name: Floor Transition Strip
description: A narrow profile used at the boundary between two different flooring materials or levels to provide a clean and safe edge.

name: Floor Adhesive / Mortar Bedding
description: A bonding agent or cementitious mortar used to securely fix floor tiles or planks to the substrate.

name: Floor Grout
description: A cementitious or epoxy filler material applied between tile joints to seal gaps and complete the tile floor installation.

name: Anti-Slip Coating / Nosing
description: A surface treatment or edge profile applied to floor surfaces to reduce the risk of slipping, especially in wet or high-traffic zones.

name: Floor Installation
description: The construction activity of laying, bonding, or fastening finish floor materials onto the prepared substrate.

name: Floor Grinding and Polishing
description: A mechanical process of abrading and buffing a concrete or stone floor surface to achieve the desired smoothness and sheen.

name: Floor Waterproofing
description: The application of membranes or coatings to the floor assembly to prevent water ingress, particularly in wet areas such as bathrooms.

name: Floor Demolition / Removal
description: The activity of stripping out existing floor finishes and build-up in preparation for a new installation or structural repair.

name: Floor Inspection and Testing
description: Quality assurance activities including moisture testing, flatness measurement, and adhesion checks performed on the floor substrate or finished surface.

name: IfcCovering (FLOORING)
description: The IFC schema class used to represent floor finish coverings such as tiles, carpet, or timber within a building information model.

name: IfcSlab (FLOOR)
description: The IFC schema class representing the structural horizontal slab element that forms the base of the floor assembly.

name: Wet Room / Shower Floor Zone
description: A designated floor area designed with waterproofing, drainage, and slip-resistant finishes to handle continuous water exposure.

name: Raised Platform Zone
description: A localised floor area elevated above the surrounding level, often used for staging, accessibility, or spatial definition within a room.

name: Weatherboard Cladding
description: Horizontal timber or fibre-cement boards fixed in an overlapping (lapped) pattern to form the primary weather-resistant skin of an outside wall.

name: Shiplap Boards
description: Timber boards with rebated edges that interlock in a lapped joint, providing a flush external face while maintaining weather exclusion.

name: Feather-Edge Boarding
description: Tapered timber boards nailed in an overlapping horizontal course to create a traditional rustic external wall finish.

name: Fibre-Cement Lap Siding
description: Pre-primed fibre-cement planks installed with a horizontal overlap, offering high durability and low maintenance as an alternative to timber.

name: Vinyl Lap Siding
description: Extruded PVC profiled planks designed to mimic traditional lapped boarding with colour-through finish requiring no painting.

name: Timber Stud Frame
description: Structural framework of vertical studs and horizontal rails to which lapped cladding boards are fixed, forming the load-bearing substrate of the wall.

name: Vertical Battens (Counter Battens)
description: Thin timber or metal strips fixed over the breather membrane to create a ventilated cavity and provide a nailing surface for lapped boards.

name: Cavity Ventilation System
description: Arrangement of top-and-bottom ventilation gaps and insect mesh within the drained cavity behind lapped cladding to prevent moisture build-up.

name: Wall Insulation Layer
description: Thermal insulation (rigid board, mineral wool or spray foam) installed within or behind the stud frame to meet energy-performance requirements for the external wall assembly.

name: Internal Vapour Control Layer
description: Vapour-retarding membrane fixed to the warm side of insulation within the wall build-up to limit interstitial condensation in a lapped-clad wall.

name: Starter Strip / J-Channel
description: Purpose-made metal or plastic profile fixed at the base of the wall to set the correct overhang angle and starter course for the first lapped board.

name: Corner Trim / Stop Bead
description: External or internal corner moulding that neatly terminates lapped boarding at wall junctions, abutments, and openings.

name: Window and Door Surround Flashings
description: Weatherproofing flashings and sill trays integrated around openings within a lapped-clad wall to prevent water ingress at junctions.

name: Wall Tie and Fixing System
description: Corrosion-resistant nails, screws, or concealed clips used to mechanically fasten each lapped board to the batten or substrate at the correct lap and spacing.

name: Drained and Ventilated Cavity
description: The air gap maintained between the back of lapped cladding boards and the breather membrane, allowing water to drain and air to circulate.

name: External Wall Build-Up (Assembly)
description: The complete layered wall system from internal lining to external cladding surface, coordinating structural, thermal, acoustic, and weatherproofing functions.

name: Cladding Installation Activity
description: The on-site trade operation of measuring, cutting, and fixing lapped boards course by course from the base of the wall upward to the soffit or parapet.

name: Priming and Pre-Treatment of Boards
description: Application of primer, end-grain sealer, or preservative treatment to lapped boards before or immediately after installation to protect against moisture and decay.

name: Painting and Finishing of Cladding
description: On-site or factory application of exterior paint, stain, or clear coat to lapped boards to achieve the required aesthetic and weatherproofing finish.

name: Wall U-Value Calculation
description: Thermal performance assessment of the lapped wall assembly to demonstrate compliance with energy regulations, accounting for each layer's conductivity.

name: Condensation Risk Analysis
description: Hygrothermal modelling or calculation to verify that the lapped external wall build-up will not suffer harmful interstitial or surface condensation.

name: External Wall Maintenance and Re-Coating
description: Periodic inspection, re-painting, board replacement, and re-sealing of joints to maintain weather resistance and appearance of the lapped cladding over its service life.

name: IfcWall (External)
description: The IFC schema class used to represent the external wall element containing the lapped cladding assembly within a BIM model.

name: IfcCovering (Cladding)
description: The IFC schema class used to model the surface cladding layer, such as lapped boards, applied to the face of an external wall element.

name: Thermal Insulation Batt
description: Flexible fibrous or foam batts fitted inside wall cavities to improve thermal performance and contribute to a soft wall feel.

name: Fabric Wall Panel
description: A prefabricated panel wrapped in textile or upholstered fabric, mounted on interior walls to provide a soft, tactile surface finish.

name: Padded Wall Tile
description: Individual modular tiles with a foam or cushioned core and decorative surface, applied to walls for both aesthetics and impact absorption.

name: Cork Wall Covering
description: A natural cork sheet or tile applied to interior wall surfaces, offering softness, acoustic dampening, and thermal insulation.

name: Felt Wall Cladding
description: Pressed or needle-punched felt sheets fixed to interior walls to deliver a soft texture with noise-reduction properties.

name: Foam Impact-Resistant Liner
description: High-density or viscoelastic foam fixed directly to wall surfaces in safety-critical spaces such as gyms or medical rooms to absorb physical impact.

name: Acoustic Panel System
description: An integrated assembly of sound-absorbing panels, sub-framing, and fixings designed to control reverberation and noise levels across a wall surface.

name: Resilient Channel System
description: A system of metal channels and decoupled framing that isolates wall cladding from the structural substrate to reduce sound flanking and vibration.

name: Textile Wallcovering
description: Woven or non-woven fabric bonded to a backing and applied like wallpaper, delivering a soft appearance and mild acoustic benefit to interior walls.

name: Vinyl Cushion Wallcovering
description: A cushioned vinyl sheet product with a foam interlayer, applied to walls for durability, hygiene, and a semi-soft surface in commercial or healthcare settings.

name: Green/Living Wall Module
description: A modular planting system fixed to interior walls, incorporating growing media and plants to create a naturally soft, biophilic wall surface.

name: Gypsum Board Substrate
description: The rigid backing board onto which soft wall finishes are mounted, providing structural support and fire resistance behind compliant surface layers.

name: Wall Framing Sub-Structure
description: The metal stud or timber frame assembly that creates the cavity space required for insulation and soft-finish panel attachment.

name: Adhesive & Mechanical Fixing System
description: The combination of construction adhesives, clips, and fasteners used to securely attach soft wall panels or coverings to substrates.

name: Vapour Control Membrane
description: A thin membrane installed within the wall build-up to manage moisture diffusion and protect soft insulation materials from condensation damage.

name: Fire-Retardant Treatment
description: A chemical treatment or intumescent coating applied to soft wall materials to bring them into compliance with interior fire-spread regulations.

name: Surface Preparation & Priming
description: The process of cleaning, levelling, and priming existing wall substrates to ensure proper adhesion of soft wall coverings or panels.

name: Soft Wall Panel Installation
description: The trade activity of cutting, fitting, and fixing padded, fabric, or acoustic panels to interior wall surfaces according to design and layout drawings.

name: Wall Covering Application
description: The application of textile, vinyl, or cork sheet wallcoverings using adhesives, seam alignment, and finishing techniques appropriate to the chosen material.

name: Inspection & Commissioning
description: A formal review of completed soft wall assemblies to confirm installation quality, fire compliance, and acoustic or thermal performance before handover.

name: Soft Flooring Zone (Adjacent)
description: A floor area immediately adjacent to soft inside walls where complementary soft finishes such as carpet or rubber flooring are specified for a unified sensory environment.

name: Acoustic Room / Quiet Room
description: A dedicated interior space designed with soft wall, ceiling, and floor finishes to achieve a controlled low-noise or high-absorption acoustic environment.

name: Recording Studio Isolation Room
description: A specialist acoustic space where soft wall treatments are integral to achieving the very low background noise and controlled reverberation required for audio recording.

name: IfcCovering (Wall)
description: The IFC schema class used to model non-structural wall coverings, including soft panels and textile finishes, within a Building Information Model.

name: Bi-Fold Window Panel
description: Folding panel units that stack to one side, creating a near-full-width opening between interior and exterior.

name: Window Hardware & Locking Mechanism
description: Handles, espagnolette rods, friction stays, and multipoint locks that control and secure wide-opening sashes.

name: Friction Stay / Hinge Stay
description: An adjustable arm stay that holds a casement or awning sash open at a chosen angle without slamming shut.

name: Window Reveal & Sill
description: The internal and external masonry or joinery surfaces framing the window opening, including the projecting sill.

name: Weather Sealing & Draught Strips
description: Compressible gaskets and brush seals applied around the sash perimeter to prevent air and water infiltration when closed.

name: Window Frame Timber
description: Treated or engineered timber species used for frame and sash construction in traditional and contemporary wide-opening windows.

name: Aluminium Window Profile
description: Extruded aluminium sections forming slim, strong frames suited to large casement and bi-fold window configurations.

name: uPVC Window Profile
description: Unplasticised PVC extrusions providing a low-maintenance, thermally efficient frame option for wide-opening windows.

name: Low-E Glazing Coating
description: A microscopically thin metallic coating on glass that reduces heat loss while maintaining high visible light transmission.

name: Window Installation & Setting-Out
description: The process of accurately positioning and securing the window frame within the structural opening to plumb, level, and square tolerances.

name: Window Opening Formation in Masonry
description: Cutting or building the structural aperture in walls, including lintel installation, to accommodate wide-opening window units.

name: Glazing & Sash Fitting
description: The trade activity of inserting, beading, and sealing glass units into sashes and hanging sashes within frames.

name: Window Flashings & Weatherproofing Works
description: Application of lead, aluminium, or flexible flashings around the window perimeter to shed water away from the structure.

name: Painting & Finishing of Window Joinery
description: Preparation, priming, and application of protective paint or stain systems to timber window frames and sashes.

name: Window Hardware Installation & Adjustment
description: Fitting and commissioning of stays, handles, locks, and restrictor mechanisms to ensure safe wide-opening operation.

name: Window Restrictors & Child Safety Devices
description: Mechanical limiters fitted to wide-opening windows to prevent falls from height while still permitting ventilation.

name: Thermal Performance & U-Value Specification
description: The engineered combination of frame, glazing, and seals assessed against regulatory thermal transmittance targets for windows.

name: Solar Shading & Blind Integration
description: Integrated blinds, louvres, or external shutters coordinated with wide-opening windows to control solar gain and glare.

name: Rainwater Drainage from Window Sill
description: Designed drainage channels, throats, and slopes on sills and heads to direct water away and prevent penetration.

name: Solid Door Panel
description: The main rigid door leaf combining a solid core or stiles/rails with one or more glazed openings cut into it.

name: Glazed Lite / Glass Insert
description: The individual pane or unit of glass set within a cutout of the solid door panel, available in single, double, or laminated glazing.

name: Door Sill / Threshold
description: The bottom horizontal component at the floor level of the door opening, providing a seal, transition, and weather barrier.

name: Glazing Bead / Stop Bead
description: A narrow moulded strip that retains the glass pane securely within the door panel rebate.

name: Glazing Seal / Putty
description: Flexible sealant, silicone, or traditional putty used to seal the perimeter joint between the glass and the door panel or glazing bead.

name: Door Core Material
description: The internal infill of the solid door leaf, such as solid timber, engineered wood (MDF/LVL), mineral board, or fire-rated composite.

name: Door Skin / Face Panel
description: The outer facing material of the door leaf, such as hardwood veneer, MDF, fibreglass, or steel sheet providing the finished surface.

name: Door Hardware Set
description: The complete assembly of lockset, handles, hinges, closers, and associated ironmongery required to operate and secure the door.

name: Door Lockset
description: The morticed or surface-mounted locking mechanism including latch bolt, deadbolt, and cylinder for securing the door.

name: Door Handle / Lever Set
description: The operable grip hardware mounted on the door face that allows users to actuate the latch and open the door.

name: Weatherstripping / Draught Seal
description: Compressible gaskets or brush seals fitted to the door frame perimeter to prevent air, water, and sound infiltration.

name: Intumescent Strip
description: A heat-activated strip fitted around the door or glass rebate that expands on fire to seal gaps and maintain compartmentation.

name: Acoustic Door Assembly
description: A door system engineered with high-mass core, acoustic seals, and laminated glass to achieve a defined sound reduction index (Rw).

name: Insulated / Thermal Door Assembly
description: A door system incorporating insulating core materials and thermally broken frames to minimise heat transfer and meet energy performance requirements.

name: Single Glazed Lite Door
description: A solid door variant with a single pane of glass offering basic light transmission without enhanced thermal or acoustic performance.

name: Double Glazed Lite Door
description: A solid door variant featuring a sealed double-glazed unit within the panel for improved thermal insulation and noise reduction.

name: Laminated Safety Glass Lite
description: A glass insert composed of two or more panes bonded by an interlayer so that fragments are retained on breakage, satisfying safety glazing standards.

name: Toughened / Tempered Glass Lite
description: Heat-treated glass used in the door insert that shatters into small, blunt fragments upon impact for improved occupant safety.

name: Wired / Georgian Glass Lite
description: Glass containing an embedded wire mesh that holds fragments together under fire or impact, commonly used in fire-rated doors.

name: Obscured / Frosted Glass Lite
description: Translucent patterned or sandblasted glass that allows light transmission while maintaining visual privacy through the door panel.

name: Timber Solid Door with Glass
description: A variant of the parent concept where the door leaf and frame are constructed primarily from solid or engineered timber species.

name: Steel Solid Door with Glass
description: A variant where the door leaf is fabricated from steel sheet over a solid core, providing high security and fire performance.

name: Aluminium Solid Door with Glass
description: A variant using extruded aluminium sections forming the door frame and panel perimeter around a solid infill and glazed lite.

name: Fibreglass (GRP) Solid Door with Glass
description: A variant moulded from glass-reinforced plastic over a solid core, offering corrosion resistance and low maintenance for external applications.

name: Door Opening / Door Reveal Space
description: The physical void formed in a wall to receive the door frame and leaf, defining the clear opening dimensions and structural head height.

name: Door Ironmongery Schedule
description: The coordinated specification document listing all hardware items, finishes, and security ratings assigned to each door in a project.

name: Glazing Installation in Door
description: The activity of cutting the rebate, inserting the glass lite, and securing glazing beads and seals within the door panel.

name: Door Fire Testing / Certification
description: The formal third-party testing and certification process that validates the fire-resistance rating of the complete door assembly.

name: Door Maintenance & Re-glazing
description: Ongoing facilities management activities covering adjustment, seal replacement, glass replacement, and hardware servicing over the door's service life.

name: IfcWindow (vision panel variant)
description: Occasionally used in IFC to model a glazed vision panel within a door when the glass element is tracked as a separate opening object.

name: Louvre Blade Assembly
description: Horizontal or vertical slats arranged to diffuse and redirect daylight entering a space while blocking direct glare.

name: Fritted Glass Panel
description: Glass with a ceramic dot or pattern frit applied to its surface to partially diffuse and reduce direct solar transmission.

name: Translucent Polycarbonate Glazing
description: A semi-opaque plastic glazing material that scatters incoming light, eliminating harsh shadows while maintaining brightness.

name: Etched or Sandblasted Glass
description: Glass with a abraded surface treatment that diffuses transmitted light and obscures direct views.

name: Solar Control Film
description: A thin adhesive film applied to glazing to reduce solar heat gain and soften the quality of admitted daylight.

name: Skylight Diffuser
description: A translucent panel or baffle installed below a rooflight to scatter and soften the quality of light admitted from above.

name: Shading Fin
description: A vertical or angled projecting blade fixed to a facade to intercept oblique sunlight and produce controlled shadow patterns.

name: Glare Control System
description: A coordinated set of blinds, screens, and sensors that automatically respond to solar conditions to prevent visual discomfort.

name: Automated Blind & Shading Control
description: A motorised system with environmental sensors that adjusts internal or external shading devices in response to real-time sunlight levels.

name: Light-Filtering Space
description: An interior zone specifically designed and enclosed to receive and redistribute softened natural light to adjacent deeper spaces.

name: Atrium with Diffused Roof
description: A multi-storey internal void covered by a translucent or fritted rooflight that provides filtered ambient daylight to surrounding floors.

name: Transitional Light Lobby
description: An entry or buffer zone designed to allow occupants' eyes to adapt between bright exterior and softly lit interior conditions.

name: Shadow Pattern Study
description: An analytical process of modelling and evaluating the shadow and light patterns cast by shading elements at different times of day and year.

name: Glazing Specification & Selection
description: The design and procurement process of choosing glass or glazing products with specific light transmission, reflection, and diffusion properties.

name: Light Simulation & Modelling
description: The use of specialist software (e.g. Radiance, Dialux) to virtually predict and optimise interior daylight distribution and quality.

name: Shading Device Commissioning
description: The testing and calibration of motorised or automated shading systems to confirm correct sensor response and operational performance.

name: Leaded Light Panel
description: A decorative window panel made of small glass pieces held together by lead came strips, commonly used in traditional and heritage buildings.

name: Glazing Bar
description: A thin structural bar, typically of timber or metal, that divides a window frame into multiple small pane sections.

name: Lead Came
description: H-shaped lead strips used to join individual small glass panes together in leaded glazing assemblies.

name: Crown Glass Pane
description: Historically hand-blown flat glass cut into small pieces for use in traditional small-pane windows.

name: Cylinder Glass Pane
description: A type of antique or reproduction sheet glass blown into a cylinder then flattened, used for small pane heritage glazing.

name: Putty Glazing Compound
description: A linseed-oil-based compound used to bed and seal small glass panes within their rebated frames or lead came.

name: Casement Window with Small Panes
description: A side-hinged window sash subdivided into a grid of small individual panes by glazing bars.

name: Sash Window with Small Panes
description: A vertically sliding window containing multiple small panes separated by slender timber glazing bars, typical of Georgian architecture.

name: Fanlight with Small Panes
description: A semi-circular or rectangular window above a door, subdivided into small panes by radiating or grid-pattern glazing bars.

name: Dormer Window with Small Panes
description: A roof-projecting window unit incorporating small-pane glazing, often seen in vernacular and cottage-style buildings.

name: Insulated Small-Pane Double Glazing Unit
description: A modern double-glazed unit engineered to replicate the visual appearance of traditional small panes while achieving thermal performance standards.

name: Glazing Bar Installation
description: The construction activity of fitting and fixing slender glazing bars within a window frame to create a small-pane pattern.

name: Lead Came Glazing
description: The craft activity of cutting glass pieces and assembling them with lead came strips to form a leaded light panel.

name: Small Pane Glass Cutting
description: The specialist activity of scoring and breaking sheet glass into small, precisely dimensioned pane pieces to fit a window grid.

name: Re-leading Works
description: A conservation activity involving the removal of deteriorated lead came and re-assembly of existing glass panes with new lead.

name: Putty Repointing
description: The maintenance activity of raking out and replacing failed glazing putty around small panes to restore weathertightness.

name: Heritage Window Restoration
description: A specialist conservation activity encompassing the repair, cleaning, and reinstatement of historic small-pane window assemblies.

name: IfcWindowPanelProperties
description: IFC entity class (schema IFC4). Supertype: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet.

name: Timber Window Frame
description: The outer structural surround, typically of softwood or hardwood, that houses small-pane sashes or casements.

name: Drip Mould
description: A projecting horizontal moulding above a window opening designed to deflect rainwater away from the frame and glazing.

name: Condensation Risk Zone
description: The area around single-glazed small panes prone to moisture build-up due to the low thermal resistance of the glass and lead.

name: Architectural Glass
description: Flat glass product specified for use in windows, available in a range of thicknesses and finishes suitable for small-pane applications.

name: Ferrous Saddle Bar
description: A horizontal iron or steel bar fixed across a leaded light panel to provide structural support and prevent bowing of the lead came.

name: Tie Wire
description: Thin copper or zinc wire used to attach a leaded light panel to its saddle bars, restraining movement.

name: Window Schedule
description: A documentation activity that records the size, type, pane configuration, and specification of all windows in a building project.

name: Base Molding
description: A half-inch trim profile installed at the junction of walls and floors to conceal gaps and provide a finished transition.

name: Casing Trim
description: Half-inch trim used to frame door and window openings, covering the gap between the jamb and the surrounding wall.

name: Chair Rail
description: A horizontal half-inch trim piece mounted on walls at chair height to protect wall surfaces and add decorative detail.

name: Crown Molding
description: A half-inch trim profile installed at the junction of walls and ceilings to create an elegant decorative transition.

name: Quarter Round
description: A small half-inch convex trim profile used to fill gaps between flooring and base molding or other surfaces.

name: Shoe Molding
description: A slender half-inch trim piece installed at the base of walls along flooring to conceal expansion gaps.

name: Flat Bar Stock
description: Flat, rectangular half-inch lumber or MDF stock used as the raw material for cutting and shaping trim profiles.

name: MDF (Medium Density Fiberboard) Trim
description: An engineered wood material commonly milled to half-inch thickness for interior trim applications due to its smooth finish.

name: Solid Wood Trim
description: Natural lumber milled to half-inch profiles for trim use, prized for its strength and ability to be stained or painted.

name: PVC/Vinyl Trim
description: Moisture-resistant plastic trim material produced in half-inch profiles, ideal for exterior or high-humidity applications.

name: Finger-Jointed Pine Trim
description: An economical half-inch paint-grade trim material made from short pine pieces joined end-to-end for stability.

name: Primed Trim Board
description: Half-inch trim stock that is factory-primed for a paint-ready surface, reducing on-site preparation time.

name: Trim Installation
description: The process of measuring, cutting, and fastening half-inch trim pieces to walls, ceilings, floors, and openings.

name: Miter Cutting
description: The activity of making angled cuts on half-inch trim ends to form tight, seamless joints at corners.

name: Coping
description: A technique of scribing and undercutting the profile of one half-inch trim piece to fit over the face of another at inside corners.

name: Nailing and Fastening
description: Securing half-inch trim to substrates using finish nails, brad nails, or adhesive to ensure a flush and stable fit.

name: Caulking and Sealing
description: Filling gaps between half-inch trim and adjacent surfaces with caulk to achieve a clean, draft-free finish.

name: Sanding and Surface Preparation
description: Smoothing raw or painted half-inch trim surfaces to prepare them for primer and final paint or stain coats.

name: Painting and Finishing
description: Applying primer, paint, or stain to installed half-inch trim to achieve a durable and aesthetically consistent finish.

name: Scribing to Wall
description: Marking and trimming half-inch trim profiles to follow irregular or uneven wall and floor surfaces for a tight fit.

name: Trim Removal and Replacement
description: The demolition and reinstallation of existing half-inch trim during renovation or repair work.

name: Interior Trim Zone
description: The architectural zone along walls, ceilings, and floor perimeters where half-inch trim is designed, installed, and maintained.

name: Exterior Trim Zone
description: Outdoor building envelope areas such as fascias, soffits, and window surrounds where half-inch trim provides weatherproof finishing.

name: Trim Profile System
description: The coordinated set of half-inch trim components—base, casing, crown, and accents—that together define a building's interior finish language.

name: Fastener System
description: The combination of finish nails, brad nails, construction adhesives, and hole-filling compounds used to secure and conceal half-inch trim attachments.

name: Paint and Finish System
description: The multi-layer system of primer, paint, and topcoat applied to half-inch trim for protection and aesthetic consistency.

name: Fixed Seating Area
description: A designated zone within a building fitted with permanently installed seats that cannot be repositioned.

name: Flexible Seating Zone
description: An open area designed to accommodate movable or reconfigurable seating arrangements to suit varying occupancy needs.

name: Tiered Seating Terrace
description: A stepped or raked space where rows of seats are positioned at progressively higher elevations for improved sightlines.

name: Bleacher Assembly
description: A prefabricated stepped bench structure, typically used in sports or assembly venues, that provides multiple rows of seating.

name: Auditorium Seat
description: An individual fold-down or fixed chair unit designed for installation in theaters, lecture halls, or assembly rooms.

name: Bench Seating Unit
description: A long, backless or backed seating element used in public waiting areas, transit facilities, parks, and corridors.

name: Seat Riser / Step Structure
description: The structural riser and tread system that supports tiered seating rows and defines the vertical change in elevation between rows.

name: Seat Mounting Bracket
description: A metal or composite hardware element used to anchor individual seat units to the floor or riser face.

name: Seat Rail System
description: Continuous horizontal rails or tracks that run along seating rows, providing structural support and alignment for seat units.

name: Seat Numbering & Signage
description: Alphanumeric labels, plaques, or digital indicators affixed to seats or rows to enable occupant wayfinding and capacity management.

name: Accessibility Seating Space (Wheelchair)
description: A code-compliant open floor area integrated within seating layouts to accommodate wheelchair users and companion seats.

name: VIP / Premium Seating Box
description: An exclusive, semi-enclosed seating area offering premium amenities and sightlines, typically elevated or segregated from general seating.

name: Press / Media Seating Area
description: A dedicated zone equipped with work surfaces, power outlets, and optimal sightlines reserved for journalists and broadcast personnel.

name: Retractable Seating System
description: A motorized or manually operated mechanism that folds and stores tiered seating rows into a compact configuration when not in use.

name: Seating Structural Support System
description: The integrated framework of beams, columns, and sub-frames engineered to carry the dead and live loads generated by seated occupants.

name: Egress & Aisle Layout System
description: The planned network of aisles, cross-aisles, vomitories, and exits that ensure safe and compliant evacuation from seating areas.

name: Seat Upholstery Material
description: Fabric, vinyl, or leather covering applied to seat pans and backs to provide comfort, aesthetics, and durability.

name: Seat Shell / Body Material
description: Molded plastic, fiberglass, or formed plywood used to construct the structural body of individual seat units.

name: Acoustic Absorption Material (Seating)
description: Sound-absorbing foams, panels, or upholstery integrated into seating elements to manage reverberation within the seating space.

name: Anti-Slip Flooring Material (Seating Aisles)
description: Textured or coated floor finish applied to aisles and step treads within seating areas to reduce slip and fall hazards.

name: Seating Area Installation
description: The construction activity of assembling, aligning, and anchoring seat units, rails, and risers within the designated seating space.

name: Substructure & Riser Construction
description: The activity of forming, pouring, or erecting the stepped concrete or steel substructure that supports tiered seating rows.

name: Seat Upholstery & Finishing
description: The trade activity of applying cushioning, fabric, or surface treatments to seat shells as part of fit-out and interior finishing works.

name: Retractable Seating Commissioning
description: Testing and adjusting motorized or manual retractable seating systems to verify safe operation, alignment, and compliance prior to handover.

name: Accessibility Compliance Inspection (Seating)
description: A formal review activity to confirm that wheelchair spaces, companion seats, and accessible routes meet applicable code requirements.

name: Seating Capacity Survey
description: A measurement and counting activity performed to verify and document the total number and layout of seat positions within a venue.

name: IfcSpace (Seating Area)
description: The IFC schema class used to represent and exchange the geometric boundary and metadata of a seating space within a BIM model.

name: IfcFurnishingElement (Seat)
description: The IFC class that models individual seat objects, capturing their geometry, placement, and associated properties within a building model.

name: Bench Seat
description: The primary horizontal surface of the front door bench where occupants sit or place items.

name: Bench Backrest
description: A vertical support panel attached to the rear of the bench seat for user comfort and structural rigidity.

name: Bench Armrest
description: Side supports mounted at the ends of the bench seat to provide lateral comfort and definition of the seating area.

name: Bench Legs
description: Vertical structural members that elevate the bench seat off the floor and transfer load to the ground.

name: Bench Base Frame
description: The underlying structural framework that ties together the legs and supports the seat panel.

name: Shoe Storage Cubby
description: An open or enclosed compartment integrated below or beside the bench for organising footwear near the entrance.

name: Coat Hook Rail
description: A horizontal rail fitted with hooks mounted above or alongside the bench for hanging outerwear and bags.

name: Storage Drawer
description: A sliding pull-out drawer unit incorporated into the bench body for concealed storage of small items.

name: Cushion / Seat Pad
description: A removable padded cover placed on the bench seat to improve comfort and add decorative finish.

name: Bench Mounting Bracket
description: Metal or timber brackets used to fix a wall-hung or floating bench securely to the adjacent wall structure.

name: Mudroom / Entryway Space
description: The transitional entry zone in which the front door bench is typically located, bridging outdoor and indoor environments.

name: Built-in Bench Joinery
description: A fully integrated millwork system combining bench, storage, and coat hanging as a single custom-built unit within the entry space.

name: Shoe Rack System
description: A dedicated freestanding or built-in racking system placed near the bench to organise and air footwear.

name: Solid Timber
description: Natural hardwood or softwood used for bench seats and frames, valued for durability and aesthetic warmth.

name: Plywood / Engineered Board
description: Structural sheet material commonly used for bench carcasses, shelves, and drawer boxes in entry joinery.

name: Metal (Steel / Aluminium)
description: Ferrous or non-ferrous metal used for bench legs, frames, and mounting hardware for strength and a contemporary look.

name: Timber Stain / Paint Finish
description: Surface coating applied to timber bench components for protection against moisture, dirt, and abrasion.

name: Bench Installation
description: The trade activity of positioning, levelling, fixing, and securing the bench unit within the entry space.

name: Wall Preparation & Blocking
description: Construction activity of installing noggings or backing within the wall framing to support wall-mounted bench brackets.

name: Carpentry & Joinery Fabrication
description: The workshop or on-site activity of cutting, assembling, and finishing timber bench components to specified dimensions.

name: Painting & Surface Finishing
description: The trade activity of sanding, priming, and applying paint or stain coats to the completed bench unit.

name: Flooring Coordination
description: Planning and sequencing activity to ensure the bench installation aligns correctly with adjacent floor finishes and transitions.

name: Lighting Integration
description: Electrical activity involving the installation of task or accent lighting beneath or above the bench to illuminate the entry area.

name: IfcBuiltInFurniture
description: IFC class representing fixed, built-in furniture such as integrated entry bench joinery permanently attached to the building fabric.

name: Wall Base Footing
description: The structural concrete or masonry foundation strip beneath a sitting wall that distributes loads to the ground.

name: Retaining Core
description: The inner structural mass of a sitting wall that resists lateral earth or load pressures when the wall also serves a retaining function.

name: Drainage Aggregate Layer
description: A granular backfill layer placed behind a sitting wall to facilitate water drainage away from the structure.

name: Mortar Bed
description: A cementitious bonding layer used to set masonry units or coping stones in place during wall construction.

name: Concrete Masonry Unit (CMU) Block
description: Hollow or solid precast concrete blocks commonly used as the primary structural unit of a sitting wall.

name: Brick Course
description: Fired clay or concrete brick laid in horizontal courses to form the body of a sitting wall.

name: Precast Concrete Plank
description: A factory-cast concrete slab used as a spanning seat element supported by piers or end walls in a sitting wall assembly.

name: Cast-in-Place Concrete Wall
description: A monolithically poured concrete sitting wall system formed on-site, offering high strength and design flexibility.

name: Dry-Stack Masonry Wall
description: A mortarless sitting wall variant where units interlock through friction and weight alone, allowing natural drainage.

name: Gabion Sitting Wall
description: A sitting wall formed by wire mesh baskets filled with stones, combining structural mass with a distinctive aesthetic.

name: Timber Sitting Wall
description: A sitting wall constructed from treated timber or hardwood sections, typically used in garden or landscape settings.

name: Landscape Sitting Wall
description: An outdoor low wall specifically designed and positioned within a landscape to provide casual, informal seating areas.

name: Integrated Planter Sitting Wall
description: A sitting wall that incorporates planting beds or pots as part of its design, combining seating with greenery.

name: Amphitheatre Stepped Seating Wall
description: A series of terraced sitting walls arranged in stepped tiers to create an outdoor performance or gathering space.

name: Perimeter Sitting Wall
description: A low wall running along the boundary of a plaza, courtyard, or garden that doubles as peripheral seating.

name: Excavation and Grading
description: Site preparation work involving earth removal and levelling to establish the correct bearing level for the sitting wall footing.

name: Footing Formwork and Pouring
description: The construction activity of setting timber or steel forms and placing concrete to create the sitting wall's foundation.

name: Masonry Unit Laying
description: The trade activity of setting and bonding brick, block, or stone courses to build up the body of a sitting wall.

name: Surface Sealing and Finishing
description: Final treatment of exposed sitting wall faces with sealers, renders, or polishes to achieve the desired aesthetic and durability.

name: Integrated Lighting Fixture
description: Recessed or surface-mounted light fittings built into a sitting wall to provide ambient or accent illumination at night.

name: Tensioned Fabric Membrane
description: The primary stretched canvas or synthetic fabric layer that forms the weather-resistant outer surface of the roof.

name: Ridge Cable
description: High-tensile steel cable running along the peak of the roof that bears the primary longitudinal tension loads of the fabric membrane.

name: Valley Cable
description: Cable routed along the low points between fabric panels to collect and transfer loads toward support points.

name: Perimeter Cable
description: Boundary cable that defines the outer edge of the fabric panel and transfers edge loads to masts or anchor points.

name: Mast / Tension Mast
description: Vertical or raking steel post that elevates the high points of the fabric roof and introduces the necessary curvature for structural stability.

name: Ground Anchor / Foundation Anchor
description: Embedded footing or rock anchor that resists the uplift and lateral cable forces transferred from the fabric structure into the ground.

name: Clamp / Lacing System
description: Mechanical fasteners, rope lacing, or crimped fittings that attach the fabric membrane securely to boundary cables and edge elements.

name: Gutter & Drainage Channel
description: Linear drainage element positioned at valley lines or perimeter edges to collect and discharge rainwater away from the fabric.

name: Tensioning Turnbuckle
description: Adjustable threaded device inserted into cables or edge ties to achieve and maintain the required pre-tension in the fabric system.

name: Structural Steel Support Frame
description: The primary steel framework of columns, beams, and trusses to which cables and masts are connected, providing the rigid boundary for the tensile roof.

name: Anti-flap / Restraint Cable Net
description: Secondary network of cables sewn into or laid over the fabric to suppress aerodynamic flutter and membrane vibration under wind loads.

name: Fabric Panel
description: A discrete cut-and-welded section of membrane material shaped to the design geometry and forming one module of the overall roof surface.

name: PVC-Coated Polyester Fabric
description: A commonly used base material for tensile roofs consisting of a woven polyester scrim coated with PVC for weatherproofing and UV resistance.

name: PTFE-Coated Fibreglass Fabric
description: A high-performance, long-life roofing membrane made from fibreglass yarns coated with PTFE (Teflon), offering superior fire resistance and self-cleaning properties.

name: Saddle / Hypar Geometry
description: The anticlastic (saddle-shaped) double-curvature surface form that gives tensile fabric roofs their structural rigidity through opposing curves.

name: Cone / Conical Tent Form
description: A synclastic pointed roof shape radiating from a single high mast point, commonly used in stadium, marketplace, and event canopy designs.

name: Barrel Vault Fabric Canopy
description: A fabric roof formed into a single-curvature arch profile, typically supported by arching ribs and used for walkways or grandstands.

name: Covered Outdoor Gathering Space
description: The protected open-sided area beneath the fabric roof intended for public assembly, markets, or spectator seating.

name: Fabric Roof Installation
description: The site activity of unrolling, positioning, and mechanically connecting pre-fabricated fabric panels to the cable and structural frame.

name: Cable Pre-Tensioning
description: The controlled tightening of cables and edge elements to the specified design tension levels using jacks and turnbuckles.

name: Membrane Patterning & Cutting
description: The off-site process of geodesic or flat-pattern computation followed by precision cutting of fabric pieces to the design geometry.

name: Fabric Welding & Seaming
description: The factory process of joining individual fabric strips using heat welding or high-frequency welding to produce the full-size membrane panel.

name: Form-Finding Analysis
description: The structural engineering computational process of determining the equilibrium geometry of the tensile surface under design pre-stress conditions.

name: Fabric Cleaning & Maintenance
description: Periodic inspection, washing, and re-tensioning operations required to maintain the membrane's appearance, waterproofing, and structural integrity.

name: Membrane Replacement
description: The planned end-of-life removal and re-installation of the fabric panels when the material reaches the limit of its service life.

name: IFC Roof Element
description: The IFC class IfcRoof used to represent the overall canvas roof assembly within a building information model.

name: IFC Member (Cable)
description: The IFC class IfcMember used to model individual cable elements within the tensile roof structure in a BIM environment.

name: Acoustic Liner / Insulation Lining
description: An inner layer of sound-absorbing or thermal insulation material attached beneath the primary membrane to improve environmental performance.

name: Lighting Integration System
description: Flood or accent luminaires and cabling integrated into the mast or cable structure to illuminate the fabric roof from within or below.

name: Wind Load Design Criteria
description: The engineering load specification and analysis framework governing the fabric roof's resistance to uplift, flutter, and dynamic wind pressures.

name: Raised Planter Bed Frame
description: The structural frame or walls (wood, metal, masonry, or composite) that form the elevated enclosure holding soil for flower growth.

name: Planter Base / Floor Structure
description: The bottom layer of a raised planter, which may include drainage boards, mesh, or a solid base to separate soil from the ground or underlying surface.

name: Landscape Fabric / Root Barrier
description: A permeable geotextile membrane lining the interior walls and base to suppress weeds and prevent root escape while allowing water flow.

name: Soil / Growing Medium
description: A specially blended mix of topsoil, compost, and amendments filling the planter to provide nutrients and structure for flower cultivation.

name: Compost / Organic Amendments
description: Organic matter such as compost, peat, or bark fines incorporated into the growing medium to improve fertility, aeration, and water retention.

name: Edging & Coping
description: Decorative or protective trim pieces applied to the top perimeter of the raised planter to finish edges and prevent soil spillage.

name: Trellis / Support Structure
description: Vertical or angled frames, stakes, or wire systems installed within or adjacent to the raised bed to support climbing or tall flower varieties.

name: Pest & Weed Control System
description: Physical barriers, netting, or integrated pest management installations designed to protect flowers from insects, rodents, and invasive weeds.

name: Planter Surround / Pathway
description: The paved, gravelled, or planted walkway area immediately surrounding the raised flower space, enabling maintenance access and pedestrian circulation.

name: Fertilisation & Soil Conditioning Activity
description: The periodic application of fertilisers, pH adjusters, and organic conditioners to maintain optimal soil health for flowering plants.

name: Planting & Transplanting Activity
description: The horticultural activity of seeding, planting bulbs, or transplanting flower specimens into the raised bed at appropriate growing seasons.

name: Pruning & Deadheading Activity
description: Routine maintenance work involving trimming spent blooms, shaping plants, and removing dead growth to encourage continuous flowering.

name: Irrigation Maintenance Activity
description: Scheduled inspection, cleaning, and adjustment of irrigation components to ensure consistent and efficient water delivery to flowers.

name: Structural Construction & Installation Activity
description: The site preparation, assembly, and anchoring of the raised planter frame and its sub-components during initial construction or replacement.

name: Seasonal Replanting Activity
description: The cyclical removal of spent annual flowers and replacement with seasonal varieties to maintain year-round colour and interest.

name: Vertical Garden / Green Wall (Flower)
description: A closely related space variant where flowering plants are grown vertically on wall-mounted systems rather than in a horizontally raised bed.

name: Ground-Level Flower Bed
description: A related planted space at grade level, tracked separately to distinguish it from elevated raised-bed configurations in building records.

name: Container Planting (Pot / Urn)
description: An independent planting variant using discrete pots or urns that can be repositioned, as opposed to fixed raised-bed construction.

name: Timber (Hardwood / Treated Softwood)
description: Wood material commonly used for constructing raised planter frames, selected for rot resistance and structural adequacy.

name: Galvanised / Corten Steel
description: Metal sheeting or profiled sections used as an alternative planter wall material, valued for durability and contemporary aesthetic.

name: Masonry / Brick / Stone
description: Hard landscaping materials used to build permanent raised planter walls, providing robustness and a traditional or high-end finish.

name: Trellis Support Structure
description: A lattice or grid framework fixed to a wall or freestanding post that provides physical attachment points for climbing plant stems and tendrils.

name: Wire Rope Guide System
description: Tensioned stainless-steel or galvanised wire lines strung horizontally or vertically to train and support climbing plant growth across a facade or pergola.

name: Wall Anchor / Fixings
description: Mechanical anchors, eye bolts, or masonry fixings that secure trellis panels or wire systems to structural walls and columns.

name: Pergola Frame
description: A freestanding or wall-attached overhead framework of posts and beams that forms the primary support structure for overhead climbing plant coverage.

name: Arbour / Arch Structure
description: A curved or pointed archway structure, typically timber or steel, designed to frame a pathway and support climbing plants overhead.

name: Plant Training Ties & Clips
description: Soft ties, rubber clips, or twist ties used to secure individual plant stems to supports without damaging the plant tissue.

name: Root Barrier Membrane
description: An impermeable geotextile or plastic membrane installed in the soil to prevent aggressive root systems from damaging adjacent hard landscaping or foundations.

name: Planting Bed / Raised Planter
description: A defined soil bed or elevated planter box at the base of a support structure that provides the growing medium and drainage for climbing plants.

name: Irrigation Drip System
description: A low-flow drip irrigation network delivering water directly to the root zone of climbing plants to maintain consistent soil moisture.

name: Green Facade System
description: An integrated facade assembly combining structural support, growing medium, and climbing or cascading plants to provide thermal insulation and aesthetic greenery on building exteriors.

name: Living Wall Panel System
description: A modular panel-based system that supports climbing or cascading plants in pre-filled growing medium panels mounted directly onto a vertical wall surface.

name: Facade-Integrated Planting Zone
description: The designated vertical or overhead spatial zone on or adjacent to a building facade where climbing plants are trained to grow and provide coverage.

name: Covered Walkway / Pergola Corridor
description: An outdoor or semi-covered linear space formed beneath a pergola or arch structure canopied by climbing plant growth.

name: Courtyard Planting Zone
description: An enclosed or semi-enclosed outdoor courtyard area where climbing plants are used on boundary walls or structures to soften hard surfaces.

name: Deciduous Climber
description: A climbing plant species that sheds its leaves seasonally, providing shade in summer and allowing solar gain in winter — e.g., Wisteria or Virginia Creeper.

name: Evergreen Climber
description: A climbing plant species that retains foliage year-round, providing continuous screening, insulation, and acoustic buffering — e.g., Ivy or Climbing Hydrangea.

name: Self-Clinging Climber
description: A plant species that adheres directly to wall surfaces via adhesive pads or aerial rootlets, requiring no additional support fixings — e.g., Boston Ivy.

name: Twining / Tendril Climber
description: A climbing plant that wraps stems or tendrils around supports such as wires or trellis rails to ascend — e.g., Clematis or Passion Flower.

name: Growing Medium / Specialist Soil Mix
description: A lightweight, well-draining soil or substrate blend formulated to meet the nutritional and drainage needs of climbing plants in confined planting beds or panels.

name: Anti-Corrosion Coating on Supports
description: A protective galvanised, powder-coated, or stainless-steel finish applied to metal support structures to resist the moist, organic environment created by plant coverage.

name: Planting & Installation of Climbers
description: The site activity of preparing soil, positioning root balls, and initially training young climbing plants onto their support structures.

name: Trellis & Wire System Installation
description: The construction activity of fixing, tensioning, and commissioning all support frameworks and wire guide systems prior to planting.

name: Seasonal Pruning & Training
description: A recurring maintenance activity involving cutting back, redirecting, and tying in new growth to maintain plant health, coverage, and clearance from windows and gutters.

name: Facade Condition Inspection
description: A periodic inspection activity to assess whether climbing plant roots, aerial rootlets, or moisture retention are causing deterioration to the underlying wall substrate or mortar joints.

name: Irrigation System Commissioning
description: The testing and balancing of drip irrigation lines and timers to ensure even water distribution to all planted zones at time of handover.

name: Plant Replacement & Replanting
description: A maintenance activity covering the removal of failed or overgrown specimens and introduction of new plants to restore coverage or change species.

name: Support Structure Maintenance & Repair
description: Inspection and remediation of corroded fixings, broken trellis panels, or loose wire tensioners to ensure structural integrity of the climbing plant support system.

name: IFC Wall Element (IfcWall)
description: The IFC wall object class representing the host facade or boundary wall surface onto which climbing plant support systems are fixed.

name: IFC Railing (IfcRailing)
description: The IFC railing class used to model freestanding or balcony-edge trellis and wire guide frameworks in a BIM environment.

name: IFC Furniture / Site Furniture (IfcFurnishingElement)
description: The IFC class commonly used to represent pergola frames, arbours, and decorative plant support structures within a site or landscape model.

name: Paving Stone / Sett
description: Individual cut or natural stone unit laid as part of the paved surface, forming the primary structural element of the pavement.

name: Joint / Gap Between Stones
description: The intentional open or partially filled space between adjacent paving stones that defines the character and drainage behaviour of the surface.

name: Joint Infill Material
description: Loose or bound material such as sand, gravel, soil, or moss used to partially or fully fill the gaps between stones.

name: Bedding Layer
description: A compacted layer of sand, grit, or mortar directly beneath the paving stones that provides a level, stable seating surface.

name: Sub-base / Granular Base Course
description: A load-bearing layer of compacted crushed aggregate or hardcore below the bedding layer that distributes loads to the subgrade.

name: Subgrade / Formation Layer
description: The natural or prepared ground level beneath all constructed layers that ultimately carries the pavement loading.

name: Edge Restraint / Kerb
description: A border element such as a stone kerb, metal strip, or concrete haunch that contains the paving stones laterally and prevents spreading.

name: Drainage Channel / Linear Drain
description: A surface or sub-surface channel integrated into or alongside the paving to collect and direct water that infiltrates or runs off the stone surface.

name: Permeable / Infiltration Drainage System
description: An engineered sub-surface system exploiting the open joints to allow rainwater to percolate through the pavement into the ground below.

name: Stone Paving Area (Outdoor Hard Landscape)
description: The defined external or internal zone covered by the cracked/open-jointed stone pavement, considered as a spatial unit for use and maintenance planning.

name: Courtyard or Plaza Paved Surface
description: A specific spatial application of open-jointed stone paving in a courtyard, plaza, or public square context.

name: Pathway / Pedestrian Route
description: A linear paved route for pedestrian movement surfaced with open-jointed stone units.

name: Stone Paving Installation Activity
description: The construction process of laying paving stones onto a prepared bedding layer with deliberate open or cracked joints.

name: Sub-base Compaction Activity
description: The site operation of mechanically compacting the granular sub-base layers to the required density prior to stone laying.

name: Joint Filling / Pointing Activity
description: The task of brushing or packing infill material into the gaps between laid stones to achieve the desired joint appearance and stability.

name: Vegetation Management in Joints
description: Periodic maintenance activity to control, encourage, or remove plant growth (moss, grass, sedum) within the open joints between paving stones.

name: Stone Surface Cleaning & Maintenance
description: Routine maintenance including pressure washing, re-sanding, and re-levelling of displaced or sunken stones to preserve surface safety and appearance.

name: Natural Stone (Granite, Limestone, Sandstone, Basalt)
description: The specific stone material type from which paving units are cut or dressed, affecting durability, slip resistance, and aesthetics.

name: Geotextile / Filter Fabric
description: A permeable membrane placed between sub-layers to prevent fines migration while allowing water drainage through the pavement construction.

name: IFC Paving Element
description: The IFC schema class (IfcCovering or IfcPavement) used to digitally represent the paved surface element in a BIM model.

name: Ceramic Floor Tile
description: Fired clay tile used as a hard-wearing floor finish in soft tile and brick spaces.

name: Skirting Tile
description: Narrow tile unit installed at the wall-floor junction to protect and finish the base of a tiled wall.

name: Brick Slip
description: Thin veneer cut from a standard brick, applied to surfaces to replicate the appearance of full brickwork.

name: Tile Installation
description: Trade activity of preparing substrate, applying adhesive, setting, and grouting tile units to floors or walls.

name: Sealing and Finishing
description: Post-installation activity of applying sealant or surface treatment to protect tiles and grout from staining.

name: Tiled Floor Space
description: Floor area finished with hard ceramic, porcelain, or stone tiles forming a durable walking surface.

name: Brick-Faced Feature Wall
description: Interior or exterior wall zone clad with exposed brick or brick slips as a decorative architectural feature.

name: Tile and Brick Transition Zone
description: Area where soft carpet tile and hard brick or ceramic tile finishes meet, requiring careful edge detailing.

name: Tile Levelling System
description: Clip-and-wedge or spindle-based system used during installation to keep tile surfaces flush and level.

name: Frieze
description: A broad horizontal band of sculpted or painted decoration, typically located between the architrave and cornice.

name: Dentil Molding
description: A series of small, evenly spaced tooth-like rectangular blocks used as a decorative band in classical cornices.

name: Egg-and-Dart Molding
description: A classical decorative molding alternating oval (egg) and pointed (dart) shapes along its length.

name: Rosette
description: A circular, flower-like decorative element applied to ceilings, walls, or furniture as an ornamental motif.

name: Pilaster
description: A flat, rectangular column-like projection attached to a wall surface, primarily serving a decorative rather than structural function.

name: Capital
description: The uppermost decorative element of a column or pilaster, often elaborately carved in Doric, Ionic, or Corinthian styles.

name: Finial
description: A distinctive ornamental element placed at the apex of a roof, spire, gable, or furniture to provide a decorative terminus.

name: Acanthus Leaf Carving
description: A stylized carved representation of the acanthus plant leaf, commonly used in Corinthian capitals and classical friezes.

name: Bas-Relief Panel
description: A sculptural panel where figures or motifs project slightly from the flat background surface, used for wall or facade decoration.

name: Cartouche
description: An ornamental tablet or scroll-shaped frame, typically bearing an inscription or coat of arms, used on facades and ceilings.

name: Plaster Ceiling Rose
description: A circular ornamental plasterwork feature mounted on a ceiling, traditionally used as a decorative surround for a light fitting.

name: Quoin
description: Decorative masonry blocks at the external corners of a building, providing both structural emphasis and ornamental contrast.

name: Pediment
description: A triangular or curved gable-like element placed above doors, windows, or porticos as a classical decorative feature.

name: Festoon / Swag
description: A carved or molded decorative motif resembling a garland of flowers, fruit, or fabric draped in a curve between two points.

name: Tracery
description: Ornamental stone or timber framework, typically in Gothic architecture, forming decorative patterns within windows or on wall surfaces.

name: Cresting
description: A decorative ridge or parapet element running along the top of a roof or wall, often of cast iron, terracotta, or carved stone.

name: Terracotta Ornamental Tile
description: Fired clay tiles produced in decorative relief patterns, widely used for external cladding and ornamental facade panels.

name: Carved Stone
description: Natural stone worked by hand or machine into decorative profiles, motifs, and figurative elements for building ornamentation.

name: Cast Iron Ornament
description: Decorative building elements produced by casting molten iron into molds, commonly used for columns, railings, and facade details.

name: Gilded Leaf (Gold Leaf)
description: Ultra-thin sheets of gold applied to ornamental surfaces to provide a lustrous, reflective decorative finish on architectural details.

name: Ornamental Plasterwork Installation
description: The trade activity of applying, casting, and fixing decorative plaster moldings, cornices, and ceiling roses to interior surfaces.

name: Stone Carving and Dressing
description: The craft activity of shaping and carving stone by hand or CNC to produce decorative profiles, capitals, and relief panels.

name: Gilding and Patination
description: The finishing activity of applying gold leaf, metallic paints, or chemical patinas to ornamental elements for decorative effect.

name: Ornament Restoration and Conservation
description: Specialist activity involving the repair, cleaning, and reinstatement of historic decorative elements on existing buildings.

name: Decorative Painting and Graining
